speaker: Beggar
en: Psst. Misthios! You, with the eagle. Over here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's with all the whispering?

speaker: Beggar
en: Shh! If the soldiers hear us, they'll kill me. You're the misthios working for Kyra and the rebels, yes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am.

speaker: Beggar
en: Yes, you are. Many whispers of your deeds, misthios. Many whispers. Many secrets, too... about the rebel girl.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who I work for is none of your business, stranger.

speaker: Beggar
en: Secrets are being kept from you, misthios. Maybe you don't know who you really work for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's Kyra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you know something, spit it out.

speaker: Beggar
en: If the soldiers see me, they'll kill me. Apollo knows they already tried. There's a house near the market, been boarded up for ages. Sneaky sneak your way in. We'll talk later.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Strange. I should find the house, see what this beggar has to say.

speaker: Kassandra
en: House is boarded up. Must be the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bloody footprints. A child's... Must have been hiding in that chest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This woman was killed. Left in the open without dignity. An Athenian spear tip broke off in her ribs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A note was left behind. A warning from Podarkes. He was paying this woman to keep quiet. About what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wooden dolls—a mother and child. One engraved with the letter "M," and the other, "K."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing else to find here. I need to speak with that strange woman.

speaker: Beggar
en: And what did the misthios find?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A body... a woman. She was killed by an Athenian spear.

speaker: Beggar
en: This is all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was a letter from Podarkes—said he'd kill them both if she broke her silence. Both. Why kill a child? Unless... it was his.

speaker: Beggar
en: Shh! They could be listening. Now, tell me, quietly, what else did you find?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The dolls. Engraved with the letter "K" and "M." "M" is for mater. You asked who I worked for. The little doll with the "K"... The child was Kyra.

speaker: Beggar
en: Yes, yes. Which means...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra's skills with the blade started young.

speaker: Beggar
en: And you're Kyra's hope for the rebellion? Gods help us all!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Beggar
en: Unbelievable! If the child belonged to Podarkes, and the child is Kyra, then that would make...

speaker: Kassandra
en: By Zeus! Podarkes is Kyra's pater!

speaker: Beggar
en: Very wise, misthios. Very wise indeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods! Podarkes is Kyra's pater!

speaker: Beggar
en: Very wise, misthios. Very wise indeed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The dust in there gave me a headache. Just tell me.

speaker: Beggar
en: And you're Kyra's hope for the rebellion? Gods help us all! If the child belonged to Podarkes, and the child is Kyra, then that would make...

speaker: Beggar
en: Unbelievable! Podarkes is Kyra's pater, misthios! Her pater!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course!

speaker: Beggar
en: Not very wise, are you, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra needs to know.

speaker: Beggar
en: She'll never believe you. Never. Her whole life, she hunts the man who sent Athenians to kill her mater in front of her terrified eyes. But the gods spared little Kyra. She escaped.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know so much?

speaker: Beggar
en: I was there, misthios. I protected the little one. The Athenians were so busy trying to kill me, Kyra slipped right past their blades.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were involved in this...

speaker: Beggar
en: My name was Otonia. I was a servant for Podarkes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Beggar
en: Night after night, Kyra's mater came to the house—little one wanted to meet her pater. Podarkes made me send her away. But she kept coming. So Podarkes sent me to her house with a note.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The warning.

speaker: Beggar
en: She didn't listen. Podarkes sent me back to her house, this time with Athenian soldiers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra needs to know Podarkes is her father. But I won't confront her until I have proof.

speaker: Beggar
en: The woman came to Podarkes's house one night, begged me to give him the doll Kyra made for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Podarkes had it, he might have kept it somewhere.

speaker: Beggar
en: Only the gods would know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will find this doll.

speaker: Beggar
en: Now the misthios knows who she works for. The rebels should know too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Podarkes hid that doll somewhere in his house, I'm going to find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place is well guarded. Need to be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's the doll.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes kept the doll Kyra made for him. She engraved it with the letter "P"... for pater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Could Kyra have known all along? The rebels deserve the truth as well. But blood is everything to some people. They could abandon her if they knew Podarkes was her father.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's Kyra?

speaker: Damasos
en: She's

speaker: Kyra
en: Miss me already, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra, there's something I need to tell you.

speaker: Kyra
en: That look on your face. So serious. Sit, relax, drink some wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What I'm about to say is for you alone.

speaker: Kyra
en: Follow me.

speaker: Kyra
en: Now that you have me all alone, what is it you want to tell me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no other way to say this... Podarkes is your father.

speaker: Kyra
en: What sort of joke is this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't a joke.

speaker: Kyra
en: I will kill you where you stand. This can't be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra, I'm sorry.

speaker: Kyra
en: He took everything from me. How did you find this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found your old house. I know about your mater.

speaker: Kyra
en: I can still hear her screams. A storm of blue armor and red blades tore through our home. I had to run through maters blood to escape. I never returned to that place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was best you didn't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How I found it isn't important. What's important is that you know.

speaker: Kyra
en: It's good you told me in private. The men don't need to know this, not yet. But please, leave me for a while. I... need to be alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't come to drink wine. I came to tell you and your men—Podarkes is your father.

speaker: Laphanes
en: What?

speaker: Kritias
en: Her father?

speaker: Gurgos
en: That's a lie!

speaker: Kyra
en: This had better be some joke, misthios.

speaker: Kyra
en: Impossible.

speaker: Laphanes
en: Is it true?

speaker: Kritias
en: The daughter of Podarkes?!

speaker: Gurgos
en: We trusted you!

speaker: Kyra
en: I trusted you, Kassandra. And you disgraced me in front of my troops. Leave! I can't look at you right now.

speaker: Kyra
en: I can't even look at myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to face the kings.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Are you ready to take back our family's land?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. But my purpose here is to bring down the Cultist king.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You make your mother proud, Kassandra.

speaker: Myrrine
en: But are you sure you have enough proof to accuse him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know. Maybe I should look some more?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Accusing a king is not something you can take back. Make sure you're absolutely ready.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I'll gather the ephors and meet you in the throne room.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are the ephors?

speaker: Myrrine
en: You don't remember? Then again, you were only a child.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The five ephors are elected from the citizens of Sparta. They have power over even the kings. You need to convince them if you wish to save Sparta from the Cult's control.

speaker: Kassandra
en: See you in the throne room.

speaker: Archidamos
en: What are we waiting for?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Sorry to keep you waiting.

speaker: Archidamos
en: You summoned the ephors?

speaker: Pausanias
en: You must have achieved some success to earn this adoring crowd.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I brought home a wreath for Sparta, though I had to enter the Games and win it myself.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Very good. But what of our Pankration champion, Testikles?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was an accident at sea before he could compete.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Games are hardly important. What about Boeotia?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stentor and I defeated the Athenian forces. You have nothing to worry about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Athenian forces in Boeotia are no more. The land is yours.

speaker: Archidamos
en: That's excellent news.

speaker: Pausanias
en: I suppose you were too busy conquering territory to bring our champion to the Olympic Games?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I brought him to Elis... but he had an accident at sea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I entered the Games myself and won a wreath for Sparta.

speaker: Pausanias
en: By Nike! Well done, champion.

speaker: Archidamos
en: And the Lykaon Wolf?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Dead. Chopped off its head if you'd like to see it.

speaker: Archidamos
en: If you have nothing but good news to share, why did you call for the ephors?

speaker: Ephor
en: We were told serious charges would be brought.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Serious charges? Against whom?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You act as if you don't know. Against you, Pausanias.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have travelled Spartan lands and beyond and found proof of Pausanias's betrayal. He's a member of the Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These traitors are willing to kill hundreds to rule thousands. Here's all the proof you need.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Proof? What proof?

speaker: Ephor
en: So the rumors are true... We never would have thought a king could be so dishonorable.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Honor belongs to history.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pausanias blackmailed Lagos of Arkadia. He held the archon's family hostage in exchange for helping the Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Lagos? Is this true?

speaker: Ephor
en: We had received word from other sources, but with nothing definite we would not accuse a king.

speaker: Pausanias
en: So, Lagos finally turned. He has more spine than I thought.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You deserve death for your crimes.

speaker: Pausanias
en: How dare you threaten a king?

speaker: Ephor
en: Pausanias, you are king no more. As of this day, you are exiled from Sparta.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Before Athena and Ares, I swear you'll regret this! Justice will be done!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll have your justice, puppet king.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Forgive us, my king. My daughter couldn't let him stay in power any longer.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Of course not.

speaker: Archidamos
en: You've more than earned your citizenship. Sparta owes you thanks and releases your home unto you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your home is returned!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Our home, lamb.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Let's leave the court to its business. We'll talk outside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sparta must be rid of Pausanias before it's too late. He's a member of the Cult of Kosmos and a traitor to Sparta!

speaker: Archidamos
en: A Kosmos cult? What are you going on about?

speaker: Pausanias
en: Is this some kind of joke?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have the proof right here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your proof is right there. You know he's guilty.

speaker: Ephor
en: This isn't proof of anything. Ephors should only be called upon for serious matters. This lack of evidence is a waste of our time and disrespectful to the thrones of Sparta. The accuser should be made into an example for all other reckless fools.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I taught her poorly! Punish me, as her mother, instead.

speaker: Pausanias
en: We gave you every chance to prove yourself, invited you back for a royal audience, and this is how you repay us? What say you, Archidamos?

speaker: Archidamos
en: Kassandra and Myrrine of Agiad: Your names are cursed. May the krypteia hunt you, and the helots scrape the meat from your bones.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Agreed. A wise ruling.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Too bad you don't have a mask or black cloak to save you this time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were there, in Delphi?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Archidamos. Sparta must be rid of you before it's too late.

speaker: Archidamos
en: What are you talking about? How dare you stand in the presence of kings and make such accusations.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Patience, Archidamos. Present your proof.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Archidamos is a member of the Cult of Kosmos and a traitor to Sparta!

speaker: Archidamos
en: The Cult of what? Ridiculous! What proof could you possibly have?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your proof is right there. You know he's guilty.

speaker: Ephor
en: This isn't proof of anything. Ephors should only be called upon for serious matters. This lack of evidence is a waste of our time and disrespectful to the thrones of Sparta. The accuser should be made into an example for all other reckless fools.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I taught her poorly! Punish me, as her mother, instead.

speaker: Pausanias
en: We gave you every chance to prove yourself, invited you back for a royal audience, and this is how you repay us? What say you, Archidamos?

speaker: Archidamos
en: Kassandra and Myrrine of Agiad: Your names are cursed. May the krypteia hunt you, and the helots scrape the meat from your bones.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Agreed. A wise ruling.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Too bad you don't have a mask or black cloak to save you this time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were there, in Delphi?!

speaker: Myrrine
en: As for Pausanias, it would be wise to deal with him as soon as possible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will. He is a Cultist after all.

speaker: Myrrine
en: When you've dealt with him, meet me at home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With pleasure.

speaker: Myrrine
en: When you've dealt with him, meet me at Leonidas' tomb. I must show you something important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find you there, mater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: King Pausanias is part of the Cult of Kosmos. I'll have to kill him myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's Pausanias. Maláka.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater— Pausanias revealed himself before I was dragged out of there.

speaker: Myrrine
en: So he is the Cultist King. It would be wise to deal with him as soon possible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will.

speaker: Myrrine
en: When you've dealt with him, meet me at home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With pleasure.

speaker: Myrrine
en: When you've dealt with him, meet me at Leonidas' tomb. I must show you something important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find you there, mater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: King Pausanias is part of the Cult of Kosmos. I'll have to kill him myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's Pausanias. Maláka.

speaker: Cultist Proof
en: This letter proves that Pausanias is part of the Cult.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Kassandra! You were condemned to be hunted!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should have been more certain before accusing Pausanias. He is a plague on Sparta and its territories.

speaker: Archidamos
en: And you say you're sure now? Where is he, so he can defend himself?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I watched him die.

speaker: Archidamos
en: You murdered him...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't matter.

speaker: Archidamos
en: It does to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found proof he was a member of the Cult of Kosmos. Undeniable proof. This letter was written and signed by Pausanias' own hand, outlining the progress of their plans in Sparta.

speaker: Archidamos
en: What is this Cult of Kosmos? You've mentioned them over and over as if I should know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're a secret group with one goal: to seize power. They are using this war to strengthen their position.

speaker: Archidamos
en: I find it difficult to think Pausanias was using Sparta this whole time. We've ruled together for years... I'll speak with the ephors to confirm what you say, but if it's true, you deserve to be called a Spartan citizen once more. And, of course, your family home is yours again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Archidamos
en: One more thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes?

speaker: Archidamos
en: Should you decide to rule Sparta yourself, at least let me face you in battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not made for ruling, my king.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Leonidas. He was Sparta's last true hero. We'd all be under the yoke of the Persian Empire if it wasn't for his courage. The same blood courses through your veins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My blood courses through these veins. Not some man's I've never met.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Leonidas was king, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And yet I grew up in the dirt!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm proud of my lineage, but I carve my own path.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You carry the blood of heroes. You can carve much more than the path of a mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, our blood is the blood of kings.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You are so much more than a mercenary. You carry the blood of heroes, blood of power. Remember what I told you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That people would try to take that power for themselves.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And then you promised...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wouldn't let them.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Hold out your spear.

speaker: Leonidas
en: All of this talk of the Pythia. The Pythia! I do not care what she says.

speaker: Cultist
en: Enough! We have grown tired of your insolent tongue! Sparta will not go to war, the Pythia has spoken!

speaker: Leonidas
en: The Pythia says what you tell her to say! She's been your puppet for far too long, the time has come to cut her strings!

speaker: Cultist
en: Oh Leonidas, the are over. You think your blood makes you special? If we opened your veins it would spill to the ground and disappear through the cracks. You are no one.

speaker: Leonidas
en: You are more than welcome to find out.

speaker: Pythia
en: Your fate is sealed, Son of the Lion. Xerxes will unite us. He will bring order to chaos.

speaker: Cultist
en: Defy the Pythia, and everyone you love, everything you stand for, will perish.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Gather the men.

speaker: Dienekes
en: My king?

speaker: Leonidas
en: If Xerxes wants Sparta, he'll have to go through me.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Now do you understand? You were always meant to topple tyrants.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do I do now?

speaker: Myrrine
en: We continue down the path our destiny has set. If we don't stop the Cult before it's too late, then all Leonidas fought and died for was for nothing. Our bloodline has risen to those who would enslave us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's time we rise again.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It's gone...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's gone?

speaker: Myrrine
en: There was a skull here, a small rabbit skull. From your first hunt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would someone take that?

speaker: Myrrine
en: There is only one person who would have taken it. Nikolaos...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe seeing each other again made him think of this place. It did the same to me.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Seems I wasn't the only one yearning for home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This house has been vacant for a long time. Many robbers could have come and gone.

speaker: Myrrine
en: They would have no reason to take an old rabbit skull.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe they thought it was valuable. It was on display, after all.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Perhaps...

speaker: Brasidas
en: I hope I'm not intruding.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas! Come in!

speaker: Brasidas
en: It's good to see the two of you back home.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It feels good to be here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're here instead of in training, what's wrong?

speaker: Brasidas
en: I'm heading to Pylos as soon as I can. I think you may want to come as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd be happy to return the favor. What's waiting for us in Pylos?

speaker: Brasidas
en: Glory. The Athenians are pushing the Spartans back even as we speak. It would be a devastating loss for Sparta, and I can't allow that to happen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It sounds like you've lost confidence in Sparta's warriors.

speaker: Brasidas
en: They're as strong as they've ever been. But now they're facing a power they can't even imagine.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Do you mean Deimos?

speaker: Brasidas
en: Yes, that's what the rumors say. A force of nature in the body of a mortal, who can cut down any soldier in his path.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've finally gotten our home back, and you want me to leave?

speaker: Brasidas
en: The Cultists appear to have lost their patience. Their moves in Pylos are bold and ruthless.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Is Deimos there?

speaker: Brasidas
en: I've heard rumors. If they're true, not even a phalanx of Spartans could stop him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Deimos is in Pylos, we have to stop him.

speaker: Brasidas
en: I'll wait for you at the ship, but be quick. Each moment we waste is another Spartan dead.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Alexios is in Pylos... You have to bring him back, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bring him back?

speaker: Myrrine
en: We have our home again. We can be a family. It isn't too late.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll bring him back. No matter what.

speaker: Myrrine
en: This is serious, Kassandra. We may not get another chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I understand. He must have seen the Cultists for what they truly are by now.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It doesn't matter what you have to do. Bring back your brother. You must.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing will stop me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shouldn't keep Brasidas waiting.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Be safe, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I can, mater, but I can't promise anything.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Please, don't say that, yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult of Kosmos has had too much time with him. He is beyond reason.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Isn't it worth trying everything we can?

speaker: Kassandra
en: And if I can't save my brother?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Then we will have tried. We thought him dead for so long. I refuse to give up just yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I can. I should leave for Pylos now.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Be safe, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't do it. I wish I could tell you otherwise, but he's too far gone.

speaker: Myrrine
en: That can't be true. You both have the same blood coursing through your veins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's nothing we can do. He sees us as nothing more than obstacles in his path.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You can't just give up on family so easily. You didn't give up on me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We haven't been a family since I was thrown from that mountain. I won't pretend that bringing Deimos back will unmake the past.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You're giving up on your own brother. On us?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's too late, mater. I can't save him. He's made his choice.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The Cult of Kosmos never gave him one. We've thought him dead once, and you're choosing to kill him again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should go... Brasidas won't wait for long.

speaker: Markos
en: Help! Somebody? Anybody? Hello?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Markos?

speaker: Markos
en: Kassandra? Chaire!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How...

speaker: Markos
en: Kept myself busy, haven't I? No time to explain here. Get me out!

speaker: Markos
en: You're as nimble as ever! Now, carry me to my house on the other side of the mountain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have to carry you the whole way?

speaker: Markos
en: I-I'm so weak. I'm so frail...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Markos. Another vineyard?

speaker: Markos
en: I am nothing if not consistent, my friend!

speaker: Markos
en: Ah, much better! No one makes a hasty exit like you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're welcome.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Interesting... it seems Xenia doesn't control the entire island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, I can almost hear my staff's voice. I wonder if it can hear mine...

speaker: Ide
en: I'm over here! I need your help breaking out!

speaker: Ide
en: Let's get the fuck out of here!

speaker: Ide
en: Misthios, thank you! Those fuckers thought they could hold me, but they just didn't understand. No prison can hold me. Nobody can hold me down. Not even that stupid Order...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right...

speaker: Ide

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Order think they know pain. But I will teach them. They think they know hurt. But I will show them. They think they know fear... But I swear to you, Natakas, I will bring them terror.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find our boy. I'll bring him home. Trust me.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Kassandra... By the gods. I'm sorry.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The Order did all this...

speaker: Barnabas
en: This weaponry they brought would make even Ares turn his head. There's only one place in the Greek world that makes anything like it. Messenia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They came for us. For me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Order is in Messenia... that's where I'll go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a message on the board. What's the matter?

speaker: Woman
en: Yet another young man swore he would prove himself the sole person worthy of my affection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's... nice?

speaker: Woman
en: Maybe so, misthios, but I don't think this one will return. The poor fool has gone lion hunting. He is a good client... it would be a shame to lose him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you'd like me to protect him.

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, he must remain unscathed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll do it.

speaker: Woman
en: Good. You're doing me a great service.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when I'm done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to look after you.

speaker: Man
en: Thank the gods! I hear them coming!

speaker: Woman
en: Misthios! Were you able to keep him safe?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: You're a true warrior. Please take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Happy to help.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra. Kassandra. Kassandra.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra. Kassandra. Kassandra.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Kassandra. It was never supposed to be like this.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Decades ago, a group of people gathered together to uphold a theory which they believed could control the universe. That the world functioned in equal parts, order and disorder.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: But some fell lovingly into the wicked arms of chaos. And the Cult of Kosmos was born.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: They abused their power, casting the Greek world into eternal war—one you were created to stop.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: In destroying the Cult, you have done what I could not. You are a hero. But this imbalance comes with a price, my child.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: For without chaos, there is supreme order. A loss of progression and freedom.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: But there is still hope—hope in you, hope in the future you will bring.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: We must fix the mistakes of the past. Use the staff. Repair the rift in the universe.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: The world depends on you, Kassandra. You need to be the hero again.

speaker: Aspasia
en: So you've seen it too, then? It's beautiful isn't it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you doing here?

speaker: Aspasia
en: You killed the last member of the Cult. Well, just about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Aspasia
en: It's true. I was their leader, but only for a moment it seemed. When your brother came along, it changed everything we were aiming for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You agreed with them? With the fucking Cult?

speaker: Aspasia
en: The powers that be in the Greek world weren't doing things the right way. The Cult just wanted a clean slate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By way of corruption. Dirty drachmae. They killed people in a war they made themselves.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Fueling war was one of the methods, yes. But it was controlled. Until suddenly it wasn't. And then I didn't like what we were doing anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought Deimos was on your side.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Not in the way we hoped. As you know, he's impossible to control. He worked his way to the helm, and then he held even more sway than I did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka... So you were after us.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Not you, your bloodline. People like Leonidas, like you, have always posed a threat. Then we met, and you surprised me. You were nothing like Deimos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why not just use me? I was in the palm of your hand.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You made me optimistic, that you could help me bring down the Cult that had become so corrupt. And you did, albeit unknowingly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're all the same. Selfish, and fucking destructive.

speaker: Aspasia
en: It was different in the beginning. It wasn't about destruction, it was about redirection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Telling me you're a Cultist took guts. You know what I do to Cultists, Aspasia.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I didn't want to lie to you anymore. Now that they're gone, we can work together. I think we'd make a good match, don't you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is a lot to take in. But I know you had good intentions. I don't think you lied about that.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Never. I thought I could maintain control, but I overestimated myself. It just got away from me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just don't understand. What about this... pyramid? How does it work? Why does the Cult have it?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I've been trying to figure out all of that myself. It's as much of a mystery to you as it is to me. This pyramid has been worshipped by the Cult for decades, and we have used it to replace the Oracle of Delphi, the most trusted person in all the Greek world. Using the people's reliance on a pantheon of dead gods would help to reshape humanity in our favor. The pyramid holds a mysterious power to see into time. But only certain people can activate it. People like Deimos, and the ones in your bloodline.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you've seen something, too.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I don't know how or why, but it did show me something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you see?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I saw you. In the vision, you destroyed the pyramid and you destroyed the Cult... I saw what would come after.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After the Cult?

speaker: Aspasia
en: We will be replaced by a new kind of order—control under the reign of a philosopher king. There would be a movement away from the old gods towards rational society, built in a kingdom by the people, for the people. And I must find someone to lead them. But I couldn't achieve any of this with the Cult and their chaotic regime. So I let them carry out their plans, and let the time of the Cult of Kosmos come to an end on its own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait. Did Perikles know?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I wanted to protect him, so I kept him in the dark. He would have had his own opinions. But he was never supposed to die. That is the truth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've made questionable choices. But I think that was the right one.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You knew him. All he did was worry about the state of the Greek world. If I'd told him, it would have ruined him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He trusted you. And in the end, you didn't protect him. Maybe he would be alive if you'd stopped them.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Gods know I would have if I could. When Deimos killed him, I knew the original cause was lost. I had to retreat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So. What happens now?

speaker: Aspasia
en: We shift focus. We steer towards a new republic under one supreme rule. A dream I'll make reality.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But it is still a dream. One that isn't realistic.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Abandon what you know and just imagine! Forget democracy. No more blue and red, just citizens working for a greater good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is crazy. It won't work, Aspasia. It didn't work.

speaker: Aspasia
en: It's not crazy, it's enlightened. Once in people in Athens get wind of this, they'll come to know they've wanted it all along. Even you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You've spent your whole life thinking for yourself. Let go. What I plan will require you to trust me. Come with me. This future's not a dream.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I suppose that means you trust me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... don't know what that means.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'll tell you what it means. Love is a singular comfort, Kassandra. What comes next means harmony for everyone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should go. Lead your "new republic."

speaker: Aspasia
en: I won't be the leader. We need someone with the knowledge of a philosopher and the wisdom of a king.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a tall order these days.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I couldn't have done this without you, Kassandra. You're doing the right thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always try to do what's right.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Then we're after the same thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't let you do this. You've caused so much damage. You destroyed the Greek world.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You've proven you have no understanding of what we're doing. I misjudged you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So did I.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should go. Lead your "new republic."

speaker: Aspasia
en: I won't be the leader. We need someone with the knowledge of a philosopher and the wisdom of a king.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a tall order these days.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I couldn't have done this without you, Kassandra. You're doing the right thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always try to do what's right.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Then we're after the same thing.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra. There is much left to do, lamb.

speaker: Myrrine
en: KASSANDRA! ...A storm is coming...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can weather any storm.

speaker: Heitor
en: Kassandra? By the gods, is that you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods! Heitor, is that you? You look... you look old, my friend.

speaker: Heitor
en: When was the last time I saw you? Kephallonia! That job for Markos. Remember, we ended up back to back, surrounded by angry pirates...

speaker: Kassandra
en: They were only angry because you double-crossed them. Thank the gods we got out alive.

speaker: Heitor
en: Ah! They should've paid better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Though as I recall, I had your back.

speaker: Heitor
en: Polish your memories like you would your armor, and they'll make much better tales.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd heard rumors you'd settled down in Attika. Always thought you'd die with a blade in your hand... not open up a shop.

speaker: Heitor
en: The blade I always thought I'd take with me is missing... I could use your help, if you're willing to assist an old friend?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean Harpe? You loved that blade...

speaker: Heitor
en: Some malákas commander come in here demanding I fix his fucking twig. When I couldn't, he said I was obligated to provide a new one—and the one he wanted was hanging on my wall.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get Harpe back for you.

speaker: Heitor
en: Don't do anything stupid. I just want her back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hey! You know me.

speaker: Heitor
en: That's why I'm afraid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where to find the commander.

speaker: Heitor
en: He's here in Attika, at Fort Phyle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why go so much trouble for an old sword?

speaker: Heitor
en: She's the only thing I loved that never left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And how will I know her when I see her?

speaker: Heitor
en: How could you forget a hilt of gold with a curling serpent moving up the blade? Always sharp no matter what, and when you swung her, well... she'd sing a siren song of death. Kept me alive through many a scrape.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That I do remember.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should be going.

speaker: Heitor
en: Remember, we don't want trouble. Just sneak in and take it. You're still good at that, right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't lower myself to answer that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be Fort Phyle. If Heitor's right, I'll find the sword inside.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier 1
en: Did you see that new sword the commander just bought?

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier 2
en: As fine a blade as ever I've seen.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier 1
en: Got it from the new smith, I heard him say.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier 2
en: Yeah, the smith didn't make it, though. He can knock a dent out all right, but that sword...

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier 1
en: That's real craftsmanship, that is.

speaker: Harpe
en: Harpe is an incredibly crafted and distinct blade. No one's exactly sure how Heitor ended it up (sic) with it originally as his story seems to change with each telling.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is Harpe all right. No mistaking this blade.

speaker: Heitor
en: Glad you're back safely. Did you get my Harpe?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, I found Harpe.

speaker: Heitor
en: Good, good.

speaker: Heitor
en: And what of that malákas commander?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He didn't survive our... encounter.

speaker: Heitor
en: You are a true friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what of him?

speaker: Heitor
en: Oh, no matter—you have my sword. That's what's important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have a feeling there's more to the story of Harpe's disappearance than you're letting on...

speaker: Heitor
en: What? Come now, you've always had such suspicious mind. Still seeing conspiracies everywhere, are we?

speaker: Heitor
en: You've done me a great favor here—let's not sour the celebration.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sword wasn't stolen from you, was it? You used me.

speaker: Heitor
en: Truth be told, I never said it was stolen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You...

speaker: Heitor
en: Ah, a crime of omission only, my friend. You know how important Harpe is to me. I had no money, couldn't fight anymore. I would have died without a drachma by the side of the road. Selling Harpe enabled me to start my business. You wouldn't begrudge a man a second chance, would you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No... but I don't like being lied to.

speaker: Heitor
en: I'm sorry, OK? I'm sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Heitor, you had my back and taught me so much on Kephallonia. Don't worry about the drachmae you promised—consider the favor repaid.

speaker: Heitor
en: You've grown into a fine woman, Kassandra. A better mercenary with both a strong arm and a kind heart would be hard to find.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sometimes too kind. Just don't tell anyone. Can't have people thinking I'm weak.

speaker: Heitor
en: No, of course. A misthios reputation is everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Getting Harpe back wasn't easy. I had to go to a lot of trouble... A little drachmae wouldn't hurt.

speaker: Heitor
en: Ha! You truly are a mercenary, through and through.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I learned from the best, remember?

speaker: Heitor
en: Of course, of course. I'm happy to pay. You did me a great service today, and great work deserves a great reward. Here, take this.

speaker: Heitor
en: Even if I don't swing her anymore, I'm glad to have Harpe back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Take care of yourself, Heitor, and try not to lose anything else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I searched every camp, but there was no sign of it.

speaker: Heitor
en: What happened?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe whoever stole it sold it on? It's a valuable and unique weapon.

speaker: Heitor
en: Huh, yes... perhaps. Well, you tried. I can't ask for more than that. At least we can rely on our friends. If not, who could we trust?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gods be with you, Heitor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the one who left the message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: I have an important message for the Athenian commander... It's concealed inside a dried bear's bladder for complete secrecy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you hiding the message?

speaker: Woman
en: Because, misthios, the message contains information on the Spartans' movements! Unfortunately, this is my last bear bladder. I'll need more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Does someone sell them?

speaker: Woman
en: I usually take them from dead bears I find in the forest. But they've been scarce lately, and I need to get this message to the commander.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to deliver it to the Athenian commander.

speaker: Woman
en: That's exactly it. Will you do it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Woman
en: Good. Please handle this... delicately.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're done here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A woman told me you'd be expecting this.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, misthios! Here, this is for you.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Aphrodite. Artemis. Athena. Mothers and daughters of Olympous. Please, lead us to safety. We can't lose anyone else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm none of those, but I am Kassandra, a misthios. What's wrong?

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: My people are in grave danger. We lost our leaders and our warriors, and now our hunters have disappeared.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hunting parties can be gone for weeks before returning. What happened to everyone else?

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: War. The fight between Athens and Sparta has reached our borders, so the men left to offer their swords. I fear that those remaining will be lost to the Sons of Xerxes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't heard of the Sons of Xerxes. That's quite the name.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Persians left over from the Battle of Thermopylai. They have no nation except the heritage of an ancient king... But their numbers are great, and ours are not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would not trade our roles in this situation. Though killing is my specialty, and I can hunt and track.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Do you deal in advice? I don't know how to address my people. They know something is wrong, and I'm not sure what to do about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're the leader, then act like it. High road or low road, you must still pick your path.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: You're right. I need to make preparations instead of panicking. But then there's still the missing hunting party... Would you find them for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no easy answer. If you were to take it one step at a time, how would you start?

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: I can't bring back the men or stop the Sons of Xerxes by myself. I know it's a lot to ask, but can you bring them home? Even if it's just bones, we'll need to honor them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll look for the missing hunters.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: My cousin Agnodike volunteered to look for them. She hasn't returned either.

speaker: Agnodike
en: Those bastards. Those bastards!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Agnodike
en: Do I look all right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You survived. It's more than we can say for your companions.

speaker: Agnodike
en: That was our warning. First our hunters, then the rest of the village. I need to warn our Magistrate about the Sons of Xerxes and their plans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And I need to see her about my payment.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: You've returned! What news of Agnodike and the hunters?

speaker: Agnodike
en: Magistrate Periktione... I have grave news. The Sons of Xerxes are preparing to strike.

speaker: Agnodike
en: Oh it's you. Magistrate, this misthios saved me from certain death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For double the reward, I hope.

speaker: Thyia
en: Finally, someone around here who knows how to use a sword! I've been trying to convince Peri to build our defenses since we first saw the Sons of Xerxes creeping closer to the village.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: This is my sister, Thyia. She considers herself to be... acting general of Lalaia in the men's absence.

speaker: Thyia
en: It was your husband who shielded us before... Someone must do so now! Did you hear anything Agnodike said? If we wait on the gods for help we will be massacred!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The only language the Sons of Xerxes seem to understand is violence.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Misthios, what if I hired you to protect the village?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I can.

speaker: Thyia
en: Good! Meet me at Kephisos Spring. I have plans for those Sons of Xerxes.

speaker: Civilian
en: Empedokles can lead us all to meet the gods! He knows the way! We must worship him! Your insults may be strong, and—and quite hurtful, but my devotion to the god Empedokles is stronger!

speaker: Priestess
en: Your false god, this "Empedokles," is a delusional vegetarian. His presence, and yours, will not be tolerated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What seems to be the problem?

speaker: Civilian
en: Empedokles be praised, a misthios! I've done nothing wrong, yet these priestesses mean me harm! Please—my god is powerful! And rich!

speaker: Priestess
en: His "god" is a malákas—a blasphemous blight on Aphrodite's hallowed soil! This is a matter for priestesses alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said "rich"?

speaker: Civilian
en: Indeed! Empedokles rewards those who come to his call! These priestess have imprisoned him in the fort. He's a god—he deserves worship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're threatened by a mob, but you want me to save him, not you? Sounds like quite the god.

speaker: Civilian
en: Only Empedokles can lead us to his brothers and sisters on Mount Olympos. He is far more important than any one man.

speaker: Priestess
en: Surely you cannot be considering helping these lunatics! You would oppose the will of Aphrodite!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He doesn't sound like much of a god to me.

speaker: Civilian
en: How could you

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't keep a god bound, and anyone who tried would die in the attempt.

speaker: Civilian
en: Empedokles is not that kind of god.

speaker: Priestess
en: He is no god at all! Your words are an affront to the will of Aphrodite!

speaker: Civilian
en: If these priestesses speak for Aphrodite, then I speak for all three slobbering heads of Cerberus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to go save a god. Apparently.

speaker: Priestess
en: Do as you will, misthios. But even you cannot be everywhere at once.

speaker: Civilian
en: I'll be fine. Is there anything else you need to know?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find this god of yours?

speaker: Civilian
en: They have him locked in a cage in Skandeia Bay with the livestock. This would be shameful for any regular god, and more so for a vegetarian god!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Does he stand out in any way? There may be more than one prisoner.

speaker: Civilian
en: The guards stripped him naked. And when you are confronted with his "gift," Empedokles's godly nature will be hard to deny.

speaker: Kassandra
en: His "gift"?

speaker: Civilian
en: Let's just say you'll know it when you see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know all I need. Your Empedokles will be freed.

speaker: Civilian
en: Do not worry for my safety, misthios–it is Empedokles who needs your help!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's the Murex Camp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's over there.

speaker: Empedokles
en: A god such as I deserves more leg room! I! Am! A! God! And you will return my robe to me, washed and neatly folded! Imprison me if you must—but do not hurt my beloved cloak, you, you MONSTERS!

speaker: Empedokles
en: Do you see, feeble humans? I, the great Empedokles, cannot be caged! Worship me, and I offer you an audience... with the gods! Put down your blades. I offer those who follow me an audience with my brothers and sisters, the gods! Gods cannot bleed! So—so you best put down your blades. DO NOT STAB MY GODLY GROIN!!! Look upon my form, mortals! Regard my godly gifts and know the truth of my words!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No need to thank me for your rescue, your drachmae is thanks enough

speaker: Empedokles
en: Me, thank you?! Here? With no audience? No, no, no, my heroic friend—the stage is not set! Our performance is missing that most vital ingredient: an audience! Meet me by my personal statue so we may continue.

speaker: Empedokles
en: We worship a little differently where I'm from. We don't kill a man for what he believes. We show respect.

speaker: Priestess
en: Respect is for the gods, not those who pretend to be them.

speaker: Empedokles
en: The world is full of strife, yes, but also love. Embrace it—embrace me, and I will personally introduce you all to my family... the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw Empedokles risk his greatest treasure—running naked through a military camp—and showed no fear. There is clearly something... special about this man.

speaker: Priestess
en: You've made no friends today.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who needs friends when I have the gods?

speaker: Empedokles
en: Thank you for your support, misthios. In the future, my Empedoklites could use someone with your talents.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If being locked naked in a cell makes someone a god, the pantheon would be overflowing.

speaker: Civilian
en: Maybe Empedokles is a god, maybe he's not. All I know is that he doesn't beat young men to death.

speaker: Civilian
en: I follow you, proudly.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Brothers, sisters of Kythera: join me.

speaker: Priestess
en: You think betraying Aphrodite will go unpunished?

speaker: Empedokles
en: You may not believe in my godliness, misthios—but I believe there's some god in you. And that... we can put to use.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even a god won't work for free.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Of course! What else would I spend my drachmae on? Clothes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Clothes would do you some good.

speaker: Empedokles
en: You're just scared—of my true form! But there's another matter we need to discuss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course, why would you?

speaker: Empedokles
en: Perhaps you could aid me in another matter?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. How often do you get to help a god?

speaker: Empedokles
en: Of my caliber? Never! Come, my well-muscled friend. There is much to discuss. But first!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're not the god of "getting to the point?"

speaker: Empedokles
en: The likeness is terrifyingly good, don't you think?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Terrifying, yes. What did you need?

speaker: Empedokles
en: A god never needs help! But yes, please. I've been having trouble with my brothers and sisters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods?

speaker: Empedokles
en: Family problems. When I first arrived on Kythera, I was imprisoned for my beliefs. They stole my purple robe, and inside it is a very special disk... the key to my family estate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you want this disk retrieved.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Of course! The disk is a key! A key that opens a door to the gods themselves! This disk must be returned to me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...This disk?

speaker: Empedokles
en: Praise ME and all my glorious glory, yes this is the disk! Only a god such as I could be so fortunate!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said this robe-thief intercepted you at the dock. Do you know where he is now?

speaker: Empedokles
en: He and his guards patrol along Kythera's main roads, but he enjoys roughing up recent arrivals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods would protect themselves with more than a locked door opened by a disk.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Oh but you should see the door, misthios! Something so beautiful was not crafted by mortal hands! And my brothers, my sisters, I hear them calling me home from beyond it...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are your godly brothers and sisters really like, Empedokles?

speaker: Empedokles
en: As any sibling—loving. Filled with strife. They once caught me eating lamb and cast me out. Though between you and me, that lamb? Worth it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods wait for no one.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Patience is not one of our virtues, no. Will you help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This disk sounds important. I'll find the man who stole it and return it to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Magistrate Xanthe told me that you've been having trouble with your farm.

speaker: Lanike
en: Crop failure. It's as if Eris herself salted the earth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How are the crops failing?

speaker: Lanike
en: Blight! Few plants grow, and the ones that do are wilted and covered in spots. The gods would never let this happen if they were happy. It's my godless helots, I tell you. You're a messenger of Zeus, you show them the light.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out what's happening.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have time right now.

speaker: Lanike
en: Magistrate Xanthe said you would examine my fields and see why the gods have cursed me so.

speaker: Lanike
en: Oh, thank Zeus. My helots, Teuta and Maron... They work the fields, but they do not respect the gods. Teach them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't seen other farms in the area with blighted crops. What could be causing the difference?

speaker: Lanike
en: The grain grew in short and dry, then the animals started to grow ill. Obvious signs of displeasing Persephone or her mother. Maron claims the animals have been poisoned, but I have no enemies to speak of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What makes you blame your helots for the blight? Have they tampered with the plants and animals?

speaker: Lanike
en: They do not worship as you and I do. I thank Demeter for all she gives us at the end of each day. But they just reap the bounty of her hard work!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, it's divine intervention?

speaker: Lanike
en: What else dictates our fates? Teuta won't stop babbling about the soil. Thinks I overwork my farm. Idiot woman. As if this farm hasn't been in my family for generations.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go talk to your helots and see what they know.

speaker: Maron
en: Misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Your master claims this blight is the will of the gods. What do you think?

speaker: Maron
en: Sometimes crops fail. Could be dry soil. Could be insects. It's a shame about the donkey, he was more crucial to the farm's success than the master. Or you, for that matter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're looking for a fight, helot, you're going about it the right way.

speaker: Maron
en: Come on then! Everyone's looking for an excuse to beat a helot.

speaker: Maron
en: You've proved your worth as a Spartan. You hit hard. Something upstream is making the water taste like a rusty blade.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The water? I'll have to take a look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can I make clearing the ground easier?

speaker: Maron
en: The hoe I'm using is falling apart. I have to fix the blade every few swings. Something more sturdy would make it go faster.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not like you're shackled to this patch of land. What's preventing you from getting a new hoe?

speaker: Maron
en: Have you ever been beaten so hard you lose hearing in one of your ears? That's what happened last time I went to market without permission.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh. Of course. I'll look for one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here you go. This should make digging easier.

speaker: Maron
en: You're all right for a stranger. Look, the water's tasted like a rusty blade for the past few weeks. Last time I had water like that was when I was downriver from a blacksmith.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mauled to death? May your journey across the Styx be a more peaceful end than this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Debris might be getting stuck in this net. Maybe the dead man was a fisherman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. These don't look like the knife wounds of a man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll bet it's the metal from the armor giving the water a bad taste.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ugh, that smell is going to linger on me. At least the river runs clear now.

speaker: Teuta
en: You there. Could you help an ailing woman by getting some mint?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I heard that the crops haven't been producing this season.

speaker: Teuta
en: Lanike expects more crops every year. The soil needs to rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, there's nothing else causing crop shortage?

speaker: Teuta
en: I didn't say that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I asked you a question, helot. I don't have all day.

speaker: Teuta
en: I'm going to teach you to respect your elders, misthios.

speaker: Teuta
en: You call that a fight? You've barely winded me. I just need... to sit down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what you know.

speaker: Teuta
en: When I was a girl, the farm I lived on suffered a blight. My master burned everything. The plants, the diseased animals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Must've been quite the smell.

speaker: Teuta
en: Quite the offering to the gods... The ashes fed the soil and the next year, the stalks were higher than ever before.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope you're right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know more than you're saying.

speaker: Teuta
en: My stomach aches, and it's hard to concentrate. It's a shame that there's no mint around to chew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where would I get mint?

speaker: Teuta
en: The master keeps dried herbs up at the house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't get some mint for yourself because...?

speaker: Teuta
en: The master keeps all the medicine. I can pick and dry the herbs, but I'm not allowed any for myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go find some mint for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here you go. The herbs you needed.

speaker: Teuta
en: Fresh is better for my stomach. But since the blight, dried is all we have left. The back patch of land is riddled with blight like I've only seen once before. My old master lost his whole farm to it. I'll never forget the smell.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The back of the farm? I'll take a look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a wonder anything grows in this field with all this mess crushing the plants.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The tanners in Kephallonia use something that smells awful to make leather. It can't be good for the soil.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The earth is stained here, that can't be good for the soil. It seems like fire is the only way to be sure of ending the blight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't believe I have to tidy everything up around here. Now I'm beginning to understand Teuta's anger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The diseased crops have been burned and the river is cleared. That should be the last of the blight.

speaker: Lanike
en: Oh! You truly are gods-sent. What was the cause of the rot?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can see why your helots would anger Demeter.

speaker: Lanike
en: Yes! You see how they mistreat me and disrespect me? They don't know how good they've got it. I'm glad you were able to strike a modicum of fear and respect into them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We must all learn to fear and respect the gods. To do otherwise is to risk their wrath.

speaker: Lanike
en: Eagle Bearer! You touched my farm with your godly spiri, and the blight has left us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were so busy looking to the sky that you ignored what was in front of you! The gods are not responsible for cleaning the fields or the river. That's on you!

speaker: Lanike
en: What! You dare?! Xanthe said you were an agent of Zeus, but you are a false champion as godless as my helots. Get out from here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The poison in your fields is nothing compared to the poison in your heart.

speaker: Lanike
en: Just Ignore her. Zeus will recognize his mistake in choosing a champion soon enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The old lady...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened?

speaker: Civilian
en: Some mercenary came out of nowhere and stabbed her in the back. She stumbled back here mumbling something about how they weren't going to ruin her view...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This wine's for me. Thanks for the view, Old Lady.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The view is pretty good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't hide forever. I'm coming for you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This one's for you, Old Lady.

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: Come sail away! Find your bliss on Korfu! Boats leaving daily!

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: Care to visit paradise, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Paradise? Does the boat go to Elysium?

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: To Korfu Island! A land with no work and all play. A vacation destination.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Vacation? What's that?

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: A state of mind. Where your only responsibility is to get much-needed rest. It's a new concept.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It does sound tempting.

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: There are no clearer waters than off the coast of Korfu...

speaker: Kassandra
en: How about soldiers? Criminals? People. That's who I really need a break from.

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: If there are, they're too busy relaxing. Can I interest you in today's passage?

speaker: Kasssandra
en: It's just what I need. Vacation. For a couple of days, at least.

speaker: Cruise Barker
en: Then step aboard. Your next destination: bliss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates, it's good you're here.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Is it? Look around you. Athens is dying...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you think is going on?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I don't know. What I do know is that it kills without discrimination. Rich, poor, philosopher, or farmer—and I'm helpless to stop it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's happening to the victims?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Leaking, pustulant rashes, raging fevers, pallid, sweaty skin. I find many dying in their own excrement.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there nothing that can be done?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I try and ease the suffering where I can.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: The plague is spreading through the victims' excretions—I'm sure of it. The bodies must be burned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your compassion for the people has always inspired me.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Unfortunately compassion is all I have to give. The gods have shown me how arrogant I had become.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're only mortal, and the gods like to remind us whenever they can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if you get sick?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: It seems I am immune.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you can continue to give comfort to those who aren't.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I need help burning the bodies, Kassandra. Fanatics are roaming the streets, trying to stop me in my work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What fanatics?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: The Followers of Ares—superstitious fools. They believe burning the dead is sacrilege, and attacked me. Can you believe it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: These Followers of Ares don't worry me. I'll help burn the bodies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: May you reach Hades safely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The white bull. Am I too late?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Doesn't look like he died "willingly." I'll take his heart for the sacrifice—it'll have to do. Ugh. Not the best feeling. I hope the heart is enough. If they want the whole bull, they can come get it themselves.

speaker: Sacred Bull Heart
en: This muscular organ is used to pump blood through the mighty animal's blood vessels. Well, was used.

speaker: Priest
en: Did you find the white bull?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I couldn't bring it back alive, but I did manage to collect its heart.

speaker: Priest
en: This won't be enough to please Asklepios. The beast died unwillingly, and with just the heart, we'll only be able to pray for one life.

speaker: Farmer
en: Please, misthios. The white bull you killed was mine. My farm feeds half of Argolis. If I die, people will starve.

speaker: Wealthy woman
en: I beg you! My husband was killed by the sickness. I have two small children. Who will take care of them if I die? I am wealthy, and will pay you for this blessing.

speaker: Child
en: It's OK, give the sacrifice to them.

speaker: Priest
en: You did this. You choose whose prayers get heard by the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pray for the farmer. The bull was his, its sacrifice will help feed the people of Argolis.

speaker: Farmer
en: Thank you, misthios.

speaker: Priest
en: Very well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pray for this woman. The world has too many orphans already.

speaker: Civilian
en: Gods bless you, misthios! My children thank you.

speaker: Farmer
en: You'll pay for this!

speaker: Priest
en: It will be done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what it's like to be small and forsaken. Pray for the girl.

speaker: Farmer
en: You'll regret this!

speaker: Priest
en: Not an easy choice, misthios. But it's been made.

speaker: Priest
en: The rest is in the hands of the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did my part, priest.

speaker: Priest
en: This Spartan woman you're after...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've met her?

speaker: Priest
en: Her visit to the sanctuary is legendary, but sadly it was before my time. The man you want is Mydon the Elder Priest. He spoke of her often. That is, before he cut out his tongue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Cut out his tongue?

speaker: Priest
en: When he's not healing the sick he's in the guesthouse. Spends a lot of his time being... tended to by servants.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. I won't forget you helped me.

speaker: Priest
en: And these people won't forget you helped them.

speaker: Child
en: My parents are afraid. I'm not. One day, I'm going to become a hunter like Artemis.

speaker: Dolops
en: Go away!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Calm down. Hippokrates sent me.

speaker: Dolops
en: The great doctor is concerned for my health?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. And we need some information.

speaker: Dolops
en: Tell him someone tried to kill me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kill you? He said you worked with orphans. That's why I'm here.

speaker: Dolops
en: That was long ago. Now I'm just a farmer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And I'm a misthios. If I stop this killer, will you speak with me?

speaker: Dolops
en: I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what happened.

speaker: Dolops
en: I was on my way home when a man dressed in black attacked me. I ran as fast as I could. Once I reached safety, I thought I heard wolves. Maybe they scared him away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Dolops
en: No, thank Hera.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would someone attack you?

speaker: Dolops
en: My neighbor thinks I'm back luck. He may be right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a difference between insulting someone and attacking them. What else?

speaker: Dolops
en: I'm behind on my rent. I think my landlord wants to get rid of me and find a new tenant.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out who wants you dead.

speaker: Dolops
en: It was either my neighbor or my landlord who attacked me. But you can't punish someone unless you know they're guilty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when I've figured it out. Then we're talking about your past.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This armor is broken, but it was valuable. If it belonged to the attacker, he's either wealthy, or very lucky.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you see someone attack Dolops?

speaker: Civilian
en: Yes! It was terrible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who did it?

speaker: Civilian
en: I couldn't see clearly, but I think it was that bull-headed neighbor of his. He must have finally snapped.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks for letting me know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This knife has seen better days... like something a poor farmer would use.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This black cloth is fine enough for a king. Would do well as a mask, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for the person who attacked Dolops.

speaker: Civilian
en: I saw it happen! His face was covered, but I'm sure it was our landlord. He lives all alone, and hires soldiers to protect him. He has to be hiding something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks for letting me know.

speaker: Dolops
en: Misthios! You scared me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know who did it.

speaker: Dolops
en: What do you think? Who tried to kill me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your neighbor tried to kill you.

speaker: Dolops
en: I knew it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of him.

speaker: Dolops
en: Good luck.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I heard someone tried to kill your neighbor.

speaker: Farmer
en: Dolops? That mouse turd? Who'd give him trouble?

speaker: Kassandra
en: People say it's you.

speaker: Farmer
en: He's a fool. I like to give him a hard time—but I wouldn't try to kill him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you want me to believe you're innocent, prove it.

speaker: Farmer
en: I heard he was attacked with a knife. I only ever had one knife, and it was stolen moons ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't think you did it, but you're going to have to clear your name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By Hades! The killer must have been waiting for me to leave. I hope Dolops left some sign of his days as a priest, or this has all been for nothing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this? A letter. "Chrysis, you cannot keep taking children to the Altar of Apollo Maleatas. It is not the gods who condemn them, but you. I will take this to the authorities if you don't stop. Your son, Dolops."

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was your landlord.

speaker: Dolops
en: Of course! He wants me out of the way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of him.

speaker: Dolops
en: Be careful. He's dangerous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your landlord is dead. He was a lot more than that, though.

speaker: Dolops
en: He... was one of those people, wasn't he? I can't...

speaker: Dolops
en: Please, take this. You might find it useful.

speaker: Dolops
en: You wanted to know something?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates said you used to work with orphans.

speaker: Dolops
en: I did, but Chrysis drove me away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So she did. Where did you last see her?

speaker: Dolops
en: In the woods near the Sanctuary of Asklepios, but that was many years ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where do you think Chrysis is now?

speaker: Dolops
en: I can't be sure. But she used to pray at the Altar of Apollo Maleatas. That's where she decided which children to train and which to let die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you come to work with Chrysis?

speaker: Dolops
en: I didn't have a choice. She's my mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chrysis kept you a secret.

speaker: Dolops
en: My birth brought shame to her. I could never redeem that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What was Chrysis doing that was so terrible?

speaker: Dolops
en: She would take the children and teach them terrible things—turn them into spies and even soldiers. I couldn't take it anymore and left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At a secret meeting in Delphi, I overheard Chrysis mention a great warrior. Could these children have been part of her plan?

speaker: Dolops
en: So she did see the Oracle! Yes, Chrysis spoke of building an army with a champion at its head. It must have been for her associates... the masked ones.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've done your duty to Hera. I'll deal with Chrysis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So Chrysis is the key to finding my mater. I must find this Altar of Apollo Maleatas.

speaker: Nikaia
en: If it isn't the new Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trust me. I'm a lot better than the last one.

speaker: Nikaia
en: Look, you want to be useful, new Eagle Bearer? Get back the stallion the other one of you lost to the pirates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can get your stallion back, but we're going to need a lot more than one horse.

speaker: Nikaia
en: What for?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The pirates are coming, and at least with mounts, the villagers have a fighting chance.

speaker: Nikaia
en: Sure enough, but I bred this one just for Megakles himself. Without his stallion, he isn't riding into battle. You've ever seen a general strutting into battle?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not a good one.

speaker: Nikaia
en: Exactly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where did the stallion go?

speaker: Nikaia
en: That other Eagle Bearer rode him east past the Salts. Came back and said some bandits stole him in the night. Imagine that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to find this other Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Nikaia
en: Wouldn't mind giving him a piece of my mind, too. If you find him, punch his bird right in the beak for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: His eagle?

speaker: Nikaia
en: Ha! It was barely a chicken.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get back Megakles's stallion, then you and I are going to talk about getting horses for everyone in Alponos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK. Hopefully this goes better than last time.

speaker: Nikaia
en: Princess Purple Pie. You're back safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here you go. When the real Eagle Bearer says she's going to do something, she does it.

speaker: Nikaia
en: There, there, Princess Purple Pie. Eat up. Let it flow through you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Nikaia
en: The first of you Eagle Bearers rode east to find this fruit. Said any horse that eats it turns into Pegasos. Leave it to the gods to hide it in plain sight!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The "Eagle Bearer" obviously lied to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why not take a bite yourself? Maybe it'll turn you into a Pegasos, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard of magic fruit left by Dionysos, but it just gets you drunk.

speaker: Nikaia
en: Don't believe me? For how much I paid, this fruit has to be real. Here, watch this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait!

speaker: Nikaia
en: Fly, Pegasos! Fly!

speaker: Kassandra
en: These people are cursed. / This has been a long, long day.

speaker: Barnabas
en: There! See that island. That is where I saw the Beast

speaker: Barnabas
en: The war has changed the face of the Greek world. If it's not Spartans or Athenians, it's bandits and pirates. Gods protect us all from mankind.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The Athenians have blocked the entrance to the bay!

speaker: Barnabas
en: You did it. We're through! From what I've heard, Megaris is home to the fiercest fighting so far. The Spartans are preparing for a final push to rid the region of Athenians.

speaker: Stentor
en: The Wolf takes no prisoners!

speaker: Nikolaos
en: See how the Athenian dog Perikles fears you! He cowers in his Parthenon, surrounded by playwrights and sophists. He dares not face you with honor on the battlefield. He knows you are too strong. He knows Athens' days in Megaris are numbered. And he knows Athens is next!

speaker: Stentor
en: You. You destroyed the Athenian blockade?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They were in my way.

speaker: Stentor
en: Sparta owes you thanks. Tyche has blessed you, my friend. You arrived in time to watch my pater achieve a glorious victory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Nikolaos is your father, I guess that makes you my brother.

speaker: Stentor
en: Did you take a blow to the head during battle? What are you talking about?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Wolf is my father as well as yours.

speaker: Stentor
en: Ridiculous! Before he adopted me into his home he had two children, and they both died in Sparta many years ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Except for the one standing before you now.

speaker: Stentor
en: You almost fooled me, but I wasn't born yesterday, misthios. Let's stick to the subject of why you're here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't be his son. I heard his children died in Sparta many years ago.

speaker: Stentor
en: He adopted me into his household after his previous family failed him. I would never bring dishonor to him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sometimes things happen in a way that you don't plan or expect. History has a way of remembering things strangely.

speaker: Stentor
en: You talk as if you were there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe I was.

speaker: Stentor
en: Nonsense. You're too young to have witnessed such things. But enough of the past, let's discuss the future.

speaker: Stentor
en: What is a mercenary doing sailing into a war they aren't being paid to fight in? Tell me why you're really here before I cut you down for wasting my time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was just passing through and smelled opportunity on the breeze.

speaker: Stentor
en: The only thing I smell is lies. You're a sell-sword. The only thing you're here for is to try and kill the Wolf like all the rest. Maybe you should have kept sailing past.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw fellow Spartans in trouble and thought you could use the help of a well-armed mercenary.

speaker: Stentor
en: We are Spartans. We do not need anything from the likes of you, but my father taught me to use every resource at my disposal. I could make use of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come to meet the Wolf of Sparta.

speaker: Stentor
en: You cannot simply meet with Nikolaos. He has command of the entire Spartan army. If you truly came all this way to meet him, you might be disappointed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you sure you're in charge here? You don't strike me as a typical Spartan. Perhaps it's best I just talk with Nikolaos.

speaker: Stentor
en: A sense of humor is not a trait I see being useful for a sell-sword. If you're here to earn drachmae though, I could make use of a capable mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's my honor to serve Sparta. I've come to pledge my sword to the Wolf of Sparta.

speaker: Stentor
en: If you wish to pledge your services to my pater, you can do so by helping me.

speaker: Stentor
en: The fleet might be destroyed, but Megaris is firmly in Athenian control. We need to weaken their position if we are to take to the field and drive them back to Athens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your father. Who is he exactly?

speaker: Stentor
en: Nikolaos, the Wolf of Sparta. He was impressed with my skill when I was a boy and took me under his wing. He trained me himself and eventually adopted me into his house. He is my father and mentor. I live to make him proud. Surely you've heard of him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just rumors really.

speaker: Stentor
en: I doubt they do him justice. He is a great warrior and a greater general. I'd follow him to the gates of the underworld.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How goes the war effort?

speaker: Stentor
en: The Athenian blockade was a desperate attempt to stop our advance through Megaris. Now, we can prepare to drive them from this region once and for all. Our forward scouts are identifying key targets in preparation for our assault. Under the Wolf's command, we shall be victorious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you need a mercenary to do that? You seem to have plenty of soldiers at your disposal.

speaker: Stentor
en: It's not a question of manpower. The Megarians are our allies. We do not want to commit troops until we know victory is assured. My scouts are already locating key targets that we can hit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready to serve. Together we will ensure that Sparta is victorious.

speaker: Stentor
en: You're a different kind of misthios, aren't you? You're just what we need to help deal with that meddling Athenian mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
