en: I'll help you rid Megaris for a price.

speaker: Stentor
en: Typical of your type. No honor or sense of duty, but your skills are better serving us than our enemy. The Athenians already have a mercenary working for them, they don't need more help.

speaker: Stentor
en: If we can draw the leader out and eliminate him, we will crush the Athenians on the battlefield and drive their forces all the way back to Athens. Destroying their supplies, stealing their war chest, and killing their elite troops should leave him vulnerable.

speaker: Stentor
en: Take this and present it to my scouts. If you find them in the field be sure to check for new information. They might also have need of your skills.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is the Athenian leader?

speaker: Stentor
en: He is in Megaris, hiding behind stone walls and a full garrison of troops. But if you kill his troops, destroy his supplies, and steal his riches, then he'll be open to attack.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What supplies should I destroy?

speaker: Stentor
en: Anything the Athenians need. Look for crates of supplies, and weapons. The Port of Nisaia in the Valley of King Lelex would be a good place to start. It's where their supplies come into the region.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This chest you want me to steal, why is it so important?

speaker: Stentor
en: An army is made of men that need paying. Take away their drachmae and they lose all the will to die for other men's ambitions. The Athenians keep their treasure well guarded in the fort at the foot of Mount Geraneia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I know what must be done.

speaker: Stentor
en: Remember, every Athenian soldier you eliminate will also help us achieve victory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And once I've brought the Athenians to their knees for Sparta, I'll get that meeting with Nikolaos. Or you'll be next.

speaker: Stentor
en: Send those Athenian dogs to Hades, misthios. Do this and the Wolf will personally see to it that you are rewarded.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I want to get closer to the Wolf, I'll have to help Stentor defeat the Athenians. I shouldn't waste any time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The size of it... That's no ordinary wolf! There it is!

speaker: Persephone
en: What do you think about my southern realm? I don't come here much anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's lovely.

speaker: Persephone
en: I try to offer a comfortable home to the glorious dead. It helps them accept their fate and keeps them from wandering too far. So when a human wanders and doesn't return, I can't help but take it personally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What am I doing here?

speaker: Persephone
en: When Leonidas was alive, he brought chaos and bloodshed. Hermes spotted him mingling with delinquents recently. We can't have him falling into old habits. If he won't fight with me, then he won't fight at all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermes is exaggerating. When I heard Leonidas was in Elysium, I went to see him. He's found peace here—he's no threat to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Isn't everyone in Elysium already dead?

speaker: Persephone
en: Elysium is a gift for the worthy. The unworthy experience a second death and are sent to Tartaros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leonidas doesn't deserve that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leonidas of Sparta is my grandfather. If you think I'm going to stick a blade in him, you're wrong.

speaker: Persephone
en: Hermes told me why you're really in Elysium. That Staff of yours. Cross me and you'll fail.

speaker: Persephone
en: But Leonidas means a lot to you. I understand this will be difficult. Which is why I'm willing to make you a deal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of deal?

speaker: Persephone
en: Bring me the body of Leonidas, and I will bring back a departed beloved of your choosing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can do that?

speaker: Persephone
en: I'm queen of the dead darling, I can do anything. So, who does Kassandra want back in her life?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would see Nikolaos again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to see Phoibe again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas deserves to live.

speaker: Persephone
en: Help me protect Elysium from chaos, and you'll see your loved one again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even in paradise, people want my family dead. Is killing my grandfather worth bringing someone back to life?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you doing out here?

speaker: Leonidas
en: There is something I wanted to ask you. Will you fish with me?

speaker: Leonidas
en: This is nice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are so many things I want to talk about.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Talk, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After everything you lost at Thermopylai, your men, your wife, your children, Sparta... in the end, was it worth it?

speaker: Leonidas
en: Who rules the Greek world right now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Greeks.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Then my answer is yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater told me of our bloodline and our ancestors. Did you know?

speaker: Leonidas
en: Only what my mater told me. We were born from greatness and we were destined for greatness. The world was divided in two, those who wanted us dead, and those who would follow us to the gates of Hades.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I imagine the spear was in one piece when it was given to you.

speaker: Leonidas
en: My mater handed it to me when I was a boy. Said it came with a certain burden but

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's so peaceful here.

speaker: Leonidas
en: I think I got a bite. Get a basket—quickly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, grandfather.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Forgive me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There, I delivered. Your turn.

speaker: Persephone
en: Thank you. Yes, a promise is a promise. I'll bring back your beloved dead. But I'll need your patience—these things take time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Grandfather, I

speaker: Leonidas
en: You're here to kill me.

speaker: Leonidas
en: In Sparta we were trained to spot predators long before they pounced.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need Persephone's approval, but she sees you as a threat. If I don't take care of that threat...

speaker: Leonidas
en: Why not bring her the head of a greater threat?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's a greater threat than you? Actually, there is someone. A spy. I delivered him to Persephone as a bodyguard, but he's working against her from the inside.

speaker: Leonidas
en: I am only a threat to her soldiers on the battlefield. A spy threatens the heart of Elysium. Bring her his corpse, and she should be satisfied.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, grandfather. We should go fishing more often.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Persephone won't like this. Maybe if I bring Kyros alive, she can deal with the traitor herself.

speaker: Kyros
en: What are you doing? We're family!

speaker: Persephone
en: Kyros of Zarax? This isn't who I asked for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's a spy working for the rebellion.

speaker: Persephone
en: But you're the one who first brought him to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't know his intentions.

speaker: Persephone
en: I trusted you. Guards.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Persephone, listen to me. Hermes is right, trouble's brewing in Elysium. Even though Leonidas is against you, you're much stronger than he is. But Kyros was an enemy you couldn't see. That made him far more dangerous to you and Elysium.

speaker: Persephone
en: But he's still breathing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Death is a gift traitors don't deserve. I thought you'd want to deal with him yourself.

speaker: Persephone
en: Defying me comes at a cost. Our deal is off. But for bringing me this vile deceiver, you may stay. Figure out that mysterious little Staff of yours.

speaker: Eppie
en: By Zeus... I would have been a goner there if it wasn't for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lucky I came by.

speaker: Eppie
en: Pleased to make your acquaintance. I'm Eppie. Well, Epizelos, but my friends call me Eppie. Not that I have "friends," necessarily.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm Kassandra.

speaker: Eppie
en: Charmed! You have the look of someone used to being out in the world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have the look of someone who, um... spends lots of time reading.

speaker: Eppie
en: I don't look like much, it's true. But when discovery knocks, what other choice is there?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look like you shouldn't be outside on your own. At all.

speaker: Eppie
en: It can't be helped. I've been overcome with adventure.

speaker: Eppie
en: I have in my possession a Mycenaean tablet that leads to a sacred burial site. I'm calling it the Cave of the Oracle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good for you.

speaker: Eppie
en: Mycenaeans were known for their elaborate grave sites full of precious things.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How precious?

speaker: Eppie
en: Ancient jewelry, ceremonial swords and daggers. So, very precious. If you escort me, I'll show you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can I turn down the promise of precious things?

speaker: Eppie
en: The Fates have delivered you onto my path, and thus we travel together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Fates have been known to have a sense of humor.

speaker: Eppie
en: Happening upon you, hero, is fortuitous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Glad to hear it. So you dig through book roll?

speaker: Eppie
en: No! Well, yes and no. I dig through dirt, too. I uncover our history. Sometimes... hopefully this time, it will uncover ancient wonders!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hate to break it to you, but clay pots and dirt aren't that wondrous to most.

speaker: Eppie
en: I've dedicated my life to it. It's so much more than treasure to be looted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is it though?

speaker: Eppie
en: It's who we are! knowing where we come from tell us where we are headed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You educated people and your riddles.

speaker: Eppie
en: Some people don't care about the past. They only want to steal something that will make them a few drachmae. Imagine that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hard to believe.

speaker: Eppie
en: My peers are no more than treasure hunters and art dealers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well. You did mention precious jewels.

speaker: Eppie
en: These ruins and relics are notoriously hard to find. I found this one through clever searching and deduction.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more about it.

speaker: Eppie
en: Mycenaeans held specific rituals. Some tales speak of objects made by the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. The gods like to play their hand on occasion.

speaker: Eppie
en: Think of this, misthios! How would you like to have had the gods help you in battle?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A good warrior doesn't need any help from the gods or anyone else.

speaker: Eppie
en: True. True. But think of what we might find there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You think we'll find something with this power?

speaker: Eppie
en: See? Now are you interested?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I certain am.

speaker: Eppie
en: What's this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay back.

speaker: Eppie
en: They seem drawn to this place. I hadn't expected that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Does it have to do with—whatever that name was you said?

speaker: Eppie
en: The Mycenaeans? I don't see how they could know. It must be related to Trophonios. I'll observe them and see what I can learn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. I'll search further inside.

speaker: Eppie
en: Wait! Take this stele piece. See if there are markings that match it.

speaker: Mycenaean Stele Piece
en: The carefully engraved stele once held a position of prominence within the ancient tomb. How it had come to be scattered across the lands would remain a mystery, but it was Eppie's duty to restore it and thus breathe life into the past.

speaker: Eppie
en: The worshippers puzzle me. They murmer something... ... I can't make it out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not much of a burial site. Mules are buried in higher places of honor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The stele piece looks like it can be placed...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is... unexpected.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is more elaborate than I thought.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah, this is more like it. Let's see what we have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. This statue depicts a warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The markings match Eppie's stone!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eppie will want to see all of this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're in the right place. Unfortunately, my friend, it's been looted. All I found was this armor.

speaker: Eppie
en: That is highly significant. The Mycenaeans were a warrior culture, you know. So this must be a warrior's tomb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh. Well, it's a decent piece. But where's the rest of it?

speaker: Eppie
en: Hmm... That was only one part of the stele. If we find the others, I can decipher the text.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe that will reveal more armor. The rest of the stele you speak of could be anywhere.

speaker: Eppie
en: If I can find clues for where to look, are you interested in finding the other stele pieces?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll look for the others.

speaker: Eppie
en: Excellent! Now I need to see those markings. Let's go inside.

speaker: Eppie
en: I didn't expect the stele keystone to actually be a key.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wonder what happens when all of them are in place.

speaker: Eppie
en: Even with only part of the stele, I can start to decipher the writing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does it say?

speaker: Eppie
en: Um... I think that says, "of the gods."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Really? To think, you were someone yelling for help not long ago.

speaker: Eppie
en: Look at me now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think you're going to need all of them, though.

speaker: Eppie
en: According to this, it seems that the stele pieces have been deliberately seperated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wonder why they were seperated on purpose.

speaker: Eppie
en: It doesn't matter if we can find them. Will you look for the other stele pieces?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. Where should I look?

speaker: Eppie
en: According to this, the next stele is... Oh, better you than me! I can't swim. Explore the Ruins of Arne.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's the connection between this tomb and those worshippers?

speaker: Eppie
en: The writing mentions "of the gods." It's not clear which gods, though. Once we decipher more, we should understand the connection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The armor must belong to the ancient warrior. But why remove it and spread it out across the lands?

speaker: Eppie
en: Good question. It must have something to do with the text.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So these markings are an ancient language?

speaker: Eppie
en: Mycenaean. There are languages even older than that, which have been lost. When this died out, sadly, we fell into a .

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait. I found one already. It caught my eye.

speaker: Eppie
en: By Zeus, you're a natural at this. Did it also come with armor?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Part of it.

speaker: Eppie
en: There must be a piece of armor with each missing stele.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But why?

speaker: Eppie
en: This section here refers to a ritual.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't explain why the armor was separated and hidden with a stele piece.

speaker: Eppie
en: Maybe that was part of the ritual? We need to find the other stele pieces. Are you ready?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time for me to go.

speaker: Phaidon
en: So now they have people watch us get punished? That's a different kind of shame.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not here to watch—I just saw you by chance.

speaker: Phaidon
en: What you saw was a man who paid his master for his freedom, but is being kept a slave.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can do that?

speaker: Phaidon
en: My master gave me a price for my freedom, and I saved until I had enough. Now that I've given him the drachmae, he pretends as if the deal never existed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That isn't right. Let me talk to him for you.

speaker: Phaidon
en: Really? You'd do that? My name is Phaidon. I don't know who you are, but surely you were sent by the gods—they must have heard my prayers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They did, and you deserve their help.

speaker: Phaidon
en: I can sense something in you—you're special.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I like to think so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're waiting on help from the gods, I can leave.

speaker: Phaidon
en: No, please don't. Someone or something brought you here to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. My legs did.

speaker: Phaidon
en: Gods or not, I'm grateful. My master should be near the silver mine—he's likely overseeing other slaves like myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you always been a slave?

speaker: Phaidon
en: Since my youth. I was in the wrong place and born to the wrong family. I've been sold more than once.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you just now got enough to buy your freedom?

speaker: Phaidon
en: More like I found a master who was willing to give me that sort of deal. I should have known he'd lie. It was my only hope, and now it's gone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you often get whipped like that?

speaker: Phaidon
en: More than you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you do?

speaker: Phaidon
en: I don't always know. Not working fast enough, looking at someone wrong, asking for water... Sometimes they do it just for fun. I'm not sure how much more I can take.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll talk to your master and make sure he listens.

speaker: Phaidon
en: He's not really the listening type.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He will be with me.

speaker: The Master
en: You look strong. I could always use more people to keep the slaves in line, if you're looking for work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm already working. I'm here about one of your slaves, Phaidon.

speaker: The Master
en: As if I know their names. You're wasting my time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me a moment to explain.

speaker: The Master
en: That's close enough to begging for me. Fine, speak.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a man who paid you for his freedom. He'd like you to follow through on that promise.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shouldn't even be here. You're the one wasting my time.

speaker: The Master
en: Ha, nobody has spoken to me like that in quite a while. Spit it out while you're still entertaining.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phaidon paid you for his freedom. Give it to him.

speaker: The Master
en: Hmm, doesn't sound familiar. But I'm feeling generous. Do something for me, and I'll give this Phaidon his freedom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it?

speaker: The Master
en: There's a woman I'd like you to kill. It'll leave her family to fend for themselves... but the Cult of Kosmos needs it done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a member of the Cult? If that's true, then you know who I am.

speaker: The Master
en: You're smarter than they make you out to be, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me why I shouldn't just kill you now?

speaker: The Master
en: You could. Of course if I'm killed, the slave stays that way... and I'm the only one who knows where his papers are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why does this woman need to die?

speaker: The Master
en: Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't realize you needed to know that. Wait... you don't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phaidon said you already broke your promise once. This better not be another of those times.

speaker: The Master
en: Look around. I have plenty of slaves. In exchange for the woman's death, I can let one go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Most people prefer to keep their Cult status a secret.

speaker: The Master
en: You can't do a thing about it if you want to help... whatever his name is. Also, it adds a bit more fun to the situation, don't you think?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be on my way.

speaker: The Master
en: Kill the woman or not—it's your choice. But if you want your slave friend to go free, it's the only way.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Kassandra! What chance that we should meet here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't really feel like chance...

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, so you wish for today's topic to be about fate?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, not really.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Good, because I had another in mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do I have to leave Attika to be rid of you? It feels like you're everywhere I go.

speaker: Sokrates
en: It is very strange. But to answer your question, yes, leaving Attika would help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Attika is large, yet fate keeps bringing us together.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, you're trying to bring us back to fate once again. I won't let you avoid answering my questions, though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So how much did you overhear?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Oh, all of it. You have a difficult choice to make, clearly. How much is the freedom of one person worth? Do you believe one life is worth more than another?

speaker: Kassandra
en: People aren't equal, even if we wish it were true.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So you would say, for example, that your life is worth more than another's? Then would you also say that there are some who are more worthy of life than yourself?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I wouldn't say someone else is more worthy of life than I am.

speaker: Sokrates
en: But to say that contradicts your point. Unless, of course, you believe yourself to be the most worthy of life out of all who currently live?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not that naïve. There are many who likely deserve life more than me.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So you would admit that a life's worthiness is dependent on a person's actions and what they have done or can do for the world?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no difference between one person and another. We all take our first breath the same way.

speaker: Sokrates
en: But are the breaths you take equal to my own? Would you not say the breath of Perikles is put to better use than that of someone in prison?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't matter which two people you compare, the answer is the same.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So a thief is equal to a priest... A politician to a child. An interesting view.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course Perikles can do more than someone like a thief.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then perhaps people aren't equal after all. Your changed mind makes it clear how difficult a question this is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I've said enough.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, you're right. I know you are busy, and your mind is weary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That does sound like me.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Go now. It has been an honor having these conversations with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You too, Sokrates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I kill her, Phaidon goes free... But that means Odessa dies, and I help the Cult...

speaker: The Master
en: What is it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I killed the woman.

speaker: The Master
en: Wonderful! I don't know why this slave is so special to you... Perhaps you wish to keep him as your own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's free, then?

speaker: The Master
en: Yes, yes, he's free. You purchased him with the life of another. A fair trade. Now leave before I changed my mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not going to kill someone so you'll free Phaidon when he should have been already.

speaker: The Master
en: Fine. I'll find someone else to kill her and Phaidon will remain my slave. I'll be sure he receives a grand reward for wasting so much of my time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The "Wings of Hermes"... could this be it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka! That was fast.

speaker: Adonis
en: Hermes, how many times do I have to tell you? I'm not going to the palace.

speaker: Hermes
en: Persephone isn't asking. She's demanding your presence.

speaker: Adonis
en: You know I want out of Elysium. If you help me escape, I promise you'll never see me again.

speaker: Hermes
en: As happy as that would make me, Persephone wants you to stay.

speaker: Adonis
en: How long until you realize you're just one of her pets?

speaker: Hermes
en: Watch yourself, human.

speaker: Adonis
en: Careful, or Persephone will have you neutered. Oh, I forgot. She did that ages ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't think the dead could feel pain.

speaker: Adonis
en: I'm one of the few miserable fools around here who's actually alive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're so miserable, why not just leave?

speaker: Adonis
en: I've tried. If Persephone wants you to stay, dead or alive, you stay. Hades taught her well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can you stand it? The dead really don't want us here.

speaker: Adonis
en: I can't stand it. I'm doing everything I can to escape Elysium, but Persephone's little spies are everywhere. Hades taught her well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're the troublemaker I've been hearing so much about.

speaker: Adonis
en: Adonis, at your service. With an army at Persephone's disposal and most of Elysium under her control, my troublemaking days are coming to an end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I helped you?

speaker: Adonis
en: And why would someone with their whole life ahead of them want to do that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hear Persephone has everyone in Elysium on a leash. I want to cut them free.

speaker: Adonis
en: Of all the lies in the underworld, that's the best one I've heard yet. No one cares about the dead. Try again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to find Hades' realm. If overthrowing Persephone is the key to escaping Elysium, then I'm in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to find Hades' realm. If overthrowing Persephone is the key to escaping Elysium, then I'm in.

speaker: Adonis
en: Why didn't you just say so from the beginning?

speaker: Adonis
en: Did you hear that, my love? She wants to enter Hades's realm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to find it with or without your help. We might as well work together.

speaker: Adonis
en: Tell you what, southwest from here is the Fortress of the Three Sisters. One of Persephone's strongholds. If you kill her Overseer, destroy her Torches of Hypnos, and steal Persephone's resources—all while avoiding the attention of her Kolossi—then maybe I'll trust you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about the Overseers.

speaker: Adonis
en: Persephone's most trusted and deadly servants. They are the eyes and ears of Elysium. Killing them will leave the queen blind and deaf.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Torches of Hypnos?"

speaker: Adonis
en: Constructed by the god of slumber, these devices keep human minds under Persephone's control... Destroy their centers to extinguish their flames.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't like the sound of... Kolossi.

speaker: Adonis
en: The Kolossi are best left asleep. They protect the Overseers. Bloodshed wakes them, and they do not like being woken.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're the troublemaker, why do I feel like I'll be causing all the trouble?

speaker: Adonis
en: What can I say. I'm a lover, not a fighter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Luckily for you, I'm both.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I told you I already cleared that fortress?

speaker: Adonis
en: Impressive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trust me now?

speaker: Adonis
en: You've brought me one step closer to my love. It's a good start.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is this "love" you keep mentioning?

speaker: Adonis
en: The most beautiful being in existence. With a face so fair, to gaze upon it is to forget all others. Perhaps you've heard of her—Aphrodite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, Aphro who?

speaker: Adonis
en: Very funny. The last person who provoked her wrath was turned into a field pig.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't take you for a poet.

speaker: Adonis
en: She brings it out in me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I bet you I could inspire a verse or two.

speaker: Adonis
en: You sound like Persephone. Always trying to make me forget Aphrodite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do whatever I can to get you back to her. You have my word.

speaker: Adonis
en: You've given me something I haven't had in a while. Hope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, what's next?

speaker: Adonis
en: Not here. Come find my camp in Iapetos' Ruins.

speaker: Adonis
en: Before you go. Persephone has Overseers and Torches of Hypnos across Elysium. If we're going to weaken her influence, we must destroy them. And we're going to need all the help we can get.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's about time I go meet the infamous Persephone.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Eagle Bearer. What did I do to offend you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing. I just want to know if you saw what happened to the girl, Myrto?

speaker: Heriphile
en: I saw the girl steal a taste of food for your feast. And she fell ill.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She tasted it?

speaker: Heriphile
en: Yes! I'm sorry! Please don't punish me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? No, of course not.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Please, I told you all I knew about the girl stealing a bite of your feast!

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Oh! Eagle Bearer! Do not curse me with your anger!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Why would I curse you?

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Your anger is well-storied! We seek only to please you, unlike that disrespectful waif, Myrto.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did Myrto do?

speaker: Chalkippe
en: I couldn't say! I only know that Hexione called Myrto a wrongdoer and said you had punished her for her transgressions as a warning to us all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That is ridiculous! I need to find Hexione.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Your greatness, we will all try to do better! So you will not visit your wrath upon us as you did upon Myrto.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Grayhair, where can I find the Priestess Hexione? You must know.

speaker: Hevmonos
en: The priestess and her sisters have a secluded retreat. None know where it is, for it is hidden from common eyes. I cannot say more for risk of offending them, or you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those women do not speak for me. Tell me now or I'll get angry...

speaker: Hevmonos
en: Yes! Yes! They appear from and retreat to a secret den, past the border to Elis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to have words.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hexione! Why did you flee from the village?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: I left to consult with my sisters. We needed to understand why the poor girl was struck down.

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: Did Linou offend the divine Eagle Bearer somehow?

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: Or are we being tested by greater powers of Olympos?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Are the gods testing our faith... or yours?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do not speak in riddles! Tell me what you mean, or face my anger.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Wrathful Eagle Bearer, we want only what you want!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to know what happened to Myrto and how to help her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't want to play games. Please, tell me what you know so I can save Myrto.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Of course, beloved Eagle Bearer. We want the same.

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: We prayed for an answer, and it was delivered!

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: In the sacred cave there is a plant that can save her. But it is too dangerous for us mere mortals to descend into.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go get it.

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: Brave Eagle Bearer, your path leads you to the sacred cave.

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: Fierce Eagle Bearer, the answers you seek are there!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Divine Eagle Bearer, find the truth!

speaker: Kassandra
en: By Zeus, that's a beast!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The priestesses expect me to become bear shit? Malákes. First the bear, then the plant.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I get the feeling the priestesses were hoping for a martyred god and not a pissed off misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Got it... wait, this plant is nothing but pig feed! It won't do anything! Maláka!

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: I told you we should have focused our prayers around a foreign spirit!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Sew your mouths shut, the two of you! As soon as the divine bear eats the Eagle Bearer's heart, we'll have nothing to worry about!

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: I haven't heard anything from below for awhile now...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hexione! I killed your bear.

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: You're here!

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: You're alive!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Very much so. And angry. You better have an antidote for poor Myrto, or else...

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Or what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You used my name to try to control the village, and when I arrived you poisoned Myrto and then tried to have me eaten by a bear.

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: No! Never!

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: Yes! It's all true!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Shut your mouth, you insipid...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me the antidote, Hexione, before I turn you all into slugs and bury you in salt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Now, return the wealth you've stolen to the village or I'll make you wish you'd pissed off Hera instead of me.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: No! Eagle Bearer! As you command!

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: At once!

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: We obey!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go. Do. It!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shut your lying, filthy mouths! You poisoned Myrto to try to hurt me, and then when I found you, you tried to feed me to a cursed bear!

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: Yes!

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: No!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: We didn't mean it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Didn't mean it?! You lying malákes, you've got Linou wrapped around your fingers and you're living fat off the villagers in my name!

speaker: Priestess Xenokleia
en: It's true!

speaker: Priestess Thelxiope
en: So true, your divinity!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not a god, you thieving swine! Give me the antidote for Myrto or I'll split your heads open!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now, begone!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have the medicine for Myrto. Quick, let's give it to her.

speaker: Myrto
en: Kassandra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shh. Rest.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: You did it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was close.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: You need to talk to the villagers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen and obey me. I want glory for you!

speaker: Menalkas
en: Don't listen to her. She ruined my crops and made Myrto sick. She's just as bad as the priestesses. She's no real god!

speaker: Hevmonos
en: Get out of here, misthios!

speaker: Akatos
en: I cannot thank you enough for saving my daughter, but it may be best if you left?

speaker: Kallistratos
en: Tear the statue down to rubble. We don't want chicken-killers like you here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look inside yourselves. You'll know that I'm no god and you can live for yourselves.

speaker: Akatos
en: Mabe you're right. Still, you saved my daughter. I'll never forget that.

speaker: Menalkas
en: Thank you, Eagle Bearer, for giving us the courage to stand on our own!

speaker: Polykleitos
en: When I eventually finish your statue, it will be a reminder to the village of your message, and a guide for them to do for themselves.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: You showed immense strength of character in helping the people of Linou and not taking the easy route with them, Kassandra. I hope to capture something of your nobility in the final form, however long it takes.

speaker: Myrto
en: It is good to know that we can choose our own paths, no matter what the gods want. I hope to be as brave as you when I get older.

speaker: Menalkas
en: I pray to Demeter regularly, and she constantly speaks to me in my dreams, telling me how happy she is now.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Eagle Bearer! You found me! I have done all you commanded and never returned to Linou. In truth, I have rededicated myself to the gods and try to live a life you would be pleased with.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My spear... what happened? It's like it's asleep. Dead. This can't be right. My spear's never felt like this. Where did Herodotos go? And what happened to Barnabas?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper... do you hear me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aletheia? Is that you?

speaker: Aletheia
en: We need to talk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas! How did you find us?

speaker: Barnabas
en: It's a little morbid, but I followed the trail of bodies and it brought me here. I tried to follow the pirates who took Herodotos, but I couldn't quite keep up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you both all right?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Never mind that! Did you see that star shoot across the island? A sign from the gods, no doubt!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Not a star, Barnabas, an artifact. The letter spoke of a gold object among the treasure - so powerful it turns men into their darkest fears.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or into monsters. Literally and metaphorically. I've fought them myself.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Surely you're joking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've dealt with these artifacts before. They're as dangerous as the letter said.

speaker: Barnabas
en: What mythical power! Who knows what this one's capable of?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It breaks spears, for one thing.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Are you sure? It looks like the same spear of Leonidas to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trust me. Something's... off.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I'm sure it's fine - allow me to fix it! I know ships aren't spears, but sea captains are good handy men.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't know anything about spears, let alone this spear. It's... special.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I meant no harm by it. I-I just feel it is, you know... my fault.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I appreciate the thought, but I know my spear. It's nothing like a ship.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I can't help but feel like this whole mess is my fault.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't. I'll go see what can be done, and I'll find you two later.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Good. Why don't we go see those waterfalls you were telling me about, Barnabas?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah, yes! I have not yet paid my respects to Asopos. He's god of the river here and won't be pleased with all our hubbub.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay safe - no more pirates!

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where do I go?

speaker: Aletheia
en: The Tomb of Phaiax, hidden in ruins. Come alone. Go west to the waterfalls. Go to the north. We'll meet there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: North.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the place Aletheia mentioned. Now to find a way in. With my spear broken, I'd better be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eugh. The Followers of Ares did this. Ruthless.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ugh, snakes. Better watch out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This far, and still not hidden enough? Who knows how deep this tomb goes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are there so many snakes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aletheia?

speaker: Aletheia
en: You found me, Keeper.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why all the secrecy?

speaker: Aletheia
en: A precaution. Mortal eyes can't see what I have to show you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, before you do...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know what happened. I went to take an artifact like I've done before and... can you fix it?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Unfortunately, I cannot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There must be a way. My grandfather's spear

speaker: Aletheia
en: is most likely useless. The spear of Leonidas was overwhelmed by the Isu energies it held. Some force in the artifact must have pushed it to its limits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So it's gone. After all it's done for me.

speaker: Aletheia
en: I'm afraid so. But your powers are not limited to the spear. Your oath as Keeper of the Staff makes your destiny much more complex. Let me show you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What... am I looking at exactly?

speaker: Aletheia
en: The world. The planet, Earth, where you live. And on it are all its people: good and bad. Innocent and knowing. Peaceful and violent. These are the places where you will find the world's Isu artifacts. They lie hidden, for now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more of them? Who put them there?

speaker: Aletheia
en: They aren't there without reason, but we aren't always wise to the why and who. They serve a mysterious purpose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you saying?

speaker: Aletheia
en: There is a task that lies ahead for the Keeper of the Staff if you are willing to take it. A task that will take the rest of your immortal life.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Undisturbed, the artifacts are no threat. But if found by the wrong kind, human life may be destroyed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, my spear has no power, and I have to leave the world I know to find more of the things that took it away? Things that turn people to monsters?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Yes. To stop more monsters from existing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're asking for way too much. Do you know how tired I am? Every day exhausts me. Show me no more.

speaker: Aletheia
en: I only show you to prepare you for a potential destiny. You know what can happen if the artifacts find their way to mortal hands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're asking me to leave my home. To leave everyone I love.

speaker: Aletheia
en: It is a sorry fact, but that will happen no matter what you do. They're mortal. One day, they will die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look, I came to you to have my spear fixed. If you can't do that, then I'm leaving.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You know their power, Keeper. Their potential. Humanity does not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't ask for this! Maybe I don't want to live forever! Don't I get a say in my own fate? Forget you. And forget the artifacts. I'm leaving.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Consider what I've said.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So my spear is broken, and I'm being asked to find countless artifacts around the world. Forever. Happy vacation, Kassandra. This is... too much.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How could I ever explain this to Herodotos and Barnabas? They'd never understand. What to say when I find them...

speaker: Herodotos
en: Kassandra! We have a problem.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's Barnabas?

speaker: Herodotos
en: He took off alone - to find the object that broke your spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Has he gone mad?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I tried to explain to him it would be fruitless, but he wouldn't listen. He thought finding it was the answer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should have stopped him! Do you understand what that thing can do?

speaker: Herodotos
en: He wanted to help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So he does that instead of staying out of trouble? I have to find it before Barnabas does. Maláka!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a message on the board. What's the matter?

speaker: Woman
en: My play was a disaster, misthios! The actor was drunk, the malákas! He ruined it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did he do?

speaker: Woman
en: What didn't he do? Stumbling around, slurring the lines he didn't forget - he even spewed vomit on the front row! I was a fool to think an idiot goatherd could be an actor, but I'll have my revenge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And let me guess, you want me to kill him.

speaker: Woman
en: His blood must be spilled.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You'll find Phoenix in the villa at the center of town. All the city's business is conducted there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then that's my next stop.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Have you thought about what you'll say to her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have questions about my past. My mater has answers she kept from me that I need.

speaker: Aspasia
en: About your family?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are secrets... Someone important told me she would be able to help me understand.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You should be cautious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Aspasia
en: Think about your questions carefully. What we know about our past can shape our future.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... haven't really thought about it.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Well, I'm sure you'll have plenty to talk about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, we do.

speaker: Aspasia
en: We'll reach Naxos soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've had quite the adventure.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Yes, although I don't think it's over yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where will you go?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I have some business to attend to before moving on, and I have friends in the city I need to see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I doubt there's a speck of land in the Aegean where you don't know someone.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You might be right. It comes with the profession I suppose.

speaker: Aspasia
en: And who knows, maybe I'll see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't seem that big of an island. Anything's possible.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'd like to know if all the trouble to find Phoenix was worth it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like to know too.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Your heartbeat is as loud as the sea itself!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're approaching Naxos.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Are you excited?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nervous. What will I say to her?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Kassandra, you've travelled half the Greek world to find her. You don't have to say anything. Just being there will be enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But what if she is disappointed in me?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Listen. Any mother would want a child as brave and as loyal as you. If I were your mother, I would be the nervous one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You think so?

speaker: Barnabas
en: I know so. Now, go on and find her. You waited long enough for this!

speaker: Myrrine
en: I won't be intimidated. Stock the barracks... And double the patrols. If Paros is sending them, I want to know the moment they make landfall.

speaker: Timo
en: Yes, Archon.

speaker: Civilian
en: But Archon, please. The merchants

speaker: Myrrine
en: Chersis—I understand your concerns. But protecting the town and the quarries is what's most important. You may all go.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The meeting is over.

speaker: Myrrine
en: ...Kassandra? How?

speaker: Myrrine
en: When I close my eyes, I can still see you falling. I thought I had lost you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alexios is alive.

speaker: Myrrine
en: They have him, don't they?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I rebuilt my life from ashes, do you understand? And now you tell me... you're alive. You're both alive.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It's really you. It's not some trick of the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No—I found you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Your brother—we have to get him back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's too far gone.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I gave up on you both once—never again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What have you...

speaker: Myrrine
en: How did you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have... a lot of questions.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I think we both do. But ask. I'll answer what I can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to know about my real father.

speaker: Myrrine
en: How did you know?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was told.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Nikolaos? You saw him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: In Megaris, yes.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Nikolaos was your father. He was the man who raised you... until he took his Spartan duty too far.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He mentioned another. What can you tell me about him?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I always hoped you would never need to discover the truth, but there are things you need to know if we are to stop the Cult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Myrrine
en: He sought me out before I knew your fa... Nikolaos. I've not heard from him in a long time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to you in Argolis after that night?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I found your brother and rushed to a young doctor's apprentice, Hippokrates. I thought I'd lost you... I wasn't ready to lose you both.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I spoke with him recently. That night still haunts him.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I was heartbroken when the healers in Asclepius told me Alexios was dead. The two of you were my whole world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But he did live, they lied to you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: They... must have realized he was special and handed him over to the Cult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean, he was special?

speaker: Myrrine
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Timo
en: Soldiers from Paros just made landfall in the cove. A small force, maybe a dozen.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Maláka! Timo, gather the troops.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Questions will have to wait, lamb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to help.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I assume you can use those weapons?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Better than when you last saw me.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Good. Come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is attacking?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Paros, across the bay. It seems Silanos has finally grown tired of sharing the marble trade.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why now?

speaker: Myrrine
en: We've always had problems with Paros. I expected an attack, just not so soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess the time for talking is over.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Allies often forget their allegiances when opportunity beckons...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you working with Sparta given all that's happened?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Paros made an alliance with the Athenians, so they left me little choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You needed support.

speaker: Myrrine
en: A rivalry with Paros is one thing, but they turned it into a war. Their partnership with Athens was too much to weather for Naxos alone.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well, you can't say I wasn't successful in getting Kassandra out of her funk!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Out of my funk, but into a lot more trouble.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Oops. Did I already apologize for that?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Coming to Korfu, I had no inkling that we would get caught up in a tale of legendary treasure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They say life gets dull without surprises.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Now that's a reason to cheer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And to you, Ikaros!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Yes, we all have but one life to lead. We have to do the most with it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: One life? Speak for yourself!

speaker: Herodotos
en: You're right, Barnabas. Heroes like Kassandra will live on in the stories and legends of their triumphs. They live forever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen. I want you two to know... I'll be leaving soon. To travel across waters I've never dreamed of crossing. And I don't know when I'll be back.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You're leaving? Again? Where? Why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go wherever I'm needed in the world. I can't run from my responsibilities. Someone—I mean, something tells me my journey is not over yet.

speaker: Herodotos
en: We couldn't possibly keep you for ourselves. Though you'll be everywhere in my writings, that's for certain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm honored. Maybe you could give me one of your manuscripts, Herodotos. I'm sure even those from far off lands would love to read it.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Don't trouble yourself. These lands will do for now. But if you're serious...

speaker: Herodotos
en: A storyteller is always prepared. Take it. But feel no need to share it. It's for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have something for you too.

speaker: Herodotos
en: No. The spear?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You knew what it was the moment you met me. But I've...outgrown it. It's yours now. Careful. It's still sharp.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'll cherish it forever.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well, though I'm not one to refuse a gift, the gift of friendship is enough for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You only want friendship? I guess I'll need to find another second-in command for my trip.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Me? Travelling the world? With you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you'll have me as your captain.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I don't know how much longer these old bones can hoist a sail, but I'll go as far as I can. The Adrestia is yours.

speaker: Herodotos
en: What will be your first stop, Kassandra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know. What I do know is that I need a new weapon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Egypt has always fascinated me.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Ah, one of my favorite places. Let me tell you one of my best stories...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone will read your words, Herodotos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hades' Palace. And those must be the escaped prisoners of Tartaros Charon spoke of.

speaker: Mortal Man
en: It's our hero!

speaker: Mortal Woman
en: He's here to rescue us from the prisoners of Tartaros!

speaker: Elpenor
en: Kassandra! I don't believe my eyes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpenor?

speaker: Elpenor
en: The fates have mercy, after all. Oh, misthios, your appearance is what I've been waiting for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Funny. You're the last person I want to see.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Of course, of course. Our parting terms were... less than amicable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You sent me to kill my father and tried to kill me.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Which I now regret. Deeply. Seeing the underworld torn apart by chaos has shown me the error of my ways.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you think after everything you did, I'd believe a word you say... maláka!

speaker: Elpenor
en: I'm not the same man you knew. I promise I can prove it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough talk. If you want me to believe your change of heart, prove it with action.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Of course. I'd expect nothing less.

speaker: Hades
en: What a mess. Elpenor, I expect this to be cleaned up.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Of course, Hades.

speaker: Hades
en: And consider finding a more permanent solution to the Monger's attacks while you're at it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Monger's here, too.

speaker: Elpenor
en: The Monger escaped Tartaros. He's continuing the Cult's work by recruiting other escaped prisoners as they exit the rifts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen them... They put up a good fight.

speaker: Elpenor
en: We've captured one of them, but he won't tell me where the Monger is hiding. Threaten him, perhaps...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What makes you think I'd help you?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Hades and I are close. And you need him to teach you about your Staff. Helping me helps Hades. He'll appreciate this, Kassandra. As would I, of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. But I'm doing this for myself.

speaker: Mortal Man
en: By Zeus. Not you again, Elpenor. I've heard enough of your spineless posturing to last two lifetimes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like you and I are on the same side. I can't stand Elpenor either.

speaker: Mortal Man
en: You two seem pretty friendly to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm the one who sent him here in the first place.

speaker: Mortal Man
en: He's a traitor to the Monger's cause.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where the Monger's hiding, and I'll deliver Elpenor to him myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where the Monger's hiding, or I start breaking bones.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Come now, Kassandra. There's no need for that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said

speaker: Elpenor
en: My friend, I offer you freedom from Tartaros if you tell us where the Monger is hiding. Which I know is what he promised but will inevitably fail to deliver.

speaker: Mortal Man
en: All right, fine, fine! If only to shut you up. He's hiding out in the Lost Temple of Nyx. You'll never be able to take him down, anyway.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Exceptional. I've been tracking the Monger from the moment the rifts appeared. There's just one problem. The Lost Temple of Nyx is behind the Veil.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Veil?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Since Cerberos was killed, it's spilled out into the underworld. The Veil of Tartaros was created to keep out living mortals so that only those beyond redemption could enter the prison for the wicked.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Which means you'll make it through just fine. But Charon said I would need armor.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Yes, the Armor of the Fallen. Lucky for you, I may be able to help so we can both infiltrate the Monger's hideout.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want to storm the Monger's hideout together?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Of course. A chance to fight alongside the mighty Eagle Bearer? No one would turn that down. Besides, this is my opportunity to prove that I've changed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Charon already told me that four of the armor pieces are guarded by the Fallen, but that the gauntlets were lost long ago.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Charon tends to confuse lost with misplaced. Rest assured, I will help you find the gauntlets. Meet me at Kronos' Treasury.

speaker: Anais
en: It's been nice having you around, Kassandra. But I feel bad. All these years apart, and you've spent most of your time with Arion. Let's get away from all this, just you and me. There's a market in Tegea I haven't been to in ages. There's food, and wine, and music.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An evening alone sounds perfect. But what about Arion?

speaker: Anais
en: Don't worry about him. All you need to worry about is meeting me in Tegea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should find out what Anais likes before our evening together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anais never told me she made honey.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So this is where Anais keeps her wine. Smells strong... I'm getting light-headed just smelling it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anais must have a lifetime supply of olives stashed here.

speaker: Anais
en: There you are.

speaker: Anais
en: Now, let's find something to eat and drink, shall we? The merchants have the most delicious selections. And tonight, I'll leave the decision making to you.

speaker: Anais
en: Remember when we used to steal food from the markets of Kephallonia?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We could steal from this one, for old times sake.

speaker: Anais
en: Always the troublemaker.

speaker: Merchant
en: Welcome, my friends. I have a wonderful selection of wines for you and the lovely lady. Only the finest grapes from the finest vineyards. Do you prefer your wine dry, sweet or strong?

speaker: Anais
en: You've been all over the world, you must know all the best wines.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll have the dry wine.

speaker: Anais
en: I like my wine strong, but this will do... I suppose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll have the sweet wine.

speaker: Anais
en: I like my wine strong, but this will do... I suppose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This woman is a single mother who runs her own farm. She likes her wine strong.

speaker: Anais
en: You know me too well! Strong wine is the best wine.

speaker: Anais
en: Everything smells so delicious, my mouth is watering

speaker: Merchant
en: Smell that? That's the tastiest food in all of Tegea. Tell me, what will it be? We have leg of lamb with rice and olives, roast chicken with fresh vegetables, and slow-cooked goat stew.

speaker: Anais
en: Decisions, decisions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll take the lamb with olives, please.

speaker: Anais
en: I love olives! I'm going to devour this meat... then I'm going to devour you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The chicken with vegetables sounds nice.

speaker: Anais
en: This will be tasty I'm sure. I only wish it came with olives.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll have the goat stew.

speaker: Anais
en: This will be tasty I'm sure. I only wish it came with olives.

speaker: Anais
en: I can't tell you how much I needed this.

speaker: Merchant
en: Welcome, welcome! If you've got a sweet tooth, then I've got sweet treats for those... teeth. What will it be? Grape pudding with walnuts, fresh strawberries with cream, or baked pears with a honey glaze?

speaker: Anais
en: Yum. Choose wisely, I love sweets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll have the grape pudding.

speaker: Anais
en: This is fine, I suppose. Nothing's as sweet as honey though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll have the strawberries.

speaker: Anais
en: This is fine, I suppose. Nothing's as sweet as honey though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The pears sound delicious.

speaker: Anais
en: Homer called them gifts from the gods. But it's the honey that makes them truly divine.

speaker: Anais
en: This was lovely. Tonight was almost perfect.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Almost?

speaker: Anais
en: There was just one thing missing.

speaker: Anais
en: Tonight was perfect. You knew exactly what I wanted. Now, tell me what it is that you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me show you.

speaker: Anais
en: This was... fun.

speaker: Anais
en: It's late. We should get back to the house. Don't want Arion to worry.

speaker: Arion
en: Mater! Mater! You're not going to believe it!

speaker: Anais
en: What is it, Arion?

speaker: Arion
en: Bandits attacked the house but I found one of pater's old swords and did everything Kassandra taught me and I scared them away because I'm a warrior like the mighty Eagle Bearer!

speaker: Anais
en: That's incredible Arion, you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hate to say I told you so...

speaker: Anais
en: Don't lie to me, you love to say "I told you so." You always did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The boy defended what's his. You should be proud.

speaker: Anais
en: I am. I am...

speaker: Kassandra
en: But?

speaker: Anais
en: Oh please. I know you're dying to say "I told you so." It's written all over your face.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Guess it's why I'm not an actor.

speaker: Anais
en: Kassandra, there's something I need to tell you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anything.

speaker: Anais
en: Having you here was the first time I felt joy since my husband died. I hoped you were still the same person I loved back on Kephallonia, and that if you felt the same, there'd be a place for you here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anais...

speaker: Anais
en: Please, let me finish. The fact that you taught Arion to fight, when I explicitly asked you not to, shows me that you're not the partner I'm looking for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But he fought off those bandits! He could have been injured, or worse.

speaker: Anais
en: I understand, and it's OK. You felt you knew what was better for my son, and you're right. But I'm looking for someone I can trust wholeheartedly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But I love you. I've always loved you.

speaker: Anais
en: I know. And I loved you too. But I think it would be best if Arion and I moved on with our lives. Stopped living in the past and started building our future.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just not the person you thought I was. I should go.

speaker: Anais
en: It wasn't fair of me to have these expectations. You're wonderful the way you are, and I'm happy we got to spend time together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Parting as friends, then?.

speaker: Anais
en: Of course. We will always be friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Say goodbye to Arion for me.

speaker: Anais
en: I will, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Anais
en: Arion! What's wrong? My gods what's happened to you?

speaker: Arion
en: Bandits. They came and took everything. I tried to protect the house, but they were too big.

speaker: Anais
en: You shouldn't have tried to fight them. Anything they took can be replaced. But I can't replace you.

speaker: Arion
en: This wouldn't have happened if you'd trained me to be a warrior!

speaker: Anais
en: He'll be alright. Just a few scratches.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right. He's safe now, and that's what matters

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just a few scratches? he could have been killed.

speaker: Anais
en: You think I don't know that? Every time he leaves the house, I worry about him being killed. And every time he comes home, I'm just grateful he's alive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You truly are one of the strongest people I know.

speaker: Anais
en: Kassandra, there's something I need to tell you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anything.

speaker: Anais
en: Having you here was the first time I felt joy since my husband died. I hoped you were still the same person I loved back on Kephallonia, and that if you felt the same, there'd be a place for you here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anais...

speaker: Anais
en: The fact that you listened to me and didn't teach Arion to fight... shows me that you're someone I can trust. I would love it if you stayed with us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I care about you and your son, but I'm a mercenary. It's what I do. Life on the farm just isn't for me.

speaker: Anais
en: I understand. Just know that whenever you're in Arkadia, you'll always be welcome here with open arms.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd stay with you, I would. But in all honesty, I just don't know what would happen to Barnabas if I left him alone on that ship.

speaker: Anais
en: I understand. Just know that whenever you're in Arkadia, you'll always be welcome here with open arms.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I love you Anais, I've always loved you. But

speaker: Anais
en: I know. I know. You always hated staying in one place. Couldn't wait to get off Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were my favorite part of that island. But it's time for me to go.

speaker: Anais
en: I understand. Just know that whenever you're in Arkadia, you'll always be welcome here with open arms.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people are happy.

speaker: Barnabas
en: As they should be! For the first time since Ares cursed us with war, the Delos Islands know freedom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But where is Kyra? It's not like her to miss a chance to drink with her troops.

speaker: Barnabas
en: She told me you kept her secret... I'm still shocked. Podarkes was a complicated man, but he was still her father. She snuck off to send him to the Ferryman alone.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I haven't seen her celebrate with her troops since you revealed her past. She's gone to send her father to the Ferryman alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All good warriors deserve their sendoff, I suppose. Even Podarkes.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Pray that we're shown the same kindness when our time comes. In the meantime, there is wine to be drunk, and tales to be told.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Podarkes were my family, I'd have tied him to a tree and left him to rot.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You and many others on Delos. But, this is still more celebration than funeral. There's wine to drink, and tales to tell.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Make the tale great. The troops deserve it. Thaletas especially.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Make the tale great. The troops deserve it. Even Thaletas.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Indeed he does! He's just up the stairs, that way. I've been meaning to tell him how I lost this eye.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Certainly... if you can find him. And when you do, remind him—I still plan to tell him how I lost this eye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And the crew? Ready to sail?

speaker: Barnabas
en: On your order. But first, let the crew enjoy a drink and a song. You deserve one, too.

speaker: Aeson
en: Misthios! Over here!

speaker: Aeson
en: Sokrates said you're the one who saved my pater!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That lunati... rebel was your pater?

speaker: Aeson
en: They had them and you saved them!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He needed saving. I saved him

speaker: Aeson
en: That's not true. You're a hero!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your pater wasn't like the other rebels. I don't know if they'd welcome him here. You're not safe.

speaker: Aeson
en: It's all right now! Sokrates said the fighting is over, and Delians can all be friends again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're here, where are your parents?

speaker: Aeson
en: Mater's at home. I told her we were safe, but she says we have to leave now - that the bad people will come for us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not safe. The rebels are drinking and getting rowdy.

speaker: Aeson
en: They said they're building a school. I'm going to learn to read legends of heroes like you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. And try to stay out of trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For the ferryman.

speaker: Kyra
en: Go now, into the river of black night, and embrace the boundless gloom. You shall wander obscure even in the house of Hades, flitting among the shadowy dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You shouldn't have to say goodbye alone.

speaker: Kyra
en: I'm glad I'm not alone. I've wanted to watch him burn for so long. Now that it's happened... I thought I'd feel peace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what do you feel?

speaker: Kyra
en: I used to feel vengeful... Now... empty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's dead, and nothing we can do will bring him back.

speaker: Kyra
en: We? We didn't kill him. You did. I had a chance to say goodbye to him and you took it from me. The gods demanded justice from me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right here, right now, all that matters are the people who have fought for you. They need you now—not the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the gods are displeased, offer them a sacrifice.

speaker: Kyra
en: A sacrifice... What do I have left that they haven't taken from me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: People gave their lives for you, Kyra. I nearly gave my own. The gods have blessed you, and you don't even see it.

speaker: Kyra
en: No one can see what the gods do. They tricked me into wanting him dead. They tormented my thoughts until I could think of nothing else. And now, I see them laughing at me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was in your place, once. The vengeance dies, then the emptiness dies too. Give it time.

speaker: Kyra
en: Time! I've given my entire life. I want it done! Kronos devours his children—rips them flesh from bone. Zeus had Prometheus torn open by birds for an eternity. Fate is cruel, and the gods are wicked.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right here, right now, all that matters are the people who have fought for you. They need you now—not the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the gods are displeased, offer them a sacrifice.

speaker: Kyra
en: A sacrifice... What do I have left that they haven't taken from me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: People gave their lives for you, Kyra. I nearly gave my own. The gods have blessed you, and you don't even see it.

speaker: Kyra
en: No one can see what the gods do. They tricked me into wanting him dead. They tormented my thoughts until I could think of nothing else. And now, I see them laughing at me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's gone, but you're still here. The people need you. If you don't protect them, there will be another Podarkes to come and take his place.

speaker: Kyra
en: You're right. They do need me. And I need them. We're rebels with nothing left to rebel against. They need me now more than ever.

speaker: Kyra
en: They don't need me. You made sure none of them would ever trust me again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We all have complicated pasts, Kyra. It's nothing to be ashamed of. Your family—your real family, is celebrating tonight in your honor.

speaker: Kyra
en: We're rebels with nothing left to rebel against. That's not much to start a family on... but it's more than I ever had. You're right.

speaker: Kyra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What will you do next? Mykonos will need to rebuild.

speaker: Kyra
en: Then that's what we'll do. But not to put it back as it was... not as pater wanted. We'll make this place a new home for our people to be free. To live good lives.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra... He's gone. Your rebels are waiting.

speaker: Kyra
en: They're celebrating. Let's celebrate with them.

speaker: Kyra
en: Goodbye, pater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra, stop. You're too close to the edge.

speaker: Kyra
en: Nothing. All of this was for nothing. I'm a rebel with nothing left to rebel against. It didn't bring her back.

speaker: Kyra
en: Nothing. All of this was for nothing. You made sure of that... and now nothing will bring her back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Her? Who?

speaker: Kyra
en: Curse our cruel gods. I will see you, mater. And pater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra! Stop!

speaker: Kyra
en: No shame. No pain. We will be together again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Rest in Elysium, Kyra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas. What are you doing out here?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Thinking. Praying. This was my time, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Thaletas
en: This glory was supposed to be mine, but you took everything from me. You took Podarkes. You took these islands. You took Kyra, my love!

speaker: Thaletas
en: You took everything from me. You took Podarkes. You took these islands. This glory was supposed to be mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't "take" anything!

speaker: Thaletas
en: Even after you tried to turn the rebels against her, Kyra still chose you over me!

speaker: Thaletas
en: This glory was supposed to be mine. Podarkes was mine to kill. These islands were mine to win for Sparta. You were mine, and Kyra took you from me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Be reasonable, Thaletas.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I tried to be reasonable. I am not reasonable. I. Am. Spartan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas. Listen to me. Kyra is dead.

speaker: Thaletas
en: What? No! You... you killed her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one belongs to you, Thaletas. I didn't take your glory, I helped you.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You did nothing! We were in love, you know. We can be again... I can still have her heart, still prove to her I'm the warrior she wants.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas. What are you doing out here?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Thinking... Praying... We should talk.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Sparta's that way. Just past the crests of the waves. I can almost hear her singing us home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Us? Thaletas...

speaker: Thaletas
en: Leave your crew... Come with me. Join my side, and we can win glory for Sparta together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd love to join you, if I could. But you're a Spartan general now, and I have my own destiny.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I know it's crazy. But I came to these islands expecting nothing but death.

speaker: Thaletas
en: And then I found you. I know you have your life to live, and I want you to live it. Who knows, maybe the Fates will bring us together again one day...

speaker: Kassandra
en: But not today.

speaker: Thaletas
en: My troops are going to start looking for me soon. I'll see you at the celebration.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't sail by anyone's side, Thaletas. You know that by now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you wanted true glory, true freedom, you are welcome to join me on the Adrestia.

speaker: Thaletas

en: Please hurry, there hasn't been—I can't hear anything inside the lair. It's gone quiet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said Ligeia knew how to get into the lair—where exactly is the key?

speaker: Bryce
en: The Daughters of Artemis hide their most prized possessions in a cave in their village. It's protected by wild beasts and fierce warriors. The key is shaped like a disk. If they have it, it'll be there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This mercenary, the "Slayer of the Writhing Dread," where can I find him?

speaker: Bryce
en: He waits in a temple atop the hill in Ancient Pearl. Champions from all over seek to challenge him to build their reputations, but there's no way he killed the Creature. If he did, how was Ligeia taken?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you see the Creature yourself?

speaker: Bryce
en: No, but only the Writhing Dread would be strong enough to take Ligeia! She's too fierce. ...And too stubborn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back.

speaker: Bryce
en: With answers, not questions, I hope.

speaker: Odessa
en: Hey, get me out of here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's get out of here. Can you fight?

speaker: Odessa
en: I'd be happy to.

speaker: Odessa
en: My thanks. I can't believe I let those malákes sneak up on me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ithaka is a dangerous place to wander around on your own.

speaker: Odessa
en: You're wandering around on your own.

speaker: Odessa
en: You're right. I can't fight a camp of bandits by myself. Could you help me get to Odysseus' palace? I can pay.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you get to the palace.

speaker: Odessa
en: Well, I'm in luck then. What do I call you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra

speaker: Odessa
en: I'm Odessa. Named after the great Odysseus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would you want to go up there?

speaker: Odessa
en: I'm a descendant of Odysseus. I'm on a pilgrimage.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a descendant of the former king of Ithaka?

speaker: Odessa
en: And the man who created the Trojan Horse and defeated the Cyclops The one who traveled to the land of the . The one the Odyssey is about? Yes. I am. Why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not the first who's said that, is all.

speaker: Odessa
en: Well, I trust I don't need to prove my lineage to get up to the palace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should head to the palace while we have the chance.

speaker: Odessa
en: This... is it? It's just rubble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What were you expecting?

speaker: Odessa
en: I don't know. Something more grand. My parents name me Odessa... I'm Odysseus' namesake. I thought if I came here I might... understand him more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, do you?

speaker: Odessa
en: Not at all... Take me to my boat. I'll pay you there.

speaker: Odessa
en: Well, this is for you. Such a disappointment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why is that place so important for you?

speaker: Odessa
en: Are you joking? Odysseus lived there. Ruled there. He ended the Trojan War. Eluded Skylla and Charybdis. He had everything. Loyalty. Love. Fighting spirit!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He had the attention of the gods, too. That caused him a lot of trouble.

speaker: Odessa
en: And it made him a legend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You aren't a child. Stop acting like one.

speaker: Odessa
en: Wanting what Odysseus had without trying would be childish. I'm willing to do whatever is necessary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's easier said than done.

speaker: Odessa
en: Greatness is what I seek. It's what I've desired my entire life. I refuse to end up like everyone around me, content to go about their daily lives until they're forgotten in death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you keep trying, you'll get there. Giving up guarantees you never will.

speaker: Odessa
en: You're the first one to encourage me like that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just know it's your decision to make.

speaker: Odessa
en: Greatness is what I seek. It's what I've desired my entire life. I refuse to end up like everyone around me, content to go about their daily lives until they're forgotten in death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look cute right now. As if nothing can get in your way.

speaker: Odessa
en: I don't usually like being called cute.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are a few other ones I can think of that would suit you.

speaker: Odessa
en: I can't wait to hear them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How about beautiful? That works even better. The other ones will come later.

speaker: Odessa
en: I hope "later" comes soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In time you'll learn to love all the things I have to tell you.

speaker: Odessa
en: You seem so certain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've had lots of success in the past.

speaker: Odessa
en: I'm sure you have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, you're ugly then.

speaker: Odessa
en: That's... not what I meant at all. I can't tell if you're serious or not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what do you think?

speaker: Odessa
en: I think I was a much poorer mood before now. There's just so much I desire. To be as great as Odysseus... Where do I even begin?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you want Odysseus' greatness, you have to do it your own way. He was famous because of his cunning. What have you done?

speaker: Odessa
en: I've traveled all the way here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: To see the ruins of Odysseus' life. Not to live your own.

speaker: Odessa
