en: I should have known better than to take advice from a mercenary. Leave me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Odysseus didn't want to go to war. And once it was over, it took him ten years to get home. He wasted years of his life, all because gods interfered. Stay home. Spend time with your family. Live your own life.

speaker: Odessa
en: But who will remember my story then?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Would you rather be remembered? Or happy?

speaker: Odessa
en: Hmm. I'll have to give that some thought. Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems like you're looking for advice. I have none to give.

speaker: Odessa
en: No surprise there. Well, thanks for the help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to see Sokrates.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know who I am?

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Of course I do! Sokrates never stops talking about you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you are?

speaker: Xanthippe
en: His wife, of course! I'm Xanthippe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sokrates never told me he had a wife.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Typical. The only time he's quiet is when he's eating, yet he can't find the time to mention me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. With how much Sokrates has told me, it's like I already know you.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Oh? What sort of things has he said?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He said how beautiful you are. I see now how true his words were.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: You flatter me. Though I'm surprised Sokrates said as much as to you. He's not the type to focus on looks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He claimed you're the smartest woman he's known.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: He always said it was his favorite thing about me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Actually... that wasn't the truth. I didn't know Sokrates was married.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Ha! You should have let me believe it a bit longer. I would have loved to see his face when I asked him about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So where is Sokrates? I got a note that said to meet him here.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: That's what I'd like to know. He went to another symposium last night and he didn't come home after.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a good place to start looking.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: I was just about to head there myself. Come - keep me company.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How long have you and Sokrates been married?

speaker: Xanthippe
en: It's been quite some time now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it about him that you love so much?

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Love is not the word I'd use. He frustrates me to no end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That doesn't surprise me.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Even so, it's worth the frustration. His mind is like no other... Not to mention he's quite a good lover.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That is not something I wanted to picture. It must be why Alkibiades seemed so infatuated with him.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: Don't mention that name around me. Always coming by drunk, sending Sokrates gifts like giant cakes...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... didn't know.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: It's fine.

speaker: Witness
en: Xanthippe!

speaker: Xanthippe
en: What is it?

speaker: Witness
en: Sokrates. They took him away. They said he was under arrest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For what?

speaker: Witness
en: I have no idea. We were just talking after the symposium. I'd say go ask him yourself, but he'll be guarded. They took him southeast of here.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: That fool. I knew this would happen to him one day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find him, don't worry.

speaker: Xanthippe
en: This is his doing. It's best to let things run their course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't believe Sokrates was arrested. I need to find out what happened.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Kassandra? What are you doing here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could ash you the same.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Well, here I am. Though I'm more curious about how you are here. The guards let you in?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I only had to tell them how close we are, and they let me come see you.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, then you used what you learned from me. I'm impressed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: My... words cut very, very deep.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've known each other a long time now. You know how I got in here.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You've taught me that the blade can sometimes be necessary, but I don't think this was one of those times.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was worried about you.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Your care is appreciated, but if you had waited only a bit longer, I'm sure my trial would have taken place and I'd be free.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not going to trial. We're getting you out of here.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I appreciate your concern, but what good would escaping do other than prove I'm guilty? No, in I'm looking forward to this trial.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You would go to trial just to prove you can convince them of your innocence?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Exactly! You have your ways to find excitement, and I have mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if they find you guilty, and your punishment is severe?

speaker: Sokrates
en: That will never happen. I'll convince them I deserve to go—you'll see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What were you arrested for?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I haven't the slightest idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And that doesn't bother you?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Sometimes, understanding doesn't come at the moment we would like. More importantly, this is giving me necessary time to think.

speaker: Kassandra
en: About?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I went to see the Pythia, and she told me there is none wiser than me. An intriguing thought, and one I've been unable to stop thinking about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sokrates, the Pythia is

speaker: Sokrates
en: It matters not what you believe she is or she isn't. I must examine not only her words, but my own self as well. I know nothing, so how could I be called wise?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does that have to do with being locked up?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I believe my time here and this trial may help me find the answer. I will be fine. Trust me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've known you for a while now.

speaker: Sokrates
en: That's true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you'd call us friends?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I would.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And friends share important things with one another, is that so?

speaker: Sokrates
en: It is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then how did I not know you were married?

speaker: Kassandra
en: From what you just said, that means either we're not friends, or that friends don't share with one another. So which is it?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ha! I've often wondered how much of our conversations you've taken to heart, and now I have my answer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Were you doing anything when you got arrested?

speaker: Sokrates
en: If speaking my mind is worth imprisonment, then I suppose I was.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In the future, you may want to be more careful.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You risk life and limb every time you draw your blade. Just because it's my tongue that is sharp doesn't mean I'm not prepared to face the consequences of using it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Since you won't leave with me, I'll go see the Pythia myself.

speaker: Sokrates
en: That's not necessary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out why she told you that. I won't let you go to trial, even if you think you'll be found innocent.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Kassandra, you

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I have what I need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The good wine should be in that fort. If the officers haven't drunk it all already.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the good wine Thespis mentioned, but it smells awful. I should try it...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ugh! This tastes like horse piss. I can't serve this. There must be something better nearby.

speaker: Wine Society Invitation
en: Those who appreciate the finer qualities of wine should join us in the underground storage for a tasting event. DON'T TELL THE OFFICERS.

speaker: Soldier
en: You see, the grapes from the southern side of the mountain are always sweeter. And that's why this wine tastes like apricots.

speaker: Brute
en: No, no, no. These grapes are clearly imported from Thebes. And they're called "the Pharaoh's Honey Grapes," because they taste like, well, honey.

speaker: Soldier
en: No, it has the distinctive aftertaste of apricots!

speaker: Brute
en: It lingers in the mouth like honey.

speaker: Soldier
en: I can't believe that idiot commander kept the terrible wine for himself. That fool couldn't tell fine wine from horse piss!

speaker: Brute
en: Yeah!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found your wine.

speaker: Thespis
en: Wonderful! Our guests will be in a fantastic mood before the play even starts.

speaker: Rhodanthe
en: I sampled the wine, it's excellent! I'll try selling tickets in the better parts of town. Our wealthy patrons won't be disappointed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, when will I be able to see this play?

speaker: Thespis
en: Well, there's a little complication with the cast. Finding them, I mean.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've lost your actors?

speaker: Rhodanthe
en: None of them showed up at the last rehearsal. And the time before that, they seemed terribly discouraged. Someone might have been too harsh with them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one will get paid if they don't come back.

speaker: Thespis
en: Exactly. There's three of them in all. They're playing Ephialtes, Xerxes, and Dienekes. I can give you an idea of where they might be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's playing Leonidas?

speaker: Thespis
en: I am, of course. I trust no one but myself to carry the starring role.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So Xerxes, King of the Persians, is in your play?

speaker: Thespis
en: Yes, and I found a tremendous actor to play him. He plays marvelous villains. He did mention that the Dyspontion Ruins were inspiring him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Dienekes... that was Leonidas's favorite lieutenant.

speaker: Thespis
en: Yes, and played by a charming young fellow. A bit of a nervous type though. I was surprised when he told me he was going gambling in the great square here in Elis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So the traitor Ephialtes is missing. What a surprise.

speaker: Thespis
en: Usually, my good friend Tros is dedicated to his craft. But last time we spoke, he seemed touched by a certain religious fervor. He said he would pray at the Spring of Piera.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope the actors turn up.

speaker: Thespis
en: When you find our actors, send them back to me. And do your best to encourage them! Our performance will be terrible if the actors' hearts aren't in it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And that means no one will pay us. Got it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The pirates are Poseidon's problem now.

speaker: Megakles
en: What have you done? Didn't you hear me screaming? You sunk our reinforcements!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They sure looked and fought like pirates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You didn't say anything about reinforcements. You said pirates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those ships attacked me. I fought back. That's what I do.

speaker: Megakles
en: I sent a message to the supply ships to disguise their sails. "Look like a pirate and sail in unseen." Those ships had supplies and troops.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I'd known they were reinforcements, I wouldn't have attacked. I need to set this right.

speaker: Megakles
en: There's still time. If we can get these villagers ready for battle, they can fight off the pirates themselves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not an actual general, are you?

speaker: Megakles
en: Not... a... Listen to me, misthios. I've fought in three wars. No training prepares you for this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You had no strategy.

speaker: Megakles
en: These villagers are as good as slaughtered because of you. But if we can get them ready, they can fight off the pirates themselves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now you tell me.

speaker: Megakles
en: Didn't think I had to say, "Don't sink the fucking reinforcements!" Without those troops, we need to get these villagers ready for battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do it. I don't see an armory, though. Where's the smith?

speaker: Megakles
en: He hasn't worked since the last Eagle Bearer was here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get him making swords. Can the villagers ride?

speaker: Megakles
en: For salt workers, they're not bad. And there's a horse breeder in town.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll talk to them.

speaker: Megakles
en: Though we can't just arm them and tell them to fight. There's only one man who can rally the people, claims to be a reborn Ajax the Lesser. Find him and get him back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So where's the blacksmith?

speaker: Megakles
en: The forge caught fire. The smith's in the village, but you'll need to help him rebuild before he can work again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more about the horse breeder.

speaker: Megakles
en: She knows horses better than Poseidon. Get her to put a mare under each of these villagers, and we'll have a chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If dead heroes are anything like me, they don't like being impersonated. Are you sure this Ajax guy is a good idea?

speaker: Megakles
en: Let the dead judge us all they want. We need to shake the fear out of these villagers. The last time I saw Ajax, he was headed to the hills southwest of here, on the northern border of Phokis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what you know about the one using my name.

speaker: Megakles
en: He came in with a vicious little bird. Called it... Ikaros? Something like that. Anyway, said he'd help, then made things worse at every turn. So far, you two have a lot in common.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The villagers will be warriors when I'm done.

speaker: Megakles
en: You're back just in time. How's Nikaia? I heard she's trained a stallion for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nikaia's dead. She thought your horse was Pegasos and rode it right off a cliff.

speaker: Megakles
en: She what? All right. We don't need horses to fight if we have weapons. How many has Kallipides made?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, Nikaia's great. There's more horses than this village has people.

speaker: Megakles
en: She's as reliable as they come. And Kallipides? Has he armed the villagers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kallipides... had an accident.

speaker: Megakles
en: What kind of accident?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The really bad kind. He... didn't see some stone blocks. He walked right into them, and

speaker: Megakles
en: Enough. Without weapons, we're doomed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We haven't even talked about Ajax yet.

speaker: Megakles
en: Did you find him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The villagers are all armed. Every single one. Nothing to worry about there.

speaker: Megakles
en: Good! Spilling a little pirate blood on the salt might make it taste better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You never know. Now, as for Ajax.

speaker: Megakles
en: Tell me he inspired the villagers to make a stand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ajax had this helmet that he thought would make him immortal...

speaker: Megakles
en: And?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It didn't.

speaker: Megakles
en: Malaka.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about it.

speaker: Megakles
en: I would ask literally anyone else, but what choice do I have? I need everyone with a blade fighting with me. You can at least fight, can't you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ajax put on a real show. I've never seen anything like it.

speaker: Megakles
en: Good! Very good. The villagers are a superstitious type.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In this village, I can see why.

speaker: Megakles
en: You did good. The villagers should be able to defend their homes thanks to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They may still need a bit of help.

speaker: Megakles
en: Agreed! We can leave them to defend the village while you and I stop any pirates that are storming the Salts. What do you think?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go.

speaker: Megakles
en: Not a lot of people would have been honest with me the way you were. I respect that. I just hope there's still a chance that we can make this right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will do everything I can to save these people.

speaker: Megakles
en: When you sunk those ships, I thought we were as good as dead. But you did well, getting these villagers ready to fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right, well... It was the least I could do.

speaker: Damia
en: You are the Eagle Bearer. Wonderful! Magistrate Xanthe has spoken highly of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Very kind of her.

speaker: Damia
en: So, here's the thing. My children have promising futures. But they refuse to learn and study. They think they know better, but they can't recite a poem to save their lives.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where do I fit into this?

speaker: Damia
en: They've heard of the Eagle Bearer and worship the ground you walk on. If you related an epic story to them, I'd bet they'd retain it and impress their tutors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's an odd request, but I've been asked to do stranger things. I'll do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not the one you want. Everyone who has ever heard a poem thinks they are a natural born storyteller, but it takes a talent I'm not sure I possess.

speaker: Damia
en: Will you help me now, and tell my children an inspiring tale to set their imaginations and memories alight?

speaker: Damia
en: My children are waiting inside the Temple of Dionysos Kolonatas for today's epic story. The subject is Perseus, which they should know well, but seem to forget all when questioned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know the story well, of course, but my preferred version may not be what your children expect...

speaker: Damia
en: Do not fear! If you need a reminder, there are many relics related to Perseus in the hall adjacent to the Temple of Dionysos Kolonatas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good to know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perseus? I know his story well, as if we were cousins both raised at the base of Mount Olympos. Do not fear, I will hold your children fast with my tale.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hello, I'm

speaker: Danae
en: The Eagle Bearer! We've heard all about you!

speaker: Kristos
en: Are you going to tell us a story today? Do we have to listen? We've heard it a hundred times.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, that's me. And yes, I'm telling you a story.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gather round and listen, children, while I spin you the yarn of Perseus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let us sing with the voice of the goddess about the exploits of brave Perseus and noble Pegasos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need a moment to prepare... and then I'll tell a story to take your breath away!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Akrisios, the king of Argos, was not a good man. He had one child, a daughter, Danae. Bitter that he had no son, he went to the Oracle of Delphi, and heard a prophecy that chilled him.

speaker: Danae
en: Ooh. What was it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Oracle said Akrisios would be killed by his grandson, but Danae was unmarried and childless at the time. To protect himself, he locked Danae in a bronze room, open only to the sky.

speaker: Kristos
en: Ooh!

speaker: Kassandra
en: However, mighty Zeus saw the girl and fell in love with her. He transformed into a golden shower and seduced her. Danae gave birth to a son, Perseus.

speaker: Kristos
en: I knew it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: King Akrisios couldn't kill the boy for fear of angering Zeus, so he put his daughter and grandson in a wooden crate and tossed them into the wild sea, to be drowned.

speaker: Danae
en: How horrid! Poor Perseus!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The great god of the sea, Poseidon, visited a mortal woman, Sarra, a fisherman's daughter. The god of the sea frolicked with her, in the shape of a dolphin, and she knew his love.

speaker: Kristos
en: Is this a kissing story?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Relax, I'm just setting it up. Soon Sarra gave birth to a child, the half-blood hero Perseus!

speaker: Kristos
en: I thought Perseus' mother's name was Danae, like my sister?

speaker: Danae
en: Yeah, and his father was Zeus!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Uh, well, that's true in some versions... Anyway, at some point baby Perseus fell off a boat and almost drowned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perseus and his mother, Danae, were rescued on the island of Seriphos, and Perseus grew up under the care of a kindly fisherman, Diktys.

speaker: Danae
en: Lucky them! Did the gods help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe. Perseus learned to swim, and ride, and fight, and how to be good and just, even though his faster was only a fisherman.

speaker: Kristos
en: I can do all those things, too!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good for you.

speaker: Kristos
en: Except swim.

speaker: Danae
en: Or be just!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hush. Now, Diktys' brother was ruler of the island, but he was not a good man.

speaker: Danae
en: He's scum!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A kindly old couple, and Alkmene found Perseus in the sea and brought him to their farm in Smalpolis, taking him as their son.

speaker: Danae
en: What about his mom, my namesake?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shh, listen! Hera was angry, though, and sent snakes to kill the baby. But Perseus was too strong, and he strangled the snakes in his crib, revealing his godly nature.

speaker: Kristos
en: That doesn't sound right!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are different ways to tell the story, you know!

speaker: Child
en: And? This story is for the crows.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The cruel king of Seriphos, Diktys' brother Polydektes, decided he wanted to marry Danae for she was still beautiful and noble. But Perseus knows his mother does not want this. Diktys couldn't stop his brother, so it was up to Perseus to interfere and be annoying.

speaker: Danae
en: Kristos, that's your job!

speaker: Kristos
en: I would keep the stinky king from marrying you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The cruel, uh, stinky king became angry. To get rid of Perseus, Polydektes sent him on an impossible quest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Prove yourself a warrior and fetch me a worthy wedding gift," the king said, "by killing a great monster!"

speaker: Kristos
en: I knew it!

speaker: Danae
en: Shh! I knew it, too!

speaker: Kassandra
en: When Perseus grows up, he travels to Joppa and falls in love at first sight with the beautiful princess Andromeda. However, Andromeda's mother boasts that her daughter is more beautiful than the goddess Thetis, offending her!

speaker: Kristos
en: Never say you are better than the gods!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thetis proclaims that Andromeda must be sacrificed to the gods, or else the whole city of Joppa will be destroyed!

speaker: Danae
en: I... don't think that's right. Wasn't Andromeda an princess?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hush! Perseus asks his grandmother, Tala, how to save his love. She turns into a manta ray and says, to save Andromeda, he must bring back curly hair of gold, fit for the king of the mountains, who yet owns less than the humblest helot.

speaker: Danae
en: I don't know that riddle.

speaker: Kristos
en: It's too hard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Uh, it was hard for Perseus, too. But eventually he figured it out.

speaker: Danae
en: How?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He just did is all!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Polydektes told Perseus to bring back the head of Medusa, the gorgon whose gaze could turn anyone who looked into her eyes to stone.

speaker: Kristos
en: Ahh!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Polydektes knew that Medusa would be Perseus's death...

speaker: Kristos
en: That stinker!

speaker: Kassandra
en: But the evil king did not know Perseus was favored by the gods. Hermes gifted Perseus with and a silver sickle, and Athena gave him a bronze shield, polished mirror-bright. Perseus flew to Medusa's lair, and used the shield to watch her reflection. He cut off her head with the sickle of Hermes. As she died, the winged foal Pegasos sprung from her neck!

speaker: Danae
en: Yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Flying home, Perseus found the maiden Andromeda chained on the cliffs, waiting to be sacrificed to the baleful sea monster, Ketos. Perseus used Medusa's head to turn Ketos to stone, rescued Andromeda, and married her.

speaker: Kristos
en: Take that, Ketos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perseus returned home to find King Polydektes relentlessly pursuing Danae. They quarreled, and Perseus showed the king his wedding gift... When he saw Medusa's head, Polydektes turned to stone!

speaker: Kristos
en: YES!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perseus figured out what he needed - the of the winged ram! Said to be guarded by a monster who could turn any to stone. Luckily, Perseus was blessed by the gods, and he was guided by Athena's golden-geared to the monster's lair...

speaker: Danae
en: Athena's golden owl? That's dumb!

speaker: Kristos
en: Sounds cute! I want one!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And armed with the vorpal sword from the mighty , he faced the snake-necked, large-headed, shaggy-maned, stony-gazed !

speaker: Kristos
en: No!

speaker: Danae
en: Huh?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perseus avoided the Catoblepas' killing gaze and snicked the sword, lopping off the creature's head.

speaker: Kristos & Danae
en: Ew!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He grabbed the golden fleece and wrapped the Catoblepas' head in it, then flew back home astride winged Pegasos to save Andromeda, who was about to be eaten by the ! He used the deadly head to turn the Kraken to stone.

speaker: Kristos
en: Wait, the what? What's a Kraken?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Er, like a giant squid?

speaker: Danae
en: Don't you mean the sea monster, Ketos?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pretty sure Homer said, "release the Kraken," not "release the Ketos."

speaker: Danae
en: You just made that up!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perseus traveled to Argos with his family, and one day competed in the great athletic games. He hurled the , and his throw was so great that it shot into the stands and struck King Akrisios. So doing, Perseus killed his grandfather and fulfilled the prophecy.

speaker: Kristos
en: Hurrah!

speaker: Danae
en: You can't escape your fate!

speaker: Kassandra
en: In the end, Perseus and Andromeda settled in Mycenae as king and queen, and had seven sons and two daughters, the Perseids.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was not all! Hades appears with a pack of giant scorpions called scorpiochs, and kills Andromeda and tries to kill Perseus!

speaker: Kristos
en: Huh?

speaker: Kassandra
en: But Perseus throws his sword of Zeus at Hades, forcing him back into the underworld!

speaker: Danae
en: Wait, wait, it's supposed to be Hermes' sickle! And Andromeda doesn't die!

speaker: Kristos
en: You're telling it wrong!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Uh... In the end, Perseus wins. Zeus offers to make him a god, but Perseus refuses. So instead, Zeus brings Andromeda back to life because she was only mostly dead.

speaker: Danae
en: Wow, that was so wrong and so boring!

speaker: Kristos
en: You are a stinky storyteller, and that story was poop!

speaker: Damia
en: I, ah, I'm sorry for your audience, Eagle Bearer. Though from what I heard, it did sound like you deviated somewhat from the traditional tale.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Uh, apologies.

speaker: Danae
en: That was a great telling of the tale. I'll never forget it!

speaker: Kristos
en: Maybe the best! I can't wait to tell all my friends!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aw, thank you.

speaker: Damia
en: I couldn't help overhearing the end of your story. Truly inspiring, Eagle Bearer. Thank you.

speaker: Danae
en: I told a story of Perseus to my tutor, and he said it was the best rendition he'd ever heard. My mother is so happy with us!

speaker: Metiochos
en: Help me! Please, someone. By the gods, why did it have to be snakes? Help me! If you leave, these snakes will kill me! Get me out of here! Hurry! Kill these snakes before it's too late!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are there so many snakes?

speaker: Metiochos
en: Blessed be the god that sent you here. I'd have been eaten alive if it weren't for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't think they'd eat you.

speaker: Metiochos
en: But they would have certainly killed me, so thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm always happy to help someone in need.

speaker: Metiochos
en: The world could do with more like you. Especially now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My life-saving services aren't free.

speaker: Metiochos
en: Of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perikles sent me. He was worried about you. Do you often get tied up and surrounded by snakes?

speaker: Metiochos
en: How can you joke about this? Thugs broke into my home, dragged me here, tied me up, and surrounded me with these hideous creatures. They must be stopped!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The snakes?

speaker: Metiochos
en: The THUGS!!!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would anyone do this?

speaker: Metiochos
en: Politicians are easy targets in these troubled times. When they tied me up, they said I was a snake—that I should die by my own kind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you recognize the people who did this?

speaker: Metiochos
en: Perikles asked me to go down to the Fishing District and talk with the poor and sick—to give them hope. That's how I recognized their voices.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, yes?

speaker: Metiochos
en: They threw rotten food and yelled insults at me. These thugs disguised their faces, but their voices and the stench of fish were unmistakable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where should I look?

speaker: Metiochos
en: I couldn't see their faces, but I recognized their voices from one of the districts I visited. They're regulars at Kleon's rallies—they live in the flooded part of the city near the wall.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll track them down, Metiochos. Don't worry.

speaker: Metiochos
en: Tensions are high right now. At this rate we'll tear each other apart within the city before the Spartans can breach the walls.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The part of Athens I doubt Perikles is proud to talk about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Snakes... like the ones that were meant to kill Metiochos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, snake bites, and someone hid the body. Though I have a feeling this death was an accident.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It looks like the thugs who attacked Metiochos weren't the masterminds behind this plot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the house of Metiochos's attackers, but the letter proves they're just tools in someone else's plan. Whose?

speaker: Pratinos
en: What the fuck are you doing sniffing around my house?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You attacked Metiochos. I found the snakes, the letter from your friend, and a body... all here.

speaker: Civilian
en: Ah, poor Aktis.

speaker: Pratinos
en: We all knew the risks. Change don't happen without a bit of blood being spilled.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why kill Metiochos with snakes?

speaker: Pratinos
en: We're prisoners in our own city because of Perikles and his crooked friends. The snake dealer told us it's time to send a message—time they suffered.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't take the law into your own hands. Now I need to decide what to do with you.

speaker: Pratinos
en: Kleon says it's time we took the city back from the elite—time to fight. Don't matter what you do to us, there'll be others who follow our lead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know someone gave you those snakes—they used you to do their dirty work. I want to know who.

speaker: Pratinos
en: He's a real hero of Athens. No puppet of Perikles is going to stop him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what I want to know, or I'll cut you down right now. Your cause will be forgotten and so will you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't be someone's puppet. Tell me where the snake dealer is.

speaker: Pratinos
en: All right, all right. He's got a camp just outside the walls. Sells his snakes from there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've crossed a line. Now you must pay the price.

speaker: Pratinos
en: We'll never surrender to the likes of you. We will make Athens great again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not too late to make a difference, but we have to work together.

speaker: Pratinos
en: Maybe you're right—you didn't have to show us mercy. But where do we start?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Start here—this district is your home. Ignore the politicians and concentrate on where you can make change.

speaker: Pratinos
en: Thank you, we will try.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to rid Athens of this snake seller.

speaker: Mercenary
en: You'll feel the sting of my venom. I'll end you, misthios. You can't stop me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: His death should keep friends of Perikles safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like your situation's improved since we last met.

speaker: Metiochos
en: The danger has passed for now, but while those monsters are out there, no one is safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A group of fishermen tied you up. They were being used by a snake dealer working for enemies of Athens.

speaker: Metiochos
en: What did you do with them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I showed them the errors of their ways and sent them on their way. They won't be bothering you again.

speaker: Metiochos
en: I'm glad no blood was shed, but how do you know they won't return?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I made it very clear that doing anything stupid would make me angry.

speaker: Metiochos
en: Well that must have been a terrifying experience for them. Thank you for your help, misthios. I'll be sure to mention this to Perikles. Thank you for your help, my friend.

speaker: Phoibe
en: The last I heard about my parents, they were hiding near the Ixion Wheel.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hiding? From what?

speaker: Phoibe
en: The underworld is scary. Maybe they're not fighters like us? I could teach them what you taught me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure you could.

speaker: Mortal Woman
en: Help us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe, stay back!

speaker: Survivor
en: Please! I already told you—go tell the Cyclops the girl isn't here, and neither is her family. Now get back!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Relax. We're not going to hurt you, but we need to know what happened here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one threatens me. Put down the blade and start talking.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Kassandra! Sorry. What she means to say is we're not goingt to hurt you. We just need to know what happened here.

speaker: Survivor
en: Those thugs followed the Cyclops of Kephallonia to their graves, and now they follow him in the underworld. He sent them through here looking for a girl.

speaker: Phoibe
en: The man with one eye...

speaker: Survivor
en: Have you ever met a girl named Phoibe?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is Phoibe.

speaker: Survivor
en: So you are. My dear, I loved your parents as I loved my own. They hid here with me and told tales about the great warrior Phoibe who sailed to Elysium.

speaker: Phoibe
en: They called me a warrior?

speaker: Survivor
en: When Cerberos died, they snuck off to find you themselves... But the Cyclops is looking for you, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We don't know a Phoibe... Why were they looking for the girl?

speaker: Survivor
en: I'm not sure. I was a friend to her parents. They used to hide here. They told tales of their daughter, a great warrior who sailed to Elysium.

speaker: Phoibe
en: They called her a warrior?

speaker: Survivor
en: When Cerberos died, they snuck off to the golden fields to find her, but now the Cyclops is looking for them all.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Excuse us, please.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I remember now. The man with one eye is the Cyclops. He forced me to drink the water.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He must know we stole your eagle back and came to retaliate.

speaker: Phoibe
en: What do we do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gates to Elysium are open, but you know the Cyclops. He won't stop until he gets what he wants. We have to deal with him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gates to Elysium are open. That's how your parents got through. I know the way.

speaker: Phoibe
en: What about her? She's a friend of my parents. I want to help her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She seems like she can fend for herself.

speaker: Phoibe
en: The Keres are magic, and they heal people who get hurt in battle. They live close by. I could...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe...

speaker: Phoibe
en: I can do this! I'll be quick, then we can fight the Cyclops.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I can do this! I'll be quick, then we'll go to Elysium and find my parents.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. But don't take too long, or I'm coming after you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Muse, huh?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Hmm, not my usual type. Too many muscles, but if you've got the drachmae, we can come to an arrangement.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thespis said I'd find you here.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Ah, my darling Thespis, an artist in so many ways... But let's talk about us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought you were Thespis' great love.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: That is love, this is commerce. So what are you into?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't understand, I need your help.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: So many do. These hands have helped more people than Hippokrates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, Thespis told me to find you.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Well, I'm not giving discounts to his friends if that's what you're thinking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, Thespis wants you to go to him. He needs you to help him perform tomorrow.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Thespis does love to perform, but he'll be doing it without me this time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you're his muse?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Commander Rhexenor has made it clear it would cost me my life if I were to associate with Thespis right now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been hearing about this Commander Rhexenor a lot recently.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: He's one of Kleon's favorite dogs. I've heard stories from some of the girls. Likes to play dress up. Got a fancy robe and mask—likes to hurt people too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry...

speaker: Aikaterine
en: He runs the local garrison—his men are always here. They'd tell him in an instant if I was gone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would this Commander threaten you?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: It's all to do with this stupid play. They're doing everything they can to protect Kleon's image.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Still, to threaten you?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Actors are a superstitious bunch. Commander Rhexenor knows Thespis won't perform without his muse waiting in the wings.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, I'll deal with Commander Rhexenor.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: You don't understand what a bastard he is. He's more than just some Athenian soldier.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Secret meetings, strange visitors—he gives me the creeps... You'll have to kill him. There's no other option.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I do this, will you go to Thespis?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: It'd be my pleasure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find the Commander?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: In the barracks across the street, to the north. The girls have to visit him there when he wants servicing - doesn't have the stamina to come down here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can you describe him?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: He wears one of those big stupid helms... makes up for other areas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, I'll take care of him.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Bring me back his little sword, as proof!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There seems little doubt that Rhexenor is aligned with the Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's for what you did to my family.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is this proof enough of his death?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Not quite the sword I meant... But, as long as he's dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My part is done. Go make sure Thespis is at the theater in time for his performance.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: You are too tense. Come here and lie a while. We've time to have a little fun... Or is it always business with you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it with you? There is more at stake here than a few moments of pleasure.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Only a few? You don't rate yourself highly in love, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This play could help decide the fate of Athens. I need you to keep your word and go to Thespis.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Do not worry. I will see you at the play, with Thespis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is it with you?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: So blood does pulse in those veins...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It roars, but what of Thespis?

speaker: Aikaterine
en: Thespis is an actor, half the girls here have been his muse at one time or another.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now... we need to worry about Thespis and Aristophanes' play.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: This play is important to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With it, we hope to make change... for the better.

speaker: Aikaterine
en: I can see there is more in your eyes, but we are all entitled to our secrets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's enough for you to know that I plan to stop men like Commander Rhexenor and Kleon.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Please tell me you have news of Thespis?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's fine, and he'll be fit to perform in your play tomorrow.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Oh, thank the gods. I know what actors can be like.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Athenians' lives are too complicated. I would rather be a farmer than work in the theater.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: True, it's not for everyone—but it's a wonderful life!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Compared to what I'm used to, it was a breath of fresh air.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: That is so good to hear!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Here, for your troubles. The people may be the heart of Athens, but my play will be its voice!

speaker: Chorus leader
en: Oh happy day for us and for our children if Kleon should perish.

speaker: Chorus member
en: You also know what a pig's education he has had!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Such insults! And to think I was going to propose a statue to be erected in the city to each of you for your bravery!

speaker: Chorus leader
en: See! He treats us like old dotards and crawls at our feet to deceive us; but the cunning wherein his power lies shall this time recoil on himself!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Alas! The conspirators are murdering me!

speaker: Civilian
en: Help m...

speaker: Phoibe
en: Kassandra... You're back! Gotta run, sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait! Where...

speaker: Phoibe
en: I'll be right back. See you at Aspasia's!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sometimes I think you are too much like me.

speaker: Kleon
en: Friends, I know you're angry. And you have the right to be—why do they hide in their houses and not quell the chaos that's come to Athens? Understand Perikles is a sick man. Don't blame him for that. Blame him for bringing this curse that grips our once-great city. We are Athenians. We settle our disputes democratically, but there comes a time when words are not enough, and the people must take action. Athens's name was once held high in the world. Now what has it become? Let's return Athens to greatness. We will be feared again! Raise your voices! I promise you, you won't be ignored any longer.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Kassandra, it's good to have you back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never seen anything like this.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Those who aren't killed by the plague run wild in the streets. Death is rampant... And it's only a warning. We have ignored what truly plagues us for too long. Kleon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can you worry about him at a time like this?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Under his reign, Athens will lose the freedom and glory that has put it on the world stage.

speaker: Sokrates
en: It is time to turn my words into actions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How?

speaker: Sokrates
en: You'll find out as soon as I do.

speaker: Kleon
en: I didn't expect to see you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you think you're doing? You're driving this mob to madness.

speaker: Kleon
en: This? This is nothing.

speaker: Kleon
en: I will make Athens great again!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to find Aspasia and get out of this crazy city as soon as possible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspasia.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Oh, Kassandra. You've returned to Athens.

speaker: Aspasia
en: What's left of Athens. The world we've built is crumbling at our feet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's as loud as a battlefield out there. And as violent.

speaker: Aspasia
en: They're calling for Perikles's head—as though he should know how to handle this catastrophe. No one is prepared for the end of the world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's bleak, but it hasn't killed you.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You're right. But everything Perikles has built is being destroyed. It's chaos outside these walls. People have forgotten how to be people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came to talk to you. I found out some things about my mother. Her name, her ship...

speaker: Aspasia
en: Kassandra, it's not the time. Perikles is dying. He won't see me. He won't let Hippokrates in his room... He only babbles about going to his precious Parthenon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perikles is a strong man. I'm sure he can fight the sickness.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You heard the mob—he can't defend himself. He'll die with no glory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Athens has known him a lot longer than they've known this plague. He gave them a voice. His accomplishments will speak for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The reason I came back to Athens was to talk to you about Myrrine.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Your mother will live to see tomorrow. My love won't live to see another sunset.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've had many sunsets with him. I've spent all my nights alone.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Perikles needs treatment, and the gods know he won't let me in. He respects you. Could you go to him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could try.

speaker: Aspasia
en: If you do, I will make the time to talk about your mother. For now, he needs your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's worth a shot.

speaker: Medicine
en: Hippokrates says this medicinal drink should reduce fever. Perikles needs it desperately.

speaker: Perikles
en: Aspasia, my light, I told you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's Kassandra.

speaker: Perikles
en: Yes. Come in.

speaker: Perikles
en: It's embarrassing—someone so strong seeing me like this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look healthy as ever.

speaker: Perikles
en: Tell Aspasia that. She won't worry so much about me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I admit you don't quite look yourself.

speaker: Perikles
en: I don't feel like myself either.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I brought your drugs.

speaker: Perikles
en: Ah, yes. It's usually Phoibe who does the delivering. At least I'm alive... Though I can't say the same for my city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a shadow of what it was.

speaker: Perikles
en: Well, it will belong to Kleon now. He will have to lift it out of its sorry state.

speaker: Perikles
en: I wish to see it with my own eyes. Come, to the balcony.

speaker: Perikles
en: Much has changed. I can't even stand up straight to look death in the eye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll recover sooner if you let Hippokrates see you.

speaker: Perikles
en: It's my time. The plague chooses no favorites. I fear I've failed Athens. Its people. Aspasia...

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, you haven't.

speaker: Perikles
en: You're kind, but I've lost. Aspasia needs protection. As does Athens. I thought I gave enough to Athena, but it seems it isn't so.

speaker: Perikles
en: I should be out there on the streets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'd be overtaken. There are mobs, and Kleon's doing nothing to calm them.

speaker: Perikles
en: Thank the gods Kleon won't see me like this. But that's all I can thank the gods for. They've turned on me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not the gods' fault. It's the world—it's turned upside down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods definitely aren't in Athens. I hardly recognize it here—it's like the Tartaros.

speaker: Perikles
en: Athens fate is decreed. All we can do now is wait.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should go back inside. You need to rest.

speaker: Perikles
en: Where I should be is in the Parthenon, my greatest legacy to Athens. We need the gods' blessing. But Aspasia...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspasia's right.

speaker: Perikles
en: She often is. But not about this.

speaker: Perikles
en: Yes. I'll go inside. Thank you, Kassandra. Tell my Aspasia I was a good boy and took my drugs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perikles let me in. He took his drugs without complaint.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something wrong?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I expected Phoibe back by now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw her in the crowds outside. Did you send her somewhere?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I had her go to Anastasios to see about a ferry. As soon as Perikles is strong enough, we're leaving Athens. We have to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But now she's missing.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'm sure she's alright.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspasia, there's a plague. You've seen the streets—she's just a child.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Give her the credit she deserves—she's more of a fighter than I was at her age.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told Perikles the Cult is in Athens. It's too dangerous.

speaker: Aspasia
en: The Cult? I thought it was the sickness talking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did Perikles tell you what I said about the Cult in Athens?

speaker: Aspasia
en: This Cult! I thought it was his sickness speaking for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's true. But Phoibe's smart. She knows the way back.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I hope so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to look for her. Where is Anastasios' house?

speaker: Aspasia
en: It's across from the Odeon of Perikles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: A power I wield indeed! I told you last time I thought I could summon you when needed, and it has happened yet again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And for what this time?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: My friend here needs to be taken to the Sanctuary of Eleusis near the border of Megaris. He'll finish the trek across the border on his own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you have the power to make me come when you want, stop using it.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Oh I'll... no. That's too easy. Anyways, the power doesn't work every time, sadly. You weren't in my bed last night, no matter how many times I thought of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, do you want to lie to me now, or later?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Whatever do you mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is this "friend" of yours actually a friend? I'm not going to find out they're a wanted criminal, or they don't actually want your help, am I?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'm hurt that you'd jump straight to accusations. A good relationship must be built on trust, after all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'd rather lie than trust me.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Some things are better left unsaid, and many things are for your own protection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can protect myself. You know that.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Fine, I'll try to be more forthcoming in the future.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fuck you, Alkibiades. To get trust, you have to prove you deserve it. And you've lied to me more than once.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: You and I have different views of trust, nothing more. I've kept things to myself, but never to hurt you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right. Just remember, trust goes both ways.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'm very familiar with things that go both ways.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm always happy to help a friend of yours. Is this one drunk as well?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Not at all. And that politician was not my friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's get to it. I'm just supposed to take your friend across the border?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing else?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Carefully, if you can. Avoid roads, people... Be invisible. My friend must be kept safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make sure he's safe.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'd hoped you'd say that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friends has feet. He can walk.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Care to help my friend across the border?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Every time you ask me to do something secretly, someone dies. What is it this time?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Not everyone was born with your beautiful muscles built for... well, everything. Some of us work better by avoiding fights. This time, that's all I ask.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are lots of safe passages through these parts. Tell your friend to go alone.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: He could, but imagine if something happened, and you saved him. Imagine the things I'd do to show my gratitude.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And why do you always turn to me?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: You've proven yourself worthy. Plus, I like watching you walk away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should be on our way.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: He needs to get to the Sanctuary of Eleusis. It isn't far, although it may take you longer than usual.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It won't be a problem.

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm glad we aren't going by sea.

speaker: Civilian
en: Alkibiades told me about you. He said you're blessed by the gods.

speaker: Civilian
en: It's nice of you to help someone you don't know at all.

speaker: Civilian
en: We should stay on the safest route possible.

speaker: Civilian
en: Ah, that's better. I was starting to get sweaty under that hood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a woman!

speaker: Civilian
en: Nice of you to notice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alkibiades said

speaker: Civilian
en: Exactly what I told him to. It was safer that way. I owe Alkibiades a lot for his help, and for trusting you with my life, as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough lies. Tell me what's happening.

speaker: Civilian
en: I said I was a man so nobody would recognize me. I needed to escape my husband unseen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you trusted Alkibiades?

speaker: Civilian
en: No one escapes my husband—he'd find me. It's been... tough. I'm not sure I would have lasted much longer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, let me guess. Alkibiades owed you a favor... or now has some scheme where you owe him.

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm not sure what you mean. He didn't ask anything of me, and I've never known him to do so. I know many people he's helped at the expense of nobody but himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad I could help.

speaker: Civilian
en: Please give Alkibiades my thanks. I only wish I had more to offer him, and you, for the help. I'll never forget either of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm where I need to be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here we are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's Aletheia, waiting in Agamemnon's Tomb.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper. Come closer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aletheia.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You've discovered Agamemnon's Tomb, a place where the Heir of Memories, will find the symbol she seeks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what now?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Now is relative. With this information, will the Heir open her eyes and unlock the symbol?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She will now. So, do I just... wait here, or something?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Our task is already complete. What comes next, she must do her own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready to meet the Heir now. When will I?

speaker: Aletheia
en: You're understanding. What you do not know is that while you are yet to meet her, she already knows you very well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what do I do with the Staff?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keep it, and let it keep you. The Keeper's task is to never succumb to death. All those you will ever know, and all you will ever love, will die. Then you will learn to love again, and those will die too. But you will remain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was easy enough.

speaker: Auxesia
en: A misthios! Well, aren't you a sight to my aged eyes. Young. Energetic. Perhaps I should just pay for your body instead of your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Watch yourself. That's not my line of work.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Forgive me. I'm amazed the gods would send someone so well-suited to help me, but who is also so appealing to me physically.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All things get better with age, don't they? Even you.

speaker: Auxesia
en: The Oracle said that if I'm to live a long and happy life, I need to stay young... at heart. But I mustn't lose focus. I need your help more than your magnificent body.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad to hear it.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Koragos, my husband, is having some difficulties keeping up with my hunger for... pleasure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I imagine any man would.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Oh, I have many lovers, but he's my soulmate. When we're together, it's indescribable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then don't describe it.

speaker: Auexesia
en: When we were younger, we would run into the moonlight forest, shed our clothes, and pleasure each other until sunrise. Our howls of ecstasy would echo throughout the valleys.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods, woman, I said spare me the details.

speaker: Auxesia
en: I wasn't expecting a tough-looking mercenary to be so squeamish about a little fun.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope I'm as feisty as you at your age.

speaker: Auxesia
en: I'm feistier now than I've ever been.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does this have to do with me?

speaker: Auxesia
en: I've learned of a powerful elixir, which if consumed will give someone the vigor and stamina of Eros. If you can gather me the ingredients, I can make it for my husband.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll find the ingredients... If you promise to keep your nocturnal activities to yourself.

speaker: Auxesia
en: I have some drachmae, and Koragos has more. If you can bring me some bear scrotum and a deer tongue, I can make the elixir.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, is that all you need?

speaker: Auxesia
en: Don't worry, I'll reward you well. I'm sure Koragos will be thankful also.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find a bear near here?

speaker: Auxesia
en: I heard there's a cave near the sanctuary that a large male bear has claimed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are there any deer nearby?

speaker: Auxesia
en: This is Phokis, there's deer all over the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This elixir sounds odd. Where did you learn about it?

speaker: Auxesia
en: Why, the Pythia told me about it. She's so wise, solving a problem I didn't even know I'd have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back with the ingredients soon.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Please bring back the ingredients quickly. I miss the touch of my Koragos's fingers upon my skin.

speaker: Bear Scrotum
en: From the smell, you can tell this is a fresh scrotum from a bear. The medicinal properties of this item are still a topic of some debate amongst medical scholars.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This smells awful. Who would drink an elixir made from this?

speaker: Deer Tongue
en: This is one long and slippery deer tongue. Supposedly this grisly object can help reignite a person's passion if prepared correctly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of elixir uses ingredients like this?

speaker: Auxesia
en: Misthios, you're back. And not a moment too soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got what you asked for.

speaker: Koragos
en: Who is this, Auxesia?

speaker: Auxesia
en: This is the misthios who's going to reignite our spark, my love.

speaker: Koragos
en: Oh no! We've been going through this, I can't satisfy you anymore. You're going to kill me with your lust.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Nonsense. I'm going to make you an elixir that will give you the vigor of a man a fraction of your age.

speaker: Koragos
en: Gods save me. I cannot do this anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By all the gods, will someone just pay me? If I hear any more of this talk I'm going to be sick.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Bah! Young people. They don't understand true love. Here, this should be more than enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My thanks.

speaker: Auxesia
en: Come, Koragos. I'll mix the elixir. You get the oils ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your husband is tired. Allow me to satisfy your hunger.

speaker: Auxesia
en: I've never been with a mercenary before. Very well, let's see what you're made of.

speaker: Koragos
en: Did she... have fun?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should hold her for a few days at least.

speaker: Koragos
en: Thank you, misthios. Here, take this as payment. You've more than earned it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need any payment. I'm just glad I could help.

speaker: Auxesia
en: You are too kind, misthios. The gods have truly blessed me by crossing our paths.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You two have fun... but not too much fun.

speaker: Agis of the North
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's over there.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: This gods-forsaken helmet. I can't see anything in this stupid, good for nothing...

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: An adorer! You simply must tell me. What do you think of the helmet? I just got it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think it's alright.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: I knew it! It's ancient, but it's like it was made for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It suits you. It makes your head look even bigger than it is.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: As it should! My head is my second best feature.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever you say. You're the one who the villagers worship?

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: I don't know about worship. But they do call me Ajax.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then I'm bringing you back to Alponos. Pirates are coming, and I need someone to inspire the villagers to fight.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: Didn't you hear? Our ships were sunk by some crazed misthios. Now bandits are banditing anyone going in or out village, and there's no one to stop them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm the Eagle Bearer. Smart bandits know to stay away from me. Now let's go.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: You don't look anything like the other Eagle Bearer. Are you two a team or something?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There is no other Eagle Bearer. He's an imposter, like you.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: If I'm an imposter, what am I doing with Ajax's... I mean, my helmet?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's Ajax's helmet?

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: But of course. It gives the wearer immortality. I paid the other Eagle Bearer a fortune to find its whereabouts for me. Then, I set off to retrieve it, as any hero would. I was on my way back when

speaker: Kassandra
en: There is no other Eagle Bearer. Get that through your thick helmet!

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: Chaire, fair citizens of Alponos. Your great warrior, the eternal Ajax, has returned.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: People of Alponos, rise from your salt mills! Descend from the White Crystal Hills! Lokris is under attack!

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: The great Ajax has returned, now with the true child of Zeus - the real Eagle Bearer!

speaker: Villager
en: You are not Ajax. And that is no more the actual Eagle Bearer than the last one!

speaker: Villager
en: You are not Ajax. And that misthios squished poor old Kallipedes to bits!

speaker: Villager
en: You are not Ajax. And that new Eagle Bearer pushed sweet Nikaia off a cliff with the general's steed!

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: Nonsense. I am Ajax reborn, and we will now prove to you I am immortal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough! Prepare yourself, Lokrians. You must choose to stand and fight, or let the pirates invade and destroy your homes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough! This man is Ajax reborn.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: This'll be easier than I thought. Now, light me on fire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: It's OK. This is a magical helmet. The other Eagle Bearer told me it would protect me. You light the fire. The people will see I'm immortal, and then they will eat out of our hands. No more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: I will now endure pure flame to show you the gods bless us. The gods... want us to rise to battle. And I'll prove it by surviving Athena's wrath. Any moment now, the Eagle Bearer will light me on fire. Right?

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: Wah! It hurts! The helmet's not working! The helmet's not working!

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods. This is going to be a long day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am not lighting you on fire. That old helmet isn't magical, and you're not Ajax.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: How dare you? The last Eagle Bearer humiliated me in front of everyone, and now you are, too?

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: I will not be humiliated again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you insane? I only wanted you to rally the villagers.

speaker: Ajax the Lesser
en: My performance is more than some trick. I am Ajax immortal!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This could not have gone worse. That... That's not good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I take it you're the harbor master.

speaker: Glaukos
en: I told you, I'll pay when I get paid!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Diona sent me. She said you needed help.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Diona? Wait, wait, wait. Who are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just helping her out. She has some information I want.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Liar! I bet you want her more than you want information, don't you?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just tell me what needs to be done.

speaker: Glaukos
en: You think you can do better than I have?

speaker: Kassandra
en: As a matter of fact, I do.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Fine! You want to prove yourself to Diona, right? The military has been a real pain in the ass lately. They've captured some mercenaries who are of interest to her at the fortified warehouse. She needs you to free them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see to it, but it's going to cost you.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Ha! If you make it back alive, I'll fatten your pockets with drachmae myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deal. But first, I have some questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Freeing prisoners sounds treasonous. Why would she want to do that?

speaker: Glaukos
en: In her paranoia, the High Priestess has ordered anyone suspicious to be detained. But these prisoners were mercenaries minding their own business.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A mercenary's business is rarely their own.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Still, Diona wants them to help fight against her enemies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And let me guess, the only ones she can trust are those who can be bought with drachmae.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Exactly. Of course, she trusts me too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is Diona someone special to you?

speaker: Glaukos
en: I-I'm her lover! And I'll be the one to help her get rid of her enemies! I promised that in exchange for - Why am I telling you any of this?! I don't care what you think your relationship with her is, she's just using you. I'm her true love!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right. You keep telling yourself that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Describe these mercenaries to me.

speaker: Glaukos
en: They're all massive brutes. The kind you approach when you want things done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds familiar. I saved some earlier. As brutish as they come, and not a hair on their heads.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've got enough to go on. You better get my drachmae ready.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Come back when you're done. If you make it out of the camp alive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's over there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is!

speaker: Greek Brute
en: I won't die here, misthios. Let me out!

speaker: Greek Brute
en: Get me out of here. Quick, before the guards return!

speaker: Greek Brute
en: They'll execute me! I did nothing wrong!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've freed the prisoners at the military camp.

speaker: Glaukos
en: There were three of them, did you get them all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, three of them in all their balding glory.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Guess you're more useful than you look. In that case, Diona needs one more task fulfilled. A man needs to die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm listening.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Diona's enemies have forces on Chytra Atoll. They're going to use it as a staging area to launch attacks on Kythera. You need to exterminate these pests.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to go alone to an island swarming with enemies?

speaker: Glaukos
en: Oh, is that too hard a task for Diona's new champion?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tread lightly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will wipe the enemy off the face of that island.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Your humility is moving, misthios. But I wouldn't underestimate them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, it's you who underestimates me.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Enough pointless chatter! She needs you to take out the captain there. His men should disperse after that. But, still, leave none alive. Will you do it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The captain? I slayed a very... flamboyantly dressed man earlier by a shipwreck.

speaker: Glaukos
en: That sounds like him. All that peacocking, no doubt to catch Diona's eye. Here, take your payment and go. I have no need for you anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hold on. You've been fighting for Diona against the Cult. Tell me everything you know about them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Consider it done. What more can you tell me?

speaker: Glaukos
en: What more could you possibly need? Just kill the man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any idea where I can find the captain?

speaker: Glaukos
en: That rat should be somewhere around the shipwreck off the north coast of Chytra Atoll. I led a small party that managed to maroon his ship, but we couldn't finish the job. He and his men will be on their guard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is the quickest way to Chytra Atoll?

speaker: Glaukos
en: Sail south from the southern tip of Kythera until you come across a shipwreck.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what you know about the Cult.

speaker: Glaukos
en: What Cult?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Isn't the captain a Cultist?

speaker: Glaukos
en: He could be a malákas god for all I care. Diona says he wants to destroy her for rejecting him. That the only way for us to be together is if I remove him from the picture. Aren't you here for the same reason? To win her over?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's already mine. And after I slay the captain, which you failed to do, you'll be forgotten.

speaker: Glaukos
en: You couldn't have done it without my help! Diona will appreciate all I've done for her! She can't just— J-Just forget about me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be sure she does.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Truth be told, her sister is more my type.

speaker: Glaukos
en: You better not let Diona hear that. She's a jealous one. She's spent her life living in her sister's shadow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why isn't Diona the High Priestess?

speaker: Glaukos
en: Because all anyone cares about is who's the first born.

speaker: Kassandra
en: True.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to dismantle the Cult of Kosmos. I have no time or interest in the Priestess.

speaker: Glaukos
en: You can't fool me with your "Cult" bullshit. No one can resist Diona's charm. And no one would ever call themselves that. Malákas "Cult of Kosmos."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all I need to know.

speaker: Glaukos
en: We'll send a fat amount of drachmae to your ship when you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Excellent.

speaker: Glaukos
en: Go! Get out of here! And don't you go talking to Diona anymore!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or what?

speaker: Glaukos
en: Or I'll—Ugh, just go!

speaker: Kassandra
en: These don't look like Cult members. Probably just well-paid mercenaries.

speaker: Always Vengeance
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Lysander
en: We'll not be outmaneuvered by the Athenians the way the Persians did to Leonidas.

speaker: Lysander
en: You're not one of my soldiers. You better have a good reason for being here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need a reason, good or otherwise.

speaker: Lysander
en: Ah. Some bite to you, is there?

speaker: Kassandra
en: More than some cowering dog.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We Spartans stand together. So here I am.

speaker: Lysander
en: Yes. Spartan blood matters most.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like this victory will bring you glory.

speaker: Lysander
en: The rewards of skill and effort!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's the Spartan way.

speaker: Lysander
en: From slave to general, bathing in the blood of this war, while our leaders stuff their faces and preen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The polemarchs believe it's an easy victory.

speaker: Lysander
en: I will end this war in my favor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have a strategy?

speaker: Lysander
en: Athenian polemarchs are paralyzed with indecision. They serve too many masters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Making them slow to react.

speaker: Lysander
en: And that's where you come in. Infiltrate their forts and kill their polemarchs. I need the way clear for my troops.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do my part. Consider the commanders already dead.

speaker: Lysander
en: Bring me their Athenian seals as proof. You'll be rewarded for your efforts.

speaker: Lysander
en: The blood of the enemy will show our leaders that my strategy is the right one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These seals should help convince them.

speaker: Lysander
en: You've done well. Our troops are on the move.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They underestimate Spartans.

speaker: Lysander
en: They consider me much lower than a Spartan.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: It'll be a disaster, a disaster I tell you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Calm down. What are you talking about?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: My masterpiece! it will change everything—amuse, astound, titillate, and open people's eyes to Kleon's machinations! But I need you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm no actor or poet, Aristophanes.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: By the gods, no! it's Thespis. My leading man is missing! A play with no star is no play at all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know he's missing?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: He never misses a rehearsal... unless he's drunk, or with a woman... or a man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Could be anything, then?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: No, he knows how important this is. He wouldn't let me down... Something must be wrong!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You could just get another actor.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Oh, no. Thespis always draws a huge crowd for his performances. The more people who experience my blistering indictment of Kleon, the better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So where would I find him?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Thespis usually doesn't go far from his home. You'd best start there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This shouldn't take long. Prepare the show, and I'll be back as soon as I find him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be Thespis' house.

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: Come on, come on. It's got to be here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't look like an actor, unless you're playing an Athenian guard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hush. I'm going to ask some questions, and you're going to answer.

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: But Commander Rhexenor...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's your name?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: Bulis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well Bulis, it's your choice whether you walk out of here. Do you understand?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: Yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me, what are you looking for?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: Some stupid play. They don't tell me anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Play?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: I just do what I'm told, and they told me to destroy the manuscript.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What have you done with Thespis?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: Some of the boys are meant to keep him drunk in the tavern down the street.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'd better be telling me everything.

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: All I know is they wanted to keep this actor busy. See for yourself—he's at the tavern.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're sure that's all?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: I just follow the Commander's orders. I don't ask questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, but you can't be trusted to live.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do something worthwhile and join my crew. You're loyal, and you follow orders.

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: You'd take me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you say?

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: To get away from Athens... Thank you, thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get out of here, and count yourself lucky.

speaker: Athenian Guard
en: Thank you, thank you...

speaker: Thespis
en: ...And then I saids to him, if this is your wife, why did she charge me?! I'd loves to stay, but my cup's drained, and I'm to perform tomorrow.

speaker: Andras
en: Another drink! Come, one more tale. The night is young...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think he's had enough.

speaker: Andras
en: And what business is it of yours, friend?

speaker: Thespis
en: Yeah, was business... Oh, look at you!

speaker: Andras
en: You'd best be leaving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for his employer, Aristophanes.

speaker: Andras
en: So? He's not working now.

speaker: Thespis
en: Yes! I's not working... I like him though. Aristophanes, funny man... buts opinions. Told him it's dangerous.

speaker: Andras
en: That it is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need him sober and rested.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just here for Thespis. He's drunk, and I need to get him home.

speaker: Andras
en: What are you, his mater?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's say extended family.

speaker: Andras
en: I don't think you understand the situation. Commander Rhexenor's orders are he's not to leave.

speaker: Thespis
en: I saids I'd stay... Don't want trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go take your boys somewhere else.

speaker: Andras
en: You'll regret that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get going—from your smell, you already know where the goat pens are. I'm sure they miss you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you don't want to leave with your heads stuffed up your asses, you'll go now.

speaker: Andras
en: We'll be seeing you, misthios. The Commander's not a man to be messed with.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No need for jealousy, just because your mother was a goat. Like mother, like kid.

speaker: Andras
en: You need to die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I sometimes wonder if leaving Kephallonia was a good idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me Thespis, and I'll give you something in return. I'm sure we can come to an arrangement.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, for your troubles. I'll look after him now.

speaker: Andras
en: Huh, a fool and his drachmae... Very well, you won't see us again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Take this and get out of my sight.

speaker: Andras
en: Do you think we're farmers that can be bought for beans? Take your money and stick it up your ass.

speaker: Andras
en: We'll be seeing you, misthios. The Commander's not a man to be messed with.

speaker: Thespis
en: I's not feeling too good...

speaker: Thespis
en: He said you're behind a mask—you'll be perfectly safe, he saids... You's sooo strong, Aikaterine. Wheee, giddy ups! My parents said you'll be either an actor or a drunk... Ha, fooled them.
