I becames both! Told him, Kleon will kill us all. It's more assaults than satire! The sausage seller was my idea! Then I will... I will... gather my... what was it again? Oh yes... sausages! Mmm... sausages... Let me tell you a secret... It's a good one... I uh... I forget. Listen to me... I love you. I do.

speaker: Thespis
en: Thank you, but you can go no further... For I know true love!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just need you ready to perform tomorrow.

speaker: Thespis
en: Of course, and I just need my muse... My love! I can't, I won't perform without her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You will perform.

speaker: Thespis
en: Uh-uh, not with out Aikaterine, a divine name for a divine body... I mean being.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those men in the tavern... Who were they?

speaker: Thespis
en: Oh, the admirers. Harmless really... And I do like a man in uniform.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You need to sober up. This play's important.

speaker: Thespis
en: So's Aikaterine! I need my muse.

speaker: Thespis
en: Please? She's just west of here at the House of Aphrodite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it means you'll do the play, I'll find your muse.

speaker: Andras
en: Going to enjoy this. I'll mess that pretty face right up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No need for jealousy, just because your mother was a goat. Like mother, like kid.

speaker: Andras
en: You need to die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can't we come to some arrangement here?

speaker: Andras
en: I'd never make an arrangement with you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're wasting my time.

speaker: Andras
en: You need to die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I sometimes wonder if leaving Kephallonia was a good idea.

speaker: Markos
en: Ah! Here you are, and not a moment too soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cyclops is more important than a bowyer. We need to talk.

speaker: Markos
en: Precisely what I was thinking! Let's hope Drucilla has a good sense of humor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well? Your plan?

speaker: Markos
en: Right! The Cyclops and I have a score of drachmae to settle. The same score as you, my rough-and-tumble friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He wouldn't be after me if it wasn't for you, "my friend."

speaker: Markos
en: Heh, right. But—I swear—this will put an end to it! If he insists on sending his goons after us, we'll make sure his last good day was yesterday.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's hear it then. What do I have to do?

speaker: Markos
en: What will we do, you mean! As the brains to your brawn, I consider it a joint effort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course you do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not a war, it's a pissing match.

speaker: Markos
en: You know just how to hurt me, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not that hard, trust me.

speaker: Markos
en: Think! What does the Cyclops value most? His men, his land, his ships? No. His obsidian eye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get to the point, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: Oh, fine. We're going to steal it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you crazy? You borrow his drachmae, then you steal his eye?

speaker: Markos
en: Having it means we win. Then, it goes to market. We kill two birds with one obsidian eye!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'd better hold still, or he'll lose both eyes.

speaker: Markos
en: No, no! It has to be done without the Cyclops knowing. You cannot be seen!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then my new bow will come in handy.

speaker: Markos
en: He keeps the eye in his house—it's too valuable to wear out. A wise choice, until you show him the error of his ways. Wait for the sun to set, sneak in, and then! Bring me the eye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Better be worth something.

speaker: Markos
en: Do you know how much obsidian goes for on Kephallonia?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never seen it.

speaker: Markos
en: Exactly. And not only is it obsidian, it's veined with gold. Gold! It's no wonder he saves it for special occasions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So we'll use the profits to pay him off?

speaker: Markos
en: It'll pay for the bulk of it—a vineyard's expensive, you know!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know where the Cyclops lives.

speaker: Markos
en: Keep to the west side of the island... There, you will find his lair.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. But you won't get away with being cheap.

speaker: Markos
en: Cheap? You wound me, Kassandra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's your defining trait.

speaker: Markos
en: Bring me the eye, and I'll prove you wrong. Remember! Not a soul can see you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Got it.

speaker: Markos
en: Pull this off, and our heads won't be the Cyclops's trophies when he comes back!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now to find the eye. If it's as valuable as Markos says, it'll be hidden.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hello, eye. I see you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need cover. If I'm quiet, I can hide in the bushes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Malaka! Must be some eye to have that much protection. I have to stay out of view.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By Zeus, the Cyclops doesn't mess around.

speaker: Markos
en: Ai! Be careful!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know how many of his guards were there? All for a fucking rock...

speaker: Markos
en: Aiyee! Someone do something! Where's a misthios when you need one? My beloved silos! My darlings!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shit. I should take care of that.

speaker: Markos
en: Ai! Be careful!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know how many of his guards were there?

speaker: Markos
en: Considering how many showed up here, yes! What did I say about being seen? At least you taught them a lesson.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All for a fucking rock...

speaker: Markos
en: This "rock" could buy a house, my friend!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And yet, it's still not enough to pay back the Cyclops.

speaker: Markos
en: Oh, don't be upset! Think of all the fun we've had!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right. Your fun, my blood. You can't keep dragging me into things, Markos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cyclops is going to kill us, Markos. It's as simple as that. And there's nothing fun about it.

speaker: Markos
en: This will work, I promise you! Would I lie to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't make me answer that.

speaker: Markos
en: Take the eye—but don't sell it yet! No vendor would believe we came by it lawfully. They know exactly who it belongs to!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine.

speaker: Markos
en: Better your pocket than his socket!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think that's enough for one day. Chaire, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: W-wait! I saw a boat! One I've never seen before!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So?

speaker: Markos
en: The vessel's too good for this dirty town. It must be the Cyclops—and he brought friends!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's back? I can never catch a break, can I?

speaker: Markos
en: Take them out, and that's one less thing to deal with! Besides—these strangers look rich as Kroisos—the Cyclops pays them well! It's win-win, my friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It can't hurt. What do I have to lose?

speaker: Markos
en: You? You're a winner if I ever saw one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then where are they?

speaker: Markos
en: In an abandoned house on the eastern coast. Who knows what golden fortunes shine in their hideout? Send them to Hades, then loot them for all they have... We'll be rich!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The eastern coast. Can you be more specific?

speaker: Markos
en: I think they've settled in an abandoned house. By a small forest—south of Sami!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So if these visitors aren't from Kephallonia, where did they come from?

speaker: Markos
en: All I know if Kephallonia will be the last place they'll ever see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm keeping some of these "golden fortunes," though. No negotiations.

speaker: Markos
en: Not even a drachma for the man who sent you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The rest goes to pay your debt. These are my terms.

speaker: Markos
en: Oh, fine, fine! Now, teach those strangers what it means to be Kephallonian: draw blood, or bleed.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: This is incredible. The knowledge stored here is overwhelming. It will take me years to decipher it all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about sealing Atlantis... Have you found a way to do it?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Oh... Yes, yes I think so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well? What is it?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: The staff, the staff is the key.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. It's time.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I can't. Not yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can't stay here, we don't have the time.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: There is so much to learn. With this knowledge, we can turn the tide of fate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That is not your destiny. You said so yourself. You're losing sight of what's important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the staff is the key to this place, I don't want to get locked in.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I can't hand it over yet. There's still so much to see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That wasn't the plan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen to yourself—you've gone mad. You need to accept some knowledge was not meant to be had.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Knowledge is power—the only power worth having.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At what cost?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I will not be ordered around or lectured by you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was your plan to seal this place, and I agreed to help.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: That was before I realized what we could uncover about the First Civilization—the creation of humankind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We are sealing this place to keep the Cult from using it to enslave humanity. That is bigger than your quest for knowledge.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: The Cult will be nothing but an insect to swat once the power is ours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's too dangerous to leave this place open, and you know it.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: You wouldn't understand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your pride will cost us all in the end.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: It's not about pride.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What good is knowledge if you curse all of humanity in the process? It's what you wanted to avoid in the first place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sometimes it's better if we find our own path. We are not ready for the power this place offers.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: You're right. I cannot save humanity directly, but I can save it from itself.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: This is your burden now. Humanity's fate will be decided by the choices you make.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I understand.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Choose wisely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me the staff. You have to—for the sake of everyone.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: The knowledge contained in here could fix everything for generations to come. I can't just walk away from that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What good is knowledge if there's no one around to use it?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Leave if you must, but I will not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not going without the staff.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I may be old, but I'm not as weak as I appear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give up the staff.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: The knowledge is mine. Mine.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I will not let you have it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have it! I want it destroyed!

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Liar!

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Pathetic! You were supposed to be better than this. Bigger than this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will be whatever I want to be.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: A misthios? A common thug? You are an embarrassment to yourself, and to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough!

speaker: Pythagoras
en: This is my chance to make things right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. It isn't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's over. Give me the staff.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: You do not deserve the infinite knowledge of our creators.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the point. Nobody does.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: No!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlantis is too dangerous. I must seal it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods. What happened here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was savage... Done to send a message.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad Phoibe wasn't here. Hopefully she's safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos must be carrying through on his threat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe! No! Hey! Stop!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe! No, no, no, no, no. Ela, ela. (Come, come.)

speaker: Kassandra
en: Earth, mother of all, I greet you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aniazo. (I grieve/mourn.)

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Kassandra! Are you all right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to speak to Aspasia.

speaker: Sokrates
en: We must find Perikles first. He's missing

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't fucking care! Tell me where Aspasia is!

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry... Phoibe.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Aspasia went to find Perikles at the Parthenon. She should be there.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I think we'd better go with her.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I agree, my friend. I agree.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never would've guessed you were a lover.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Well, I wasn't. My theory—that all atoms exist with a great void between them—s a bit like the life I've lived.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But not anymore. Now you're filling that void.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Maybe... maybe what fills the void, and what draws us together, is love.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Save that line for the poet, Demokritos. It's a good one.

speaker: Demokritos
en: You think so? All right, I will!

speaker: Demokritos
en: No! That's her! Those bandits... Stop them!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Demokritos... I'm sorry.

speaker: Demokritos
en: They killed her. For it to end like this... after all this time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have your theorem, and the others... read them to her. Let her see your poetry.

speaker: Demokritos
en: It's too late.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's never too late.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone's going to find us here and think we did this. Demokritos... we have to go.

speaker: Demokritos
en: I... I left once before, I won't leave again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Demokritos, please.

speaker: Demokritos
en: You can go. In another life... she might've known my love for her. You might have been my student. Imagine the happiness we'd have known.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A wise man told me, "The richest person in any land is the one who wants for the least." Don't want for the past, Demokritos.

speaker: Demokritos
en: I'll leave soon enough. But for now, I think I want for privacy. Take this, and leave me to mourn, Kassandra.

speaker: Demokritos
en: There is no force in the universe greater than that which binds two people together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Can I help you with anything?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I picked up your message from the board. What's happening?

speaker: Woman
en: You think you're so incredible, don't you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Woman
en: You play hero for the Spartan army in Megaris, and now you think you can do anything. Can't believe the town is asking me to build a statue of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What I did couldn't have been achieved by some Malákas like you. Glad to hear I'm finally getting some recognition.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did what had to be done. A statue may be... overdoing it.

speaker: Woman
en: Before I agree to making some statue in your honor, I want you to do something for the people. There's a pack of wolves that's been harassing my village. You want to be a real hero? Now's your chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wolves, huh?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, real wolves. Not just some self-important Spartan in a silly helmet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me guess, you want me to hunt the wolves?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, all of them must be gutted. Do you accept?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in.

speaker: Woman
en: You're truly brave, mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra

en: That doesn't take anything away from the tragedy. She was a special girl.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That doesn't matter. She had to sacrifice herself for others, over and over...

speaker: Aspasia
en: And those who sacrifice themselves deserve more glory than any other. She is a hero in her own right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope she knew that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a tragedy. She should be here.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Of course she should. But you know the cost of living this life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do. But did Phoibe?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe was killed. By Cult guards. Before I could get to her.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Oh, no. Dear Phoibe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She died alone in the street.

speaker: Aspasia
en: No, you found her—she wasn't alone. I know how much of a friend she was to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't let them get away with this.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You have to fight. For her.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Aspasia, you're here.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Any sign of Perikles?

speaker: Aspasia
en: If he's here, he's inside praying. He refused to stay safe in the villa.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Things have gotten even worse in the agora. It's madness.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Speak later and act now. Perikles

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go!

speaker: Deimos
en: I'm going to destroy everything you ever created. Athens is mine.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Perikles

speaker: Deimos
en: Stay out of my way!

speaker: Aspasia
en: All is lost now.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: He was a great man. Perhaps greater than we even knew.

speaker: Sokrates
en: We need to get her out of Athens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll take my ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We have to leave. Don't let him in die in vain.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Never.

speaker: Aspasia
en: We have to move quickly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay close. Just in case.

speaker: Athenian Strategos
en: Stop!

speaker: Athenian Strategos
en: Kleon has ordered that no one leave Athens. And he wants Aspasia brought to him.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'm not going.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave!

speaker: Athenian Strategos
en: Don't let them go!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all clear now. Let's go.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: We're going to stay, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Why?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: My work is here. I can't leave the Athenians in the state they're in.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You don't need us to protect Aspasia. Leave Athens to us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The city has been taken. This isn't the Athens you used to know.

speaker: Sokrates
en: That is why I must stay. We must begin again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You saw what happened to Perikles. You want the same to happen to you?

speaker: Sokrates
en: If every dissenting voice disappears, the people won't turn against him. They need me here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're sure?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I have lived as an Athenian, and I will die as an Athenian.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then do something for me. Both of you.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Retrieve Phoibe's body. Give her a proper burial.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Everything she deserves and more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Time to go, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And I expect to see you both again—alive.

speaker: Aspasia
en: The farther we get from Athens, the quieter it grows. As though it's peaceful. But I know better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, Aspasia. About Perikles. And Athens.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You have no need to apologize. For anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did everything I could to keep people safe.

speaker: Aspasia
en: No one thinks otherwise, Kassandra. The Cult of Kosmos simply had a plan we didn't see soon enough. And they struck when the time was right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It feels like... I let everyone down. I didn't get to them quick enough. Didn't make the right decisions.

speaker: Aspasia
en: It's not your fault. There's no one to blame but the Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: About Phoibe...

speaker: Aspasia
en: No, allow me. Phoibe was my responsibility. I should have kept her closer to me. It was a mistake.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, I wanted to apologize. It wasn't your fault. I'm sorry.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Yet another murder to the Cult's credit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make each of them beg for mercy before I kill them.

speaker: Aspasia
en: That time will come. For now, let us look to the future. Do you have a heading?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was hoping you would help me with that.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Yes, of course. This woman...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoenix. Her ship was called Siren Song.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Phoenix. Yes, I know the name. Last anyone heard, her ship was docked on the island of Naxos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then, we go to Naxos... to see Phoenix.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you two doing here?

speaker: Barnabas
en: You know us—always on your tail. Old Herodotos couldn't wait to see you.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I told you, Barnabas, Thera is said to hold a secret. A secret no one can fathom.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Yes, but a lost world?

speaker: Herodotos
en: It's perfectly possible—Atlantis may exist.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Sounds like hooey to me. But he's insistent about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos is right. Atlantis exists.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Incredible!

speaker: Herodotos
en: I-it's true? I can't believe it. Tell me everything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll tell you some day. It's too complicated for small talk.

speaker: Barnabas
en: It's not me, is it? I've proven I'm very competent!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm exhausted, Barnabas.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Ignore him. When you're ready, I'm all ears. I need every last detail.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mother sent me here to meet my real father. You know... Pythagoras? It's him.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Your father was living in a volcano?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Pythagoras?! That's unthinkable—it would make him immortal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He had a staff that belonged to the Ancient Civilization.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It kept him alive all this time... Makes perfect sense.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well, where is he? Invite him along—he's your father after all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He was a stubborn man. He wanted to keep all the knowledge of Atlantis to himself.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Huh, stubborn. I suppose that trait runs in the family.

speaker: Herodotos
en: He means he's sorry for your loss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But none of this can ever pass your lips. This stays between us.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You have my word.

speaker: Herodotos
en: But the world needs to know! We could tell the most amazing tale of our time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos...

speaker: Herodotos
en: Oh, fine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then it's settled. Let's move forward.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Like always.

speaker: Barnabas
en: We've learned a lot, haven't we, you know-it-all?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Speak for yourself—I'm on the hunt for truth. Gods know not all your myths are accurate.

speaker: Barnabas
en: They come from the gods themselves, who are the most reliable sources we have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For all we know, anything's possible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've both been a great help to me. It doesn't matter who's right or wrong.

speaker: Barnabas
en: And you would know, as the eagle-bearing demi-god you are.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Perhaps she, too, is immortal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure I am.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I do know one thing for certain. This has been an odyssey I won't forget.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These don't look like Cult members. Probably just well-paid mercenaries.

speaker: Mercenary Correspondence
en: We'll cover Boura. Aias will work with the soldiers and their Polemarch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: More mercenaries sent by the Tempest. Must be some bounty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The statue. It's gone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It must only work at night. I should come back after dark.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Another challenger. I hope you're more resilient than the last one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods! The statue came alive!

speaker: Sphinx
en: I am no statue, child. If you cannot comprehend what stands before you, how are you to entertain me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you?

speaker: Sphinx
en: The Sphinx. The guardian of truth and knowledge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you here?

speaker: Sphinx
en: The gods sent me to protect something, and I've been its guardian ever since.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I—I came here for another reason.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Oh? Then tell me, little one. Why are you here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come to end you and take your power.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Many before you have tried. All have failed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't.

speaker: Sphinx
en: While it would amuse me to see you try, harming me will not give you what you seek. The only way to acquire the power I possess is to impress me with your mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds simple enough.

speaker: Sphinx
en: If you are correct, I will surrender that which I guard. If you are wrong, I shall end you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You protect an object of great power. I have been asked to return it to where it belongs.

speaker: Sphinx
en: A most noble of causes. Sadly I cannot grant your request.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's too much at stake. I won't leave without it.

speaker: Sphinx
en: The power I guard is not for the weak-willed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can resist.

speaker: Sphinx
en: One must risk everything in the pursuit of knowledge. If you can answer my questions wisely, you will have proven yourself worthy.

speaker: Sphinx
en: What is always old and sometimes new; never sad, sometimes blue; never empty, but sometimes full; never pushes, always pulls?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The moon.

speaker: Sphinx
en: An interesting choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The tide.

speaker: Sphinx
en: How fascinating you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sky.

speaker: Sphinx
en: That is a bold choice.

speaker: Sphinx
en: This thing all things devour: birds, beasts, trees, flowers; gnaws iron, bites steel; grinds hard stones to meal; slays kings, ruins towns; and beats high mountains down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Armies.

speaker: Sphinx
en: This is most entertaining.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I'm impressed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nature.

speaker: Sphinx
en: How fascinating.

speaker: Sphinx
en: In spring I am gay in handsome array; in summer more clothing I wear; when colder it grows, I fling off my clothes; and in winter quite naked appear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a tree.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Impressive, little one. Most impressive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a goat.

speaker: Sphinx
en: That's one way to look at it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a mountain.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Only time will tell.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Never resting, never still; moving silently from hill to hill; it does not walk, run, or trot; all is cool where it is not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The wind.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You do amuse me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's the sun.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Your perception is admirable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The rain.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I wonder why you chose that?

speaker: Sphinx
en: What can run, but never walks; has a mouth, but never talks; has a head, but never weeps; has a bed, but never sleeps?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A chariot.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You do amuse me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A child.

speaker: Sphinx
en: An interesting choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A river.

speaker: Sphinx
en: That could be.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I create my lair with earthen string, and dispatch my prey with a biting sting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A snake.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I wonder what led you to choose that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A wasp.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You do amuse me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A spider.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Good thinking, little one.

speaker: Sphinx
en: As small as your thumb, I am light in the air. You may hear me before you see me, but trust that I'm there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A hummingbird.

speaker: Sphinx
en: How clever you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A mosquito.

speaker: Sphinx
en: A likely answer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A bumblebee.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Perhaps.

speaker: Sphinx
en: What can bring back the dead; make you cry, make you laugh, make you young; is born in an instant, yet lasts a lifetime?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Memories.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You're full of surprises.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Names.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I can see your reasoning.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Jokes.

speaker: Sphinx
en: That is a bold choice.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Some try to hide, some try to cheat; but time will show, we always will meet. Try as you might to guess my name; I promise you'll know, when you I do claim.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Destiny.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I wonder why you chose that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time.

speaker: Sphinx
en: A keen mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Death.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Well done, mortal.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I'm alive, but without breath; I'm as cold in life as in death; I'm never thirsty, though I always drink.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a jellyfish.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I see your logic.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a fish.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You're highly perceptive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a crocodile.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Such imagination.

speaker: Sphinx
en: What is large, yet never grows; has roots that cannot be seen; and is taller than trees?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A city.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You're sharp, for a human.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A mountain.

speaker: Sphinx
en: How fascinating.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A forest.

speaker: Sphinx
en: This is most entertaining.

speaker: Sphinx
en: At night they come without being fetched, and by day they are lost without being stolen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sun.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I expected no less.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The moon.

speaker: Sphinx
en: I can see the wisdom in that answer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The stars.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You're a wise one.

speaker: Sphinx
en: You are an interesting one. Now, take what you have learned and touch the symbols that reflect your choices.

speaker: Unknown
en: ...Outwit our oppressors, hide our truth within lies...

speaker: Prize of the Sphinx
en: An ancient Artifact taken from the remains of the Sphinx. The sphere glows with barely contained power.

speaker: Sphinx
en: Like those who came before, you have failed.

en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Menalkas
en: Great and terrible Eagle Bearer, why did you burn my farm?! You are no god, no here. Your touch turns all to ash!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The world is full of pain and mysteries. I did not mean to harm you, but... I'm sorry you were hurt.

speaker: Menalkas
en: Why have you forsaken me, Eagle Bearer?! What have I done to offend all the powers on Olympos? How can I redeem myself?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Forsaken you? I don't think we've ever met.

speaker: Menalkas
en: Eh? Who? You? You!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, me. Tell me what's wrong.

speaker: Menalkas
en: I have been cursed by the gods! They speak to me all day and night, filling my head with visions and fears. I cannot work, and my crops wither.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did the gods curse you?

speaker: Menalkas
en: I do not know what I did. I've heard the voices of the gods, day and night, since I took over the farm after my father passed. The voices won't let me sleep nor rest, and the farm is so much work!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is the curse?

speaker: Menalkas
en: The gods speak of terrifying things. That the sky will open and drown the fields and my farm. That dark writhing things will come from the ground and feast on my crops and on my flesh. That the earth will open and swallow us whole.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take a look around the farm and see if I can find out what has befallen you.

speaker: Menalkas
en: Thank you, Eagle Bearer! You are of Olympos! They will listen to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perhaps. But first I must determine if this truly is the work of the gods, or if your plight is of a more earthly nature.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These vases were dedicated to the gods. If Menalkas broke them, the gods might be angered. Demeter and Dionysos might have sickened his crops and polluted his mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look at this little guy. These offerings look abandoned and long neglected. Not a good way to honor Demeter or Zeus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. These crops stink... Could that rot affect the mind? I wonder if all the crops in the silo are the same.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The water in this pot reeks like the Styx. Maybe the disease is seeping into the water. This seems like an earthly cause, not a sign of the gods.

speaker: Civilian
en: Menalkas is a sad case. Thinks he's been cursed by the powers that be. I told him that's ridiculous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why ridiculous?

speaker: Civilian
en: Because if you wanted to punish him, you'd just smite him, or have an eagle fly down and eat his eyes, or the like. You wouldn't curse his harvest. Of course not. You're the Eagle Bearer, Arrow of Artemis, Shield of Athena, Child of Zeus. Not the Mistress of Blighted Crops. That's beneath you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So Menalkas's problems are caused by...?

speaker: Civilian
en: Some kind of sickness in the crops. That's what's making him crazy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I've seen everything. Is Menalkas affected by the gods, or is there a more earthly cause to his illness? I should talk to him.

speaker: Menalkas
en: Eagle Bearer, do you know why the gods have cursed me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think some infestation has taken root in your crops and is polluting your mind.

speaker: Menalkas
en: What do we do?! How do we appease the gods?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This has nothing to do with the gods. I will set fire to the silo where you keep your harvest and burn out the rot to clear your mind.

speaker: Menalkas
en: I... I hope you are right, Eagle Bearer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have been cursed because you didn't show proper respect, and let sacred artifacts fall into ruin.

speaker: Menalkas
en: What must I do to appease Cthonic Demeter and Stygian Persephone?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need a big sacrifice to get their attention. I'll burn the silo that holds your harvest as a sign of your devotion.

speaker: Menalkas
en: If... If you think that is best, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do not doubt me!

speaker: Menalkas
en: All that work, gone to smoke!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one said it would be easy.

speaker: Menalkas
en: It had to be done. I confess, I do feel a bit better already. Thank you for all your help and guidance.

speaker: Pandaros
en: Help! Come help me!

speaker: Pandaros
en: You've got to free me before those vultures peck my eyes out! Not to mention the wolves! I saw them in the bushes earlier.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You called me "misthios" – you must know my help comes at a price. You don't look like you're in much of a... position to pay.

speaker: Pandaros
en: W-wait! Hear me out! The people who did this to me – they took everything I had and left me for dead! They've got plenty of other treasures and trinkets at their hideouts, too! Free me, and I'll tell you where to find them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean the treasure at the Follower of Ares hideout?

speaker: Pandaros
en: O-oh.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The treasure underwater? Yeah, I got it all. What else do you have to offer?

speaker: Pandaros
en: Well, no, there's more!

speaker: Pandaros
en: Quick, misthios! Untie me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Malákes wolves!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're alive and free. Now tell me about my reward.

speaker: Pandaros
en: Those malákes took my only prized possession. A family heirloom–an amulet handed down from my mother. They keep their spoils underwater in a cave just west of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Which on of the thugs took your amulet?

speaker: Pandaros
en: The "leader,"—a burly man with a huge axe wears it now. Take his head, and the amulet is yours to keep.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who left you like this?

speaker: Pandaros
en: The Followers of Ares! I joined them thinking I could get rich quick. But the sacrifices and murders, misthios... It's terrible. I tried to sneak away with some of their stuff

speaker: Kassandra
en: And got caught.

speaker: Pandaros
en: You've got to kill them all, misthios. They're crazy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You deserted the Followers of Ares and expect to live? What's your plan?

speaker: Pandaros
en: I assumed I'd become carrion. But wait! Maybe...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't like the sound of this.

speaker: Pandaros
en: How... how about I work for you? I know how to fight! The Followers of Ares gave me that much, at least. What do you say?

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK, you work for me now. I don't see much value in you... but it's better than nothing.

speaker: Pandaros
en: I'll see you back at your ship then, Commander.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not before putting on some clothes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have no need for the likes of you. Go, malákas! Or I'll take care of you like I did the wolves.

speaker: Pandaros
en: Y-yes! Right away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let the hunt begin.

speaker: Pandaros
en: Thank you, misthios! Knowing that they are dead will help me sleep easier.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here we are.

speaker: Mercenary
en: This amulet will work perfectly. My love will look beautiful in this.

speaker: Heirloom Amulet
en: This amulet was apparently passed down from generation to generation as a precious family heirloom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the amulet the naked man was going on about. Looks expensive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean this amulet?

speaker: Pandaros
en: Why, yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are there any other valuables?

speaker: Pandaros
en: Uh...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not called freedom because it's free. I'd say you owe me for my services.

speaker: Pandaros
en: How... how about I work for you? I know how to fight! The Followers of Ares gave me that much, at least. What do you say?

en: OK, you work for me now. I don't see much value in you... but it's better than nothing.

en: I'll see you back at your ship then, Commander.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not before putting on some clothes!

en: I have no need for the likes of you. Go, malákas! Or I'll take care of you like I did the wolves.

speaker: Pandaros
en: Y-yes! Right away.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Hey, over here! Come on!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Welcome to the Olympics! Breathe in. Can you not taste the excitement in the air?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you going to be like this the whole time we're here?

speaker: Barnabas
en: By the gods, yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll try and win quickly then.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Come now. You must be feeling something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just having fun with you. Who wouldn't be impressed?

speaker: Barnabas
en: It is a place of immortal glory—you can be sure Hera and Zeus will be watching your performance closely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, no pressure, then.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Forget that for the moment, and let's enjoy the sights and see what Olympia has to offer.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Isn't this magnificent?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's certainly impressive. Though I'm sad we'll be missing the chariot races.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Oh, what I would have given to see that!

speaker: Barnabas
en: We should take in the sights and praise the gods to be here at such a time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Which sights should we see?

speaker: Barnabas
en: There're so many! Let me think... The Temple of Zeus, the Altar of Zeus, and of course, the Olympic Tree.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have fun Barnabas—I'll catch up with you later.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enjoying the Olympics so far?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Even more than I imagined. There's so much to see and do!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should make an offering to Zeus for good luck in the Games.

speaker: Barnabas
en: To think I would see such an offering to the gods in Olympia itself...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never seen anything like this.

speaker: Barnabas
en: And this is nothing! On the final day the mageiros will slaughter a hundred bulls for the hecatomb to honor Zeus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ugh, I think I've had enough of the stench of offal and burned meat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could eat.

speaker: Barnabas
en: But that's not for people like us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong with people like us?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hey, give me some of that meat. The gods won't miss it.

speaker: Butcher
en: I won't anger the gods for your belly. Get lost.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My friend here would like to savor your offering. I have the drachmae.

speaker: Butcher
en: Won't say no to some extra drachmae.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Mmm, delicious. Thank you, my friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gladly. I know how much this all means to you.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well then, I think we've spent enough time here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Agreed. Let's go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about the Altar of Zeus?

speaker: Barnabas
en: We've already been.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All these things with Zeus in the name—I get confused!

speaker: Barnabas
en: It's Olympia. What do you expect?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're in Olympia. It's only fitting we visit the Temple of Zeus.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I heard it's one of the wonders of the world—and sculpted by your friend, Phidias!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd hardly say friend. Even acquaintance might be pushing it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Can't you just feel the presence of Zeus and Hera when you stand here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought it was the wind.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Don't mock the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My life's been tainted by prophecy and the word of the gods. I've yet to see their hand in anything in this life.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You may not see it, but they have steered you to greatness. You will be a hero for the ages!

speaker: Kassandra
en: At what cost?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry. I don't want my feelings to cast a shadow on your day.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Don't think of yourself as tortured by the gods, but as molded for greatness by their hands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am molded by no one's hands. If the gods know me, they watch in silence.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Come. Let's leave this place. Fortunately for you, I have enough faith for the both of us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have I seen the temple?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Yes. Are you paying attention?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like to see the Olympic Tree.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You brought me to see a tree?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Not just any tree. This is the sacred tree from which the winners kotinos are made.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd rather have drachmae than a wreath.

speaker: Barnabas
en: A kotinos is no ordinary wreath. The olive branches are harvested by children and taken to the temple of Hera. There, the ', or judges, make the wreaths.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess they'll be lighter to carry back to Sparta than gold.

speaker: Barnabas
en: At least you see the practicality, if not the wonder, of the Olympic wreaths.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Should we see the Olympic Tree?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Were you sleeping? We've been there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Yes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you for this. I hope I wasn't too much of a distraction.

speaker: Barnabas
en: No, it was made better by your company.

speaker: Barnabas
en: A flock of harpies couldn't dampen my spirits—we're at the Olympics! You're competing, and I believe you'll win.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anything a mercenary can do for you today, healer?

speaker: Woman
en: I heard you hate bald people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Woman
en: It's OK. I hate bald people too. It's OK. I hate bald people too. That Hippokrates is one ugly malákas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bald or not, Hippokrates is a nice man. I don't think he should be judged on his hair loss.

speaker: Woman
en: It doesn't matter if he's nice, he just shouldn't be bald. I have a cure, though, and it isn't herbs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what is that?

speaker: Woman
en: Hippokrates' ugly bald pate has given me inspiration. Do you know what makes a good substitute for hair? Bear hair! If all the bears around here were to drop dead, I may cure this world of baldness.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to find and slay all the bears?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, all of them must be gutted. Do you accept?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Woman
en: Thank you, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: The gods thank you, and so do I. Take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Beating the Hammer
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You... uh... look to be in great health!

speaker: Man
en: Don't lie to me, you brute. I would look as good as you say if the Athenians hadn't taken my life out from underneath me before the Spartans turned up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Man
en: The Athenians took all my drachmae and drove me from my home before the Spartans took Megaris. Thanks to you, their forces are now scattered.

speaker: Man
en: Do you bring me good news, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all yours.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, misthios. Take this, it's yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Barnabas
en: That's Kos! I recognize it from my vision. A painted wall guards a siren's den there. Be careful!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That sound... Are there actual sirens here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should put the beeswax in my ears, just in case.

speaker: Unknown
en: Aarrrgggghhhhh

speaker: Kassandra
en: An aulos. Looks old.

speaker: Eurylochos
en: Please... don't hurt us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not going to hurt you, I will free you. What are you doing here?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: My whole life, I heard tales of the siren song—a sound so sweet men would gladly die to hear it. You have no idea how dull life is for a fisherman with a love of poetry and music.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You chose to be here?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: I... I didn't know this is what I would find. By the time I realized, there was no escape.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found this aulos. What do you know about it?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: That one was special. They stole it from the woman who escaped. But that was a long time ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This tomb is full of bloodthirsty women. Who are they?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: No one speaks. They drain my blood, then boil and drink it. In their rituals, they scream into the night. I'm so tired, but I never sleep. Please, save me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what are you doing here?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: My whole life, I heard tales of the siren song—a sound so sweet men would gladly die to hear it. You have no idea how dull life is for a fisherman with a love of poetry and music.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't stay here. Join my crew. A man named Barnabas will greet you on my ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're obsessed with poetry and you're a fisherman. I have an opportunity for you to have both those things, without being held like some animal.

speaker: Eurylochos
en: Anything would be better than this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't stay with you, big guy, but I think I found someone you should meet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eurylochos, this is Polyphemos. Polyphemos, Eurylochos.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Show you cave?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: Show me everything, my big friend. This is the grandest, most spectacular shore on which I've ever laid my weary eyes. I want to see it all!

speaker: Polyphemos
en: You Little. But big heart. Take this. Special gift.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Meet me at my ship, the Adrestia. I promise you, you will not be disappointed.

speaker: Eurylochos
en: It's been so long since I was shown kindness. My thanks.

speaker: Barnabas
en: About my Leda, do you have any news?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found this aulos on a "siren"... if you could call her that.

speaker: Barnabas
en: An aulos! My wife always loved these. I bet she learned to play it alongside the sirens as they sung men to their deaths. Just like her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll bet the sirens and Leda were good friends.

speaker: Barnabas
en: She was so mesmerizing. Her song always worked on me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There were no sirens, just bloodthirsty priestesses. And this aulos? It could be anybody's.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Then how did we know where to look? It's a clue, and Persephone led us right to it.

speaker: The Poisoner
en: Perikles' pet! Oh, how I've waiting for this day. I am going to fill your veins with the venom of a thousand snakes.

speaker: The Poisoner
en: You failed to save Perikles. When I'm done, I'll send him your body!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was the hired killer who tried poisoning politicians in Athens.

speaker: Epiktetos
en: I can still feel Deimos smashing my head against the artifact. Thanks to the power Deimos gave me, I am immortal!

speaker: Epiktetos
en: After I kill you, Deimos is next.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Epiktetos... The one my brother killed to spare me.

speaker: Deianeira
en: Come to fight a real champion, have you? I will mount your pretty head on a spear.

speaker: Deianeira
en: No one bests a Boeotian champion. No one!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deianeira... You're shorter than I remember.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Swordfish will have the Athenian's sword.

speaker: Swordfish
en: I've been waiting for you, misthios. Come to be food for the sharks? So be it.

speaker: Swordfish
en: Poseidon, give me strength.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Back to swimming with the fishes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the sword.

speaker: Xenia
en: Ah, the mighty misthios. You proved yourself capable before... I could use your talents. One like you is always interested in more drachmae, yes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Always happy to hear the clink of drachmae. Tell me what you want.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Payment is well and good. But I'm happy to help you. Tell me what you're thinking.

speaker: Xenia
en: I have an appetite for rare treasures. I've heard many veiled rumors and provocative stories, and I want you to recover some of these lost wonders for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where to look, and I'll bring you these treasures.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have the patience to go chasing after children's stories.

speaker: Xenia
en: What tide sweeps you back to me, Kassandra? Are you up for finding my treasures now?

speaker: Xenia
en: Have you heard of the mighty Ajax?

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of Homer's heroes.

speaker: Xenia
en: Yes! He had a golden eagle feather, a gift from Zeus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And why do you care about it?

speaker: Xenia
en: It is a rare reminder of a glorious age. And so deserves to be in my grasp. Take these maps and see if you can find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where will I find this golden eagle feather?

speaker: Xenia
en: Different tales place it at different locations. I have maps showing where you might find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about Ajax's feather?

speaker: Xenia
en: The son of Telamon was said to be a fearless giant. Some say the golden feather that gave him courage was woven into a shield crafted of seven ox hides. The shield is long destroyed, but Zeus' feather remains.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find this feather for you, if it's there to be found.

speaker: Xenia
en: You return on the wind. Do you have Ajax's golden feather for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here. One golden eagle feather, per request.

speaker: Xenia
en: What a pretty, pretty thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Glad you're happy. Now, my pay?

speaker: Xenia
en: Calm yourself. Here, for your trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, have it. It's lovely, no?

speaker: Xenia
en: Yes, it will fit nicely in my collection.

speaker: Blades of Justice
