speaker: Bleeding Blue
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Praxos
en: Scouts came back from Delos. The misthios likes to set fires.

speaker: Kyra
en: She just might be the answer to our prayers.

speaker: Praxos
en: She's only mortal.

speaker: Kyra
en: From what I've heard, she's much more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Athenians are weak. Now we strike Podarkes where he'll hurt most.

speaker: Kyra
en: His kidneys?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's good to see you, Kyra.

speaker: Kyra
en: Since you came here, I've actually started to believe we can win this rebellion. So... you were saying we strike?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Guards protect the island's treasury in one location. If we find it and steal it, the soldiers go unpaid, unfed, and unarmed. Podarkes will finally be vulnerable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Delos keeps its wealth in one place, under constant guard. We steal it, and the soldiers will go unpaid, unfed, and unarmed. Podarkes will be vulnerable.

speaker: Kyra
en: Then we can stick our blades in between his ribs... Feed his liver to the dogs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Before we start feeding organs to animals, can you get me to the nation's purse?

speaker: Kyra
en: Our spies have located it in Miltiades Fort. I'll have Praxos gather the troops.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's best if it's just the two of us. Easier to sneak in and out undetected.

speaker: Kyra
en: You just want me all to yourself, don't you? Let's get going then.

speaker: Kyra
en: Good thinking. Let's move.

speaker: Kyra
en: Victory is close. I can feel it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We haven't won yet. The fort will be treacherous, and the gods can be fickle.

speaker: Kyra
en: It was the gods who sent you to me—I refuse to believe they'd send you here to die. So, what do you think of our islands?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I prefer Mykonos. They really don't like you shedding blood on Delos.

speaker: Kyra
en: The priests are so terrified of desecrating the sacred grounds of Apollo, women about to give birth are shipped over to Mykonos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happens if they don't make it to shore?

speaker: Kyra
en: Boat babies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The nation's treasure, ripe for the picking.

speaker: Kyra
en: I'll keep an eye out for reinforcements. And don't you die on me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Guards everywhere. I need to be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This fort has seen better days. They should have spent some of that silver on upkeep.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Done! Kyra's going to want to see this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I already looted Delos' treasury. Kyra should hear about this.

speaker: Kyra
en: Kassandra, there you are! Good news, I hope?

speaker: Kassandra
en: When the people of Delos discover Podarkes lost every coin of their nation's treasure, they're going to rip him to pieces!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have a surprise. The treasury was already looted... by me. I'm surprised the soldiers haven't already ripped Podarkes to pieces!

speaker: Kyra
en: You've weakened Athens' grip over Delos, exposed Podarkes, and made way for a Spartan alliance. I could kiss you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't see anything holding you back.

speaker: Kyra
en: You breathe life into me. If only you'd arrived on Delos before Thaletas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You and Thaletas? But the way you were at each other's throats in the cave...

speaker: Kyra
en: He's a stubborn, arrogant, glory-hungry Spartan!

speaker: Kyra
en: But behind all the bronze and brawn, there's a man I could see by my side when this is all over. If we survive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The two of you fighting Athenians on the beach sounds romantic. I'd hate to interfere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These are dangerous times. I'd hate to meet Hades without having tasted those lips.

speaker: Kyra
en: Very poetic for someone covered in blood. I like it.

speaker: Kyra
en: Would you even recognize me in the underworld, I wonder?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't tell Thaletas if you don't.

speaker: Kyra
en: You're a bold one. I'd be lying if I said it wasn't tempting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the one who threatened to kiss me.

speaker: Kyra
en: Threatened?! I don't threaten, misthios. I act.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The job is done. Payment is my reward.

speaker: Kyra
en: Coins are as cold as death, misthios. They soothe me as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should probably move. They're going to come looking for us.

speaker: Kyra
en: I don't think I've ever really said thank you for coming here. You've given us hope.

speaker: Kyra
en: I'll go back to the hideout. But if you keep this up, Podarkes is as good as dead. I may finally know peace.

speaker: Slave 1
en: Who were those men?

speaker: Slave 2
en: It's better not knowing.

speaker: Slave 3
en: Those men. Are they from The...

speaker: Slave 4
en: Do not say it.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Misthios! Over here.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Did Agapios send you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Were you followed?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Are you sure you weren't followed?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even I can't be completely sure I wasn't followed.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Then we're in great danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a misthios, it's a dangerous line of work.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Not like this. Not like The Dagger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no way I was followed. I made sure of it.

speaker: Former Slave
en: You covered every track?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Every. Single. One.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Malákas liar! You've led them right to me...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who?

speaker: Former Slave
en: The Dagger.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Their corruption, their reach—it's limitless. They're watching that shipwreck, and I don't doubt they're watching you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What exactly went down with the ship?

speaker: Former Slave
en: I'm not sure. All I know is that this particular ship was part of The Dagger's fleet. They keep trying to salvage whatever's down there. If it's important to The Dagger, then it's important to us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know The Dagger's watching the shipwreck?

speaker: Former Slave
en: I see them row out to it. Men dive down and never come up. Those who do are half-drowned and terrified. They're forced to go back down again and again until they're dead. The Dagger's looking for something and won't stop until they've found it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you get involved in all this?

speaker: Former Slave
en: It was my master's boat that engaged The Dagger's ship, but he and many of his men perished in the ensuing battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get whatever's down there.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Thank you. Is there anything you need to know before leaving?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where exactly is the shipwreck?

speaker: Former Slave
en: Directly south of here. You can't miss it, some of the debris is still visible on the surface.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You must know a few things about Agapios.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Oh, I could tell you many things about Agapios... But I'll tell you the only thing that matters—he's a good man. He values trust above all else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have enough to go on.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Whatever's in the ship's cargo is of great interest to The Dagger. If you can get it, then maybe my master didn't die for nothing... Meet me down in Eretria when you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Debris from The Dagger's sunken ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An unusual blade. This must be what The Dagger's after. Now to find the woman in Eretria.

speaker: Slave 1
en: Who were those men?

speaker: Slave 2
en: It's better not knowing.

speaker: Enforcer
en: We've seen you watching us. Tell me why! What's your interest in the shipwreck?

speaker: Former Slave
en: Interest? No, I have no

speaker: Enforcer
en: Don't lie to me!

speaker: Former Slave
en: Help! Somebody help me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't be afraid. You're safe.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Thank you for saving my life. Did you find anything?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found this blade, covered in strange markings. The important item The Dagger were after was... a dagger?

speaker: Former Slave
en: This blade, it's used in sacrifices in the name of Achilles. The Dagger must be devoted to him. Find the right temple of Achilles, and you'll find The Dagger. But which is the right temple?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What will you do once The Dagger's gone?

speaker: Former Slave
en: It'll be nice to live without fear, but I'm still a slave without a master.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A slave without a master... is free.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Agapios will know when I show the blade to him. You should find a safe place to lie until this is over.

speaker: Former Slave
en: There's nowhere for me to go. I only have the clothes on my back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here. This should help get you started.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Thank you, misthios. I'll never forget what you've given me—freedom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already played my part–you're free now. The triumphs and struggles of that are yours and yours alone.

speaker: Former Slave
en: You're right. Having my freedom is all I need. I'll never forget what you've given me—freedom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already explored the Dagger's ship.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Well? Did you find anything?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Dagger's dagger. Seemed important.

speaker: Former Slave
en: It's not just important, misthios—this is a sacred sacrificial blade. These markings... This weapon's used to make sacrifices to Achilles. Find the right temple of Achilles, and you'll find The Dagger.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Quickly! Take this blade back to Agapios, and let's end this. The days of being pressed under The Dagger's thumb will soon be over.

speaker: Former Slave
en: Misthios. I decided to stay and rebuild my life, and Eretria with it. Without you, I never would've had the opportunity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How prepared are we?

speaker: Villager
en: We're under attack! Thyia and her warriors are holding them off, but we need reinforcements.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: As prepared as we're going to be. Go! I'll stay with those who can't fight.

speaker: Villager
en: This way! They've got us pinned against the rocks.

speaker: Thyia
en: I can't believe we did it. But the cost...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thyia, this is war.

speaker: Thyia
en: The extra bows from the Daughters of Artemis sure helped. They took blows away from my people. For that I'm grateful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure they were happy to help.

speaker: Thyia
en: We killed them. How? All I remember was swinging until my arms hurt, then swinging more. If you hadn't killed those scouts, I might have died thinking of them.

speaker: Thyia
en: That was... well, it wasn't easy, but it was easier than I expected. The Sons of Xerxes won't be invading Lalaia anytime soon. Still, I worry about Peri back in the village.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad it's over.

speaker: Thyia
en: I may not be a champion of the gods, but it'll take more than a few wounds to fell me. Let's return to Lalaia.

speaker: Thyia
en: Peri? Peri!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Over there.

speaker: Thyia
en: Peri!

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Thyia! I'm here. It's OK.

speaker: Thyia
en: It's over. We beat them back. All that's left to do is burn the bodies.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: You protected my sister and my village, and for that I'm eternally grateful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We protected each other.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: I don't know how we can ever repay you.

speaker: Thyia
en: I can think of a few ways I can repay you.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Really? You're having this discussion here? In front of your sister and the whole town?

speaker: Thyia
en: Later then.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Gratitude, misthios. Here is the drachmae as promised. You will always be welcome in Lalaia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My grandfather died not too far from here. I'm glad he defended this place from the Persians.

speaker: Thyia
en: Kassandra, if you could come see me before you leave, I'll be by the waterfall.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: And now the work of rebuilding begins.

speaker: Thyia
en: Peri? Peri!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Over there.

speaker: Thyia
en: Peri!

speaker: Agnodike
en: Thyia! I'm so sorry. They came without warning.

speaker: Thyia
en: Peri, no!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who did this?

speaker: Agnodike
en: Bandit scouts, I would guess. They carried bows and daggers.

speaker: Thyia
en: The scouts! Why doesn't anyone ever listen to me? Now my sister is dead, and the village is awash in her blood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thyia, we couldn't be in two places at once. We got back here as soon as we could.

speaker: Thyia
en: Not soon enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing I can say will make it right.

speaker: Thyia
en: I was supposed to be there to protect her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thyia...

speaker: Thyia
en: I have to visit Kephisos Spring and pray to Hades. Thank you for your help misthios. Meet me there for payment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's good to see all this beauty at peace once again.

speaker: Thyia
en: Mmm. And for years to come, thanks to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't promise you peace.

speaker: Thyia
en: But you did give us the tools to preserve it.

speaker: Thyia
en: It was good to get to know you. I'm glad the gods smiled upon us by bringing you here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Thyia
en: Someone needs to stay and keep Lalaia safe. I'm about to start training the children in combat. We won't be caught off guard again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could think of no better general.

speaker: Thyia
en: Chaire, Kassandra of Sparta. May you have a long life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what kind of reward did you have in mind?

speaker: Thyia
en: My first thoughts were of getting you out of those clothes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If that's the first thought, I can't wait to see how the second and third thoughts go.

speaker: Thyia
en: Oh, there won't be much thinking, but there will be seconds and thirds.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is it alright if we just enjoy the water?

speaker: Thyia
en: Of course. I'd say we've both earned a rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Thyia
en: With everything taken care of, I'm free to do what I want—a list that includes spending more time with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come with me then. I could always use someone who can think and use a sword.

speaker: Thyia
en: You only want me around for my brains and my brawn?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Would you prefer I said I wanted you to keep my bed warm?

speaker: Thyia
en: I've lived here my whole life, to leave it... well, that would be an adventure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even when your men do return, I get the feeling they'll need you to help defend Lalaia.

speaker: Thyia
en: They'll have to listen to me now that you've shown me that kick. Still, I'll miss you.

speaker: Thyia
en: I don't think I'll ever be able to see the beauty again. Not without Peri.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I lost my own family, I didn't think I'd ever find peace.

speaker: Thyia
en: And have you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not yet. You probably want nothing to do with me now.

speaker: Thyia
en: Everything that happened. I just can't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I understand.

speaker: Thyia
en: It's better this way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Thyia
en: Our magistrate is dead. We are without a leader, so I will step in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll make a good one.

speaker: Thyia
en: Thank you for all your help.

speaker: Elpis
en: Now that I have the Isu device forged, we need to move quickly. You distract Atlas while I sneak into his private chambers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: More sneaking.

speaker: Elpis
en: After Poseidon outlawed human experiments, Atlas confiscated a device and kept it. That device theoretically could add a third helix to my DNA.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen what these Isu devices can do. It's not pretty.

speaker: Elpis
en: The science is sound, and I've even found evidence of tests being done on humans that looked promising. In previous cycles, of course, before Poseidon outlawed experimentation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just tell Atlas the truth. You have good intentions

speaker: Elpis
en: If he's afraid of his enemies hurting me now, what will he think of me undergoing this procedure? Besides, he can't break Poseidon's law.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Last I checked, he seemed pretty power hungry. I don't think he wants to share his throne.

speaker: Elpis
en: Behind every great man is a great woman. I can make Atlas see that, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure a good Dikastes goes behind the back of an Atlantean Archon.

speaker: Elpis
en: I've been preparing for this my entire life. Don't worry. Just keep Atlas talking while I'm in his chambers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't think we have anything in common. What are we supposed to talk about? The weather?

speaker: Elpis
en: Atlas is a jealous lover, and he's already threatened by your role as Dikastes. Why not play to that advantage? Whatever you do, don't mention my plans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Great. This will do wonders for our relationship.

speaker: Elpis
en: Everyone knows it's lonely at the top, Dikastes. Let's go.

speaker: Elpis
en: I've studied this science extensively. Once I impart Isu DNA into my body. I should be able to use the device without side effects.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's the "should" that worries me.

speaker: Elpis
en: Remember, whatever you do, don't reveal my political plans to Atlas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could trick Atlas into thinking you and I are closer than we are.

speaker: Elpis
en: Are we not close? What's there to trick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know what I mean.

speaker: Elpis
en: Yes, making Atlas envious would certainly be a good distraction.

speaker: Atlas
en: Elpis? What are you doing here? With her no less?

speaker: Elpis
en: The Dikastes and I were just taking a stroll and I remembered I left a book on Atlantean cyclical history here. She'd like to borrow it Do you mind if I fetch it?

speaker: Atlas
en: I - No. Do you need me to help you look for it?

speaker: Elpis
en: No, no. You two stay here. I'm sure you have much to discuss.

speaker: Atlas
en: What game are you playing at, Dikastes?

speaker: Atlas
en: Elpis wouldn't have anything to do with why you were sneaking around the Adamant Metallon, would she?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know what you're talking about.

speaker: Atlas
en: I'm sure by now Elpis has told you about the nature of our relationship. She's hardly as discreet as I'd like her to be. What business do you have with her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Is Elpis not allowed to have friends?

speaker: Atlas
en: Of course she can have friends. But I suspect there's more going on here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've had enough of these secrets! Elpis wants to become Isu like you. She's using a device in your palace to do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpis was just sharing her thoughts on ways we can improve relations between Isu and humans.

speaker: Atlas
en: That woman is always angling to stick her nose where it doesn't belong.

speaker: Atlas
en: Really? You have nothing to say for yourself?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have nothing to worry about, Atlas. I have no schemes against you.

speaker: Atlas
en: Maybe you don't play games, but Elpis lives for them. I can tell when she's up to something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't talk about Elpis that way. She's not manipulative. She's passionate.

speaker: Atlas
en: So you do care for her, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've had enough of these secrets! Elpis wants to become Isu like you. She's using a device in your palace to do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpis cares about policy in Atlantis. Involve her, and hear what she has to say.

speaker: Atlas
en: It's not her place! It's mine.

speaker: Atlas
en: This is the price I pay for involving myself with someone so ambitious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't talk about Elpis like you love her.

speaker: Atlas
en: And you're not speaking of her as if you're merely her casual acquaintance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpis makes great points about improving the lives of humans in Atlantis. I support her cause. Why don't you?

speaker: Atlas
en: She should support me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've had enough of these secrets! Elpis wants to become Isu like you. She's using a device in your palace to do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The truth is Elpis and I are in love!

speaker: Atlas
en: What?

speaker: Atlas
en: What... What have you done?

speaker: Elpis
en: I'm not weak anymore, Atlas. I can rule Atlantis at your side!

speaker: Atlas
en: This is your doing. You're trying to revolt against the Isu with hybrids.

speaker: Elpis
en: No!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you do?

speaker: Elpis
en: I didn't mean to. He was going to kill you!

speaker: Azaes
en: Ah. It seems my brother finally got his due. Was this your judgment, Dikastes?

speaker: Elpis
en: I killed Atlas. It wasn't my intention. I...

speaker: Azaes
en: You hoped to rule by his side to ease the conflict between humans and Isu.

speaker: Elpis
en: He wasn't as supportive of my dreams as I would have hoped.

speaker: Azaes
en: I support you. You can assume his role as you see fit. I will handle Poseidon and my brothers.

speaker: Elpis
en: Thank you, Azaes.

speaker: Azaes
en: You can't be more corrupt than Atlas. And Atlantis can't fear progress if it hopes to pass this cycle.

speaker: Poseidon
en: So this is your judgment, Dikastes? That all my sons are to die?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't kill

speaker: Poseidon
en: But your actions allowed this to happen. Did you not help this human? And are all my sons not dead?

speaker: Elpis
en: This was my fault. I take full responsibility for my actions.

speaker: Poseidon
en: This could not have happened without the Dikastes. The very one I appointed. I will need to ponder what this means for our cycle. Still, you bested Atlantis's highest Archon. By our laws, that means you may rule. But beware the ramifications this will have on our society.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlantean politics are even more dramatic than in the Greek world. What will you do now?

speaker: Elpis
en: I'm not the first Atlantean ruler to take power by force. If the Isu can do it, why not me? Still, I didn't want my reign to start this way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bring the good you've always dreamed of to your reign.

speaker: Elpis
en: I will, Dikastes. thank you for your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You started your reign by saving my life. Normally, I do the saving.

speaker: Elpis
en: I wouldn't have it any other way. Thank you, Dikastes.

speaker: Elpis
en: Hopefully this is the start of me saving many lives here in Atlantis. Thank you, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said it yourself. The Isu are cold and calculating. You need to rule with strength if you hope to survive.

speaker: Elpis
en: I will, Dikastes. thank you for your help.

speaker: Elpis
en: I'll make progress for humans in Atlantis, slowly but surely. thank you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpis will make a better ruler than Atlas. Sher certainly can't do any worse.

speaker: Elpis
en: Atlas, stop!

speaker: Atlas
en: You betrayed me. You used knowledge I told you in confidence for your own political gain.

speaker: Elpis
en: It was for Atlantis! I don't want to be your weakness anymore. I can help you, Atlas!

speaker: Atlas
en: Lies! You used me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait, don't!

speaker: Atlas
en: This is your fault! Dikastes wasn't enough? You had to steal away my father's love. Turn Elpis against me. You want to rule my Doma, too?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, it had nothing to do with that!

speaker: Atlas
en: Traitor! You're no longer welcome here. Guards!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka! I need to get out of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was a lot to take in. I need a moment to clear my head.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These fishermen should know something about Swordfish.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for Swordfish.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: I-I know nothing!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for Swordfish. Can you help?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Piss off, maláka!

speaker: Street Vendor
en: You're going to get both of us in trouble! Leave.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fishmonger, I'm looking for Swordfish.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Shh! Are you crazy?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: You don't find Swordfish - Swordfish finds you. Now go before I get my nose cut off.

speaker: Civilian
en: Hey, misthios! Over here!

speaker: Civilian
en: I hear you're lookin' for... a certain fish.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yeah - Swordfish.

speaker: Civilian
en: I hope you know what you're in for. He's ruthless - cut off a man's nose just for sneezin'.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why is it that every time I mention his name, people jump?

speaker: Civilian
en: Swordfish controls Heraklion and everyone in it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is he?

speaker: Civilian
en: No one's seen him in a long time.

speaker: Civilian
en: But there's... a rumor he controls Heraklion from a hideout underground.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's ridiculous.

speaker: Civilian
en: It's all I know, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If he's so dangerous, why are you talking to me?

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm old, tired - sick of bowin' down to pay "fees."

speaker: Civilian
en: If you can take him out, we're all better for it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll keep that in mind

speaker: Thug
en: Not another word out of you, maláka!

speaker: Thug
en: I have orders. Everyone who talks about Swordfish must die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods - What's going on here? ...Swordfish.

speaker: Swordfish
en: ...Isn't enough - sharks need more. I need more. More... more... Never find me - they can never find me. The sharks need more. Need more sharks. Fishermen are late - no fish for the sharks... The wives and children will have - To - Do! The sharks need more... Need more sharks...

speaker: Swordfish
en: Deimos. I knew you'd come. Dog. Dog of Kosmos, have you come to bite?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have nothing to do with the Cultists.

speaker: Swordfish
en: Think I believe you? You're mad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come to tear your face off, Swordfish.

speaker: Swordfish
en: You think I haven't been preparing for this day?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for the

speaker: Swordfish
en: I WON'T GO BACK. I won't go back in there. I don't care if I owe the Cult! I want out. You want that artifact - Go fetch it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Minotaur is dead. I went into the labyrinth and killed it.

speaker: Swordfish
en: Then you have the artifact. I can be free! Give it to me. GIVE IT TO ME. GIVE IT TO ME.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Once a Cultist, always a Cultist.

speaker: Swordfish
en: What do you want from me then, Deimos?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Answers. And you will give them to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened in there that drove you to - this?

speaker: Swordfish
en: The Minotaur happened! I was lucky - Nikios, though... The Kosmos promised me everything. Not this!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you end up here?

speaker: Swordfish
en: I'm hiding amongst the filth... and from it. I can't show my face anymore. But Heraklion is still mine! All its fish - And all its people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're insane.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you get into the labyrinth?

speaker: Swordfish
en: Nikios had a key - he put it into the stele. But you can't go in there! It'll kill you. It'll get out and kill us all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You underestimate me.

speaker: Swordfish
en: That's what Nikios said. Raaaaa!

speaker: Swordfish
en: I'll feed you to the sharks!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not so good with a sword after all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A broken man... Haunted by the Minotaur till the very end.

speaker: Civilian
en: 5 drachmae says he jumps.

speaker: Civilian
en: 25 says he doesn't.

speaker: Civilian
en: How long's he been up there?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Three, maybe 4 days?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Should we get him water, or...? How long have you been here watching him?!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Like I said, 3, maybe 4 days?

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Come down from there!

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Athena, give him strength...! Please, just come down.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: It's not safe up there! Come down and fight the Minotaur!

speaker: Morys
en: I said stand back! I'll jump! I mean it! I—clear a space! 'Cause I'm jumping! I don't want anyone to get hurt! From my jump! Which I'm about to do! Right NOW! Riiight now! Here we go! My feet are kinda over the edge! My big toes are no longer safe—only air is beneath them! Everyone stand back, or the rest of my feet are sure to follow!

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Why's he up there?

speaker: Civilian 6
en: I heard he fell in love with the Minotaur, who rejected his advances—and his broken heart drove him to madness.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Really? I heard he just wanted to get a really good view of Lato, and forgot how to get down

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Someone help him! Don't be a fool! Think of your mater! And if that makes you want to jump more... Maybe think of something else!

speaker: Morys
en: Back! Stay back! I'LL JUMP!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't have to do this. There's always something to live for.

speaker: scaffolding
en: No! Not for me! I-I've got nothing. I AM Nothing... This isn't even armor! It's my mother's third-favourite serving tray! I'm a failure. A failure!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stop wasting everybody's time and come back from the edge. If you were going to jump you'd have done it by now.

speaker: Morys
en: Wha-what? I will! Any second now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No you won't. You're a coward.

speaker: Morys
en: I'm no coward! I'll show you!

speaker: Morys
en: By Zeus's tunic, you're right. Of course you're right. I am a coward.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come away from the edge. Talk to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look like a warrior to me. Even warriors feel fear. There's no shame in it. Fear helps us survive. It's temporary. ...But honor is not. You'll find no honor jumping off this building. Only death. Talk to me.

speaker: Morys
en: ...Honor. Yes.

speaker: Morys
en: My village, we're poor. We get little trade, fewer visitors. We're dying. I was chosen to kill the Minotaur hoping it would make us famous, put us on the map. Save us, maybe. But look at me—I'm no Minotaur slayer. I got robbed by a tiny tour guide my first day here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Minotaur's already dead. I killed it.

speaker: Morys
en: You—no, I was supposed to do it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sorry.

speaker: Morys
en: Then my people are doomed...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Minotaur slaying isn't for everyone. Even if you go home without the beast's head, there will be another way to save your village.

speaker: Morys
en: You're right! All I have to do is... lie to everyone!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do not put words in my mouth.

speaker: Morys
en: Why not, they're good words! My people are kind, and loving, and somewhat dim

speaker: Kassandra
en: Really? Hard to believe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That

speaker: Kassandra
en: That might actually work.

speaker: Morys
en: I just have to make them think I've killed the Minotaur. Our village would become a shrine to me, the new Theseus. Morys the Magnificent, Slayer of the Minotaur! We would prosper again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a dream.

speaker: Morys
en: A dream where people care about my village? Trade with it? That's a dream worth having. I'll need to look convincing—like a regal, conquering, Minotaur-killing hero! Best steal the Pephka leader's shiniest armor. Oh, and I'll need a weapon! Something I can say I pried from the Minotaur's cold dead hands! Cold dead hooves?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, I'm here to help.

speaker: Morys
en: Good. Good, good, good. Is there anything else I can tell you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: An axe that looks like you've looted it from the corpse of a Minotaur... Is there a merchant for that in Pephka?

speaker: Morys
en: When I first arrived, I heard rumours of a legendary axe kept in Fort Lato. That's where you'll find what I need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's so special about this axe?

speaker: Morys
en: They say Theseus touched it. Twice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure Theseus handled many axes in his time.

speaker: Morys
en: Well, yes. But he touched this one twice. Now THAT'S the sort of axe you'd expect a Minotaur to wield!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned the..."shiniest" armor was the Pephkan Leader's. Where does he keep it?

speaker: Morys
en: Somewhere safe. Somewhere little street kids couldn't steal it. His house is well guarded—I'd look there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like you could use some Minotaur Hoof Elixir.

speaker: Morys
en: No, no, no, only a fool would buy such a blatant scam! "Minotaur Hoof Elixir"! Why would a Minotaur need elixir for its hooves?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...Right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard enough—I'll find you an axe and armor worthy of a true Minotaur slayer. Just don't... jump.

speaker: Morys
en: I wouldn't think of it!

speaker: The Shiniest Armor in All of Pephka
en: This is very fancy armor that commands respect.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the armor Morys described. It is shiny.

speaker: Axe-That-Theseus-Touched-Twice
en: This is an ancient axe that Theseus definitely saw and touched. Twice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the axe the man from the roof wanted. It's pretty heavy. I wonder if he could even lift it... Now I have both items the man on the roof needs to bring glory back to his village. I better get these to him before he actually jumps.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm back, and I have everything you need to successfully lie to your people.

speaker: Morys
en: Oh fantastic! And fear not, friend—this is a lie that will save my people. It'll put us back on the map! Well, um... Can I—can I have my items now please?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course, the axe and armor are yours.

speaker: Morys
en: Just, uh, turn around for a second... While I... change...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look heroic. Like a warrior who could kill a whole family of Minotaurs.

speaker: Morys
en: Really? You're not just saying that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I mean it. Even I'm a bit intimidated by you now.

speaker: Morys
en: Wow! It's OK guys! I'm a hero now! I'm coming down! I feel pretty heroic.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. The axe and armor are mine. You think they could make you look like a Minotaur slayer? No matter what armor you wear, you'll always be Morys the Pathetic. You fool no one.

speaker: Morys
en: I—no, I'm a, I'm a

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go home, "hero."

speaker: Morys
en: I sure hope that boat captain shows up so I can get home. He took the last of my drachmae...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like the camp. Time to send some guards to Hades.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The fort at last. Should find a quiet way in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah. These must be the barracks mater spoke of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The camp is clear. I still have to find the barracks and the fort. The fort is also in Smuggler's Forest—I should start there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now that the fort and camp have been cleared, I should head to the barracks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That takes care of the barracks and the camp. Now I need to clear the fort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The barracks are clear. But Lagos still has guards at the camp and the fort. Both are in Smuggler's Forest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That takes care of the camp and the barracks. My last target the fort, which is also in Smuggler's Forest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That takes care of the fort and the barracks. Time to deal with Lagos's guards at the camp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The camp should be nearby, I'll head there first. Then on to the barracks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Two strongholds down. Now I just need to find these barracks mater spoke of. She said they were in Tegea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The barracks and the fort are clear. Time to find the camp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater said Lagos is hiding in Fort Samikon. Time to go pay him a little visit.

speaker: Melannipos
en: You're a fool, Melanippos. A fool.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you lose your pankration match?

speaker: Melannipos
en: Worse. I lost my one true love. My Drakon has found someone else—I just know it. he avoids me, and when we're together he's always distracted...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I admit, it doesn't sound good.

speaker: Melanippos
en: Even you think I've been replaced. But I can't let him go. He's my golden demigod.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you must have a plan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe there's still a chance?

speaker: Melanippos
en: I can't leave this up to the whims of Tyche. I won't let Drakon go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then what's your plan?

speaker: Melanippos
en: I'm going to make a potion. It's a recipe that guarantees eternal love.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's an honest way to save a relationship.

speaker: Melanippos
en: It's simple. I'll "borrow" his precious armor for a few days, coat the inside, and let the potion seep through his skin—straight to his heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So... Drakon will be left without his armor. Aren't you worried he'll be vulnerable?

speaker: Melanippos
en: Oh, he's the strongest, most chiseled man in Thebes. He'll be fine without it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good to know.

speaker: Melanippos
en: My problem is the last ingredient. I need to buy the rarest herb in Boeotia from my herbalist, but she hasn't come to Thebes in a while.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can find her for you. I must believe in love after all.

speaker: Melanippos
en: Thank you, thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where will I find this herbalist?

speaker: Melanippos
en: She lives on a farm west of the city near the Tomb of Menoikeus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Rare herb, huh? What is it?

speaker: Melanippos
en: A herb hot enough to impassion him. Red hot to make his affections—and his skin—sizzle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me how you met.

speaker: Melanippos
en: It's a tale for the ages. I moved to Thebes with dreams of becoming a great champion. I came to this gym and saw him... A mighty warrior with an even mightier smile. I wanted to learn from the best, but the only muscle he truly worked on was my heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're going to a lot of effort for Drakon. Is he worth it?

speaker: Melanippos
en: He's a living, breathing Herakles—you tell me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If he's not here, where is he?

speaker: Melanippos
en: Normally we're both here night and day. The only time he leaves is to perform at the training ground.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go find that herb for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like the place.

speaker: Farmer
en: Don't. Don't.

speaker: Archer
en: Then get her out of the house. You die if she doesn't. The farm is ours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bandits! What a surprise...

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're gone, you can come out now.

speaker: Farmer
en: Thank you, misthios. If you hadn't intervened we'd surely be dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They must have really wanted something from you.

speaker: Farmer
en: The farm. It's one of the few untouched by the war. Herbs aren't free, you know. They'd uproot 'em and sell 'em.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Speaking of herbs, that's why I'm here. I need to buy one for a man named Melanippos. Says he knows you.

speaker: Farmer
en: That troublemaker still wants to make the love potion?

speaker: Farmer
en: Well, he'll have it his way. I can sell you the herb he needs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saved your farm. I feel like that deserves some gratitude.

speaker: Farmer
en: I have to make a living, don't I?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, here.

speaker: Farmer
en: Tell Melanippos to let it really soak in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shouldn't have to pay anything. I risked my life for you.

speaker: Farmer
en: I never asked you to, but suit yourself. You won't find anyone else with this herb in Boeotia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, here's the drachmae.

speaker: Farmer
en: On second thought, you did save Episthenes and me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. I appreciate the gesture.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think exchanging herbs for your life is a fair trade.

speaker: Farmer
en: While I'm thankful for your help, I didn't ask for it. I can't be giving my herbs away for free in such trying times.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, here.

speaker: Farmer
en: Tell Melanippos to let it really soak in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shouldn't have to pay anything. I risked my life for you.

speaker: Farmer
en: I never asked you to, but suit yourself. You won't find anyone else with this herb in Boeotia.

speaker: Farmer
en: Ready to pay now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's the drachmae.

speaker: Farmer
en: On second thought, you did save Episthenes and me. Here, take the herb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, I appreciate the gesture.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shouldn't have to pay after risking my life for you.

speaker: Farmer
en: Suit yourself, but no one else in Boeotia has this herb.

speaker: Farmer
en: Ready to pay now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There, your herb. It better be worth all the trouble.

speaker: Melanippos
en: Yes, yes. Drakon is mine 'til the end of time. Maybe I'll take him for a moonlit walk at the Site of Iphigenia's Sacrifice... He won't have to go far from his training site.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And his armor?

speaker: Melanippos
en: It waits patiently for the potion in my house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Be sure you take your time with it... for the potion to work best.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anything a misthios can help you with, stranger?

speaker: Woman
en: One of my clients gives me nothing but excuses. I cannot live on such wretched offerings. The other hetaerae all receive beautiful gifts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It sounds like he's trying to cheat you.

speaker: Woman
en: I won't stand for that. Here I am, without so much as a necklace or new robe—not even a coin for all his promises. The other girls have started mocking me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You need me to deal with him.

speaker: Woman
en: You understand quickly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in.

speaker: Woman
en: I'm in your debt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can leave everything to me.

speaker: Kasssandra
en: Time to collect.

speaker: Woman
en: Has he been... dealt with, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He won't be bothering anyone anymore.

speaker: Woman
en: You've set great things in motion. Take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Now that we know you can fight... I have a serious matter to discuss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh?

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Two of my older students have gone missing, and I need someone I can trust to find them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They should know enough to take care of themselves...

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Yes, but the world is full of unexpected dangers, and I cannot leave my charges to investigate properly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can look for them. Tell me what I need to know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My duty was to bring Makarios here. I don't have time to help you now.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Your help finding my missing students would be welcome.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What were their last orders?

speaker: Iatrokles
en: I had sent them to a lookout camp, where they were to survive on their own for a few days. It is up to them to treat it seriously... But when I went to check on them, there was no sign.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What dangers did you expect them to face?

speaker: Iatrokles
en: The students learn to watch for wolves and bears. But I saw no spoor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perhaps a different sort of beast...

speaker: Iatrokles
en: The two students who are missing are called Akamas and Theoros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Theoros? Makarios' brother?

speaker: Iatrokles
en: The same. I fear I have failed the magistrate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll look at the campsite and see what I can find.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Look at the campsite where Theoros and Akamas were stationed and determine what happened to them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A burned patch. Someone dropped a torch in surprise.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A lost shield... that is a bad omen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Signs of battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A body. Hmm. He doesn't look much like Makarios or Xanthe. Must be the other boy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A trail... someone ran towards the mountain heights. Could be Theoros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found him!

speaker: Theoros
en: Gods be good, please untie me!

speaker: Theoros
en: Have mercy! Cut me free!

speaker: Theoros
en: Help me, before these murderers butcher me!

speaker: Theoros
en: My gratitude, warrior. I was certain I would not see another day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's your name?

speaker: Theoros
en: Theoros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trainer Iatrokles will want to know what happened to you and your companion.

speaker: Theoros
en: My age-mate, Akamas, was killed by these dogs when we saw them sneaking about in the night.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what happened to you?

speaker: Theoros
en: I fell in combat, and they dragged me here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw the battlefield. You ran as soon as your companion fell. A Spartan never drops his shield.

speaker: Theoros
en: Curse you. Yes! I don't want to be a soldier, I never wanted to! All I wanted was a small boat, a small life. To fish and live in peace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A fisherman?! I came all this way for a coward?

speaker: Theoros
en: So what? I didn't ask for this. It was forced upon me. A boy in Sparta has no other choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your mother and Makarios will be disgusted by you.

speaker: Theoros
en: At least I'll be alive to pray for them and love them from afar. Thank you for my life, misthios, but tell them I'm not coming back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brother, Makarios, will be glad to see you alive. And he'll be impressed by your bravery.

speaker: Theoros
en: Makarios is at the agoge?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I escorted him there myself, on behalf of your mother. He's a bright boy. Eager to learn from the brother he favors so much.

speaker: Theoros
en: I don't know if I can face them all again...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course you can. Remember, the trick is just to keep breathing. Put your body in a state of fearlessness, and your mind will be free of fear.

speaker: Theoros
en: I will try. I can't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Breathe. Release the fear.

speaker: Theoros
en: Yes. I feel it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good! Your shield is where you left it. Collect it on your way back to the agoge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brother worships you and will be overjoyed to see you.

speaker: Theoros
en: Makarios? Has the time come for him to join the agoge already?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, he already studies with Trainer Iatrokles.

speaker: Theoros
en: Curse all of Olympos! He isn't ready for this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The world is tough. But if we look out for those we love, we can shield them from at least a little harm.

speaker: Theoros
en: I do not know that I can face my brother—all my brothers—again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course you can. Makarios worships you. But you can use that love to fuel your bravery and defeat your fear. Retrieve your shield from where you left it and return to the agoge. Soon you'll embrace your brother again.

speaker: Theoros
en: Thank you, my friend. I will! Please, tell my mother that her sons will do the family proud.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Will you be a Spartan and retrieve your shield and your place in the line, or will you run off and offend the gods, leaving your duty behind?

speaker: Theoros
en: If the gods are offended by my choices, they should never have put me in this skin! I never wanted to be a warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We do what we must in this world, not what we want.

speaker: Theoros
en: I must leave Sparta, then, or else die by slow suicide. Thank you for my life, but tell my mother I won't return!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trainer, from what I could tell, your two charges spotted bandits sneaking across the mountains in the night.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: And? What happened then?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Akamas fell, but I found Theoros, and helped him find his way back.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: I'm sorry to hear of the fall of Akamas. But I suspect you've inspired Theoros to new heights. He will be a model for the younger ones to follow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: May Zeus guide them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have bad tidings for you, Trainer.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Let's have it. Better to take a hardship face-on than drag it out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bandits were in the mountains. Akamas died trying to fight them. Theoros survived, but his spirit is broken. He has no will to fight.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Akamas fell, and Theoros abandoned his duty? These are bitter fruits you bring me, misthios. It will be up to Makarios to one day restore his family's honor for his brother's cowardice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As you say.

speaker: Xanthe
en: What do you have to share with me, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Magistrate Xanthe, I have black news for you. Your older son is lost.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Dead?

speaker: Kassandra
en: In the face of danger, Theoros abandoned his shield and fled his duty.

speaker: Xanthe
en: This is... hard news. A blow upon my heart. I do not thank you for your words, but they needed to be heard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Makarios has started his training at the agoge. And who knows, maybe one day Theoros

speaker: Xanthe
en: I have but one son now, misthios. To other matters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Theoros and his age-mate, Akamas, were on overnight watch when they encountered a group of bandits. I found Akamas' corpse, but Theoros's body was gone. Lost to the mountains, or taken by wolves.

speaker: Xanthe
en: I see. His death will be an inspiration to his brother to train all the harder. My gratitude, Eagle Bearer, for this news. And the bandits?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Dead and given to the crows.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Good. Now, to other matters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Makarios is well placed at the agoge. The trainer, Iatrokles, will be a hard taskmaster, but he will grow strong and brave.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Gods willing, he'll find a way to endure and thrive. It is not easy to send one's heart into the world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's eager and bright. And he has Theoros there to guide and inspire him. They will support each other.

speaker: Xanthe
en: You demonstrate the wisdom of Athena, Eagle Bearer. You are a blessing to this family.

speaker: Xanthe
en: There are several in the region who could benefit from your presence, Eagle Bearer. Help them. Inspire them. And I'll reward you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me their names.

speaker: Xanthe
en: The farm owner, Lanike, as well as several of the town's important women—Zita, Damia, and Zeuxo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is this farm owner?

speaker: Xanthe
en: Lanike runs the farm for her family. Recently, it has been underperforming. She blames the gods and believes the land is cursed. But I wonder if she's too quick to punish her helots.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does Zita need?

speaker: Xanthe
en: Her daughter, Zopheras, is as wild and headstrong as an untamed filly. Zita constantly prays for guidance, but I suspect Zopheras needs a more grounded hand to direct her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What should I know about Damia?

speaker: Xanthe
en: She has two precocious children who rule the roost in the agora. They reduce their tutors to tears and stir up their other age-mates. She is hoping you can instill some respect in them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about Zeuxo?

speaker: Xanthe
en: Her husband is off training for war, and she specifically requested an audience with you for help with something quite personal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find them and see what they want of me.

speaker: Xanthe
en: May the Dioskouri watch over your path.

speaker: Brutal Force
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Building on Ashes
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan in 2017 through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Leonidas. He was Sparta's last true hero. We'd all be under the yoke of the Persian Empire if it wasn't for his courage. The same blood courses through your veins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My blood courses through these veins. Not some man's I've never met.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Leonidas was king, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And yet I grew up in the dirt!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm proud of my lineage, but I carve my own path.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You carry the blood of heroes. You can carve much more than the path of a mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, our blood is the blood of kings.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You are so much more than a mercenary. You carry the blood of heroes, blood of power. Remember what I told you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That people would try to take that power for themselves.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And then you promised...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wouldn't let them.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Hold out your spear.

speaker: Leonidas
en: All of this talk of the Pythia. The Pythia! I do not care what she says.

speaker: Cultist
en: Enough! We have grown tired of your insolent tongue! Sparta will not go to war, the Pythia has spoken!

speaker: Leonidas
en: The Pythia says what you tell her to say! She's been your puppet for far too long, the time has come to cut her strings!

speaker: Cultist
en: Oh Leonidas, the are over. You think your blood makes you special? If we opened your veins it would spill to the ground and disappear through the cracks. You are no one.

speaker: Leonidas
en: You are more than welcome to find out.

speaker: Pythia
en: Your fate is sealed, Son of the Lion. Xerxes will unite us. He will bring order to chaos.

speaker: Cultist
en: Defy the Pythia, and everyone you love, everything you stand for, will perish.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Gather the men.

speaker: Dienekes
en: My king?

speaker: Leonidas
en: If Xerxes wants Sparta, he'll have to go through me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Incredible!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Now do you understand?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What must I do?

speaker: Myrrine
en: It's time we embrace our destiny — both of us. If we don't stop the Cult before it's too late, then all Leonidas fought and died for was for nothing. Our bloodline has risen to those who would enslave us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's time we rise again.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Well, well, well. Mother and daughter united in Sparta at last. And look at you! Goddessess among mortals.

speaker: Myrrine
en: King Pausanias, we're honored. I was sorry to hear about your father.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Yes. Our fathers would have been proud to see us here today.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You remember Kassandra, my king?

speaker: Pausanias
en: Who could forget? The girl who died to save her brother. Such a tragedy. An innocent child, put to death because of an ancient, merciless law.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Two innocent children were put to their deaths that day.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra, enough!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Apologies my king, she's been away from Sparta for a long time.

speaker: Pausanias
en: You both have.

speaker: Pausanias
en: This one has fire like her mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I killed an elder. Sparta didn't find that very innocent.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ancient and merciless? Most Spartans live and die by these laws. But you sound more progressive.

speaker: Pausanias
en: And you sound like you've been rubbing elbows with Athenians.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been to a symposium or two.

speaker: Pausanias
en: In any case, Sparta was weakened by losing you. Losing you both.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're examples of why these laws must change.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Oh I agree. But King Archidamos? If he could carve Spartan law across the chests of every citizen he would.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spartan laws destroyed my family. Spartan laws had me claw my way through the streets!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're here today because he defied those laws.

speaker: Pausanias
en: He did, and he lost his head for it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've spent my whole life looking over my shoulder. If Sparta is to be my home again, I'd rather it be a peaceful one.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Peace at what cost? When Spartans aren't killing, they're training to kill. And when they're not killing Athens, they're declaring war on their own people.

speaker: Pausanias
en: But we're not here to talk about the dead. Are we?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We know Sparta reclaimed our house after what happened to my father in Megaris. We want it back.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Mind your tongue, child. You may not live in Sparta anymore, but I'm still your king.

speaker: Myrrine
en: We graciously request an audience with you and King Archidamos to discuss reinstating our citizenship and reclaiming our home.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Of course! There's nothing I'd want more. Archidamos, however, still hasn't forgiven you for the whole... nose incident.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can we do to sway him?

speaker: Pausanias
en: There's rumor of a helot rebellion, and the krypteia are stoking the flames. Savagely killing helots, stealing livestock, and leaving corpses to rot in the streets.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The krypteia represents Sparta's ultimate achievement in military training. Their discipline and fearlessness make Sparta's army the most feared in the world.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Once. But the krypteia have become corrupt and bloodthirsty. And training boys to kill unarmed peasants is nothing to be proud of. Do you want your home back or not?

speaker: Pausanias
en: Good. Show the helots we no longer support the senseless slaughtering of their people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And where would I start looking for these krypteia?

speaker: Pausanias
en: One can be found in the fort on Zarax Point. Another was assigned to guard a Spartan leader's house. The third is more elusive. He was last seen in one of the villages west of Helot Hills. He's definitely the loudest of the three.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mater spoke of these krypteia. What can you tell me about them?

speaker: Pausanias
en: They are the hidden ones. Handpicked at an early age. Starved and trained in isolation. They must steal and kill to survive. If they succeed at their training, they become the king's guard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But why have me kill them?

speaker: Pausanias
en: For years the krypteia kept peace between the helots and Spartans. Troublemakers and threats among the helots were... dealt with. But lately these krypteia have been killing men, women, and children without reason or mercy. Babies ripped from their mothers and fed to the wolves... The krypteia have become a breeding ground for ruthless savages.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there anything I should know about King Archidamos?

speaker: Pausanias
en: Traditional. Brutal. Boring. Archidamos values the old ways over the welfare of his people. He sided with the elders that day on Mount Taygetos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If killing krypteia will get our home back, I'll do it.

speaker: Pausanias
en: You shouldn't waste any time. The krypteia must be killed.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Pausanias gave you a task. Spartan Kings aren't known for their patience.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Archidamos believes in the old ways, won't killing his krypteia create conflict between him and Pausanias? I miss Kephallonia sometimes. Life was simple. Even if Markos was a bumbling idiot.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Listen up. I'm only going to say this once.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: This village stinks like a pig's asshole.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Everyone shut up, or you'll eat steel. I'd be more than happy to bash your teeth in if you don't settle down.

speaker: Slave
en: Night and day we slave for Sparta. They take everything from us.

speaker: Slave
en: They treat us worse than dogs. They kill us without reason. We can't live like this.

speaker: Slave
en: Gods! We pray to you, we beg your mercy. We beg for justice.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Listen up, you dogs. Some of you seem to think that because you were born in Lakonia, you have the right to live in Lakonia.

speaker: Slave
en: My goat is older than him! But he talks like he's king. He kills our men, steals our chickens, and everyone's terrified.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: You're allowed to live on the condition you produce for the Spartan army.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Spartans fear you more than you fear them.

speaker: Slave
en: But they're trained soldiers. We're just farmers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's one. You're many. Let's start a riot, shall we?

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Lately production has been horse shit!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Watch this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your face looks like horse shit!

speaker: Slave
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Told you, starting a riot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then stop killing our men and stealing our chickens!

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: You think I want to be here? I'd rather be in Sparta, fighting or fucking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You couldn't fight or fuck your way out of a grain sack.

speaker: Slave
en: It's working!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We... also don't want you here!

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Sparta gives you everything! Land, protection from your enemies...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sparta is our enemy!

speaker: Slave
en: Yes!

speaker: Slave
en: Sparta is the enemy!

speaker: Slave
en: Sparta is the real enemy!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need protection! I want a pony!

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Who dares speak while I'm speaking?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've stolen our chickens for the last time! Down with the krypteia! Who's with me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka, I'll kill you myself!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The killing of helots ends now! You are one, we are many!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are one, we are many!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Down with the krypteia!

speaker: Atlas
en: Ah, you've arrived. I'm honored the Dikastes would accept my humble request.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're Atlas, I take it.

speaker: Atlas
en: In the flesh. I thank you for coming to see me. I'm sure you're very busy. The burden my father gave you is not a light one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your messenger told me it was urgent.

speaker: Atlas
en: Gravely urgent, indeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I seem to have a lot to do around here thanks to Poseidon, but if I can help, I will.

speaker: Atlas
en: A noble pursuit. As my messenger stressed, the situation is dire. The Dikastes is just who I need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, here I am.

speaker: Atlas
en: It's my brothers, the Archons. They have issues with the human populations under their control. Tensions between Isu and humans are mounting. Without order, the problems will grow severe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll try and use my position to help them where I can.

speaker: Atlas
en: Find Gadiros, Ampheres, and Azaes. Through your shining example, I hope they learn the valuable lessons in discipline they so desperately need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And if I help them, you're hoping it'll maintain the peace between Isu and humans.

speaker: Atlas
en: That's the plan. Poseidon should have known they weren't ready for the responsibility an Archon bears, but that's his failing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about Gadiros.

speaker: Atlas
en: You'll find him near the Arena hard at work planning his next exhilarating spectacle, I'm sure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What should I know about Ampheres?

speaker: Atlas
en: He's probably off terrorizing people near the Fortified Doma of Autochthonos. Make sure you don't sneak up on him, he's quite jumpy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about Azaes? Who is he?

speaker: Atlas
en: You'll find dear Azaes wherever there is humanitarian work to be done. I heard there were some issues near the Doma of Ampheres.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We have Archons where I'm from. Do they fulfill the same duties?

speaker: Atlas
en: They are charged with overseeing and ruling the humans of Atlantis, ensuring all live comfortably and peacefully. A job at which I fear they're failing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There always seems to be unrest between the two races. The underworld and Elysium were no different.

speaker: Atlas
en: Time passes and tensions keep building. I expected my father to handle it, but Atlantis grows steadily worse, and no one wants to see what could happen if precautions are not taken.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the Archons and make sure their problems are taken care of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's one Archon helped. I hope they're all not this intense.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just one more Archon to go. Maybe I should just do their jobs, too?

speaker: Atlas
en: Dikastes, welcome back. I'm glad you could be here to witness this momentous occasion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are the Archons in chains?

speaker: Atlas
en: I invited my dear siblings here for one final lesson in leadership.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It looks like an execution to me.

speaker: Atlas
en: Every experience in life should be a lesson. Including death. You've been to the underworld, so I know you understand what these fools do not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You asked me to help the Archons. I did. Their problems are solved.

speaker: Atlas
en: Their problems only existed because they couldn't perform the duties their roles demanded.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to make you pay for this.

speaker: Atlas
en: Calm down, Kassandra. I didn't deceive you as much as you think. My brothers' problems were real and did need solving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Careful, Atlas. I am the Dikastes. If anyone is passing judgment here, it's me.

speaker: Atlas
en: Don't presume to think you can tell me what to do. The authority of your position doesn't extend to my palace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're going to murder your brothers? For what?

speaker: Atlas
en: For order... For peace... For Atlantis!

speaker: Kassandra
en: For Atlas, you mean.

speaker: Atlas
en: I am the rightful heir to Atlantis. I should be the Dikastes! I cannot defy Poseidon's will, but these fools don't deserve their power. I'll be a better Archon in their stead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Once Poseidon finds out what you've done, he won't let you get away with it.

speaker: Atlas
en: That is our way—the way of progress. You are not one of us. I've seen your compassion to those who dwell in this city. Perhaps our ways are not as perfect as Poseidon thinks they are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Parents do what they think is best, but it doesn't mean they're always right. We have to look after each other no matter what we're told.

speaker: Atlas
en: Wise, Dikastes. I respect your decision... for the moment.

speaker: Atlas
en: Our father always encouraged us to compete with each other. If he were here, he'd execute them himself, just as you executed those poor humans in the Arena.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They were criminals!

speaker: Atlas
en: And the "resistance"? Face it, Dikastes, if the roles were reversed, you'd pass the same judgment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You might need someone new to take lessons from, Atlas.

speaker: Atlas
en: I am my own teacher.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Killing your brothers is a waste. Teach them to learn from their mistakes, and they'll do whatever you say. They can't do that if they're dead.

speaker: Atlas
en: I watched you help my brothers. You always found solutions that tried to preserve life. Some of my kind view humans as a resource to be sacrificed. If we want them to progress, we must be an example.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We all look up to someone. I think they look up to you.

speaker: Atlas
en: Wise, Dikastes. I respect your decision... for the moment.

speaker: Atlas
en: Their ultimate failure was their lack of decisiveness. When you needed to act, you did without hesitation. But for what? To put on a show in the Arena?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They were criminals!

speaker: Atlas
en: And the "resistance"? Face it, Dikastes, if the roles were reversed, you'd pass the same judgment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You might need someone new to take lessons from, Atlas.

speaker: Atlas
en: I am my own teacher.

speaker: Atlas
en: You tried, my brothers, but regrettably your services are no longer required.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlas, you're insane!

speaker: Atlas
en: They weren't just a threat to me, Dikastes. In time, they'd have threatened your authority, too. You should be thanking me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what now?

speaker: Atlas
en: If you're going to one day rule this city, Kassandra, you're going to have to learn a very important lesson.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's what I get for helping you? A lecture?

speaker: Atlas
en: Just some words of advice. Nothing in Atlantis is what it seems at face value. This city is old, and those that call it home are even older. You have helped me, Dikastes, and for that you have my thanks.

speaker: Key fragment
en: This is half of a strange, broken disk-shaped key. It has unusual symbols engraved into its surface, but their purposes are unclear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't over, Atlas.

speaker: Atlas
en: On the contrary. I'm done here.

speaker: Burn the Black Flag
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Burn Their Future
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Burned Hopes
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Burned Men and Broken Skulls
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Burning Booty
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Priestess
en: We've been expecting you. Please follow me.

speaker: Priestess
en: She's instructed me to take good care of you before she arrives. Your shoulders must be aching. I'm sure I can help loosen you up before Diona arrives.

speaker: Diona
en: Sure you don't want to reconsider?

speaker: Diona
en: You look like you're ready to go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Securing Kythera can wait.

speaker: Diona
en: Good, because

speaker: Diona
en: I can't.

speaker: Diona
en: By the F-f-fates!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did she leave already?

speaker: Priestess
en: Yes, quite awhile ago in fact.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The High Priestess could be in grave danger. We don't have time for this.

speaker: Diona
en: Your loss. Fine, I'll fetch the scout and have them give us their report.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Diona said something about the scouts and their report. Where are they?

speaker: Priestess
en: Diona is done with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka.

speaker: Cult Protector
en: That's enough charades, priestess. We'll finish the job.

speaker: Cult Protector
en: Diona's done with you, misthios! Now, die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You! What's going on?

speaker: Priestess
en: I-I was just doing as I was told. Diona told me to take you to the garden.

speaker: Priestess
en: Please don't kill me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did they attack me? I freed these men myself!

speaker: Priestess
en: Diona played you like she did the High Priestess. The captain you killed was a leader for her sister's reinforcements. A-and the poison was to be used against you if you proved too dangerous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll show that snake exactly how dangerous I am.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why is Diona doing this to her own people?

speaker: Priestess
en: Diona hates her sister. She's been second-best all her life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So she joined the Cult to take power?

speaker: Priestess
en: I never expected her to take it this far.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to kill this traitor.

speaker: Priestess
en: She's on her way to kill the High Priestess at the altar north of the temple. You'll have to hurry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The altar? Good. Aphrodite will have a sacrifice tonight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Diona! Where is she?

speaker: Priestess
en: She has the High Priestess. By the Altar of Aphrodite... Follow the road ahead... And hurry

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're identical twins?! Don't move or I'll cut you both down!

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank the Fates! They were going to kill me and blame it on you! Strike Diona down!

speaker: Unknown
en: She's Diona! Her jealousy and bitterness have driven her to work with the Cult. My own sister!

speaker: Unknown
en: This is madness! She's Diona! And she's conspired with the Cult to usurp my position as High Priestess!

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't be deceived, misthios! They've set this final trap to fool you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't believe you're twins.

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: She's always been jealous of my success, mercenary. Living in my shadow has finally broken her. Kill her, now!

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: Lived in my shadow?! I loved you, Diona. I never wanted to be your superior.

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: Misthios, you must kill her before she lets the Cult take over Kythera! It pains me, but it must be done.

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: You wouldn't feel a thing, you monster—I'm not sure you ever have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The High Priestess will know what was in the note from her handmaiden.

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: "Do not trust the Fates"!

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: How could you possibly know that?

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: Her end must have been so tragic she renounced the Fates. The poor girl, it was all my fault. I sent her to spy on you, and you had her killed when she threatened to expose you!

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: Don't listen to her lies! I am the High Priestess!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could just kill you both. Maybe I should.

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: Kill us both?! You truly think they care which one of us lives or dies?

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: She speaks true! By the Fates, with both of us dead, the Cult will simply send their own High Priestess to fill the void!

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: You would know what the Cult would do, wouldn't you, snake?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I let you settle this yourself?

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: Walk away and you'll have more blood on your hands! Diona will surely slay me!

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: Snake! She knows I am the one who will perish. If you do nothing, the fall of Kythera will be all your fault.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough!

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: Slay Diona where she stands!

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: Do the right thing, misthios! Slay Diona!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shut up!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You! I see right through you, Diona. It's over.

speaker: Unknown (right)
en: By the Fates, I'll kill you both!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your Cult leader has been sniffed out, High Priestess.

speaker: Eritha
en: My own sister.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Siblings...

speaker: Eritha
en: I hated her. But, I loved her too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know how that feels.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Her true nature was clear.

speaker: Eritha
en: I loved her despite all she's done over the years. That love blinded me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It did.

speaker: Eritha
en: You've secured Kythera for me, misthios. Now, about the Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good thing I killed the right priestess.

speaker: Eritha
en: Indeed. As High Priestess it is my duty to call out to the wayward and return them to Aphrodite's bosom. And if you've ever been to Pephka and met its inhabitants, you'll see why divine intervention is their only salvation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never been.

speaker: Eritha
en: Lucky you. One of my priestesses was sent there and came back... rattled. She spoke of a man—Melite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about him?

speaker: Eritha
en: The people living in Pephka are terrified of him. He runs some shady operations, but what exactly, I can't be sure. Maybe this will be of help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, High Priestess.

speaker: Eritha
en: Now, if you'll excuse me, it is time to rebuild. Chaire. The Cult of Kosmos is in Pephka, misthios. Seek out Melite and destroy him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You! You haven't fooled me. It's over, Diona!

speaker: Unknown (left)
en: You idiot. Aphrodite aid me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Don't trust the Fates?" This is the note I gave the High Priestess

speaker: Diona
en: By the Fates! What have you done, my beautiful stranger?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You snake.

speaker: Diona
en: You slayed Kythera's dear High Priestess? They're going to be very cross with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And now I'm going to kill her sister.

speaker: Diona
en: I won't go down as easy. I bite, remember? I always bite!

speaker: Zoe
en: Let me go! Let me go! Let me out!

speaker: Zoe
en: You there! Artemis sent you to save me!

speaker: Zoe
en: Many thanks, two-legs! It's not safe to speak here though... Meet me behind the temple in Chios city.

speaker: Zoe
en: Two-legs! Over here!

speaker: Zoe
en: Blessing to you, two-legs. I am Zoe, Daughter of Artemis. Thanks for freeing me from the stone-dwellers earlier.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Two-legs? As opposed to what?

speaker: Zoe
en: Our four-legged brothers and sisters, of course. We are all equal—our souls are the same.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't put much thought into that.

speaker: Zoe
en: You should. We both have animal insticts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I learn new things every day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are these people you call "stone-dwellers"?

speaker: Zoe
en: They came from the west years ago, and cut down our forests and dug up our earth to build their stone buildings.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seemed to be in a tight spot—looked like you could use a hand.

speaker: Zoe
en: I was outnumbered. No room to run. Now that I'm free, I can plan our revenge against the stone-dwellers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Our revenge? Who else is involved?

speaker: Zoe
en: My four-legged brothers and sisters, the woodland creatures. We'll have our revenge on the stone-dwellers, who steal from our island.

speaker: Kassandra
