en: The stone-dwellers have many weapons and defense. They won't be easy targets.

speaker: Zoe
en: That's why I need my furry friends. Will you free them like you freed me? In return for your help, I'll give you my finest bow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Animals shouldn't be caged.

speaker: Zoe
en: I knew we were kindred spirits. My four-legged brethen are held in two camps in the deforested area. Release them all so they may run free once again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Consider it done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Her caged "family" is in the deforested area.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These wolves will want blood once released. I should be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Easy, four-legs. I'm a friend of Zoe's...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nice four-legs. Don't bite—I'm here to free you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've done what you've asked. Your "family" is free.

speaker: Zoe
en: Many thanks to you, warrior of Artemis! You're worthy of this bow. May the whole world know of your deeds!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make the most of it.

speaker: Drakios
en: Warriors! Heroes! Mercenaries of all types. Sign up here for the Battle of One Hundred Hands. Would you like to be rich? Are you the next Champion? You, misthios. You look like a true contender.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I met Roxana on Hydrea. She says you're the one to talk to about entering the battle on Melos.

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed I am. My name's Drakios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra. I'm interested in competing in this... What did you call it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this battle you're calling out about?

speaker: Drakios
en: My name's Drakios. It's a pleasure to meet you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra. Tell me about the Battle.

speaker: Drakios
en: The Battle of One Hundred Hands draws warriors from all corners of the Greek world to compete for a large purse. But as competitions go, it's also very deadly—a last person standing type of affair.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Killing is how I make my drachmae. This battle will be no different.

speaker: Drakios
en: It's true. You have the look of a mythical hero about you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I expect future generations to sing songs in my honor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do my best work in the shadows. Not sure how I'd fare on an open battlefield...

speaker: Drakios
en: It's true that only the best-trained have a hope of glory in the Battle of One Hundred Hands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I make no promises.

speaker: Drakios
en: If you join the Battle, you'll have the chance to prove your mettle against the best. And because the Battle is backed by the most powerful and influential people in the Greek world, the purse is always growing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you mean the people I think you mean, then I would like to meet them and... have a few words.

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed. They are the kind of people I would never speak about openly. You know, you do look like someone I've met before, another fierce warrior. Family resemblance, perhaps?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean Deimos? Then this Battle is backed by the Cult.

speaker: Drakios
en: Of course I can't talk about that. Not with any old challenger. But become the Champion of the Battle of One Hundred Hands, and I'll tell you all I know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to fight in the Battle.

speaker: Drakios
en: I thought you might. The only rule is that every competitor must train with another competitor, and they must vouch for each other.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already met Roxana on Hydrea.

speaker: Drakios
en: So I've heard. She was going to be my top recommendation as she's amongst our highest-ranked contenders. If you can train with her, then there is certainly a place for you in the Battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you can direct me to a worthy training partner.

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed, indeed. One of our top-ranked competitors is looking for a training companion. Roxana. She spars on Hydrea, the island just north of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What started the tradition of a free-for-all battle on Melos?

speaker: Drakios
en: I started it with some financial support from the powerful people I mentioned. The metaphor is that each combatant is battling a Hecatoncheir.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The creature with fifty heads and one hundred hands.

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed. By defeating all the competitors, it's as if the Champion has slain the creature itself - quite an achievement. Not something to be attempted by the weak.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Indeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you know about Roxana?

speaker: Drakios
en: She's from a long line of aspiring champions. Indeed, virtually her entire family has tried to win the Battle of One Hundred Hands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspiring champions.

speaker: Drakios
en: None of them were as skilled as Roxana, it must be said.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you become the person who organizes the Battle?

speaker: Drakios
en: I was an up-and-coming merchant in these parts... Down on my luck, it turned out. Owed a few favors, then some powerful people called in those favors. Turned out to be good for me. Blood sports are big business on Melos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These powerful people you mentioned. They're the Cult of Kosmos, aren't they?

speaker: Drakios
en: The mysterious ones. You want to meet them. I know, but it will have to wait.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How long?

speaker: Drakios
en: I stay close with all of my champions. If you win the Battle, it's something we can discuss over victory wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready to compete.

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed. Roxana tells me your training went well. Meet me inside the city gates. The Battle will begin soon.

speaker: Drakios
en: You haven't yet finished your training. You do seem capable enough. If you gave me a heavy bag of drachmae, however, I might be able to waive that requirement.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd rather not bother with the training.

speaker: Drakios
en: The winner's purse will reflect your contribution, misthios. The Battle will commence soon. Meet me inside the city gates when you're ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I already finished my training with Roxana.

speaker: Drakios
en: Ha! Indeed, show me a misthios, and I'll show you a liar. Nice try.

speaker: Herodianos
en: Eagle Bearer! My name is Herodianos, second to Thaletas in battle. The dogs of war howl for blood, and thanks to you, Sparta now howls back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a lot of howling.

speaker: Herodianos
en: And thanks to your victory against the Athenian fleet at sea, their best troops are at the bottom of the Aegean. The day is as good as ours! Join us.

speaker: Herodianos
en: Fight with us. Together, we'll run our shields through their skulls, and spears through their hearts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd be honored to fight with Sparta.

speaker: Herodianos
en: To battle!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should find Natakas.

speaker: Natakas
en: Father almost killed her when they first met. If I hadn't stopped them...

speaker: Kleta
en: Really? Who do you think would've won?

speaker: Natakas
en: Um...

speaker: Darius
en: I can handle myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good, we're all here...

speaker: Kleta
en: We've done everything we set out to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now, to get the stranded people out of Achaia...

speaker: Natakas
en: The Tempest is on her way to install the Chimera's Breath on the Skylla.

speaker: Darius
en: But we have the Chimera's Breath now... The Tempest will never know what hit her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Without the Chimera's Breath, she doesn't stand a chance. I am Poseidon's Chosen, after all.

speaker: Kleta
en: What?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've done what we can to prepare.

speaker: Darius
en: Now we have to execute.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll surprise the Tempest. Barnabas and I will launch a sea attack. Using the Chimera's Breath to disable the Skylla will be our best chance to get everyone off the coast.

speaker: Kleta
en: The merchant ships

speaker: Kassandra
en: The distraction should buy time for them to leave.

speaker: Darius
en: Natakas and I will make sure everyone is onboard the ships. This is our chance to leave Achaia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Darius is right, Natakas. You should be on those ships. Both of you. They're your way out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Order knows both of you are on those ships, you'll be in trouble. If you're caught on the water, you'll have no way out.

speaker: Darius
en: What do you think, Natakas?

speaker: Natakas
en: It's our only chance.

speaker: Kleta
en: You have to take it.

speaker: Darius
en: We will.

speaker: Natakas
en: We'll need somewhere to stay until then... Somewhere that won't raise suspicion.

speaker: Kleta
en: I know just the place... A house on the hill near Dyme.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go there now.

speaker: Natakas
en: Look at this place...

speaker: Kleta
en: It belonged to a friend of mine. He tried getting out of Achaia, but... he didn't make it.

speaker: Kleta
en: I need to prepare the others. See you two soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go ahead. I'll meet you there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's your father?

speaker: Natakas
en: Out. He does that sometimes. He'll be back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This house...

speaker: Natakas
en: Kleta said it belonged to a friend of hers. He tried getting out of Achaia, but... didn't make it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see.

speaker: Natakas
en: There's something about this place...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a beautiful place. Peaceful.

speaker: Natakas
en: I know. Too bad we won't stay...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's nothing special.

speaker: Natakas
en: I like it. It's peaceful. Too bad we won't stay...

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what's next?

speaker: Natakas
en: We'll probably keep running. As always.

speaker: Natakas
en: At least there's wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At least there's wine.

speaker: Natakas
en: What have you done!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stop it.

speaker: Natakas
en: This is how I grew up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But seriously, your father is a very capable man.

speaker: Natakas
en: He is. But emotionally.... He's hard to open up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's hard to make friends for people like us. Living on the move, as we do.

speaker: Natakas
en: Though, we've met each other.

speaker: Kassandra
en: To our friendship.

speaker: Natakas
en: To our friendship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka.

speaker: Natakas
en: This reminds me of when we met in Makedonia—we ate boar beneath the stars. It was the first time in a long time that I felt home. I haven't felt it since... Until tonight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then let's make the most of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should find Darius and the others. The stranded people are probably at the docks already.

speaker: Kleta
en: Eagle Bearer. Over here.

speaker: Natakas
en: The boats will be ready soon. Be safe, Kassandra.

speaker: Darius
en: Eagle Bearer. Thank you. For everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My friends. It's probably the last I'll ever see of them.

speaker: Kleta
en: The last time I saw my Phila, we were arguing. We always did. I wish I had told her how much she meant to me. How proud of her I was. Now that she's back, I'm scared I won't recognize her.

speaker: Kleta
en: Real connections with people are rare, Kassandra. We shouldn't be too quick to let them go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Real connections are hard to find. I may be letting one go right now... I don't know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a misthios. I can't afford connections.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Captain! Hey, Captain!

speaker: Darius
en: What's going on?

speaker: Barnabas
en: A massive fleet has gathered nearby. They seem to be waiting for something, but we don't know what.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Tempest.

speaker: Kleta
en: The ship... These people...

speaker: Kassandra
en: She knows. Somehow she knows.

speaker: Kleta
en: They're going to kill us all in one swift blow!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We won't be destroyed. I'll sink every last ship.

speaker: Kleta
en: How?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't take on an entire fleet...

speaker: Barnabas
en: We have to do something, Captain!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas, ready the ship for battle. And the Chimera's Breath.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Aye, Captain! She's ready to go. Let's send this storm straight to Hades.

speaker: Barnabas
en: It isn't ready yet. We haven't even finished assembling it! I'll need

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll start without it. Keep working.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Aye...

speaker: Darius
en: Natakas and I can handle things here. Good luck, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas should be on the Adrestia by now. I need to hurry!

speaker: Cannibal Annihilation
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Lykinos
en: My dear Kassandra! Over here. Do you have a moment? I was hoping to have the chance to thank you for all you've done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you have in mind?

speaker: Lykinos
en: Poet may be my day job, but there's more to me than that. I'm also a very talented cook. Allow me to make you a fabulous meal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like that.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Great! There's just one thing... I'll need a little help hunting down some ingredients. Literally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're treating me, you said?

speaker: Lykinos
en: After all we've been through together, surely you can agree that I'm a lover, not a fighter?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A lover, huh? We'll see.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I hope so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For how many bandits I've killed for you, it's pretty safe to say you're not a fighter.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I have to compensate somehow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you need me to hunt?

speaker: Lykinos
en: This dish calls for venison. Any of the beasts wandering nearby should do. Meet me at the cliffs near the Hypermnestra Camp once you find some.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a start, but Lykinos will need more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This should be plenty of meat for Lykinos's dinner.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Beautiful view.

speaker: Lykinos
en: It certainly is. Did you manage to hunt down our food?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's the meat.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Perfect, I'll get started. Please, make yourself comfortable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was delicious.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I told you I could cook. Was the food worth it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The company was certainly worth it. I'm having a really nice time.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I can hardly believe someone like you wants to spend time with someone like me. I have truly been blessed by the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A few deer are no match for a mighty Misthios.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I wish I had your skill... and confidence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fighter or not, I'm sure it takes a lot to be a renowned poet in Athens.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I, uh, may have exaggerated my accomplishments as a poet a bit earlier. The truth is... I'm not just home for a visit. I ran out of drachmae in Athens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why lie to your brother about this? Or... to me?

speaker: Lykinos
en: Timotheos has always been my father's son. In every way. They both fought for Athens. Both worked in the family business. Timotheos's path was never for me, so I left for Athens to strike out on my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're afraid of what he'll think.

speaker: Lykinos
en: He'll say it was irresponsible for me to leave in the first place. And he's right, I don't have any drachmae or means to earn it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If poetry really is your passion, then you should keep at it.

speaker: Lykinos
en: If you really think so...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're an amazing cook, Lykinos. If you're looking for a way to make a living, you should start there.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I guess everyone needs to eat. Besides, any skill that impresses you is worth pursuing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You never answered my question, though. Why lie to me about your career?

speaker: Lykinos
en: Isn't it obvious? I didn't want to appear a failure to you. From the moment I met you, I knew you were amazing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just someone that's had to fight everyday of my life.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Still, you saved my life, Kassandra. I'll never forget that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I'm glad I did. This has been nice, Lykinos.

speaker: Lykinos
en: It really has.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You might not see it yourself, but I think you're pretty amazing, too

speaker: Lykinos
en: Even after everything I just told you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would I care if you failed at being a poet. Poetry isn't useful.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I may not be making any money as a poet, but it's still my passion in life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lykinos, I actually like you more for being honest with me.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Really?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. I want to know the real you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Poet or not, you're still charming.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Glad you think so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Definitely.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Kassandra, ever since I met you, it's as if the weaver of wiles herself possessed me. I can hardly resist you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Aphrodite's speaking, you should listen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've got time, Lykinos. Let's just enjoy the night.

speaker: Lykinos
en: As long as you're around, I'll revel in your company.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've barely seen what I'm capable of. I've faced trials you wouldn't believe.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Still, you saved my life, Kassandra. I'll never forget that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I'm glad I did. This has been nice, Lykinos.

speaker: Lykinos
en: It really has.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have your malákes Tokens. No more games, no more schemes to rob me of my drachmae— It's time to slay a Minotaur!

speaker: Leiandros
en: Absolutely, misthios! No problem! But first! Perhaps you'd like to buy back your exquisite, finely-crafted Trial Tokens? This offer will expire in

speaker: Kassandra
en: BY THE GODS!

speaker: Leiandros
en: They, uh make for fantastic gifts!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's strange... but I would like something to remember Pephka by.

speaker: Token of Strength
en: This Token is acquired by completing the Pre-Trail of Strength in Lato, proving one's worthiness to fight the great Minotaur.

speaker: Token of Accuracy
en: This Token is acquired by completing the Pre-Trail of Accuracy in Lato, proving one's worthiness to fight the great Minotaur.

speaker: Token of Endurance
en: This Token is acquired by completing the Pre-Trail of Endurance in Lato, proving one's worthiness to fight the great Minotaur.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not. Another. Drachma.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Oh but champion, surely you want something to help you remember the Pephka Pre-Trials?!

speaker: Leiandros
en: I—sorry. Sorry sorry sorry.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Then all that's left is facing our star attraction himself—THE MINOTAUR! Are you ready to meet your doom?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If your "Pre-Trials" are anything to go by, yes. Yes, I am.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Well, good! GREAT! I WANT you to fight the Minotaur! You'll find the beast in the depths of the Cave of the Brave on the Dikte Plateau. Two other warriors have just completed their Pre-Trials—you can speak to them for more information. They'll join you when you're ready to, you know, die horrifically.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've come all this way—join us.

speaker: Leiandros
en: No, no, no, no. I have a very important... pottery lesson to attend! So...

speaker: Civilian
en: Help! Somebody help me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's the problem?

speaker: Civilian
en: My husband is missing. He went out fishing yesterday near Anaphi and hasn't returned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your husband is a poor fisherman if he can't take care of himself at sea.

speaker: Civilian
en: He's a great fisherman. It's... it's something else

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You must miss him.

speaker: Civilian
en: This is more than a wife missing her husband. I truly fear he's in danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In danger of what?

speaker: Civilian
en: Pirates. They were spotted in the area recently. I told him it was too dangerous, but we needed the drachmae to pay Swordfish.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about Swordfish.

speaker: Civilian
en: My husband knows more about him than I do. Please save him, and he'll tell you anything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: If pirates got to him, he may already be dead.

speaker: Civilian
en: I can't give up hope. He has a fast ship - if he saw the pirates, he'd head to the nearest shore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could rescue your husband, for a price.

speaker: Civilian
en: Please! I'll find a way to pay. Just get him back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll look for your husband. Where should I start?

speaker: Civilian
en: His favorite fishing spot is on the west coast of Anaphi, north of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If he's alive, I'll find him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your wife sent me to find you.

speaker: Civilian
en: Praise Poseidon. The pirates were waiting for high tide to attack.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need to leave now. I'll escort you back to Heraklion.

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm right behind you.

speaker: Civilian
en: I owe you beyond measure. How can I repay you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My services are expensive.

speaker: Civilian
en: I - of course. You're worth every drachma. There would be more, but Swordfish already took his cut.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's enough widows in this world - we didn't need another. I was happy to help.

speaker: Civilian
en: We're behind on our payments to Swordfish, so your kindness is appreciated. But here, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Swordfish? You don't need to worry about him anymore. He's dead.

speaker: Civilian
en: Dead?

speaker: Civilian
en: He may be gone, but there will always be someone who takes advantage of the honest and the weak.

speaker: Civilian
en: Still... Thank you, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about Swordfish.

speaker: Civilian
en: Swordfish... even his name - I last saw him many years ago, diving for treasure around Fisherman's Beacon. I haven't seen him since. But his presence is felt everywhere in Heraklion. He's here, somewhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should check out the waters near the beacon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I picked up your message on the board. What's happening?

speaker: Woman
en: The midwife from the village usually comes for plants I grow for her pharmika, but she's very late.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you think something has happened to her?

speaker: Woman
en: I hope not, but she usually comes up through the barley field. I did see a wolf running throuhg there the other day...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to hunt and kill this wolf, then?

speaker: Woman
en: That's exactly it. Will you do it for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can count on me.

speaker: Woman
en: I owe you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Woman
en: Misthios! Has the beast been slain?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The beast is dead.

speaker: Woman
en: Honest pay for honest work, misthios. Take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: There's always been a rivalry between the islands. After all, Naxos used to control Paros and Andros. They're envious of our craftsmen too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And now?

speaker: Myrrine
en: They think they "deserve" expansion. Their oligarch demands their wings spread wide. But we'll clip their wings before that happens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They don't know who they're up against.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You remind me of Nikolaos. You fight just like him; ruthless and cunning. He would be proud.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never forgotten what you both taught me. I had a good education.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I wanted you to be unstoppable. And you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nikolaos might have played the part of my father, but he wasn't. He tried to kill me.

speaker: Myrrine
en: What he did was wrong, Kassandra. I hated him for it, but he did love you in his own way - I can assure you of that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The real world taught me better. When someone wants your head, you have to learn to save your neck.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I know exactly what you mean.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to know about my real father.

speaker: Myrrine
en: How did you know?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was told.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Nikolaos? You saw him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: In Megaris, yes.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Nikolaos was your father. He was the man who raised you... until he took his Spartan duty too far.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He mentioned another. What can you tell me about him?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I always hoped you would never need to discover the truth, but there are things you need to know if we are to stop the Cult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Myrrine
en: He sought me out before I knew your fa... Nikolaos. I've not heard from him in a long time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why didn't you tell me the truth about Nikolaos?

speaker: Myrrine
en: You were just a child, you looked up to him. I couldn't bring myself to take that from you then, and I'm sorry you know now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been sheltered from the truth long enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Knowing would only have complicated things.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You still had a right to know the truth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You did what you thought was best, like any mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to you in Argolis after that night?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I found your brother and rushed to a young doctor's apprentice, Hippokrates. I thought I'd lost you... I wasn't ready to lose you both.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I spoke with him recently. That night still haunts him.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I was heartbroken when the healers in Asklepios told me Alexios was dead. The two of you were my whole world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But he did live, they lied to you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: They... must have realized he was special and handed him over to the Cult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll save him from the Cult, mater. We'll get him back.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The Cult is insidious, once they have their claws in, they don't let go. I fear he is beyond saving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found you, didn't I? I know we can save him, together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's been brainwashed. He believes he is doing what's right.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Some have successfully abandoned the Cult. We could bring him back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We owe it to him to try.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't understand why the Cult targeted our family.

speaker: Myrrine
en: There are many reasons, lamb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did we ever do to them?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Now that we're reunited, it's more a question of what we could do to them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They fear us.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Your ancestors have been a thorn in their side for generations. They've decided we need to be eliminated to ensure their plans come to fruition.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult will pay for all they've done to our family and the Greek world.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You are mighty, lamb, but you cannot defeat that beast with sword and spear alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll use any weapon I can to make them suffer as we have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it's our family they fear, we'll reunite and give them a reason to be afraid.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Many have tried to stop them and failed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We are not those people. Where others failed, we will succeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know you left Sparta, but how did you end up on this island?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I couldn't stand by Nikolaos after what he did—I had to get out of Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So why here?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I saw an opportunity to help people, to grow something. I was elected to rule and protect this island from those who would ruin what we've built.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've done some incredible things. Naxos is lucky to have you as its leader.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It's not been without its difficulties, but I'm proud of what we've achieved.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a pity there aren't more leaders like you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about Sparta? You know what's happening there, and it needs your help like Naxos once did.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I thought about returning on more than one occasion, but it was too painful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sometimes the most painful things are the things we should do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's continue this discussion somewhere the smell of death doesn't linger.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Ride with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The island is beautiful.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It is. Sparta has nothing on Naxian beaches.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sparta. All I remember is the bottom of Mount Taygetos.

speaker: Myrrine
en: When I brought you to the Pythia as a baby, she never said we would live a nightmare. She said you had such promise.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Pythia can't predict everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your general acted quickly—raising the alarm.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Timo knows Paros is a threat. They make their business clear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They can't be more clear than sending soldiers. There's no treaty?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Maybe there was, but it's long over. Now there's no mistaking them for anything but the enemy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An enemy I could help you defeat.

speaker: Myrrine
en: We'll discuss that later. But I think you're right.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The temple's coming along, Evandros.

speaker: Priest
en: It'll stay in ruins if we don't secure more donations. Soldiers can't get all the funds.

speaker: Myrrine
en: They can if you don't want the temple destroyed by our enemy. But I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Priest
en: It's a good deed, restarting construction. Lygdamis was a great man who deserves reverence.

speaker: Myrrine
en: His battles against corruption and oligarchy are lessons we all should remember. I do intend to finish the temple.

speaker: Priest
en: Thank you, Phoenix.

speaker: Myrrine
en: What a strange day it has been.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But a good one.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I've certainly had worse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me too.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You have grown into a remarkable woman, but I see the burden you carry on your shoulders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Finding you has lessened it, I think.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I'm glad, but I have wondered why the gods chose to reunite us now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think they felt it was about time our family found each other again.

speaker: Myrrine
en: If we want to be truly united, we have to find Alexios and rescue him from the Cult's grasp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So we can destroy the Cult once and for all.

speaker: Myrrine
en: If only it were that simple. You are mighty, but we cannot stop them alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They are the source of all our pain and they will cause more to many others unless we act.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I put that life behind me the moment I left Sparta. I have Naxos to worry about now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me help you here. We can safeguard Naxos and then hunt down the Cult together.

speaker: Timo
en: Myrrine, the is about to start.

speaker: Myrrine
en: By the gods! I'm sorry my sweet, I forgot. Prepare the horses - I'll be out shortly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The symposium?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I need to show the people their leader is strong and in control. Sometimes the face we show to the world needs to be one of strength, despite the chaos we harbor beneath. I will help you stop the Cult, but before I can leave Naxos I have to ensure it will survive without me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you need?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Paros has to be dealt with. We need to weaken their position. Once they're vulnerable, they will make a reckless decision, and we will strike.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you have in mind?

speaker: Myrrine
en: We must force the Paros fleet to engage us and destroy it, but my admiral, Euneas, is missing. His ship was sailing for Paros to engage in peace talks, and he never returned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, I'll find him.

speaker: Myrrine
en: If you need me, I'll be at the symposium. Although... try to look less intimidating should you choose to pay me a visit.

speaker: Aristomachos
en: Whatever you're after, you're too late. They're all gone... dead or mad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't understand. Who did this to you?

speaker: Aristomachos
en: I don't understand it myself. My brethen and I were drawn to this place, but madness took over. We fought over the artifact. One of them grabbed it and ran.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Grabbed the stele?

speaker: Aristomachos
en: Search the caves. That's where they'll be hiding. Beware though, they're beyond reason.

speaker: Stele Piece from the Cave of Madness
en: This stele piece has been used in some sacrifice. Dried blood obscures its text.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Was the stele influencing them in some way?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There may be some truth in this lore.

speaker: Eppie
en: Ugh! Is that blood on it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's otherwise undamaged. There are people claiming that it speaks to them. What could do that?

speaker: Eppie
en: Strange. I don't hear anything. Do you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Words of madmen... Perhaps the next pieces will tell us more.

speaker: Eppie
en: This one needs a good cleaning... Let's hope the remaining ones are fine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll search for the remaining steles.

speaker: Eppie
en: My peers will finally listen to what I have to say. It says the ritual will activate something. But what? What will happen when we have all of the pieces? Will it lead to a treasure? Some of the translations is lost on me. This passage speaks of worth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm... What else?

speaker: Eppie
en: Um. This passage mentions something about "inner vision." But... the meaning is unclear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's almost translated. Why aren't you happy?

speaker: Eppie
en: You tell me others are hearing things. They think it speaks to them. Yet I hear nothing. I feel nothing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is an important find. You said so yourself. Why does it matter what others say or feel?

speaker: Eppie
en: I know. I see that it's important from a logical perspective. But what if I can't experience it? And this mention of worth... What if it means I'm not worthy?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if the gods are not worthy of us? Look. We aren't done yet, right? So wait and see.

speaker: Eppie
en: You're right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's natural to have doubts. You've convinced me that this search for the past has a value beyond drachmae.

speaker: Eppie
en: That makes me happy. I just can't help but wonder what the gods think of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think what's important is what you think of yourself.

speaker: Eppie
en: Thank you, hero.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to dust yourself off and focus.

speaker: Eppie
en: You're right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should carry on.

speaker: Eppie
en: There are two locations to explore this time. There's a temple in the City of Orchomenos. It's near the harbor. The other stele is difficult to pinpoint. There are ruins along the coastline, near the altar for Iphigenia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, then. And cheer up. We're almost done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think that's everyone Priestess Hexione mentioned. Time to find her again.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Wondrous Eagle Bearer! Your name and glory drop from everyone's lips. My sisters and I wish to throw a grand festival in your honor. You will be the cherished guest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you insist.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: However, there is one more who could benefit from your attention. Chalkippe frets about her brother. In truth, he is a strange one, touched by madness... or perhaps a chosen of the gods.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Ah, here she is now. Speak to her, reassure her, and then we will celebrate!

speaker: Chalkippe
en: By the gods! It's you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's me.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: It's you! By the gods! My prayers are answered!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Speak to the Eagle Bearer, my child.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: You have come to help me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Um, I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Yes! Of course! It's my brother, Kallistratos. He's always been a bit odd, but this past year, I think the gods have cursed him. Uh, that is, I don't mean to offend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go on. Your brother.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: My brother's farm is a small way from the village. Always doing his own thing. I haven't seen him for days, but when I went to pass by, I heard terrifying noises! I think something might have happened, but I'm not brave enough to go see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take a look for you.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Thank you! Thank you, Eagle Bearer! You're too kind! Too generous! Too nice! Thank you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about your brother?

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Kallistratos always tries some new scheme or crazy idea. His last one was to breed chickens that would lay giant eggs. "Each egg to feed a family," he said, and he'd sell them far and wide and become rich.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you think happened to Kallistratos?

speaker: Chalkippe
en: I don't know! Maybe a lion or wolf got into the farm. Terrible noises nearly scared my hair white. I'm sure whatever it is would be no match for you, mighty Eagle Bearer! I pray he's all right,

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is your brother's farm?

speaker: Chalkippe
en: He has a large farmstead northeast of here. He doesn't take very good care of it, though. Always caught up in some crazy scheme.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll visit your brother's farm and see what's going on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is!

speaker: Kallistratos
en: Run for your life! You'll call the Ares Ornithes down upon us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The what now?

speaker: Kallistratos
en: Who are you supposed to be?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The misthios who saved your life? You could say thanks.

speaker: Kallistratos
en: Not sure you had to kill my best chickens, though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Watch your tongue, little man. I came on behalf of your sister, who showed proper respect. Don't make me angry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your sister sent me to check on you. Chalkippe was very worried and scared by the noises she heard. Looks like she was right to be concerned.

speaker: Kallistratos
en: So tell her I'm fine, already. Hmm, maybe I can get a goat from Messara and catch a lion and breed them somehow... Maybe with a snake... I'm sure I could make a fortune...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chalkippe, your brother is... something else. But he's alive and, I suppose, well.

speaker: Chalkippe
en: Thank you, Eagle Bearer! Yes, he is a difficult one. But you have answered my prayers! I will always be your devoted servant.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Uh...

speaker: Chalkippe
en: The priestesses have begun preparing a great feast in your honor for all of Linou to celebrate you! It will be magnificent!

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Kassandra! Calamity! Myrto has been struck down by illness!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Take me to her!

speaker: Polykleitos
en: The girl was thriled about the idea of the festival to honor you. She was rushing about, buzzing with excitement, when she suddenly collapsed.

speaker: Akatos
en: Please, Eagle Bearer. Can you do anything for her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did anyone see anything? Does she have any wounds?

speaker: Akatos
en: No, no insect or snake bites. But her brow burns with fever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What was Myrto doing when she got sick?

speaker: Akatos
en: She was preparing the meat you brought in for the festival, per the priestess's instructions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is Priestess Hexione now?

speaker: Akatos
en: I don't know. I overhead her calling out for help, telling people not to be scared, but she's vanished.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's strange behavior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll ask around and see if anyone else knows anything. And see if I can't find the priestess.

speaker: Thais
en: Misthios! Can I interest you in some lumber for your ship?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a lot of chopped trees... The lumber would be a fine addition to any ship.

speaker: Thais
en: Everyone knows the finest lumber comes from Chios.

speaker: Thais
en: But... the maláka in charge of Lesbos keeps trading our product with other city states. He's gaining influence, and we're losing profits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leaders have their reasons. Maybe his dealings help more than you know.

speaker: Thais
en: How is using our lumber to strengthen the fleets of other nations helping? No! He has his own interests at heart, not the interests of Lesbos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leaders have a duty to serve their people and their land.

speaker: Thais
en: Agreed. This leader is guided by self-interest and greed, pure and simple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then he's no leader.

speaker: Thais
en: Exactly. And if we remove the source of the problem, the problem will disappear with it. The people of Lesbos deserve to benefit from its resources.

speaker: Thais
en: Can I hire you to help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: As the gods would have it, I've already killed that corrupt nation leader.

speaker: Thais
en: Good. That malákas deserved to die. Take this drachmae as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can take care of the "problem."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find the leader of Lesbos?

speaker: Thais
en: He lives in Mytilene. When he's not at home, he's inspecting the troops in the fort or praying to his chosen god. You know, anything to avoid real work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lesbos is a bountiful place. Why does the leader use all of Chios's resources?

speaker: Thais
en: Damned if I know. We keep chopping down all our trees and killing all our animals for Mytilene. Soon we won't have anything left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll remove the problem in Mytilene for you.

speaker: Thais
en: When you've finished, I'll send the reward to your ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should look for the leader in his home, the fort, and the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. Another Cultist.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Talking in circles may work on others, Sokrates, but not on me.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I don't speak in circles, or any other shape. You answered one of my questions, and that brought another to mind.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: And another... And another...

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Kassandra! I knew you'd be back for more. I can't say it hasn't been on my mind... But, alas, we must save it for another time.

speaker: Alikibiades
en: Kassandra! I knew you'd change your mind after turning me down. Unfortunately, love must wait a little longer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever you say.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I hate to cut our conversation short, Sokrates, but I believe you've talked enough for the both of us. We must find another use for that mouth of yours.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Speak to him long enough, and you may find the smallest hint of knowledge veiled deep behind his... enthusiastic advances.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: A compliment and an insult in the same sentence. He truly is gifted. You've arrived at the perfect time. I have a friend named Sophanes who wants to become an Athenian citizen, but he needs a bit of help. Your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't wait to hear why it's my help he needs.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Any misthios would do, really, but you're my favorite. All you need to do is sign my friend's name on a little list.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There has to be a reason Sophanes can't sign the list himself.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Well, he would, but he isn't nearly as... able as you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Meaning?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Meaning you have skills he doesn't possess. He'd fail if he tried on his own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why Athens? Surely he is a citizen somewhere else already.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Everyone wants to be an Athenian citizen, even if they don't say so. Sophanes has a mind for politics, but can only participate as a citizen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't realize you had a list of mercenaries you favor... And I'm at the top?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Of course you are. Although, if you ask nicely, I would happily let you be on the bottom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This sounds simple. Now tell me why it isn't.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: There's the small matter that you'll have to enter the Metroon, where you're not allowed... And forge his name well enough, of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So he's trying to become a citizen illegally. You should have led with that.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'll try to remember that next time. The building you're looking for is near the agora. Be safe.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Did you forget what you're supposed to do, or did you just miss me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There, his name's been signed. Time to get back to Alkibiades.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: My favorite misthios returns.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sophanes's name is on the list, but it came at a price.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I see. Sometimes blood must be shed... You were the right misthios for the job.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And with good news, too.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: My favorite kind. You did it then?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I did. Sophanes's name is now on the citizen list.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Perfect! I knew you were the right misthios for the job.

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios, please. I could use your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What seems to be the problem?

speaker: Civilian
en: There is serious unrest in Kydonia, misthios. The guards and merchants are at each other's throats.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The guards are here to serve the locals... What's got them riled up?

speaker: Civilian
en: Taxes. The merchants refuse to pay the increased taxes, and the guards all too gleefully extract them.

speaker: Civilian
en: Their captain, Diokles, is more a bandit than a guard. This unrest is bad for business. I need you to quiet some of the outbursts around Kydonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A power-mad captain, civil unrest—sounds like serious work.

speaker: Civilian
en: Which would be seriously rewarded. I have precious gems, which I'm sure would appeal to someone such as yourself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd be happy to help.

speaker: Civilian
en: Good. You will find areas of tension around the agora, the eastern market, and the docks. Is there anything else I can tell you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm busy. You'll have to find someone else.

speaker: Civilian
en: Lives are at stake, misthios! You can't just ignore this. Please reconsider.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Should I use "any means necessary" to end this unrest?

speaker: Civilian
en: Ever the misthios, where a blade is the answer to all things. Yes, one way to quell unrest is to kill everyone involved, but sometimes simply talking will yield the best results.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the cause of all this is increased taxes, would it be easier to lower them?

speaker: Civilian
en: Don't you know all of the Greek world is at war?! War is expensive, and Kydonia needs fleets! She needs armies! We cannot be left defenseless.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned the guard captain, Diokles. Who is he?

speaker: Civilian
en: Not a man of the people, misthios. It's at his encouragement the guards put so much pressure on the merchants.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard everything I need to hear.

speaker: Civilian
en: Do what you must to bring order, but watch your back. There are people who seek to benefit from this civil unrest. We're counting on you, misthios.

speaker: Woman
en: You're scaring the children! Stop!

speaker: Civilian
en: And did your dog of a husband stop when we begged him to stop destroying our goods?

speaker: Woman
en: Take it up with him, then. Or the military! Please, leave us alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is this?

speaker: Man
en: Justice, misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That doesn't sound like "justice" to me.

speaker: Man
en: Why do you care? These are the families of the guards who beat us and harass us! This is what they deserve.

speaker: Man
en: These increased taxes are ridiculous—they choke the very life out of us. We must stand. We must fight!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There no need for violence, we can talk this over

speaker: Man
en: Talk?! They've smashed our wares, they've beaten us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They have, yes, and maybe they should have to pay—but this family has done nothing. This child has done nothing. They're innocent.

speaker: Man
en: But—a lesson must be learned! We must teach them not to mess with us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is not the way.

speaker: Man
en: They paid you off, didn't they?! You—you work for them! Have it your way, misthios. The woman and her child will not be harmed—but we're not done with you. We have our own scary mercenaries!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stop it Now!

speaker: Man
en: Or what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or I'll make you.

speaker: Man
en: You think a threat will stop us? Every day we're worse than threatened—we're beaten, abused. No, we don't bow to threats. We fight!

speaker: Woman
en: Thank you, misthios. Those bastards deserved to die.

speaker: Greek captain
en: Break every one of these! if the merchant gets in the way, break him, too.

speaker: Civilian
en: Stop! Please! I need to sell these, my family's livelihood depends on it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Please stop them, misthios! If they destroy all of this, my family will starve.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on here?

speaker: Greek captain
en: This maláka needs to pay his taxes like everyone else. Otherwise, we'll smash every last pot in the agora—Captain Diokles' orders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave the merchant alone. You've done enough.

speaker: Greek captain
en: Ha! You itching for a beating, misthios? We'll just have to smash you, too.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you, misthios! This is all I have left...

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...If that's what it takes to stop this, I'll destroy the rest of the wares.

speaker: Greek captain
en: Looks like you know your place, little misthios. Now, get to it.

speaker: Civilian
en: What have you done?! This was my livelihood.

speaker: Civilian
en: You have no right to hold us here. Release our goods at once!

speaker: Greek captain
en: We have every right if you don't pay your taxes like you're supposed to.

speaker: Civilian
en: You must be mad if you think we're going to cough up even more drachmae for the military.

speaker: Greek captain
en: You test my patience, old man. Move away, these goods are due for confiscation.

speaker: Civilian.
en: You can't do this! What malákas city is this, where the guards prey on their own people?!

speaker: Greek captain
en: It's simple—you avoid your taxes, we take your stuff. Now, step away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or what?

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios! Please, talk some sense into these idiots. If we aren't allowed to continue doing our business, the economy of Kydonia will fall to ruin.

speaker: Greek captain
en: This does not concern you, misthios. This is the law of the land! If they give up the goods, all will end well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Laws are for the weak. People should live freely. These merchants won't pay you a single drachma.

speaker: Greek captain
en: You will regret this. Kill the misthios!

speaker: Greek captain
en: We have every right if you don't pay your taxes like you're supposed to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are safe now. Those guards won't bother you anymore.

speaker: Civilian
en: Maybe for today, misthios. But they'll be back at some point.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your takes will go a long way in helping Kydonia. You should respect the law.

speaker: Civilian
en: The military barely does a thing around here, and expects a bigger and bigger payout each year? Nonsense!

speaker: Greek captain
en: You see, mishthios? Nothing will get through their thick skulls. But my fists will. Now get out of my way before I take you out, too!

speaker: Greek captain
en: You test my patience, old man. Move away, these goods are due for confiscation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Peace has been restored. That merchant better have my gems ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka... What happened here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like Captain Diokles denied me my payment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you must be Diokles.

speaker: Greek Brute
en: Ha, look who it is! You want to meddle in Kydonia's affairs? It's going to cost you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At least the captain had the decency to keep my gems on him. Never stand between a misthios and her payday.

speaker: Clear the Land for Athens

speaker: Civilian
en: Maláka... What will I do now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Civilian
en: I've dedicated my life to becoming a Daughter of Artemis, but they said I'm not tough enough to join them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Following others is a sign of weakness.

speaker: Civilian
en: But I've followed Artemis for so long...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's human nature to want to fit in.

speaker: Civilian
en: Being part of something is all I've ever wanted. Now I'm just a feather on the wind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your life is your own. If you've lost your purpose, find another one.

speaker: Civilian
en: A new life purpose? I wouldn't even know where to begin.

speaker: Civilian
en: No! I'm not giving up that easily. I have an idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Civilian
en: I'll join them anyway! I'll infiltrate their village and live among them. Can you help me? I'll pay you all the drachmae I have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Daughters of Artemis are dangerous, and if you're found out...

speaker: Civilian
en: I accept the risks. What I'll need you to do is get me a piece of their armor, headgear, and boots.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find the boots?

speaker: Civilian
en: There's a cave in the cliffs on the western side of the Daughters' village where they train new recruits. They tested me there, but I left my boots behind when they kicked me out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any idea where I can find the armor you need?

speaker: Civilian
en: There's a small outpost camp just south of the Daughters' village. You'll find extra armor there. They barely defend it

en: Easy.

speaker: Civilian
en: Which is why it was recently overrun with beasts even they can't tame.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah.

en: Tell me where to find the headgear.

speaker: Civilian
en: You'll find it around the hut of the Daughters' most favored huntress, near the center of their village.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I have the gear.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you, misthios. You'll have to be stealthy to get the items, and please avoid harming any of the Daughters if you can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the hut of the favorite daughter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the cave where the boots are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's something different about this village.

speaker: Daughters of Artemis Headgear
en: This headgear is worn by only the best hunters of the Daughters of Artemis.

speaker: Daughters of Artemis Boots
en: These boots are perfect for sneaking up on the unsuspecting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The outpost camp.

speaker: Daughters of Artemis Chest Piece
en: Although battered, this chest piece has been recently polished.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've got the gear you asked for, but remember—the Daughters of Artemis are legendary warriors. If you choose to infiltrate them, it's likely you'll be killed.

speaker: Civilian
en: What choice do I have?

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios. I need a piece of armor, headgear, and boots from the Daughters of Artemis. Can you help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are these what you're looking for? They don't quite fit me.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you, misthios! I'll finally be able to infiltrate the Daughters of Artemis and join my sisters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You might want to reconsider. The Daughters of Artemis won't respond well to an intruder.

speaker: Civilian
en: What would you do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Find a new path that lets you really live.

speaker: Civilian
en: You're just like them. Thinking I'm not tough enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Taking a life isn't easy, and it can't be undone. You aren't a killer.

speaker: Civilian
en: You don't know me. I can do it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can see good in you. You're passionate, determined—why not help others?

speaker: Civilian
en: Really? You think I could do that?

speaker: Civilian
en: I know... I'll become a priestess—and join a temple! Thank you, misthios!

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios! Remember me? You convinced me not to infiltrate the Daughters of Artemis. You saved my life, though—I don't yet know what to do with it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a high price to pay for chasing what we want—maybe even death. You must be willing to pay it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Yes. This is something I must do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see him. There he is! Found him!

speaker: Soldier
en: Idiots... Stealing our supplies again. When will you learn not to mess with us?

speaker: Soldier
en: Stop your whining. Stop your crying.

speaker: Helot 1
en: Thank the gods! I'm alive!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can you tell me where the helot Rhode is?

speaker: Helot 1
en: Who's that? I'm free now, I don't care!

speaker: Helot 2
en: Thank you, thank you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know where I can find the helot called Rhode?

speaker: Helot 2
en: I know nothing!

speaker: Helot 3
en: You saved me. Thank you, misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you seen the helot named Rhode?

speaker: Helot 3
en: Yes, she was taken to the center of Aipeia. I heard she's going to meet her end there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The town center. I should hurry.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: You're making this worse for yourself!

speaker: Rhode
en: You made us steal the food. There's not enough to go around.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Shut up! It's not the first time you've been caught, and this time it's going to be the last.

speaker: Rhode
en: At least I'll go with a stomach full of bread!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Shut your mouth. That's what you get for taking what isn't yours. Your death shall be a warning to them all!

speaker: Rhode
en: I don't care who the food belongs to. We were hungry!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: If you're here for the show, I think you'll have a clearer view from down there with the rest. Who are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm angry, I'm impatient, and I'm out of time. So, I'm not here to talk.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: What do you mean? You want to kill this woman too?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not in the mood for mercy, so I suggest whoever wants to keep their limbs leave now.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Fine. Cowards, leave your honor at the door and run home with your tails between your legs. As for the brave—get the misthios!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: You're gonna get what you came for!

speaker: Rhode
en: Bread for the people, bread for the children!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Should've cut out your tongue, thief.

speaker: Rhode
en: Too bad!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: What are you doing here? You said I could leave if I wanted to.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I'll have to punish you now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for this woman.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Her? She got caught stealing from the kitchens again. We're under strict instructions from the commander to ensure that stops today.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need her alive. Release her, and no one gets hurt.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: There's a price for everything, misthios. We'll need drachmae to replenish our food supplies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll pay for her.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Well then, it seems that I forgot about the extra cost for our troubles. Torture is hard work, you know. Double it, and I'll give her to you.

speaker: Rhode
en: Hades! Don't give him a single drachma!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Shut up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, take your payment.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Actually, there's

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't. Push. It.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: OK, OK! Take this filthy malákas and go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough. I'm taking her... along with your heads.

speaker: Rhode
en: Yeah! Get 'em!

en: You picked the wrong side. Get the misthios!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: You're gonna get what you came for!

en: Bread for the people, bread for the children!

en: Should've cut out your tongue, thief.

en: Too bad!

en: What are you doing here? You said I could leave if I wanted to.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I'll have to punish you now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough. I'm taking her... along with your heads.

speaker: Rhode
en: Yeah! Get 'em!
