en: You picked the wrong side. Get the misthios!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: You're gonna get what you came for!

speaker: Rhode
en: Bread for the people, bread for the children!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Should've cut out your tongue, thief.

speaker: Rhode
en: Too bad!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: What are you doing here? You said I could leave if I wanted to.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I'll have to punish you now!

speaker: Rhode
en: That was close! Thanks, misthios! Good thing you came along. Bye!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait! I'm looking for the Commander. I was told you know something about him.

speaker: Rhode
en: The Commander... Oh, I know him alright. Brings back fond memories. I used to work for that malákas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This Commander sounds terrible.

speaker: Rhode
en: He's ruthless, misthios. He would work us till our hands were red and raw, and we'd bleed and cry until dawn. Even the children weren't spared. Which is why I have to pinch food when I can. It's never enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were lucky, I arrived just in time. How did you get caught?

speaker: Rhode
en: They caught me stealing one loaf of bread and sentenced me to death. So what if I stole from them ten other times? It's too much, too severe!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Point me to the Commander, and I'll stick my blade through his throat.

speaker: Rhode
en: You're looking to kill him? Great!

speaker: Rhode
en: Things are happening in Messenia, misthios. Look at how we're suffering... How the children suffer. There must be something better out there for them. I have a plan to get the children away from here. My son... and the others. Help the children, and I'll help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do it, but you better tell me where the Commander is.

speaker: Rhode
en: So kind of you, misthios! I promise, you'll find your target. Just don't gut him in front of the children.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help, but it'll cost you.

speaker: Rhode
en: What? You would ask for drachmae in a time of crisis such as this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A misthios has to eat, too.

speaker: Rhode
en: Fine, I'll give you whatever I have. Mostly bread crumbs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's your plan to get the children out?

speaker: Rhode
en: We have a fisherman nearby who is being paid handsomely for the job. We need to take the children to his boat near the docks, but we need to leave soon. Time is almost up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Rhode
en: Follow me!

speaker: Pebble
en: Mater!

speaker: Rhode
en: Hello my little Pebble. No time to talk, we need to go—now!

speaker: Pebble
en: Who's this?

speaker: Rhode
en: A misthios friend! She's going to help us get out of here.

speaker: Pebble
en: All right everyone. Mater says to follow the misthios. Stay in a group so we don't get lost.

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Stay in a group so we don't get lost!

speaker: Pebble
en: This is serious!

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: Do you have a hero name, misthios?

speaker: Pebble
en: A hero name is a code name only the greatest, bestest, heroes have. It's usually a combination of a cool animal and the weather.

speaker: Rhode
en: Tell her your hero names, children.

speaker: Pebble
en: Mine's Wolfstorm.

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Mine's Sharklightning!

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: Mine's...

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: He's Chickenrain!

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: I didn't choose that name! I hate you both!

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: Look who we have here.

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: Ahh!

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Scary man!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay back, children.

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: I knew I would find you here, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You caught me.

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: They were right, you're always at the center of the chaos. Now, why don't you step aside and let me do my job? I'll deal with you

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: And you after I take the children away. They have work to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why wait? I've been looking for you—thanks for sparing me the trouble. I can deal with you now.

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: Let's not waste any time then. I'll make an example out of your screams.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave the children out of this.

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: I'm going to have fun watching you drown in your own blood. Time to die!

speaker: Rhode
en: Cover your eyes, children! Don't look!

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: Make him pay! Impale him! Cut off his head! Roar!

speaker: Rhode
en: Language.

speaker: Commander Harpagos
en: Shut up! You children are too noisy. I'll make sure you all learn to hold your tongue when I'm done.

speaker: Pebble
en: He doesn't look very strong. Poke his eyes out!

speaker: Rhode
en: Go to the cove. Hurry, kids! A boat is waiting.

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: You need a hero name, misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why don't you choose one for me.

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Hmm...

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: Oh, oh! Eagle something! Since she has an eagle!

speaker: Pebble
en: Eaglethunder!

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Perfect!

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: You're one of us now!

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: Yay! You did it! You defeated the bad guys!

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Eaglethunder! Eaglethunder! Eaglethunder!

speaker: Pebble
en: That was super amazing!

speaker: Rhode
en: Misthios! You did it.

speaker: Rhode
en: It's time for you to go, little Pebble.

speaker: Pebble
en: You're... not coming?

speaker: Rhode
en: I can't. I have to stay here and work hard so I can visit you one day.

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: No... No! Where's my pater? Where's my mater?

speaker: Pebble
en: I can't be without you, mater. Who will hug me when I have a bad dream?

speaker: Rhode
en: Misthios, I—I'm not sure. Now that we're here, I don't know if I can bear to send them away.

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Don't make us go, please.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Children shouldn't be separated from their parents. You should stay.

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: I get to stay?

speaker: Pebble
en: Mater, we'll be together!

speaker: Helot Child (girl)
en: Pater! Pater!

speaker: Rhode
en: I'm happy my Pebble is staying, but is it the right choice?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be cruel to tear these families apart.

speaker: Rhode
en: It might be even more cruel to subject them to a life in Messenia. I don't know if I'll be able to protect them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have to go. Messenia is crawling with danger—it's not safe for children.

speaker: Helot Child (boy)
en: But what about our parents? What will happen to them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They want what's best for you. Now go, the boat is waiting.

speaker: Rhode
en: Chaire, my Pebble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Things will be better for them out there.

speaker: Rhode
en: You're right. If the children stayed, I don't know if we'd be able to protect them. I hope they have a better life ahead... Better than we could have given them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We will always fight for our children.

speaker: Rhode
en: Always.

speaker: Rhode
en: And you got your commander. Thank you, misthios. May our paths cross again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Need something?

speaker: Woman
en: Mercenary! I've heard you've had dealings with Anthousa. Tell me, how do you think she'd feel about a man trying to control her personal life?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can scarcely imagine the man who'd try.

speaker: Woman
en: Oh, he exists all right. A slimy politician is trying to stop me from seeing Anthousa. He's threatened by me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would he be threatened by you?

speaker: Woman
en: Well, I'm not exactly her client. She lets me... see her free of charge. I compose the most lovely poems about her. She's a perfect muse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No wonder the politician is jealous.

speaker: Woman
en: This pig is trying to run me out of town for it. He's even threatened to put a bounty on me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You need me to deal with him.

speaker: Woman
en: The glory is all yours if you accept. Do you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you.

speaker: Woman
en: By Apollo, thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've made a few enemies, stranger. Including the person who hired me.

speaker: Man
en: No, please. There must be something I can do to change your mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I might be able to help you escape... If you're willing to join my crew?

speaker: Man
en: I'm to leave my family behind and sail with a mercenary sent to kill me. So be it.

speaker: Woman
en: Has he been... dealt with, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He won't be bothering anyone anymore.

speaker: Woman
en: So you are as brave as you look. Please, take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, tell me about this shield.

speaker: Supideo
en: Well, according to my parents it was stolen while I was visiting the Oracle of Delphi.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stolen? It's as good as gone then.

speaker: Supideo
en: I overheard mater and pater whispering about it. They mentioned a cave behind the Red Lake. Talked about the thief as if they know her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Strange.

speaker: Supideo
en: Go to the cave, misthios. Bring me back my shield. Only then will my parents be truly safe from my fury. Find the cave near the Red Lake. The thief and the shield should be there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to find this thief. Supideo mentioned a cave beyond the Red Lake. Strange that his parents knew this. They should get the shield back themselves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like blood. I've had dreams of drowning in a lake just like this one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There she is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the cave. Perfect hiding spot for a thief.

speaker: Rogue
en: If I see one more grain of salt, I'm going to kill someone!

speaker: Ailos
en: Patience. We're going to raid that stinking village once and for all, find a ship, and finally get off this salty wasteland.

speaker: Rogue
en: What about that old couple? The ones you stole the shield from? We should slit their throats and take whatever they have left.

speaker: Ailos
en: That family is off limits to you malákes! If either of you touch a hair on their heads, I'm going to cut off your hands and make you do push-ups in the salt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's my little thief.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This shield should be enough to protect Supideo's parents from his deadly wrath.

speaker: Supideo
en: Misthios! At last! Did you find the shield?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did. Now you can protect yourselves from... the prophecy.

speaker: Pedasos
en: So... you found the thief?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh yes. Cut her in half. She won't steal anything from anyone ever again.

speaker: Katina
en: And what about the blacksmith?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, he's very much alive. We did things in the back of his workshop that would make Aphrodite blush!

speaker: Katina
en: You didn't.

speaker: Pedasos
en: This is awful.

speaker: Supedio
en: Mater, pater, what's wrong? You're safe—the prophecy's broken.

speaker: Katina
en: Actually, there's something we've been meaning to tell you. Supideo, you were adopted.

speaker: Supideo
en: What?!

speaker: Katina
en: A young couple brought you to us. They knew we'd give you a better home. That sword and shield is your inheritance from them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait, so the thief... and the blacksmith...

speaker: Pedasos
en: Are Supideo's birth parents. You killed his mater and fucked his pater.

speaker: Supideo
en: But the prophecy said pater would scream to the gods in agony.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He screamed. But not in agony.

speaker: Supideo
en: You killed mater and had sex with pater!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Supideo, I had no idea.

speaker: Supideo
en: I can't get the image out of my head. I don't want to see anymore!

speaker: Supideo
en: Aargh! I'm blind, misthios! Are you happy?

speaker: Supdieo
en: My dreams are forever haunted. Mater will bleed. Pater will scream.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's fine. Could use a cold bath, but he's fine.

speaker: Katina
en: Thank the gods!

speaker: Supideo
en: Thank you, misthios! You spared my parents from my wrath. Now, if you would release me.

speaker: Pedasos
en: Actually there's something your mater and I have to tell you. Your parents are...

speaker: Katina
en: Very happy to have such a caring son to protect us. Thank you, misthios. We're all fine now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Odd family.

speaker: Katina
en: It's best you left us alone. My son is very fragile.

speaker: Pedasos
en: I should have never let my son go to Delphi.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope this oracle gives better news than the one in Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Sanctuary of Delphi. The gods themselves watch over this land.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Kassandra, isn't this remarkable? We're so close to the gods, I can feel Apollo all around me. How did it go with Elpenor?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can talk later, in private. Who is this?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Just a simple pilgrim.

speaker: Barnabas
en: He just saw the Oracle. I couldn't help but ask if she's as glorious as they say.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, is she?

speaker: Herodotos
en: She left me with more questions than answers.

speaker: Barnabas
en: That's the Oracle for you!

speaker: Herodotos
en: You weren't lying. It really is the spear of Leonidas.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I may have mentioned you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka! Barnabas, use your head!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would appreciate you showing a bit more... secrecy.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well, it's just he seemed interested in legends—like you. I thought you might get along.

speaker: Herodotos
en: How...

speaker: Kassandra
en: One more move, and the spear will be at your throat. Tell me your name.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I also mentioned you can be a little defensive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know my spear just by looking at it? You're more than some simple pilgrim.

speaker: Herodotos
en: All things in Delphi are more than they appear. Even I.

speaker: Herodotos
en: My name is Herodotos. I'm a story teller, or I was. This war is forcing us all to new extremes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That much is true. Why are you hiding your identity?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'm here on behalf of a man in Athens. A very powerful man. We intend to finally end this war.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You told me you came to ask the Oracle a personal question.

speaker: Herodotos
en: War is personal, Barnabas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you came to seek the Pythia's guidance on how to end this war?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I did, though something is wrong in Delphi. Guards at every turn, people being turned away...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't seem convinced the Pythia can be believed. What did she tell you?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I asked her to show the path to the war's end. She said "Spring should not wish for winter, as it brings death with it."

speaker: Barnabas
en: Such wisdom... I don't understand a word of it, but that's why she's in there and we're out here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know a threat when I hear one.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You were on Kephallonia for too long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This line is ridiculous! Are there always this many people to see the Pythia?

speaker: Barnabas
en: These are more than just people! Every city sends a ', or sacred ambassadors, to seek guidance on behalf of their people. The Pythia not only shapes the destinies of individuals, but of the entire Greek world.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Imagine what power one would have if they controlled what came out of her mouth.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Apollo controls this!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Of course he does.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Delphi is nothing like they say. Has it always been like this?

speaker: Barnabas
en: No. This was once an open and welcoming place. But war changes things. People seek out the Pythia for more political reasons. Prophecies in times of war often stir... violent emotions.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It's wise to keep your blades sheathed. Drawing blood in Delphi is considered an insult to Apollo. Punishment is severe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have my own questions for the Pythia. But this line! I'll be an old woman by the time I see her.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You're joking! You carry more blades than a field of grass!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't come here to start trouble.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Trouble? Just walk in! Who's going to stop you? The priest?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, but if things get out of hand, I'm blaming you, Barnabas.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Is she not every bit as great as I said?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Can you feel that? It's as if the gods walk among us.

speaker: Herodotos
en: You fascinate me, misthios. I long for the day when we can sit, and drink, and tell tales.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to see the Pythia.

speaker: Maron
en: Only those chosen by the light of Apollo may enter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How does one get chosen?

speaker: Maron
en: One goes to the back of the line.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do I look like someone who waits in line?

speaker: Pythia
en: Enter into the light of Apollo, the light that illuminates shadow. Choose your question wisely, mortal. For you have but one. Speak truth seeker!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I lost my mother when I was young. I have to find her. Where is she?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for my father—my true father. Who is he?

speaker: Pythia
en: It's you! From the visions! The child on the mountain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How could you know that?

speaker: Pythia
en: You need to leave. Now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave? Do you have any idea what I've been through to get here?

speaker: Pythia
en: Oh, but I do. I saw you feign ignorance in Kausos. You let an unknown sickness govern your decisions. Innocents died thanks to you.

speaker: Pythia
en: Oh, but I do. While in Kausos, you didn't cower in the face of the priest. A child and her family still live thanks to you.

speaker: Pythia
en: Oh, but I do. There is wisdom in your decisions. Any other misthios would have killed those people in that cave in Megaris, but you held back for the truth, and balanced judgement with their lives.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But how?

speaker: Pythia
en: No one can hide from the light.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Please, I've come this far. You must have the answers I seek.

speaker: Pythia
en: Child of the Mountain, the Cult of Kosmos have eyes everywhere. They will kill you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Cult of Kosmos?

speaker: Pythia
en: The Oracle has spoken. The prophecy is yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You never answered my question!

speaker: Cult Guardian
en: The Pythia is done for the day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not leaving until I get answers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos, you're still here. Where's Barnabas?

speaker: Herodotos
en: He's gone back to your ship. You don't look happy with your prophecy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She... knew who I was.

speaker: Herodotos
en: She's the Pythia, it's her business to act like she knows you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was no act. She said she had visions of me as a child on a mountain.

speaker: Herodotos
en: What child hasn't stood on a mountain?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was thrown from that mountain. My life started and ended on that mountain. I'm telling you, she knew who I was. What I'd done. Tried to warn me...

speaker: Herodotos
en: Warn you? About what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She mentioned the Cult of Kosmos. Does this mean anything to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Never mind, it's nothing.

speaker: Herodotos
en: There are people in Phokis who can't be trusted, Kassandra. But I'm not one of them. If you know something, you must act quickly. The Pythia's words control all our fates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She mentioned the Cult of Kosmos. Does this mean anything to you?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'd heard whispers. A cult, unlike any other, coming to Delphi. But I paid them no mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Pythia seemed afraid of them. Guards took her away.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Took her away? Then the whispers were true! If this Cult has corrupted the Pythia... This is devastating news. Do you understand what this means? Through her, the Cult controls the world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to speak with her when she's not so well... protected.

speaker: Herodotos
en: That would require a miracle from the gods. She is always protected.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know more about the Pythia than I do. Where would she be?

speaker: Herodotos
en: When she's not in the Temple of Apollo, she's at her home in the Chora of Delphi.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't go breaking down every door until I find her.

speaker: Herodotos
en: The Oracle's home is probably easy enough to spot. She'd be the only person in the Chora of Delphi who can afford to live in luxury.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where in the Chora of Delphi does the Pythia live?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I've heard she lives on the outskirts of the village. But be warned: she will be guarded. Not everyone comes to see the Oracle with the best of intentions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find where the Pythia lives. And I will get answers.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Kassandra, don't forget: brute force is useless when finesse is required.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Goddess of War and Wisdom. Does it please you, I wonder, to watch your city on the verge of battle?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I might have a job for you, if you're as good as a fighter as I've heard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've heard for me?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Don't let it go to your head. I hear about everything that happens in this city, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With flattery like that, how could I possibly turn you down?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I'm not trying to flatter you. I'm trying to hire you. I need some Spartan military targets... removed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think you may have the wrong idea about me, General...?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Demosthenes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not a murderer, if that's what you expected.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I expected you were someone who wants to get paid. Was I wrong?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No... not completely. Fine. What do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you, if I can. Depending on what it is you need, General...

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Demosthenes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Very good.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: My spies tell me the Spartans are mobilizing. What I want you to do is hamstring them. Get into their forts and remove the commanders in charge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess that makes sense.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I'm thrilled you approve. You'll need to bring me the seals of the commanders you kill, as proof. You'll be amply rewarded.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those don't seem like standard Athenian tactics.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: They're not. But it will work, and that's what matters. We've already lost too many Athenians to those savages using "traditional" warfare. The other generals disagree, but I refuse to let them destroy our chances.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do they want to do?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: They want "honorable" face-to-face warfare, pitting our forces directly against the Spartans. We're not going to win a contest of strength against those brutes. We need to outthink them. So, will you kill the commanders?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'll take the job.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Good. I might not have approval to deploy our men to do this, but I'm not about to let that stop me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's so special about these seals?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Only elite Spartan commanders carry these seals, those in charge of entire forts. They'd all die before parting with them. So bring me the seals as proof that they're dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find them?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: The Spartans have been making inroads into the Athenian territory, taking over forts that once belonged to us. Make them pay for every inch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's your strategy?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Whatever it takes to protect Athenians lives and kill Spartans.

speaker: Kasssandra
en: That's not what I meant. What's your personal strategy?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: My career is none of your business. Know that I don't seek much. Only proper recognition of my strategic brillance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've told me enough. I'll get your seals for you, General.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Do you have my seals yet?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I do. It was easy.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: How could I have doubted your greatness? Nonetheless, I appreciate the work you've done. Would you be interested in another job?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. I have the seals for you.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: This will show those idiots in the assembly. We're making progress. Interested in getting rid of more polemarchs for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm interested.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You get started on the Spartans. I have other things to do right now.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I'm impressed with your work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you expect any less?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I had hoped, but hiring you was a gamble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Most things in life are.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I am perhaps a bit more willing to gamble than my fellow generals would like.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you take no risks, you win no wars.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Exactly! How is it a mercenary understands this when the "greatest" generals of Athens don't?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure whether I should feel flattered or insulted.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: The Spartans are trying to find our supply lines. We've caught several spies already. We cannot afford such a loss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not if you want to keep your troops alive, no.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I need you to kill more of their commanders. Leave their hoplites without leadership. They'll be scrambling.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you sure? Spartans are fierce warriors.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Warriors, yes. Thinkers, no. They react like wild animals. Put them in a situation that requires genuine thought, and they fall apart. Kill the commanders and bring me their seals. We'll see how the other generals react tothat.

speaker: Gelon
en: Fuck 'em, fuck 'em all. Gods, oracles, and especially pi—sailors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's your problem?

speaker: Gelon
en: What don't I have fucking problems with? The Oracle, for one. The sea, for another. And don't get me started on my crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have business with the Oracle? You're a long way from Delphi.

speaker: Gelon
en: Had business. And my business is none of your fucking business. I ain't shopping for a merc'. If anything, I need the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You need a god? I'm the next best thing.

speaker: Gelon
en: Oh, you're a live one. That's a good pitch, I'll give you that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you want something done, you'll have to do it yourself.

speaker: Gelon
en: You're right there. Can't trust the gods or their servants.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So who are you?

speaker: Gelon
en: Captain Gelon, of the Shark's Tooth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shark Tooth's your boat?

speaker: Gelon
en: Do I look like a fucking fisherman? I sail a ship, not a boat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Malaka... I came to see if you needed help.

speaker: Gelon
en: Fuck you, no one asked you to!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know what, fuck you.

speaker: Gelon
en: Ok. Sorry, been a bad day. I finished my business with the Oracle and was meant to meet my ship here. They're nowhere to be fucking found, and I have been here since last night.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was just a question. I'm here to help.

speaker: Gelon
en: Oh, it's not your fault. After my business with the Oracle, I came to meet my ship and crew. That was a day ago, and they're nowhere to be found.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, you sought the Oracle's advice?

speaker: Gelon
en: Her? Fuck no! I'd rather seek council in the wind from my ass.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then why seek her out?

speaker: Gelon
en: We got a deal. Suppose no harm in telling you. She lets me know where the pilgrims are coming from. Then I supply the transport for their journey, and we split the fee.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, you're trying to tell me the Oracle has divine intuition of where the pilgrims will be coming from.

speaker: Gelon
en: Fuck no! She asks her "believers" how full their ports are, then she tells me. Simple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have business here in Phokis?

speaker: Gelon
en: I got business everywhere. Right now, it's where my fucking ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So where's the Shark Tooth?

speaker: Gelon
en: I wouldn't fucking be here if I knew, would i?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ok, let me rephrase. Where was the crew meant to be?

speaker: Gelon
en: Well, um I sent my girl Gyke off. Pilgrims get stuck in the shallows 'round here, and, er, we sort of help out...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh. Your girl?

speaker: Gelon
en: Yeah, best hand I ever had, and more. Look, find my ship and my Gyke, will you? I'll pay.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out what happened and bring them back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know where they could have gone?

speaker: Gelon
en: The southeastern shore is pretty rich pickings. Nice cove there to trap lost, wealthy pilgrims.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a pirate.

speaker: Gelon
en: What if I am? I'm the pirate that's paying you. Anyway, I'm not a pirate all the time. It's more of a hobby.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A hobby! You sure the crew didn't mutiny and run off on you?

speaker: Gelon
en: Not with my Gyke at the helm. Plus they never got the cut from our last trip. They wouldn't leave without getting paid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Describe Gyke.

speaker: Gelon
en: She's beautiful, she is. Kisses like summer. From the first time I saw her, I wanted to eat her all up...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not helpful.

speaker: Gelon
en: OK, OK. She's a raven haired and has a precious band on her arm that I gave her. Always wears it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find them and return as soon as I can.

speaker: Gelon
en: I don't see my Gyke, or my fucking ship. You're going to have to try harder if you want that drachmae.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the Shark's Tooth, all right. Or what's left of her. Looks like sharks got the whole crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should tell Gelon about Gyke.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found your ship.

speaker: Gelon
en: And? Come on now, where are they? Where's my Gyke?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't really know how to tell you this.

speaker: Gelon
en: For fuck's sake, Zeus could have impregnated the whole of Athens in the time it takes you to say anything. Where are they?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're dead, all right? And your ship's gone, too.

speaker: Gelon
en: My Gyke...

speaker: Kassandra
en: All I found is her armband.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was trying to break this to you gently... I found your ship. It was wrecked.

speaker: Gelon
en: Oh... And my Gyke?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was all I could find. It was her armband.

speaker: Gelon
en: Gyke. Suppose I'm not much of a captain. Can't be a captain without a ship...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can offer you a place on my crew. I know it's not like having your own ship, but you'll be part of a family.

speaker: Gelon
en: Hmm, well I'd rather be at sea than stuck here with these pious idiots. You got yourself a deal... Just till I'm back on my feet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course.

speaker: Gelon
en: Now where's your boat?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ship. It's called the Adrestia.

speaker: Gelon
en: Whatever you say, captain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd best be on my way.

speaker: Gelon
en: You do that, misthios. You may not be the cause, but nonetheless, you're the bringer of ill fate. If I never see you or that fucking Oracle again, I'll count my blessings.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An arena seems like a strange playce for an Archon.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Dikastes! Thank the stars! I was beginning to lose all hope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlas said you needed help.

speaker: Gadiros
en: You don't understand the responsibility on my shoulders. It's my job to concoct entertainment for the masses. But I fear the crowd have grown bored of my grand spectacles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen some good plays... and some bad ones.

speaker: Gadiros
en: We need more than a simple play. If the audience leave my shows bored and restless, who knows what they'll start plotting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You think they'll become violent.

speaker: Gadiros
en: My purpose is to keep them occupied so they can't be violent.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If your shows have become boring, you just need to get more creative.

speaker: Gadiros
en: The humans are primitive, their tastes basic. They like life's simpler joys. Blood. Tragedy. Romance. That sort of thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trying to distract people from their problems will only work for so long.

speaker: Gadiros
en: I misspoke. I've seen what these humans are capable of, given the chance. I'm not distracting them. Merely... keeping them happy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So give the people what they want.

speaker: Gadiros
en: What they want... Yes. Yes, I can hear the cheers now! "The legendary Dikastes, Kassandra, takes on Atlantis's finest warriors!" You must take part in my next event!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a pankration. I can definitely help with that.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Not exactly! But I was inspired by your efforts in Elis. I know you'll do an exemplary job entertaining the crowds as you did then. If we pull this off, we'll be the talk of the city!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's worth a try.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Welcome one, welcome all to yet another miraculous show here in our beloved city. Tonight, we have a very special guest. The Dikastes of Atlantis is here to entertain you. Our hero's first challenge comes from the vaults of Atlantis itself. Can our mighty Dikastes overcome the power of the Atlantean Guard? Let's find out!

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right Kassandra, be entertaining. That's what he said.

speaker: Gadiros
en: That was thrilling. What a display.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is definitely not a pankration.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Our valiant hero's next challenge fast approaches. A Champion bested by none in the city. No mercy, no guilt. Will this be to much for even the Dikastes to overcome?

speaker: Gadiros
en: The Champion has been bested. Our mighty Dikastes is victorious and the crowd have spoken. But will she show mercy or will she spill the blood we want?

speaker: Arena Champion
en: If you don't appease the crowd, I fear what Gadiros will do. It was an honor to fight you, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't deserve to die just for losing.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Our merciful Dikastes has passed judgment, but do not dismay. Our Champion lives to fight another day, for you, the audience.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You fought honorably

speaker: Gadiros
en: A fitting end to a glorious life spent in service to you, the audience. Now, onto the grand finale.

speaker: Gadiros
en: And here we are, the end of today's event. Next to face our Dikastes's judgment, the very scum that taints our city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods... What is this?

speaker: Gadiros
en: For the good of Atlantis, today bare witness to the guilty and condemned given one final chance at redemption. They will be honored to die at the hands of our guest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they're criminals, then this has to be done.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Let the slaughter commence!

speaker: Gadiros
en: The guilty and condemned have been judged! Hail our wise Dikastes!

speaker: Gadiros
en: What a show! What a show!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people seemed entertained.

speaker: Gadiros
en: And why wouldn't they be? You put on a performance for the ages.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If this kind of entertainment keeps the peace, then maybe it has value.

speaker: Gadiros
en: I know the games seem barbaric, but sometimes we must feed the primitive beast within to keep it dormant. Now I must begin preparing for my next great event. Thank you for your help, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This won't help the relations between your people. The humans will see what's going on eventually.

speaker: Gadiros
en: I fear that if we stop, things will get worse, but you see things differently than all of us here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe their tastes aren't so "primitive". Maybe they'll surprise you.

speaker: Gadiros
en: I whis i had your optimism, but only time will tell. Perhaps I'll even recruit a few humans to help me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough! I'm not doing this.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Fear not, friends. We will make sure justice is delivered.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Well that was an unmitigated disaster.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said fight, so i fought.

speaker: Gadiros
en: The problem is that I didn't say fight. I said be as entertaining as possible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If this kind of entertainment keeps the peace, then maybe it has value.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This won't help the relations between your people. The humans will see what's going on eventually.

speaker: Gadiros
en: The games have failed. The humans are restless, and it's only a matter of time before they make their own entertainment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You just need to keep surprising them. Think like a human, not an Isu.

speaker: Gadiros
en: That's what I tried to do, but you showed the criminals mercy and the crowd reacted as I expected.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Killing people who can't defend themselves isn't entertainment. It's slaughter.

speaker: Gadiros
en: Their sacrifice helps us keep the peace and maintain order. Or, it would have if you'd played along.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you saying, Gadiros?

speaker: Gadiros
en: That my grand experiment has failed. There's nothing left to be done but start again and try for better results. The arena must be cleared

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is madness.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Port of Nisaia. If I'm going to find Athenian supplies this'll be the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those blue supply crates with the white owl are the ones I need to destroy. A single fire arrow should do the trick.

speaker: Politician
en: Thank you for jumping in. Come to think of it, I could use a mercenary of your caliber.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're paying, I'm listening.

speaker: Politician
en: Those were Followers of Ares! I can scarcely believe they are attacking people openly like this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whether you believe it or not, they will kill you. Be more careful, friend.

speaker: Politician
en: You're right. This is serious. I... We must strike against them. And send a warning to the priestess at the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I should send them all to the underworld?

speaker: Politician
en: Yes. All the Followers must die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm the one for the job.

speaker: Politician
en: You're doing me a service, mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Politician
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Politician
en: You kept your end of the deal. Now it's time I hold up mine. Take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I've started.

speaker: Cursed Gold
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Cursed Lands
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got your message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Man
en: One of my patients has lost all favor with the gods. I need help lifting the curse that's been placed on her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I might have some sway with the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure I have much say in the gods' business.

speaker: Man
en: The problem isn't the gods. It's with the person who laid the curse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you want me to deal with her.

speaker: Man
en: The gods show me mercy. That is exactly what I desire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'm in.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you. You saved me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've made a few enemies, stranger. Including the person who hired me.

speaker: Woman
en: No, please. There must be something I can do to change your mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I might be able to help you escape... If you're willing to join my crew?

speaker: Woman
en: I must abandon my life here completely to avoid death? Fine, if that's what it takes.

speaker: Man
en: Has she been... taken care of, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's no longer a concern.

speaker: Man
en: Then this belongs to you. Nice work, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what does Leda look like?

speaker: Barnabas
en: She was the most beautiful woman I've ever known. Beautiful dark hair and skin. Her green eyes sparkled like jewels. And when she drank, could she fight!

speaker: Kassandra
en: She sounds fun.

speaker: Barnabas
en: She was that and more, my young friend. So much more.

speaker: Barnabas
en: It's been so long. I wonder if Leda would even recognize this old face.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's so many bodies... Is this the underworld?

speaker: Letter From a Suitor
en: Leda of Ithaka. Your father abandoned you. In death, so has your mother. I'm here for you. Imagine your perfect life, bearing my children, tilling my fields, baking my bread. Any woman would kill for such a life. Wouldn't you?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Kassandra...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shh.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Leda?

speaker: Leda
en: Stop! I'll kill you if you come any closer. Who sent you? Pelenos? Antikles?

speaker: Kassandra
en: People who threaten me don't live long enough to regret it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Relax. We're here on our own.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You haven't aged a day. Is this the underworld?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Leda, it's me. Barnabas.

speaker: Leda
en: That was my father's name. I never told it to anyone.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Father? Young one, please, what was your mother's name?

speaker: Leda
en: The same as mine - Leda of Ithaka.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were right, old friend. Leda survived, but not in the way your visions told you. This is your daughter.

speaker: Leda
en: Impossible. You have no proof.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't listen to her. She's obviously lying.

speaker: Leda
en: I'm lying? You're the one who has no way to prove you are who you say.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Young one, a lifetime ago, your mother and I sailed side by side. The night I lost my eye, a tempest overwhelmed us and ran us into the rocks. Leda was so brave. She roped together some of the splintered hull. I held her and I said, "Don't stop paddling...".

speaker: Leda
en: "Until you reach the shore."

speaker: Barnabas
en: She told you this story. Good.

speaker: Leda
en: After all this time... Mater said you were a king who died fighting the Hydra.

speaker: Leda
en: You need to know. Mater... She's...

speaker: Barnabas
en: I understand. We'll grieve her together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hate to interrupt, but Leda, you did threaten us with a blade. And there were bodies.

speaker: Leda
en: After mater died, I took over the farm. Ever since, "suitors" have tried to marry me for my fortune. When that didn't work, they decided it would be easier to kill me for it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You've been defending yourself. Let us help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These kinds of people don't stop until they have what they want. You mentioned two names.

speaker: Leda
en: Pelenos and Antikles. They both live nearby. I can show you where.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go together.

speaker: Leda
en: With you by my side, we'll be unstoppable.

speaker: Barnabas

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Artemis found me unworthy, I would not have returned with the pelts of the Nemean Lion or Kallisto the Bear. If anything, this proves me more Artemis' champion than Zeus'.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Kassandra
en: I grew up with nothing and have not forgotten the ache of hunger. I take what I need and no more.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: Why do you care about this village and why do you expect our sympathy? What do we stand to gain from this?

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Kassandra
en: This forest may provide you with food and shelter for now, but you won't be able to fend off the Sons of Xerxes for long. You need those resources.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Kassandra
en: The women of Lalaia have food and shelter, but are not prepared to defend themselves from raiding bandits. An alliance benefits you both.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: Power radiates off you the same way it did Daphnae. I can see now why you carry her title. If you can get me and my best warrior to yield, then my bow and sisters are yours.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: I'm surprised by your compassion, Hero, and beginning to see what Daphnae saw in you. Still, I do not submit to any leader who cannot defeat me and my best warrior in combat. If you can get me on my back, then I bow. Only then.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: Telesilla, join me!

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: I yield! You have proven yourself worthy of your titles. My warriors and I are yours.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Kassandra
en: You fought well. You know the direction of Lalaia, yes?

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: Of course. We'll gather our things and join you there.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Kassandra
en: I expect to see you defending Lalaia when the Sons of Xerxes attack.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Abrota
en: Yes, Champion.

scene: Daughters of Artemis and Daughters of Aphrodite
speaker: Kassandra
en: I've done all I can for these women. Time to get back to Periktione.

en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Adonis
en: Welcome to the uprising. These ruins were abandoned when Persephone constructed her "paradise." We won't be bothered here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But there are so few of you.

speaker: Adonis
en: Well, thanks to you I now have a war horse! An invincible war horse, or so I'm told.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure how much help one horse is going to be.

speaker: Adonis
en: Most of Persephone's army consists of mind-controlled humans. Free their minds and bring them to me—we can use them as troops.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Free their minds?

speaker: Adonis
en: My dear friend Hermes is a master manipulator. And that Staff of yours looks like one of his creations. Try using that. There's an outpost southwest from here, nestled in the Hand of Hades. Warriors were spotted in its palm.

speaker: Adonis
en: You surprise me. When we first met, I was positive you were sent by Persephone to...

speaker: Kassandra
en: To what?

speaker: Adonis
en: Seduce me, confuse me, anything to make me forget my love. But when I asked you to weaken Persephone's influence, you did. I asked you to bring me warriors, and here they are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And all I had to do was risk my life for you to trust me.

speaker: Adonis
en: No one in Elysium is who they say. So when a clever warrior shows up to help me escape, you'll have to excuse me if I'm skeptical.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You think I'd be the one sent to make you forget your love?

speaker: Adonis
en: You're brave, beautiful, and if I had to guess I'd say you had the blood of the gods coursing through those veins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Careful. Flattery can get you into trouble.

speaker: Adonis
en: Don't confuse flattery with honesty. That could get you into trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're kind, but I could never compete with a goddess.

speaker: Adonis
en: You don't have to. You fight with a passion that could only come from one place. Mortality.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to find more warriors.

speaker: Adonis
en: Scouts spotted one nearby—was a Spartan hero in his former life. He's not under Persephone's influence, but keeps mostly to himself. With a champion like him on our side, we can't fail.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How will I know when I find him?

speaker: Adonis
en: From what I'm told, you can't miss him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ahem.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leonidas?

speaker: Leonidas
en: You have the eyes of my daughter.

speaker: Leonidas
en: So something did survive that day. How do you have this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Myrrine—she's my mater. I'm here because I need your help. I need you to fight.

speaker: Leonidas
en: I have found peace here. Why would I fight?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All my life I was told of my grandfather. The king who spat in the face of the gods and ran his spear through anyone who threatened the freedom of his people. Now I'm the one fighting for freedom, and I'm asking my grandfather for help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We are few, and they are many. Persephone has an army. Adonis fights for freedom, but without help we don't stand a chance.

speaker: Leonidas
en: We'll need to use the terrain to our advantage.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you'll fight with us?

speaker: Leonidas
en: Not until you fight me. You say you're Myrrine's daughter—I want to see how she trained you.

speaker: Leonidas
en: You fight well.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Warriors will only fight for you if you are willing to die for them.

speaker: Leonidas
en: An enemy on their last breath is at their most dangerous.

speaker: Leonidas
en: I could have used you at Thermopylai.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You could have used a lot of people at Thermopylai.

speaker: Leonidas
en: I am glad the spear's in your hands. I will fight with you. You have my word as a Spartan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, grandfather.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This man is tough to have survived being buried alive like this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Joining the Order... What could go wrong?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Revenge can drive people to do foolish things.

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Need anything, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I heard you're the person to talk to around here if I have... "bear pelts" to sell?

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: You're in the right place if you want to give me... "bear pelts."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here are the... "bear pelts."

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Over here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not going to hand over my "bear pelts" to just anyone.

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Oh. OK.

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Oh, wait! I forgot the code. Hold on! I always do that! In the beginning there was chaos...

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...And it's power is ancient.

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Uh... That's not the right answer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is this about chaos?

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Umm... the code. You know the code, right?

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: Uh... That's not the right answer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...And we are the Order.

speaker: Blacksmith Assistant
en: By Zeus! You're good! Good thing you knew the code. I would have needed that note back, otherwise.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This man's life was a tragedy.

speaker: Echion
en: Now we see if the rumors about your strength are true, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Echion
en: You're not what we thought. Not exceptional at all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lots of contracts about this Con of Kos. Must be a bonehead.

speaker: Dead Scouts for Healthy Sparta
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like the perfect place to hide missing humans. Locked. But I think I know what opens this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The more complicated the key, the bigger the secret.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone really doesn't want any visitors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What... is this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka!

speaker: Aita
en: I've been waiting for you, Kassandra. Welcome to the birthplace of legends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who said that? Show yourself!

speaker: Aita
en: My name is Aita. I am a scientist. And in many ways these are my children.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You created the minotaur, the cyclops, the writhing dread? They're monsters.

speaker: Aita
en: Are we not all monsters? Imperfect being striving towards our ultimate potential? Is that not why you are here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here because a little boy's parents are missing, and all signs point to you.

speaker: Aita
en: How very human of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to judge Atlantis. And right now, things are not looking very good.

speaker: Aita
en: Look closer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Grant us the sight..."

speaker: Aita
en: To protect our legacy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She nearly turned me to stone! Even now I don't feel safe staring at her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I still have nightmares from my time in the Labyrinth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who... or what are you?

speaker: Aita
en: A metal of extraordinary properties. Restructures the of the human brain responsible for emotions. We've engineered it to remove fear. Enhances your more animal instincts. Why hold a weapon, when you can become one?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Damades? Rhene? Are you here?

speaker: Rhene
en: Over here! We're here!

speaker: Damades
en: Please help us.

speaker: Lyra
en: Dikastes! You're here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lyra? What are you doing here?

speaker: Lyra
en: They came for me in the night. I'll never be safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, I'm getting everyone out of here.

speaker: Aita
en: Didn't anyone teach you it's cruel to lie?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? What's cruel is abducting and experimenting on these people.

speaker: Aita
en: Without sacrifice, there can be no progress. Without experimentation, there can be no perfection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're breaking Poseidon's law.

speaker: Aita
en: I am advancing knowledge for the betterment of Atlantis. Poseidon's lack of vision keeps us in darkness. But we are close. So very close.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Humans are not animals to be caged and tortured.

speaker: Aita
en: We created them to serve us. That is their sole purpose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlantis is on the brink of war because of Isu who think like you.

speaker: Aita
en: Which is why we are properly arming ourselves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The smartest people I've met don't resort to violence.

speaker: Aita
en: Did you not nearly raze Elysium to the ground in the pursuit of knowledge?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let these people go.

speaker: Aita
en: It's too late for them. Project Olympos has already begun. One human escaped before the transformation was complete and lives were lost. This won't happen again. Surely you understand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lyra. She took her own life after what you did to her.

speaker: Aita
en: So, you've seen the beast she becomes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm getting these people out of here.

speaker: Aita
en: But... don't you want to know what's behind this door?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll play. Tell me.

speaker: Aita
en: Why tell you when I could show you? Just know to enter the chamber is to forfeit their lives. You cannot have both.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't play your little games. I'm getting these people out of here.

speaker: Aita
en: So, you would choose to let your small-minded morality hinder your progress.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I just killed you, set these people free, and broke through your stupid door?

speaker: Aita
en: You can't kill me, Kassandra.

speaker: Aita
en: I can see you're struggling. What if I told you the greatest achievement in Atlantis is behind that door? And that we owe that achievement to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Aita
en: Through there is a path to immortality. For you. For us. Embrace your legacy—forget these miserable humans. Abandon morality, and the answers to all your questions are just beyond that door.

speaker: Rhene
en: Please! Save us or we'll die.

speaker: Aita
en: You will be reborn!

speaker: Aita
en: Don't you want to know why you're really here? Free the people and this door will remain closed to you forever. Pass through, however, and it will lock behind you—these rats will be mine. What will it be, Dikastes, their lives, or your destiny?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry.

speaker: Rhene
en: No! Please!

speaker: Damades
en: Don't leave!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? No... impossible.

speaker: Aita
en: You. It was always you. Human. Isu. Perfection. The Isu blood coursing through your human body makes you the perfect vessel. It has endowed you with their resilience, and our consciousness. More so than any of my creations, you are what Project Olympos was always meant to be. The ultimate weapon. Imagine if we controlled an army of you—the inevitable war between the humans and the Isu would be over in a heartbeat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not if I cut down every last one of these things.

speaker: Aita
en: Don't waste your energy. We can always create more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These "vessels" are empty. Your project has failed. And soon, you will be dead.

speaker: Aita
en: Entertaining to the end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These experiments have gone too far. Poseidon's going to hear about this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fuck your door. I promised a little boy I'd bring his parents home, and that's exactly what I'm going to do.

speaker: Aita
en: Very disappointing. No matter. if there are two things Atlantis has in ample supply, it is adamant and humans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come on, let's get out of here.

speaker: Damades
en: Thank you, Dikastes.

speaker: Rhene
en: I'll get to see Alkon again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hurry!

speaker: Rhene
en: How can we ever repay you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell your son if an Isu ever calls him a rat again, Dikastes Kassandra will deal with them personally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Poseidon lied to me. They've been experimenting on humans this whole time.

speaker: Deadly Precision
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Aspasia
en: It doesn't matter where I got the information.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You should know by now that I'm not one to follow orders blindly.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You are a brave warrior, Myrrine. But ignoring this danger is foolishness. These...

speaker: Myrrine
en: I know who they are.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Then you know the danger you're in.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I would like to know what makes you so certain they're coming.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Did you not hear what I said? These are their most skilled killers. You cannot stay in the public eye. They'll find you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I understand you perfectly. But I also need to be seen. The propagandist did his job well. I need more support to attack Paros.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I've seen too many people die already. Please, come away from here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspasia? What brings you here?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra! Read the room, my dear...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm interrupting. Please, continue your discussion. It sounds fascinating.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I've just come to tell your mother that the Cult's elite forces are after her, and that this place is too open.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And I've been telling Aspasia I need to appear in public to maintain the support of the citizens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this about the Cult sending soldiers?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Play along. The people here need convincing that I'm still a worthy leader. Aspasia is trying to have me hide myself away.

speaker: Aspasia
en: She is under threat of assassination. My sources say the elite forces are already in Naxos. I cannot watch this happen again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to handle the Cult's soldiers?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Not only that. My people won't believe Paros is behind this without proof. I need you to find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Good. And I'll make the rounds here, shore up my support. Be careful. They're dangerous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'll get her out of here safely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where do your sources say I should start looking?

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'd try the caves under Mt. Zas. The Cultists are so enamored with their own mysticism. It's predictable enough for them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't think anyone sent to kill you is going to admit who they're working for.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You're right. Physical proof is better. I'm sure you can find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. I'd be happy to help you both. I'll see you again later.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I know who they are.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Then you know the danger you're in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A cave entrance. They're in there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Drachmae. All stamped with the seal of Paros. And a letter? In some kind of code.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult's soldiers were paid with drachmae from Paros.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Well. I could hardly ask for clearer proof. This will settle some scores.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Take these to the merchants' guild. Tell them it's the proof I promised. And tell them... they can keep the coins.

speaker: Timo
en: Of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was also this. I assume it's their orders.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I recognize this. It's an old dialect. The Cult must use it to communicate with one another.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can read it?

speaker: Aspasia
en: This money isn't from Silanos. It's from someone in Sparta.

speaker: Myrrine
en: That's not possible.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I can translate it for you. But these orders come from a Spartan king.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The Spartan nobility has always resisted the Cult!

speaker: Aspasia
en: The Cult is like water. Any crack in the stone and they'll get in.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Sparta stands against corruption!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can you say that after all Sparta has done to you? They tore apart our family! They welcomed the Cult with open arms.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Why do you keep saying "they"?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sparta has changed since we were there. Corruption spreads everywhere, as Aspasia says - even to Sparta. They want to instill discipline across the Greek world while they rot from within. They're focused on the wrong enemy.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I am still Spartan.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And so are you.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Are you really?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I have responsibilities here. Paros needs to be stopped. But then? Yes, I will go back.

speaker: Civilian
en: The warehouse is off limits.

speaker: Agapios
en: But I need those records!

speaker: Civilian
en: And I need three fewer daughters, but we don't often get what we want, old friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on?

speaker: Agapios
en: I'm here to check the warehouse's taxation records, but I'm being refused entry.

speaker: Civilian
en: This matter is out of my hands.

speaker: Agapios
en: Fine, the wheels of Euboea will be greased once more. How much will it cost to get me the records?

speaker: Civilian
en: That's not going to work this time, Agapios. The guards are under strict orders not to let anyone in or out of the warehouse. It's an order they will enforce, my friend. Take my advice. Stay away from that warehouse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's lucky your "friend" warned you.

speaker: Agapios
en: Ha. He's just as corrupt as the rest of Euboea. I fear there's nobody honest left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not all mercenaries are cutthroats. I can be trusted.

speaker: Agapios
en: That remains to be seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This world is a haven for liars. Trust no one.

speaker: Agapios
en: But I do trust—I trust in what Euboea was, and what she can be again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's causing the corruption?

speaker: Agapios
en: A group called The Dagger are strangling Euboea with their greed. They work from the shadows, controlling the nation with bribery and blackmail. They're the reason I need the taxation records from that warehouse. I'm following a parchment trail which I believe will lead me to the person behind it all. But I'm too old to be breaking into guarded warehouses. Perhaps the shine on my drachmae can convince you to do it for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get the records for you.

speaker: Agapios
en: Perhaps there is someone left in Euboea who can be trusted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Taxation records don't concern me. You're on your own.

speaker: Agapios
en: I can't do this alone. See me again if you decide you do want to earn some drachme.

speaker: Agapios
en: You've returned! I can't find the identity of the person leading the Dagger without those records. Please, you must help me find them!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find the records you're looking for?

speaker: Agapios
en: I'll need a lot of evidence to find the person behind The Dagger—one set of records won't be enough. They'll be scattered around the warehouse... And be sure to check the guard captain—anything important, he'll have on him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about the man behind The Dagger?

speaker: Agapios
en: Other than he may not be a man? Only his reputation is known—cruel, driven by greed... A living noose around the neck of Euboea. If we can't find out who he is and stop him, our fate is that of Eretria's: total ruin.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Dagger—dramatic name. Any particular reason?

speaker: Agapios
en: They stab at Euboea without honor—from the shadows, unseen, bleeding our nation of its lifeblood. A dramatic name, perhaps—but apt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the records. The guards won't stand a chance.

speaker: Agapios
en: They don't deserve a chance. For Euboea to survive, corruption and those who spread it must be crushed. I'll wait for you here.

speaker: Agapios
en: You're back—but where are the records? Without them, I'll never uncover the leader of The Dagger!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The warehouse grounds.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The warehouse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The warehouse dock.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now to find those records.

speaker: Tax Record
en: This record contains all the transactions that have occurred in the warehouse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Records of the trades Euboea's made in the last 6 months. Maybe the identity of The Dagger's leader is in here?

speaker: Shipment Record
en: This record lists the ships that have delivered or shipped items from the warehouse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe this will help Agapios identify The Dagger's leader.

speaker: Customer Record
en: This record contains a list of all the warehouse's customers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Records of ship names—what docked where and when. This might help Agapios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've found the records, Agapios.

speaker: Agapios
en: My master will be pleased.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a slave?!

speaker: Agapios
en: Do I not look as you expect? Yes, misthios, I am a slave—but I am not without dignity. The local magistrate is my master, and I'm his most trusted servant.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would rather die than be a slave.

speaker: Agapios
en: Not all have the luxury of choice, friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We do what we have to to survive.

speaker: Agapios
en: Exactly. I don't blame my father for selling me into slavery, it's what he had to do. It got me out of my old life, and gave me a chance at a better one.

speaker: Agapios
en: Nobody chooses to be a slave. But being one provides me food, shelter, safety, and security. Especially now, with Euboea all but run by The Dagger. They cannot see past their greed., and if they go unchecked we may all end up as slaves.

speaker: Agapios
en: If uncovering the identity of The Dagger's leader and finally stopping them sounds like something you'd be interested in, meet me and my master in the Slave Market.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll think about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, Charon. I'm ready to hear about your "lost souls."

speaker: Charon
en: Oh, them. Not everyone in the underworld belongs here. These souls are lost. Their true resting place deserves to be found.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the ferryman. You tell them where to go.

speaker: Charon
en: That's not in my job description. Every soul arrives with unfinished business—some are just more sympathetic than others.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are these souls you want me to help?

speaker: Charon
en: Most die and are given proper funeral rites, but some aren't so lucky.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And the unlucky ones become lost.

speaker: Charon
en: Oh, yes. They are left to wander eternity unaccepting of their fates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you, ferryman, but where should I start?

speaker: Charon
en: There's a soldier—an Athenian. He wished to die an honorable death in battle, but as he charged towards the enemy, he slipped in the dirt... and fell.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like quite the warrior.

speaker: Charon

en: Yes, yes. Many thanks for saving me. But I must get back, my pets are waiting for me! Did they send you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Indeed, your "pets" sent me.

speaker: Doctor
en: Bless my darlings! How are they? I knew they wouldn't forget me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not sure what pets you're talking about.

speaker: Doctor
en: No, no, my pets are not animals! They speak, although a little slowly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're referring to the workers at the quarry.

speaker: Doctor
en: Yes, yes, my pets! I care for them, feed them my medicine. And in turn, they help me with my research. I have a real bond with my pets. You look strong. Yes, yes. I can never have enough pets. You could join my family? It'll be a significant contribution to my research!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't be your test subject!

speaker: Doctor
en: How about post-mortem arrangements?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No.

speaker: Doctor
en: A great loss for research advancement. The medicine I make is quite delicious, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Arrangements can be made.

speaker: Doctor
en: I knew you would be interested! Welcome to the family. Don't fret, my pet, I'll take good care of you. We'll have plenty of medicine to go around!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about this medicine.

speaker: Doctor
en: Ah, the medicine. I feed it to my pets when my special tonic produces... side effects. Sometimes, it's too strong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Side effects like forgotten memories?

speaker: Doctor
en: Ah... yes, you know it. My pets... it's my fault, yes, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yet, you still feed them the tonic.

speaker: Doctor
en: I had no choice! I was forced to do it! But I will right my wrongs. I always right my wrongs, yes, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people who captured you, who were they?

speaker: Doctor
en: It was that fellow with the eyepatch! He was taking orders from this other bald man... They wanted my tonic and forced me to create more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka!

speaker: Doctor
en: I had no choice! They threatened to kill my pets!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then they caged you.

speaker: Doctor
en: Well, they refused to let me return to my pets. So, I poisoned a few of them, yes, yes. No one can keep my away from my pets, yes, yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your "pets" must have a history.

speaker: Doctor
en: I don't know and I don't need to know. I just know that I was made to feed them my tonic in a strange cave similar to this one. If it fails, I get to keep my pets and care for them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This tonic must be special.

speaker: Doctor
en: Yes, yes! It makes my pets so strong! Ah but, like I said, the side effects can be rather dire...It was perhaps a miscalculation on my part. My poor pets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need the medicine you mentioned. Give it to me.

speaker: Doctor
en: What? Whatever for? I am not obliged to. I will do no such thing, no, no!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you are useless to me. I should end your life and misdeeds here.

speaker: Doctor
en: No, no! No violence needed! I'll do as you say!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need the medicine for someone I know. He's afflicted with the consequences of your tonic.

speaker: Doctor
en: What! It cannot be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You wouldn't forsake a pet, would you?

speaker: Doctor
en: I cannot abandon my pets

speaker: Doctor
en: But, my pet, why do you want it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need it for someone I know

speaker: Doctor
en: There are others afflicted by my tonic? It cannot be!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just give me the medicine.

speaker: Doctor
en: I'm afraid it'll take time to make. Yes,yes. First, get rid of those malákes who kept me away from my pets! They're at the fortress just down the road.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get rid of them. I expect the medicine in return.

speaker: Doctor
en: Yes, yes, it'll take time for me to gather the ingredients. You might want to take a look around Thasos City first. I heard that strange things are happening there, yes, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The medicine could be helpful to Neleus. First, I should deal with the Doctor's captors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They won't bother the Doctor again..

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's taken care of. Now, the Doctor mentioned strange things happening in the city. I should look around.

speaker: Deimos
en: You're cold-blooded. I would've done the same—at Pylos. Of course, that's not the first time you cast me away to die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So that's what they told you.

speaker: Deimos
en: It's what I know.

speaker: Deimos
en: I don't know what you were thinking back there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What, trying to save you?

speaker: Deimos
en: That's not what that was. I told you to stay out of my way—yet here you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what? I'm a prisoner until I'm killed?

speaker: Deimos
en: That's the plan. Or I could come in there and end you anytime I please. But before that. Tell me what you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought your Cultists told you everything. Sounds like you're on their side, but they're not on yours.

speaker: Deimos
en: You think I'm just a puppet? Then prove it to me. Tell me why I'm on the wrong side. Convince me—I dare you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you want to know?

speaker: Deimos
en: Everything you claim to be true. But after this, I kill you. Why was I abandoned that night on the mountain?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was the Pythia's prophecy. The Spartan ephors said there was no other choice.

speaker: Deimos
en: A prophecy?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You and I both know who feeds the Pythia her words.

speaker: Deimos
en: ...I do. A baby with a fate so terrible it was thrown off a cliff. What kind of prophecy would lead to that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Pythia said you were going to bring Sparta to greatness... or to its downfall. Waiting for the outcome was too big a risk.

speaker: Deimos
en: A risk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I heard you're unpredictable.

speaker: Deimos
en: I call it being decisive. You weren't decisive that night. You—"my family"—let me go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Let you go"? You have no idea what happened on that mountain.

speaker: Deimos
en: Then tell me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one told you that I tried to save you? I ran to catch you. I killed an elder. That ended my life, too.

speaker: Deimos
en: Always trying to play the "hero". It wasn't enough then, and it wasn't enough now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did everything I could. And I'm doing the same today.

speaker: Deimos
en: It's too late. There's nothing you could say to make me feel like family.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen. After you and the elder fell, they threw me off Mount Taygetos, too. Pater... let me go. It was his "duty."

speaker: Deimos
en: You were abandoned, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes.

speaker: Deimos
en: But we both survived. Against their wishes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We did. We're alive.

speaker: Deimos
en: Maybe it serves them right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They've kept secrets from both of us.

speaker: Deimos
en: Right. Though you claim to know much more than me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's Nikolaos. He isn't our real father. It was another man—a man like us.

speaker: Deimos
en: How many more secrets am I supposed to take? When will I get the truth?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gods are cruel.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Cult had their way, they'd be using both of us.

speaker: Deimos
en: Is that so?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They probably won't even kill me. They'll just enslave me like they did you.

speaker: Deimos
en: No, they will kill you. Use me? They need me.

en: They know their strength is in numbers. If I bowed to them like you, they'd have the Greek world at their feet.

en: We did. We're alive.

en: It's nothing.

en: Leave. Now. This was not your action to take, boy.

en: Do whatever you want with her.

speaker: Deimos
en: I am not your puppet!

speaker: Deimos
en: And you are not my master.

en: Of course, champion. An indiscretion I won't repeat.

en: Keep in mind you put yourself in the cell.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't recall doing that.

speaker: Kleon
en: You have to understand—this is all for Athens, Kassandra. Perikles would've impoverished the entire city. The people were living in squalor!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you had him murdered.

speaker: Kleon
en: You can't find the perfect yolk without breaking some of the quail's eggs. he wasn't right for us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Killing your adversaries proves what kind of leader you are.

speaker: Kleon
en: Oh, I'm just getting started. If only you'd be around to watch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you'll do things differently than Perikles.

speaker: Kleon
en: Friends flank my every side. The people trust in me. They know my every decree and law will be to their benefit. And they will delight in what I have planned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come into the cell. You're here to kill me, aren't you? Let's see what happens.
