en: Fortunately for me, there are other fires I need to extinguish. I've heard word of revolt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Already? That was fast.

speaker: Kleon
en: I have a plan—they can't revolt if they're dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know how you can take on a band of rebels if you refuse to fight this one.

speaker: Kleon
en: The act itself is out of my hands—the vote has been cast! What did I tell you? The people have given me their blessing. I use their power.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not democracy.

speaker: Kleon
en: The people have chosen their destiny, Kassandra—they've chosen me.

speaker: Kleon
en: I thought politics was a game to you, remember? It is. And I play to win.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fuck you, Kleon.

speaker: Kleon
en: I'm not alone in this! The people of Athens have spoken without me lifting a finger. That is how you treat rebellion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They don't know what they're agreeing to.

speaker: Kleon
en: You helped me in Athens—even willingly. If only you were more like your brother now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A pity.

speaker: Kleon
en: The Cult wins, Kassandra. Now, I have to see about the boat heading to Mytilene. Its people are in for a rude awakening.

en: Interesting. Death may be the greatest of human blessings, after all.

en: At least you tried.

en: Surely it's the thought that counts! Thank the gods you're alive, Kassandra.

en: If those guards aren't the last, I say we need to leave, and do so quickly.

en: Wait—we need to talk about Kleon.

en: Sokrates is onto that maláka. We know what he's doing.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Be brief! Her equipment, Barnabas.

en: Come, Barnabas! Kassandra, meet us at Perikles' Residence. There, we'll discuss all we know.

speaker: Heriphile
en: By... by the gods! It's... it's you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, well, it certainly is me. You are a shepherdess?

speaker: Heriphile
en: You know me! You know me so well!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what happened.

speaker: Heriphile
en: I was herding my flock when... it was horrible! Wolves! Blood and screams everywhere!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you get hurt?

speaker: Heriphile
en: No... you protected me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did?

speaker: Heriphile
en: I carry your totem, to pray to, to watch over me. But... I was so scared I dropped my totem as I ran.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can look for your totem.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Oh! Thank you! Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where were you attacked?

speaker: Heriphile
en: I was leading my flock to pasture through the forest south of the city. I know others have heard wolves howling there on many nights, but I took a chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about this totem.

speaker: Heriphile
en: It's... a simple thing. An eagle of rough wood and crudely fashioned. It does not come close to capturing your divine glory, but still, it has kept me safe until now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah. I, uh, wish it had protected you better.

speaker: Heriphile
en: No! It is I who must apologize to you for losing it. I feared you would be angry with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, no, of course not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll look for your lost totem.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Eagle Bearer, have you found my totem yet? The forest has become so dangerous now because of the wolves. I hope you find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wolf spoor. They must den near here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Heriphile must have dropped this basket when the wolves attacked.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Blood trail. The pack went this way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of Heriphile's flock. Or what's left of him after the wolf's breakfast.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the den of the wolves that attacked Heriphile's flock. Worth a look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Remarkable that a wolf dragged this bag here. Almost like it was driven. Here is the totem.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Invincible Eagle Bearer, the priestess said you battled the wolves as if guided by blood-stained Ares himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did she know that?

speaker: Heriphile
en: She burns offerings of young goats to see signs of your passage! She said you found my totem!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was luck that I was able to find it. The wolves had dragged it deep into their den. Here you go.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Gratitude, Eagle Bearer! Would you bless it for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't need my blessing. Just watch the world around you. And you can call me Kassandra.

speaker: Heriphile
en: Thank you, Eagle... Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The world is hard and has shaped me to be able to see things and overcome challenges others cannot.

speaker: Heriphile
en: We owe everything to you, your greatness. We will not let you down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know you won't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found him!

en: Chaire. Would you happen to have any Athenian armor in your shop? It's for Diokles's burial.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

en: Diokles sold me his armor not too long ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Timotheos said his father's armor was stolen.

en: Well, I have it here and I'm no thief. I also have another set of Athenian armor. Not as nice, but it'll do for the burial.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take Diokles's armor.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: You'll find it in the chest upstairs. Pleasure doing business with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take the cheaper armor.

en: Figures a mercenary would choose the cheap armor. Here you go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take both sets of armor.

en: Here's the Athenian armor. Diokles' armor is upstairs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Diokles' armor should belong to his son. Hand it over.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Laughs. You think you can threaten me? It's not like I store a set that valuable with my normal wares. You'll find it over my dead body.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a chance I'm willing to take.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Standard Athenian armor. I could bring this back to Timotheos. Or I could look around for his father's armor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should be ready to meet Lykinos and Timotheos at the funeral.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: A new face in Perikles's abode! That in itself is a remarkable thing. You must have seen me doing my impression of Kleon. I call it "The Orange Ape." Tell me, what does it think?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: A misthios in Perikles's abode? I never thought I'd see the day! You must have seen me doing my impression of Hermippos. I call it "The Dejected Weasel." Tell me, what does it think?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you just call me "it"?! Watch your mouth, Athenian!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: It speaks, and so feisty, too! Sometimes I wonder if I'm doomed to be the only young and beautiful thing here. So, what do they call you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am called many things. "It" isn't one of them.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: What do you call yourself then, creature of many names?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Hmm. I wouldn't peg you as a Kassandra. But never mind. I'm Aristophanes, and this man is Euripides. Oh, go on. Introduce yourself.

speaker: Euripides
en: I'm Euripides.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For a playwright, you're not much for words.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Good men lead quiet lives, as old Euripides likes to say. Don't you, Euripides?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Now, if you'll excuse us, I was just about to dazzle this old dog with my impression of Perikles. I call it "The Wooden Board".

speaker: Kassandra
en: The man is your host.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Under every stone hides a politician, I always say, and Perikles is no different.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: It's come back for more! Care to see my impression of Protagoras? I call it "The Flapping Bladder".

speaker: Euripides
en: I'm sure she wouldn't.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Well if you excuse us, I'm working on my impression of you. I call it "The Pretty Monkey".

speaker: Slave
en: I'm too busy to deal with you at the moment. Go on, now. Out of my kitchen.

speaker: Sophokles
en: I suppose you've come here to mock me for my fight with Euripides?

speaker: Sophokles
en: A misthios? Here? I suppose they've sent you to mock me for my fight with Euripides?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen a lot of fights. That wasn't one.

speaker: Sophokles
en: I really made a fool of myself this time, didn't I? I'm Sophokles, though I'm sure you knew that. And you are?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am looking for information that'll help me find someone. A Spartan woman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spare me. I'm only looking for clues to help me find a Spartan woman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a war at the city walls. Suffering. Starvation. And you're in here arguing because...someone at the party isn't giving you the attention you need?

speaker: Sophokles
en: That's no way to calm down someone who is obviously upset.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, its not. I am looking for information that'll help me find someone. A Spartan woman.

speaker: Sophokles
en: A Spartan woman in Athens? Sounds intriguing, though if you expect me to notice someone other than myself, you expect too much. You could talk to Euripides—he's the second-most worldly man here, that pediculous, xanthodontous, exophthalmic... morosoph. But he doesn't talk without a drink.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have no idea what that meant.

speaker: Sophokles
en: No, you don't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, we get him drunk, and he talks? He sounds more Argive than Athenian.

speaker: Sophokles
en: Impressive, foreigner. Euripides is from Argos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want to get Euripides drunk...Are you hoping he's going to make an even bigger scene than you did?

speaker: Sophokles
en: Ha! We both know that's not possible. But you're a feisty one, to say the least.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. If nothing else, this party could use the help.

speaker: Sophokles
en: You'll need to pick the right wine for this task. The kitchen should have what you need. Let me know when Euripides is done in, and I'll slip away unseen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know Perikles?

speaker: Sophokles
en: I believe you mean to ask me, "How does Perikles know you?" I'm the greatest dramatist in the land, mentor to Euripides, lover of Asklepios, father of theater, and so on, and so on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure it's a real honor to have you hiding in his kitchen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're awfully worked up over Euripides. You sure you're just friends?

speaker: Sophokles
en: I'm never "just" anything, foreigner. Though I confess, Euripides and I hold a bond deeper than brotherhood. Why he slums it with that banal young plaything, Aristophanes, I'll never know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get the wine.

speaker: Sophokles
en: Wonderful. Now, if you want some friendly advice, Aristophanes cannot stand sweet wine. I've seen what it can do to him—absolutely, horrifyingly delightful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It wouldn't be a party without someone losing their stomach. I'll let you know if your plan worked.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Care for another impression? My favorite is Sophokles.

speaker: Euripides
en: That one isn't funny.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I need to relax, I start a fight. For you, though...

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Quickly, bring him some wine so that he might say something clever!

speaker: Euripides
en: After my argument with Sophokles, I think I'd rather keep my head clear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm only here because I'm searching for someone.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: And yet it gave us the distinct impression it was here to fill our wine. Let's focus on that first, shall we?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You and Aristophanes could both use a drink. Let's play a game.

speaker: Euripides
en: A competition?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Ah! Wonderful idea. Euripides seems quiet, but he never turns down a challenge.

speaker: Euripides
en: Well, if you brought us some wine, I wouldn't be opposed to showing this young one how we Argives drink.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm Perikles's new servant. I'd be happy to bring some wine.

speaker: Euripides
en: An Athenian servant? You? And these are wine-pouring muscles?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was a rower on Perikles's ship, where he took pity on me. Now, I pour wine for people who question my word, and his.

speaker: Euripides
en: I... I wasn't questioning. I... perhaps one drink.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return. And when I do, you two will drink up

speaker: Slave
en: Save for that arrogant playwright, I don't see many distinguished guests in here. Can I help you with something?

speaker: Slave
en: You! You shouldn't be in here. What do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come to get your finest dry wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for your sweet wine.

speaker: Slave
en: Yes, take it. But get out of my kitchen. I'm very busy, you know!

speaker: Aged Wine
en: There was no greater wine than the wine being poured at Perikles's home, and this was no exception.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why don't you just apologize to Sophokles?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: It's he who should apologize to you!

speaker: Euripides
en: Sophokles is a friend, and one good friend is worth an entire family. He just needs time to recover from his outburst.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perikles has invited all of you here for some reason.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Either we dine here, and praise Perikles, or we dine with Kleon... But Kleon has all the charms of a typical politician—a horrible voice, bad breeding, and vulgar manners.

speaker: Kassandra
en: To Dionysos!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: This... this is delicious!

speaker: Euripides
en: This is nectar of the gods! Another round!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How about some more?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Where did you get this delicious wine? It must be Perikles's finest!

speaker: Euripides
en: You know what they say! Good wine makes good friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ready for another?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: This is the best symposium I've been to in a while.

speaker: Euripides
en: You know what? I like you. Who brought you here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's conjure Dionysus, shall we?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: This... this is pure swill.

speaker: Euripides
en: Amateur! In my day, this would be considered nectar of the gods. Another round!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ready for more?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Gah! I can hardly stomach this pig's piss.

speaker: Euripides
en: I could outdrink both of you with one hand! Let's have some more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You ready for another?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: This wine is terrible.

speaker: Euripides
en: You... I like you. Who brought you here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I brought myself. I'm on the trail of a woman who fled Sparta a long time ago.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Fled? Why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She lost two children. She had no choice.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: She fled to heal her broken heart. Euripides, write her into a play.

speaker: Euripides
en: I've heard Spartan mothers go to a sanctuary in Argolis to beg Asklepios for his divine pity. I should know—it's my home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After what she went through, I'm not sure she'd trust priests.

speaker: Euripides
en: Then she sought my friend Hippokrates. He's a physician, best of the best. He still keeps his office in Argos. If she went to him for help, there's no doubt he'd have given it.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I love getting drunk and singing. Come back if you want to sing with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll think about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates in Argos... Here I come.

speaker: Sophokles
en: How's Euripides? Drunk, I hope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can stop hiding in here. Euripides won't notice you coming out—he won't notice anything.

speaker: Sophokles
en: Hiding?! Heed this: war has come to Athens. First they take our homes, then they take our heads. I intend to be found with at least my dignity intact. Or what's left of it, anyway.

speaker: Sophokles
en: If you see Perikles, tell him I said thank you for another colorful evening.

speaker: Euripides
en: Dionysos! There you are. Everyone else here is boring. Let's play a singing game. You like to sing? You like to sing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not singing.

speaker: Euripides
en: Sing with me. Friends sing with each other. That's just what friends do. And you, me—we're friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you have in mind?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: One of use will sing, then the other, and then back again. We'll take turns making verses, and whoever makes the best is the winner.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's do this.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I want to play too! But who should start?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think you should, Arisophanes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Euripides should start. It was his idea.

speaker: Playwright 1
en: Fine, fine. But let's do a good one. A battle song?

speaker: Playwright 2
en: Is there any other kind?

speaker: Playwright 1
en: With a flick of her limb, comes Aspasia's whim. And Perikles's walls aim to contain us all, within.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Spartan hordes outside eat your cattle and children alive. They dance at your walls— they don't rain, but they squall...

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Perikles guarantees death for us all!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What Spartan families lose, they lose for duty. When Spartan fathers refuse, they refuse beauty...

speaker: Aristophanes
en: But the dangerous part are the Athenian tarts, who go for the meat when they should go for the heart!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The war... has come to Athens... No time to...

speaker: Aristophanes
en: And we have no time to care what happens! So, take your sword and shield! Let blood paint what you wield! Until the boys lay like wheat upon the fields.

speaker: Euripides
en: Oh, so bring your merchants! And bring their butlers! If they be sons, then bring their fathers! This is war, war, war!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Bring your murderers to the crimson quiver! Bring the helots, if they be spillers! It is war, war, war!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Collect your weak and collect your sinners! Line them up at the phalanx dinner! This is war, war, war!

speaker: Euripides
en: If they want blood, then blood you'll give them!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll stab their guts, and let them spill it! This is war, war, war!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Without our fathers or mothers, we row straight to Hades or the belly of Melos. We are alone, and so we row. For a short life, we row, row, row.

speaker: Kassandra
en: War is... tough... The more we fight, the more we...

speaker: Euripides
en: The more we love! Let the juices flow from the heart to the spear. We have nothing to fear when death is near. Our bodies bring with them nothing they hold dear.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: The stupid sweepers? The genius teachers? All just meats, and juice, and liver!

speaker: Kassandra
en: For when our wars are done, after lives are lost and blood has run, we must rejoin our broken daughters and our sons. Reunited together, we will be one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So grab your spears and grab your daggers! Plunge them deep in! Heroes they'll make us! This is war! War! War!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is war, war, war!

speaker: Euripides
en: War, war, war!

speaker: Aristophanes
en: War, war, war!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's hope... For peace...

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Tomorrow, at least! But today we live and breathe, so we fight to the teeth!

speaker: Euripides
en: Enough! Enough. You... you're a great singer.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: The best! You should act in my plays!

speaker: Euripides
en: Here, take this to remember the occasion! This party has turned out much better than I ever could have expected.

speaker: Euripides
en: That was awful. I'm not sure you even know how to sing.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: We might be too drunk. That was the worst song I've ever heard.

speaker: Euripides
en: You should talk to Hippokrates in Argos. I'm sure he'll help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here about the job you posted. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: You! Eagle Bearer, you were a great friend of General Brasidas of Sparta, were you not?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I knew Brasidas, but we did not see eye to eye on a lot of things.

speaker: Woman
en: Oh... That is your loss. Brasidas was my cousin, and he was the most wonderful man. You would have been lucky to call him your friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas and I worked together a few times.

speaker: Woman
en: I knew it! Brasidas was my cousin and the most wonderful man I ever knew!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas and I were very close, yes.

speaker: Woman
en: I knew it! He only ever said wonderful things about you. He was my cousin, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is that so...

speaker: Woman
en: I'd like to return his effects to his family, but a Spartan commander is holding onto them... tightly. As his best friend, you must know how important it is for his family to receive closure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you're asking me to get it for you?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, I need it back at all costs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can count on me.

speaker: Woman
en: Good, get this done quickly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Woman
en: Tell me it's been handled, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all yours.

speaker: Woman
en: Job well done, mercenary. Here, this is yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Happy to help.

speaker: Empty the Stocks
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Thank you for aiding all of us in Pitana. Stories of you will live amongst us for many years.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I help where I can. But thank you.

speaker: Xanthe
en: A reward, for all your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK, I can either kill them one by one or flood them with cold water.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the pipe. Opening it should flood the bath and get rid of the snakes.

speaker: Priest
en: And? Is the bathhouse free of snakes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I flooded the bathhouse with cold water.

speaker: Priest
en: Good riddance!

speaker: Priest
en: And? Is the bathhouse free of snakes?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I carved up every single one of those slimy malakes.

speaker: Priest (Doreios)
en: My babies! What have you done to my babies?

speaker: Priest (Pylenor)
en: Your snakes infested my bathhouse! A sick man is dead because of them.

speaker: Priest (Doreios)
en: You! You did this!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good snakes are dead snakes.

speaker: Priest
en: You'll pay for this! I curse you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I only did what Pylenor told me to do.

speaker: Priest (Pylenor)
en: What? How dare you? I never said kill them!

speaker: Priest (Doreios)
en: How could you, Pylenor? You'll pay for this. I curse you both to Hades!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well?

speaker: Priest
en: Well what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of your snakes. Now you're going to tell me about the Spartan woman and the baby.

speaker: Priest
en: I actually don't know anything. Was before my time. The man who does know is Mydon, but he won't tell you. He won't tell anyone anything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Malákes snakes. At least I got a name. Mydon.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I lost a couple of good men in the scrap with those pirates. The seas are more dangerous now that Sparta and Athens are at each other's throats.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need new recruits to better our crew...

speaker: Barnabas
en: I know where to start—the best archer I know, he'd be a valuable asset.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When can we meet him?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well... You're going to have to persuade him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Barnabas
en: You get him aboard, and I'll talk him into it... A little drachmae should sweeten the deal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, you want me to... knock him out.

speaker: Barnabas
en: No, no. Well, maybe just pacify him a little. Then get him to the ship, so we can have a little talk. Everything will be fine, I promise you.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The gods are with us today, Kassandra. The sea is calm, and the winds are warm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's beautiful.

speaker: Barnabas
en: It is, my friend. It sure is. That's the island. You'll need to be cautious - it'll be crawling with pirates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should send Ikaros up to get the lay of the land. He'll spot my target.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'll make a worthy addition to the crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got him.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Good, he'll be a valuable asset to the crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Will he be enough?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Don't worry, there'll be plenty of opportunities to recruit more people as we go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something tells me we're going to need them.

speaker: Barnabas
en: We should set a course for Megaris. A long voyage can be relaxing, but we are not really the cruising type. If you want to spice things up a bit, you can always check my log over there. I make a note of anything I hear that could be of interest... to a daring captain.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Stop! I can't let you go any further.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It isn't often you see a guard outside of an artist's workshop.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: I just do what I'm told, stranger. And until I'm told otherwise, no one is going in or out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stand aside. This is important.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: So is keeping people out. Maybe you can see Phidias after his trial... If the people spare his life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen. I'm working for Perikles. He wants me to see Phidias.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Well, I'm working for the people of Athens, and they want Phidias dead. Now back off, or you're dead too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone has a price. How much drachmae is this going to take?

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Depends how much you have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, take it.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: That'll do just fine. You tell anyone I did this and you're as good as dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Funny. I was going to say the same to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I tried to be nice. I really did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's been so long since Phidias and I have... seen each other. You understand, don't you?

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Oh! Oh... Come to pay him a last visit before the trial? He's as good as dead, you know. Better make this one count.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just don't tell anyone I was here.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Sure, sure. Keep it moving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phidias and I have been friends for a long time. I'm leaving Athens, and I don't know if I'll ever see him again.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: You won't. If you want to leave Athens in one piece, you'll go. Now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone has a price. How much drachmae is this going to take?

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Depends how much you have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, take it.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: That'll do just fine. You tell anyone I did this and you're as good as dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Funny. I was going to say the same to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I tried to be nice. I really did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sorry about that.

speaker: Phidias
en: How did you get past the guard? No one gets past the guard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Relax. Perikles sent me.

speaker: Phidias
en: Praise Athena, I knew he'd send help. I was worried they sent someone after me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He sent me to get you out of Athens.

speaker: Phidias
en: So he knows about the plot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean the trial? From what I've seen, you don't stand a chance.

speaker: Phidias
en: Pah! The people love me. I am the Phidias! But there are others. Look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka. It isn't the trial that Perikles is saving you from... these are instruction to murder you. Who wrote this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: "They" who?

speaker: Phidias
en: The shadows in the night... why you fear falling asleep. They're hunting me. Us. No one is safe in Athens anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you do know. I tried talking to Perikles, but we were interrupted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult of Kosmos... You know about them .

speaker: Phidias
en: Of course I know about the Cult. Here, look at this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These are instructions...

speaker: Phidas
en: On how to kill me. But they've been torn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then Perikles isn't just getting you out of Athens to save you from trial... He's saving you from being murdered.

speaker: Phidias
en: I don't know who to trust. I'm just an artist... I just wanted to create. Please, what am I to do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: First, you need to pull yourself together. You're on trial, the people are against you, and now I find that the Cult want to kill you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I said, pull yourself together.

speaker: Phidias
en: Yes, of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kleon said you're wasting the people's drachmae. If he has his way, he'd serve them your head.

speaker: Phidias
en: Kleon mentioned me? That's going to hurt Perikles. First impiety, now theft. After all we've done for this city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You and Perikles seem close...

speaker: Phidias
en: For Perikles and me, it started with our love of Athens. Our differences push us to greatness. That is true friendship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. We need to go. Do you have any idea where I can take you?

speaker: Phidias
en: South of Athens, there's an island called Seriphos. My friend Theras lives there. When I discovered the plot against me, I sent word to him. If anyone can help us, he can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Any clues he has of the Cultists' identities, I want them.

speaker: Phidias
en: Yes, yes, anything...

speaker: Phidias
en: A guard!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll distract them while you sneak out. Meet me tonight to set sail for Seriphos. Don't show your face until you see me at the docks.

speaker: Phidias
en: I understand.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: You didn't really think I'd let you come and go as you pleased, did you? Now, where are you?

speaker: Phidias
en: Good, you made it. I was beginning to worry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told you I'd get you out of Athens.

speaker: Phidias
en: So you did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can your friend be trusted?

speaker: Phidias
en: Theras and I have been friends for a long time. I just sent word telling him where to meet us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wasting time will only get us into trouble. Let's head to Seriphos while we still can.

speaker: Phidias
en: I never thought I'd leave Athens for good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've left places I've called home.

speaker: Phidias
en: I hope leaving Athens was the right thing to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course it was. You'll be safe this way.

speaker: Phidias
en: Will I?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Safer than you were, at least. If the Cult can't find you, they can't kill you. It's simple.

speaker: Phidias
en: So long as they don't find me, yes. But who knows where they are... who they are... we could be heading somewhere even more dangerous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe. But this is your best chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos, what's that island ahead of us?

speaker: Herodotos
en: That, my friend, is the famous island of Salamis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The place where Athens defeated the Persians?

speaker: Herodotos
en: It's in this bay that the great Athenian strategos Themistokles destroyed the Persian fleet and saved the Greek world from annihilation.

speaker: Phidias
en: Hopefully, the Cult won't bother me now that I'm out of Athens.

speaker: Phidias
en: This is a nice ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't have to do that.

speaker: Phidias
en: Do what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fill the silence.

speaker: Phidias
en: Oh! I wasn't trying to do that at all. I simply don't find myself traveling the seas very often.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It can be freeing.

speaker: Phidias
en: Yes, "freeing" seems to be an accurate word. Although I've begun to feel a bit sick...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lean over the side if you need to, otherwise you're cleaning it up.

speaker: Phidias
en: Is your stomach turning as much as mine is?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll get used to it. We'll reach Seriphos before long.

speaker: Civilian
en: It's good to see you alive and well, Phidias!

speaker: Phidias
en: And you, Theras. As you can see, I didn't get here alone.

speaker: Civilian
en: Ah, yes, the kind and thoughtful hero you mentioned in your letter!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad I could get him out alive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I wasn't getting something out of it, He'd be dead already.

speaker: Civilian
en: And for that heroism, I've found some information on a man named Brison who's plotting Phidias's early demise. Hopefully, you can make something of this clue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can.

speaker: Phidias
en: Please give Perikles my thanks and my farewell. And be careful—I still believe many in Athens are in danger. Thank you again. Don't forget to come see me under less stressful circumstances.

speaker: Kleio
en: Misthios, please. We were heading to Mykonos, which is safe. If you'll take me there, I can pay you the toll I'd have paid my crew.

speaker: Kassandra

en: Take this map. It's rough, but it's the best I could do.

speaker: Theras
en: Chaire, Eagle Bearer, and thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phew, this metal is heavy. And here's a note... The Forge of Atlantis? This can be used to create weapons! I have to find this place.

speaker: Adamant shipment record
en: Enclosed is the last adamant ingot from the old Forge of Atlantis south of the Royal Mountain of Poseidon. The rest of the ingots should be kept in multiple city archives and repositories. A meeting hall will be built in the Dikastes honor once the Forge is destroyed at a later date.

speaker: Fire at Will
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Did you find what you were looking for in Athens?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A few clues—but this won't be easy.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well it's a good start! All we can do now is trust the path the gods have laid out for us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not the only one looking for my mother. The cult that wanted Nikolaos dead? They're also on my trail.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Oh, they're no match for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You got that right.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Do you see that volcano?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's pretty hard to miss.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Some say there is an entrance to the underworld at the bottom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what, you enter by diving in it?

speaker: Barnabas
en: That's the spirit! A brave Arkadian I once knew had the same idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what happened to him?

speaker: Barnabas
en: The heat of the flames turned him to ashes before he made it halfway down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess some mysteries are best left unexplored.

speaker: Barnabas
en: We need to keep away from the shoreline here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Years ago, we found a dying man on the beach—arms ripped from his body, face scarred by terror... With his last breath, he warned of a beast who roams the woods near the shore.

speaker: Herodotos
en: A beast, really...

speaker: Barnabas
en: Yes, a monster! With big, red flaming eyes and a roar like Zeus' thunder!

speaker: Herodotos
en: And, of course, you've seen it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Like the gods, we've never seen them, but know they exist. You think Zeus doesn't exist? We can't see him with our own eyes!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Well of course, but

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos, he's got a point.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Argolis! The land of science and home to the legendary city of Argos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never thought I would get to see it with my own eyes.

speaker: Herodotos
en: The tomb of King Agamemnon, the sanctuary of Asklepios, the old Minoan ruins! The history here is astounding.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's Hippokrates' clinic.

speaker: Chrysis
en: Apollo himself should smite your precious Hippokrates!

speaker: Sostratos
en: But priestess, Hippokrates does respect Apollo.

speaker: Chrysis
en: What an outrageous claim! Your words are daggers thrust into the heart of our faith. Do you want to bring ruin to all of Argolis?

speaker: Sostratos
en: Of course not, but...

speaker: Chrysis
en: Then tell me where to find Hippokrates!

speaker: Sostratos
en: Forgive me, but I really can't help you.

speaker: Chrysis
en: Look, you insignificant peon. Tell me where he is or by Hera, I'll burn this clinic to the ground with you in it!

speaker: Sostratos
en: I already told you what I know!

speaker: Chrysis
en: I don't ask much. Hippokrates must show humility to ensure public order—prostrate himself before the gods, and declare that his skills are gods-given.

speaker: Sostratos
en: But that won't help his patients. It'll just take him away from his work.

speaker: Chrysis
en: If Hippokrates thinks he can disrupt social order to make himself into a demigod of healing... Well, perhaps the gods themselves will have their revenge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure there's no need for raised voices.

speaker: Chrysis
en: Who are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for a man named Hippokrates.

speaker: Chrysis
en: Yet another crazed follower of the madman himself! Tell your impious master that unless he makes a public apology and soon, this Priestess of Hera will gather an army of faithful and shut him down. Out of my way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Back away from the boy. Slowly.

speaker: Chrysis
en: Who dares threaten the Priestess of Hera?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me. Now step back.

speaker: Chrysis
en: It seems the gods wish me to grant you and your master another chance. Very well.

speaker: Chrysis
en: Tell Hippokrates that if he doesn't make a public show of respect to the gods, I will raise an army of believers against him. If the doctor can't think of a suitable offering, his head will do.

speaker: Sostratos
en: Oh, thank all the gods she's gone. I thought she was going to kill me this time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on?

speaker: Sostratos
en: I'm Sostratos. Chrysis has accused my master Hippokrates of impiety.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is he impious?

speaker: Sostratos
en: He believes that beyond praying, people can take their health into their own hands and make themselves well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fascinating. Can I speak with him?

speaker: Sostratos
en: I'm sorry. He isn't here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to meet Hippokrates. Is he in Argolis, at least?

speaker: Sostratos
en: Yes, but he's gone southeast of Hera's Watch to help the sick and injured.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is this his workshop?

speaker: Sostratos
en: It's Hippokrates's clinic. Here we study healing, offer treatments, and provide care to anyone who asks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why not work with the priests in the Sanctuary of Asklepios? It's what this region is known for, right?

speaker: Sostratos
en: The priests try their best, but their methods are stuck in the past. Hippokrates is researching new cures and treatments.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find him.

speaker: Sostratos
en: If you're going to meet Hippokrates...could I trouble you with a small errand?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Depends what it is.

speaker: Sostratos
en: I want you to bring him some equipment. He was in such a hurry, he left it behind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of equipment?

speaker: Sostratos
en: Just medical necessities. Knives and gut for sutures, bandages... Oh, and an enema bag for clearing the bowels.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They had better be properly wrapped.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could bring that to Hippokrates.

speaker: Sostratos
en: Really?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be sure he gets the equipment.

speaker: Sostratos
en: You have my thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My services don't come free.

speaker: Sostratos
en: Here, take this. Though perhaps Hippokrates can teach you something about helping those in need when you speak with him.

speaker: Medical Supplies
en: The contents of this bag include a myriad of medical tools and supplies, such as knives, bandages, and natural salves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How will I know when I've found Hippokrates?

speaker: Sostratos
en: Follow the road southeast of Hera's Watch to the Cave of Pan. He won't have set up far from it. Look for a long line of sick people. He's balding, but I wouldn't mention that if I were you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So many sick people... Can one man help all of them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought they were exaggerating when they said people from all around came to see Hippokrates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what has caused this man's condition?

speaker: Nurse
en: An excess of phlegm, doctor.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: In the immediate sense, yes. But more importantly, he suffers from neglect.

speaker: Nurse
en: Neglect?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Good food, warm clothing, so much could have helped. But since other "caretakers" assumed his condition was a punishment from the gods, they neglected him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Challenging tradition... You must be Hippokrates.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Yes. I'm also very busy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This will only take a moment. I won't keep you away from your patients... and your students?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Observation, experience, and experimentation are crucial for treatment. My followers are learning that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is important. Where are all these people coming from anyway?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Patience, mercenary. They come from everywhere, but this is mostly overflow from the Sanctuary of Asklepios. It's been crowded there since the war began. And with crowding comes sickness...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come from your clinic in Argos. Sostratos asked me to give you this.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I knew I forgot some things. Sostratos is a good physician, but a better apprentice there is none. Did you ask him to pay you for this delivery?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, I knew this would help you and your patients. That's good enough for me.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Quite admirable. What did you say your name was?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I did. I'm a misthios.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Ungenerous, but honest at least. What can I call you, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra of Sparta.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Well met, Kassandra of Sparta. What do you need?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been searching for a Spartan woman.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: What makes you think I would know her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was told you may have helped her a long time ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates, I need your help. I was told you may have helped my mother. I'm trying to find her.

speaker: Nurse
en: But we see all kinds of mothers. They walk all day so that Hippokrates can see their children.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Maybe the priests at the Sanctuary of Asklepios can help. They keep detailed records of all who pass through.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Please, Hippokrates. I came very far to meet you.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: As did this patient, and the one before him, and the one before her. My patients need me, but my notes on diseases of the mind were taken. Retrieve them, and I will help you find what you seek. Hurry! This patient doesn't have much time left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: According to Sostratos, you don't like people mentioning your... you know.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: My what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your hair. Or lack of it.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Yes, yes. Make your jokes while walking around like one of Phidias' sculptures come to life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where should I look for your notes?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Fort Tiryns, not far from here. Perhaps they'll return them if you ask.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or they could prepare for a new battle, with me.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Far be it from me to tell a misthios how to work, but please, for my sake, do not kill needlessly. Enough blood has been shed in this war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did Chrysis take your notes?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Ah, you've met the priestess. No, not her, but the local military commander. I can't fault his desperation. Those men suffer terribly from battle fatigue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She would have come here a long time ago, with an injured baby. Are you sure she would have passed through the Sanctuary of Asklepios?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I was a young man then. When I encountered a situation beyond my skills, I would send the patient to the Sanctuary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And these priests kept records of their patients?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Yes, engraved in stone. The elder priest might remember.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What was so interesting about these notes?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: They were my notes about diseases of the mind, including what the priests call the "". That's what this patient has. He's losing control of his limbs and throat—sometimes frothing at the mouth. I fear his breathing will stop next.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do my best with what you've told me.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Good luck. We're depending on you. I really need those notes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Need something, stranger?

speaker: Woman
en: You look just like her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who?

speaker: Woman
en: Phoenix, leader of Naxos. I can see it in your eyes. You must be related.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are right. We are related.

speaker: Woman
en: I knew it! Ever since she arrived on Naxos, things have been much better for us. But when Phoenix picked a fight with Paros, the Athenian army started stealing all our fish right from under our noses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know what you're talking about.

speaker: Woman
en: Strange. I have such a good talent for spotting those things. Well, since you're here, we've been having trouble with our neighbors, the Athenians. They keep steeling our fresh fish.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're asking me to send all the Athenians to the underworld.

speaker: Woman
en: All the soldiers must die. It's the only way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

speaker: Woman
en: You have my thanks, mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: Honest pay for honest work, misthios. Take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All in a day's work.

speaker: Beating the Hammer
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Civilian
en: You there! Misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's on your mind, old man?

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm dying, misthios. I can feel it in my bones. But first, there's something I need to do. Will you help an old man fulfil his dying wish? I can offer you what drachmae I have left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't deny an old man his final wish. What is it?

speaker: Civilian
en: I always promised my wife I'd take her to see the red flowers on the summit of the mountain in Zeus' Playground. It's a beautiful place—great view. But she met the ferryman before me, misthios. I never made good on my promise. It was always one thing or another, you know? Children, war, what have you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you'd tried harder, she might have gotten to see the view.

speaker: Civilian
en: I tell myself that every day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was a tough situation. You did your best.

speaker: Civilian
en: You're a kind soul, misthios. But I failed her... I did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what do you want me to do?

speaker: Civilian
en: I need you to pick some of those red flowers for me from the Summit of Mount Ida so I can take them to my wife when I meet Hades. Just a few would do. Bring them back to me here. I'll be waiting, misthios. And— I don't have long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I understand.

speaker: Civilian
en: I can't wait to see my wife again, but I'm going to need those red flowers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the place the old man spoke of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is. The flower.

speaker: Red Flower
en: This is an extremely rare and beautiful flower picked from the peak of Mount Ida.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The flowers... I should hurry back to the old man near Gortyn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hades claims another.

speaker: Civilian
en: In all my life, I've never seen him so peaceful. I hope he's found mater. Those flowers... Are they

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. He asked me to fetch them.

speaker: Civilian
en: You silly old man. Is this why you left Pephka? To fetch mater flowers so far from home? You silly, stubborn, old man...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you so much, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He made a promise to his wife. And I made a promise to him.

speaker: Civilian
en: I don't have anything to offer you

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your father promised me his drachmae.

speaker: Civilian
en: Oh. Here, it's all he had on him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, old man.

speaker: Civilian
en: Mater must be so glad you brought her flowers. You never did when she was alive...

speaker: Erinna
en: Kleio? Kleio? Has anyone seen Kleio?

speaker: Erinna
en: By Aphrodite, Kleio better get back here soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why call on the gods when you have one of their messengers at your service?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe there's something a mercenary can do for you?

speaker: Erinna
en: How'd you know I needed help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anthousa told me you could use a hand.

speaker: Erinna
en: Kleio, one of our girls, didn't meet me for prayer this morning. She wasn't at home, either. I'd go investigate but I'm not sure what I could do on my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She might have been taken.

speaker: Erinna
en: I asked around. One of our clients said he saw Kleio brought aboard a ship. The men were armed, so there was nothing he could do. I'd pay a lot of drachmae to get her back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Armed? Take me to the ship. We'll get Kleio back.

speaker: Erinna
en: Follow me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who do you think they took her?

speaker: Erinna
en: It wouldn't be the first time the Monger's men came after one of us.

speaker: Erinna
en: None of us have ever disappeared like this before. Some are worried they'll be taken next.

speaker: Erinna
en: Korinth may have a bad reputation, but it wasn't always that way. We used to be safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Until the Monger...

speaker: Erinna
en: We're not sure why he came here, but Korinth is worse off because of him.

speaker: Erinna
en: There! That's the boat our client described. Please, get her back safely.

speaker: Kleio
en: Stay back!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to rescue you.

speaker: Kleio
en: Rescue me? You sunk my boat, pirate!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Put the knife away. I'm a friend.

speaker: Kleio
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me? An outlaw? You wound me.

speaker: Kleio
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't make me take that knife by force. I was sent here by a friend.

speaker: Kleio
en: Lies!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friend hired me to save you from these men and bring you back.

speaker: Kleio
en: Erinna?! I commissioned that ship to steal me away from Korinth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're... escaping? From what?

speaker: Kleio
en: You have no idea what the Monger does to people. The things I've seen. No one in Korinth is safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Erinna thought you were abducted. She clearly cares about you.

speaker: Kleio
en: If she cared about me, she'd let me go. Even Anthousa can't keep us safe anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She clearly disagrees.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Greek world is being ravaged by war. You're no safer on the seas than you are in Korinth.

speaker: Kleio
en: Misthios, please. We were heading to Mykonos, which is safe. If you'll take me there, I can pay you the toll I'd have paid my crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll get you there. Next time my crew docks at Mykonos, you can depart. In the meantime, welcome aboard.

speaker: Kleio
en: Thank you, misthios! This is what's best, I promise.

speaker: Erinna
en: What happened? Where's Kleio?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friend is safe. That's what matters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friend didn't need rescuing. She hired that ship to get out of Korinth and go somewhere safe.

speaker: Erinna
en: So. She's really gone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's not coming back, no.

speaker: Erinna
en: Thank you. I'll let Anthousa know. Guess I'll be alone at prayer tomorrow. You promise she's safe?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have my word.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The ship had to be sunk. I'm sorry.

speaker: Erinna
en: What do you mean? They had Kleio!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They were too aggressive. They would've sunk me if I didn't sink them first.

speaker: Erinna
en: How am I going to tell Anthousa? Poor Kleio...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friend is safe. That's what matters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friend didn't need rescuing. She hired that ship to get out of Korinth and go somewhere safe.

speaker: Erinna
en: So. She's really gone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's not coming back, no.

speaker: Erinna
en: Thank you. I'll let Anthousa know. Guess I'll be alone at prayer tomorrow. You promise she's safe?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have my word.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anthousa will take care of you. You need to go back to Korinth. It's your home.

speaker: Kleio
en: Take me against my wishes, then. I won't fight you.

speaker: Erinna
en: Kleio! Did they hurt you? I prayed to Tyche for your safe return!

speaker: Kleio
en: I'm fine, I'm fine.

speaker: Erinna
en: There'd better not be a scratch on you. I promised this mercenary a month's salary to have you back in one piece.

speaker: Kleio
en: You did?

speaker: Erinna
en: Of course! You're my dear sister.

speaker: Erinna
en: I'm so thankful Kleio is home. Please, take this for your trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good luck to both of you.

speaker: Erinna
en: At least the excitement is over. Things can get back to normal now.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'll follow you in after you've finished...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Killing everyone inside.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Yes. That.

speaker: Herodotos
en: So this is where they've been hiding.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were right to suggest we look here. But they've been dealt with.

speaker: Herodotos
en: We still need to find out what they were doing here in the first place. Let's look around.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Athenian and Spartan uniforms...

speaker: Herodotos
en: They could have the people of Samos believe they were attacking from either side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't take the Followers of Ares to be lovers of poetry.

speaker: Herodotos
en: They're not. This work... it's awfully close to the style Theodoros uses. Why would his writings be here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't take them for the heirloom type.

speaker: Herodotos
en: How did they... That's our family's sigil.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They must have stolen it.

speaker: Herodotos
en: There's no way they could have found that on their own. It was given to them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a list of names here.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I recognize these names. They're all quite influential on Samos. But... Mestor's is missing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These coins aren't like any I've seen before.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I have. They're Persian...

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'm afraid to even say what I think is going on here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll say it. Persia want to take Samos.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I think you're right. It's close enough to places like Athens and Sparta, but small enough to not draw their attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Makes sense.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Unfortunately, that's not the worst part.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This island and these people are yours. Tell me what you're thinking.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Persia wants to take control of Samos. It'd be a good staging ground for something greater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I only wish that was all there is to worry about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it?

speaker: Herodotos
en: If Persia is involved, they couldn't have done this alone. They would have needed someone here to help them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone with ties to the empire.

speaker: Herodotos
en: And influence on Samos, yes. Other than myself, there are only two others who could be responsible. For what's going to happen... and for what already has.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos...

speaker: Herodotos
en: With everything we've found... everything you've seen and heard. Please, just tell me which of them it is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's Theodoros. He's working for the Persians and brought the Followers of Ares here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's Mestor. He brought the Followers of Ares here to help Persia.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I was afraid you'd say that, but I know you must be right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you want to do now?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I need to talk to Theodoros.

speaker: Roxana
en: Shall we continue?

speaker: Roxana
en: The champion returns.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now that we've saved the children of Hydrea from a pack of hungry wolves, I guess we can move on?

speaker: Roxana
en: You jest, but that was a real nuisance we dealt with. Your choices have an impact, Kassandra - your actions have already benefited the people here. So, shall we complete our training?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We do have unfinished business.

speaker: Roxana
en: The training... or the company?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to finish this training - that's it.

speaker: Roxana
en: All business, eh, champion? You need to loosen up once in a while.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe after this next challenge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've been having so much fun.

speaker: Roxana
en: Fighting each other... Killing wolves...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go on...

speaker: Roxana
en: I think you'll like this next challenge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes?

speaker: Roxana
en: We're going to have a foot race. First one to the high point on the island wins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The last part of training is a race?

speaker: Roxana
en: The Battle of One Hundred Hands is about skill, strength, and most of all, endurance. A tired competitor is an easy target for someone with stamina. I make regular offerings to Hermes to stay fast.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And if I win this race, what will I get?

speaker: Roxana
en: Bragging rights alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Great.

speaker: Roxana
en: It's not the result you should be after, it's the training. After this, you will be ready to enter the Battle of One Hundred Hands. I will vouch for you, and you will vouch for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready. You said race to the high point

speaker: Roxana
en: Yes! The plateau on the other side of town. When I say go, the race is on. Three... Two... One... Go!

speaker: Roxana
en: Come on, champion! Is that all you've got?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not over yet!

speaker: Roxana
en: You'll need to move faster in the Battle, champion!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm pacing myself!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought you'd be faster!

speaker: Roxana
en: Just enjoying the view!

speaker: Roxana
en: Now you're just showing off!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Should I slow down?

speaker: Roxana
en: You're fast, even with all that gear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's easy to forget how beautiful it is here.

speaker: Roxana
en: When you're training so hard, you mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm trying to restore balance to my life, and to the Greek world. To find closure. But there are people standing in my way I must take care of first, and I think winning the Battle of One Hundred Hands will help.

speaker: Roxana
en: What makes you think that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Call it a hunch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I travel a lot, but it's often at the service of others. I can be so focused on drachmae that I lose sight of what's in front of me.

speaker: Roxana
en: And what's that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The ocean breeze on my face. The sun on my skin. A sturdy horse to ride.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All this training leaves no time for fun.

speaker: Roxana
en: I can tell you're holding something back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...Maybe.

speaker: Roxana
en: I come up here to remind myself to live in the moment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can see how that might work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you told Barnabas there was a sea monster living in your ear, he'd believe you.

speaker: Roxana
en: He sounds like a real dimwit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Actually, he's one of the most genuine people I've ever met.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm telling you, he was never fully dressed. And some people on Kythera built a statue to this man. Malákas Empedokles.

speaker: Roxana
en: What became of him?

speaker: Roxana
en: That's Melos island right there. Where so many warriors go to die. At the Battle, we may have to fight each other. And only one of us will survive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought you came up here to live in the moment?

speaker: Roxana
en: How's this for in the moment?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's make it more than a moment.

speaker: Roxana
en: Must you wear so many layers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Comes with the job, I guess.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess this is goodbye. Until the Battle, I mean.

speaker: Roxana
en: Let's not make this difficult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't help thinking... we don't have to cross swords.

speaker: Roxana
en: You could skip the Battle as easy as I can. But you won't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Goodbye, Roxana.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, Roxana. I don't want to do this.

speaker: Roxana
en: You're right. Getting closer could mean a half second's hesitation before killing you... You're tough, I know that. I can't give up any edge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was good to meet you, Roxana, but it's time to get back to the real world. Good luck in the Battle.

speaker: Roxana
en: You too, champion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've killed more soldiers, mercenaries, and masked men than I can remember. The day of the Battle will be like any other for me.

speaker: Roxana
en: You don't know what I'm capable of. You don't know how different it will be from my average day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know one way it'll differ.

speaker: Roxana
en: How's that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It will be shorter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was good to meet you, Roxana, but it's time to get back to the real world. Good luck in the Battle.

speaker: Roxana
en: You too, champion.

speaker: Kleon
en: You there! Misthios! I have something you may be interested in.

speaker: Kleon
en: Chaire, friend. I saw you talking to my associate, Perikles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: From what I saw, you weren't doing much associating.

speaker: Kleon
en: That's hyst politics. Perikles is a good man—a fine man—just not the right man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not what I heard.

speaker: Kleon
en: From whose lips? His?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard you both speak—you treat people's lives like it's some sort of game.

speaker: Kleon
en: Politics is a game, and one with high stakes. I play for the people, while Perikles plays for power.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We all play for power. It's what we do with it that matters.

speaker: Kleon
en: True, but understand we have a dangerous, weak, leader. The times demand strength

speaker: Kassandra
en: Politics should be about the people. Isn't that the heart of Athenian democracy?

speaker: Kleon
en: I'm not saying Perikles doesn't care for the people... Just that he doesn't lead them with a firm enough hand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He was elected—Athens is the seal of democracy.

speaker: Kleon
en: Oh, it is. It's just that the wrong man is sitting in that seat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you actually need something, or did you just want to educate me on the finer points of democracy?

speaker: Kleon
en: Perikles is holding parties for the rich and powerful while we are under siege. What I want is for my people to reclaim control. You could help me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My services don't come cheap.

speaker: Kleon
en: I understand the wheels of commerce and the needs of the people. I will pay you handsomely for your services.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And how do you want me to help?

speaker: Kleon
en: Help Athens, not me. The Spartans howl outside our city walls. Create chaos among their ranks—make them suffer as we do. Think about it. Will you take my commission and show the Spartans we are not defeated yet?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have no problem killing Spartans.

speaker: Kleon
en: Good. Kill their commander Nabis, destroy their supplies and return to me with proof of your exploits. Show them we have teeth, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get it done.

speaker: Kleon
en: Trust me. This is a huge opportunity for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh, this might interest Kleon, and it'll give him the proof he wants.

speaker: Kleon
en: You've returned. Did you bring the proof I asked for?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think this might interest you. I took it from the commander after I killed him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know what it's about?

speaker: Kleon
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your reaction betrayed you.

speaker: Kleon
en: Yes, the man mentioned in this note was on important business for Athens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why was the messenger trying to get to Mytilene?

speaker: Kleon
en: He was to help distribute supplies to the people there, to help them against their oppressors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is this man to you? You look concerned.

speaker: Kleon
en: He was only an aide—it was his mission that was important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope this proves I can be trusted to get the job done.

speaker: Kleon
en: Proved you're competent, yes. Trusted... You did read the note.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I had to make sure it was proof of what I did—it could have been anything.

speaker: Kleon
en: A good point. And because of this, I have another task for you.

speaker: Kleon
en: I need you to find my messenger, Heremos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was the messenger from the note.

speaker: Kleon
en: Yes, it's imperative Heremos is freed and reaches the ship I've readied for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's the ship I need to take him to?

speaker: Kleon
en: For now it's safer you don't know. Once you find him, he will tell you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about this messenger of yours.

speaker: Kleon
en: He is of no significance, but his mission is. Find him so he can complete it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What mission is your messenger on?

speaker: Kleon
en: The fewer people who know, the better—but understand, it is vital to the future of Athens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where should I look for Heremos?

speaker: Kleon
en: If the Spartans have him, he'll be in the old quarry. I have it on good authority they're holding all their prisoners there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry. I'll get this Heremos of yours to the ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you need from me?

speaker: Kleon
en: Free my messenger Heremos from the Spartan prison at the quarry, and escort him to my ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back as soon as I can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These must be the silos. There's enough grain in here to feed hundreds of hungry soldiers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That hatch on top looks like it'll burn, and the wheat will catch fire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good, now two more left to burn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Only one left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That settles it. Without grain, Lagos won't be able to feed his troops—or pay for more.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I call that impressing "The Lap Dog." I wonder how many scraps Hermippos has received from Kleon's table?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Hermippos has gone too far, Sokrates. Perikles gave everything to Athens, yet we must still hear of Kleon's greatness?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Aristophanes, have you not done similar things to Hermippos?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: How dare you compare me to that man! His plays are a nuisance - something I could come up with in an afternoon, and a drunken one at that. Mine are for a clever audience.

speaker: Sokrates
en: The same audience you judge, should it not be clever enough.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Careful Sokrates, else I make you a character in one of my plays.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Do you agree with Sokrates that Hermippos should say what he wants?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're only words. Hermippos should be able to say what he wants.

speaker: Sokrates
en: No matter what he says? What if he devoted his life to slandering you - not just in Athens, but throughout the land?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Saying what he wants doesn't mean he would escape my spear.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then everything we say has a consequence, even if we are allowed to say it. An intriguing thought, wouldn't you agree?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This may be the first time I've seen Sokrates listen more than he speaks.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Remember it well - you may not see it ever again.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I prefer to think before I speak. And now, having thought, I shall. Tell me - just as I am allowed to say what I wish, should not all be allowed to do the same?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Of course not! And there's much you've said that I'd say you shouldn't have, Sokrates!

speaker: Sokrates
en: What if what I say offends one, but is loved by another? Should I say nothing nothing in fear of what people may think?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: That would be nice, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Most people should keep their words to themselves, including Hermippos.

speaker: Sokrates
en: What if you believe Hermippos should not be given the right to speak, but others do? Who then decides what speech is allowed? It is a dangerous path to tread.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: And one I clearly must. How you can stand up for Hermippos when he attacks Perikles is beyond me.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I stand up for no one, only truth and freedom of speech.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you have such an issue with Hermippos, why not do something about it yourself?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I'd like to, but I haven't been able to find him. Maybe you'd have better luck?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It can't be that hard to find Hermippos.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: That's what I thought as well. Maybe he's afraid I'll find him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Once Hermippos is in front of you, what are you going to say?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I'm not entirely sure yet, but I promise you it will be a grand spectacle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It almost sounds like you're jealous of Hermippos.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Ha! Me, envious of him? Making someone sad is easy, but making someone laugh takes true skill and talent.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wherever Hermippos is, I'll find him.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I hope you do. His residence would be a good place to start.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Doesn't look like Hermippos is here... I should take a look around.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like Kleon made notes for Hermippos on his play... Everyone's a writer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is a lot of money for someone, like Hermippos. Explains his residence, at least.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A mask of the Cult of Kosmos. Hermippos must be a member.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: What is it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I couldn't find Hermippos, but I did find out something about him. He's a member of the Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Then it's no wonder he attached himself so closely to Kleon. Discrediting Perikles and his beliefs in Athens would benefit Hermippos and the Cult, I'd imagine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermippos is definitely a problem.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Do you still believe he should say what he wants, Sokrates?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I know not what I think, nor what I know.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Yes, you deserve a play of your own...

en: These slaves are local—straight from Eretria! They're experienced workers. formerly part of the rebuild happening right now. They could be yours! Don't let their skills go to waste! We start the bidding at 500 drachmae per slave!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: 500 drachmae!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Please, please, these aren't legless goats—these are strong, educated, and quite willing workers.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Sold!

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Do these look like Pephkan slaves to you?! 250 drachmae, minimum.

speaker: Civilian 7
en: But can they read? Write?

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Well, uh, one can!

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Really?

speaker: Civilian 6
en: ...Yes!

speaker: Civilian 7
en: 300 drachmae for the lot

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Sold!

speaker: Civilian 8

speaker: Civilian 9

speaker: Civilian 10

en: Sir, this is a set—you get husband and wife together!

speaker: Civilian 10
