speaker: Agapios
en: No, no, no, this can't—how is this possible?!

speaker: Magistrate
en: Agapios, what's wrong? What have you found?

speaker: Agapios
en: Master, it's a name. Written in the records over and over again. The name of the man leading The Dagger. The Kingfisher.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Once you know the Kingfisher's real name, bring him to a court of law. he and The Dagger have wounded Euboea—Euboea should have a chance to decide his fate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should tear this Kingfisher open with his own blades and hang the corpse as a warning to any who would dare cross Euboea.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Typical misthios thinking. It's not that simple.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Agapios, tell her.

speaker: Agapios
en: When we were young, when we'd play, I was the Robin, and the Kingfisher... was my brother. But he died, he-he... should be dead. I mourned him. I made him a grave! Please tell me he's not one of them. I beg you, tell me my brother's not a Dagger!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know your brother better than these records. If you believe this Kingfisher isn't him, then you're right.

speaker: Agapios
en: Thank you, yes. The boy I knew—there's no way he could be involved in this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brother is likely involved in this, Agapios. If he is the Kingfisher, he's working with The Dagger.

speaker: Agapios
en: No. That's not the boy I knew. He protected me, saved me. He's—whoever this Kingfisher is, it can't be my brother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When your brother died, did you... did you see his body?

speaker: Agapios
en: No, no body at all. No sign, no word, nothing. After mater died, pater was... not as fit to feed us as he once was, so my brother made sure we never went hungry. He would fish, every day. Until he didn't return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brother can't have been born the "Kingfisher."

speaker: Agapios
en: Of course he wasn't! Neritos. His name was Neritos. Older than me—More trouble than me, too. Fighting, stealing—But he always looked out for me.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Nothing is more important to Euboea's survival than stopping The Dagger. I'm sorry, old friend—the Kingfisher must be dealt with, whether he's your brother or not.

speaker: Agapios
en: I—yes, master. I understand.

speaker: Agapios
en: Please misthios, help me uncover the Kingfisher's true identity. We can clear my brother's name and stop The Dagger. Euboea would be in your debt—more in your debt. The Magistrate's treasury runs deep... Your reward would not be small.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever it takes, I'm in. Family can be... complicated. We'll clear your brother's name and save all Euboea while we're at it.

speaker: Agapios
en: I know a farmer who's had dealings with The Dagger's inner circle. If anyone's seen the Kingfisher's true face, it's him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should pay him a visit. Any other leads?

speaker: Agapios
en: There's a shipwreck along Euboea's southern coast, and the theater in Chalkis City has been spreading The Dagger's lies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're in a war, ships are sunk daily. Why does this ship matter?

speaker: Agapios
en: Because this ship appears to belong to The Dagger. A slave I trust waits by a temple above the ruins in Eretria. Speak with her to learn more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said you know a farmer who's had dealings with The Dagger. Maybe I could beat some information out of him...

speaker: Agapios
en: Ha! No, no, he wasn't friends with them—he was targeted by them! He's rich—or he was. Anytime someone in The Dagger needed to line their tunic with drachmae, they'd visit him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then he may know the Kingfisher's true identity.

speaker: Agapios
en: Which would clear my brother's name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A farmer who's had dealings with The Dagger... I've met your farmer! He didn't know anything important.

speaker: Agapios
en: Did you try mentioning my name?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't know you were famous, Agapios.

speaker: Agapios
en: I'm not saying I'm famous, but in certain circles, well... My name will open doors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned... an evil theater?

speaker: Agapios
en: The theater in Chalkis City is a more potent weapon than you realize, misthios. The Dagger use propaganda to poison the minds of Euboeans. See what you can learn there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem well connected. How is that?

speaker: Agapios
en: For a slave, you mean? We're not without eyes and ears, misthios. We see much, and we share it, slave to slave. Leads, warnings, anything that might help us survive all the way from today... to tomorrow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have enough to go on. And the Kingfisher, if I discover he is your brother, if he is the man behind The Dagger...

speaker: Agapios
en: He won't be. Return to me when you've learned all you can.

speaker: Agapios
en: Have you found what we need to prove my brother's innocence and stop The Dagger?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not yet.

speaker: Agapios
en: The Dagger works in the shadows—we mustn't make a move until we've learned everything we can. Is there anything else I can tell you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard enough. I'll return once I've uncovered all I can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the last of Agapios' leads. Better tell him what I've learned. He isn't going to want to hear this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the one who left the message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: My commander is in love with a priestess of Hecate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong with that?

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: She asked him for a letter expressing his eternal devotion written in his blood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And he gave it to her?

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: Love turns people into idiots. I just know she's going to do something evil with that letter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you want me to deal with her.

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: I knew I asked the right person.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can count on me.

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: Thank you. Please be quick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: You. Have you killed her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's no longer your concern.

speaker: Athenian Soldier
en: Well done, my friend. You've earned your keep, that's for sure. Please, accept this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Caretaker
en: Misthios, help! The Cult is after the boy. I have to save him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The boy? Ardos?

speaker: Caretaker
en: Yes. How do you

en: I'm a friend. Hurry up, let's get you out of here.

en: This must be Ardos's House.

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: Where's the boy?! Ardos?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're his caretaker?

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: Of course! I need to speak with him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry about Ardos. He's safe, far from here.

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: Where is he?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was told to expect an old man. You don't look the part.

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: I-it's very important I see him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't you recognize me? Remember all the times we shared? The secrets?

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: Don't take me for a fool!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who told you about the boy? Speak!

en: It's nothing personal with the boy or the old man, but if I tell you anything, I'm good as

en: Dead? Guess what'll happen if you don't tell me anything?

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: OK! What is it you want to know?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is the old man?

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: They're at Phaistos Village, southwest of here. They got him tied to a post and they're beating him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is to happen to the boy?

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: I don't know, misthios! They just told me to bring him back! But we both know what they're capable of...

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you'd bring them an innocent boy?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'd stand by as an old man gets beaten

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: B-but

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you agreed to kidnap the boy.

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: They're just up the road - the Cult! Go kill them all. You'd be doing me a favor, too. Let me go, and I won't tell anyone what happened.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You put innocent people in harm's way. You won't get out of this alive.

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: Stay away!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll let Zeus decide your fate. I need to find the old man.

speaker: "Caretaker"
en: Thank you, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The old man is alive. I should check the temple in Phaistos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The old man is here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's the old man amongst those guards.

speaker: Caretaker
en: I've told you everything I know! W-wait, who are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ardos sent me. Can you walk?

speaker: Caretaker
en: The boy! Thank the gods. Let's get out of here before they return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a friend. Hurry up, let's get you out of here.

en: Breathe, old man

en: Ardos. The boy! Is he safe? Alive?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's made a lot of enemies with his... charm.

speaker: Caretaker
en: At least he's safe from any danger I may have caused him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't let anyone hurt him. Though I do sometimes think about strangling him myself.

speaker: Caretaker
en: Ardos has been known to test even the most resolute of wills.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for a way into the labyrinth. Ardos said you might know something.

speaker: Caretaker
en: I know this—that place is death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What drove everyone out of the labyrinth? Something must have happened.

speaker: Caretaker
en: I never went inside. I'm not a fool. But Nikios wanted me to watch the boy. I stayed outside and prayed, but I heard it—the Minotaur. Two returned, but Nikios...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ardos says his father is in the labyrinth. Is this true?

speaker: Caretaker
en: Yes, he never came out. Though two who did... will never truly escape it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ardos says you refuse to speak or talk to him about his father.

speaker: Caretaker
en: How can anyone tell a boy the person he looks up to—his father and only family—is dead?! What I can do in Nikios's honor is to stop his son from entering that cursed place!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would they hurt you?

speaker: Caretaker
en: When the survivors fled the Minotaur, they left behind a disk—the key to the labyrinth... and I kept it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then why do they think Ardos has it?

speaker: Caretaker
en: Because he does. He stole it from me. And I told them about it. They tortured me, misthios! I—I tried not to break. I've failed him. I've failed him all these years.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people who tortured you belong to a powerful cult. They have broken stronger men than you. You can still make things right with Ardos. As smart as he is, he still needs someone looking out for him—family. He needs you.

speaker: Caretaker
en: He doesn't even want to see me, misthios

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keep trying.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You sold out a small boy and put him in danger! Luckily he's resourceful, smart, and has more backbone than you ever will.

speaker: Caretaker
en: About the disk. He doesn't know its true purpose, misthios. With it, you'll be able to open the labyrinth. Just promise to keep him safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'll be safe with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should ask Ardos if the old man is telling the truth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be a piece of Theseus' armor. Fancy.

speaker: Gaia the Fist
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Amorges wants respect for his soldiers. I'll give them some.

speaker: Persian Soldier
en: Remember, mark the Greeks but don't engage. If a helot get in your way, kill 'em. Kill anyone. We can allow no disrespect.

speaker: Persian Soldier
en: Stay alert. The Greeks won't fight openly, but that doesn't mean they won't send arrows at us from the shadows.

speaker: Persian Soldier
en: Keep formation. You're Persian, not Greek. Tighten it up!

speaker: Philonoe
en: Who are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra. Brasidas sent me.

speaker: Niloxenos
en: Are we going home?

speaker: Philonoe
en: I have no idea.

speaker: Philonoe
en: We've been trapped in this filthy cave for days with no word from Lagos whatsoever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're free, but it's not safe to return to Lagos, yet.

speaker: Niloxenos
en: Are those scary men still with pater?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you heard of the Cult of Kosmos?

speaker: Philonoe
en: Only in whispers... Ever since my husband found new "business partners," they've stationed guards around our home. For our safety, he said. Then one day, those guards dragged us here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're making your pater do things he doesn't want to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find Lagos and release him from these scary men.

speaker: Philonoe
en: And what of us? I can't go back to that wretch, and now that these guards are dead, we're in danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For now, go to my friend, Brasidas. He'll meet you at the safe house northeast of Tegea.

speaker: Philonoe
en: Where Lagos has his secret meetings...

speaker: Niloxenos
en: Are you angry, mater?

speaker: Philonoe
en: I am grateful you saved us. We'll go find Brasidas. Chaire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a note on the board. What's happened?

speaker: Woman
en: It is time to honor Dionysos! Time to drink wine, misthios! But there is much to prepare, and the ghosts will soon rise from the earth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure they will.

speaker: Woman
en: I have to bring pitch to the farmer to paint his door with... it keeps the ghosts out. But game must be hunted, and goats must be slaughtered, as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So... you want me to kill a bunch of goats?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes. All of them must be gutted. Do you accept?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It won't be easy, but I'll take care of it.

speaker: Woman
en: Good. Get it done soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: You earned your pay, mercenary. Take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I've started.

speaker: Praxos
en: Misthios! I have message for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for Kyra.

speaker: Praxos
en: Not here. Gone hunting. Wants you with her, she said.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in. Where is she?

speaker: Praxos
en: Praying to the gods for a good hunt. The Altar of Artemis. East from here, on the north bit of Tavern Point.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks.

speaker: Kyra
en: Keen-eyed Artemis, guide my bow.

speaker: Kyra
en: I pray to you with all my heart that Kassandra doesn't scare off the animals with her heavy footsteps.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought I was being quiet.

speaker: Kyra
en: If that was you being quiet, we'll have nothing but trampled grass to eat for dinner.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nice altar.

speaker: Kyra
en: The flowers remind me of sweeter days.

speaker: Kyra
en: But your real concern should be, how skilled are you with that bow?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need to pray to the gods to hit my targets.

speaker: Kyra
en: They've been known to disguise themselves as animals. I just like to warn them I'm coming.

speaker: Kyra
en: Because I always hit my targets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen you hunt. You don't need my help.

speaker: Kyra
en: Oh, I bet you capture any prey you lock those sharp eyes with.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a challenge.

speaker: Kyra
en: Come. the ibex is swift. We're not going to catch any by standing and chatting.

speaker: Kyra
en: There's a spot down here where I used to hunt as a young girl. It was hunt or starve in those days.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Same for me. I started by catching and cooking rodents.

speaker: Kyra
en: Ha! They make a good soup. But look how far you've come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How far we've come.

speaker: Kyra
en: There. Isn't it beautiful?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It is. Now show me how you use that bow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was a great idea. I'm glad you invited me.

speaker: Kyra
en: I'm glad you accepted.

speaker: Kyra
en: Artemis smiles on you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell Artemis I've got my eye on someone else.

speaker: Kyra
en: Don't make her jealous!

speaker: Kyra
en: Your form is perfect.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With the bow?

speaker: Kyra
en: That too.

speaker: Kyra
en: You're skilled with a bow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Among other things.

speaker: Kyra
en: Excellent shot!

speaker: Kyra
en: My people will be well fed, and the gods will have their sacrifice, thanks to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a great hunter. Why did you actually want me here?

speaker: Kyra
en: Don't be naive. There's something between us, even though I know I shouldn't act on it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Because you love Thaletas.

speaker: Kyra
en: Or at least I thought I did... until you arrived.

speaker: Kyra
en: The hunt clears my mind to reflect on the words that passed between us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is that a good thing?

speaker: Kyra
en: I know a spot down by the water. It's quiet. We'd be alone. What do you say?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm all yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We still have that wine I gave you. Bring it.

speaker: Kyra
en: Delians have suffered for so long. This is the first time I've felt happiness since the war began.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can bring that to your people. These islands deserve peace—so do you.

speaker: Kyra
en: And what about you? When this is all done, we could always use another set of capable hands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My journey isn't over yet, but I may settle down some day.

speaker: Kyra
en: You can do many things, misthios. But settle down? I'm not so sure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another challenge?

speaker: Kyra
en: Stop looking to the future to be happy, when true happiness is right in front of you. You taught me that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, the pirate has one blade at my throat and one at my stomach, and he says, "How do you want to die, misthios, fast or slow?"

speaker: Kyra
en: My gods, what did you do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He was so focused on me, he never noticed my spear in his leg. He was dead before he knew what happened.

speaker: Kyra
en: His leg?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A little trick my mater taught me.

speaker: Kyra
en: No!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, Sokrates turns around, and everyone who was trapped in the conversation had wandered off.

speaker: Kyra
en: Ha! You mean escaped.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Exactly. He's not so bad. You just need to know how to handle him.

speaker: Kyra
en: Is that what this is? You know how to handle me?

speaker: Kyra
en: Relax. I'm joking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ha! Yeah. Good one.

speaker: Kyra
en: No!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I finally get to the beach, and find this giant bear had eaten the crew of smugglers.

speaker: Kyra
en: A bear? By Callisto, what did you do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well... I killed it. What else could I do? It would've torn me to shreds.

speaker: Kyra
en: Ha! I'm starting to think no one is safe from that spear of yours. And what of the woman?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I spared her. She's probably halfway to Lakonia by now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She attacked me... on Delos! The sacred soil's never seen so much action.

speaker: Kyra
en: Why is it so easy to talk with you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Because we've lived similar lives, been through similar struggles... Even though we grew up so far apart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wine always helps loosen the tongue.

speaker: Kyra
en: It does.

speaker: Kyra
en: I want you, Kassandra. Here. Now. Under the stars.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've wanted you since I laid eyes on you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mykonos is definitely my favorite island.

speaker: Kyra
en: And you're my favorite misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas should know about this.

speaker: Kyra
en: He will. In time. For now he needs to focus on the rebellion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So do we.

speaker: Kyra
en: But first...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas can't know about this.

speaker: Kyra
en: I agree. In time, he will. For now he needs to focus on the rebellion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So do we.

speaker: Kyra
en: But first...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyra, I'm flattered.

speaker: Kyra
en: But you don't want me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're beautiful, and brave, and strong. The people of Delos are lucky to have you fighting for them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But us laying together wouldn't be right.

speaker: Kyra
en: To new friendships, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: To friendship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know where this is going... Kyra, I came here to do a job, and that's it.

speaker: Kyra
en: Oh. No, of course. I'm a rebel leader. You're a mercenary. I... get it. I do. I should gather the spoils of the hunt and get back to my people.

speaker: Kyra
en: Take some with you. It's as much yours as it is mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks. But I'm not hungry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks. But your people need it more than I do.

speaker: Kyra
en: And I always will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You... But you just said...

speaker: Kyra
en: You've been of great help to me, Kassandra, and for that I'm thankful. There is something between us, but it died when you gave me pater's doll in front of my people.

speaker: Kyra
en: I should gather the spoils of the hunt and get back to my people.

speaker: Kyra
en: Take some with you. It's as much yours as it is mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks. But I'm not hungry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks. But your people need it more than I do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a note on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: I've made sacrifices to Artemis, goddess of the hunt, but ever since the leader died, the whole area seems cursed. I need to purify it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How are you planning to do it?

speaker: Woman
en: Artemis loves the hunt like I do - there are many goats and predators in this area. I think blood from the hunted will please her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to spill the beasts' blood.

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, all of them must be gutted. Do you accept?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you.

speaker: Woman
en: Good. Get it done soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: You've done me a great service, mercenary. Take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All in a day's work.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks so peaceful from up here. It always does, but it never is.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: I know, Ikaros. I'm tired too. I've met so many people... archons, kings, and now Isu. They're all the same. "Go do this. Bring me that. Go kill him." I don't know if I can do this anymore. If I were ruler, things would be much, much different.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: What's that Ikaros? A speech from your new ruler?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: You, bring the food. You, bring the wine. For tonight, we feast until our bellies are as round as the moon.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: That sounded good.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: I don't have wine, but if I brought you some bread, would you help me?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlanteans! Tonight we tear off these clothes and make love until the sun comes up. I wonder what Alkibiades is doing these days. Or who...

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Who is Alkee beeadees?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: You, bring me the biggest bed in Atlantis. You, all the pillows you can find. Tonight, we sleep! For we are very, very tired.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: We're almost done, Kassandra.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: I'm too small to carry a bed. But if I brought you a pillow, could you help me?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: You shouldn't sneak up on people like that.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: I'm sorry. I didn't want to interrupt the Dikastes speech.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: it was more of a fantasy really. Call me Kassandra.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: I thought it was wonderful, Dikastes Kassandra.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Just Kassandra is fine. And what's your name?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Alkon. You're even more special than all the bedtime stories my parents used to tell me.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: My parents are missing. They left for their assignments but never came home. The Isu won't help me.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: But then I remembered the story of you helping a lost girl in the underworld who found her parents in Elysium. So I came to you.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Her name was Phoibe. We were good friends. She's in a better place now than when I found her.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: She was lucky to have a friend like you.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: I could always make a new friend. Maybe you, Alkon, and I could help you. Would you like that?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: More than anything.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of people won't help a child find his missing parents?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Some of them are nice. But some of them hate us. Call us rats. I'm not a rat, am I Dikastes Kassandra?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course not Alkon. You're more of a mouse, really.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Hey!

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: A child without his parents? Not on my watch. As Dikastes of Atlantis, I declare this unacceptable!

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Oh thank you, Dikastes Kassandra.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: You said your parents never came home. If you could tell me where they're assigned, and what their names are, it would be very helpful.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Mater's name is Rhene. She's assigned to the harbor. Pater is called Damades, and he's assigned to the adamant quarry.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: You're very brave. Now go home where it's safe. I'll go talk to the harbormaster, and whoever is in charge of the quarry. I'll come find you once I have some answers.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Alkon's probably wondering where I am. I'll go see him.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Dikastes Kassandra! Did you find mater and pater?

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Not yet. But I know they were taken to some sort of experimentation chamber by an Isu named Xarios.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: Xarios? But he was always so kind to us. He gave us food and defended us when the others called us rats.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know where I could find him? The doors to the chamber are locked and he's my last hope of getting in.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Alkon
en: He's usually at the Fortified Doma of Mneseas. But he's always protected by guards.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: That never stops me.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: Xarios. You've abducted your last human.

scene: Good From Far, Far From Good
speaker: Kassandra
en: This key looks like the one Atlas gave me. Maybe it can help me get into the experimentation chamber.

speaker: Hekate
en: Good, you're just in time. A woman in Stroma needs your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Unless this brings me closer to taking down Persephone, I'm not interested.

speaker: Hekate
en: Haven't I made it clear we share that goal? Helping the woman will breach Persephone's power.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm surprised you're interested in helping humans. They don't seem interested in you.

speaker: Hekate
en: Humans are simple creatures who fear what they can't understand. But I'm not doing this out of the goodness of my heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does she need?

speaker: Hekate
en: Helping her will bring us closer to breaking Persephone's grasp on Elysium.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's special about her?

speaker: Hekate
en: She's an orator who'd be willing to join Adonis' rebellion. That man has beautiful lips, but a silver tongue like hers is necessary to inspire the public.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then it sounds like we need her. I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There she is!

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Elysium is a paradise crafted by her majesty, Persephone herself. No human should seek to leave it, for in Elysium, we want for nothing.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Who are you? Who sent you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hekate mentioned you could use some help.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Quiet! If the other humans think I associate with Hekate, my career is over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm an ally to Adonis.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Don't speak of the rebellion so loudly. Persephone has ears everywhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just tell me what you need me to do.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Free the villagers being held captive in Persephone's Broken Daydream. My son, Theron, is working there as a guard against his will. It's like Persephone possessed his mind. Can you help him too?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Better let the silver tongue know I couldn't save Theron.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: You're back. Where's my Theron?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I freed him of Persephone's influence. He's joined Adonis' rebellion.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Wonderful news! I didn't know there was a cure. What of the other villagers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wasn't able to save him.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Theron! My dear boy... The others. Tell me you have better news of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They've made their way safely to Iapetos' Ruins already. You'll find them there.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: As promised, I'll join the rebels. What message would you like me to spread once I'm there?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell the truth about Persephone. Make sure the humans know her reign must end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: End the fear mongering against Hekate. Make sure the other humans know she is their ally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let the humans know that Adonis will lead them to freedom. Only he has their interests at heart, not Persephone.

speaker: Silver Tongue
en: Your words shall be spoken. Thank you for your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Silver Tongue is on her way to help the rebellion. She'll bring in plenty of recruits. Adonis will be pleased.

speaker: Hekate
en: Relieving Persephone of her power is what's important. Don't concern yourself with that man's feelings. Or your feelings for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis is a friend. Nothing more.

speaker: Hekate
en: Make sure it stays that way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's it to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you seen him?

speaker: Hekates
en: If you are truly so weak that you can't control the feelings you have when you look at Adonis, stop looking at him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you care?

speaker: Hekate
en: Divine love affairs never end well for the humans involved. Stay out of them. And stay focused on the task at hand.

speaker: Hekate
en: Now, a young woman is suffering from a terrible affliction. She's agreed to help the rebellion if we provide a cure. However, Persephone long ago outlawed the water that can relieve this woman and destroyed the last of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me guess... Or so she thought.

speaker: Hekate
en: There are rumors that someone hid a vial of it in a cave off of Hypnos' Path. Retrieve it and bring it to her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would Persephone outlaw this water?

speaker: Hekate
en: Her need for control has grown beyond understanding. What matters is that the humans of Elysium get the help they desire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is this woman's sickness?

speaker: Hekate
en: The worst affliction that can befall a human in Elysium. A broken heart for eternity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's lovesick?

speaker: Hekate
en: You know nothing of grief after death. It haunts humans with an intensity unparalleled on earth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I've delivered the water.

speaker: Hekate
en: Remember, it's forbidden. You can't be seen when you bring it to the villa in Adonis' Gardens.

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios! I have a job for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on?

speaker: Civilian
en: This job will be dangerous and could get us both killed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All my jobs are dangerous.

speaker: Civilian
en: This job is about power—the power to rule Gortyn by starting a war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wars cost both drachmae and lives.

speaker: Civilian
en: I know the price. A war will be devastating, but in the end it's what's best for Gortyn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you have in mind?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can't start a war on our own - we'll need supporters and soldiers.

speaker: Civilian
en: I have support from the captain of the army and the region's upper class.

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK, then tell me your plan.

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm the head of the boule council, and according to our code, after a war is lost, the council chooses our next leader... Me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you need some heads to roll to get things started?

speaker: Civilian
en: Just one head... There's a visiting herald from Phaistos. No doubt here to broker peace with Gortyn. His murder will guarantee that war is the only option for Gortyn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And my fee?

speaker: Civilian
en: You'll be paid very handsomely for your efforts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll start the war for you. But first, I need more information.

speaker: Civilian
en: Before the war can truly begin, we'll need your help weakening Gortyn. Destroy their supplies, steal their valuables... and kill that malákas visiting herald.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find the visiting herald?

speaker: Civilian;
en: This "man of peace" stays at the Leader House at night, and wanders around Gortyn during the day. Kill him, and Gortyn will be blamed for his murder.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about the supplies I should destroy.

speaker: Civilian
en: The weapon racks and supplies in Daidalos Fort must be destroyed to ensure they don't win the war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's plenty of valuables to be found in Daidalos Fort.

speaker: Civilian
en: Stealing from there will hurt the Gortyn war effort most.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll start this war for you. I hope you know what you're doing.

speaker: Civilian
en: We've been planning this for a while. See me when everything is complete.

speaker: Towards a Unified Messara
en: Your aid in helping us defeat Phaistos is greatly appreciated. As promised, I will personally see to it that you are made part of my boule council. I am aware of your concern with Ptolemaios. I will get rid of him if he proves to be an obstacle. Speak of this to no one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's done. Gortyn is weak and ready for new leadership.

speaker: Civilian
en: Praise the gods! Here's a reward for your troubles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After war, the boule council chooses a new leader.

speaker: For the Blue Banner
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

en: You left a note on the board. What's happened?

en: I know you killed the Monger, you home-wrecking malákas.

en: You're right. I killed that pig so everyone could see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't understand why you're so upset. The Monger was running Korinthia into the ground.

speaker: Hetaera
en: Who cares about Korinthia?! I care about my own fucking life that you've ruined. He was going to marry me. Me! How many chances do you think a hetaera gets in a lifetime?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... don't know what you're talking about.

speaker: Hetaera
en: If it wasn't you who killed my husband-to-be, you're going to find the fucker who did. I want you to go out there and kill the mercenary that slit his throat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you need me to send him to Hades?

speaker: Hetaera
en: That's exactly it. The mercenary must die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Hetaera
en: Good. You're doing me a great service.

en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Hetaera
en: You again. Have you killed him?

en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Hetaera
en: You've set great things in motion. Take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All in a day's work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're bleeding. A lot.

speaker: Iola
en: Come to turn me in to the priests?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Depends what you've done.

speaker: Iola
en: Don't know if anyone told you, but it's illegal to die on this gods-forsaken island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I've been told.

speaker: Iola
en: Shame nobody told the beast roaming around. Drachmae to the one who kills it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're paying, I'll hunt and kill this beast for you.

speaker: Iola
en: You're not the first hunter to tell me that... But I still have all my drachmae.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've hunted many beasts. What am I hunting this time?

speaker: Iola
en: I'd call it a bear, but I'd be lying. This creature is Artemis's nightmare.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's the beast now?

speaker: Iola
en: Got as far way from that thing as I could. You'll find it north of here, near the coast. Just follow the trail of bodies—the bloodier the mess, the closer you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not from around here, are you?

speaker: Iola
en: Came through Arkadia, but Korinthia is my home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the beast and kill it. Try not to bleed out before I return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were a mighty beast. But you did not belong here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A corpse. This one's had his guts ripped out—a feast for the birds.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A bloody handprint. Hasn't been here long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A shipwreck. Might explain how that bear got to Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This record says the bear came from Arkadia. That woman was smuggling the beast... But why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This record says the bear came from Arkadia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's nothing left to find here. I should return to the woman.

speaker: Iola
en: You're alive. And the monster?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The bear's dead, and you owe me payment. But first, let's talk about you. Arkadia, right?

speaker: Iola
en: Yes...

speaker: Kassandra
en: The bear was being smuggled from Arkadia. I found a record of what was on your ship, and your bloody handprints. Talk.

speaker: Iola
en: All right, all right! We were smuggling the bear for a man named Sargon. Poseidon had other ideas—one of his storms crashed us here, and that evil beast broke free. It went right for the crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That explains the bodies.

speaker: Iola
en: They were my family!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where you're from. Now.

speaker: Iola
en: I came from Arkadia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a smuggler. You only wanted the beast dead because you knew if it started killing Delians, they'd have your head.

speaker: Iola
en: What would you have me do? I couldn't kill the thing. I tried! The Delians are crazy—do you know what they do to foreigners who bring death to their island?

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you let a bloodthirsty bear roam free?

speaker: Iola
en: We were smuggling cargo from Arkadia to Kos for a man named Sargon. Ran aground during a storm and the bear broke loose and killed the crew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know. I saw the bodies.

speaker: Iola
en: Those bodies were my friends! Please, I'll pay you. You can't tell the Delians this was my fault.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've suffered enough. What the Delians don't know won't kill them.

speaker: Iola
en: A misthios with a heart. You're as rare as that monster. Here, take what drachmae I have left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. And don't let the Delians catch you bleeding everywhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know, the Delians would pay a good price for the person who brought this curse to their sacred land.

speaker: Iola
en: You wouldn't!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would. Pay me, and maybe your secret dies with that bear.

speaker: Iola
en: Despicable misthios! My family is dead, and you want more drachmae?!

speaker: Iola
en: I might be injured, but I can still kill you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What matters is my pay.

speaker: Iola
en: Here, you've earned it. Now let me bleed in peace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The bear is dead. I've never seen one like it.

speaker: Iola
en: You killed it? So this is over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found some bloody handprints and a shipping record near a broken crate.

speaker: Iola
en: The bear is dead, and that's all that matters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You wouldn't be talking about the giant bear down by the beach, would you?

speaker: Iola
en: You saw the beast, and you still live?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That bear wasn't from this world. The vicious pet of some angry god. I sent him back to his owner.

speaker: Iola
en: I don't know who you are, warrior, but take this. You've earned it. Now go, let me bleed in peace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ros? ...Good dog. Good dog.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bad dog.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods. Ros? What happened to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cerberos is no god.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh good. Now it's angry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ros? Is he... dead?

speaker: Unknown
en: ...Protect the unseen that others wish they saw...

speaker: Hades
en: You reek of mortal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hades.

speaker: Hades
en: The last mortal to dance with Cerberos and live was Herakles. But then, he had Athena and Hermes wrapped around his mighty finger. So tell me, who's wrapped around your finger? Which god helped you slay my beast?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There were no gods in that pit. Just me an my spear.

speaker: Hades
en: So you did have help from the gods.

speaker: Hades
en: I know who you are. What you've done. And I'd say you owe me, "Keeper."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your wife's the one who pushed me into a pit with your "beast."

speaker: Hades
en: My sweet Persephone pushed you to your death. And you've done us all a great disservice by not dying.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am Kassandra of Sparta, Bearer of the Eagle of Zeus, Keeper of the Staff of Hermes, Wielder of the Spear of

speaker: Hades
en: So you have friends in high places, I see. No matter. You're in my realm now. And I'd say you owe me, "Keeper."

speaker: Kassandra
en: It wasn't my plan to be thrown down that hole. But here I am. What do you want from me?

speaker: Hades
en: Thanks to you, my realm is more chaotic than ever. With Cerberos gone, there's nothing to stop the dead from crossing over to the world of the living.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So find another dog.

speaker: Hades
en: You find another dog!

speaker: Hades
en: I'm sorry you had to see that. The blood runs hot in my family. You did this, so I think it's only fair that you fix it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. Tell me where you keep the multi-headed monsters around here, and I'll be right back.

speaker: Hades
en: No no no, my dear Keeper. My realm, my rules. I have four gates. Instead of one guardian for them all, I want you to find me four guardians—one for each of them. The underworld is filled with kings, heroes, legends. All lost, all trying to find purpose. You could give them that purpose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cerberos was a fierce guardian. What human could replace him?

speaker: Hades
en: No human could. A legend, though, immortal in the minds of the living, would strike terror in any who dare to cross over. Find me four of those.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And if I don't find these guardians, then what?

speaker: Hades
en: Boundaries between the world of the living and realm of the dead will melt. The vile creatures locked away in Tartaros will roam free. Mortal souls will wander lost for eternity, and I will be very, very angry with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Teach me how to use this staff, and it's a deal.

speaker: Hades
en: Ah yes, the trials of the Keeper. I've already heard how you'll stop at nothing to figure out that boring little stick of yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This "boring little stick"

speaker: Hades
en: Tell you what, go talk to my ferryman, Charon. Help him put things back in order, and I'll help you fulfill your destiny.

speaker: Hades
en: Ugh! See what you've done? These are everywhere now. Fix. It.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, I'll fix it.

speaker: Hades
en: My brother and I have a little wager on whether or not you'll succeed in your quest. Don't let me down. You don't want to owe me twice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What were those things? Why did I feel so weak?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Hey you, misthios! Would you like to learn about your future?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. I would like to know what the Fates have planned for me.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: You would! Yes, of course you would. Everyone wants their future told by the Great Ouzo!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, what is it?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: I see great things...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Like what?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: You know things, and... it's going to be sunny tomorrow.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Thank you, thank you. Tell your friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Oracle at Delphi ruined my life. You think I want to hear your lies, too?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: No worries! How about I clean your sandals?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not today.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My sandals are fine.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Then what about your...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need anything. Go!

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Well, no accounting for taste, but suit yourself!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it with the Olympics? Everyone's out to make drachmae...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka, my drachmae! Hey, stop, thief!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like Phoibe... And as nimble a thief!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have to find her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hey, come back here! Thief!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A street thief. Just like Phoibe...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You led me on a good chase, but I caught you. Hand it over.

speaker: Maia
en: Hand what over?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My drachmae. Give it back.

speaker: Maia
en: Here, please don't hurt me. They made me do it, I didn't want to, honest...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hush. I'm not going to hurt you, I promise.

speaker: Maia
en: But the Captain will!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Captain?

speaker: Maia
en: Yeah, it's him that makes us do this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Us?

speaker: Maia
en: The other street kids!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why is he making you steal?

speaker: Maia
en: For the drachmae, stupid!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should be more polite to adults.

speaker: Maia
en: Why? What've adults done for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fair enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like this Captain needs a good talking to.

speaker: Maia
en: Don't talk, just hit. He even stole my mater's necklace from me... Says I'll get it back if I steal for him. It's all that I had left of her...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you get your necklace.

speaker: Maia
en: Why would you care?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You remind me of someone... Someone very special.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't rely on me or others for help. You need to learn to solve your own problems.

speaker: Maia
en: Thanks for nothing, maláka!

speaker: Maia
en: What do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you need me to do?

speaker: Maia
en: Get my necklace and save my friends from the Captain... But you'll probably just disappoint me again.

speaker: Maia
en: Did you get my necklace from the Captain? Where are my friends? Did you help them? Was there a fight? Why are you standing there? Did you do anything?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keeping children in cages? Whoever did this will pay.

speaker: Athenian Heavy Soldier
en: Why do I feed those little shits? Let 'em steal their own food.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's that maláka I saw in the market. He must be in on this scheme.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Well, Captain, if you don't feed them, they'll be too weak to run away with the loot. If they get caught, you'll have to train new ones.

speaker: Athenian Heavy Soldier
en: You want me to give them your food? Maybe I should beat you more, set an example for the brats.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Please, no. I was just trying to help. It's in your interest to keep them healthy and...

speaker: Athenian Heavy Soldier
en: I don't need street scum like you telling me what's in my interest.

speaker: Athenian Heavy Soldier
en: You think this is a game? You're supposed to bring me drachmae, not excuses!

speaker: Athenian Heavy Soldier
en: You! Get the fuck out of my camp before I beat you like the dog that you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be Maia's necklace... Maláka kept it on him.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Please, I only wanted to help the children. Spare me, and I'll do better. I'll look after them all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should return to Maia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got something for you.

speaker: Maia
en: Thank you, thank you, thank you! What happened to Alopex?

speaker: Maia
en: You know, the guy who distracted you while I nabbed your purse!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I had to kill him. He was a partner in this. He could have enslaved you all again.

speaker: Maia
en: Oh...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have to move on now, but I'm glad I could help.

speaker: Maia
en: What? I...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all right. You don't have to thank me. Take care, Maia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I spared him. He's promised to help you and the others.

speaker: Maia
en: Good, I always liked him. He used to share his food with us and stand up for us when the Athenian got mad!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll do fine. Take care.

speaker: Maia
en: Thanks for saving us from the Athenian. Now we get to keep everything we steal!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm coming for you, Podarkes.

speaker: Podarkes
en: Guards! Kill her!

speaker: Podarkes
en: You will die for standing against us, child!

speaker: Podarkes
en: You've been a thorn in my side since you landed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Soon I'm going to be a blade in your throat.

speaker: Podarkes
en: Even if you kill me, you will lose, Eagle Bearer. We are everywhere. There isn't a rock you can hide under where we won't find you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are the snakes who hide! I'm going to bury you so deep only Hades will find you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was for my family, maláka.

speaker: Podarkes
en: What I did, I did for the glory of Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You acted alone, and you will die alone.

speaker: Podarkes
en: Tell my daughter... She should have killed me herself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's not your daughter anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nice view.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It just got a lot nicer. I was hoping to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alkibiades. What are you doing outside of Athens?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Someone like me is always on the move. I've docked my ship in every "port"!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure you have.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: If you're here for more than the view, I have a task for you. It is crucial this package gets to its proper recipient. It's not from me, but a man named Diodoros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll have to find another delivery girl.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Did you regret turning down my package?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help, but it's only that little box?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: One should never judge something by its size, you know. A small thing may very well make a huge impact.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. Who am I giving the package to?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: There's a man named Bardas near the Korinthian military fort. He's one of their stronger... assets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And I just tell him it's from you?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: No, from Diodoros. Don't forget. Diodoros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said this package isn't from you. Why do you have it, then?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It simply came into my hands, that's all. Diodoros asked for my help, like I'm asking for yours now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why can't this Diodoros deliver it himself?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: You're a curious one, aren't you? Some questions don't have answers. Sometimes things just... are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've traveled a lot—where's your favorite place to go?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Oh, a personal question... interesting. The world is filled with beautiful places. To pick my favorite would be like picking my favorite hetaera. I could do it, but the answer changes based on my mood.

speaker: Bardas
en: You aren't the misthios I sent for. What do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is for you.

speaker: Bardas
en: Give it here.

speaker: Bardas
en: Is this some kind of joke? This is a cast of someone's dick! What's this engraving? "This is for your wife Thelia, for when she starts to miss me."

speaker: Bardas
en: Tell me now! Who sent this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know a man named Diodoros?

speaker: Bardas
en: Diodoros? He'll pay for this with his life! I'll destroy his men. I'll destroy his ship. He'll regret ever touching Thelia!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A man named Alkibiades gave it to me.

speaker: Bardas
en: Alkibiades? Just because Perikles took him in and he's friends with important people, he thinks he can do whatever he wants. I won't let him get away with this!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's from me, Bardas, can't you tell?

speaker: Bardas
en: Do you think this is a joke? You'll pay for that!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone doesn't have a sense of humor.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I was just starting to miss you. I hope you delivered the package.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bardas threatened to kill Diodoros when I told him. I also wasn't expecting the package to be... well... that.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It was a nice surprise, wasn't it? I can make another one for you, too, if you'd like.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another one? You

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It was mine, yes. It looked good, didn't it? I needed to get Diodoros out of the way, and now he will be. I impress myself sometimes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever you say.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Why don't we let our bodies do the talking? Surely you had thoughts of it as well when you saw the cast of me...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here? Before the gods?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Let's make an offering.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like to see the gods stop us.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I have a feeling they'd prefer to watch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd say we gave the gods a good show.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I couldn't agree more. I'd love an encore soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not interested.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: A shame... Aphrodite would have loved it. Maybe another time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told Bardas that... it came from you.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: You did what? I specifically told you to say it was from Diodoros. Now I have to come up with another plan. It took me a long time to make that final cast.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait, so it was yours?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Yes, that impressive specimen was mine. I really wish you hadn't told him that. You can go now. I need to think.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought I'd make a joke and tell him it was mine, but he didn't laugh.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Why would you do that? Bardas is an angry, emotional man. I hoped to get rid of Diodoros, but now you've ruined that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you wanted to get rid of Diodoros, then that package wasn't from him after all.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Of course not. It was a perfect plan, but now I have to come up with something else. Don't think I'll ever make a cast for you now.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: The sun and moon combined could not grant the beauty that my bride-to-be was gifted! If the gods blessed me, they did so with one eye closed. But their eyes were wide open for her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Please stop. Your poetry is sweet enough to make someone vomit.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I won't stop until the whole world knows how I feel.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm hurt. You never talk about me like that.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: My sweet misthios, such words can not be handed out at will. It's as though Apollo himself is speaking through me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm impressed. If I only heard the words, I'd swear you were a poet.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: My words are nowhere near what she deserves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So... You're in love.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Yes, the wedding nears, and there is so much to be done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you need help, I'm here for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not going to let you put your wedding duties on me.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Think you've got it in you to help?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Accepting before knowing what I ask of you? That's a rare surprise. I do still need a few things: food for an offering, a ring, and some flowers. If you could bring them to my bride, Iris, she'll make use of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've known you for a while now, but you've never mentioned Iris.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: There's plenty I haven't mentioned. I'm sure you could say the same to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what is it about Iris that turns you into... well, what I saw.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: You're not jealous, are you? Don't worry—she's very open. I suppose that's one of my favorite things about her. The... openness.

speaker: Kassandra
