speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like I was too late for Heremos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh, seems Kleon's messenger wasn't the only one captured. Maybe I can help them, too.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Please, Eros! Let it be me. Let him pick me!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: I got here first, back off! The scion will pick me!

speaker: Aetios
en: I'll see you all at the selection ceremony, ladies! I especially hope

speaker: Aetios
en: You show up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me guess, he's rich.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: That's Aetios! The scion of the most influential family in Keos. And his wife-choosing ceremony is tomorrow! We need Eros' blessings to be picked.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You hope to marry into riches.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: No! My feelings are for Aetios, not his wealth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even if your feelings for him are real. They get stronger with drachmae.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: No! I really am in love with him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your eyes tell of your true feelings.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: I-I feel like you're making fun of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You better start praying like the rest of them.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: No, I have to stand out! If I do what everyone else is doing, I'll never be picked by Eros or Aetios. I need to do something, anything!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Anything?

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Yes, anything!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Eros? Please, his ears are stuffed full with the prattling of these women. Let me help, I'm a witch of Hekate, goddess of witchcraft and magic. I know just the thing. A love potion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ridiculous. Love potions are a myth

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen stranger things work.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: I'll buy it from you, please! Sell it to me, and don't let the others hear you.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: I don't need your drachmae, I spread the word of Hekate freely. But—A love potion is tailored to the imbiber. I have to make one. Just. For. You. And once you've drained every last drop of it down your pretty throat, you will exude pure, irresistible beauty. Aetios will fall in love with you instantly!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: First, we need two things. A cask of the finest wine, and some wild mushrooms.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Where can I find that at such short notice?

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: I'm sure the misthios could procure these items for you.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Please, misthios! Please, you've got to help me. In the name of love. And a lot of drachmae! Well, I'll give you all I've got. If Aetios picks me, I'll be sure to give you even more!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. I'll get the ingredients for your love potion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "The finest wine" isn't much to go on. How will I get it?

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: A shipment of expensive wine was lost in a shipwreck recently. Look around the wreckage in Pirate Bay, and you'll find a cask or two, if it hasn't already been pillaged by pirates. It's beached on the west coast of the island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where will I find wild mushrooms?

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: No, no! A new shipment of very special mushrooms has arrived at the Customs Warehouse. Fetch me some of those.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all. I'll see to the items.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Excellent. Meet us at the temple on the hilltop when you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the shipwreck with the wine. Hope the pirates haven't gotten here yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the warehouse. The wild mushrooms will be in there somewhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Customs Warehouse. Better get looking for those mushrooms.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: Have you heard of that pirate woman, Xenia?

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Malaka. She's bad news.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: I know, that's why I'm bringing it up! What if she, I don't know, has plans for these mushrooms that just came in?

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: What does a pirate need with mushrooms?!

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: I heard they can be made into weapons! Or a poison, I can't remember.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Just shut up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These should do fine. Though... they don't look safe to eat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wine and wild mushrooms. That's all of it. I should go to the girl and the witch at the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the shipwreck she was talking about.

speaker: Soldier
en: This is strong stuff.

speaker: Brute
en: Save that wine for Xenia!

speaker: Soldier
en: I'm just pinching a little bit, she'll never know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is all the wine left. The looters stripped the shipwreck clean.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wine and wild mushrooms. That's all of it. I should go to the girl and the witch at the temple.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Look who has returned.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Misthios! We're over here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's everything you asked for.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Thank you, misthios!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Now, I just need a more... personal artifact, the last ingredient.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come this far, I'll see it through. What else do you need, witch?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not fetching anything else for you.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: No, no. What I need, the girl can provide.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: I'll give you whatever you need to be with Aetios.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: We'll just need a little snip of your beautiful locks. Your part in this is done, misthios. Come to the selection ceremony at Aetios' house to witness the fruits of your labor. It's the one overlooking the sea.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: You've gotta come! Once Aetios picks me, I'll make sure to pay you your due!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope he has deep pockets. His love didn't come cheap.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Come. There's much left to do. See you at the ceremon, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Misthios! Kill this snake! She did this to me! She made me bald!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: I'm sorry, my love. Give me a moment, some peasants need my attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said "a little bit" of her hair. Explain this.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Explain? It's clear. Beautiful, gullible, idiot girl falls prey to

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Her competition.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: She set me up! Aetios picked her instead. H-he didn't even take a second look at me...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would you do such a thing?

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Aetios can be no one's but mine. I'm the one who truly loves him. I grew up with him. I've always been the one looking out for him! You think I'd let some starry-eyed fledgling after his wealth steal the love of my life from me?

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Aetios... doesn't know what's good for him. He's been eyeing this one for a while now. He liked the way she looked. So, I changed that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to the potion?

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Why, she drank it! And look! It worked wonderfully.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: She added a lock of my hair to the potion and then made me drink it. I didn't feel anything strange at the time, but when I did... All my hair... it just began to fall off.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What trickery is this?! You used her hair in a spell

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: A spell? Are you idiots? If only something so convenient existed. It's simple alchemy. With a little knowledge of poisonous local flora, anything is possible. And wild mushrooms are known to cause violent reactions, but honestly—I've never seen anyone go bald! Just a horrible rash, at best. This went better than I expected!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was promised drachmae. Just give it to me. I didn't up for any of this drama.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Technically the girl asked you for the items, not me.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: She's making fools of us both! Kill her, misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're crazy, you'll pay for this.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: She played the game and she lost. There's nothing to pay for. You believe she's innocent in all this? She tried to get ahead with magic. So, spare me the hypocrisy. Just leave and take your bald friend with you.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Please, misthios... do something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll cut through every last one of your guards to get to you.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Guards! Stop this misthios!

speaker: Aetios
en: What have you done to my wife?! You'll pay for this, misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Guards! There's a witch in our midst!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Kallikleia
en: The misthios speaks the truth! Look what she did to me. She poisoned me and made me hideous. Someone please help!

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: Ugh! You watch your back, misthios. I'll have your head.

speaker: Aetios
en: W-what? I've known her all my life. She's a witch? That explains a lot...

speaker: Kallikleia
en: Thank you, misthios... for everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You... make a fair point.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: What?! How could you say that! She's a liar! And a cheat!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The witch is crazy but she did what you tried to do. Anything and everything to be with the one she loves. I can't fault her.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: How could you say that after what she did to me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Know when you are beat. Go home. Well, pay me. Then go home.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: See? The misthios gets it. Come, my Aetios, my dear. Let us leave these peasants to their theatrics. We have a wedding to plan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The witch is crazy but she did what you tried to do. Anything and everything to be with the one she loves. I can't fault her.

speaker: Kallikleia
en: How could you say that after what she did to me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Know when you are beat. Go home. Well, pay me. Then go home.

speaker: Hekate Witch
en: See? The misthios gets it. Come, my Aetios, my dear. Let us leave these peasants to their theatrics. We have a wedding to plan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These must be the ruins Thaletas mentioned. The beach is east of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like the beach, but he's not here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A trail of flowers? He wouldn't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas should be nearby.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I was beginning to think you wouldn't come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Doubting yourself, Spartan?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Ha! I was doubting your tracking skills.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm surprised you left flowers. Was nice following something other than blood for a change.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, those flowers. I'll be honest, you didn't strike me as the type.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I... I'm not very good with these kinds of things. There's flowers all over Delos. I saw them, and thought...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thought what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tracking skills? You didn't notice my eagle?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Does he watch your every move?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can send Ikaros away. Unless of course, you like being watched.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Much has happened since we first met on the beach.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were surrounded by Athenians. Drenched in blood.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You fought by my side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were irresistible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I couldn't let you have all the fun.

speaker: Thaletas
en: When I first laid eyes on Kyra, I knew I never wanted to leave these islands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And now?

speaker: Thaletas
en: I don't know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas, look at me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what I want.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Not here. Come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are you taking me?

speaker: Thaletas
en: To one of my favorite spots on all the Delos Islands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Isn't a Spartan's favorite spot the battlefield?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Fair enough. I'm taking you to my second favorite spot.

speaker: Thaletas
en: When I got here, I had just lost so many people. Every man I ever looked up to sank on that ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You needed a place to get away from all this death. I understand.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I knew you would. That's why I'm showing it to you. This place isn't just where I go to clear my thoughts. It...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It what?

speaker: Thaletas
en: It reminds me of home.

speaker: Thaletas
en: This is where I come to train. I found it after arriving on Delos. Exhausting my body clears my mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a beautiful spot, Thaletas. I'm honored you'd share it with me.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I'm glad you like it. Because this is where I'm going to see what you're really made of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place is beautiful, Thaletas. As are you.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You've won my heart, Kassandra. But to claim it, I need to see what you're really made of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Fight me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh?

speaker: Thaletas
en: You claimed to be Spartan when we first met. I want to see if you fight like one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've seen me fight.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Against Athenians, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well?

speaker: Thaletas
en: When we first met, you denied being Spartan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And?

speaker: Thaletas
en: The only way to truly know someone is through combat—hand to hand, flesh to flesh, bone to bone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. Just don't get angry when I break that pretty face of yours.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Come on, Kassandra. Don't hold back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're more than just a pretty face.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Stop hitting like a child, and really hit me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So when does the real fighting begin?

speaker: Thaletas
en: No doubt in my mind. You trained in Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've got you now.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You'll pay for that.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You don't fight like a Spartan. You fight like a god.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not so bad yourself.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Are you going to just stand there, or are you going to finish me off?

speaker: Thaletas
en: You amaze me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How so?

speaker: Thaletas
en: For the first time since I was a boy, I forgot about war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Glad I could help.

speaker: Thaletas
en: What about you? Are there things you'd like to forget?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There is much of my past I wish I could forget.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I'd love to hear about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And I'd love to tell you. But we have a war to fight.

speaker: Thaletas
en: When this war is won, then. We'll drink and share our deep, dark secrets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sooner we forget what happened here, the sooner we can focus on the rebellion, and I can set sail again.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I... I loved Kyra, but I chose you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a mercenary. You're Spartan. Your love for Kyra is safe. I won't tell if you don't.

speaker: Thaletas
en: So, that's it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course not. There's still a war to win. And, for now, we're fighting on the same side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's nothing I want more right now, Thaletas. You're a brave warrior and a true Spartan. But I've seen the way you and Kyra look at each other.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You have honor. I feel ashamed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't. You and Kyra belong together. That hasn't changed.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Misthios!

speaker: Thaletas
en: Don't tell my men about the flowers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's the temple on the hill.

speaker: Zetes
en: Our lives are like the rising and setting of the sun.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Excuse me?

speaker: Zetes
en: We're born into darkness and rise up to the greatest peaks... before descending into darkness once more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A warrior and a sophist. This is a first.

speaker: Zetes
en: It's not philosophy... it's truth. Learned through violence, fate, and seeing evil... true evil.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're talking about the Writhing Dread?

speaker: Zetes
en: The Creature.

speaker: Zetes
en: When it ambushed us outside, we thought only of survival. My spear allowed me to stay out of its gaze. I was lucky. My friends weren't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me how you were able to defeat the Creature.

speaker: Zetes
en: It all happened so fast. We had a plan to break into the temple and corner it, but it ambushed us before we got inside. There was no time for strategy after that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why go after the Creature in the first place?

speaker: Mercenary
en: We were hired to steal an ancient item from within its lair by masked soldiers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about the item they wanted you to steal.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Truth is, I don't even think they knew exactly what it was. After I killed the Creature I went to search the lair, but it was sealed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll leave you with your heavy thoughts.

speaker: Zetes
en: When fighting your own battles is all that's left, you are already lost.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're fighting the ghosts of your friends.

speaker: Zetes
en: Are you ready to face your destiny?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me that spear.

speaker: Zetes
en: We're warriors—to let it go without a fight would be to dishonor my fallen friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing special about this spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Heitor.

speaker: Heitor
en: Ah, my friend! I'm so glad you're here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know that look... If you need a favor, just tell me.

speaker: Heitor
en: Well... yes. A small one. A mercenary and old friend of mine has gotten himself captured.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you'd like me to free him.

speaker: Heitor
en: Sadly, I'm no longer able to do these things myself, otherwise I wouldn't ask.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ok, I'll do it.

speaker: Heitor
en: Thank you, my friend. Once you've rescue him, take him to the beach. I've left a boat there for him to escape.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where to look for him.

speaker: Heitor
en: He's in a military camp just north of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you so worried about a mercenary?

speaker: Heitor
en: He's a friend. Didn't I do the same for you? Remember that trouble you and Markos got into...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, yes, you're right.

speaker: Heitor
en: If we're not going to look out for each other, who will?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to go get your friend.

speaker: Heitor
en: There you are! I was starting to think you wouldn't show up.

speaker: Himilko
en: You!

speaker: Heitor
en: Hello, Himilko. Long time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Heitor, what's going on? Why are you here?

speaker: Himilko
en: Of course. He didn't tell, did he? You've been used, my friend.

speaker: Heitor
en: Shut up. I'm not here to hear you talk. I'm here to see you die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You deceived me! You asked me to rescue him just so you could kill him.

speaker: Heitor
en: I didn't lie... just omitted some details, that's all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You lied to me again. This isn't how friendships work, Heitor.

speaker: Heitor
en: Listen, please. I'm sorry, but you don't know what this man did to me.

speaker: Himilko
en: That's fucking rich, Heitor. Why don't you tell her the truth?

speaker: Heitor
en: Shut up, murderer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on?

speaker: Heitor
en: Trust me, this man needs to die. I gave you a contract to bring him to me. Do not interfere, and I will reward you well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got him out as you asked, so why kill him now? I could have dealt with him if that's what you wanted.

speaker: Heitor
en: Because I had to see him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why?

speaker: Heitor
en: Because he killed the love of my life.

speaker: Himilko
en: We both shared guilt in that, but she was my wife!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your wife?

speaker: Heitor
en: She wouldn't have died if...

speaker: Himilko
en: What? If I hadn't caught you? If you hadn't attacked me? If she hadn't tried to stop us? If our blades hadn't struck her down? Who's to blame here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Despite what either of you did, this won't bring her back.

speaker: Heitor
en: It will make me feel better...

speaker: Himilko
en: And that's more important to you in the end isn't it? Easing your conscience.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You think killing him would make you feel better? I guarantee it won't, and it sounds like she wouldn't have wanted either of you to get hurt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're both at fault in her death. And Heitor... I don't know, and don't want to know, why you were sleeping with another man's wife.

speaker: Heitor
en: We were in love!

speaker: Himilko
en: You idiot. Do you think you were the only one? When we went on campaigns, do you think she worried about her husband? About as much as we worried about our wives!

speaker: Heitor
en: No, she loved me. She told me so. We were going to run away together.

speaker: Himilko
en: She'd leave her home for you, with nothing. I heard you had to sell your sword, the only thing you ever owned of value. Why would she go with a lowly misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You malákes need to sort this out between yourselves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It sounds like neither of you was at fault.

speaker: Heitor
en: He drew his weapon first.

speaker: Himilko
en: You were with my wife. What did you expect? It is my right to restore my honor!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems neither of you wanted to kill her. There are no winners here, and neither of you has to die. Let it go.

speaker: Heitor
en: You're right. I'm sorry.

speaker: Himilko
en: Fuck your sorry, you destroyed my life that night. But I agree with your friend. Let's just pray we never see each other again.

speaker: Heitor
en: Why you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let him go. You made the right choice here.

speaker: Heitor
en: Sometimes we cannot make up for the mistakes of our past. I'm just glad all those years with me didn't rub off on you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sometimes we need to move on from the past, like I did from Kephallonia. You have a chance to make a new life—use it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need to know your reasons or hear your excuses.

speaker: Heitor
en: This man has wronged me, Kassandra. If you'll just listen...

speaker: Himilko
en: Oh, just get it over with. To be honest, it will be a relief for me. We're both guilty—at least I can accept that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just pay me. I don't want any part of this.

speaker: Heitor
en: Here, this should be more than enough. I threw in a little extra for old time's sake.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean for lying. I'm done with old times—it's why I left Kephallonia.

speaker: Lykaon
en: Is it a big hurt or a little hurt?

speaker: Child
en: I dunno.

speaker: Lykaon
en: Well, does it hurt like a bear biting you, or a mouse?

speaker: Child
en: Like three mouses. No, like four.

speaker: Lykaon
en: So a puppy-bite-sized hurt. Go it.

speaker: Child
en: Will the hurt go away?

speaker: Lykaon
en: Tell you what, you have to scare it away. If you roar like a lion, it'll run.

speaker: Lykaon
en: Good job. Now run along home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You must be a physician.

speaker: Lykaon
en: Yes, I'm Lykaon. You must be a misthios. Are you here for treatment?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That depends. Will I have to roar for you, too?

speaker: Lykaon
en: Sometimes the best medicine I can give my patients is a dose of hope. I take it you're not in need of care?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm healthy as a horse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Play-acting instead of medicine? When I'm wounded, I prefer to see someone serious.

speaker: Lykaon
en: The gods and the medicines they give us can do little when a patient has no hope. That's the best treatment I can give.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've thought this through.

speaker: Lykaon
en: You look strong and prepared for anything. My patients need mandrake herbs. There's a patch of them growing by a little stream southeast of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you too busy to pick them?

speaker: Lykaon
en: Too chewy. A pack of wolves is resting near the stream. I'll pay you generously for your trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know how to talk to a misthios. Is that all you want, the mandrake herbs?

speaker: Lykaon

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be Hyrkanos's camp...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, this has been quite profitable. Maybe I should hunt down more mercenaries.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The mercenary Hyrkanos is dead.

speaker: Dolios
en: Sparta thanks you, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about my reward?

speaker: Dolios
en: We never entered into a contract. This is something you did yourself... But be assured Sparta is grateful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Great...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Delos. The faces change, but the war carries on. Now Sparta has asked me to take two of Athens' finest off the board. Time to find my targets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alexios' blade. I hope I am making better use of it than he did.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: It's getting harder and harder to get the right goods in. I can barely break even.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Athens is on its knees. When Sparta wins the war, everything will go back to normal, you'll see.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: You think? We used to do well under Athenian rule. But Sparta? We might all end up like those slaves of theirs. What are they called?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Helots. But I'm sure it won't come to that.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: I hope you're right. For all our sakes.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: What happened to those supplies of yours? Weren't they in the warehouse by the dock?

speaker: Civilian 4
en: A hoplite loaded them onto the boat and thanked me for my "contribution for the war effort". The audacity! And now they won't let me back in!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: You should complain to the governor.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Oh, I intend to!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would have come here on the Adrestia, but my mission needs discretion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I miss seeing Ikaros in the skies above.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phaidos and Straton should be here, but the area is guarded by Athenian soldiers. I'll need to be careful.

speaker: Strategos 1
en: No, admiral Phaidos does not need another bodyguard, he's quite safe aboard the Bellerophon. What I need is for you to keep watch here, in case anyone tries to help themselves to our supplies. Now go, attend to your duties.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Interesting...

speaker: Kassandra
en: "We must be ready to sail with the morning tide. Come find me aboard the Bellerophon when all our supplies are accounted for." It is signed, "Phaidos".

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phaidos. After he's one of the few admirals Athens has left.

speaker: Phaidos
en: The provisions for the voyage?

speaker: Hoplite 1
en: All aboard, admiral. With a fair wind, the journey to Athens will not be long.

speaker: Phaidos
en: A fair wind... it seems we have had little but ill winds of late. But you're right. This grain must reach the city, and we must see that it gets there safely.

speaker: Hoplite 1
en: Poseidon is on our side.

speaker: Phaidos
en: Let's hope so, because every Spartan ship between here and Attika wants to see us at the bottom of the sea. Now, enough talk. Be about your business.

speaker: Hoplite 1
en: As you command.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One down, one to go.

speaker: Hoplite 2
en: I think Straton is going to stay in that courtyard for the rest of the war. He never got his sea legs, and after Aegospotami, I don't think he ever will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Could be useful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Straton. The Athenian magistrate for Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A note from Phaidos, the Athenian admiral. "At the first sign of enemy vessels, light the brazier. If we plan to show the Laconians that we still rule the seas, we cannot be taken by surprise."

speaker: Hoplite 3
en: The ships will be here in the morning. We can move the grain then, and be away.

speaker: Straton
en: Excellent. Sparta has long held the land, and now they rule the seas as well. Athens suffers already—if this shipment does not get to the city, the people will starve. Phaidos is ready to sail? The convoy will depend on his protection.

speaker: Hoplite 3
en: The admiral is overseeing preparations for the voyage as we speak. He looks forward to you joining him.

speaker: Straton
en: Good, good... Wait a moment. "Joining him"?

speaker: Hoplite 3
en: Yes, eminence. He has reserved a place for you aboard the Bellerophon.

speaker: Straton
en: He thinks I'm coming on the voyage?

speaker: Hoplite 3
en: Of course. His vessel is the pride of the Aegean.

speaker: Straton
en: And we've just lost a hundred and sixty other prides of the Aegean to the Spartans. It's incredibly dangerous out there! Look, just... just tell Phaidos I'm sick. Yes, I think I need to stay here on the island a little longer, until I feel ready to travel. (laugh) Yes. The convoy should go ahead without me. Now go. Convey the message.

speaker: Hoplite 3
en: As you wish, eminence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's done. Now to report in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An order for the guards to be alert for Spartan agents on the island. I hope Kastor stays out of trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Prayers to Apollo. Ever the popular choice.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: The tides are turning for the Athenians. Once our friends, now our masters, soon they will be gone altogether.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: I doubt the Laconians will be better bedfellows.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Yes, a pity they did not wipe each other out completely, but there may yet be a bright future for Delos in all of this.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: You are ever the optimist.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A note, maybe from a priest. "The Athenians have taken our treasures to fund their war, but they shall not have everything."

speaker: Civilian 7
en: I'm telling you, if the Spartans come here, we'll make a fortune.

speaker: Civilian 8
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Civilian 7
en: I've already sold "Achilles' sword pommel" to every Athenian soldier stationed here, and I've got three dozen more gathering dust in the warehouse. Some new customers are just what we need.

speaker: Civilian 9
en: I was on my way to the Temple of Artemis this morning, and a hoplite turned me away. He was quite rude.

speaker: Civilian 10
en: What would soldiers want with a temple? Are they storing something in there?

speaker: Civilian 9
en: I have no idea, but they are depriving me of my right to worship. I won't stand for it!

speaker: Civilian 10
en: If I were you, I'd wait until they've gone. I'm sure Artemis won't mind.

speaker: Civilian 11
en: The Temple is closed—a soldier told me to "keep out and mind my own business". Can you believe that?

speaker: Civilian 12
en: I think they're stockpiling provisions for a voyage, but they could have chosen a better place.

speaker: Kastor
en: Is it done, Kassandra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I dealt with your Athenians.

speaker: Kastor
en: Good.

speaker: Kastor
en: They were organizing a grain shipment to Athens. Their deaths will delay it, and help bring the city to terms.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's that?

speaker: Kastor
en: An old friend.

speaker: Odessa
en: Well. It's really you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Odessa? What... what brings you to Delos?

speaker: Odessa
en: I'm in search of a treasure, left here by Odysseus long ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What treasure is that?

speaker: Odessa
en: His bow. It's said to be hidden on the island.

speaker: Kastor
en: Hm, a local legend.

speaker: Odessa
en: Some legends are true. The story goes that if the statues in the Temple of Apollo match one another, the path to the Bow of Odysseus will be revealed. All they're missing is a bow, a wreath...

speaker: Odessa
en: ...and a lyre.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So there is some truth to this.

speaker: Kastor
en: And what of the wreath and the bow?

speaker: Odessa
en: Held in the island's treasury, right here in the Sanctuary of Apollo.

speaker: Kastor
en: Then they're under lock and key, and guarded by Athenian soldiers.

speaker: Odessa
en: But we have the tools for the job...

speaker: Odessa
en: ...and a misthios to do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So. You want me to find this bow for you.

speaker: Odessa
en: You wouldn't refuse an old friend, not after all we've been through.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can I forget? Very well, where do I start?

speaker: Odessa
en: You'll need the lyre, but you'll also need the bow and the wreath. With them, you can go to the Temple of Apollo and find my ancestor's bow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Every guard on Delos is looking for me.

speaker: Kastor
en: Then you'll need to wait until nightfall. As for me, I need to get back to Sparta.

speaker: Kastor
en: Good fortune to you both.

speaker: Odessa
en: I'll remain here, Kassandra. Come find me when you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Delos is quite beautiful at night. Now, to the treasury.

speaker: Civilian 13
en: Is it me, or there are more guards on the streets this evening?

speaker: Civilian 14
en: And at the treasury too. No-one's allowed inside. I think the incident at the harbor today has them on edge.

speaker: Civilian 13
en: Perhaps they should take the hint and leave Delos?

speaker: Civilian 14
en: You'd welcome Sparta over Athens?

speaker: Civilian 13
en: I'd welcome a change.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An inventory of items for one of the treasuries. It includes the bow Odessa told me about. Not the Bow of Odysseus though. It won't be that easy.

speaker: Hoplite 4
en: Night duty again?

speaker: Hoplite 5
en: I don't know why we're here. Anything valuable is locked away in those two big treasuries. Who's going to get in?

speaker: Hoplite 4
en: Well, perhaps you should complain to the strategos?

speaker: Hoplite 5
en: And find myself in the front line of our next battle with Sparta? I'll take what I've got, but I can still complain about it. Chaire. (Goodbye.)

speaker: Hoplite 4
en: Chaire (Goodbye), friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Voices near my position.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the location the guards were talking about. There must be something valuable in here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't the Bow of Odysseus, but... maybe it'll help me find it. The wreath must be in another building.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "To Strategos Diocles. There is a killer among us, and they are still on the island. Lock the treasury doors, and post additional guards tonight. If they strike again, we'll be ready."

speaker: Kassandra
en: A note from a soldier. "The wreath from the temple is in the small treasury building. If that old priest comes asking for it again, tell him Athens appreciates his contribution to the war effort."

speaker: Strategos 2
en: I know what's in that treasury, so if any of it goes missing—the amphoras, the wreath, the chests of drachmae—I'll know that too. Now, go to your duties.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That could be helpful to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another locked door. I should find a way inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is it. The wreath. A symbol of Apollo. That's everything Odessa said I'd need. I should go to the Temple of Apollo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Temple of Apollo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be one of the statues Odessa told me about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's another one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another statue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It worked!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place is deserted... But it could still be dangerous. I should tread carefully.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A trap! Something I can use must be nearby. Odessa, the things I do for you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: A shield. That could be useful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did Odysseus build this place? Or someone else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This bow had better be worth it, Odessa...

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is—Odysseus' bow!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have the bow, now to get back to Odessa. Somehow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A row of axes. Like in the legend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There. Perhaps Odysseus and I have something in common.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the Gods! Now I've seen everything...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phew! Alright. Time to get out of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have the bow. Now to get back to Odessa.

speaker: Hoplite 6
en: There's the intruder!

speaker: Hoplite 7
en: Down there! You see her?

speaker: Hoplite 8
en: Hey, stop! Halt!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've attracted some attention. Time to test my new bow.

speaker: Hoplite 9
en: I saw you cheating at dice the other day.

speaker: Hoplite 10
en: I did no such thing.

speaker: Hoplite 9
en: Come off it, I saw you.

speaker: Hoplite 10
en: Don't tell anyone. I'll be ruined if the rest find out.

speaker: Hoplite 9
en: Teach me how you do it, then.

speaker: Hoplite 10
en: If that's what it takes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I come bearing gifts.

speaker: Odessa
en: Kassandra?

speaker: Odessa
en: You're back? Is that...? You found the Bow. Let me see it. Come on, hand it over.

speaker: Odessa
en: It's real. The things this weapon has seen...

speaker: Odessa
en: But it was never made for ordinary people. It belonged to Odysseus. A hero.

speaker: Odessa
en: He's not here any more. But you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am honored, Odessa. I'll make good use of it. You have my word.

speaker: Odessa
en: So what now? It seems the war may soon be over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's always work for a misthios somewhere. Perhaps a return to Athens, once it's under Spartan rule.

speaker: Odessa
en: Then I suppose... this is goodbye?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Only until the next time. Chaire (Farewell), Odessa.

speaker: Hunting the Huntsman
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan in 2018 through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas!

speaker: Brasidas
en: I don't belong here!

speaker: Brasidas
en: You're next, soldier!

speaker: Brasidas
en: You fight like someone I once knew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We fought the Monger's thugs in a warehouse in Korinth. That's where we met.

speaker: Brasidas
en: The warehouse was on fire. We were surrounded.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We fought Athenians together at the Battle of Pylos.

speaker: Brasidas
en: The battlefield was engulfed in flames. I was cut down by a warrior like no other. The same warrior who sent me here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We fought together when Kleon and the Athenians landed in Amphipolis. Don't you remember?

speaker: Brasidas
en: We fought side by side. Victory was near, but then...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were killed.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Deimos. There is nothing but darkness after that.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Kassandra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's good to see you, old friend.

speaker: Brasidas
en: What are you doing here? Tell me you're not dead.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Friend? Friends watch each other's backs, but you were always out for yourself. My needs, the needs of our people were never a passing thought.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Friend? If you'd kill your own father, what would you do for a friend? You were always driven by vengeance, out for yourself. Never thinking about the greater good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All you cared about was Sparta. Did you ever consider that Sparta never cared about anyone else? We need to put the past behind us now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know I let you down. I tried to make it up to you at Amphipolis,, but I couldn't save you in time.

speaker: Brasidas
en: What are you doing here? You're not dead, are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, not yet at least. I have a Staff from my father, my real father. It has powers. I was sent to the underworld to learn how to use them.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Powers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a long story, but I've been all over Elysium looking for answers. My search brought me here.

speaker: Brasidas
en: You've been to Elysium?

speaker: Brasidias
en: "Honor the gods. Honor Sparta. Keep your oaths, and Elysium is yours." My father told me this as a child, and every single day of my life I lived by that code. But now in death, I'm sentenced to this misery.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nikolaos thought throwing me off a mountain upheld Spartan "code." Fathers don't always have the right answers, Brasidas.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Then I wasted a lifetime believing in a lie.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If there's anyone I fought with who deserves paradise, it's you.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Then why am I here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe you didn't fully live up to that code.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Impossible. I recited those words every morning and every night. They've been burned into my mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should be taking this up with Hades.

speaker: Brasidas
en: This was Hades' decision. He says I can go to Elysium on one condition. I need to confront my greatest enemy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Deimos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas, you shouldn't be waiting here to fight him.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Why not?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos still lives. Hades tricked you.

speaker: Brasidas
en: No matter. He'll show up, eventually.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did Hades tell you, exactly?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos lives. I had the chance to send him here, but I spared him.

speaker: Brasidas
en: He slaughtered my men. He sent me here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know, but the Cult destroyed my family. I did what I could to make it whole again. Besides, you once taught me "not all situations need to end in bloodshed."

speaker: Brasidas
en: Knowing this changes nothing. I will see Elysium.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't stand in your way. What did Hades tell you, exactly?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've met Hades. There must be a catch. What did he say exactly?

speaker: Brasidas
en: He said, "To walk Elysium in death, the son of Sparta must confront that which defeated him in life."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gods and their fucking riddles. Can't they ever just say what they mean? But, I think I've already solved your first problem.

speaker: Brasidas
en: And that is?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A true son of Sparta wouldn't dare face an enemy without their shield. We need to find yours.

speaker: Brasidas
en: It's in the Forgotten Sepulchre. I tried to retrieve it, but Hades sent guards to defend the tomb after some malákas killed Cerberos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That malákas was me. And now I'm stuck working for Hades.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Why am I not surprised? You've made things around here complicated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of malákas just goes around and kills Cerberos? Seriously.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Whoever it was certainly made things around here complicated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were always good to me in times of need. Now let me be a friend to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wasn't the friend you needed in life. Let me be a friend to you now

speaker: Brasidas
en: Courage eludes me in the underworld. Deep down, I hoped I'd never have to face Deimos again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about this Forgotten Sepulchre?"

speaker: Brasidas
en: It houses the armor, trophies, and weapons of dishonored warriors. Things they were buried with in death, but were stripped of in the underworld.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How will I know which shield is yours?

speaker: Brasidas
en: You should know my shield by now. It bears the colors of Sparta and has been through many battles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The weight of your shield will help you feel like your old self.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Make sure to take only mine. Taking any others will be your doom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I picked up your message on the board. What's happening?

speaker: Woman
en: Uncultured fools. Swine. At least the Athenian soldiers behaved like humans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your music wasn't popular with the Spartans?

speaker: Woman
en: They spat on me. They threatened and leered. Told me to go back to the city and give birth to sons. May the crows take them and the commander who invited me to come play here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me guess - you need me to kill the Spartan commander?

speaker: Woman
en: Obviously. Do we have a deal?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

speaker: Woman
en: Thank the muses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Woman
en: You again. Have you killed him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Woman
en: You're truly a great warrior. Please take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, commander. What can I do to serve Sparta?

speaker: Man
en: You! Misthios! You're the one who won the battle for Megaris for us Spartans!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your army needed a champion, and I responded. Easy.

speaker: Man
en: Thanks to you, Athenian efforts are fractured in this area, and my regiment is finally ready to strike.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you need?

speaker: Man
en: A certain Athenian commander is all that stands in our way to victory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. You want me to deal with the Athenian commander.

speaker: Man
en: You read me like an oracle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll handle this.

speaker: Man
en: Well met! Sparta thanks you.

speaker: Man
en: You again. Have you killed him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, mercenary. Now, your reward.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I've started.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw the message you left on the board. What's happening?

speaker: Man
en: An Athenian ship is supposed to arrive soon, and these waters are full of pirates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Athenians can handle them, no?

speaker: Man
en: They can row. They can fight. But both at the same time? My drachmae's on the pirates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like I need to sink some pirate ships.

speaker: Man
en: Exactly, my friend. The horizon must be cleared.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in.

speaker: Man
en: I knew I could trust you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should get going.

speaker: Man
en: Back already. Did you destroy them all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be hard to piece them back together.

speaker: Man
en: I owe you more than words can say. So I'll let this payment speak for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Diona
en: Weaklings! You cannot stop us!

speaker: Diona
en: You're a gift from the goddess herself!

speaker: Diona
en: And by the Fates— She chose well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're making me blush, stranger.

speaker: Diona
en: And I could do so much more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure about all of that, but you can definitely fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, your goddess has blessed you. I am a fine specimen. But, so are you.

speaker: Diona
en: I've always liked the charmers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess you didn't like these guys. You can fight, I'm impressed.

speaker: Diona
en: I may be a priestess of love, but I also bite. I always bite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One has to be bold to attack a priestess. You must be important.

speaker: Diona
en: I am Diona, a simple acolyte born to serve Aphrodite. These thugs are dogs of the Cult of Kosmos, and this has not been the first attempt on my life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult? Tell me all that you know. Now.

speaker: Diona
en: Not here. We'll be safer in the city. Escort me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go. You can tell me everything you know about the Cult when we arrive.

speaker: Diona
en: I need to get back into the city. It should be safe there.

speaker: Diona
en: Fucking bandits! I'll cut you all down!

speaker: Diona
en: I'm safe here. The Cult of Kosmos would never strike inside the city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Tell me more about them.

speaker: Diona
en: Right now? At least let me catch my breath. And take a good long look at your beautiful self.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll be fine on your own.

speaker: Diona
en: Well, when you can be bothered, I'll be in the city. You might find what I have to say interesting.

speaker: Diona
en: Missed me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You clearly didn't need an escort.

speaker: Diona
en: But who doesn't want some company?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Some of us enjoy solitude.

speaker: Diona
en: You're just here for the Cult of Kosmos, aren't you? You break my heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough idle chatter. Tell me what you know about the Cult.

speaker: Diona
en: If you insist. We've always kept tabs on the Cult, and lately they've gotten bolder. By the Fates! They've driven my sister, the High Priestess, to lock herself in her chambers!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A Cult leader must be involved if they are trying to kill such a public figure.

speaker: Diona
en: We're not dealing with the usual rats. My sister wants me to secure Kythera from the Cult and sniff out the Cultist behind her troubles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Risking your life while she hides away? Ridiculous.

speaker: Diona
en: Sadly her life is more valuable to Kythera than my own. By the Fates, misthios! I cannot secure Kythera by myself. You've got to help me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That could work. Your sister sounds smart.

speaker: Diona
en: The plan isn't that praiseworthy. I was nearly killed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Unfortunate, but her plan is still good.

speaker: Diona
en: Then help us secure Kythera and root out the enemy. By the Fates! You've seen what can happen, I can't do this on my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Secure Kythera? I don't work for free.

speaker: Diona
en: A misthios indeed. The Cult has plans for the Greek world. And with my ways, I know what they will do next and where they plan to do it.

speaker: Diona
en: I imagine this information would be useful to you. Or if that isn't enough to satisfy you— I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, it has been a while since I've

speaker: Diona
en: Communed with the gods? And don't worry, drachmae will also be given for your services.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You drive a hard bargain. So, what do you need me to do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm only here for information on the Cult of Kosmos. And drachmae. Lots of it.

speaker: Diona
en: You don't know what you're missing, misthios. But drachmae it is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Excellent, so what needs to be done?

speaker: Diona
en: Just three simple tasks. First, my associate by the harbor needs help. Pay him a visit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What else?

speaker: Diona
en: My sister believes she has leads on a traitor within our ranks. If that's true, she'll need your help. Look for her in the temple. And lastly. Poisoned blades are a priestess' weapon of choice. But some bandits sacked our apothecaries and have taken refuge in the Mycenaean ruins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it's not the Cult, it's malákes bandits.

speaker: Diona
en: Retrieve our poison vials, they will come in handy when fighting against the Cult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lucky for you, I came across some bandits earlier in the ruins to the south. Is this yours?

speaker: Diona
en: By the Fates! It is! Thank you, misthios. Now we can prepare for battle against the Cult.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more about the rest of your requests.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This associate of yours, where is he?

speaker: Diona
en: Ask for the harbor master at the tavern in Skandeia Harbor. He'll be the obnoxious drunk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The temple. Where is it?

speaker: Diona
en: It's on Aphrodite's Watch, up the hill. You'll find the High Priestess there, hiding in her chambers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How will I get to these ruins?

speaker: Diona
en: The Mycenaean Ruins are to the south of the city, north of Skandeia Bay. The poison vials should be in the bag. It'll probably be in a chest in the ruins. Be very careful with it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I can for you and Kythera.

speaker: Diona
en: Thank you, misthios. Perhaps... when all this is over, we could unwind together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Priorities, Diona. I'll see you later.

speaker: Civilian
en: Oh, a real adventurer! Please, help! Please, misthios! It's my idiot husband!

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios! My husband!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong with him?

speaker: Civilian
en: He's an idiot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's one problem I can't solve.

speaker: Civilian
en: He's a fisherman who thought he could make better drachmae hunting lynx—spent everything we had on a bow! I haven't seen him in three days. Please, misthios, will you find my idiot?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not only will I find your idiot, I'll bring him home.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you! He was last seen west of Skandeia Harbor. Please hurry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So he's an idiot—but is he a good huntsman?

speaker: Civilian
en: He struggled with fish, misthios. Tiny, toothless fish. And now the fool is hunting lynx.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said your husband headed

speaker: Civilian
en: The biggest lynx live in caves near the ruins. Knowing my idiot, that's where he'd go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How much is your husband worth to you?

speaker: Civilian
en: You can keep his bow. It was the talk of the agora before he bought it. Then I'll make sure he never uses it again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's been gone a while. I should get going.

speaker: Civilian
en: You'll find him. I know it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How?

speaker: Civilian
en: Because you're not an idiot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lynx don't prowl for nothing... Must be something in that cave.

speaker: Civilian
en: That... is a lot of blood! Help! I can hear you! Please, I—there's so much blood, help!

speaker: Civilian
en: I knew you weren't a lynx. Heard you're footsteps. Only two. Lynx have four.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're seriously wounded.

speaker: Civilian
en: These lynx—uh, they're a bit tougher than the sea bass I usually catch. Could you help a fellow hunter home to his wife?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank the gods! She's in Skandeia Harbor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about your wife.

speaker: Civilian
en: She's the real lynx!

speaker: Civilian
en: Please don't tell her I said that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I get you home safe, what's my reward?

speaker: Civilian
en: My bow. It's my pride and joy—sold almost everything I owned to buy it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said you usually catch sea bass—what made you think you could take on a lynx?

speaker: Civilian
en: Never seen a Kytherian sea bass, have you? Even a lynx wouldn't touch 'em! If you fancy yourself a hunter, though... there's a monstrous beast in the south. Was gonna go after it myself once I broke in my bow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Monstrous beast, huh? I'll have to see it for myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've lost a lot of blood. If you're going to make it home, we'll need to move now.

speaker: Civilian
en: Ow, ow, ow!

speaker: Civilian
en: How much blood can a man lose? I'm getting tired.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you must be his wife.

speaker: Civilian
en: The wife of an idiot, I'm afraid.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Missed your idiot?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: My love, you're alive!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: So. Are we having lynx for dinner?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Enough about the lynx.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm happy to see you reunited.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are the strangest people I've ever met.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Love is strange, misthios. Best to embrace it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wonderful. I'll leave you to, ah— Chaire.

speaker: Woman
en: What happened?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found him in a cave, surrounded by lynx. He'd killed a few, but was too far gone to bring home.

speaker: Woman
en: So my husband was alive when you found him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He was badly wounded

speaker: Woman
en: But breathing? You - you could have helped him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did all I could

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found him in a cave not far from here. He was wounded, but alive.

speaker: Woman
en: I - what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I stopped the bleeding and offered to bring him home, but he didn't want to come back.

speaker: Woman
en: Liar! How - you killed him! I'll send every mercenary in the Greek world after you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've freed your mercenaries and dealt with the captain as you desired.

speaker: Diona
en: That's good news. You've dealt a heavy blow to the Cult's forces. You're getting sexier by the minute. Anything else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's your apothecary's bag.

speaker: Diona
en: With this, we can make sure all our priestesses are armed for battle. Excellent work, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your sister sends her regards.

speaker: Diona
en: Did you find out anything about this "traitor"?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There seems to be a traitor in the temple, but she's unsure who. There was just a note reading "Do not trust the Fates."

speaker: Diona
en: Interesting. It really is as my sister says, we can't trust anyone... Thank you, misthios. I'll watch my back. Is there something else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your sister has definite proof of a traitor.

speaker: Diona
en: W-what? That can't be! Who is it? You must tell me, or I won't know who to trust.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We don't know yet. But your sister is looking into it.

speaker: Diona
en: I see. I too shall take my own precautions. A visit to see her might be in order. Thank you, misthios. Is there something else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've done what you asked. What now?

speaker: Diona
en: My scouts will meet us at my villa. They'll fill us in on what they've discovered, thanks to your efforts. I have something else to attend to, but... If I get there, and we have some time on our hands, by the Fates, we'll have some fun.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'd better hurry. I'll see you at the villa.

speaker: Diona
en: I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. the Cult is what's important right now. I'll see you at the villa.

speaker: Diona
en: By the Fates, you can only resist me for so long...

speaker: Female Atlantean
en: That's the murderer!

speaker: Lyra
en: Murderer? I didn't do it!

speaker: Male Atlantean
en: Stop her before she kills again!

speaker: Lyra
en: Leave me alone!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Want to tell me what that was all about?

speaker: Lyra
en: No. I'll be fine.

speaker: Lyra
en: Dikastes! You can make this all go away. My name is Lyra. And you're...you. You've helped so many people! You're amazing and wonderful and powerful and...and...you're here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. That's nice of you.

speaker: Lyra
en: You deserve all the praise and more!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough. I don't like...whatever it is you're doing.

speaker: Lyra
en: Forgive me! It's just that your being here confirms all the legends. You're real! To be face to face with you right now, it's

speaker: Lyra
en: Sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They called you a murderer. You don't seem the type, but as Dikastes, I have to be sure.

speaker: Lyra
en: They're sure I'm responsible for what happened to that poor family. They said it's like the other murders. But... I couldn't live with myself, I swear! Please. Clear my name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where were you when the family was murdered?

speaker: Lyra
en: If it happened last night like they said, I was here trying to sleep. Although, lately it's been restless, filled with strange dreams. It's always the same one, over and over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Were you alone?

speaker: Lyra
en: Well, yes. I've been so tired lately I decided to stay in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said something about other murders.

speaker: Lyra
en: This was the third time. I just don't understand why they'd blame me. I don't have the stomach to do... that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out what really happened. Just point me in the direction of the attack.

speaker: Lyra
en: Just down the road, not too far from here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I were you, I'd hide until I return.

speaker: Lyra
en: Good idea. Thank you! You truly are a great Dikastes.

speaker: Witness
en: The great Dikastes! What did I do to deserve a visit?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking into the attack that happened nearby last night.

speaker: Witness
en: Ah, of course. I thought that was meant to be handled already.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean the mob harassing that woman?

speaker: Witness
en: I've said enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I understand your hesitation, but I'm trying to get to the bottom of this. I'll make sure whoever—or whatever—did this is punished.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm the Dikastes, remember? Trust me, people who don't tell me what I want to know end up regretting their silence.

speaker: Witness
en: You've already met the guilty one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lyra? You agree with the mob.

speaker: Witness
en: Of course I do! I'm the one who told them it was her! I saw her last night—bloody, and in a frenzy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was dark. How do you know it was her?

speaker: Witness
en: I know what I saw!

speaker: Witness
en: I told you what I know. It was Lyra I saw.

speaker: Witness
en: Is this about what happened last night?

speaker: Kassandra
en: How'd you know?

speaker: Witness
en: It's all everyone's talking about. And, if the Dikastes is here, you must be looking into it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you saw or heard anything, I need to know.

speaker: Witness
en: I saw it from the distance. Heard it too... Its howl will never leave my mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You saw a wolf?

speaker: Witness
en: "Beast" is more like it. If you see it, run!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The footprints tracked the blood out of the house. Whoever murdered them left this way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These aren't stab wounds... they're claw marks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This bloodied cloth doesn't match the mother or daughter's robes. It must have come off the murderer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should return to Lyra and let her know what I found.

speaker: Lyra
en: Well? Did you find out what happened?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The evidence I found was... conflicting.

speaker: Lyra
en: Tell me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Two people saw what happened. One woman heard a wolf howling. But a man said he saw you, covered in blood and leaving the family's house.

speaker: Lyra
en: He's lying!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or mistaken. It was dark, so it could have been anyone. There's more. The killing blows weren't made by a weapon.

speaker: Lyra
en: Then by what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It almost looked like... claw marks. And then there was this piece of cloth. It didn't match the clothes of anyone there.

speaker: Lyra
en: That's... that's mine. How did it get there? Someone wants me to look like I was responsible. Tell me the truth, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Drop the act. You killed them.

speaker: Lyra
en: You're not serious. What about how they died? I don't have claws.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The marks could have been from animals that smelled the bodies and came to feed.

speaker: Lyra
en: But, the howl

speaker: Kassandra
en: Means nothing except there was a wolf nearby.

speaker: Lyra
en: You were supposed to prove I was innocent! Do you know what they do to human murderers? They send them to the Arena! I won't let you take me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to go after Lyra before she hurts someone else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whether it was a wolf or something else, it's clear it wasn't you.

speaker: Lyra
en: Of course it wasn't! But, why would someone make it seem like I'm the murderer?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll figure that out together. After I kill the beast.

speaker: Lyra
en: You're going to kill it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What other choice is there? Do you want another mob after you?

speaker: Lyra
en: No, of course not. I've just always hated the killing of animals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I don't kill it now, it will kill someone later.

speaker: Lyra
en: I have a friend who can keep me safe while you end this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to find the beast and kill it before it grows bloodthirsty again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is no ordinary wolf.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka. Lyra...

speaker: Lyra
en: It was me... What am I?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen this before. A Minotaur, a cyclops, a Gorgon... All were humans possessed by powerful Isu devices. The only way I could stop them was by killing them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you're able to change back. Somehow, you're different.

speaker: Lyra
en: I don't remember coming here. Or why.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I had to guess, that side of you knew it was caught. Maybe it thought coming out here was the only choice it had.

speaker: Lyra
en: That side of me. I've had dreams lately of being in a bright room... tied down... pain throughout my body... But now, I think that all really happened.

speaker: Lyra
en: I did kill them, then. I don't remember it, but it was me, wasn't it?

speaker: Lyra
en: If you knew you would harm people again, and you could never control yourself... never stop... would you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Would I what?

speaker: Lyra
en: Jump?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I lost control of myself and knew I'd never get it back, I'm not sure what I'd do.

speaker: Lyra
en: I thought so. This is the only way. If I'm to die, I want to be the one to decide when that happens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't need to do this.

speaker: Lyra
en: The choice was made for me. I can't go on after what I've done. And what I'd likely do again.

speaker: Lyra
en: Thank you. For everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She didn't deserve this. Whatever was done to her wasn't her fault.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I wouldn't!

speaker: Lyra
en: But you accused me of killing that family. And you were right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have to understand. That wasn't the real you!

speaker: Lyra
en: It is. And you said the only way you beat this before was by killing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I also said you were different.

speaker: Lyra
en: Whether I remember it or not, it's a part of me. It did terrible things.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are always answers.

speaker: Lyra
en: How could that be? It feels so... permanent.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's only one part of you. It's not all of you. I know what it's like to be part human, and part something else. Trust me, you can live with this burden.

speaker: Lyra
en: I'm not as strong as you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look at yourself. Yes you are. You're stronger than you think.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Plus, I've been thrown off a cliff before. I wouldn't recommend it.

speaker: Lyra
en: But you're still here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am. And you are too.

speaker: Lyra
en: You're right. Now that I know what's inside of me, I can do something about it, and I know who can help! Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope she'll be okay.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Isu technology can and will change whoever isn't strong enough to command it. That explains your own aggression, Layla.

speaker: Layla
en: I'm still me. I'm not as weak as you think I am.

speaker: Priestess
en: Mighty Kephalos, I entreat you! Send us a champion! Someone worthy of your might spear! Help your priestess in her hour of need!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You called?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm the only one here. But maybe I can help you.

speaker: Priestess
en: Oh! Oh... Kassandra. You startled me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you looking for a champion?

speaker: Priestess
en: I need someone worthy to win the Spear of Kephalos! I've been deciphering some of the sanctuary's stone carvings. They say the spear was hidden in the caves beneath Kephallonia when the temple was built! You could get it for me, couldn't you? I can give you a reward!

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the spear is in the caves, I'll find it.

speaker: Priestess
en: Well! Maybe you were sent by Kephalos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kephalos had a spear?

speaker: Priestess
en: Kassandra. Surely you've heard this story since you were a child.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't have much time for stories.

speaker: Priestess
en: Well. Perhaps you didn't. But you know Kephalos founded Kephallonia and started the line of Odysseus. His spear was a gift from the Gods. It was said never to miss its target. He must have hidden it in the caves after killing his wife with it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He threw a spear that wouldn't miss at his wife?

speaker: Priestess
en: He was hunting and heard her in the bushes. He thought she was a deer. It's a sad story.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds dangerous.

speaker: Priestess
en: Well, only if you throw it at someone!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you need a spear? Not thinking of becoming a soldier, are you?

speaker: Priestess
en: Of course not. But think how many people will come to the shrine if we have the Spear of Kephalos! With their donations, I could do so many things! Repair the sanctuary. Feed the hungry families in Sami.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So where is the spear?

speaker: Priestess
en: Apparently it's hidden deep in the caves beneath Kephallonia. There's an entrance north of here; maybe you can try that way first.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not much to go on.

speaker: Priestess
en: You have so little faith in the gods! If Kephalos means for us to have the spear, you will find it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can find.

speaker: Priestess
en: Oh, thank you. I'll prepare a spot in the sanctuary!

speaker: Priestess
en: Kassandra! Have you come back to talk about the spear?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have.

speaker: Priestess
en: Oh good! Tell me, did you find it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned a reward.

speaker: Priestess
en: Oh. Of course! You've certainly earned it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Consider it a donation to the temple.

speaker: Priestess
en: What, no reward? Oh, Kassandra, I'm in your debt. If ever there's a way my temple can help you—or anyone. Send them here. I will remember.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I looked in the caves. The spear isn't there.

speaker: Priestess
en: I had hoped to revive the sanctuary. But... it is as Kephalos wills it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get you your seals.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: First, I have some questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who does a general like you look up to?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: You know who was a true hero?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm guessing you're about to tell me.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Odysseus . He used his wits to triumph. Wily Odysseus, they call him. Without him, the Trojan war would have been lost. And the other generals understood that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you think your future holds?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Victory or death. You don't stay a general for long if you don't win battles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I suppose many generals die on the field.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Not the majority. The Athenian people are the greatest threat to a general's life. If you displease them, they'll remove you from office. Ostracize you. Or even condemn you to death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you want this job?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: There is no greater purpose than the glory of Athens. It's my duty and my honor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why is it I always find you here?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Athena is the goddess of wisdom. And war. What better place for a general to ask for blessings?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't seem very devout to me.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I'm not the first general in my family. My father was as well, and his father before him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You would have learned military thinking from a young age.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Exactly. My grandfather brought me here when I was a child. He stood me here and told me Athena was our patron. That we must always offer her our respect on the eve of war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He sounds like a wise man.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: He was. He died in battle the next day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You come here to remember him.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: And to remember that though the gods may be our patrons, they will not always protect us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Since you're being so polite, I already have them.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: And the other generals dare to doubt me! There's no way Neon can take credit for this one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's taken credit before?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: You could say that. However, I'm the one who hired you. I have more work for you, if you're ready.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Do you have my seals yet?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why yes, I do.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Good. The Spartans will soon realize someone is picking off their senior commanders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Probably, but they haven't caught me yet.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Interested in more work?

speaker: Aietes
en: Ugh, I shouldn't have drunk so much. I need to train or I'll never beat Neleus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Long night?

speaker: Aietes
en: Ugh...Waaay too long. I need to—ugh—shake this off and start training so I can... Defeat Neleus! And ride that victory to become the Olympic

speaker: Aietes
en: Ah, who am I kidding, maybe I am just not cut out for this Olympic stuff..

speaker: Kassandra
en: I take it you're Aietes. Mikkos sent me. Neleus

speaker: Aietes
en: Neleus?! What now? Did he break another record?!.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, he did.

speaker: Aietes
en: Oh, curses! What record did he break this time? I bet it was the discus throw. No, wait. Maybe...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Projectile vomiting.

speaker: Aietes
en: Huh? Zeus! He even beats me at throwing up?! Curse you and your perfections, Neleus! So Mikkos sent you here just to break my spirits?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, he didn't. He's bound to his bed.

speaker: Aietes
en: Oh, just another drunken night of celebration, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then it must have been quite a night.

speaker: Aietes
en: Huh?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Neleus has taken ill. Mikkos sent me here because you were the last one to see him well.

speaker: Aietes
en: He was fine when we went to Karpos's house for the usual, uh - dose of hedonism - But I didn't leave the party with him. Or seen him since

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something must have happened at the party, then.

speaker: Aietes
en: Look for Karpos at his house on the hill, he probably knows what happened to Neleus. He's a reclusive man, though. You will need to get his attention. I'd say smashing some of his valuable wine, the stuff that gets me this drunk, would get him to come out and play.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, Aietes. I'll look into it.

speaker: Aietes
en: Well, I better get started, or I'll never catch up to Neleus and the rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Being the Olympic champion doesn't sound as impressive as travelling across the Greek world. Come work for me on my ship and see new sights. I could use someone with your arms. Strong, rower's arms.

speaker: Aietes
en: I've always wanted to travel...And you know what, I'm sick of this training day in and day out. Count me in, misthios! I mean, captain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aietes, you will be an Olympic champion. Believe in yourself.

speaker: Aietes
en: You're right! I can do this. I've just got to work extra, extra hard. Thank you for believing in me! I'll beat Neleus and all the others.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It'll start with the right attitude.

speaker: Aietes
en: Olympic Champion Aietes! Yeah, that sounds perfect! I'll be the best the Greek world has ever seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do your best, Aietes. See you later.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Ooh! Look who it is! Oh, misthiosss! Comeee over hereee! You know you want some of this. Heyyy! Don't ignore me, misthios! Am I not your type? Well, you're not my type either! Fine. Don't come over here. OK, OK, I'm joking Come here. I'll make it up to you, I promise. Hello, hello? Misthios?

speaker: Mikkos
en: Loook whooo's hereee!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mikkos? You should be at home taking care of Neleus. I should be doing a lot of things, but right now—I want to have some fun. You look like you could use a little fun. And I'm plenty of it. So how about it? You and me. Let's have a great time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why don't you tell your little friends to leave?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm all you'll need.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Well, you heard the misthios. Get lost!

speaker: Mikkos
en: I... I can still continue

speaker: Kassandra
en: I honestly doubt you could even stand right now.

speaker: Mikkos
en: I mean, I could just lie here

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe later. Goodbye, Mikkos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Just us?

speaker: Mikkos
en: Ohhh! Now we're talking.

speaker: Mikkos
en: So what were you thinking? Him? Or her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm the greedy type. Let's go with both of them.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Oh, you just made my night, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shut up already.

speaker: Mikkos
en: I... I can still continue

speaker: Kassandra
en: I honestly doubt you could even stand right now.

speaker: Mikkos
en: I mean, I could just lie here

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe later. Goodbye, Mikkos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have work to do, Mikkos. Work you sent me to do. I'll pass.

speaker: Mikkos
en: But nooo. Work can wait just for a bit. I promise I won't take long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Increasingly less interested.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Maláka! Ah, no matter. Got space for another? Make a little rooom!

speaker: Cult Scion
en: Stop stealing sips of it, you idiot. You know what this wine does, right?

speaker: Cult Guardian
en: But it's just so good. Maybe more of it will make us stronger?

speaker: Cult Scion
en: More of it will make you dead. You've seen the athletes in the armory

speaker: Cult Guardian
en: What damage could one more sip cause

speaker: Cult Scion
en: We're supposed to be protecting the wine, not drinking it. Stop.

speaker: Karpos
en: What have you done?! You murdered the—Oh, no, no, no. The general is going to kill me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're with the Cult, aren't you? What did you do to Neleus

speaker: Karpos
en: No! No, no, no. I'm just uh, business associates with them, I work for the general

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what your "business" is with the general, or I start removing your teeth one by one.

speaker: Karpos
en: Maláka! Fine. I help the—more like, I'm being blackmailed by—the Cult of Kosmos to deliver them drunk athletes for their army. The good ones fetch more. Good ones like Neleus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And now, he's very sick.

speaker: Karpos
en: They do something to the students... It makes them... different. How do you think the elite guards can do what they do? Their strength... it's not normal. Not natural!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No matter their strength, it pales in comparison to mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're definitely a rank above most soldiers, that's for sure.

speaker: Karpos
en: I've messed up, misthios. I couldn't defy them before, but - With you on my side, maybe we can turn this around

speaker: Karpos
en: The Cultists always took the drunk students from my docks to a cave along the coast, south of here.
