speaker: Kassandra
en: There might be redemption for you yet.

speaker: Karpos
en: The people of Thasos are my people after all, misthios. The Cultists may have lined my pockets, but my heart is empty. Save the students. Please. I can't do this anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Switching sides already? If I hadn't caught you, you'd still be slinking about in the shadows.

speaker: Karpos
en: They aren't going to forgive what happened to their guards in my house, and my life is worth more to me than drachmae. My loyalty is not to the Cult

speaker: Kassandra
en: Or Thasos. You're just thinking of yourself, trying to stay alive.

speaker: Karpos
en: We're all reduced to that when our lives are truly in danger. Save the students for Thasos, misthios. And—Cull the Cultists while you're at it. That's just good for everybody.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll save the students for their own sake, not yours. If anything happens to Neleus, you're a dead man.

speaker: Karpos
en: I'm sure he'll be fine. Go to the students, they are in a cave to the south. Follow the coast and you'll see it. Good luck.

speaker: Cult Protector 1
en: The Doctor should be here by now. He's late.

speaker: Cult Protector 2
en: Hey! No one's allowed in here.

speaker: Student
en: Help us...Please. Where am I?

speaker: Drugged Student
en: Rarghhh!

speaker: Karpos
en: Misthios, help! The tonic has driven him crazy!

speaker: Karpos
en: Misthios! Thank Zeus, he was going to kill me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is your fault. These prisoners—they've had the tonic already.

speaker: Karpos
en: Hmm...The—the doctor must have come by to administer it. Only one of them has had a bad reaction. The other one look like he still stands a chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then there's still hope for Neleus.

speaker: Karpos
en: Looks like this was quite the reinforced hideout. The Cult are a bigger force to be reckoned with than I took them for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The moment I arrived on Thasos, the Cult of Kosmos never stood a chance

speaker: Kassandra
en: We were lucky this time. Who can say what happened to the other students.

speaker: Karpos
en: The Cultists need to pay for what they've done. Now is the time to retaliate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You sound like you have a suggestion.

speaker: Karpos
en: We need to storm their Ancient Stronghold, misthios. With you leading the charge, we'll kill the general of the Cult guards. We can deliver them a crushing defeat here that reverberates across the Greek world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You just want me to get the general off your back for failing him.

speaker: Karpos
en: Happy coincidence, I guess

speaker: Kassandra
en: This general, tell me more.

speaker: Karpos
en: That malákas strong-armed me into this whole mess. He's the head of the elite Cult guards, and rumor has it he beheaded eight men with one swing of his polearm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This Ancient Stronghold, where is it exactly?

speaker: Karpos
en: It's a massive structure sitting on Lemnos in plain sight. I'm told that the best way to reach it is by boat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At least now I know for sure Neleus didn't just have a cold. Mikkos needs to know about this. This is all your fault, so make sure these students get home safe.

speaker: Karpos
en: I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Need any help?

speaker: Woman
en: Eagle Bearer! I don't know how to thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I accept your gratitude. I'm sure I've done something to warrant it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure what I've done that warrants your thanks.

speaker: Woman
en: You saved baby Alethea from that terrible witch, Chrysis. Because of you, both mother and child are reunited, and the whole village knows the mistake the priests of Asklepios made.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hopefully no more innocent children will be taken from their mothers in the name of Hera.

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, we need to put a stop to this madness once and for all. The village hopes you will help them this one final time to destroy the remaining shrine that Chrysis built.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I must find and destroy it?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, the shrine must be destroyed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

speaker: Woman
en: I'm in your debt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Woman
en: You again. Has it been destroyed, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's been smashed to pieces, just like you asked.

speaker: Woman
en: You're truly skilled, misthios. Here. For you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Pentheus
en: My life is already over. I'm nothing but my suffering.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: There may still be hope if I can learn more about what ails you.

speaker: Pentheus
en: It's no longer about me. I'm worried for my son.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: A boy still needs his father around. Besides, Dikaios is a smart boy. He'll be fine.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Not if my rivals have their way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates—you know it's unwise to upset a patient.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: He asks me to end his life when he knows I can't.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Misthios, please help me. I'm in such terrible pain.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: You cannot simply ask someone else to kill you in my presence. I'm your physician—I will not allow it. I can ease your pain, analyze your symptoms, and try to cure you, but that's all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pain is just part of being mortal. It reminds us that we're alive and keeps us sharp.

speaker: Pentheus
en: I have known many pains in my life. My own suffering isn't what I worry about right now, but making sure my family's future is secured.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Life is about choice, and we should all be able to choose for ourselves when we leave this world.

speaker: Pentheus
en: And I will, once I know my family's future is secured.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Secured how?

speaker: Pentheus
en: My family is one of the richest in Thebes, and we have many rivals. When I die, my son will become the head of our house.

speaker: Pentheus
en: He's just a boy.

speaker: Pentheus
en: I need to ensure they can't take advantage of my death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll deal with your rivals and give your son a fighting chance.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Thank you, misthios. If you steal their assets, it will weaken their position and prevent them from posing a threat to my family. That will buy my son time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your family will be fine. Stay focused on your treatment, and do what Hippokrates tells you.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Have you decided to grant a dying man his wish?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do I need to steal?

speaker: Pentheus
en: To really weaken them, steal their debt registry, their mortgage testimonials, and their collection of fine jewels.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where do I need to go?

speaker: Pentheus
en: Their estate is nearby. It's one of the most finely decorated homes in all of Thebes—except for mine, of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why not just kill them and remove the threat for good?

speaker: Pentheus
en: If they're weakened, they won't pose a threat to my family's position. If they're removed, another family will rise up to take their place and still pose a threat.

speaker: Pentheus
en: This solution keeps my family safe, and their position secure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stealing isn't normally what I'm paid for, but I'll get it done.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: If doing this helps bring him some semblance of peace, I will pray for Tyche to watch over you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should be everything worth taking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've done what you asked. Your family's position will be secure for quite some time.

speaker: Pentheus
en: You have given me hope that my name will live on long after I'm gone. All that I ask gods for now is that my son lives a longer and happier life than I. I'm in your debt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't owe me anything, really.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm always happy to help a wealthy noble with his problems.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Now... it pains me to ask, but I need your help with one more thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what you want to ask.

speaker: Pentheus
en: This disease will claim me, be it today or another in the future. It's a matter of when, not if.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates won't just let me kill you.

speaker: Pentheus
en: No, but he'll listen to you. If you can convince him it's what's best for me, he might change his mind.

speaker: Pentheus
en: I don't want to slowly waste away. I want to die in peace while my family remembers me in a good light.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates is stubborn, but for good reason. He believes in helping people, not hurting them. I don't think I'll convince him otherwise.

speaker: Pentheus
en: I know he means well, but he must know I'm beyond saving.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Still, I understand your choice. Now, I think I need to rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll talk to him for you.

speaker: Pentheus
en: I appreciate your help. You've shown me more kindness in the last few days than most have my entire life.

speaker: Pentheus
en: Now, I must rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Anything you need a mercenary's help with?

speaker: Man
en: You! You sail aboard the Adrestia with Barnabas!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know this, stranger?

speaker: Man
en: I once stood alongside him, until a filthy pirate ran his blade through my back. Now I can barely stand straight. I was replaced by you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry to hear of your injury. I had no idea I was taking anyone's place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I had nothing to do with your back or Barnabas' decision.

speaker: Man
en: Now I'll never get to sail with my son. You took everything from me. Now I'll take everything from you!

speaker: Man
en: The worst part is I always dreamed of sailing with my son. But with my back, I can't even collect enough wood to build a felluca for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you want me to give you some drachmae?

speaker: Man
en: Yes. Any drachmae you can give helps.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. Here it is.

speaker: Inside Threat
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should go to the fort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Run! The others are down the mountain!

speaker: Civilian
en: Oh thank Zeus! And you!

speaker: Civilian
en: My girl, have you seen my girl?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your child is down the mountain with the others. Go!

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you!

speaker: Greek Brute
en: A man with yellow eyes is hard to miss.

speaker: Kleta
en: I told you, I saw no one matching that description.

speaker: Greek Brute
en: Don't lie to me.

speaker: Kleta
en: Believe what you will.

speaker: Greek Brute
en: How about a misthios with a bird? An eagle?

speaker: Kleta
en: That's ridiculous. Stop asking me stupid questions and let me be caged in peace.

speaker: Greek Brute
en: Why you...!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get to the bottom of the mountain. There's people there.

speaker: Kleta
en: A misthios? Thank you.

speaker: Darius
en: We've been in Achaia too long. The Order will catch up with us soon.

speaker: Natakas
en: People. Need. Our. Help.

speaker: Child
en: Mater!

speaker: Civilian
en: My child! You're safe. Thank Zeus!

speaker: Natakas
en: Kassandra! You're back.

speaker: Kleta
en: You're the misthios who saved us. Thank you. I'm Kleta.

speaker: Kleta
en: I'm sheltering the stranded in Boura, a village not far from here. I've been in Achaia for a long time... but something has changed. A dangerous presence is closing in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've found a note belonging to someone called the Tempest.

speaker: Darius
en: You know this name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you know?

speaker: Kleta
en: Everyone in Achaia knows the Tempest. She's the most ruthless commander to ever sail the Aegean. No one's faced her and lived. And her rage... Poseidon himself fears her. I house those who can't escape the Tempest's wrath in my village. But they can't stay here forever. The harbor is closed. Soldiers are combing the area, looking... I'm working on a plan to get them out of Achaia.

speaker: Kleta
en: If you can help, misthios, come find me in Boura.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She knows more than she's saying.

speaker: Darius
en: It doesn't matter. The Order is here. Amorges and the rest will not forgive our actions in Makedonia. Amorges will not forget the Huntsman's death at the hand of a Tainted One. His cunning

speaker: Darius
en: is sharper than any blade. He may already be here, observing us. Learning from our movements, from our choices, discovering our weaknesses...

speaker: Natakas
en: The stranded people come from both foreign lands and all over the Greek world—merchants, farmers, sailors, families... They are being imprisoned and interrogated. They are being asked about Makedonia. These people are suffering because the Order is looking for us.

speaker: Natakas
en: These people need our help—we have to do something. Isn't this what we're fighting for? Aren't they worth the risk?

speaker: Darius
en: We can't save them.

speaker: Darius
en: Not if the Tempest is still strong. We need to hit her hard—it's the only way to get the stranded people home.

speaker: Natakas
en: We should get started.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where will you start?

speaker: Natakas
en: Patrai is overflowing with the Tempest's forces. I'll look for leads there about the closed harbor, and maybe more about the Tempest herself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That woman, Kleta...

speaker: Darius
en: There's more to the Tempest's tale than she's telling. But... she needs help. The people in Boura need help. They could do with someone like you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then I'll pay her a visit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your father sure knows how to make an exit. Where did he go?

speaker: Natakas
en: He's been following up on some leads in Patrai. Look for him in the hull of a ship near the Patrai harbor—he's made a small hideout there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Against the three of us, the Tempest doesn't stand a chance. We'll break her

speaker: Kassandra
en: And then you'll be free to leave the Greek world forever.

speaker: Natakas
en: I'll go to the harbor and track down the Tempest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She can't be the only Order member in Achaia. I'll keep an eye out for the others.

speaker: Natakas
en: See you soon, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could find Darius and Natakas in Patrai... Or I could look for Kleta in Boura.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The seas are treacherous around Keos. We should be careful.

speaker: Herodotos
en: What? Charybdis and Skylla await at the bottom of the sea, I suppose?

speaker: Barnabas
en: No. Pirates. A lot of them.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Huh. Only pirates?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, I don't see any soldiers here. Only pirates. They must be running the whole island.

speaker: Soldier
en: Gods have mercy!

speaker: Xenia
en: You—want—mercy?

speaker: Xenia
en: Those who trade in slaves anywhere on my island will be marked as slaves themselves...

speaker: Xenia
en: ...Then hauled to Attika and fed to the system they tried to profit from.

speaker: Xenia
en: Get this scum out of my sight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought all pirates were slavers.

speaker: Xenia
en: And you are?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My name is Kassandra.

speaker: Xenia
en: Well, Kassandra, we're all thought to be murderers too. So, tell me why I shouldn't kill you right here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was told you're a trader of information.

speaker: Xenia
en: Among other things, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for someone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came to find the great pirate Xenia. That's you, isn't it?

speaker: Xenia
en: I like the sound of that, but what was your plan once you found me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came to offer you a deal.

speaker: Xenia
en: Entering my city and killing my followers is a strange way to strike a deal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't think they'd let me just walk in, and I don't have time to waste.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I butchered several of your "men" to get here. What makes you think you'd fare any better?

speaker: Xenia
en: You are a bold one. I like that, but don't think your words scare me, girl. There's a fine line between confidence and disrespect.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lucky for both of us, I didn't come looking for a fight.

speaker: Xenia
en: Sneaking into my city is a strange way to make a first impression.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I needed to speak with you directly. I didn't think your pirates would just let me walk up and knock.

speaker: Xenia
en: Then speak.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for a woman. She left Sparta when I was a child.

speaker: Xenia
en: I'll need more than that, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She has birthmarks on her arm that form the constellation Aquila.

speaker: Xenia
en: Now that is something I can work with. Just who exactly is this woman?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's my mother. I haven't seen her since I was a child.

speaker: Xenia
en: So, you're on a quest to find your family.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something like that.

speaker: Xenia
en: Then your path is not an easy one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't matter who she is to me.

speaker: Xenia
en: Maybe not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's a criminal who fled Sparta many years ago. I was hired to bring her back.

speaker: Xenia
en: I see. So, she's dangerous?

speaker: Kassandra
en: To you, I don't think anyone is dangerous.

speaker: Xenia
en: If only that were true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspasia's the one who sent me to find you.

speaker: Xenia
en: Aspasia? Now why would she do that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She said you might have information that could help me in my search.

speaker: Xenia
en: You can have anything for the right price.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what is that price?

speaker: Xenia
en: Considering you butchered a few of my people, I feel like compensation is in order.

speaker: Xenia
en: One you can afford, I'm sure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you need so much drachmae?

speaker: Xenia
en: I have a city to secure and people to protect. I have no interest in going to war—I just want to make sure the war doesn't come to us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have that kind of drachmae.

speaker: Xenia
en: I find that surprising, given your profession.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What proof do I have that you'll even find her?

speaker: Xenia
en: I already know Myrrine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know that name?

speaker: Xenia
en: That's not all I know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Getting that much drachmae won't be easy.

speaker: Xenia
en: You have a ship and a crew. That's enough to find work here in Koressia. And there's a stockpile of drachmae held in the fort on the far side of the island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to steal from your island?

speaker: Xenia
en: The other locals aren't too happy about us pirates. Their leader has amassed a fortune. If they have no drachmae, they can't do anything stupid.

speaker: Xenia
en: Don't worry. As long as you're working for me, you're one of us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have the drachmae yet, but I'll return when I do.

speaker: Xenia
en: There's no rush on my part. If you need work, check with my people in the city. I'm sure they'd have use for a capable mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trust a pirate to only help for a boat-load of drachmae. If I'm going to pay her, I need to find some work on this island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It should be much easier to travel the island now that everyone won't try to kill me on sight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Xenia and her crew really destroyed the place. If they burn everything, how do they expect to keep the people quiet?

speaker: Xenia
en: The mighty not-Spartan returns!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, take it.

speaker: Xenia
en: A pleasure doing business.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, take your drachmae.

speaker: Xenia
en: Nothing feels better than a heavy purse filled with coin.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The information I need, how long will it take?

speaker: Xenia
en: I already have it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You do?

speaker: Xenia
en: Your "Myrrine" now sails under the name of Phoenix. She started as a member of my crew, but we parted ways not too long ago.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I'm leaving soon.

speaker: Xenia
en: Keos is your home.

speaker: Myrrine
en: But this isn't my true calling—my purpose.

speaker: Xenia
en: You might never find what you are looking for, Phoenix.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I can't stop until I do.

speaker: Xenia
en: You are a great pirate.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And you are an even greater friend. Don't forget me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know where she is now?

speaker: Xenia
en: She sailed southeast with her crew in search of a greater calling.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She was part of your crew?

speaker: Xenia
en: For a time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did she leave?

speaker: Xenia
en: Much too interested in the politics of war—a waste of a good pirate if you ask me. I haven't heard from her since she left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keos is a long way from Sparta. How did your paths cross?

speaker: Xenia
en: On the sea, long ago. In her, I saw a better life. In me, she found freedom. Together, we owned the waves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't believe she was a pirate.

speaker: Xenia
en: She's the kind of woman who, once she sets her mind to something, gets it done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. I...

speaker: Xenia
en: Home isn't a place, it's the people you're with. If you don't find what you're looking for, there's a place for you here. Good luck with your search.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoenix. There have to be people who know that name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka. There are Followers of Ares fanatics up ahead.

speaker: Fanatic #1
en: You ate the last piece?

speaker: Fanatic #2
en: There's some leg left over there. Maybe an ear?

speaker: Fanatic #1
en: I killed the man, I should get first pick.

speaker: Fanatic #2
en: Shut up and eat! It'll go bad. The rest of him's starting to smell.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He must've fallen off this cliff running away from the cannibals. Not a good way to go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who was he going to meet? I should find out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to talk to him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What was that all about?

speaker: Smuggler
en: The military suspects me of smuggling deserters from the warfront.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Okay, fine. They knew I was doing it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mm-hmm.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Argh, malákes guards. They hit like bricks. Did you see a man on your way here? Skinny sort of idiot, wearing army colors?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found a body near a cliff in the gulch. He had a note on him.

speaker: Smuggler
en: No, no, no! He can't be dead! We had the perfect plan to get him home to his wife. I promised her I wouldn't let him end up like the other deserters...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can't say I have.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Curses! I promised his wife I'd take him back to her in Kydonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you sure he ran away from the army, or from her?

speaker: Smuggler
en: The army. He's a dead man walking now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You must be close to him to risk your life to help. Or was he paying you a lot.

speaker: Smuggler
en: I-I did it for the girl.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Girl? What girl? His wife? There's always a girl, isn't there?

speaker: Smuggler
en: Look, he got drafted into the war— She wouldn't stop crying. And my specialty is making people disappear— In a... different way than you do. So, I decided to help them get back together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's rare to find a man with a good heart these days.

speaker: Smuggler
en: We've all got people we want to look out for. Need to look out for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, we do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You just want her for yourself.

speaker: Smuggler
en: That's not it! I mean, I have thought about it, but— Look, I just— I just... want to see her smile, all right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure you do.

speaker: Smuggler
en: We need to get to Isabel—I mean, the wife. If the guards came after me, she'll be in danger, too. Please go to her! I'll catch up when I can to take her to safety.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make sure she's safe. Where will I find her?

speaker: Smuggler
en: Follow the road to Kydonia! Her house will be on the left—look for the green cloth on the doorpost. Quickly! I'll catch up as soon as I can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Greek Soldier 1
en: She put up a real fight back there.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: We weren't suppose to kill her, you idiots. Now we'll have to explain ourselves to the captain.

speaker: Greek Soldier 3
en: She refused to spill the beans on her deserter of a husband. She got what she deserved.

speaker: Greek Soldier 2
en: Who in the gods' names are you?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It looks like she put up a good fight... but not good enough.

speaker: Smuggler
en: I saw the guards dead outside. Good job, misthios

speaker: Kassandra
en: They got to her before me. There was nothing I could do but avenge her.

speaker: Smuggler
en: She trusted me, misthios! All I wanted was to make her smile. But every time I tried... All I brought her was pain. ...It's all I ever do. I shouldn't have told her about my stupid plan to reunite her with her husband. I did this to her, didn't I?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, you didn't. Nobody wanted things to end like this—least of all you.

speaker: Civilian
en: Everything seemed okay when she smiled, you know? I didn't care who she was smiling at.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You did your best.

speaker: Civilian
en: No one's "best" is ever enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. No it's not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, this is your fault. If you hadn't made promises you couldn't keep, she would still be alive.

speaker: Smuggler
en: But she was heartbroken, misthios! What would you have had me do? Just sit idly by, and watch her waste away?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would have had you do nothing. She might've been sad, but at least she'd be alive.

speaker: Smuggler
en: I just didn't - didn't want to see her sad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now you can see her dead instead.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Take this.

speaker: Smuggler
en: I was going to give it to her when I helped them escape Kydonia. To get them through tough times. They won't need it anymore, and it's too heavy for me to bear. Take it as payment for your troubles. And leave me, please.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Isabel... I should've gotten here sooner. I'm sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here it is, the '! Now I can decode the messages. I will avenge you, Phidias. Rest assured of that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The scytale message told me to find a secret room in the stronghold in Lemnos... So that's where I should go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe if I press here...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone went to a lot of trouble to hide this.

speaker: Lagos
en: I knew you'd come find me sooner or later.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What tipped you off?

speaker: Lagos
en: You killed my soldiers. But— You helped my family when I couldn't. Even if we're apart, I know they're safe thanks to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's the least I could do.

speaker: Lagos
en: I know it was you who freed my family. They're safe thanks to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did what I had to—even with everyone in Arkadia trying to kill me.

speaker: Lagos
en: The world is so chaotic now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult made it that way.

speaker: Lagos
en: We're living in divided times. Sparta against Athens. Old against new.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you think the Cultists aren't stoking the flames on both sides?

speaker: Lagos
en: I've seen what they can do. What they're willing to do. I want what's best for Arkadia... I'll consider what you have to say.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's nothing to discuss. You're a Cultist, and that's all I need to know.

speaker: Lagos
en: I had no choice. Please!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not too late. Leave the Cult of Kosmos and join Brasidas.

speaker: Lagos
en: You consider me your ally today... How can I know you and Brasidas won't change your minds?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can work together against our common enemy. You deserve better than to live under the threat of the Cult.

speaker: Lagos
en: You sound like Brasidas when he was your age. You give me hope.

speaker: Lagos
en: The Cult gave me this. They said it was a sign of my devotion. Maybe you can use it against them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure I can find a way.

speaker: Lagos
en: I'll lift the bounty on you and Myrrine. And may you find success in your fight against this evil.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, Archon. We appreciate it.

speaker: Lagos
en: You saved my family from the Cult by yourself... You're courageous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why?

speaker: Lagos
en: You've made an enemy of a king. Pausanias threatened my family with torture and death if I betrayed him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pausanias?! Do you have proof?

speaker: Lagos
en: Here—evidence of his treachery.

speaker: The Ring of Pausanias
en: Recognizable by the lion's head engraving in its bezel, this signet ring was used by the Spartan king to seal official documents.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. I'll see about this king of lies.

speaker: Lagos
en: You expect me to trust you? After how you slaughtered the Monger? I know what you do to Cultists. I won't bow my head just for you to cut it off.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That wasn't my plan.

speaker: Lagos
en: Then I should thank you for letting me face death as Spartans do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The bounty is lifted—Lagos is alive.

speaker: Brasidas
en: See? I knew we could solve this without violence.

speaker: Myrrine
en: That Cultist deserved to die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lagos is no longer with the Cult. I convinced him he's safer without them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lagos was a victim of the Cult. He shouldn't share their fate.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The Cult of Kosmos would eat their own young if it served their needs!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not Lagos. He was being blackmailed by King Pausanias. He had Lagos' family at knifepoint, and I have proof.

speaker: Brasidas
en: King Pausanias?! We must return to Sparta to confront him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. The kings were clear in their requests. Boeotia must be brought under control, and Sparta must win a wreath at the Olympic Games.

speaker: Myrrine
en: There is much left to do, lamb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We may have won the wreath, but the kings also wanted us to conquer the Boeotians.

speaker: Myrrine
en: True, you are needed there before we return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Boeotia may be at peace, but the kings also wanted an Olympic victory for Sparta.

speaker: Myrrine
en: True, you must travel to Elis and win the wreath.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right. we've done all we can. It's time to go to Sparta.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Yes. It's time we returned.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Very well. I'll take my leave of you, Kassandra. I won't soon forget your good work here.

speaker: Brasidas
en: It was good to see you again, Myrrine. Though we had our disagreements, I do hope you regain your house soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's dead.

speaker: Brasidas
en: This complicates things.

speaker: Myrrine
en: One less Cultist. Seems simple enough.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Lagos was a dear friend once. I should have been there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, Brasidas. But when Lagos joined the Cult, he sealed his fate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Should have been there? Brasidas, that man stopped deserving your loyalty the moment he joined the cult.

speaker: Brasidas
en: If only you'd followed my advice with Lagos like you did with the Monger.

speaker: Brasidas
en: So you executed the Monger in public against my advice, and now you kill Lagos? If you were under my command—you wouldn't be, anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't follow orders. I do what I have to.

speaker: Brasidas
en: So it's done. I suppose you'll be wanting to report the news to Sparta soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. The kings were clear in their requests. Boeotia must be brought under control, and Sparta must win a wreath at the Olympic Games.

speaker: Myrrine
en: There is much left to do, lamb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We may have won the wreath, but the kings also wanted us to conquer the Boeotians.

speaker: Myrrine
en: True, you are needed there before we return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Boeotia may be at peace, but the kings also wanted an Olympic victory for Sparta.

speaker: Myrrine
en: True, you must travel to Elis and win the wreath.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right. we've done all we can. It's time to go to Sparta.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Yes. It's time we returned.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Myrrine. You are as determined as ever. I'm sure you will regain your house soon.

speaker: Brasidas
en: With Lagos dead, arrangements must be made to ensure Sparta doesn't starve.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Arkadia is safe once more.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And the bounty is lifted. We are free to travel without fear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then let's continue our journey.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: This woman has disrespected the gods and shown contempt for tradition.

speaker: Civilian
en: Shame! Shame!

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Please, I only want to see my son compete.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: You mean you wanted to gaze lustfully upon the bodies of the athletes!

speaker: Kallipateira
en: No, I swear!

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: You have dishonored yourself and the Games.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Please, let me explain.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: No excuses. You know the price for your transgression.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What crime has this woman committed?

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: Exactly that—her crime is that she is a woman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's news to me that's now a crime. Shouldn't you lock yourself up first, then?

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: I am the Priestess of Demeter—I preside over the Games. She's a married woman who tried to watch them. Disguised as a man, no less!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And why is any of this a crime?

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: For a married woman, there's too much... temptation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are you?

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Kallipateira. I just wanted to see my son compete. My family has a proud lineage at the Olympic Games—my father, brothers, nephew, and son have all won . Do I not have the right to see them?

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: Enough of your lies!

speaker: Kassandra
en: She doesn't deserve to be punished like this.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: This is nothing! Death is the punishment. She shall be thrown from the mountain.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Help me—prove I have a right to see my son compete.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: You have no right. You broke a sacred tradition, and for that you will be punished.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your laws are wrong, and I'll prove it.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: As you're so outspoken in her defense, I will give you a chance. Present me evidence of Kallipateira's noble heritage—or she will die as she ruled, to appease the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not my place to interfere.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Please help me! Prove that I had the right to see my son in the Games.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should find Kallipateira's son, he should be able to help prove his mater's innocence.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: Well? Your "proof"?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find something to prove her innocence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know Kallipateira?

speaker: Civilian
en: I don't know her well, but she dotes on her son—and she's always making offerings.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Offerings?

speaker: Civilian
en: For her husband. She's a pious woman. He's long since crossed the Styx, and she misses him terribly... But we all have our time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. You've been a great help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know Kallipateira?

speaker: Civilian
en: I seen that one, all right. Always hanging round the athletes' tents. Disgraceful, if you know what I mean.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure I do.

speaker: Civilian
en: All those young, oiled, rippling bodies. Gives you shivers. Muscles everywhere! Ahem, disgusting it is, and her a married woman and all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no harm in looking at an attractive man, is there?

speaker: Civilian
en: Yes, yes there is! You young ones, always thinking with what's between your legs, and she definitely was. Saw her meet a man regularly on that bench over there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You saw her meet a man? Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for Kallipateira's son. Do you know him?

speaker: Peisirrhodos
en: I should hope so—it's me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your mother told me you're competing in the Olympics.

speaker: Peisirrhodos
en: Just like my grandfather, the great Diagoras himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's good to know, but I need more. The Priestess of Demeter has accused your mother of sacrilege.

speaker: Peisirrhodos
en: Is she alright? What happened?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your mother has been accused of impiety.

speaker: Peisirrhodos
en: What! What's going on? What happened?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Please, calm down.

speaker: Peisirrhodos
en: Calm down! Do you know what they'll do to her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's fine for now. She snuck into the stadium to watch you, and I need to prove that she had a right to do it.

speaker: Peisirrhodos
en: If anyone did, it was mater. Her brothers were champions, as I am now. No one honors the Olympics like her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. Sit tight, and I'll prove your mother was in her right to attend the Games.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, the poem Diagoras of Rhodes... Dedicated by Pindar himself... To K, always be proud, little one. Your father is the greatest of pankration champions.

speaker: Anonymous Love Letter
en: I have always longed for you, though your eyes do not speak the same language as my heart. Your devotion is an aspiration, and how I wish to comfort you, though I know it will never be—My sweet, sweet K.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this? "I have always longed for you..." Kallipateira has an admirer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That priestess was in a hurry to carry out her sentence on Kallipateira. I should find them quickly.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: You fool, you've doomed me and yourself! You've broken the sacred truce of Olympia!

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: We are gathered here today to carry out the will of the gods. To carry out justice.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Please, you must believe me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait!

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: You found the evidence you were looking for?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. Kallipateira is the daughter of Diagoras. I found the poem of Diagoras of Rhodes dedicated to the family by Pindar.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: And this proves her story?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I talked to her son and people who know her. She is a good woman who loves the Games and respects the gods. Her family has turned out champions for three generations.

speaker: Priest
en: Perhaps we have judged her too harshly. Her family has been a credit to the Olympic legacy.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: As you say, it would be a shame to tarnish such a proud family name.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: The gods forgive you. Go.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: Thank you, thank you.

speaker: Kallipateira
en: And thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nobody deserves such a fate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There isn't enough evidence to prove her innocence. In fact, I even found some to the contrary.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: Then justice must be served.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: For your time in this matter, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need more time. I'm sure I can convince you.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: You've had enough time. She was caught. She is guilty. The gods demand justice.

speaker: Priestess of Demeter
en: The gods are appeased.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, this is Kallisto the Bear!

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast Slayer, I'm glad to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The pelt from Kallisto the Bear.

speaker: Daphnae
en: I wish I'd had the chance to see this creature in the wild. It must have been stunning.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was, but there are other things on this earth far more beautiful.

speaker: Daphnae
en: And wild?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If not, then where would the challenge be in pursuing it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was too busy trying to survive to wonder at the majesty of nature.

speaker: Daphnae
en: A pity...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've found the final stele pieces. All of the armor has been found as well.

speaker: Eppie
en: I can hardly contain myself. This will be life-changing, hero! Primordial gods, worth, inner vision! What can it all mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll know soon enough, when you finish translating.

speaker: Eppie
en: Yes! You're right. The stele needs to be assembled. Come!

speaker: Eppie
en: This is the cusp of a great discovery. Will the gods speak to us? What will I say to them? What will they say to me? Does it matter?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perhaps when you read it...

speaker: Eppie
en: Yes, yes! Hmm... Only those who possess inner vision, a gift of the primordial gods, will be deemed worth to wield power of the Great . Dipsioi? What do you make of that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am amazed.

speaker: Eppie
en: I don't understand. There's no change that I see. It's the same place as when we first arrived.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look around you.

speaker: Eppie
en: I see nothing. What do you see?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing's happening. It's only dust in my eyes.

speaker: Eppie
en: Really? We are a pair, aren't we? I feel ashamed to think that I was hoping for more. Knowledge is reward enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the idea.

speaker: Eppie
en: At least I have this discovery. But you, misthios, all you have is the armor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's good armor. You know, Eppie? I think maybe you should continue on your journey.

speaker: Eppie
en: Should I? Hmm. Well, there are other clues to follow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would like you to join my crew.

speaker: Eppie
en: Really! Will it require swimming? Because you know I can't swim. And what about horses? I don't think my backside can take it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll figure something out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Take care, Eppie. I'm sure our paths will cross again.

speaker: Eppie
en: I hope so. Especially if I'm being attacked by something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The room has come to life. The gods are speaking to us.

speaker: Eppie
en: How can that be? Why can't I see any of this? Why should the gods not present themselves to me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I promise you, I have no idea.

speaker: Eppie
en: Is it because I'm not worthy? Do you have inner vision? It isn't fair.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eppie, you have the tomb. And there will be other discoveries.

speaker: Eppie
en: Enough. Just leave me. Can you please leave?

speaker: Eppie
en: I don't understand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't meant for you.

speaker: Eppie
en: Who are you to decide?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It isn't my decision. But I know that neither of us can know what the gods want with us.

speaker: Eppie
en: I have value, too!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Calm yourself. I have no control over this. You have your discovery. That should satisfy you.

speaker: Eppie
en: Why not me? It isn't fair.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Your death will bring me great fortune, Eagle Bearer. I'll name my new villa after you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Too bad you'll never see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Mercenary knew nothing. He never made it inside the lair.

speaker: Bryce
en: Then it was a waste of time! Ligeia waits, and we've done nothing to help her!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not exactly—the Mercenary carried this spear, which he claims killed the Writhing Dread.

speaker: Bryce
en: No, no, the Creature took Ligeia! It can't be dead—it awaits in its lair, even now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then there may be a piece of this puzzle we don't yet understand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found the Mercenary. Just another man obsessed with his spear.

speaker: Bryce
en: Aren't they all?

speaker: Bryce
en: Well? What else did the Mercenary know? How do we get inside to save Ligeia and kill the Creature?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't question him very thoroughly. ...Or take his spear.

speaker: Bryce
en: Then who knows what vital clue you may have missed?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It might be worth returning to see what he knows...

speaker: Bryce
en: Have you found a way inside the lair?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ligeia's story was true. The Daughters of Artemis were protecting this... Disk... Key? This

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have what opens the lair.

speaker: Bryce
en: And... You didn't hurt any of the Daughters when you took it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They didn't hear me or my blades... but they felt them, Bryce.

speaker: Bryce
en: Why?! Why would you

speaker: Kassandra
en: This disk is a prized possession—if I hadn't killed them, I never would have made it out alive, and Ligeia would be lost.

speaker: Bryce
en: I—I suppose you did what you had to. Ligeia's worth any price.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was no need for violence. The Daughters of Artemis didn't even know I was there.

speaker: Bryce
en: Then Tyche truly is on our side. Ligeia still stands a chance.

speaker: Bryce
en: Then what are you waiting for? Use the disk! Open the door!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no time for the Mercenary. Whatever he knows/ we'll find out ourselves. We're opening that door, now.

speaker: Bryce
en: You have Ligeia's heart, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...No. I'm not walking in there without talking to the Mercenary first. He might know something we could use.

speaker: Bryce
en: He might know how not to be a coward! Kassandra, Ligeia needs us now! Open the door. Open it!

speaker: Bryce
en: The cowardly misthios! What terribly important items might you need now, before you keep your promise to save my lover?

speaker: Bryce
en: Did you find anything, coward?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found the Mercenary's spear. He says it was made for the slaying of mythical beasts.

speaker: Bryce
en: Then let the slaying begin.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: Your shield, General.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: I'll never forget the day this was first handed to me. I was a boy, it was as tall as I was. My commander told me, "To hold this is to hold up Sparta. Drop it, and Sparta falls."

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: Tell me what Elysium is like.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: It isn't what you think.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: It's... Do you feel cold?

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Elysium is boring.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: Not since I showed up.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Ah yes. You do have a knack for livening things up wherever you go.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Still dreaming of paradise I see. Well, no one wants you to get what you deserve more than me.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: I'm glad you two have found each other. We could all use a little help from time to time. Well, you've got your shield. Are you ready to face your enemy?

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: I am.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't look, Brasidas. Hades is trying to get to you.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Deimos
en: It's been a long time, Brasidas. Come, face your undoing.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: I am not afraid of you, Deimos.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: What is this?

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Bane of Brasidas
en: An even greater enemy defeated you long before Deimos ended your life. Deimos was blessed by the fury of the gods, and even after he cut you down once, you still didn't learn.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: It wasn't hubris – I fought for honor.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen, Brasidas. It was hubris. Don't make this mistake a third time.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: As Spartans... I should have known. We live together, train together...

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: You made Sparta proud that day, Brasidas. You honored your father's oath.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: Perhaps I didn't. A Spartan should trust the warrior at their side.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: This time we fight together.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: It would be my honor.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: It was good fighting together again.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: I guess it's time to say goodbye.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Very good. The spears were my brother's idea. Poseidon can be cruel sometimes.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: I did as you asked. you promised me Elysium.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Hmm, not quite.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Brasidas
en: But you said

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: I said that to walk Elysium in death, the son of Sparta must confront that which defeated him in life. And you have not yet done so.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: I know, I know, It's all very hard to wrap your little mortal minds around. Which is why I'm going to help you.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: Why these games? Why not just let him go?

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Because eternity is long. Letting you go wouldn't be much fun, now would it?

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: Find the Forest of Oizys. The dead will point the way.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: The Forest of Oizys, sounds inviting.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: It's where I keep the miserable humans who ended their mortal suffering by their own hand.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: If there's one thing I hate, it's uninvited guests.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: The dead will point the way to what?

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Hades
en: I wouldn't want to spoil the surprise. You'll just have to trust me.

scene: Kill Me Once, Shame on You
speaker: Kassandra
en: Come Brasidas, the sooner we get this done, the sooner you can be free of this place.
