speaker: Kassandra
en: Can I be of service, priestess? You left a message on the board. What's the matter? What can I do to serve the gods today, priestess?

speaker: Woman
en: Oh good, it's you. The gods must have heard my prayers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here I am. Gods' blessing and all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't believe everything you hear. I'm just a mercenary, lady.

speaker: Woman
en: I heard of your kindness towards Hippokrates, and how you helped him with his errands. I have something I could use your help with, too, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what would that be?

speaker: Woman
en: Religious fanatics have been stealing valuables from my temple in protest of my work with Hippokrates. These thieves need to be dealt with before the situation gets worse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to kill every last one of them.

speaker: Woman
en: All the bandits must die. Do we have an agreement?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'll do it.

speaker: Woman
en: By Zeus, that's a relief.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: The gods thank you, and so do I. Take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Brasidas
en: There you are. I can take you in to see the kings when you're ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do I need to know before I go in?

speaker: Brasidas
en: That's right. You've never had an audience with the two kings.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've met Pausanias.

speaker: Brasidas
en: King Pausanias. Really.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Kings Pausanias and Archidamos share rulership. Impress them both, and your home will be returned to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't expect this to be pleasant.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about Pausanias?

speaker: Brasidas
en: He's young. Don't mistake his smile for kindness—as with all kings, those who cross him learn to regret it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What should I know about Archidamos?

speaker: Brasidas
en: Archidamos is... a traditionalist. Not one to back down from a fight. He's also got a temper. Try to stay on his good side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Waiting won't make this easier.

speaker: Brasidas
en: They won't look kindly on you asking for favors without offering some kind of help first, like taking care of the soldiers arming the helots.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm tired of doing people favors. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Come on then. Your mother's waiting inside.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Then let's go. Your mother's already inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are the kings?

speaker: Brasidas
en: There.

speaker: Archidamos
en: What do you say now?

speaker: Pausanias
en: You made your point, Archidamos. I yield.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Another two squadrons to Boeotia, then. As I said.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is that how they solve arguments?

speaker: Brasidas
en: Sometimes.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Archidamos' guard has improved. He should thank me.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Brasidas! You've come with news. Let's hear it.

speaker: Brasidas
en: My kings, may I present Myrrine, descendant of Leonidas, and her daughter Kassandra.

speaker: Archidamos
en: I heard you'd come back. How dare you step foot on Spartan soil?! I should cut it off for what you did.

speaker: Brasidas
en: They helped us secure Korinthia, my king. I beg you to listen.

speaker: Pausanias
en: They are descendants of Leonidas. For that reason alone they should be allowed to speak. And if we don't like what they have to say, you can chop off any limb you see fit.

speaker: Archidamos
en: How dare you show your face in Sparta.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Kassandra helped me secure Korinthia, my king. She helped with the helot rebellion. They want what's best for Sparta. I beg you to listen.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Let's hear what they have to say before we bloody the palace floor.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Speak, Myrrine. Why are you here?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I have returned to reclaim my Spartan citizenship. To reclaim our home.

speaker: Archidamos
en: You exiled yourself. Your daughter killed an elder and ran.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Not to mention the crooked nose she gave you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: My family was betrayed, my king. Sparta was betrayed. We've come to expose these traitors.

speaker: Archidamos
en: You haven't cared for Sparta for many years.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your elders had both her children thrown off a cliff! They tore our whole family apart.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra, not here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: But the minute she thought Sparta was in danger, she came back. She brought us both back to help. How dare you accuse her of not caring!

speaker: Archidamos
en: I've heard your grandfather couldn't control his temper either.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then blame me. I killed the elder. I started all of this. So if you want someone to prove their loyalty, it should be me.

speaker: Archidamos
en: I'm not sure if I should congratulate you on your honesty or punish you for the crime you've just confessed.

speaker: Myrrine
en: What you say is true. But I swear by the two gods my intentions are pure.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Myrrine has made her intentions known. What are yours?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My intentions are to hunt down those who betrayed my family and Sparta. And kill them.

speaker: Archidamos
en: And who exactly do you think betrayed Sparta?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's what I'm here to find out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My intentions are to return home. Here. Where I was born.

speaker: Archidamos
en: What happened on Taygetos brought shame on Sparta. You and your family have no home here.

speaker: Pausanias
en: First, prove yourself loyal. Bring glory to Sparta, and redeem yourself in the eyes of the gods. Until then, neither you, nor your mother, have a right to your lands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what I must do, and it will be done.

speaker: Archidamos
en: The Spartan army fights the Athenians in Boeotia. Join the commanders there. Come back victorious, or do not return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You expect me to win a war when your own troops can't?

speaker: Archidamos
en: My troops will crush any army under Helios. And if you want your home back you'll go to Boeotia and mind your tongue.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Good, you're learning.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Consider the battle won.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Spoken with the confidence of a child who hasn't seen real war.

speaker: Archidamos
en: You will find my commander at Mt. Helicon. Give him this and tell him I sent you.

speaker: Spartan Royal Edict
en: The mortal who carries this edict acts on behalf of King Archidamos of Sparta. May their shield defend Sparta's interests, and may their blade run through her enemies.

speaker: Pausanias
en: Not so fast. Two kings. Two tasks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what would you have me do? Conquer the rest of the world?

speaker: Pausanias
en: I'd leave the conquering to Archidamos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herakles completed twelve. Two shouldn't be a problem.

speaker: Archidamos
en: First Spartan thing you've said all day.

speaker: Pausanias
en: The Olympics will be starting soon in Elis, and our fighting champion requires an escort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to be an escort?

speaker: Pausanias
en: I want you to make sure the Spartans return with a wreath.

speaker: Archidamos
en: That's how she'll bring glory to Sparta? By winning an event in the Olympics?

speaker: Pausanias
en: Not an event, my king. By making sure Sparta wins the entire Olympics.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perfect.

speaker: Archidamos
en: One last thing. When you come asking a favor, it's customary to bring a gift. But you didn't. So now, I will choose your gift for you. A wolf has been attacking farmers on the Dioskouroi Peninsula. People say it's King Lycaon himself, cursed by Zeus to live out his days as a wolf.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will kill this animal and bring you its head.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your reports are out of date. I killed the wolf some time ago.

speaker: Pausanias
en: She follows orders swiftly.

speaker: Archidamos
en: We'll see if that's true when you get to Boeotia.

speaker: Pausanias
en: You have your orders. We'll see you when your tasks are completed.

speaker: Archidamos
en: If they're completed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get them done, and you'll give us back our home.

speaker: Pausanias
en: There's some Spartan left in you after all.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Brasidas, show them out.

speaker: Archidamos
en: Next?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That went well.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Considering you still have a head on your shoulders, yes I'd say it went very well.

speaker: Myrrine
en: The kings were generous to give us a second chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And all I have to do is win the Olympics.

speaker: Myrrine
en: And a war.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Is there anything you need to know before setting off?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on in Boeotia?

speaker: Brasidas
en: The Athenian army is pushing Sparta back bit by bit. Winning won't be easy.

speaker: Myrrine
en: If anyone can turn the tide there, it's you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you know about this fighting champion I'm supposed to take to the Olympics?

speaker: Brasidas
en: The pankration fighter. His trainer will know where he is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My thanks.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Things are not quite what they seem. But you must keep this champion safe at all costs to succeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about this wolf. It's under a curse?

speaker: Brasidas
en: It's causing a lot of trouble on the Dioskouroi Peninsula. You'll be doing the people there a favor if you get rid of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find it?

speaker: Brasidas
en: I'd start near Diros Cave. That's where it was last seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of the kings is a Cultist... so one of these tasks is surely a trap. But which one?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Brasidas?

speaker: Brasidas
en: Wouldn't say that within earshot of the palace. But I've fought with both of them. I can't believe either is a traitor.

speaker: Myrrine
en: We need to find proof before we make any accusations. Keep your eyes open.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I'm ready. And you? What will you do while I'm gone?

speaker: Myrrine
en: I received a message just before we went in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of message?

speaker: Myrrine
en: A clue to the whereabouts of another Cultist. I'm going to Arkadia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alone?

speaker: Brasidas
en: The fates are smiling on us. I was ordered there. We can travel together.

speaker: Myrrine
en: That would be helpful. My thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll meet you both in Arkadia, then. Safe journeys.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Sparta has missed you.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I know you do what's right in your heart, but you have to put your family first, lamb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There they are!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is!

speaker: Mercenary
en: The Tempest demands your head, Eagle Bearer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: She'll have yours instead.

speaker: Mercenary Correspondence
en: We'll cover Boura. Aias will work with the soldiers and their Polemarch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's over there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another one of the Tempest's hired hands.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Your death will bring me great fortune, Eagle Bearer. I'll name my new villa after you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Too bad you'll never see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This mercenary was sent by the Tempest. He won't be the last.

speaker: Kassandra
en: More mercenaries sent by the Tempest. Must be some bounty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Tempest will run out of mercenaries eventually.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should be the last of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. I'll kill more for you.

speaker: Lysander
en: My soldiers think me bloodthirsty. I know the cost of war. Neither side will be clean of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your plan is working.

speaker: Lysander
en: And the Athenian think me battle shy!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That makes you happy?

speaker: Lysander
en: I held my army back, so they dropped their guard. And then we ran them aground.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I take it the war is going well for you, then?

speaker: Lysander
en: Enough questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What will you do if you win?

speaker: Lysander
en: Enough talk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. I won't ask any more questions.

speaker: Lysander
en: Tell me then, Eagle Bearer, you must be pleased with our progress.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As you said, tactics will win this.

speaker: Lysander
en: When this is over, I'll try my hand at politics.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure it'll suit you.

speaker: Lysander
en: Go then, kill the enemy command. This is our war to win.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do it, General.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have the seals. Spartan troops have the outpost.

speaker: Lysander
en: While you were gone, I oversaw the capture of three thousand. Yet still my men suck their thumbs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Three thousand prisoners?

speaker: Lysander
en: Not anymore. They've been executed. Do you disapprove?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They'd do it to us.

speaker: Lysander
en: So we understand one another then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perfectly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Our actions live on long after we're dead.

speaker: Lysander
en: Don't you dare lecture me, Eagle Bearer. The gods approve of my actions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then I'll leave you to the gods.

speaker: Lysander
en: Your Spartan blood boils, does it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: These seals should provide you ample proof.

speaker: Lysander
en: My command on the battlefield has been more than secured.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're welcome.

speaker: Lysander
en: We're well-positioned for battle. Troops have been deployed and will control more ground soon. Your efforts were invaluable. I won't forget it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, General.

speaker: Kyra
en: Don't exactly blend in, do you?

speaker: Kyra
en: Kassandra! I'm glad you came.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad you didn't throw another blade at me.

speaker: Kyra
en: I know, I know. You came all this way, and I was cruel to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you?

speaker: Kyra
en: I lost my temper in the cave. I'm sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: First you throw a dagger at me, then you storm out. I'm starting to take it personally.

speaker: Kyra
en: I know, I know. I feel terrible. You came all this way, and I've been nothing but cruel.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, you weren't the first, and you won't be the last.

speaker: Kyra
en: Delians are kind people. At least we were. Before... him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes, and others like him, want me and my family dead.

speaker: Kyra
en: He executed my family when I was very little. I survived on the streets. Was raised by hunters, rogue warriors, and mercenaries like you. They are my family now.

speaker: Kyra
en: And one day I will fire an arrow into his black heart—one for every Delian family he's destroyed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then why have you let him live this long?

speaker: Kyra
en: Let him live? Let him live? I've been trying to kill him since I was old enough to draw a bow! But that coward hides behind endless shields, and this the closest I can get without people dying.

speaker: Kyra
en: This is why I sent for you.

speaker: Kyra
en: To help me get close enough to fire an arrow into Podarkes's black heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean your father.

speaker: Kyra
en: I was raised by hunters, rogue warriors, mercenaries. They are my true family. That man is nothing to me.

speaker: Kyra
en: And one day I will fire an arrow into his black heart—one for every Delian family he's destroyed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It isn't your fault that he's your father, Kyra. We can't choose our families.

speaker: Kyra
en: No. We can't choose them. But we can avenge them. And I will make him pay for what he did to my mater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then it's time we turn this predator into prey.

speaker: Kyra
en: How do we get past his guards?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Soldiers need two things to fight. Swords in their hands and food in their bellies. Take them away, and the guards fall.

speaker: Kyra
en: Scouts reported Podarkes's supplies and weapons were stockpiled in the old ruins on Delos Island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In the ruins on Delos? It's not much of a stockpile any more.

speaker: Kyra
en: What? Why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already been there.

speaker: Kyra
en: That's wonderful! And, did you make Podarkes feel our sting?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go to Delos, find their stockpiles, and destroy them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Kynthos Ruins. This is where I'll find Podarkes's weapons and supplies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A supply crate. Should destroy these without attracting attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes's troops will be helpless.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who knew rebelling was this much fun?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Break their supplies, break their will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The soldiers' weapons. Don't mind if I do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes thought he was clever hiding weapons on Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This should cripple Podarkes' defenses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should do it. Kyra will want to hear about this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Athenian wine. I'm sure Kyra would enjoy this. Come to think of it, so would I.

speaker: Kyra
en: Kassandra! You've returned in one piece!

speaker: Kyra
en: And? Is it done?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes' guards will have to fight with their fists and on empty stomachs from now on.

speaker: Kyra
en: Excellent!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I also found this.

speaker: Kyra
en: You sneaky, sneaky misthios. Athenian wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When all this is said and done, I thought we might share some.

speaker: Kyra
en: You surprise me. And to think I nearly threw my blade through your neck.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one's perfect.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what will you do once Podarkes is dead and the rebellion is won?

speaker: Kyra
en: The sad truth is I have no idea. For as long as I can remember, every day has been a struggle. To live, to laugh...

speaker: Kyra
en: Vengeance has all but consumed me.

speaker: Kyra
en: And what will Kassandra do one this is over?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your destiny is to free the people of Delos. I still have my own to fulfill, far from here.

speaker: Kyra
en: Of course. I will always remember what you've done for us. And if the gods will it, I can one day help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As long as there's war, there's always work for a misthios.

speaker: Kyra
en: You fight with such passion. I keep forgetting you're only here for the money.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We have a lot in common. I was hoping when the smoke clears, we could find somewhere quiet.

speaker: Kyra
en: And what exactly do we have in common?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know you've struggled to get where you are. You've had to fight and claw for everything you have. I know... because I've done the same.

speaker: Kyra
en: We're survivors. I'm glad the gods brought you to our shores, Kassandra. Some time alone would be nice. You must have many tales.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen you with a blade. You have a skill that could only come from the pleasures of battle.

speaker: Kyra
en: Podarkes and his troops force me into battle. I take no pleasure in it. My dreams are of peace, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just... We... I just thought that's what people said to each other. I wasn't expecting a follow up.

speaker: Kyra
en: The mighty Kassandra, caught off her guard!

speaker: Kyra
en: Relax. A moment together would be nice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's time we got going. When Podarkes learns of what happened on Delos, he'll want revenge.

speaker: Kyra
en: And the first to suffer will be the Delians.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Hades
en: Ah, Kassandra returns. Victory written across her face.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's your brother? Not here to settle any bets?

speaker: Hades
en: It's already been settled. He lost.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gates have their guardians, Charon's lost souls have found peace. Now, tell me what you know about the Staff.

speaker: Hades
en: I never promised you that. I promised to fulfill your destiny.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough games, Hades. I did as you asked. We had a deal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mastering the Staff is my destiny. And you're going to show me.

speaker: Hades
en: You were never in a position to bargain with me. Your life was mine the moment you killed Cerberos. I could have had anyone place guardians at those gates. Truth is, I needed you to grow accustomed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Hades
en: Oh, did I not mention? I have a fifth gate, and you're going to spend the rest of eternity protecting it. That is your destiny.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't bow to your wife, and I won't bow to you.

speaker: Hades
en: Oh, you'll fucking bow.

speaker: Hades
en: Shame it has to end this way. You'd have made an excellent addition to my dead hero collection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Collect this!

speaker: Hades
en: All you pathetic humans end up here eventually. Why fight it?

speaker: Hades
en: Last chance. Work for me or suffer forever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listening to you, I've suffered enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't see what's funny.

speaker: Hades
en: You act like any of this matters. But you're a prisoner wherever you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka!

speaker: Lacerated Leaders
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Lakonian Vessels
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Ancient Rusted Key
en: Though corroded, the key is heavy. Its roughly carved ring depicts a figure, hands raised as if in prayer. To which deities, one can't help but wonder...

speaker: Stele Piece from the Underwater Ruins
en: Seawater has worn the edges of this stele piece, but the etchings will still serve their purpose.

speaker: Ancient Wax Tablet
en: Among the faded markings, the tablet has a partial translation which reads thus: council of Elders... the dead ones. Curious. Was this a tribute of some kind? Has some ritual taken place here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your clue was right. I found a part of the stele. Along with another piece 'of armor.

speaker: Eppie
en: There must be a piece of armor with each missing stele.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But why?

speaker: Eppie
en: This section here refers to a ritual.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't explain why the armor was seperated and hidden with a stele piece.

speaker: Eppie
en: Maybe that was part of the ritual? We need to find the other stele pieces. Are you ready?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If we found these, then we'll find the other stele pieces too. I'll go look.

speaker: Eppie
en: Even with the full keystone in place, some of the meaning may be lost on us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have faith in you.

speaker: Eppie
en: Oh! You won't believe what this section says... "Of the primordial gods..." Primordial!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's interesting.

speaker: Eppie
en: That's ancient.

speaker: Kassandra
en: it could just be a prayer on behalf of the warrior.

speaker: Eppie
en: That's what I thought, too. Until I read this part...

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more?

speaker: Eppie
en: It mentions that the ritual will be activated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What ritual?

speaker: Eppie
en: I have no idea. I'm presuming it means we need all of the steles in place before something happens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you have the location for the missing piece?

speaker: Eppie
en: This text is hard to make sense of. It appears to be a warning. Be careful when you explore the Tomb of Orion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The has had its time. Why look backward?

speaker: Eppie
en: There is truth and insight in looking backward. Take Homer for example, he often spoke of our past in his stories.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. So digging through dirt and cobwebbed words is your ambition?

speaker: Eppie
en: My role is to breathe life into the ancients.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do any of your peers support you in this?

speaker: Eppie
en: None. My ways are too different for them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're right, you'll gain their respect after this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you worry that your expectations are too high? It may be a dead end.

speaker: Eppie
en: How can it? The clues have proven me right thus far. The stele mentions a ritual that once performed, will activate something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does that have to do with primordial gods?

speaker: Eppie
en: I have no idea. When we have all of the stele pieces. we'll know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I might. What would you like me to do?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: You've impressed me, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For a Spartan.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Yes, as you say. It seems our fleet is under attack, and I need to redirect the troops to help. I will ask you to take on the Spartan command again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The commanders will be taken care of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem to admire art and philosophy... But how can someone who truly values that go to war?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: If you have any care for knowledge or the arts, you must be ready to defend these rights. I am here to take up arms so that they can continue to enrich our culture. As long as they are threatened, battle must be fought.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You expect total obedience from your soldiers, I suppose. So why do you fight for democracy?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: What is free will? It's essential that citizens play an active role in the function of their state.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But Athens recognizes only select citizens. Spartans recognize merit. In Sparta, a slave can rise.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Spartan rule would mean the demise of democracy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll leave now.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Perhaps Athena was smiling down upon Athens when she sent you to me. You've far surpassed my expectations.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always aim to do a good job.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: You have. Beyond that, you've shown an understanding of war and its price. That's a lesson some never learn. This General Lysander, you know him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What Spartan doesn't?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: If he's as good as he seems, then I'm even more grateful for your help. I respect his reputation, if not the man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: War changes the rules for us all.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: So it does. Thank you, Eagle Bearer. I'm sure we'll meet again.

speaker: Lawless Hearts
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Leading Forces
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the whole hunting party?

speaker: Erykios
en: We're all Lalaia has to spare since the Sons of Xerxes killed our husbands and sons. You must be the misthios Periktione hired.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am.

speaker: Beroe
en: We may not be the big brutes you're used to, but we're versed in killing well enough.

speaker: Erykios
en: Well, we know how to fish.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a start.

speaker: Beroe
en: We're ready. Do you have everything you need?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. Get your bows and we'll go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about Lalaia.

speaker: Erykios
en: We've been blessed both by the waters of Kephisos and by Aphrodite herself, for she is the source of all beauty.

speaker: Beroe
en: All settlement needs to be near water. Ours just has a lot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you fish in the pools and river?

speaker: Erykios
en: Kephisos provides us with what we need.

speaker: Beroe
en: Not enough in there to provide for all of Lalaia. That's why we need you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With the Sons of Xerxes so close, is there less game around?

speaker: Erykios
en: We've been relying more on fish and fruit. It's enough for now.

speaker: Beroe
en: Animals don't scream and beg for mercy the way humans do. I doubt they interest the Sons of Xerxes as much.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're still food. Perhaps their numbers aren't as high as we think.

speaker: Beroe
en: They may not have enough archery to black out the sun with arrows, but they do have enough to fill every citizen of Lalaia with holes.

speaker: Erykios
en: Here we are. A great bear is said to live nearby.

speaker: Beroe
en: Don't mention the bear. I'm already regretting being here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: To shoot, you need to raise your elbow to be level with your ear, keeping your arm straight and relaxed. Your arrow needs to be just below your eye, then exhale on release. Try to aim for the eye so that you don't damage the rest of the meat.

speaker: Erykios
en: Thank you, misthios. I've learned much from the bow. Aphrodite may provide, but Artemis acts.

speaker: Beroe
en: Lalaia is such a beautiful place... I'm glad I can do my part to take care of it. Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should be enough to get you through the week. But, there's still much to be done for Lalaia.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Nothing like a sea breeze!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Does the deck always feel like it's moving?

speaker: Barnabas
en: I've got the perfect opportunity for you to get your sea legs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, what would that be?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Well, when the Cyclops was giving me a drumming, his pirates took my cargo. I know their ship, and I know where they're heading. What say we get it back?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure. It'll be a good opportunity to see how your ship and crew perform.

speaker: Barnabas
en: All right there, let's get moving! Let's see how the sails have held up.

speaker: Barnabas
en: There she is!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ram them from the side, and cleave that ship in two!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, statesman. I don't suppose you could use a mercenary's help today? / Need something, statesman?

speaker: Man
en: I'm losing everything. Not only was my brother Elpenor murdered, but my whole political career is about to disappear, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am the one who killed your brother.

speaker: Man
en: You? You bastard! You will pay for what you did to him! He was massacred! You deserve a fate worse than death.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what it's like to lose family. Toughest thing you'll ever face in your life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpenor? Can't say I've heard of him.

speaker: Man
en: Elpenor was a kind and wealthy man. He financed my love for politics and protected me from harm. And now that he's gone, I risk losing everything I have left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there something I can do?

speaker: Man
en: Ever since my brother disappeared, bandits have been attacking me. They're after the family fortune, and I'm left defenseless. If they take the money from me, then I can't continue my political career.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you're hoping I'll kill all the bandits?

speaker: Man
en: I beg you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'm in. / I'll handle this.

speaker: Man
en: Get this done quickly. / Thank you. Please be discreet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can leave everything to me.

speaker: Man
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Man
en: Excellent work, my friend. Please, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Greek Brute
en: Purple dye might stink like rotten dog guts, but I'll be fucked if doesn't make me look like a god!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Technically it's made from rotten snail guts, boss.

speaker: Greek Brute
en: ...I'm wearing snail guts?

speaker: Key to Olympos
en: Though it may look like an ordinary disk, it is allegedly the key to unlocking the gates of Olympos.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Ah, look how she strides! The confidence! If I didn't know better, I'd say there were two gods on Kythera!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found your disk.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Praise me! Clearly, I have worked through you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Clearly. Time to meet the gods, then?

speaker: Empedokles
en: I'd love to introduce you to my family—of course, if you're ready to join me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: First, I have other matters to attend to..

speaker: Empedokles
en: Matters more important than meeting the gods?! Your life must be a blessed adventure.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Praise Empedokles! Oh, oh praise him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This should be interesting.

speaker: Empedokles
en: That, my dear misthios, I can absolutely guarantee. A moment please, while I address my audience.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Rejoice! For I, your humble god, shall introduce you to my brothers and sisters. Athena awaits you! Ares demands your audience!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a big promise.

speaker: Empedokles
en: You doubt me?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I doubt you could get us to the ocean. It's behind you, by the way.

speaker: Empedokles
en: How dare you mock—I—I'm a god! A god!

speaker: Empedokles
en: What am I?!

speaker: Civilian
en: A—a god?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks for clearing that up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't doubt the joy you've brought to your followers.

speaker: Empedokles
en: Their loyalty will be rewarded. As will yours.

speaker: Empedokles
en: We set sail for the Gulf of Korinth, and all the secrets she veils! Meet us there and see the truth for yourself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And meet your siblings? Wouldn't miss it.

speaker: Empedokles
en: To the Gulf of Korinth, and all she hides, misthios!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Do you really think Empedokles is a God?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: I couldn't give a shit if he was a rooster - I'm just here to get away from the Priestesses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Amorges... Today you bleed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpidios... I'm almost there. My son... Maters coming.

speaker: Amorges
en: Calm, aren't they? Moments like these. The moments before the end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you've hurt my son... nothing will protect you. No man. No beast. No god.

speaker: Amorges
en: He's safe with me, Kassandra. Happy. Healthy. And I promise you, he always will be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is Elpidios? Where is my son?!

speaker: Amorges
en: Far from war, far from danger... far from you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Think about where we're going, Amorges. This path can only end in one place. Unless you tell me where to find my son.

speaker: Amorges
en: I'm sorry, Kassandra. I can't do that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I once swore to people I loved I would crush the Order. Believe me, I will keep that promise.

speaker: Amorges
en: You think you can destroy us? The Order's plan goes well beyond you, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What...?

speaker: Amorges
en: Ever the hero, thinking this is all about you. This isn't about any one of us—it's about that most precious of things... peace. This war between Athens and Sparta threatens to incinerate more than just the Greek world. The carnage and butchery have spread to Persia and beyond. The Order has the power to save the world... And so we will.

speaker: Amorges
en: My agents are rooted deeply in every aspect of Greek life. We have seeped into your establishments, your temples, your homes... We are winning the hearts of your people. Through the Order's influence and Persia's wealth, Sparta will end this war. A new chapter in history will be written by us. We have planted a seed in the fertile soil that is the Greek people, and now peace will grow. Only one threat to that peace remains... you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How could you think I'd—I don't want a war, I want my son!

speaker: Amorges
en: You don't want a war? You brought one to my door!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want a war, you monster? I'll give you a war.

speaker: Amorges
en: You already have.

speaker: Amorges
en: You're a Tainted One, the strongest, most dangerous force the Order has ever seen. You are fire. Only you stand in the way of the Order's purpose.

speaker: Darius
en: You've forgotten our promise, old friend.

speaker: Amorges
en: Artabanus! I wondered when you'd make your dramatic entrance.

speaker: Darius
en: Think of the innocent lives that were lost, Amorges. You claimed to want peace, but what good is peace when it's enforced by tyranny?

speaker: Amorges
en: I fought for the greater good, for our children, for their futures. I saved your grandson, and I saved Artaxerxes that night... Do you remember? I saved him from you.

speaker: Darius
en: Tell us where Elpidios is.

speaker: Amorges
en: I'm sorry. As long as I breathe, I will never endanger the child—By letting her raise him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is Elpidios? Tell me. Tell me!

speaker: Amorges
en: You cannot raise the boy. With you, he'll never be safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's my son!

speaker: Darius
en: Do you remember the truth I whispered in the ear of King Xerxes?

speaker: Amorges
en: Remind me, old friend!

speaker: Darius
en: For all the Order's power, they could not protect you—Not from me!

speaker: Darius
en: We must protect the people we love, Amorges.

speaker: Amorges
en: That's what I'm doing!

speaker: Darius
en: Where is the child?!

speaker: Amorges
en: In safer hands than yours, "Darius"!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Return my son, and your pain will end, Amorges!

speaker: Amorges
en: Never.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll kill every last one of you!

speaker: Amorges
en: There is no "last one of us," Kassandra. We're the waves. We're the ocean. The Order is endless!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Darius!

speaker: Amorges
en: The sun rises, but she also sets. My time is over, old friend.

speaker: Darius
en: We were protectors, Amorges. We were champions of Persia. Of the people!

speaker: Amorges
en: I still am, Artabanus. I only wanted to keep our home safe—the world safe.

speaker: Darius
en: The child, Amorges. Please.

speaker: Amorges
en: He's on a small island, just off the coast of Messenia. Perfect spot for fishing...

speaker: Amorges
en: The Order will never give up, Kassandra. You and your boy will always be hunted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And he'll always have me to protect him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know...

speaker: Amorges
en: The Order aren't just a group of people—they're an idea. An idea cannot be beaten. An idea cannot be destroyed.

speaker: Darius
en: Not by blades, but through knowledge, through wisdom... Through ideas of our own. Nothing is absolute, Amorges. You taught me that a long time ago.

speaker: Darius
en: "There will always be tyrants..."

speaker: Amorges
en: "And there will always be you, my brother... to stop them..."

speaker: Darius
en: Go in peace, old friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Amorges was true to his word... Elpidios will be there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater's coming...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just a moment more, Elpidios...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hold on... Just hold on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My boy, my son... My beautiful son. I'm here, Elpidios... Mater's here...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've kept watch over my son.

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day. Every night. Amorges made sure of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Unknown
en: You know... He has a real Spartan appetite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater's got so many stories to tell you

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you've got some stories for Mater too, I see...

speaker: Darius
en: Who are you?

speaker: Son of Artaxerxes
en: I am Darius. Son of the Persian king, Artaxerxes.

speaker: Darius
en: Artaxerxes...

speaker: Son of Artaxerxes
en: You know my father?

speaker: Darius
en: We've met... But it's been a while.

speaker: Son of Artaxerxes
en: He's a good king and a great father. Persia knows peace. She prospers. I miss him.

speaker: Darius
en: Keep Persia safe... That is his legacy.

speaker: Darius
en: It's time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just a moment longer.

speaker: Darius
en: It has to be now.

speaker: Darius
en: What will you do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Amorges was right—I am fire. I'll use that, a beacon to the Order. If they want to come after my bloodline, they'll know exactly where to find me... But they'll never find

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what will you do, Darius?

speaker: Darius
en: The Order was created for a purpose. If I can understand our enemy, I can outmaneuver them. I'll protect the boy, Kassandra—be a guardian to Elpidios and to all those who share his blood.

speaker: Darius
en: When the day comes, when he asks of his mater, what should I tell him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell him he had a mater and pater who lived incredible lives, who saw incredible things... and none of it was as incredible as him. His smile. His laugh. The sight of him asleep in my arms...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Should a day come where he feels unloved or alone, you tell him there is no such day—because he will always be loved.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You hear me? You will always be loved.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Elpidios comes looking for me, it might be the Order who find him. Tell him only that his parents are dead... But you are loved, Elpidios. You will always be loved.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll fight and you'll fall. There will be times when you'll think you can't rise again. You'll want to stay down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you will get up, Elpidios. Because you're strong. Because our bloodline is strong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And because we always get up. You'll ask why.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And while you'll never know me, know this—You are my son, and I'll always fight for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You, and those that will come after.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems like the training has paid off.

speaker: Roxana
en: I was about to say the same.

speaker: Drakios
en: Enough chatter. Our patrons demand a champion. Finish this!

speaker: Roxana
en: There's no escaping our fate, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can lay down our weapons. There's nothing more to prove.

speaker: Drakios
en: This is outrageous. Roxana—only one of you can win the Battle and become champion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We don't have to kill each other.

speaker: Drakios
en: Think of the riches, Roxana. Indeed, everything you've dreamed of is almost within your grasp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can walk away.

speaker: Drakios
en: Only one of you can walk away a legend.

speaker: Roxana
en: The stakes were clear from the beginning, Kassandra. Don't do this. I'm so close

speaker: Drakios
en: Enough! The Battle must end now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. Roxana, we decide how this ends. Not him.

speaker: Roxana
en: I'm beginning to think there are things more important than riches and glory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Join me on my ship. There are more adventures for us out on the Aegean.

speaker: Roxana
en: I will! I will join you!

speaker: Drakios
en: No! You must finish the battle!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's over, Drakios.

speaker: Drakios
en: It's over when I say it's over. Guards!

speaker: Roxana
en: Thank you, champion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, I'll see you at my ship?

speaker: Roxana

en: That maybe. But it's my destiny to win this Battle, a destiny that's been years in the making. I sincerely hope you're as strong as you say. It will make the songs they write about this day that much more epic.

en: I am a Spartan by blood. But I'm also just another misthios chasing drachmae.

en: You must have learned to fight like that somewhere.

en: I grew up alone and fought for everything I've ever had. Must have picked up a few tricks along the way.

en: A pity. I hoped to fell a celebrated opponent here to fix my legend. Oh well. You'll have to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How's the patient?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: He'll survive if I treat his injuries.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: This man is a monster. He's a slave trader who treats people so terribly that they injure themselves just to avoid working for him.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: If I help him, he'll continue to hurt others. But if I choose to do nothing, many will be spared pain and suffering.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This man is a rich slaver. If we save him, he'll reward us both. Think of the people you could help with that drachmae.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: No amount of money can undo the damage he's inflicted upon innocent people. Men like him think they can pay their way out of every situation, even death. He's wrong. No one can escape the Ferryman forever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It shouldn't matter what this man has done, he deserves to be treated like anyone else. We can't judge others when they're at our mercy.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I know it's my duty to help this man, but if you'd seen some of the injuries I've treated that he's caused, you would understand my doubts. The innocents of the Greek world have suffered enough lately.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I free his slaves? If he has no slaves, he can't mistreat them anymore, and you'll be able to treat him without guilt.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Yes, I can save this man, and you can prevent him from hurting others. Our kindness here will show the error of his ways—show him a different path to walk. You would do this for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I'll free the slaves for you.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Thank you, my friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those slaves' freedom is their own to fight for.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: If you free the slaves, I can heal this monster.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are the slaves being held?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I remember paying a visit to a camp on the river bank east of Lake Kopais to treat a slave for self-inflicted injuries. I'd try there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are hunting parties often attacked this close to the city?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: It's quite unusual, but with the war raging all around us, and the plague consuming everything else, it's no surprise the beasts are becoming more desperate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the slaves are in danger, I'll need to hurry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to talk to her.

speaker: Slave
en: Thank you for freeing us. That beast Galeos has worked all of us to the brink of death. Now I can return home to my family.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've freed the slaves.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I've treated his injuries enough to stabilize him, but he isn't out of danger yet...

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I don't know if I can bring myself to complete the treatment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're just going to stand here and watch this man die? You need to do what you do best, and heal him. It's what the gods put you here to do—help people, not judge them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've freed his slaves, and his business is finished. Perhaps our kindness will show him there is another path.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: If I do nothing, I'll be no better than him. I'll make sure he recovers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When he does, be sure to tell him how his life was in our hands.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Only the gods have the power to decide life and death. What I do is insignificant compared to their benevolence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen you save many from a trip down the Styx.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: But look at the plague—for all my knowledge and experience, I could do nothing against it. I have to accept that my reach only goes so far. Thank you for your help, my friend.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I must go, I have an appointment with a patient elsewhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Herodotos
en: My parents...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos, I'm so sorry.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I thought I'd be able to see them again. To show them my life's work. But now... I'm sorry to ask this of you, but could you take me to Samos? I need to pay my respects.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course, my friend.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Thank you. I'm not sure I could make this trip alone.

speaker: Herodotos
en: This is it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How does it feel being back?

speaker: Herodotos
en: It feels... like... Huh. Words escape me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a first.

speaker: Herodotos
en: To my eyes, it's home. The smells and sounds are familiar. But it's been so long. I don't know if I can do this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've done more difficult things.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Challenges we overcome always seem easier when they're behind us. What would you do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hold my head high. Walk with purpose. Push those feelings of doubt aside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Take it at your own speed. You'll get through this.

speaker: Herodotos
en: When I hear you say it, it does feel more true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're stronger than you know.

speaker: Herodotos
en: You're right. I suppose we should head to my family home first.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Living near the docks was so exciting as a child.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How so?

speaker: Herodotos
en: There was always a new ship to see. New people to watch. From the sailors, often a new word to learn. Most of which got me in trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure your mother remembered those days fondly.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I know I do.

speaker: Herodotos
en: So many faces I don't recognize.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've been gone a long time.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Even so, I was hoping there'd be someone I know. Someone who'd remind me of my life before I left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've only just arrived. It'll be OK.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Here we are. This is where I called home for most of my childhood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Most?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I came to Samos at a young age, but I was born in . Those are days I'd rather not remember. Hmm. It doesn't look like it's changed much in my absence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A tablet? Looks like some old writing. "The ships never stay for long. Samos is a place people come for a visit. but not to live. Is there something about this place I don't yet see?"

speaker: Herodotos
en: One of my first writings. I was always restless here, Always wanting to learn more about the world beyond and the world that was.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of your toys?

speaker: Herodotos
en: It was my brother's. I often hid it when he wouldn't let me play with it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This pottery looks special.

speaker: Herodotos
en: My father always felt art was a great outlet when things seemed overwhelming.

speaker: Mestor
en: Herodotos!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Mestor!

speaker: Mestor
en: Praise the gods. It's been far too long!

speaker: Herodotos
en: It has indeed. You're looking well.

speaker: Herodotos
en: As are you, Theodoros.

speaker: Theodoros
en: I can't believe you've come skulking back. After all this time...

speaker: Mestor
en: I should go. I'm glad you're back.

speaker: Theodoros
en: You have some nerve, little brother. You stroll back into this house when you didn't even return for the funeral. I regret ever sending you that letter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stop it. This isn't helping.

speaker: Herodotos
en: We came to Samos as soon as we could after receiving your letter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why doesn't everyone just take a deep breath...

speaker: Herodotos
en: How could you say I didn't come back when I'm here right now? We came as soon as the letter arrived.

speaker: Theodoros
en: You must have swam here then! It's been five moons since I sent that. And who are you exactly? How does any of this involve you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a...

speaker: Herodotos
en: She's a friend.

speaker: Theodoros
en: How nice. You went off to write and explore while making friends, and you left me here to take care of... everything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm someone you don't want to upset.

speaker: Herodotos
en: There's no need to be angry at her. She's a good friend of mine. She brought me here.

speaker: Theodoros
en: I have every right to be angry, brother. You abandoned your family to pursue your dreams.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I couldn't stay here. I needed to leave.

speaker: Theodoros
en: You could have taken me with you! I have things to attend to. One of us still cares about Samos.

speaker: Herodotos
en: At least tell me where they died.

speaker: Theodoros
en: We marked the spot on the nearby cliffs. Pay your respects and then leave. There's nothing for you here now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give him some time. I'm sure he's just surprised to see you.

speaker: Herodotos
en: His eyes showed hatred.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He probably missed you. You'll see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's... not like you at all.

speaker: Herodotos
en: He means well. He's been here this whole time grieving and thinking I didn't care.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't your fault. Don't let him make you feel guilty.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It's a bit late for that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know this wasn't the welcome you were expecting.

speaker: Herodotos
en: But perhaps it was the one I deserved. For now, I only want to see where they died. I owe that to them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come with you.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'd like that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're ready, we should go.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Waiting to face reality will do me no good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to get to the Adrestia. I have to stop those ships before it's too late.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Here they come...

speaker: Barnabas
en: Captain! The Chimera's Breath is prepped and at your command!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, Barnabas. Let's see what this thing can do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Chimera's Breath sure would help right about now, Barnabas...

speaker: Barnabas
en: You bet Poseidon's ass, Captain... We're working on it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas?!

speaker: Barnabas
en: We're working on it!

speaker: Barnabas
en: We did it!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Captain! Another ship... Look at the size of that thing...

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's on there... The Tempest. Phila. She's on that ship...

speaker: Barnabas
en: The Chimera's Breath is active, Captain! Let's bring Hades to our enemies!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to see what this thing can do...

speaker: Barnabas
en: I'm going to call you Prometheus from now on, Captain!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Because you've tamed fire!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Maláka! At this rate, she'll sink us!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Direct hit! She felt that!

speaker: Barnabas
en: She's hurting! Keep it up!

speaker: Civilian
en: Hey... You OK?

speaker: Civilian
en: You need help. You need

speaker: The Tempest
en: I don't need anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already destroyed your boat. Don't make destroy you, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tempest... Neither of us has to die.

speaker: The Tempest
en: You. Amorges told me all about the Tainted Ones... It's not your fault you were born as you are, but it is your fate to die like the rest. I will do what the Order needs done.

speaker: Kleta
en: Phila!

speaker: The Tempest
en: You—what are you doing here?

speaker: Kleta
en: There's so much I want to say, so many things... Please, give me a chance

speaker: The Tempest
en: You had your chance! You had years!

speaker: Kleta
en: I had to protect you.

speaker: The Tempest
en: I was drowning. Who do you think pulled me out? You? The Order is my family. You're just a memory... My past.

speaker: Kleta
en: You'll never be one of them. You're a Tainted One, Phila.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What

speaker: The Tempest
en: I know what I am! Amorges gave me purpose. Guided me. I'm no monster. I am the Tempest!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't have to prove anything to anyone, Phila. You don't have to be the Tempest. You can just be you. That's enough. Can't you see that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're too far gone. You're Amorges' puppet. Can't you see that?

speaker: The Tempest
en: No...

speaker: Kassandra
en: We might be Tainted Ones... But that doesn't make us who we are.

speaker: The Tempest
en: No! I control my fate. I control my future!

speaker: Kleta
en: Please, Phila. Let's just talk. You and me. Forget everything here. Come with us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She needs you, Kleta.

speaker: Kleta
en: Please... You still have family. You still have me.

speaker: The Tempest
en: Mater!

speaker: Kleta
en: You're my daughter, Phila. I should never have pushed you away. I have always... been... so...

speaker: The Tempest
en: Mater...

speaker: The Tempest
en: This is all your fault, Eagle Bearer...

speaker: The Tempest
en: Your fault!

speaker: The Tempest
en: I'll carve you from the face of this world!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Face me!

speaker: The Tempest
en: They said you were tough, Eagle Bearer!

speaker: The Tempest
en: Finally, an opponent worth my time...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kleta! Don't! She's too far gone. She's not your daughter anymore. She's the Tempest... I'm sorry.

speaker: The Tempest
en: I'll carve you from the face of this world!

speaker: Kleta
en: Phila!

speaker: The Tempest
en: I'm finishing this. You can't stop me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Face me!

speaker: The Tempest
en: They said you were tough, Eagle Bearer!

speaker: Kleta
en: Phila! Stop this! Now! Please stop! Please! It doesn't have to be like this, Phila...

speaker: The Tempest
en: Finally, an opponent worth my time...

speaker: Order Guard
en: Get up! Complete your mission, Tempest! It's the will of Amorges.

speaker: Darius
en: We are not your enemies, Phila. The Order think they control you, that you're nothing more than an instrument who kills on command. Be more than that—don't let them take away your humanity. Stand... and fight!

speaker: The Tempest
en: Mater... Please don't die. I have—there's still so much I need to say

speaker: Kleta
en: You're my daughter, Phila. I have always... been... so...

speaker: The Tempest
en: Kassandra... There is no simple life for us, only death. I always knew it would end like this...

speaker: Natakas
en: Father, the waters are open. We should get out while we still can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At least they're together now.
