speaker: Kassandra
en: The region of the Ancient Pearl.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Fair is fair. Are you going to get my wood? Those fucking bandits need a thrashing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fair is fair. I'll fix your wood problem.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Finally. Markos sure is lucky he's got you as his scapegoat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any idea where these bandits are?

speaker: Drucilla
en: I'm not a tracker. I'm a bowyer. They're in the mountain somewhere—that much I know. I'd check close to the lumber camps.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's plenty of trees around. Why do you need this type of wood?

speaker: Drucilla
en: I've been working on a new type of bow. It's more flexible, so it lasts longer and can fire at greater range. Only a very special type of wood that grows high in the mountains will do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of the bandits.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Make sure that you do, and be quick about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your moaning won't get the job done any faster. I'll kill the bandits and get your fucking wood back.

speaker: Drucilla
en: I-I know you will. Take your time finding them. I trust you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll deal with these bandits and get you the wood you need as fast as I can. Have patience, it won't take long.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Ha! If you knew how long Markos has been feeding me excuses, you wouldn't be saying that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a lot of footprints. A group left this area headed west.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The cart was emptied, then left behind. The thief can't have gotten far with that much cargo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shot in the back while fleeing. Must be the work of bandits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the bandit camp I'm looking for.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Ah, it's Markos' assistant! Bringing me the wood i need, I hope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Assistant? I don't think so.

speaker: Drucilla
en: I-I meant Markos' muscle! How stupid of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This will tide you over until the rest of the wood arrives in town.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Oh, look, it's Markos' mighty champion. Don't tell me you actually did what I asked?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I tracked the bandits and sent them to Hades. Your wood should arrive in town soon.

speaker: Drucilla
en: And you expect me to believe the word of a mercenary?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't expect you to believe me, so I brought this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's your proof. A sample of the special wood you want so badly. These bows you're making had better be worthy of Apollo for all the trouble I've gone to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You really should have more faith in people. I said I'd get it done, and I did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I brought you some wood back to work with until the rest arrives.

speaker: Drucilla
en: By the gods! You sure you work with Markos? He's never once delivered on a promise. Incredible!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I might work with him, but we're nothing alike. I'm true to my word.

speaker: Drucilla
en: Then take your pay. Give none to Markos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Can I help you with anything?

speaker: Mercenary
en: I have a problem... I may have stretched the truth a bit to secure a mercenary contract... It might be a bit bigger job than I'm used to, if I'm honest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How much did you stretch the truth?

speaker: Mercenary
en: I told the Spartan commander I have sunk whole fleets of ships before. So he sent me after the pirates in the area... and the Athenians.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You haven't ever sunk a ship, have you?

speaker: Mercenary
en: I sank one, once. But it was mine. And I was in it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I have to sink the Athenian fleet.

speaker: Mercenary
en: You read me like an oracle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Woman
en: I owe you one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should get going.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Back already. Did you destroy them all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be back to piece them back together.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Payment well earned, mercenary. Take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Happy to help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Praxilla? I have flowers for you from Orchimedes of... somewhere.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Did I not tell you to get the wine five minutes ago?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Kassandra of Agiad. May I introduce to you my dear friend, Praxilla. Apollo's muse, and mistress of the golden strings.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're Praxilla?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Didn't expect an aged bard, Mercenary of Agiad?

speaker: Kassandra
en: People your age tend to have more wealth, so if anything this is better for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be foolish of me to assume a master of the craft would be young.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Praxilla, this is Kassandra of Agiad. Eagle Bearer, Messenger of Zeus, launcher of a thousand

speaker: Praxilla
en: Kassandra. Ka. Ka? Casts stone and light alike. Leaves ladies and lads alight, alive? Ailing women and awestruck men cling to her side.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Ah, a true genius.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Look at those shoulders. A soldier. A Spartan? A thorn in the side of tyrants. She who dares challenge Poseidon. Alkibiades, this one I'm keeping my eyes on.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: The poems she writes about me are never so kind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have flowers for you. They're not from me. They're from Orchimedes. He's right over...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well he was over there.

speaker: Praxilla
en: A Coral Rose? I'll have to get my servant to add these to the pile.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a gift. Show some gratitude.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I also prefer actions to easy gestures.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Where is that servant girl? I swear, her head must be rattling with rocks.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I wish she'd rattle my rocks.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Achaikos is missing! That idiot must've taken it with her and run off!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Achaikos?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Achaikos is Praxilla's legendary lyre.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I set it down after tuning moments before you arrived. I can't go on stage without Achaikos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did see Orchimedes leaving in quite a hurry.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: We need to get that lyre back. Please, without Praxilla getting everyone's juices flowing, this festival is just a bunch of young men measuring the size of their verse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This lyre was special? Can you play another for your recital?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Perseus without winged sandals or a mirrored shield was just a man. Would he have the same legends, the same mystery, if he performed each task without a legendary weapon?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It's very valuable both in significance and in drachmae.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Orchimedes and the missing servant both disappeared as the lyre was stolen. They could be working together.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: And he seemed like such a nice boy.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Alkibiades invited a viper into my tent.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there somewhere they could have taken it?

speaker: Praxilla
en: It's a poetry festival. There is no better hub for shady trade.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the thief and return the lyre.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Praxilla's lyre has gone missing. Have you seen it?

speaker: Phaenna
en: Praxilla's lyre is missing? That's terrible news. First no Euripedes, and now this? Kreusis really has gone to the dogs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am looking for a man named Orchimedes.

speaker: Laches
en: I know an Archimedes. Otherwise, no.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He might have been holding a lyre.

speaker: Laches
en: There are as many men holding lyres here as there are blades of grass on a field.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for a missing lyre.

speaker: Drymon
en: Aren't we all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are we?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know a man named Orchimedes?

speaker: Krantor
en: Orchimedes? Orchimedes. That's the kid who hands out around the Vipers. Yeah, I know him. He's been coming to the festival for three or four years, maybe?

speaker: Krantor
en: You know how it is. People feel small, so they band together to make the rest of us feel smaller. They took over the Temple of Athena Itonia awhile back. Now it's hard to take the road without being held at knifepoint.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you think that's where Orchimedes would take a lyre?

speaker: Krantor
en: Hope not, for his sake. The Vipers are dangerous. If he did have the lyre on him, they'd probably rough him up for it. He's one of those kids they've been keeping around for fodder, if you get me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did he have a lyre on him?

speaker: Krantor
en: I didn't see him with one. I saw him talking to you, then walking towards Praxilla's tent. He and Praxilla's pretty helot have been sneaking around lots. Just assumed they were, you know, planting a garden.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is the Temple of Athena the best place to sell a stolen lyre?

speaker: Krantor
en: You can buy and sell anything here, unfortunately, but going to the Vipers guarantees the person you stole from won't follow you in. Shame, it was such a beautiful temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you for your help.

speaker: Krantor
en: Hope you find the lyre. Watch out for the Vipers at the Temple of Athena Itonia!

speaker: Ismene
en: Someone, please help!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're that servant. The one who disappeared at the same time as the lyre.

speaker: Ismene
en: I can explain. Orchimedes talked me into it and said he'd use the drachmae to buy my freedom. When we escaped, he said he wanted to bring the lyre to the Vipers. I said no. The Vipers said yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, the Vipers have Orchimedes and the lyre now. As for you, you can go back to Praxilla and apologize if you really want help.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: Oh, thank the gods, I'm saved. These horrible thugs blackmailed me into stealing the lyre.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I doubt that.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: They took it from me when I was captured.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: Maláka. Got what they deserved.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did they force you to steal Praxilla's lyre?

speaker: Orchimedes
en: No. They gave me the confidence I was lacking. We would drink and complain about poetry at the festival, and I let slip that Praxilla's my mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Praxilla's your mother?

speaker: Orchimedes
en: She is. She abandoned me and my father when I was a child. Something about following her destiny to be a wandering poet. My father, Achaikos, built that lyre for her as a wedding present. She loved it more than us. I just... I wanted her to feel the way we did when she left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Praxilla got what she deserved for leaving her family.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: I just wanted her to feel some of the pain I've felt. Why don't I feel better?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Orchimedes, I know you still have the lyre. Give it to me.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: It got broken in the struggle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Praxilla was born with a calling for the arts. It was her right to follow it.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: She should have thought of that before she decided to have a family. I wish my father had never made her that lyre.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Speaking of the lyre, I know you have it.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: Maláka. I do, but it was damaged in the struggle.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: Wait, before you leave... I need some advice. Should I talk to Praxilla? I don't know what to do!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Approach Praxilla as yourself and talk to her. Maybe she missed you and didn't know how to come home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what it's like to be angry at a parent and want retribution. It brought me no peace. Go, be with your father. You are worth more than a lyre to him.

speaker: Orchimedes
en: I need time to think about everything. My father, my mother, my friends. Please don't tell Praxilla who I am.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was able to get the lyre, but not in one piece.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Thank you. Oh Achaikos, what mischief did you get yourself into?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's a little girl doing in a clay pit?

speaker: Khloe
en: Ooh! A misthios!

speaker: Khloe
en: Hi, misthios! I'm just preparing something for my friends.

speaker: Khloe
en: I've been here allllllllll day, but I still need more clay! I need enough for all of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What you're doing for your friends is very nice. I'm sure they'll appreciate it.

speaker: Khloe
en: Really? You think so?

speaker: Khloe
en: I was thinking of getting them some other things though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friends will be upset with you for giving them dirt.

speaker: Khloe
en: Silly misthios! I'm not going to give this to them. I have other things in mind to give them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a generous friend. What do you want to give them?

speaker: Khloe
en: I want to get them some nice goo-werry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean jewelry?

speaker: Khloe
en: That's what I said!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't look like you could afford any, honestly.

speaker: Khloe
en: I know! That's why I was going to get some shiny stones in the Abandoned Mines and a few pearls from the lagoon. But I've been stuck here all day with the clay! And the Abandoned Mines are kinda scary... Do you think you could help me get some gifts for my friends? It'd make them happy, and that'd make me happy! I'll make some goo-werry for you too for helping him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gladly, young lady. I'll see to it you get the best pearls and shiny stones. And I wouldn't mind some "joo-werry" myself.

speaker: Khloe
en: Yay! Thank you! You're really nice for a big, scary-looking person.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These pearls you talked about. Where can I find them?

speaker: Khloe
en: North of the claypits! In the lagooooooon! They're just sitting there in the water, but there are some biiiiig sharks in there. Be careful!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are these Abandoned Mines with your shiny stones?

speaker: Khloe
en: The mine is in the meadow! West of the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can find.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are all your friends?

speaker: Khloe
en: ...They'll be coming soon. Just a little longer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Speak up, child, I can't hear you.

speaker: Khloe
en: Never mind! I'll introduce you to them later!

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK, that's all I need to know. I'll see you later.

speaker: Khloe
en: I should be done here soon! Meet me at the cliff overlooking the lagoon, OK? I'll introduce you to my friends. Thanks, misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah, the mines. That's where the shiny stones are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the lagoon with the pearls.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Abandoned Mines with the shiny stones.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These weren't too hard to find.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've got the pearls and the shiny stones. I should return to the little girl.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the lagoon the little girl mentioned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's enough pearls.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've got the pearls and the shiny stones. I should return to the little girl.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The little girl and her friends. She got her sooner than I thought she would.

speaker: Khloe
en: Silly Theo! Don't put that in your hair! You look funny.

speaker: Khloe
en: Misthios! You made it just in time. My friends have finally arrived.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... don't see anyone else here but us.

speaker: Khloe
en: What? Silly misthios, can't you see them? They're right over there.

speaker: Khloe
en: The one on the left is Theo, and the one on the right is Airla!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They look... friendly, but I don't think they really count as your friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your friends?! They're made of clay! How can they be your friends?

speaker: Khloe
en: What do you mean? They're my friends. I made them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know you made them, but that

speaker: Khloe
en: Mater told me to make friends, misthios. A—and I did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't the way to make friends. Tell your mater

speaker: Khloe
en: I can't. She's dead, misthios...

speaker: Khloe
en: Mater is dead. She joined the pirates—told me she'll bring back so much drachmae, we could swim in it! B-but one day, she came back, misthios. Her favourite white robe was all red. And she told me—To take care of myself and make more friends.

speaker: Khloe
en: But... I've never had any friends. I didn't know what she meant. So I thought really, reaaaaaaaally hard, and made my friends out of clay.

speaker: Khloe
en: Did I make a mistake? Mater won't be upset at me right? I didn't mean it! I didn't mean it!

speaker: Kassandra;
en: No, child, no. You did great. Your mater would be proud of you. Friends come in all shapes and sizes. I have an eagle, and he's a close friend of mine.

speaker: Khloe
en: Wow, really? That's so cool...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here you go, your gifts for your friends, as promised. Why don't you go put them on for them? I'm sure they'll like that.

speaker: Khloe
en: Thank you, misthios! You're the best! I'll go do that right now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, child. I could not break your heart, even if it was good for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should check in on her later...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't do this anymore.

speaker: Khloe
en: W-what are you doing? Those are for my friends!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They are not your friends! "They" are lumps of clay!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You need to make real friends. Go into the towns, find children your age. You cannot live out here alone.

speaker: Khloe
en: But all the townsfolk told me to stay away... They say I'm a cursed girl.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then go somewhere else, find other people. There are still good people left

speaker: Khloe
en: You just don't get it! You're not me! You don't understand...

speaker: Khloe
en: Goaway!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should check in on her later...

speaker: Child (1)
en: Woooow! You made this doll on your own?

speaker: Khloe
en: Y-yes! I make them out of clay.

speaker: Child (2)
en: Can you make one for me, too?

speaker: Child (1)
en: Me too! Make one for me too! Then we can all play with them together!

speaker: Khloe
en: Sure!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cerberus should stay away from you now.

speaker: Markos
en: Er, well, maybe not after all. One of the farmers ran over. She was uh, not happy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why?

speaker: Markos
en: It seems I may have—or, I did—accidentally, of course... sent you to someone else's farm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It wasn't the Cerberus' farm.

speaker: Markos
en: I could have sworn it belonged to the Cerberus! You have to believe me, my friend—an honest mistake.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How could you not know? You know the island. I thought you had a plan.

speaker: Markos
en: His men are always hanging around that farm... Must have been that pretty farmer. A common misconception!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka! Markos, sometimes I wonder how you walk around with a brain so small.

speaker: Markos
en: You don't mean that! Come on, think of all the smart things I've done. Remember the Cyclops' eye?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I destroyed someone's farm. I knew something was off.

speaker: Markos
en: I'll take on the debt and help them rebuild. Nothing else can go wrong!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another mess.

speaker: Markos
en: You've known me longer than anyone. If you can't forgive me, Kassandra, who can?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone with more patience.

speaker: Markos
en: Are you going to make me beg? Because I'll beg. Spare me from the Cerberus!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Markos...

speaker: Markos
en: Have I led you down the wrong path? A few times, yes. Many times, maybe. But this is it for me, my friend!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't keep you safe if you keep getting into trouble, Markos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to "everybody benefits"!? I've never benefited from helping you.

speaker: Markos
en: Think back to that sunny day when I found you, Kassandra. That was your day of need, and Markos came to the rescue! Come to my rescue today.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've paid you back plenty.

speaker: Markos
en: That I can't deny. But the Cerberus will come with its dogs and its devotees, and I'll be finished! Protect me, and we'll come out on top.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's that "we" again...

speaker: Markos
en: I'll tell you what. You protect me, and you get Mama's beloved battle axe! She used to be quite the fighter, believe it or not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. Let's keep you alive.

speaker: Markos
en: Oh, I've never heard words more sweet! You'll never get rid of me now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's why I do what I do.

speaker: Markos
en: And just in time. I hear them approaching!

speaker: Markos
en: All right, Markos, this is it. The grand finale!

speaker: Markos
en: We did it, my friend! I'd say I was invincible, but I don't want to jinx myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, that's why you're alive.

speaker: Markos
en: I joke, I joke. I owe you everything, Kassandra! For this, you get a lifetime supply of wine, and my friendship. Lucky you! Oh, and Mama's axe. Life will now be simple. All thanks to you. It's always thanks to you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A less dramatic life is just what you need, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: Go now, and adventure. Come back anytime for that cup of wine!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right... We'll see about that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm done, Markos. I've stuck my neck out for you more times than I can count.

speaker: Markos
en: I have to do this all on my lonesome?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good luck. Chaire, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: You're really leaving? Ay! I have to hide!

en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a note on the board. What's happened?

speaker: Woman
en: A great Spartan has died. A leader who inspired me. I've been creating likeness of him until my fingers bleed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're quite devoted to your leaders.

speaker: Woman
en: I am devoted to Sparta. I want my art in the hands of the commander that let him die as a painful reminder. And as for his inept replacement... Well, I have plans for him, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to deliver it to the Spartan commander.

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, it needs to get there in one piece.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

speaker: Woman
en: You're saving me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: May the Fates be on your side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A delivery for you.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, misthios. Please, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The path of betrayal. This is where that traitor snuck the Persian army past Sparta's defenses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Taking this path feels as if I'm betraying Sparta, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All my life I've heard stories of Leonidas. I can't believe I'm finally seeing where history was made.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thermopylai... They say you can't walk this battlefield without getting blood on your toes. This is where Leonidas was laid to rest. I wish I had known him.

speaker: Herodotos
en: If you close your eyes, you can hear them. Their final war cries, before every last one of those brave Spartans perished. Their voices were silenced that day, but their story will be sung for an eternity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You didn't bring me here to talk about dead Spartans. What's on your mind, Herodotos?

speaker: Herodotos
en: The battle of Thermopylai still echoes in our hearts, but to stand here is to feel it in your bones.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's nothing here but ghosts. My concerns are with the living.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Very poetic. Can we please go to Athens? We can talk about the dead on the way

speaker: Herodotos
en: Patience. I didn't bring you here to talk about the dead, I brought you here so you can learn to protect the living.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can I protect the living if I'm hanging around statues of lions?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Hold out your spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My spear? What for?

speaker: Herodotos
en: I need to know something.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Dienekes!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Uh...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos!

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'm fine. I'm fine. The stories are true. This is the spear of Leonidas. The hero's blade.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where were Sparta's allies?

speaker: Herodotos
en: The Spartans weren't alone in facing Xerxes and his hoards. Many from across the Greek world were armed and ready to fight alongside Leonidas and his three hundred. But when the mighty king looked into their eyes and saw fear, he sent them home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That sounds like madness, not bravery.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It was foretold by the Pythia that Sparta would lose either its freedom or its king to the Persians. Leonidas made his choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to Leonidas after the battle?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Xerxes was famous for honoring warriors who fought valiantly against the Persians. But Leonidas infuriated him so much, he cut off his head and impaled it on a pike. A bloody battle ensued, and his remains were reclaimed by the Spartans and buried here. Now, however, he rests where he belongs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to the traitor, Ephialtes?

speaker: Herodotos
en: King Xerxes paid him well, but treachery breeds treachery. A contract was put on his head, and he died as he lived—a coward.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You knew this would happen.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I didn't know—but I did suspect. There is a place I'd convinced myself was a dream... until now. A peculiar structure on the island of Andros—mysterious shapes carved in stone. Like nothing I've ever seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want to sail to Andros so you can show me shapes?

speaker: Herodotos
en: In my travels I heard whispers of an ancient civilization, a people who came... before. Your spear and that place are connected.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned a people that came before. Who were they?

speaker: Herodotos
en: They were not gods, but they lived longer than any mortal and were far more intelligent. I've seen carvings, strange symbols that suggest it was this ancient civilization that created humankind... and .

speaker: Kassandra
en: But Zeus blamed Prometheus.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Yes. Well perhaps his eagle has been feasting on the wrong liver.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The spear awakened to you, Herodotos. I trust you.

speaker: Herodotos
en: You understand... I will do everything in my power to help you find your mother, I promise. But first we must sail to the island of Andros.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll meet you at my ship.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Welcome aboard the Adrestia, Herodotos! Will you be traveling with us?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Only for a short trip. I have business to attend to in Athens.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos is helping me find my mother.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Seeking help from the gods has put Herodotos on your path, just as they put you on mine. They work in ways beyond our comprehension, and all we can do is follow their lead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You could be right. Herodotos and I share enemies, too.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Like Elpenor?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He is—was—part of a very powerful group called the Cult of Kosmos that controls the Greek world through the Oracle.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Control the Oracle! Apollo would not allow that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now they are looking for my mother. I need to find her before they do.

speaker: Herodotos
en: And I believe they will hurt others who oppose their views along the way.

speaker: Barnabas
en: By Hermes... The Oracle lost to corruption, and now this Cult? Do we know who leads them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know for sure but... I think it might be my brother.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Your brother?! By Zeus, your life is complicated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: But don't you worry! This Cult of Kosmos now has three new enemies. And one of them fights like Athena and shits thunder like Zeus! We'll bring the wrath of the gods down upon them.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Is he always this positive?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Always. That's why I like him.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Poseidon carry us to Athens!

speaker: Kassandra
en: First we need to go to Andros.

speaker: Barnabas
en: To Andros, then!

speaker: Herodotos
en: The bay of Marathon is ahead!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Marathon...

speaker: Herodotos
en: You know, the battle where a handful of Athenians pushed back the first Persian ?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm...

speaker: Herodotos
en: The great Themistokles? King Darius of Persia?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure

speaker: Barnabas
en: The site where the great Theseus slayed the vicious Kretan Bull!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh! That Marathon!

speaker: Herodotos
en: You're both hopeless...

speaker: Herodotos
en: Kassandra, there's a question I've been meaning to ask you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go on.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Your spear. How did you find it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mother told me that the Spartan army brought it back from the Battle of Thermopylai.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Why bring it back to her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leonidas was her father.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Incredible... And it gives you visions. Perhaps it's trying to guide you? Show you a path?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more. It helps me in battle.

speaker: Herodotos
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't really describe it... It's like I know what my opponent's next move will be, just before it happens.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Fascinating... This is just extraordinary... We are approaching the island of Andros, Kassandra.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Yes! Here we can see the tomb of the greatest Myrmidon, Achilles!

speaker: Herodotos
en: I was more excited by the fact that Andros exports some of the most expensive marble in the world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is this the place with the rumored ancient civilization ruins you were talking about?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Indeed it is. Look for a large gate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do I get inside? I wonder if...

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: Who's there? Come out!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Hesitation only hastens

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: the grave. I know, mater.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Your form is improving, your resolve is strong. But you're not taking action.

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: I was going to!

speaker: Myrrine
en: I know. But it's the moments in between that decide everything. Your turn.

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: Leonidas's spear!

speaker: Myrrine
en: You're old enough now. My father's spear holds a certain burden, but... you're ready.

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: I felt something.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Oh?

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: The spear... it has magic.

speaker: Myrrine
en: It carries with it a long line of power. A bloodline of incredible heroes—the same blood within you and me. And our family.

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: All of us?

speaker: Myrrine
en: Think of Leonidas. He had great courage. And he made a great sacrifice. You share in his blood and the strength he possessed. We are able to feel certain things happening around us. That is our family's gift. But not everyone understands that. Some recognize the power we bear, and want it only for themselves. They will try to take it from us.

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: I won't let them.

speaker: Myrrine
en: I know. You're a warrior. If we keep moving forward—always moving forward—we're untouchable. Storm's coming in.

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: Then maybe we should move forward now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater... I haven't forgotten you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods... Who built all this? How does a place like this exist? How could I even explain this to someone like Markos? Something's glowing over there.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Forge activated. Synchronizing retransmission chronicity... Contact engaged.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My spear's stronger now. The Cult won't stand a chance. Well, Herodotos will be happy. It's clear someone was here far before we were. Did Leonidas know this place existed?

speaker: Deimos
en: Time to talk.

speaker: Deimos
en: You're not hard to track.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you come alone? Are you all right? Alexios, you're alive.

speaker: Deimos
en: Don't touch me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come on, little brother. You have to tell me everything. What's happened to you?

speaker: Deimos
en: I don't have to tell you anything. I don't know you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I know you. It doesn't matter. There's more important things to argue about.

speaker: Deimos
en: You're right. Like that stunt you pulled with the artifact. It got my attention, if that's what you wanted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? The artifact showed the truth. We're family, and we made it out of Sparta alive.

speaker: Deimos
en: Yes, it did show the truth. It confirmed what I always knew. You threw me off a fucking mountain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If that's what you think, Alexios, you must've hit your head on the way down.

speaker: Deimos
en: I've heard the story, and not from a liar like you. And never call me Alexios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You think it's that simple? Come on, Alexios. Let's talk about it.

speaker: Deimos
en: Stop calling me that. I already know what happened that night.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right, Deimos. Now him, I don't know.

speaker: Deimos
en: He's a demigod. Worshipped and feared by the Cult and all the Greek world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a fantasy to me. Did the Cult cook that story up, too?

speaker: Deimos
en: I'd watch your fucking mouth. Or I'll shut it for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You didn't when you had the chance before. And I bet you won't now. This is stupid. We need to find our mater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then why do the Cult's bidding?

speaker: Deimos
en: Have you been paying attention? They're following my lead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then make a choice on your own. Help find our mater.

speaker: Deimos
en: I'm not interested in reunion. I just want to know what you think you're doing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Same thing as your Cult. Looking for Myrrine, our mother.

speaker: Deimos
en: They don't need her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your Cultists think differently. She's their next target.

speaker: Deimos
en: If they ever pursued her, it would be to kill her. But if you don't know where she is, that means she abandoned you, too. How sad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even if we were abandoned, we survived. We can go back to the way things were if we can find her.

speaker: Deimos
en: The Cult has no interest in sentimentality. Or "family." Its only aim is control.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then get them off her trail. Send them after me instead.

speaker: Deimos
en: You really do like attention. They'll be after you soon enough, not to worry. And they'll dominate you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They'll have their work cut out for them.

speaker: Deimos
en: I doubt it. The "family" will be exterminated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it's true they're after us, tell them they'll never find Nikolaos. He's off the map. Trust me, I've searched myself.

speaker: Deimos
en: If I could find you, the other long lost child of Nikolaos, then I can find him. And when I do, he'll wish he was thrown off that mountain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they're after all of us, there's one less person to find. I killed Nikolaos.

speaker: Deimos
en: Yet here you are acting so righteous. When really, you're just like me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't care what you think. I'll find Myrrine. Do the right thing. Come with me.

speaker: Deimos
en: What?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We could find her—together. You could help me.

speaker: Deimos
en: Oh, you think friendship is the answer? Running around like lost children looking for dear mater? You're so weak.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's responsibility, not weakness. I won't abandon the whole family just for spite.

speaker: Deimos
en: Responsibility? Get off your high horse. The Cult has a plan, and it won't be interrupted by the likes of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Weak? I've had to kill for much longer than you've had to.

speaker: Deimos
en: Oh, I'm so scared. I have an army behind me. One false move, and you're obliterated. That's the plan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Taking your own mother isn't enough for them?

speaker: Deimos
en: We're not abductors. We're political. Those who don't stand with us, stand against us. And they pay for that mistake.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Like me.

speaker: Deimos
en: Like you. I heard you're planning a trip to Athens. When you go, tell Perikles and his elitist scum they're next.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult let Myrrine live. They let Nikolaos live. Why kill them now?

speaker: Deimos
en: Because you live. You brought this on her and yourself. The Cult is powerful, but they're mortals. I have the blood of gods, so they think you do, too. But they'll see how wrong they are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going after the Cult, you know.

speaker: Deimos
en: You've seen our numbers. You've seen what I can do. And you still think you stand a chance?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Try me.

speaker: Deimos
en: So having guts runs in the family, does it? You claim we have the same blood, so let's see what you can do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're being an asshole.

speaker: Deimos
en: You'll have to be stronger than that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We still found each other, brother.

speaker: Deimos
en: I told you not to touch me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take the challenge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka. Herodotos won't believe this. I have to tell him what happened.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Well, was the legend true? Was it magnificent? What happened to you? And your spear?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Slow down, Herodotos. My spear's stronger now. I can feel it. You were right. There was some kind of artifact there. It showed me a vision... of me and my mother.

speaker: Herodotos
en: So the ancient civilization is real. Kassandra, you have no idea the power you possess—all harnessed in Leonidas's spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not everything. Deimos followed me here. The Cult's already moving—he told me himself. They're going after us—my family, Perikles...

speaker: Herodotos
en: Why would he tell you, unless it was a trap?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't matter. We have to get to Athens—to warn Perikles. And we need to find my mother before they do.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Then we go to the Pnyx. If Perikles is anywhere, he's there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should've known it was you who'd ask for the furs, Ilos.

speaker: Civilian
en: And I should've known it was you to get them for me. Kassandra is always on the job.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't tell Markos, he'll get jealous.

speaker: Civilian
en: I post it publicly to give the others a chance, but you're always so keen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are the pelts for this time?

speaker: Civilian
en: The Athenians want armor for the war. Good protection for them, good drachmae for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here they are, all encountered for.

speaker: Civilian
en: In record time, too. Take your pay, it's well earned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay out of trouble, Ilos.

speaker: Civilian
en: You should take your own advice!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just like she said. The cart looks pretty worse-for-wear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like these new baskets were off to market—until the cart broke.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This should help. Better them than the bandits.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Who among you is afraid?! Who among you is frail or weak?! Who among you... IS STRONG?! Then I say prove yourselves! Come face-to-face with He of the Blood-Soaked Hooves! He of the Entrail-Splattered Horns! You know his name, you know his roar! The Beast, the Myth... THE MINOTAAAAAUR!!! Maximum of three members per Minotaur hunting party; purchase of Minotaur-themed merchandise is mandatory before proceeding; no legendary warriors, pregnant heroes, or legitimate gods (demi, semi, or otherwise) are eligible to fight the Minotaur; and no pushing—you'll all get a chance at dismemberment.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Ah, a mighty specimen approaches! Are you ready for honor? For glory?! For certain death?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready for two-thirds of that.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Then you seek combat with... THE MINOTAUR!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Minotaur's already dead, by my hand.

speaker: Leiandros
en: You killed the Minotaur?!

speaker: Leiandros
en: I'm sorry my friend, you're very mistaken! Some scam artist fooled you with flame-lit corridors and flimsy costumes! The 100% genuine and completely real Minotaur lives here! And, uh, you better believe it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No self-respecting Minotaur would live in Lato.

speaker: Leiandros
en: He does.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here?

speaker: Leiandros
en: Yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: ... In Lato?

speaker: Leiandros
en: Yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This Lato?

speaker: Leiandros
en: I assure you, the beast lives here, and he wants nothing more than a wealthy - uh, a worthy opponent to battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't see any labyrinths or golden balls of string... but, if there's a Minotaur to be fought, I'm listening.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Then listen well, my observant friend!

speaker: Leiandros
en: If you slay the Minotaur, you would be Theseus reborn! And you'd get to take home the Prize of Pephka!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your Minotaur must die.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Sounds like we have... another contender!

speaker: Leiandros
en: It's time for the Trials of the Minotaur.. Pre-Trials.

speaker: Kassandra
en: ... Did you just say Minotaur "Pre-Trials"?

speaker: Leiandros
en: To face the Minotaur, you must first prove yourself worthy by completing three heroic trials. We can't let people fresh off of the triremes casually stroll to their deaths! Pephka policy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do these Pre-Trials require me to do, exactly?

speaker: Leiandros
en: There's the Trial of Strength, where you fight the greatest warrior in all of Krete. The Trial of Accuracy, which only a keen eye can overcome! And the Trial of Endurance, where you must brave... The water!

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of your Trials is swimming?! That's—this is a scheme to fleece me.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Misthios, I—that's—how could you even think such a thing? You're a terrible person.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What exactly is the "Prize of Pephka"?

speaker: Leiandros
en: Why, it's limitless riches of course! Warriors defeated by the Minotaur no longer need their drachmae, so we collect their coins into a grand prize that only a champion who kills the beast may claim.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your grand prize is drachmae looted from the dead?!

speaker: Leiandros
en: Misthios, please believe me, many of those coins go straight to the Lato School for Children Whose Parents Were Tragically Killed By the Minotaur!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about your "Minotaur."

speaker: Leiandros
en: Part man, part beast, all monster. His horns are as sharp as blades, and his blades are as sharp as... horns? Wait, no, I always mess that up

speaker: Kassandra
en: A vivid portrait. You must have seen him personally.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Many times. And I'll tell you this much—no one's ever returned from where he dwells.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How would you react if I said the name... "Melite"?

speaker: Leiandros
en: Uh, Melite? Well, I—No. I've not heard of them. It's a strange name, one I'd remember.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do your Trials

speaker: Leiandros
en: Pre-Trials!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do your Pre-Trials, but then the Minotaur's head is mine.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Fantastic! Don't forget to collect Tokens of Success from the Trial Masters to prove your victories.

speaker: Kore
en: Ugh, another "champion," here to save us all from Pephka's long queues and overpriced Minotaur merchandise.

speaker: Leiandros
en: Ah, may I introduce my wife, Kore! A rare beauty, and so— So loud, in front of my new friend.

speaker: Kore
en: Please, Leiandros—there are more important things than glory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing stands in the way of glory. Statues aren't carved to honor the insignificant.

speaker: Kore
en: And what about my daughter? Is she insignificant, "hero"?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not everyone with a sword seeks glory. Family comes before all else.

speaker: Kore
en: Exactly, misthios. That's what I keep telling this cowardly slime in the shape of my husband.

speaker: Leiandros
en: ..Hey!

speaker: Kore
en: It's—it's our daughter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your daughter?

speaker: Kore
en: Amara. She ran off days ago.

speaker: Leiandros
en: I'm sure she's—she's just fine! Don't worry about Amara—not when there's a Minotaur to slay! "GRR!" "Slash-slash!" Big fight! Lots of blood! Think of the fame, misthios! Think of winning the Prize of Pephka!

speaker: Leiandros
en: Please trust me, champion—nothing is what it seems in Pepha. Solving one problem may just solve all the others...

speaker: Leiandros
en: Go, my legendary friend! The Pre-Trials of the Minotaur await!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all 3 Tokens. Better meet Leiandros at the Warrior's Rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been looking for you... I saw your message. What's happened?

speaker: Woman
en: My husband has been captured by bandits. They think he is a spy, and those malákes know the Spartans will reward them for his capture.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Being a spy is dangerous work.

speaker: Woman
en: It is but he's not even a spy! It was me. I can't let this happen, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to rescue him.

speaker: Woman
en: No. All the bandits must die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Woman
en: Perfect. Time is of the essence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: Thank you for all you've done. Please, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All in a day's work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your plan seemed to work. The Monger's thugs ambushed me.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I heard. I also heard you had no problems dealing with them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It wasn't my first fight in Korinth.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Or your last. We're going to take the Monger to task at the theater. I've arranged a Korinthian drama no one will forget.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas is worried about the anarchy that could follow the Monger's death. He wants him dead, but wants it done quietly.

speaker: Anthousa
en: That man is a long way from Sparta. This is Korinthia, so we'll do it the Korinthian way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm with you. We'll put on a show.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Meet me and my girls there. The public has no idea what spectacle they're about to witness.

speaker: The Monger
en: You wanted a fuckin' show?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wanted you to see the face of every person you've wronged.

speaker: The Monger
en: I'll cover their faces with that precious blood of yours. Just like I shoulda done with Myrrine.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You'll never rule these streets, you pig!

speaker: The Monger
en: Oh, you bet your pretty face I will.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Get your filthy hands

speaker: The Monger
en: And when I do, I'll rip your fucking head right off and send it to the Cult as proof.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You... you knew my mater?

speaker: The Monger
en: She was big fuckin' trouble. But I'll pay her back. When I'm done with you, I'm gonna find your mater and bring her your fuckin' head.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not if I bring her yours first.

speaker: The Monger
en: They won't have much to say after I smash your brains all over the stage. Get the fuck off my streets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're not yours anymore.

speaker: Anthousa
en: People of Korinth! Behold the weasel that steals your bread! The scourge that spoils your crops!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've waited long enough to get your hands on him.

speaker: Anthousa
en: The pleasure is all mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Feel better?

speaker: Anthousa
en: I have been starving for this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He deserved all of it.

speaker: Anthousa
en: And you deserve your answers. Come, let's speak. In private.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos would be disappointed in you.

speaker: Anthousa
en: He is dead!

speaker: Anthousa
en: It's time. Soak in your victory, then meet me somewhere quiet. I'll tell you all I know about your mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I agree with Brasidas. I say we take him to the Sacred Cave.

speaker: Anthousa
en: This isn't what we planned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Monger needs to be erased from existence. We'll fight him in a private place, and he'll die. A simple transaction, remember?

speaker: Anthousa
en: If you insist. We'll meet you at the Sacred Cave.

speaker: The Monger
en: So it is you. A demi-god in the soot-and-shit streets of Korinth? Killing my men? Helping those fuckin' parasites?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's me.

speaker: The Monger
en: Arrogant, just like your mother.

speaker: Myrrine
en: You'll never rule these streets, you pig!

speaker: The Monger
en: oh, you bet your pretty face I will.

speaker: Myrrine
en: Get your filthy hands

speaker: The Monger
en: And when I do, I'll rip your fucking head right off and send it to the Cult as proof.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? You knew...

speaker: The Monger
en: Oh, I fuckin' knew her, all right. She was big fuckin' trouble. But I'll pay her back—when I'm done with you, I'm gonna find your mater and bring her your fuckin' head. Deimos will wish he was watchin' this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not if I bring her yours first.

speaker: The Monger
en: Get the fuck outta my city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not yours anymore.

speaker: The Monger
en: Wish I coulda been there to watch Deimos break your neck.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't make me laugh.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Wait! No!

speaker: Anthousa
en: The people of Korinth must see him die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anthousa...

speaker: Anthousa
en: Take him out of here and bring him to the theater! Show everyone his cowardice!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You wanted him dead. Here he is.

speaker: Anthousa
en: It's a shame the people don't get to see him bleed. His cries should have run out across the city!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's dead. I've delivered. Your turn.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Yes, you're right. He's dead. Take his body to the square. Let the people get a last good look at him. As for you, Kassandra, I owe you information. We'll talk about your mother. Just not here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. Lead the way.

speaker: Anthousa
en: To the theater! For all to see him as he really is.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I can't give enough thanks for what you've done. And for once I can also thank Alkibiades—he sent you here, after all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There is more to him than meets the eye.

speaker: Anthousa
en: He knew you could save Korinth from that beast.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everybody benefits, everybody wins.

speaker: Anthousa
en: You've proven to be a very valuable business partner.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Speaking of business. You owe me, Anthousa.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's no secret that I'll also benefit from his death. Let's talk.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Yes, Myrrine. She came and left Korinthia in a flurry, but made an impression on me. Like a great storm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I remember that part of her well.

speaker: Anthousa
en: A strong woman with great intensity. She wanted to find her place here in Korinth, but never found what she was looking for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You speak of her kindly. You were her friend.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Perhaps on the surface. But she had a great pain in the middle of her that no one could get to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you come to know her?

speaker: Anthousa
en: There was so much rain that night... I saw her sleeping in the streets and gave her shelter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She was a vagrant? I wonder what my father'd think of that.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I didn't know what happened to her. All she told me was that she'd left the place that tore her apart. Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did she find work?

speaker: Anthousa
en: She kept to herself—with one eye always on the port.

speaker: Anthousa
en: She could have stayed with us. But I think she was looking for something else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Was there no mention of her past? A husband, family...

speaker: Anthousa
en: Nothing. Speaking of Sparta only brought her misery. It's like a part of her was missing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After Korinth—where did she go?

speaker: Anthousa
en: That, I don't know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She must have given you some hint.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I don't think even she knew where she was headed. All I know is she won a ship thanks to a lucky dice throw. Tyche owed her that much, at least. I remember the ship's name well—Siren Song.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Siren Song.

speaker: Anthousa
en: It was famous for weathering all that Poseidon threw in its path.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, Anthousa.

speaker: Anthousa
en: May the gods look well upon you, Kassandra. Visit me any time—I'll catch you up on Korinth's affairs. It seems I have an interesting future ahead of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So do I.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Siren Song. If I can find someone who knows the ship, I'll be one step closer to finding her.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Tomorrow is a new day. Korinth will be reborn.

speaker: Morality Issues
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should find Natakas...

speaker: Darius
en: Natakas has gone out hunting, if you're looking for him.

speaker: Natakas
en: Kassandra. What are you doing here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was going to ask you the same.

speaker: Natakas
en: I find doing something practical helps me get my thoughts together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You like hunting.

speaker: Natakas
en: I do. There's deer here usually.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everytime I've seen you, you're trying to save lives, not end them.

speaker: Natakas
en: I don't see an issue if it's done with balance in mind and respect for the animal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a nice idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're anything like Darius, I bet you're good with a bow.

speaker: Natakas
en: I do all right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Modest.

speaker: Natakas
en: I was just about to start. Would you like to join me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like that. It'd be nice.

speaker: Natakas
en: Let's see how good you really are. How many deer do you think you can get?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's find out...

speaker: Natakas
en: The deer are usually around here...

speaker: Natakas
en: Nice shot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Darius is good in a fight. He must train a lot.

speaker: Natakas
en: Never misses a day. He doesn't know his age...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your father is a man of few words.

speaker: Natakas
en: And you caught him on a more talkative day.

speaker: Natakas
en: Another one!

speaker: Natakas
en: Shh! Did you hear that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Natakas
en: Follow me. Stay quiet. There!

speaker: Natakas
en: He's tricky...

speaker: Natakas
en: Shh...

speaker: Natakas
en: Trust me.

speaker: Natakas
en: Look...

speaker: Kassandra
en: A boar? In Makedonia?

speaker: Natakas
en: Almost unheard of. Delicious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It is...

speaker: Kassandra
en: They taste... Filthy animals.

speaker: Natakas
en: Keep quiet... It'll hear you.

speaker: Natakas
en: I can almost taste it...

speaker: Boar Meat
en: The thick layers are moist with fat and juices.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this?

speaker: Natakas
en: That makes everything better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're an amazing cook, Natakas. Good enough for the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I usually hate boar. But what you've managed to do here—it's fit for the gods.

speaker: Natakas
en: It's an old family recipe. My grandmother would be happy to hear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should all indulge as gods when we can.

speaker: Natakas
en: Us? Gods?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Speak for yourself. I'm already a god.

speaker: Natakas
en: There is something special about you. Everyone can see it, obviously. But no one, not even you, can fully tell what it is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We could pretend, for a while. In truth, I'm a misthios. I hunt for food, like you. I work for drachmae, like you. I live on the road. Like you.

speaker: Natakas
en: Yet, I've seen the Eagle Bearer. Your deeds are worthy of the stories.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With all that's happened in Makedonia... I guess you can't stay here.

speaker: Natakas
en: I don't know. We always run. Ever since I was a child. My mother would find a way—no matter if it were by the side of a road or in a cave somewhere—she'd find a way to keep us warm. Safe. Like we had a home. I don't know if I'll ever feel that again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's gone now?

speaker: Natakas
en: Years ago. Same with my siblings. The Order. The last time we saw them was the last time I saw my sister Neema alive. What about you? What about your past?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never knew a true home, either. I grew up fending for myself, hoping there'd be a place out there where I'd feel, as you said, warm. I haven't found it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And anyway, I don't think it exists.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have a family. Not one worth considering anyway.

speaker: Natakas
en: We're shaped by our pasts, not defined by them.

speaker: Barnabas
en: They're Persians, you say?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Darius claims to have killed King Xerxes himself.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ha! You don't believe that, do you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do believe it. Of all the lies he could tell, that's one of the most unbelievable.

speaker: Barnabas
en: A lie worthy of Dolos himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't believe him. It's too wild of a claim, even for me.

speaker: Barnabas
en: And yet we've heard wilder claims that turned out true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know what to believe anymore. Darius says the Order of the Ancients are here to find me. The note he found mentioned others

speaker: Barnabas
en: There are others like you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I believe him, there are. But how do I know that Darius isn't working for the Cult, or in the Order himself?

speaker: Barnabas
en: You say he's heard you're a great warrior. Maybe he wants to use you to help him fight against this Order.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If he's not one of them.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The simple question is, do you trust him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I trust Darius. He's mysterious, but not a liar.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's too much left unsaid. So, no, I don't trust him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's impossible for me to truly trust anyone.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ouch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Except you, Barnabas.

speaker: Barnabas
en: It sounds like you need to go back to these Persians if you want to know what's really going on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Darius is hiding something, that much is clear.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Then be careful. Make sure whatever he is hiding isn't a trap.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be as careful as I always am.

speaker: Barnabas
en: That's what I'm afraid of.

speaker: Elpis
en: Dikastes! Over here.

speaker: Elpis
en: Quick! Follow me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And trust a stranger?

speaker: Elpis
en: I'm no stranger. I'm Elpis. And I've been watching you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not ominous at all.

speaker: Elpis
en: I'll drop the cloak and dagger. I've been training to become like you. But training isn't enough—you're more than a warrior. The blood of the gods runs through your veins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought they preferred "Isu" in Atlantis.

speaker: Elpis
en: The Isu may as well be the divine with how they rule. Cold. Calculating. Indifferent to the people milling beneath them. But it's not just Isu blood that makes you special, is it? There's something else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, you tell me.

speaker: Elpis
en: I'm talking about this. Your spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I almost decapitated the last man that looked at my spear. Give it back.

speaker: Elpis
en: Of course, Dikastes. I was just showing off.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Showing off for me, are you?

speaker: Elpis
en: Just a little. Are you impressed?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stealing is not the way to my heart.

speaker: Elpis
en: Just having a bit of fun, but I'll get to the point.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're strangely charming for a thief.

speaker: Elpis
en: Flattering, but we have business to attend to, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I wasn't so distracted by your beautiful face, you would never have gotten close to my spear.

speaker: Elpis
en: Flattering, but we have business to attend to, Dikastes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You weren't kidding when you said you'd been training. You're quite skilled.

speaker: Elpis
en: That means a lot coming from you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what do you want from me?

speaker: Elpis
en: I'm... involved with Atlas. He's afraid of taking the relationship public. He says his enemies would exploit me as his weakness, so he keeps me a secret.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait, you're in love with Atlas?

speaker: Elpis
en: From my experience, I'm not sure Isu men truly love. Nevertheless, I need to make him see that I can be his strength. Our partnership might be a key to bridging the gap between Isu and humans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your love is strategic.

speaker: Elpis
en: If we take the relationship public, we could marry and I could rule the district by his side, influence policy, and ease then tension between the two groups. But, so long as I am merely human, it can never be. That's why I want to be like you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem very passionate about Atlantean politics.

speaker: Elpis
en: Atlas doesn't approach the human and Isu conflict with compassion for humanity. I believe I can bring that compassion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone so eager to kill his own brothers hardly strikes me as husband material.

speaker: Elpis
en: Atlas is like any Isu, aloof and unchanging. That's why we make a good team. I bring out his... humanity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be nice to have another ally in Atlantis. What's your plan?

speaker: Elpis
en: At the Adamant Metallon, they harvest a metal used to create devices just like your spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My spear is the strongest metal ever forged. Could this be used to forge other weapons?

speaker: Elpis
en: Well... adamant ingots could. But what I need is raw adamant. I know the one who can forge it for me. Atlas can't suspect what I'm up to, so make sure you're not seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He doesn't know about this?

speaker: Elpis
en: I'll tell him the truth when the time is right. Please, hurry back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpis is... interesting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the Adamant Metallon elpis told me about. She said I should get the raw adamant without being seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shit! Hope Atlas doesn't find out I was here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like this might be where they stor the raw adamant after mining it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Got the raw adamant. I'll bring this to Elpis. It#s reacting with my Staff somehow... almost like they were meant to be together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Raw adamant. As promised.

speaker: Elpis
en: Nice to see that you're as skilled as you look. I'm making the right choice to become more like you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It takes more than a weapon crafted from adamant to be like me.

speaker: Elpis
en: Luckily, I'm not crafting a weapon, but a powerful Isu device.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem fine to me. I don't know why you're trying to change.

speaker: Elpis
en: Just as you were destined to be Dikastes, I am destined for this. I just know it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlantis isn't worthy of the type of change you're hoping to bring if they can't accept you as you are.

speaker: Elpis
en: Like most great politicians, I'm ahead of my time. that means I need to do something drastic if I'm going to push Atlantis forward for humans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Atlas is hardly worth all this trouble. You shouldn't change yourself for him.

speaker: Elpis
en: This is bigger than Atlas. Wait and see what a human Archon could mean for Atlantis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Humans in Atlantis are lucky to have someone like you fighting for them. You'll make a great leader.

speaker: Elpis
en: I'm glad you understand what this means to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got where I am through hard work and training, not by taking short cuts.

speaker: Elpis
en: Of course, Dikastes. Your work ethic and drive to survive are traits I aspire to mirror.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Still... all you have is raw adamant.

speaker: Elpis
en: Until I take it to a skilled blacksmith so he can forge an Isu device from the adamant.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, you know where to find the Dikastes when you need her.

speaker: Elpis
en: The forging shouldn't take too long. I'll meet you near the Doma of Atlas when it's done. Then we can proceed to the next phase of my plan.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I sometimes feel like we've spent as much time at sea as on land.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You may be right. We've traveled a lot together.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I think it may be time I set off on my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. As much as I like you by my side, I can't expect you to stay forever.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I figured I'd take my leave while you still feel that way. It will feel strange, though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I knew it'd happen one day. But I wish it didn't have to.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I know. We've been through far more than most people will ever experience in their lives. But, even so, it will be a weird feeling.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It will take some getting used to. Well, where should I take you?

speaker: Herodotos
en: The docks near Athens should do. There are some others I'd like to say goodbye to as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure they'll be sorry to see you go. To Athens!

speaker: Herodotos
en: I sometimes pinch myself to make sure that I'm awake and that all we went through truly happened.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With your writings, it won't soon be forgotten either.

speaker: Herodotos
en: The world will be better knowing. My mind is flooded with the memories of all we experienced.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you have a favorite?

speaker: Herodotos
en: How could I possibly decide? You opened my eyes to so much. Uncovered so many secrets and mysteries that will change the course of the world. Your spear and all it suggests... Atlantis... The Cult...

speaker: Kassandra
en: When you start listing everything, you're right... I'm quite amazing.

speaker: Herodotos
en: And humble!

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of my stronger traits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: None of those things are mine alone to take credit for. You were there through it all.

speaker: Herodotos
en: How could I ignore what was so clearly in front of me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You couldn't, which is why you have as much of a claim to all we did.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I wonder what the great Eagle Bearer will remember best from this journey?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's like you said... it's impossible to pick just one.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It feels we met so long ago now, but we've also been through a lot in such a short time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad you visited the Pythia that day and saw Barnabas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The symposium won't easily be forgotten.

speaker: Herodotos
en: No, I'd imagine not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was overwhelming, but looking back on it now and everyone I met... I'm not sure how I'd put it into words. I guess that will be up to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Our trip to Samos holds a special place in my heart.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Mine as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you thought of returning?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Not just yet. But I hope my next visit is far more uneventful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't think you'll have to worry about that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've been through a lot, but I'm not sure anything will ever match Atlantis.

speaker: Herodotos
en: To think we're some of the only people to know of its existence. Of your true father...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Which you promised you'd keep to yourself!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Of course, of course!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You may be leaving, but I'll find you if I have to.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I guess this is it. As much as I'll miss our conversations, this is where our paths diverge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is your path taking you now?

speaker: Herodotos
en: To .

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's waiting for you there?

speaker: Herodotos
en: That's the exciting part. I have no idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Know what? I'm not sure anyone loves the unknown as much as you.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It only stays that way until someone cares enough to make it known. In Thourioi, that someone will be me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Will I see you again?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Our paths may cross once more, and I hope they do. If that comes to pass, after all, it likely means something big is following close behind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then I hope our adventures are nowhere near complete.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never been great at saying "goodbye."

speaker: Herodotos
en: To do so is to impart a sense of finality, and we have no way of knowing if this is truly goodbye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good luck in your travels, Herodotos. I can't wait to hear what you get yourself into.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I'll share my stories with you so long as you bring some new ones of your own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can do that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should check in on Timotheos and Lykinos as their father's house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This looks like one of the bandits that killed Diokles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whoever did this didn't take anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lykinos! Are you all right?

speaker: Lykinos
en: They took him. The bandits who killed my pater took Timotheos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where did they go?

speaker: Lykinos
en: To the ruins of Mycenae! Please, you have to help him!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Timotheos! We have to get out of here. Timotheos?

speaker: Timotheos
en: Die, Spartan dogs! To the Ferryman with you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Timotheos. It's over!

speaker: Timotheos
en: Where are they? Cursed Spartan dogs! Where are they hiding?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're safe, Timotheos. I promise.

speaker: Timotheos
en: Kassandra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's me. You're all right now.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Timotheos! You're safe!

speaker: Timotheos
en: You've saved us once again, mercenary.

speaker: Lykinos
en: In more ways than one.

speaker: Hypatos
en: The famed Eagle Bearer hasn't saved you just yet.

speaker: Hypatos
en: It's nice to finally meet Diokles's boys.

speaker: Lykinos
en: Who are you?

speaker: Hypatos
en: I'm dear Diokles's business partner. Or at least I was. Until I had to terminate our arrangement.

speaker: Timotheos
en: You mean you had him killed?

speaker: Hypatos
en: A last resort. Our partnership funded poor Diokles's gambling for years. His mistake was gambling not with drachmae he earned from me, but with drachmae he stole from me.

speaker: Lykinos
en: You're lying. There's no way our pater would ever work with you.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Believe what you want. It doesn't change the fact that Diokles screwed me over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You got your payment in Diokles's blood. What do you want with Lykinos and Timotheos?

speaker: Hypatos
en: Diokles may be dead, but I haven't received my drachmae yet.

speaker: Timotheos
en: You expect me to pay?

speaker: Hypatos
en: One way or another, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough. Let's finish this already.

speaker: Hypatos
en: So be it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can't we come to a more peaceful arrangement?

speaker: Hypatos
en: If the brothers can't pay, there's nothing left to discuss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about you and me?

speaker: Hypatos
en: You? Maybe there is something the great Eagle Bearer could do for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well? What is it?

speaker: Hypatos
en: There's a man in Korinth. He's my biggest competitor. I need him taken care of. Publically. Big guy, swears a lot. Can't make it five steps in Korinth without hearing about him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean the Monger?

speaker: Hypatos
en: Exactly.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Oh and Eagle Bearer? His death better be a bloody spectacle. Otherwise the debt goes unpaid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're talking about the Monger, I already took care of him.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Impossible! I would have heard about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I dealt with him quietly.

speaker: Hypatos
en: How would a secret execution send his customers to me? This changes nothing. We're done here.

speaker: Hypatos
en: I was going to clear Diokles's debt through his boys, but you took out my biggest competitors in Korinth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Glad I helped?

speaker: Hypatos
en: You did me a favor, so I'm willing to let these boys go to repay what I owe you, misthios.

speaker: Lykinos
en: He killed my pater. Are you really going to let him go.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Yes, misthios. Are you going to let me go?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. You'll pay for what you've done.

speaker: Hypatos
en: Have it your way, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's been enough bloodshed. You can go.

speaker: Hypatos
en: A smart move. Consider the debt repaid.

speaker: Timotheos
en: Thank you for saving me, Kassandra. There is something I've been meaning to tell you.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I need to tell Kassandra something, too.

speaker: Timotheos
en: I'm sorry for running from you the other day. It wasn't... how I really feel about you.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I would never leave you.

speaker: Timotheos
en: What I mean to say is, I shouldn't have run from you when... I want to be with you.

speaker: Timotheos
en: When I'm with you, the darkness inside me fades away. I didn't think I'd feel happiness like this again.

speaker: Lykinos
en: I'm the only reason you even know each other.

speaker: Lykinos

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said sirens?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That is ridiculous. Sirens aren't real.

en: Of course they are. I've lost many sailors to their calls.

en: Good advice, from both you and Demeter... But what should I use?

speaker: Barnabas
en: You believe me? Here, take this! Beeswax.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Leda is alive, I'll find her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods, that smells good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All that for a bracelet, an aulos, and some spices.

en: But look! I know this bracelet too well. The women of the Sieged Plains wear them. These spices are native to the lands of Demeter. And this aulos is marked by a craftsman in the Parnes Mountains.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're all from Attika.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The cave! They're all around the one known as the Entrance to the Underworld. It can't be a coincidence. Is that where Leda is?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's only one way to know. Let's go.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Most would have called me crazed, but not you. You truly are my best friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's nothing. Now, let's find your wife.

en: There's only one way to know. Let's go.

en: I know you've doubted me. I must have sounded like a crazed old fool. But you won't regret this.

en: Such a foolish old man.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Leda. My love. I swear to you, so long as there is wind in my sail, I will never stop seeking your shore.

en: You'll be together again one day, Barnabas.

en: It's down this way! This place is going to blow your mind, misthios. There's a hugeeeeee room and there's a hugeeeeee hole in the ground with a hugeeeeee door. speaker: Ardos
en: The Minotaur is still alive! And hungry!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Great.

speaker: Ardos
en: I'm glad you came along. Now pater has a shot of getting out of that damn labyrinth.

speaker: Ardos
en: They really didn't have to put the entrance this deep. Almost there. What were these Minoans thinking? Here we are!

speaker: Ardos
en: Isn't this amaaaaaazing?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen some things, Ardos. But this...

speaker: Ardos
en: IS AMAAAAAAAAAZING.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's just a ruined door. A big door, sure.

speaker: Ardos
en: No, it's not! It's a really - a - S-Stop ruining everything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So the Minotaur lies beneath Knossos Palace...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Open the door. I've got a minotaur to slay.

en: Ah. Uh, right. It's locked.

en: Don't worry, we'll find a way. You must know something.

en: If you don't know how to get in there, I swear

en: They'll speak to me. Who are these people?

en: The Collector, Swordfish, and my old caretaker. My old caretaker— Boooooooring old man— Never wanted to talk to me about my pater of the Minotaur, so I left him to find out the truth on my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bold.

speaker: Ardos
en: And the Collector is this guy who buys weird stuff. He's a merchant in Gortyn.

speaker: Ardos
en: Oh! And the last guy! They call him—Swooooooordfish.

en: Of course.

speaker: Ardos
en: He's the boss of Octopus Bay. And he's mean.

en: Where should I start looking for "Swordfish"?

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Swordfish"? He must have a long, pointy nose.

speaker: Ardos
en: No, no! He's really good with a sword and... He's really good with fish? I guess?

en: This "Collector," where is he?

en: Don't let me catch you "borrowing" from me.

en: Tell me more about this old man.

en: Okay, so, my old caretaker recently sent me a message about wanting to meet in Phaistos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's nice of him.

speaker: Ardos
en: Ha! He never answered me about my pater or the Minotaur, ever. That's why I left in the first place!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go in your place and see what I find.

speaker: Ardos
en: The message said to meet him at our old house northeast of here, near Phaistos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make sure they all talk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a note on the board. What's happened?
