en: An Spartan ship was sunk just off the coast. The warriors on board will never see battle again, but their weapons still could. The ship was carrying a chest with their gear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So go get them.

speaker: Man
en: Spartans weren't made for fighting the sharks in these waters.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to go diving for it?

speaker: Man
en: That would be the idea, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Man
en: Please, get it done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

en: Did you get it?

en: I'll handle this.

en: Please, get it done.

en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

en: Someone's being hurt. Open this door, or I'll kick it in!

en: Don't mind her. She likes to watch. Look at you. Such authority, such aggression. I can see why Perikles has taken such an interest in you. Did you come to join us?

en: It sounded like someone was in pain.

en: Well, it can sometimes be... hard to distinguish between sounds of pleasure and pain. Had I known you were going to knock, I would have left my door wide, wide open for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I only came to this symposium to find someone.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Sounds like we can help each other then, doesn't it? You fetch us a bit of oil, I help you find who you're looking for. Maybe they're in here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's not in here.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I think I'll check all the same.

en: Let them have their meeting of the minds. I'm more interested in meeting... other parts.

en: Allie! We're out of oil again!

en: Allie?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean naked.

en: It sounds so good when you say it.

en: I only came to this symposium to find someone.

en: Sounds like we can help each other then, doesn't it? You fetch us a bit of oil, I help you find who you're looking for. Maybe they're in here.

en: I think I'll check all the same.

en: Shame. If you change your mind, I promise to pour the oil on you. And lick it off.

en: I was just about to come find you. Clearly you were thinking the same thing I was.

en: After your... display earlier, it's probably safer I get the oil.

en: Obedient too? I knew I liked you. Don't take too long.

en: If you don't get the oil soon, all our fun will end.

en: Just can't stay away, can you? Did you bring the oil?

en: You've grown up in Perikles's home, and yet you're so... different.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When you walked in, you seemed like you and Sokrates were...

speaker: Alkibiades
en: How I wish you were right. One day we will have that man in here with us. I promise you that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I might be back.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: If you come back with a jar of oil, I promise to show you how grateful I am.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Just can't stay away, can you? Did you bring the oil?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I come bearing gifts.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: We're saved! Today, these women grieved for their sons, and these men worked the wall. But tonight we forget all that. Let's have some fun! What do you say? Care to join us?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time for some fun. You'll have to help me strip off these uncomfortable Athenian robes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time for some fun. You'll have to help me get out of my clothes.

en: Now it's time for you to help me, "Allie." I'm looking for someone.

en: Focus. I'm looking for a woman who fled Sparta a long, long time ago.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Fled Sparta? No one flees Sparta! But, let's pretend she did. If she were stupid, she'd be dead. If she were smart, she'd do what Aspasia did—she'd earn her independence. The smartest and most... resourceful woman I've ever met have been in Korinthia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The hetaerae? I've heard they play some sort of role in Korinth, but I assumed it was the same as any other city.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Oh no, these women are unlike any other you'll meet—a force, and the only ones there with any smarts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Prostitutes? This is serious.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: They don't like being called that. And for good reason. They offer so much more than their bodies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Such as?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: These women are companions. Counselors. Confidantes. Powerful men come to the hetaerae asking for advice, and value their words more than those of their closest friends and advisors.

speaker: Man
en: Allie! Come back inside!

speaker: Alkibiades
en: The celebration continues! When you reach Korinth, find Anthousa. No one goes in—or out—of the city without her knowing. Until we meet again, warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anthousa in Korinth. It's not much, but it's a start.

en: I'm sorry, but I can't. It's too much even for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What brings you to Kos, of all places?

en: I've learned a thing or two about soil. Turns out, Kephallonia wasn't the best place for grapes. Plus, the locals here love wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everybody loves wine.

en: Besides, how profitable could I have been in a town of thieves and mercenaries? Not very.

speaker: Markos
en: On top of that, Kephallonia isn't as, uh, busy as it was before. Plague came from Kausos, and many died. It was bad for business.

en: Been here long?

en: I see the resemblance.

en: Funny. I remember you telling me your mother died a long time ago.

en: Well, Mama is the owner of the vineyard. When her husband met his untimely death, it was going to be auctioned off. Something had to be done!

en: So you stepped in to help. How generous.

en: It's ridiculous a wonderful lady such as Mama can't inherit her own property. Now, we run the vineyard together. Isn't that right, Mama?

speaker: Markos
en: She'd put up a fuss if she disagreed. It's her land, but she shares it with her precious son—me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a nice place you've commandeered, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: If I didn't know you so well, I'd think you were serious! I'm always laughing these days.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You weren't laughing much when you were tied up in that fort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't think I've forgotten that "Markos always has a plan." Sounds like one of your schemes.

speaker: Markos
en: Kassandra, that was the old Markos. These days, I live a peaceful life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were tied up in a fort. That's peaceful?

speaker: Markos
en: Eh—about that. I have a bit of a problem on my hands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why am I not surprised?

speaker: Markos
en: But it's something I know you could help me with, my friend! I know your credentials.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go on.

speaker: Markos
en: You know me... I borrow some drachmae, and before I know it, they're calling me the Con of Kos! All thanks to the Cerberus—whom I owe the most.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cerberus? First the Cyclops, and now this? Don't tell me it's a three-headed dog.

speaker: Markos
en: Don't be ridiculous! This is nothing like the Cyclops. This time, I wish to make a peace offering—with nothing less than my finest wine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Finest?" Palatable, maybe.

speaker: Markos
en: Kassandra, you're like family to me. And since I'm family to you, I'm sure you wouldn't mind helping.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're sure, are you?

speaker: Markos
en: I promise I can afford to pay you this time. Just take my wine to the Cerberus—simple!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. For old time's sake.

speaker: Markos
en: I can always count on you! And the Cerberus can count on a nice wine pairing with dinner. Take it to his house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cerberus better not bite me.

en: Are you the Cerberus?

en: It's a peace offering. A thank you for waiting so patiently for him to pay you back.

en: All right.

en: You tricked me!

en: I'm gonna be sick.

en: Ugh. Still have the taste of Markos' wine in my mouth.

en: Guards! Guards!

en: That's wonderful, midwife. And he is healthy? How is the mother?

en: How do I make drachmae from this news, midwife?

en: The mother and son are strong, so there is work to be done. The father is a commander – a message must be delivered to him. And a sacrifice of goats must be made to thank the gods.

en: It was a joke.

en: Sokrates the horse thief... I can almost hear the stories they'll tell. Aristophanes will love this.

en: What story is that?

en: There is a man nearby who is responsible for stealing the horse. I've been contemplating the proper course of action, but I'd like to know what you think is right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll leave this one to you.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Did you change your mind about helping?

speaker: Kassandra
en: And how should I make my decision?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Your thoughts are your own, but speaking to the thief himself may help you decide. Can such a crime be justified? It's an interesting thought.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's the thief now?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I told him to wait by the stables southwest of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you caught him stealing a horse, what's to say he won't just run away?

speaker: Sokrates
en: The hope of keeping the horse. That's where you come in. I'll let him tell you the rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the thief! You won't escape.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you the one who stole the horse? Sokrates said I should talk to you.

speaker: Civilian
en: Bad enough being caught, but to have a misthios judge me...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Better me than an Athenian guard. Anything to say?

speaker: Civilian
en: The man I stole it from won't even miss it. He has plenty of others, while my only horse died last week. If I had the drachmae to buy a new one, I would have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you steal the horse to use it or sell it?

speaker: Civilian
en: I have a family to feed, and this horse will help me on the farm. Plus I have no other way of traveling right now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no other option?

speaker: Civilian
en: Not that I could think of. Trust me, I feel shame for what I did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any reason you picked this specific horse?

speaker: Civilian
en: It was the easiest one to take. Other than that, not really. Though I did make sure is wasn't his best horse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A courteous thief?

speaker: Civilian
en: I didn't steal it for fun. I did it because I had no other choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have enough information to make a decision.

speaker: Civilian
en: I hope you can understand. Wouldn't you do the same if it was your family?

speaker: Civilian
en: Was there something else?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Have you decided what should be done?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't matter why he stole the horse – it belongs to someone else.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You surprise me yet again. I truly believed you would choose the other side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Because I am a misthios?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Of course! Yet, when it comes to someone else, you decided a crime deserves a consequence no matter the reason. A safe choice, although I can think of times when it may not be right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If he needs the horse more than the man he stole it from, let him keep it. It will do him more good.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So determining whether a crime deserves a consequence or reward is dependent on the reasons behind it. An intriguing thought, although I can see how dangerous such thinking might be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I thought about it, I realized I didn't need to talk to the man to make the decision.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So you didn't feel a need to know why he stole it? Your decisiveness is something to both marvel at and question.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The real question is whether my decision matters at all, or if this was just another test to see what I would do.

speaker: Sokrates
en: There's a good chance it is both, but an equally good chance it is neither.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now you're not making sense on purpose.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Let me ask you one more thing. If one man kills another in order to save many, can his actions be considered just? Or should the man be punished?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The outcome may be better, but he should still be punished for his crime.

speaker: Sokrates
en: That is true, yet if his peers were to decide – especially those he saved – they may argue that though the action was wrong, it was necessary and just.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure the law cares about the reasons.

speaker: Sokrates
en: But if we are to decide whether the law should act on a man, or if his crime should be pardoned, the worthiness of the action should be taken into account, should it not?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the action was for a good reason, then he is in the right.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So in times like these, people like us get to determine the law? Many would believe a murder still deserves consequence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people whose lives were saved would disagree.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then perhaps making choices that affect the most people for good is the correct path, wouldn't you agree?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are we done yet? I can't stay here all day.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Of course you can't. It is a luxury few can afford. Even those with the time for it often lack the mental capacity for such things.

speaker: Kassandra
en: OK.

speaker: Sokrates
en: If a farmer steals a fruit today, but gives some of his crop to the poor tomorrow, who may decide if he is good? Hmm...

speaker: Kassandra
en: "We've done your cult favors and we've come to claim ours." Signed by the Tempest. The Order and the Cult working together. Not surprising.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here it is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "We need time to get the new weapons fitted onto our fleet." New weapons? I don't like the sound of that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: "The Tempest is performing flawlessly, but I will continue my observations." Someone sent this woman to spy on the Tempest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Capture the stranded people in Boura. We can't let them establish a foothold there." I wonder if Kleta knows about this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Tempest has heavy influence here. I need to know more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to know more about the Tempest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all the letters I need. The Tempest is a brilliant strategist. A straight fight won't work. We'll need a plan to defeat her.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: I can't believe they stole it. Of all the things they could take!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You say somebody stole something?

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Somebody stole something? Look around. Bandits took almost everything. And worst of all, they stole my family's vase. After so many generations, it's gone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're wealthy. You could buy yourself a new vase.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: A new vase? Didn't you hear me? It's a family heirloom, you can't replace something like that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I carry with me something passed down from my mother. I appreciate the value of family heirlooms.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: It's strange how inanimate objects can generate real feeling in us, isn't it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: How much is this vase worth to you?

speaker: Slave Owner
en: I'd pay a substantial amount of drachmae for it. A very substantial amount. Is finding my vase something you could do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find your vase, but I'll need some ideas of where to look for it.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Speak with my slave near the warehouses. I sent him to uncover what he could from other slaves in the area. Hopefully he's learned something by now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return if I find the vase.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mean this?

speaker: Slave Owner
en: My vase! You found it!

speaker: Slave
en: Master, I have a concern.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: A concern about what?

speaker: Slave
en: How do we know that this misthios isn't one of the people who took it in the first place?

speaker: Slave Owner
en: That's a good question

speaker: Slave
en: Let me talk to her privately to be sure.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Yet another example of why I'll miss you when you're gone.

speaker: Slave
en: Misthios, I know you must've taken the vase from the bandits. But, that's not the point. I have a favor to ask of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Unless I know what it is, I won't know if I can gift you with this favor.

speaker: Slave
en: You're willing to hear me out. That's a start.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of favor are we talking about?

speaker: Slave
en: My master recently told me that after the coming summer solstice he will release me. But I don't want to go. I want you to say that I told the bandits where to find the vase. And then, for atonement, I'll offer my services.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Well? Who took my vase?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your master tells me you might've learned something about the missing vase.

speaker: Slave
en: I have. But I'll need something from you before I can talk about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't like conditional deals like this. I have a job to do.

speaker: Slave
en: I understand. But what I need from you isn't a labor or an action, it's a commitment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have a working agreement with your master. We're all on the same side, so tell me what you need.

speaker: Slave
en: You're a rose amongst the weeds.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what do you need?

speaker: Slave
en: I'm hoping that after you retrieve the vase, you'll tell my master that I told the bandits to loot the house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would you want to do that?

speaker: Slave
en: After the summer solstice, my master plans to give me my freedom. But I don't want it. I'm hoping that if I take partial blame for the crime, I can offer my continued servitude as atonement.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's ridiculous, but I'll think about it. Now, tell me about the bandits.

speaker: Slave
en: Other slaves in the area assure me that bandits from the northern hills of Mount Ochi are the ones ransacking the nearby homes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The northern hills of Mount Ochi... Is there a more precise place I should look for these bandits?

speaker: Slave
en: The slaves mentioned there's a copper mine in the area. That's where I'd put my hideout if I was a bandit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm curious why you're not excited to have your freedom?

speaker: Slave
en: With my master I have purpose, responsibilities, food, and shelter. All the things I wouldn't have on my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With your freedom you can acquire all that, you know.

speaker: Slave
en: We all have different circumstances and abilities, misthios. This life offers me the best chance of survival.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will go find these bandits and get your master's vase.

speaker: Slave
en: Remember what we talked about when you return it to my master.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is. The copper mine.

speaker: Heirloom Vase
en: This ornamental vase holds great sentimental value to the family it belongs to, but little value to anyone else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All this trouble over an old vase...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't believe that slave wants me to lie for him.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Have you found my vase?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: That's great news! Who took it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was taken by bandits hiding in the copper mine north of here.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Well, you returned it, so at least there's some justice. Here's the reward I promised.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know, your slave is very loyal. You've already granted him his freedom, but I think you should keep him on. He may even want that.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Is it true? You want to stay?

speaker: Slave
en: Yes, I do.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Then why didn't you say something?

speaker: Slave
en: It's not a slave's place to question his orders. Isn't that right, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even though you're a slave, your life is still your own. You should've just asked your master to stay.

speaker: Slave
en: Please accept my humblest apologies, master. I will never do it again.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: All is forgiven. It worked out the way it was supposed to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should respect your master's wishes. Maybe he sees something in you that you don't see yourself.

speaker: Slave
en: Is that true? You think I'm ready to be on my own?

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Yes. While your body and mind are still able, you should go. Start your own life.

speaker: Slave
en: Thank you, master. I will.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Thank you for returning my family's vase.

speaker: Slave
en: You were right by not lying to my master. I don't know what I was thinking, but I'm glad you did what you did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It turns out your slave told the bandits to loot your home and take the vase.

speaker: Slave Owner
en: What? Can this be true?

speaker: Slave
en: Yes, master. If you'll allow me to make atonement, I'll...

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Atonement? Never. I won't allow a slave who tells bandits to steal from his master to work for me.

speaker: Slave
en: What? No. Please no. Let me stay!

speaker: Slave Owner
en: I won't hear it. Leave now, before I pay this misthios to kill you. Go!

speaker: Slave Owner
en: Just when you think you know someone. Here's your payment for returning my vase. Thank you for returning my family vase and exposing my slave.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: Found them!

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: Found him!

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the marble quarry Brasidas mentioned.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: The weapons have to be here somewhere.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: There's only one Spartan here that I need to kill. It'll be easier if I don't alert the others.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: One down, four to go.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: That's two. Time to find the others.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: Three weapon racks destroyed. Won't take much longer.

scene: One Bad Spartan Spoils the Bunch
speaker: Kassandra
en: Only one more to go.

speaker: Lysander
en: Time to strike again. Athenian command will be slow to retaliate. Ready to kill more of their fort commanders?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll kill the commanders and clear the way for your troops.

speaker: Lysander
en: Only fools want war. And so far it seems both sides are made of fools.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good news, General?

speaker: Lysander
en: Athenian commanders have been dismissed for negligence because of my tactics!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Better unemployed than dead.

speaker: Lysander
en: You're proving a solid ally. There's no time to lose. We need to control the enemy forts..

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me ask you something first...

speaker: Lysander
en: Waste of time!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't think much of Spartan leadership.

speaker: Lysander
en: When I rise, they'll bow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Lysander
en: Why are you still here? Go kill the enemy command!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Consider it done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The fort commanders are dead. Here are the seals as proof.

speaker: Lysander
en: Excellent. Our ineffectual leaders will see my value.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure they will.

speaker: Lysander
en: My spies tell me Athenians have gained ground. Infiltrate the forts and attack their command. Understand?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. I'll do as you ask and attack the commanders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They must be faltering by now.

speaker: Lysander
en: Athenians fail because they fear risk.

speaker: Barnabas
en: So, did you kill your father?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stepfather.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I suppose the gods won't judge you too harshly for a "step-patricide."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nikolaos raised me. Trained me. He was my father, even if he did try to kill me.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Is that better or worse? No matter. Yours isn't the only complicated family in the world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks. I'm glad to have you around, Barnabas.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I'm happy to be here. Would anything else help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: if you're trying to make me feel better, stop.

speaker: Barnabas
en: What would make you feel better then?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Finding my mater. She's alive, Barnabas! At least... Nikolaos thought so.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Some good news, praise Hera. What's your plan? What course should I set, captain?

speaker: Kassandra
en: For now, we go to Phokis. Elpenor said he'd meet me there. He owes me money and an explanation.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Aye, Kassandra. And let's seek the wisdom of the Pythia while we're there. If anyone has answers for you, it's the Oracle of Delphi.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Oracle's predictions destroyed my family.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The Pythia has the wisdom of Apollo himself! Now I'll admit, if people choose to ignore her, they might court disaster

speaker: Kassandra
en: If we'd ignored the Pythia, my brother would still be alive and our mother would be safe at home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll think about it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Good. You know, kings and queens travel to Phokis to consult the Pythia. She can start wars or end them. They say that

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, I know. That's enough Oracle talk for now.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Back to business. You know where to meet Elpenor, I suppose?

speaker: Kassandra
en: His home is in Pilgrim's Landing. But... Nikolaos's last words to me were a warning of snakes in the grass.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Sounds like you should make extra preparations.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpenor is the one who should prepare.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Meet me at Apollo's temple in Delphi when you're done dealing with the snakes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpenor has a lot of explaining to do.

speaker: Open Season
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Order of the Storm
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone's beaten me to it. I'll have to take a closer look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A battered scarf. I'm looking for someone with torn clothes...

speaker: Kassandra
en: These pots were broken before the fire.

speaker: Augeia
en: Is nothing sacred? Ancient and valuable relics were housed in this temple. Now the scum has taken it all and burned it down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They've burned it to cover their tracks.

speaker: Augeia
en: The scum ran off towards town with an armload of our most sacred items. Likely in the beggars' quarter, from the look of him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, his clothes are torn... and they match the color.

speaker: Stele Piece in Orchomenos City
en: This stele piece smells of smoke, and its edges are charred by flame.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper. The Tomb of Orion awaits the Heir.

speaker: Aletheia
en: In this tomb, the Heir of Memories will see how life grows from a dead place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Life growing from a tomb? If I hadn't seen the Staff work, I wouldn't believe it.

speaker: Aletheia
en: The Heir's task is to bring life where there was death. And your task dooms you to endure loss. Close your eyes and picture the face of one you will never see again. What would you tell them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's hard for me to apologize, but I would say I'm sorry... for everything I failed to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've waited so long and lost so much. If I could, I'd say, "Take me with you."

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would hold them... and tell them to be strong, and that we will be together again.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Remember that answer, and the path from which it comes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't have to tell me, Aletheia. I will always remember... I will always "keep."

speaker: Aletheia
en: And now, will the Heir of Memories rise to face the tomb?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I suppose she will.

speaker: Civilian
en: You must be the one Perikles sent.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am. He said there is an ostracism vote, but didn't tell me what I'm here to do.

speaker: Civilian
en: Of course he didn't. That's what I'm for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If someone is exiled, can they return?

speaker: Civilian
en: If they do, they'll be punished.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does someone have to do to be ostracized?

speaker: Civilian
en: Anyone seen as a threat to the city or the people is enough. And then it is up to the vote. Some have been ostracized for simply being more disliked than the person they're up against.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's my role in this?

speaker: Civilian
en: The votes have already been cast. We don't have long before they're counted. Take the ostraka in this bag and exchange them with the ones currently under guard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to rig the ostracism?

speaker: Civilian
en: Perikles does, and he has his reasons I'm sure. Bring me the bag you took from the room, and I'll take care of the rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one will see me go in or out. Stay here.

speaker: Civilian
en: We don't have much time.

speaker: Fake Ostraka
en: Perikles's contact provided these ostraka to rig the vote at Anaxagoras's ostracism.

speaker: Real Ostraka
en: These ostraka are the real votes for Anaxagoras's ostracism.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should do it. I should let Perikles's contact know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's done.

speaker: Civilian
en: Hm, you work quickly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you going to do with them?

speaker: Civilian
en: Dump them in a well. Ah, it looks like the official has arrived.

speaker: Civilian (official)
en: The votes have been tallied. Overwhemingly, the people have decided that Anaxagoras should be ostracized from Athens.

speaker: Civilian (official)
en: I apologize for the delay. There was evidence someone attempted to tamper with the votes.

speaker: Civilian (official)
en: Don't worry. The ostraca are all accounted for. The votes were counted, and Anaxagoras is to be ostracized.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Be slow to fall into friendship—but once you do, continue firm and constant. It will be more difficult for me now that Anaxagoras must leave Athens. We were quite close, although he and Perikles were much closer. It's strange Perikles wasn't here today to defend him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Would Perikles normally defend someone?

speaker: Sokrates
en: A good friend? Of course. Yet Anaxagoras seems pleased with the result. This day has brought more questions than answers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said you were close...

speaker: Sokrates
en: He was like a mentor to me. Many of my best thoughts came to fruition through our conversations.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are you?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ask anyone and they'll tell you Sokrates, but a name gives you nothing. Our actions determine who we are, and every action has its pleasures and its price. With that said, then, who do you claim to be?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My name is Kassandra.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And still, I don't feel I know you. Perhaps I can find out who you are a different way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want to know me?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Knowledge is the one good thing in this world. Surely you agree?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't be paid in knowledge.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, then you're driven by the desire for wealth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Drachmae is the one thing people need.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Many believe they need more than they actually do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And others have to risk everything just to survive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. Knowledge drives everything I do.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then we are the same in that way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Knowledge of when to attack, what weapon to use, or when to use reason instead of violence.

speaker: Sokrates
en: We seem to put our love of knowledge into practice quite differently.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I use it how I need to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know the price of actions. I have to as a mercenary.

speaker: Sokrates
en: That simple piece of information tells me more about you than your name ever could. Explaining oneself must be carefully done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Explaining myself would take more time than I have.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then let us focus on a single, recent event. Tell me, as a mercenary, is there anything you wouldn't do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everything has a price.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And you're the one who decides when the pay is worth it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have the luxury of turning down a job.

speaker: Sokrates
en: What of duty? The greater good? Are they not their own kind of payment?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. They're not.

speaker: Sokrates
en: It seems you know yourself well, but know it is better to change one's thoughts than to persist in those that are wrong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My thoughts are fine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Some people might see duty as a good enough reason, I guess.

speaker: Sokrates
en: The greater good is all we should care about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Easy to say if you're never worried about going hungry.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I eat to live, but I do not live to eat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just because I'm a mercenary doesn't mean I'll do anything.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Even if the pay was more than adequate for the task?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even then.

speaker: Sokrates
en: What if you were offered something you desperately needed? Something you couldn't get anywhere else? Would you move this line you've made for yourself?

speaker: Kassandra
en: My line has moved countless times since I was a child. But it still exists.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And will likely move again if what you say is true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It may.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It moves when I need it to.

speaker: Sokrates
en: A strategy for those who must be adaptable. Or for those who wish to justify their actions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I decide if my actions are just.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You are clearly someone who would do whatever you feel is necessary. Perhaps for drachmae, or maybe to further a personal goal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That describes a lot of people.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I suppose I'm curious why you did it. How could I not be when you're the reason my friend is being forced to leave the only home he's ever known?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did what I was asked to do.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And your needs are greater than those of the man you helped ostracize? Still, you raise a fine point. Who is more responsible: Anaxagoras for getting himself mixed up in this, or you, for simply sealing his fate?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not responsible for his actions. I have one thing to think about—my own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. I'm more responsible. But I did it because I have one concern—myself.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then I hope you also think about today. About Anaxagoras. About choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think you have the wrong person.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You are claiming that you are the wrong person? Life's one true happiness is knowing yourself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even if I did know who rigged the ostracism vote, I wouldn't tell you.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And yet, I never said anyone rigged anything.

speaker: Civilian
en: Sokrates. There you are.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Here I am.

speaker: Civilian
en: You're late. They're all waiting for you.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I wished to see Anaxagoras's fate. And so I have. Tell them I'm on my way.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Well, it seems our conversation is at an end. Although I hope it isn't the final one we have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wouldn't know.

speaker: Out for Blood
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Out of Here
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a note on the board. What's happened?

speaker: Woman
en: Cursed bandits stole my papyrus! Do you have any idea how expensive it is, misthios? I can't afford more, and the guards do nothing about these malakes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you want me to give you some drachmae?

speaker: Woman
en: Yes. Any drachmae you can give helps.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, take this.

speaker: Paint the Land Red
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Paint the Ocean Blue
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.
