speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is, hiding in plain sight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even the gods couldn't save you, soldier.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One general defected, and is hiding on Delos. These are orders to kill him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's one. All the marble in Mykonos can't save you from my spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas sends his regards.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thought you could hide on Delos... Found you, coward.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Neokles! You can't hide forever!

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: We're going to find you, traitor!

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Think we won't spill your blood on Delos? Ha!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The commander has guards. But they're not there to protect him...

speaker: Neokles
en: Thank the gods. Those soldiers are blood hungry. They want me dead! They say I'm a deserter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look like a commander to me.

speaker: Neokles
en: I don't recognize our army anymore. The things they do in the name of duty...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been sent to kill you, and that's exactly what I'm going to do, maláka.

speaker: Neokles
en: Please! I beg the gods to forgive you for this!

speaker: Kassandra
en: One less Athenian on Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll never survive on Delos. I have a ship. Can you fire a bow?

speaker: Neokles
en: I was an archer before I was a commander.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And now, you're an archer again. Find my ship, the Adrestia. A man named Barnabas will be waiting for you. He'll keep you safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thaletas? What are you and your men doing out in the open?

speaker: Thaletas
en: The Athenian cowards are too afraid to attack anyone on their sacred lands. We like coming here to taunt them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spartans... You're all the same.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I take that as a compliment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You haven't asked me about the commanders.

speaker: Thaletas
en: I already heard. Their forces are in chaos, and soldiers are defecting. Sparta owes you. I owe you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Careful. You never know what I'll ask for.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Ha! Try me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We may die tomorrow. If I could ask for anything, I'd ask for tonight... with you.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Kassandra, I...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't say anything. You have a battle to prepare for. And I have an Athenian army to weaken.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd ask for you, Thaletas. Now and forever by my side.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Kassandra, I...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't say anything. You have a battle to prepare for. And I have an Athenian army to weaken.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I would ask for Kyra.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Kyra...

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you. I want you both, Thaletas. I know the way you two feel about each other. But...

speaker: Thaletas
en: Kassandra, I... Maybe we should focus on the war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spartans. All war and no play.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more. I also found your helmet.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Kassandra. I would have died many deaths if not for this. I owe you more than just thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Focus, Thaletas. The end is in sight. The Delos Islands will be ours.

speaker: Thaletas
en: We're still outnumbered, but you haven't been wrong yet.

speaker: Thaletas
en: When you're not busy saving these islands, meet me on the beach, east of the Kynthos Ruins. There's something I want to show you. Look for the smoke.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You're a fine warrior. You've done much for the rebellion. And Sparta. But I sailed to these islands for Kyra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have honor, Thaletas. You don't know what you're missing, but you have honor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pan's flute! Xenia will love this.

speaker: Paios
en: Your next opponent is Doreius—claims to be descended from Herakles himself!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready.

speaker: Paios
en: You ever faced an Olympic champion before?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, but I've gotten this far.

speaker: Paios
en: Well, you don't look the part—you're not even oiled, for Zeus's sake!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do have some oil. It could come in handy... and it smelled good. I'll use it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Less talking. More fighting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've fought all sorts of people... and they were with more than just their fists. Let me in there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come to wish me luck?

speaker: Kallias
en: Of course, and if you win you should come dine with me sometime.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe I'll hunt you down after the event... To take you up on your offer.

speaker: Kallias
en: Of course... after the event.

speaker: Leander
en: Huh. You smell better than last time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's get this over with.

speaker: Leander
en: For Hera!

speaker: Leander
en: We've seen our esteemed newcomer rise quickly to become a contender... But let's see how she goes against our reigning champion... Doreius!

speaker: Leander
en: By the gods!

speaker: Dorieus
en: I will suck the marrow from your bones!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll have to try harder if you want to live!

speaker: Dorieus
en: I hope you like pain.

speaker: Leander
en: Just one mistake can change everything!

speaker: Leander
en: Victory! Nike!

speaker: Leander
en: The gods have looked kindly on these, our champions... but there can only be one winner! SPARTA!!!

speaker: Leander
en: Yours is eternal glory!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got your message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: A crate of good wine was lost at sea - pirates sank a merchant ship. I need that wine for tonight's banquet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can probably still get it back... if you don't mind getting wet.

speaker: Woman
en: Only someone truly brave would wade into those waters now. The pirates are still nearby, and I've heard rumors of a shark spotted close to the port.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I should kill all the sharks.

speaker: Woman
en: Ah. Not only do you possess the strength of Herakles, but the wits of Hermes, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'll do it.

speaker: Woman
en: Good. You're doing me a great service.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can leave everything to me.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: Job well done, mercenary. Here, this is yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Happy to help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to destroy all the pirate ships.

speaker: Woman
en: The horizon should be clear of ships once you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'm in.

speaker: Woman
en: Glad to hear it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, stranger.

speaker: Woman
en: Did you destroy them all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be hard to piece them back together.

speaker: Woman
en: You've earned your payment, misthios. Here. This is for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All in a day's work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The air is thick here. It's hard to breathe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "How was my day? Well, I killed a three-headed beast, got yelled at by Hades, and now I'm on my way to meet the ferryman of the underworld. How was yours?"

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sun gives off no warmth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you the ferryman?

speaker: Charon
en: A busy ferryman. Someone just had to kill the guardian of the gate, and now I'm up to my eyeballs in rotting newcomers. So unless some god sent you to plug all the holes and clean up the mess between the realms, I don't want anything to do with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It just so happens that Hades sent me.

speaker: Charon
en: What did a shiny, living fleshling like you do to end up in debt to the god of the underworld?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... may have killed Cerberos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: From all the stories I heard as a child about the ferryman, you are not what I was expecting.

speaker: Charon
en: Let me guess, you were expecting some withered mute made of bones, with flaming eyes and a cloak spun from the unfulfilled dreams of the departed. You fleshlings are all the same.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just thought you'd be taller.

speaker: Charon
en: Did someone send you to harass me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hades sent me. I may have killed his beast and caused this rift problem.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It started with marriage problems between gods, then I had to fight Cerberos... Long story short, this mess is probably all my fault.

speaker: Charon
en: Well, now that Hades' big dog is dead, rifts have opened all across the underworld. My passengers are being attacked by prisoners of Tartaros and all of his little dogs!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen, I have to find four guardians to protect the gates and close the rifts. Hades said you'd need my help.

speaker: Charon
en: Unbelievable. He sends a fleshling through the underworld to fix a problem only the dead can solve.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Only the dead can solve"... So that's why I felt so weak when I fought those things.

speaker: Charon
en: The last fleshling who worked for Hades wore a special suit of armor, but he's been torn to shreds. Now the armor's been scattered across the realm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mother told me my path would be tough, but she never prepared me for this.

speaker: Charon
en: And you're going to have to fight some pretty vengeful warriors to collect four of the pieces. The fifth, a set of gauntlets has gone missing.

speaker: Charon
en: You'll... do fine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What makes this armor I need so special?

speaker: Charon
en: Forged on the bronze anvil that fell into Tartaros, it allows fleshlings like yourself to see things they shouldn't see and go places they shouldn't go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course Hades never mentioned this.

speaker: Charon
en: He's very selective.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said something about prisoners?

speaker: Charon
en: The underworld's most horrific offenders are locked away in the prison of Tartaros. Many have escaped through the rifts and are putting the rest of us hard-working, dedicated, passionate souls in peril.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you mean exactly when you said "little dogs"?

speaker: Charon
en: The Hounds of Hades. Nasty little creatures who hunt and destroy the lost souls who weren't granted passage across the Styx by yours truly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to put this place back in order.

speaker: Charon
en: All you need to do is collect some armor, defeat angry warriors, and find four guardians to protect the underworld.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right.

speaker: Charon
en: Seeing as you're new here, I'll give you some advice. The Barren Pond, the Eternal Battlefield, and Hades' Palace are all excellent places to start.

speaker: Charon
en: And if you happen to have any spare time, I've got some work for you as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Headed to Odysseus's island on a tiny boat. Let's try not to piss off Poseidon, shall we?

speaker: Odessa
en: Hey, get me out of here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's get out of here. Can you fight?

speaker: Odessa
en: I'd be happy to.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Penelope's shroud. In the flesh. I mean cloth.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Kassandra. Good news, I hope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Safe and sound.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Well done. And now the shroud is yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't want it? After all that?

speaker: Elpenor
en: I gained something more valuable today. For your troubles, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I knew any better, I'd think you were testing me.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Perhaps.

speaker: Elpenor
en: You did well, misthios. Tell me, how do you feel about killing a general in Megaris? Do this for me, and earn double what you earned today. Are you up to the task? It would take you far away from Kephallonia. So far away you might never return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Generals bleed like anyone else.

speaker: Elpinor
en: Good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not an assassin.

speaker: Elpenor
en: There's a first time for everything.

speaker: Elpenor
en: What do you say?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is this general?

speaker: Elpenor
en: They call him "The Wolf."

speaker: Kassandra
en: He do something to offend you?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Yes... He's costing me drachmae. He's not good for business.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anything I should know about Megaris?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Only that it's the most valuable land in the Greek world, from a military perspective of course. Unfortunately for Megarians, it has two very powerful neighbors who just can't seem to play nice. In the tug of war between Korinth and Athens, Megaris is the rope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why me?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Because no one knows who you are. You're invisible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I accept.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Splendid. You'll need a boat. You have one, don't you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I had a boat, we wouldn't be having this conversation.

speaker: Elpenor
en: A shame. It's too far of a swim I'm afraid, even for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find one.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Good. I hope it's sturdy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And why is that?

speaker: Elpenor
en: The seas are much more dangerous, I'm afraid. War is coming, and the Wolf is on the wrong side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: War? With who?

speaker: Elpenor
en: The entire Greek world is at each other's throats. What rock have you been hiding under, exactly?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And how do I know you're on the right side?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Because I'm the one paying you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You won't be disappointed.

speaker: Elpenor
en: When your job in Megaris is done, come find me at Pilgrim's Landing in Phokis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's everything Perikles wanted. Time to return to him and find out what these Athenians know about my mother.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: We'll be watching you, misthios.

speaker: Athenian Marksman
en: Ah, at least give them a welcome first.

speaker: Athenian Light Soldier
en: Fine. Perikles welcomes you to his symposium.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Kassandra! It's you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe?

speaker: Phoibe
en: You promised we'd see each other again, and now we have!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I also said to stay out of trouble.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Which I have!

speaker: Phoibe
en: You said you weren't coming back to Kephallonia, so I decided to leave too!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I said I wouldn't be coming back, but I don't remember saying you should leave.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Well here I am!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you even get here, Phoibe?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Well... I did make some drachmae working for Markos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you paid someone to bring you to Athens?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Not exactly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I needed the drachmae for when I arrived. I couldn't use it all to leave, and I didn't want to wait any longer, so I sneaked on a ship. Don't worry, nobody saw!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just can't believe you made it.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I don't remember much of Athens from when I was a baby, but every once in a while, something feels familiar. It's nice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't believe you're here.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Me either! I can't believe we both made it to Athens. It's so much different than Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But what are you doing here?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I'm here to get you ready. I have to make sure you leave all your weapons and change into these clothes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, you somehow work here... For Perikles.

speaker: Phoibe
en: No. For Aspasia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't understand why I have to change.

speaker: Phoibe
en: It's just what you do here. I felt weird at first, but you forget about it pretty fast.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And my weapons?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Don't worry, I'll take care of them! You don't want to scare people in there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well...

speaker: Kassandra
en: How is it you're working for Aspasia?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Well, I did get into a little bit of trouble after I got to Athens. I may have been the leader of a small group of orphans that tried to cheat Aspasia. We didn't know it was her, though!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you... convinced her to hire you?

speaker: Phoibe
en: No, she asked me on her own!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was lucky.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I'm ready to go in.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You can't! Not like that, anyway. The Athenians like it best when you try to fit in. But don't worry, I have just the outfit for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get changed. Promise you'll take care of my things?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Yep. Leave your weapons in the corner, and I'll come back when you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I feel... uncomfortable in this.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Now you look like everyone else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You say that like it's a good thing.

speaker: Phoibe
en: It is! If you want them to take you seriously, this is the easiest way. Trust me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no way I'm wearing that.

speaker: Phoibe
en: But if you don't

speaker: Kassandra
en: I mean it, Phoibe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You have to leave your weapons here, though.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Don't say I didn't warn you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is that everything?

speaker: Phoibe
en: You're all ready to go in! Don't worry, you've done scarier things than this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm struggling to think of any right now. Are you sure I can't keep just one weapon with me?

speaker: Phoibe
en: No weapons! Now, hurry and go in. Oh, and don't leave without saying bye!

speaker: Phoibe
en: You just got here. You can't leave already!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Chaire, Kassandra! The mighty mercenary and traveler has finally made her grand entrance. Only slightly late, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos! Athenians have no problem letting me know when I'm not welcome. It's a relief to see your friendly face.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Don't let the company here tonight intimidate you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Perikles is no king. He needs these guests to love him, so that the people love him. And they, in turn, need Perikles. You're no different from any of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you really think these people will help me?

speaker: Herodotos
en: They will if you get them to trust you. And you've wisely dressed for the occasion. Appearing trustworthy is the most important part of being trusted, after all. Now then, come let me introduce you to everyone.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Perhaps your... individual fashion sense will get their memories working. Now then, come let me introduce you to everyone.

speaker: Herodotos
en: They may not look it, but this group holds the way to the future on the tip of their opinionated tongues.

speaker: Herotodos
en: Ah, Sophokles and Euripides, for example. Two of the most celebrated playwrights to date. No one can throw stones as far as they can. They appear to be locked in some kind of intellectual struggle, as is their way.

speaker: Sophokles
en: He's a writer of comedies, of all things! Comedies, Euripides!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard of Sophokles. In my line of work, it pays to know who the richest and most famous men are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It looks more like a lover's quarrel to me.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Hermippos has also written his fair share of comedies...

speaker: Hermippos
en: You should drink more.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Lately his attitudes have garnered him more notice than his works. However, the fellow beside him, Protagoras, is a sophist worthy of as much praise as the great Sokrates himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Inviting Sokrates seems like a good way to ruin everyone's night. I'm surprised they would let him in the door.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not sure "great" is the term I would use...

speaker: Herodotos
en: Oh, don't let Sokrates get under your skin. At least he wore shoes for the occasion... And the poor thing gesticulating like an ape is Thrasymachos. If you listen closely, you'll notice he and Sokrates are actually arguing the same points. But the wind from his wild gestures deafens him to critique.

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: That isn't at all what I mean!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is Perikles?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Oh! He never attends his own parties. Which reminds me, there's something I need to get his help with...

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Vile Sokrates! Always appearing where I least expect him. Warrior, protect me from his amorous gaze! ...Oh, Alkibiades. This is not a time for jealousy, but for love!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Let's not use Alkibiades as an example. Be good, and don't drink too much. So, tell me, what does a misthios like you think of a party like this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This party could be fun. Alkibiades drinks like a Spartan. Maybe he fights like one, too.

speaker: Herodotos
en: If I could suggest anything—please don't start a fight. Or end one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is going to be a long night. Parties should be about vomiting up blood, not vomiting up poetry. These people are so... clean.

speaker: Herodotos
en: If these guests aren't up to your own... unique tastes, then just focus on why you came here in the first place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, Herodotos.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Now, if you'll excuse me. Perikles is here somewhere, and I need to prepare him... If he's alone, I'll tell him what your brother said.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Agreed, Perikles needs to know. I'll stay here and look for clues.

speaker: Herodotos
en: I hope they know something about your mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your leaving me alone with these people?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Ha! You'll do fine without me. I promise. Just relax, talk to the others, and focus on finding your mother.

speaker: Metiochos
en: Thank you for your help, my friend.

speaker: Protagoras
en: Chaire! We were just discussing Hermippos's failures in his indictment of Aspasia.

speaker: Hermippos
en: Well, you were. I was sleeping with my eyes open.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And so it isn't the rich and powerful, but the gods who are the source of justice?

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: What? No! Have you been listening to nothing I say?

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: Yes, you come and talk to this infuriating air bladder. I've had my fill.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Perhaps later. First, explain to me your point again.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, the misthios from the ostracism! Let's talk later.

speaker: Protagoras
en: Of course, I only use terms war, or god, or civility, in context of what can be observed. So, I can observe soldiers fighting, but does that bring me any closer to understand war?

speaker: Hermippos
en: I haven't seen you around before, citizen. Perhaps you'd like to spare me conversing with this man of nonsense?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All you people do is talk. I'd rather not.

speaker: Hermippos
en: You're back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure, we can talk. What about?

speaker: Hermippos
en: Before Protagoras changed the subject, we were talking about the next greater leader of Athens—Kleon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw Kleon speaking at the Pnyx. He is a real man of the people.

speaker: Hermippos
en: So! You have a taste for politics. That's certainly better than most of the elitist blowhards in this house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I take it you and Perikles aren't friends.

speaker: Protagoras
en: Hardly! Hermippos led the charge to have Aspasia ostracized and to see Perikles stripped of power—not that it worked.

speaker: Hermippos
en: Yet. Perikles is the past. He's more worried about losing a few precious statues than he is fighting and winning the war. Kleon will rule this city and return it to greatness—mark my words.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for clues to help me find a woman. She was Spartan.

speaker: Protagoras
en: Looking and finding are quite different things, wouldn't you say? I could observe a priest offering sacrifice to the gods, but does that mean in so doing that I have, found god? Or...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, forget it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll change the subject again. I'm looking for someone—a Spartan woman.

speaker: Hermippos
en: Spartan? Hopefully she's dead in the gutters—it's better than those mongrels deserve.

speaker: Protagoras
en: I wonder... if you found the woman, even if you saw her with your own eyes, would you believe her existence to be true?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is getting nowhere. Forget it.

speaker: Protagoras
en: If you don't want to discuss that, then what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw Kleon talk at the Pnyx. Even for a politician, he's scum.

speaker: Hermippos
en: Bah, you sound like every other blowhard in this place. Kleon is a champion of the people, and he's ready to tear down Perikles' elitism.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I take it you and Perikles aren't friends.

speaker: Protagoras
en: Hardly! Hermippos led the charge to have Aspasia ostracized and to see Perikles stripped of power—not that it worked.

speaker: Hermippos
en: Yet. Perikles is the past. He's more worried about losing a few precious statues than he is fighting and winning the war. Kleon will rule this city and return it to greatness—mark my words.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for clues to help me find a woman. She was Spartan.

speaker: Protagoras
en: Looking and finding are quite different things, wouldn't you say? I could observe a priest offering sacrifice to the gods, but does that mean in so doing that I have, found god? Or...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, forget it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're an ally of Kleon, why would Perikles invite you?

speaker: Hermippos
en: You're not from Athens, outsider. Here, we keep our enemies closest of all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why isn't Aspasia here?

speaker: Protagoras
en: Can you be certain she isn't? To observe her presence is still no guarantee that she is here.

speaker: Hermippos
en: In my opinion, it's just like her to cower in the shadows while we stand out here in the light.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This has been... useless. Chaire.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, here comes the one who claims to value drachmae over the noble path that leads to knowledge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Like I told you, "knowledge" can't feed me.

speaker: Sokrates
en: But the mind must be fed as well!

speaker: Sokrates
en: Ah, if it isn't the one who agrees that knowledge is most important!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think we agreed our use of that knowledge couldn't be more different.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You remember! Perhaps that conversation can continue.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I admit, I'm surprised to see you here. But, "everything has a price," as you said. I can't help but wonder what price you paid to gain entry to this symposium.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keep wondering.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Being so new to Athens, and gaining access to this symposium, is no small feat. Though you said there are things you wouldn't do, you gained Perikles's trust so quickly...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've made my choice.

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: You really intend to use this young distraction to avoid the point being argued?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you've been arguing this long, and you haven't agreed yet, just give up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have been arguing a single point all night, and no one has a black eye? You have my attention.

speaker: Sokrates
en: We're discussing the nature of rulers. Where better to do so than here? I'll ask you the same question I asked Thrasymachos: would you agree that the act of ruling is an art?

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: It is an art, as all worthy undertakings are. That is not up for argument.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Yet, medicine is for the betterment of the patient, and not the physician. Carpentry improves the building, not the builder. Then—is the art of ruling not for the betterment of the ruled rather than the ruler?

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: Don't be absurd!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have seen enough of the world to know that there are no "just" rulers. Even Perikles is self-serving.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Is a Spartan general who brings order to his troops, thereby saving his own life, self-serving? I'm not sure that's the case.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ruling a city and fighting in battle are different things.

speaker: Sokrates
en: By practicing the art of war, doesn't the general guarantee some of his troops a ferry ride to Hades, when a swift retreat would save all their lives?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You just said a general isn't self-serving when he brings order to his troops. Then you said he is self-serving because retreating would save the lives of his men. What are you trying to say?

speaker: Sokrates
en: I never try to say anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you just said those things.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I said the words, but I didn't say anything at all. I only attempted to gain your view on the matter.

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: You're wasting your time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already had conversations like this with you, Sokrates. I'm not in the mood to spend the rest of my night standing here.

speaker: Sokrates
en: I'd never ask you to do such a thing! You've said plenty, and I feel I know you even better now.

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: Go while you still can. Perhaps you've loosened his ears to my point.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This argument between you two is pointless.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Perhaps. How do you define art?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not getting dragged into this.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Very well. Answer this: does the artist not give form and symmetry to her subject?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, yes.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Laws and justice do much the same for people, do they not? And is there any better way to communicate the story of a people than by revealing its customs and laws? If yes, then ruling, and thus justice, must be an art, as Thrasymachos says.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so.

speaker: Thrasymachos
en: Aspasia.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I couldn't help but notice your talent for debate. Well done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sokrates is an... interesting character.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You shouldn't be too hard on Sokrates. He really has a brilliant mind, even if he comes off a little strong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He isn't always like that, is he?

speaker: Aspasia
en: Ah, Phoibe. Perikles has retired to the balcony already, has he? His ability to sneak off and sulk is second to none.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I can go get him, and Kassandra can help! Everyone listens when she talks.

speaker: Aspasia
en: That'll be fine. Run along. Kassandra will be right behind you.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Now, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Aspasia. I had to go to great lengths to cover up your work in Megaris.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have no idea what you're talking about.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Oh now. To convince someone in this house, even your eyes must tell a lie.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, it was me. But my actions were personal, not political.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your spies have been watching me. I knew you people cannot be trusted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did what I had to do, and I'd do it again. I make no apologies.

speaker: Aspasia
en: We do what we must to survive, and there's no shame in that. It's how you got here—how I got here. The clothes, they fit you well, I trust?

speaker: Kassandra
en: These may be the nicest clothes I've ever worn, but I feel... a bit uncomfortable, to be honest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd be more comfortable in these clothes if I had a blade in my hand.

speaker: Aspasia
en: We do what have to to survive, and there's no shame in that, believe me. You make an interesting choice, Kassandra, in not dressing to fit in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fit in? Fancy clothes wouldn't help me fit in. Your Athenian s are strange to me.

speaker: Aspasia
en: You never really get used to them.

speaker: Aspasia
en: It seems we have the attention of the entire room without a single eye being fixed on us. If you'd like to talk, do it now, and do it discreetly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been searching for a woman named Myrrine... My mother. I think she may be in danger, and my search brought me here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm searching for a woman who fled Sparta with her child years ago. I was hoping you might help.

speaker: Aspasia
en: What clues do you have to her whereabouts?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A physician named Hippokrates may have seen her in Argos.

speaker: Aspasia
en: He's a good man. If you find a woman named Agathe there, let her know Aspasia sends her regards. What else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alkibiades gave me the name of a woman in Korinth.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'm sure he did. My dear friend, Anthousa, is the only one I know who's enjoyed a life in Korinth through legitimate means... mostly legitimate, anyway.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all I have.

speaker: Aspasia
en: There is another option. In a former life, when I needed something done, or someone found, I contacted a friend. An admiral, of a sort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's his name?

speaker: Aspasia
en: Her name is Xenia. When we last spoke, she was in Keos. A word of caution: when you go to her, be on your guard. Sea life makes a monster out of most people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you, Aspasia.

speaker: Aspasia
en: When you're done, return here. Together, we will find who you're looking for.

speaker: Aspasia
en: Now do me a favor and get Perikles to come down here to greet his guests.

speaker: Aspasia
en: I'll help you however I can during your travels.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Kassandra?

speaker: Perikles
en: I didn't send for you. No matter how you've dressed for my party, Phoibe shouldn't have let you in.

speaker: Perikles
en: I don't recall sending for you, misthios. Phoibe shouldn't have let you in here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aspasia told me to come find you. She wants you to come down to the party.

speaker: Perikles
en: She says I don't interact with our guests enough. But these parties aren't for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe did nothing wrong. Aspasia asked her to let me in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've been hiding from your guests long enough. Aspasia seems to think so, too.

speaker: Perikles
en: She usually does.

speaker: Perikles
en: Technically you're a guest. If you join Herodotos and me, that should be enough for her, don't you think?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You really don't want to go downstairs, do you?

speaker: Perikles
en: When your days are spent speaking in front of crowds, you begin to crave these moments of silence.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Or as silent as I let it be, at least.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phidias was awaiting trial, but you had me get him out of Athens. I figured you, of all people, would want to follow the law.

speaker: Perikles
en: Phidias is a very dear friend. I didn't want to risk him being found guilty. And, of course, there were other threats.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you knew.

speaker: Perikles
en: I know he's delusional, but... one day when you have a friend you'd do anything for, you'll understand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't understand why you had Anaxagoras ostracized. Sokrates said he was your friend.

speaker: Perikles
en: I won't risk the lives of those close to me if there's something I can do about it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you did this to protect him?

speaker: Perikles
en: Anaxagoras understood my fears. Ten years may be a long time, but at least he'll be safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why send Metiochos to the fishing district if it's dangerous?

speaker: Perikles
en: I would have never sent him into danger willingly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems you have many loyal friends.

speaker: Perikles
en: My people are important to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your life is in danger.

speaker: Perikles
en: Yes, yes. Herodotos was saying. This Cult doesn't worry me—I have my life threatened by far worse people every day. My true concern is Athens. I fear for her future.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Spartans aren't your real concern, Perikles. The Cult is coming. And they're bringing their strongest weapon.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Listen to her, Perikles.

speaker: Perikles
en: The Spartans are immediate. A Cult's threat is ambiguous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm... related to one of the Cult members. And I believe him when he says they're coming after you.

speaker: Perikles
en: Sound counsel to consider. I'll be sure to let my men know regardless.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spartans outside the walls, people crammed inside... I don't envy you.

speaker: Perikles
en: Even so, there isn't another city I'd rather live in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't say I know how that feels.

speaker: Perikles
en: When you find your place, you'll know it.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Aspasia sent me to see what's taking you so long.

speaker: Perikles
en: Tell Aspasia I'll be right there. I suppose this is where our conversation ends. Thank you again for helping me. I hope my guests are able to help you in your search.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time will tell.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You look tired!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Only of conversation. I think that's the most talking I've ever done.

speaker: Phoibe
en: See, you didn't need a weapon after all! Are you leaving?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've had enough to Athenian hospitality to last me a lifetime.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You get used to it. It's nice! What are you going to do now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a woman on the island of Keos that I need to meet. I think I'll head there first.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I've heard there are pirates there!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be sure to be careful.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There is a physician in Argolos that may be able to help me.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You're sick? You've never been sick!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, no, I'm fine. I just need to talk to him.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Okay, good. It would be weird if you were sick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a woman in Korinth I'd like to talk to.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I've heard about that place from Alkibiades... he says you don't go there to talk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alkibiades says a lot of things.

speaker: Phoibe
en: He sure does!

speaker: Phoibe
en: Before you go, I heard something from Aspasia... about Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it?

speaker: Phoibe
en: She said there was some sort of plague. You don't think... My friend... The blood fever...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't think like that. Whatever happened on Kephallonia isn't our fault. I'll go myself and find out if this plague even happened, OK?

speaker: Phoibe
en: OK... thanks. I knew I could count on you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not going to beg to come along this time?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Nope! I'm happy here, and this isn't Kephallonia. That means you'll be back!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's very true.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Plus, I really like working for Aspasia. She says she has a mission for me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see you soon, Phoibe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Bye, Kassandra.

speaker: Adonis
en: There she is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How's Leonidas fitting in?

speaker: Adonis
en: Morale's never been higher. Scouts are reporting Persephone's influence is weakening across Elysium. You're definitely causing havoc out there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't rest until it's done.

speaker: Adonis
en: You know, I'm starting to think Elysium isn't such a bad place with you in it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, if only you weren't in love with Aphrodite and trying to overthrow the Queen, and everyone else wasn't dead, Elysium would be perfect.

speaker: Adonis
en: All I'm saying is you breathe life into this world filled with dead people. Anyhow, we have a bit of a situation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm starting to see why Persephone won't let you leave.

speaker: Adonis
en: Wait a moment, whose side are you on?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where I'm going, there's no love like yours waiting for me.

speaker: Adonis
en: Perhaps you're going to the wrong place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So tell me, what's the right place?

speaker: Adonis
en: I wouldn't know. Aphrodite... she's not too fond of sharing. Let's focus, we have a bit of a situation to deal with.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe when Persephone is overthrown, we can leave Elysium together.

speaker: Adonis
en: But, Aphrodite...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aphrodite's not here... but I am.

speaker: Adonis
en: Clearly the gods have sent you to test me. My destiny is clear. Aphrodite has my heart. Now let's focus, we have a serious issue to deal with.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course we do.

speaker: Adonis
en: Persephone's guards have cut off supply lines, overtaken hideouts—secrets and locations she couldn't possibly have known without inside help. We suspect there's a spy in our midst.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who?

speaker: Adonis
en: One is a messenger. She was sent with crucial information to one of our camps. When she didn't return, we sent a scout. The entire camp was killed, and she was nowhere to be found. The other is a blacksmith. Soldiers love to gossip while getting their blades sharpened. We think he may have overheard some of our plans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a good start.

speaker: Adonis
en: What Persephone doesn't realize is two can play this game. A little spy of my own has penetrated the queen's inner circle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should tell me who they are so I don't accidentally... kill them.

speaker: Adonis
en: Whisper the words "violets only bloom in Elysium winters." Anyone who doesn't respond with "cold as Hades' heart" is free for the killing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Poetic. Now tell me where to find the messenger and the blacksmith.

speaker: Adonis
en: They both have homes in the village. Return to me once you're done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Definitely the house of a blacksmith.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, a list of people Adonis has spent time with. Mine and Persephone's names are on this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A note written to Aphrodite. The blacksmith told her everything. Adonis' escape plans, the rebellion...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the messenger's house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A broken piece from one of the Torches of Hypnos I destroyed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So Persephone knows we've recruited Leonidas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Detailed information about one of Adonis' rebel camps.

speaker: Adonis
en: And, who's the dirty spy? The messenger or the blacksmith?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Both have been spying on you. Both have information that could undo your rebellion.

speaker: Adonis
en: Lousy malákes! My scouts tell me they're on the move. We only have time to dispose of one before they disappear completely. Which is more dangerous to our cause?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The blacksmith had a list of people you've spent time with and a note to Aphrodite outlining your plans for escape.

speaker: Adonis
en: And what about the messenger?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She had detailed information about one of your rebel camps, a note to Persephone about Leonidas joining the fight, and a fragment of one of the mind-control devices I destroyed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The blacksmith. I'll go after him.

speaker: Adonis
en: Last I heard, he was spotted near the village.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Making me chase you will make your death even worse!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The blacksmith was working for Aphrodite. This news could break Adonis' heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The blacksmith is dead.

speaker: Adonis
en: That's something at least. There was an ambush. The messenger led Persephone's guards to one of our camps. No one survived. The messenger escaped.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The blacksmith could have led Persephone's guards to all your camps.

speaker: Adonis
en: Thank you, Kassandra. Once again, you've been a great help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis, I'm not sure how to tell you this. The blacksmith was working for Aphrodite.

speaker: Adonis
en: What? Why would you say that?

speaker: Adonis
en: My love, why?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one in Elysium is who they claim to be.

speaker: Adonis
en: I must escape this world of lies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The messenger needs to be stopped.

speaker: Adonis
en: Last I heard, she was spotted at a small rebel camp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The messenger is dead. The camp was ambushed—I did what I could. Any news on the blacksmith?

speaker: Adonis
en: He escaped. If he reports back to Persephone, many lives are in danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Our next move needs to be swift and deadly.

speaker: Adonis
en: Meet me later at the Palace of the Kolossi. I've acquired a little something that will turn Persephone's paradise upside down.

speaker: Hermes
en: Keeper, there you are. The queen is in Deukalion's Heritage and requires your presence. She says it's quite urgent.

speaker: Hermes
en: There you are. The queen is in Deukalion's Heritage and requires your presence. Don't keep her waiting.

speaker: Natakas
en: Look.

speaker: Natakas
en: A weapons demonstration.

speaker: Soldier
en: We weren't expecting you, Tempest

speaker: The Tempest
en: My weapons, lieutenant. Where are they?

speaker: Soldier
en: They're installed, but not tested.

speaker: The Tempest
en: Fire them.

speaker: Soldier
en: But it's not stable

speaker: The Tempest
en: Fire. Them.

speaker: The Tempest
en: You stay here.

speaker: Soldier
en: F-Fire!

speaker: The Tempest
en: Fix this. By tomorrow.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Y-yes, Admiral.

speaker: The Tempest
en: The Skylla awaits my return. But first, I will inspect your work in the shipyards and see what else you idiots have managed to mess up. Move!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Tempest.

speaker: Natakas
en: This won't be easy. Especially if they get that weapon to work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ha! They couldn't even get it to work properly.

speaker: Natakas
en: It's only a matter of time before they succeed. We need to do something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they manage to harness that kind of power... the Adrestia might not be able to match it.

speaker: Natakas
en: I don't think a fleet could. We need to be a step ahead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like you have a plan.

speaker: Natakas
en: We need to go after her. If we can end things here, we're all the better for it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need to catch her. Let's go to the shipyard.

speaker: Natakas
en: It's not too far. Come on.

speaker: Child
en: My pater left to sell our goods on Delos, he was supposed to be back by now. Will he be in danger? They're blowing up ships. How will he get home?

speaker: Child
en: It'll be OK! I'm sure he'll be back soon.

speaker: Civilian
en: What's going on here? How am I supposed to work with all this debris around?

speaker: Civilian
en: You have no right shutting down our harbors.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: This is for your own safety. The waters are a dangerous place to be now.

speaker: Commander
en: You heard the Tempest! Double all production and rebuild them from scratch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The shipyard.

speaker: Natakas
en: The Tempest will be easier to find if we split up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just food and kitchen supplies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The woman in charge. Do you know her?

speaker: Civilian
en: I—I don't know anything. Please leave me alone...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something doesn't feel right.

speaker: Worker
en: The Tempest can't find me... She'll kill me! The weapons aren't ready. They are not ready!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The woman who came by here. Where is she?

speaker: Civilian
en: She left... I hope. Poseidon save us...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something is out there... Or someone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for the woman who runs this place.

speaker: Civilian
en: The weapon is not ready. It's not! It's

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone is following me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you seen the woman in charge here?

speaker: Civilian
en: Don't let them hear you. There are eyes and ears everywhere.

speaker: Natakas
en: Kassandra. Quickly, over here!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't find the Tempest.

speaker: Natakas
en: I found this

speaker: Natakas
en: The Order suspects we're here in Achaia. They've tasked the Tempest with capturing us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We walked into a trap.

speaker: Natakas
en: Father. He'll need to hear about this. Quickly

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're being followed.

speaker: Natakas
en: No, we're being hunted.

speaker: Natakas
en: There, that warehouse. I'll draw their attention and hide. You can take it from there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. Cause a scene and head to the warehouse. I'll stay back and see how many there are before making a move.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you ready

speaker: Natakas
en: How could you? I loved you! You monster. Don't come near me!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Let's split up and look for her. She could be somewhere nearby.

speaker: Mercenary
en: The Eagle Bearer is no easy opponent. Be on your guard.

speaker: Natakas
en: Kassandra! You made it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just in time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. I'll run to the warehouse and get their attention.

speaker: Natakas
en: Have it your way... But don't leave me behind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't. I want you to have my back.

speaker: Natakas
en: That's more like it. Go, go!

speaker: Natakas
en: Is that all you've got?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's over.

speaker: Mercenary
en: You won't get away with this. The Tempest will hunt you down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where the Tempest is... What's her plan?

speaker: Mercenary
en: She's building a weapon to be installed on her ship, the Skylla. And she's locked down all of Achaia to trap you, Eagle Bearer. There's nowhere left to run. The Skylla will blow you out of the water. Her fleet will crush you!

speaker: Mercenary
en: You'll never defeat her...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go. I'll see your father first, then meet you at the ship hideout.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Tempest is looking for us, then destroying her fleet should get her attention.

speaker: Natakas
en: They tried to trap us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We almost had the Tempest.

speaker: Natakas
en: At least the Order has lost our scent. For now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Be safe, Natakas. I'll see you later at the ship hideout.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's destroy the patrols before they call for reinforcements.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Some fleet, Tempest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the one who left the message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: A man in the city will not leave my friend in peace. He is infatuated, truly... he follows her, begs her...

speaker: Kassandra
en: He sounds obsessed with her. Does she... like that?

speaker: Woman
en: Of course not. What started out as a silly crush has become something much worse. His words now make her think he will do her harm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you want me to send him to the Ferryman.

speaker: Woman
en: His blood must be spilled.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll handle this.

speaker: Woman
en: Then I can rest easy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Woman
en: You again. Have you killed him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Woman
en: Thank you for all you've done. Please, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe I can convince them to stand up for Sokrates at the trial.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: It's as Xenophanes said, of course! We have given the gods human forms because we wish them to be as we are.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: No, they are as they are. Who are we to give form to the gods?

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Exactly my point! As he said, if oxen or horses or any beast could produce art as we do, they would form the gods in the image of themselves.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: Yes, well they can't. And you've simply shown me again why Xenophanes is problematic.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Come now, don't be like that. It's OK to be wrong... sometimes.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: Ha! I wouldn't know what that's like.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Do not students take what they learn from their teachers? What then if the teacher is wrong? Does that not simply perpetuate these wrong teachings among future generations?

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: You assume the students aren't wise enough to understand the flaws of the teacher. Think of those who came before us. First Thales, then his student Anaximandros, and then Anaximenes. Without the teachings of those before him, it's safe to say Anaximenes would not have reached the conclusions he did.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: I don't think that's true. Perhaps this new face can offer a different perspective.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never heard the names you just mentioned.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: It's never too late to learn. But even so, one doesn't need to know who they are to answer. Is it not a risk that wrong ideas will be passed along if a student doesn't have the wisdom to seek the truth?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't hear a single thing you just said.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Is that so? Well, let me simplify it quickly. Thales taught Anaximandros, who taught Anaximenes. Wouldn't you agree that students learn from the failings of their teachers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never heard the names you just mentioned.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: It's never too late to learn. But even so, one doesn't need to know who they are to answer. Is it not a risk that wrong ideas will be passed along if a student doesn't have the wisdom to seek the truth?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A student gets to take all the knowledge of their teacher without needing to come up with answers themselves. If they're smart, they should surpass those they studied under.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: An astute observation. The time saved by receiving the knowledge allows the student not only to expand on the ideas, but to come up with more of their own. But what if the student expands on ideas without first seeking the truth behind them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A student gets to take all the knowledge of their teacher without needing to come up with answers themselves. If they're smart, they should surpass those they studied under.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: An astute observation. The time saved by receiving the knowledge allows the student not only to expand on the ideas, but to come up with more of their own. But what if the student expands on ideas without first seeking the truth behind them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If we listen to others and take what they say as fact, we only have ourselves to blame.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: So, no matter who is speaking, student or teacher, we must spend time trying to understand if what they say is even true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If a student asks questions before first learning from their teacher, they've not only failed their teacher, but themselves.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: Yes. And more would do well to challenge what they hear.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Your appearance betrays you, misthios. Clearly you've taken on a teacher of your own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something like that. He's the reason I'm here. Sokrates needs your help.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: Sokrates? Ha! If it's another debate you want, it will be hard for us to decide who hates that man more. Why would we help him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can either help him, or I can show you that I'm not a misthios only in looks.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: I didn't realize Sokrates taught his students to harm those who disagree with them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a different student than you're used to.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: We wouldn't stand a chance against you in a fight, but that doesn't mean we'll do what you say through threat of violence. You've been an interesting part of the conversation thus far, so we'll give you another chance. Why should we help Sokrates?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't matter if he's your worst enemy. If they're willing to imprison someone like Sokrates only for his words, what's to say they won't do the same to you?

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: So you want us to help out of fear of being imprisoned ourselves?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't care why you help. If I hadn't said his name, would you think it was right Sokrates was locked up?

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: If it's as you say and it was for his words, then no.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And aren't you afraid it could happen to you, too?

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: Of course. If we can't speak our words, what else are we to do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you believe that, then you should help.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: Fine, fine, you've made your point and you've made it well. Sokrates deserves our help, but we don't give it lightly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That makes it worth even more.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: We'll be on our way then. We'll gather some others as well. Make sure our voices are heard. Believe it or not, we're pretty good at causing a scene.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're like Sokrates, that's not hard to believe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shouldn't we help those in need?

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: As much as we possibly can, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And isn't Sokrates in need?

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: I suppose so...

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you saw a traveler wounded on the side of the road, would you help him, or would you first find out if he was a good person?

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Obviously we would rush to help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right now, Sokrates is that wounded traveler. He needs your help.

speaker: Philosopher 1
en: Fine, fine. You've made your point and you've made it well. Sokrates deserves our help, but we don't give it lightly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That makes it worth even more.

speaker: Philosopher 2
en: We'll be on our way then. We'll gather some others as well. Make sure our voices are heard. Believe it or not, we're pretty good at causing a scene.

en: If you're like Sokrates, that's not hard to believe.

en: If it's as you say and it was for his words, then no.

en: And aren't you afraid it could happen to you, too?

en: Of course. If we can't speak our words, what else are we to do?

en: We'll be on our way then. We'll gather some others as well. Make sure our voices are heard. Believe it or not, we're pretty good at causing a scene.

en: If you're like Sokrates, that's not hard to believe.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Wow, I've never seen someone convince them so easily before!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is that so? Guess I should feel proud. I'm surprised to see a child here.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Is there an age where it would suddenly be OK to debate with them? What then of the night before I turn that age? Should we be prevented from doing what we wish due to the world's view of us?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't even have a normal conversation with a child.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Normal is no fun! Look around. Everyone here wants the same thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Headaches?

speaker: Aristokles
en: Debate!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I regret doubting you at all.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Thank you! There are few things greater than gaining the understanding of another.

speaker: Kassandra
en: On that we disagree.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Disagreements can lead to even more understanding!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the first kid I've met who'd rather debate than play.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Don't tell the others, but I'm envious you're a student of Sokrates. I hope one day to be one as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're on the right path. What's your name?

speaker: Aristokles
en: Aristokles. Although, I've never liked that name much.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It does sound like countless others I've heard around Athens. Why not choose another?

speaker: Aristokles
en: I can do that? Hmm... my brother always had a problem saying my name, so he called me Plato instead. Perhaps I'll use that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I like it.

speaker: Aristokles
en: Thank you. Well, I better hurry after the others. Chaire!

speaker: Photios
en: Kassandra! Get over here, you spineless jellyfish, you!

speaker: Photios
en: Maláka! If it isn't the Eagle Bearer herself. You got big since Kephallonia!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you got old, Photios the Dog's Breath! Last time I saw you, I think I lit your ship on fire.

speaker: Photios
en: My ship and my beard. These days, thankfully, I've semi-retired.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do people pay mercenaries here more than they did in Kephallonia.

speaker: Photios
en: Course they do! Better than Markos, that's for sure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone pays more than Markos. You're lucky I took all his crazy contracts.

speaker: Photios
en: I was a learner—he's a rotten cheat! I only accept the easy stuff now. I'm working as a watchman this very moment. A cushy job... most days.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could use a break myself.

speaker: Photios
en: Some break this is! Today feels just like old times. The job got harder than anticipated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Once a mercenary, always a mercenary. It's a job you can never shake off.

speaker: Photios
en: Right you are. I'm learning that all the more now. Trouble goes, then comes back twice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did something happen?

speaker: Photios
en: A couple of priests ransacked this treasury. They took the sapphires offered by a Thrakian king, the bastards.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your employer won't like that.

speaker: Photios
en: No, but you'll like this. Make an example of the thieves. You find them and the sapphires, and I'll pay you much better than you're used to in Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'll help you, but...

speaker: Photios
en: But what?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't forgotten the old days. I owe you one, Photios. No reward necessary.

speaker: Photios
en: Ha! I thought I was getting soft.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know my help doesn't come cheap, Photios.

speaker: Photios
en: You were always reliable. Deadly, and drachmae hungry, but reliable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, I'm hunting priests. Where do I start?

speaker: Photios
en: Priests aren't used to thief business... They probably hid somewhere quiet. Check the caves west of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wouldn't expect priests to be jewel thieves.

speaker: Photios
en: They didn't take the drachmae or the silver. They knew those sapphires were the most valuable things here. That's priest knowledge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shouldn't be long before I find them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the cave Photios mentioned. Those priests came this way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's one of the priests. But no sign of the sapphires.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nice view. And there's the Desphina Fort to the south.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come to think of it, I found a dead priest. He had a letter on him.

speaker: Photios
en: Well slap me silly and call me Hermes! That's them alright. Any clues?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It said something about going to the Desphina Fort to sell their loot. I'll head that way.

speaker: Bloody Sapphires
en: This satchet contains the treasury sapphires — but covered in blood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here they are. A bit of blood on them, but the sapphires still shine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good news. Found the sapphires.

speaker: Photios
en: Should I ask why they're bloody?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The priests couldn't cut it as thieves.

speaker: Photios
en: You said you'd do it for free, but we both know that was horse shit. Here, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, old man.

speaker: Photios
en: If I were only a little bit younger, I might've tried to cheapen the reward a bit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good thing you got old.

speaker: Photios
en: Here's a little trinket from the treasury. No one will miss it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's hope not, or you'll send another mercenary after me. Goodbye Photios.

speaker: Photios
en: If you ever see that dog Markos again, tell him you demand minimum wage!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, these sapphires are really valuable, right?

speaker: Photios
en: You spawn of a salty slimeworm, you have them already, don't you? Hand them over. And don't you dare tell me I can't pay you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Great to see you again, Photios. Savor your retirement.

speaker: Photios
en: And you savor your youth! Don't become a washed-up seadog like me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These look like the ruins Diona spoke about. Best be on my guard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Poison... a coward's weapon. Diona will want this back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the last one. Time to head back to Olympia and Phidias to find out what all this means.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This won't be an easy task, but whatever the messages reveal must be important...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phidias! I should've never doubted that you were in danger.

speaker: Natakas
en: You're back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You did well back at Potidaia. But we still need more information about the Huntsman.

speaker: Natakas
en: You're right. We know he commands an army of animals, but Makedonia's a huge

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll follow up on the other leads.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've killed the Recruiter, your father was there too. He didn't have much to say about the Huntsman apart from the fact that he's near a lake.

speaker: Natakas
en: And my father? Where is he

speaker: Kassandra
en: He left to continue his search. Don't worry Natakas.

speaker: Natakas
en: Easy for you to say.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That contact of yours in the wetland led me to a madman. I believe it might've been the Huntsman himself.

speaker: Natakas
en: If you're back here looking the way you are, he must've gotten away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He won't the next time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should go back to Natakas with these clues. He might know what to make of them.

speaker: Natakas
en: You're back. What did you find?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Clues. Maybe you'll know what to do with them. One, the Huntsman is supposed to be waiting in the forest. Two, he's surrounded by animals. And three, he's by a lake.

speaker: Natakas
en: I think I know where that might be. There's a crack in a cliff face that leads to a glade. If it's where I think it is...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go!

speaker: Natakas
en: I can't, not yet. This is the Huntsman. We've suffered at his blades for years. Father should be there to see him die. I'll find him and join you at the glade.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Huntsman's in this glade, I won't be able to wait for you and Darius.

speaker: Natakas
en: I'll be there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I picked up your message on the board. What's happening?

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: Not much food around lately. Since the plague, there not enough farmers, and too many desperate hunters. I'm going to try for fish.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds sensible.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: There's sharks in these waters, though. I'm not equipped for those. But you seem well-armed.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: So I should kill all the sharks.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: Yes, all of them must die.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll handle this.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: Thank you, misthios. I couldn't do this without you.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: Great work. Take this as thanks, misthios.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: I have a good crew, but we're missing someone with your talents. I want you on board with us. What do you say?

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Man
en: Never considered myself a seaman... But an adventurer? I'll join you.

scene: Plagues, Sharks, and Other Good Times
speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I start.
