speaker: Praxilla
en: Ah, Kassandra, thwarter of thieves. I appreciate you bringing Achaikos back to me, but I need to ask another favor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You need help fixing the lyre?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Perceptive, too. Look at it. Wood's gone soft, body's splintered. It's toneless, tuneless even.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can be done to save it?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Kreusis has been having this festival for years. The town is built around it. Of course, because instruments are as fragile as a poet's heart, there's a master lyre maker at Kreusis Port.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not too far away.

speaker: Praxilla
en: And since it's been proven that nothing is safe on these hills, I'll need some muscle for protection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can help you get there safetly.

speaker: Praxilla
en: The journey will be worth your while. Come now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm right behind you.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I have many fond memories of this place. I've watched the port grow into a town, and a small gathering of freinds grow into a massive festival. It's more home than home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your true love is a lyre, and your home is a poetry festival? You never wanted to settle somewhere?

speaker: Praxilla
en: You sweet young child! My life isn't as simple as you make it out to be. I'm like , needing to go where I please. I learned this the hard way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you care only for yourself?

speaker: Praxilla
en: If you only live your life for others, what's the point? You're nothing but a slave... a loyal beast, at best.

speaker: Kassandra
en: People can get hurt.

speaker: Praxilla
en: If I had lived the life expected of me, traditional and domestic, I would have died. Died inside, and like as not thrown myself into the sea. I know what I need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Seems like the festival here is much less formal than the others I've encountered.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Yes. Dionysos claimed our offerings to Apollo and granted us the gift of ecstasy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can see why it would attract people from far and wide.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Do not misunderstand. Hedonism is one part of worship, but there are many here who dedicate themselves to the strings and to the verse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Timycha! Where are you?

speaker: Timycha
en: Who is making all of that fucking noise?

speaker: Praxilla
en: Ah, the smell of the sea is almost enough to cover your stench, Timycha.

speaker: Timycha
en: Praxilla! I've been gathering fruits to throw at you all week.

speaker: Praxilla
en: High praise coming from you. I need a favor. Achaikos was kidnapped by some idiot and needs a new neck.

speaker: Timycha
en: This idiot?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This idiot carries a sharp spear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sadly, there have been many idiots on this journey.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I hired this muscle here to get Achaikos back. Now she's keeping me company.

speaker: Timycha
en: All right, give him here.

speaker: Timycha
en: Poor fellow's been brutalized.

speaker: Praxilla
en: But you can fix it, right?

speaker: Timycha
en: Of course I can fix him. I am the best pair of hands you're gonna find outside of Athens. Problem is, Achaikos is a special boy. I have materials, but nothing worthy of putting him together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What materials do you need?

speaker: Timycha
en: I have what I need for the neck, but the old one took the strings and yoke out when it snapped. Ah, and there's a crack running through the sound box. That needs to be replaced.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What should I be looking for?

speaker: Timycha
en: Some use bone for the yoke and neck, but nothing beats wood in my opinion. Strings are made from gut, and we could use a shell for the sound box.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those strings don't look like guts to me.

speaker: Timycha
en: They are. Just soaked for a long time and pulled thin. I'm sure you'll enjoy killing some legendary beasts to help Achaikos sing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen some lyres with turtle shells for the body.

speaker: Timycha
en: Not a lot of turtles on this coast, but a good sturdy conch should do the trick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's a yoke, and what wood do you need to replace it?

speaker: Praxilla
en: The yoke is the crossbar that all of the strings are attached to.

speaker: Timycha
en: Sure is. It needs to bend, so a springy wood is best.

speaker: Praxilla
en: I think we all can agree on that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will return with the materials to repair Achaikos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wolves are fierce animals. I'll gut them for Praxilla.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hope these are enough guts for fixing Achaikos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This shell should be perfect for Praxilla's lyre.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should be enough wood for a new lyre.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have everything we need.

speaker: Timycha
en: Excellent, give it here.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Be careful with it!

speaker: Timycha
en: He'll like me better when I'm done. You always were too rough with your fingering.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Well, that's the first complaint I've heard about it.

speaker: Timycha
en: There he is, looking more handsome than ever.

speaker: Praxilla
en: You call this your best work? You're robbing me blind.

speaker: Timycha
en: Oh, shut up and go deafen the masses with your wailing.

speaker: Praxilla
en: Thanks for the help. Here's your drachmae. I need some time to put Achaikos through his paces. I might need some help after though, so swing by my tent when you have a minute.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure, if I'm in the area.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're... They're all dead.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The crew fought off what they could, but we were too late.

speaker: Doctor
en: Cursed Cult guards, misthios, look what they've done. They've killed them. My poor pets slaughtered like animals.

speaker: Barnabas
en: We have to move, Neleus may be in danger. I'll ready the ship.

speaker: Doctor
en: You should go. There's nothing left you can do here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Save your strength. You may still survive this.

speaker: Doctor
en: I'm a physician, misthios. I know when a patient is dying. Here, the antidote I promised. I always right my wrongs. Yes, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll give this to Neleus.

speaker: Doctor
en: It's his best hope. But don't expect a miracle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't leave you like this.

speaker: Doctor
en: You can kill me and end my misery once and for all. Please, it's all I ask.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What exactly happened to all these people? It looks like a slaughter.

speaker: Doctor
en: The Cult guards happened. Yes, yes. It was a slaughter. They were here to send a message to you, misthios. They know you've been snooping around.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hold still so I can make it clean.

speaker: Doctor
en: Thank you, misthios.

speaker: Doctor
en: I'm ready, misthios. Do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was still some good you might have done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't just kill you. There must be another way.

speaker: Doctor
en: Please, misthios. The alternative is I lay here and die slowly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Cult guards did this, I'll need to hurry back. Neleus.... There won't be much time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need to move fast. The Cult guards are on a rampage.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah, but I've sent some crew ahead to check on Neleus. They should bring him back to the ship so we can keep a closer eye on him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This madness needs to stop.

speaker: Barnabas
en: But it will! We have the Eagle Bearer on our side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's the Cult.

speaker: Barnabas
en: They mean to keep us from Neleus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, Barnabas. We'l' sink them.

speaker: Barnabas
en: With you at the helm? Ah, yes, the Cult is doomed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The villagers are dead. I need to hurry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm too late.

speaker: Elder
en: Yes! A misthios. Kill those masked malákes. Kill them good.

speaker: Cult Guardian
en: The misthios! Get her!

speaker: Elder
en: This is an outrage. We've had enough of those masked soldiers. They need to leave Lemnos one way or another!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did they burn this house?

speaker: Elder
en: You know why. Maláka... Those cursed soldiers came down here from their cursed stronghold. They thought Mikkos was up to something. Working against them. This has to end!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It will end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those soldiers are Cult guards, and there is a general among them. Don't worry, they won't be here much longer.

speaker: Elder
en: Yeah! Because we're going to go up there to end this. Right?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should all stay home. Keep each other safe. I'll take care of the Ancient Stronghold and the Cult guards.

speaker: Elder
en: Yes, you're right. Maláka, you're right. They're professional soldiers. We're humble merchants and fishermen. We're counting on you, misthios. They have plagued this region for too long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now's my chance to take this stronghold.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the general.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The villagers won't have to worry about these Cult guards again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people of this island deserve revenge against the Cult guards.

speaker: Elder
en: That's right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We will storm their stronghold and retake it for the people of Lemnos.

speaker: Elder
en: That's right! Leave us to gather our weapons, misthios. We'll meet you at the gates.

speaker: Elder
en: The misthios is here. It's time, everyone. Ready your weapons and CHARGE!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the general.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shouldn't have encouraged the villagers to fight. They're all dead now.

speaker: Barnabas
en: What did you find? Are they OK? Did you run into the crew I sent? They haven't returned either.

speaker: Roxana
en: Not so fast, champion. We found Mikkos and Neleus before the Cult arrived.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Neleus! Thank Zeus!

speaker: Neleus
en: Hello, uncle.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Let him go. He needs to rest.

speaker: Roxana
en: We arrived just before the Cult burned the house. They probably think Mikkos and Neleus are dead.

speaker: Mikkos
en: We're here!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Neleus!

speaker: Mikkos
en: They found us just before the Cult guards arrived. We were nearly killed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're lucky Neleus wasn't killed. It sounds like certain death was just minutes away. Here, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You did the right thing, sending the crew to check on them. They'd be dead if you hadn't.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I don't think I would have, except you told me to be easier on Neleus. I thought better to lend help rather than to leave him in the shadow of my tough love.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Glad I could help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Drink that. It should help you get better.

speaker: Barnabas
en: And what of all the other villagers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm afraid many of them charged the Cult stronghold along with me. None survived.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Such loss of life. At least I have Neleus. And you, Eagle Bearer. Come, Neleus. We have much catching up to do.

speaker: Barnabas
en: And how about the villagers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The villagers are fine. I sent them home and chased the Cult out of their stronghold myself.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You continue to amaze, Kassandra. You didn't just save my nephew, you saved all of Lemnos and Thasos from the Cult guards plaguing them. Come Neleus. I have many stories to catch you up on.

speaker: Roxana
en: Finally. I thought they would never leave.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's been a while, hasn't it, Roxana?

speaker: Roxana
en: Too long. Do you have some time now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Since you joined our ship, I haven't seen much of you. What have you been doing?

speaker: Roxana
en: Oh, you know, the typical things. Firing flaming arrows, bracing for impacts... and rowing. Lots and lots of rowing. Look at these arms.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For you, Roxana, I can make time.

speaker: Roxana
en: Good. I've got a couple minutes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was thinking a couple hours.

speaker: Roxana
en: Let's try one minute at a time.

speaker: Mikkos
en: We're all alone now, misthios. After such an adventure, I'm sure you want to take some to relax.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So much has happened. Has it changed what you will do now?

speaker: Mikkos
en: It hasn't changed a thing. We will rebuild the house and we will rebuild Neleus's stamina. He will be an Olympian yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know, I would like to relax.

speaker: Mikkos
en: In my younger days, I was known for my massages.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't want a massage.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Then what do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: First, I want you to kiss me. Then, I'll want you to take me somewhere private. Finally, I'll want you to take off all of your clothes.

speaker: Mikkos
en: As you command.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm afraid there is still too much to do. Too many to kill. Relaxing is not an option.

speaker: Mikkos
en: That's unfortunate. I thought... Well, I thought... Nevermind what I thought. I see how it is. Goodbye, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Goodbye, Mikkos. And good luck.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's Darius.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone killed these Spartans... and hid them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There you are. Those Spartan guards down the hill... Why hide them?

speaker: Darius
en: If Order guards saw their fallen allies, they'd be on high alert. Buys me time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found you.

speaker: Darius
en: I'm found when I want to be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Natakas says you found something. Could it lead to the Huntsman?

speaker: Darius
en: The Order has been making plans. You want "the Huntsman"? Then stick around and help me stop them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm listening.

speaker: Darius
en: One of the Huntsman's lieutenants is in charge of recruitment for the Order in Makedonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So we locate him and we'll have a lead.

speaker: Darius
en: Look for any notes, messages, ledgers—they will tell us where the next meeting is. And do it quietly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll rip through that fort and deal with what's to come.

speaker: Darius
en: You lack foresight. But the choice is yours—just get what we need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do my best not to be seen.

speaker: Darius
en: Good.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you?

speaker: Darius
en: I'll go down to the village and find out when the meeting is taking place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I'm done at the fort, I'll meet you there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's what I'm looking for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Darius said to keep this quiet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Meet me tonight beneath our favorite tree. I need you." Hmm... Steamy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "The goats shall bleed, and the moths will draw to the flame. The snake will be reborn. New fangs, new skin, new life." Maybe Darius will know what this means.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Food shipment delivered. Village cook has verified contents." Ordinary receipt, not helpful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should be everything. Time to meet Darius.

speaker: Darius
en: Over here.

speaker: Darius
en: How did it go?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everything went well. No one even knew I was there.

speaker: Darius
en: Indeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They saw me. Security was tight.

speaker: Darius
en: There may be consequences.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was fine

speaker: Darius
en: I could hear you all the way from here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then why ask?

speaker: Darius
en: Integrity is important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you make of those? They don't look like secret messages.

speaker: Darius
en: This note. New fangs? New recruits. And bleeding goats

speaker: Darius
en: A goat farm, like this one. That's where the meeting will be. The Order uses goat's blood in their initiation rituals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The notes meant nothing to me. Your knowledge of the Order is helpful. What else do you know?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know too much about the Order.

speaker: Darius
en: I don't know enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you know?

speaker: Darius
en: I know the meeting is soon. There's always a signal to draw them in.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There must be more to the note.

speaker: Darius
en: This part about moths to a flame...

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they use goat farms, they might have been here. We should look around for clues.

speaker: Darius
en: True. Where do you want to start?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That granary over there. It's small but full, I'm sure people still flock to it like

speaker: Darius
en: Bees to honey? I don't think so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me neither.

speaker: Darius
en: This is about flames and fire. There's something here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe that rack of wine jars over there by the house... There could be goat's blood stored in them for the Order ritual.

speaker: Darius
en: We already solved the goat part.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right.

speaker: Darius
en: This is about flames and fire. There's something here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those pyres of hay... There are soot marks at the base.

speaker: Darius
en: What of it?

speaker: Darius
en: Look. Soot and ash.

speaker: Darius
en: They must have used some of these pyres in their last meeting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're onto something. This does seem suspicious.

speaker: Darius
en: Take a closer look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those? If they used hay for the fire, there wouldn't be any left

speaker: Darius
en: Look closer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Somebody has been burning hay here. The flames are the signal.

speaker: Darius
en: Which means night is the only time they can meet because

speaker: Kassandra
en: Moths to a flame.

speaker: Darius
en: That's right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We just have to wait for the meeting to start.

speaker: Darius
en: There's another goat farm nearby, across the bridge.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. I'll meet you there at nightfall.

speaker: Darius
en: I found a place to watch the meeting. We'll wait there.

speaker: Darius
en: The meeting is soon. Come.

speaker: Bubares
en: The Huntsman will be pleased with this turnout.

speaker: Darius
en: The Recruiter.

speaker: Bubares
en: To the matter at hand—the Eagle Bearer! Your mission is simple.

speaker: Bubares
en: Bring me her head!

speaker: Bubares
en: There's been a disturbance at the Olynthos Fortress. Artabanus must be behind this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Artabanus?

speaker: Bubares
en: Your mission is to find the Eagle Bearer, but if you bring me both of them—All the better.

speaker: Darius
en: I'll flank them. Don't let him get away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We shouldn't split up. Don't

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need your help. Just

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait for the meeting to end... Or go in now? Where did Darius go?

speaker: Bubares
en: There you are. I'll take your head myself, Eagle Bearer. The Huntsman will be pleased.

speaker: Bubares
en: The numbers here are sufficient. But the Huntsman needs more. Drink and consider yourself one of us! You will play an important part in restoring balance and order to your homeland. The Eagle Bearer alone is at fault for Makedonia's woes. The blood, the bodies! Tragic. So very tragic. The Order is the answer. We will rid your lands of this Tainted One. With her gone, Makedonia's balance will be restored. We've drawn the Eagle Bearer to Makedonia. Now go! Find her.

speaker: Captain
en: Recruitment is going well, sir. But most of them can't fight. They are villagers, farmers—They stand no chance agaisnt the Eagle Bearer. You saw what she did at the village we burned.

speaker: Bubares
en: Then you understand why no price is too high to stop her. Now go find the Eagle Bearer instead of questioning the Huntsman's orders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he goes. All alone. Now's my chance. I can't wait for Darius.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another note. "I expect good news about the recruitment. Report to me at the lake." The Huntsman.

speaker: Darius
en: A lake. Interesting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where were you hiding?

speaker: Darius
en: Closer than you'd have thought. You were never in any real danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Huntsman's lieutenant mentioned an... Artabanus. Who's that?

speaker: Darius
en: A dead man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left. Why?

speaker: Darius
en: I needed to be sure you weren't with the Order.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You still suspected me.

speaker: Darius
en: And you've never questioned my relationship to the Order?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's true I've had my suspicions. You identified the coded note immediately and knew of their rituals and ways.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is not the same. I thought I had back up.

speaker: Darius
en: I know you're clean, and we've got our answers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The note said that the Huntsman is near a lake.

speaker: Darius
en: I have other leads to follow up on. And I'm sure Natakas has more for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever Darius is hiding, I'll find it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Help! Someone please help me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Calm down and tell me what's wrong.

speaker: Civilian
en: My husband, he's late... no—missing! He and his friend have tracked a giant wolf south of Mytilene. They want its pelt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He better be a good hunter.

speaker: Civilian
en: Without knowing, all I can do is worry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said yourself he was likely late. I wouldn't worry.

speaker: Civilian
en: But a savage creature could be devouring them as we speak!

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so.

speaker: Civilian
en: Can I hire you to find my husband and kill the giant wolf for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would I need to kill the wolf? I can just bring back your husband and his friend.

speaker: Civilian
en: If you won't, those two idiots will continue their hunt. I need this nightmare to stop, and I'll give you my husband's helmet as payment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find your husband and kill the giant wolf once and for all.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you, misthios. If there's anything I can do to help...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What makes you think it's not just an ordinary wolf?

speaker: Civilian
en: My husband says it's twice the size as any he's seen!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where south of Mytilene did he track the wolf to?

speaker: Civilian
en: He tracked it southwest to the mountains and set up a lookout near a shrine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find your husband and his friend, and kill the giant wolf for you.

speaker: Civilian
en: May Artemis guide your arrows.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hunting gear. The men were here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found one... killed by the wolf. I wonder if this is the husband?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Blood... The wolf must've dragged the other man. To a cave, maybe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's huge! But if it's dead... what killed these men?

speaker: Hunter
en: Who... who's there?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A woman sent me to kill a giant wolf and save her husband and his friend.

speaker: Hunter
en: I'm the friend. Her husband... he's dead. We killed a giant wolf, but she was full of pups. A terrible mistake. We didn't know...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's down there?

speaker: Hunter
en: We... um... finished skinning the she-wolf, then heard a sad and terrible howl. It was the mate! It tore into my friend, then dragged me here. It's waiting...

speaker: Kassandra
en: It wants revenge.

speaker: Hunter
en: You've got to kill it, or we die!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You killed its mate and unborn pups. It seems fair.

speaker: Hunter
en: What? No! Don't leave me. Don't leave me!

speaker: Hunter
en: No! Nice wolf! Nice wolf! No - Ahhhhhhhh!

speaker: Kassandra
en: For what you two did, I think it's time you and the wolf were reacquainted. Hunter, meet wolf. Wolf, eat hunter!

speaker: Hunter
en: What? No! You can't! You monster. You

speaker: Hunter
en: No! Nice wolf! Nice wolf! No - Ahhhhhhhh!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not here to judge—I was hired to kill a wolf. Wait here.

speaker: Hunter
en: Oh thank you. Thank you.

speaker: Civilian
en: My husband hasn't returned. Please tell me he's coming.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your husband is dead.

speaker: Civilian
en: No!

speaker: Kassandra
en: But I killed the wolf and brought you its pelt. You can take comfort knowing he was avenged.

speaker: Civilian
en: Comfort? Avenged? My husband is dead. Nothing will ever change that fact! Take his helmet and leave!

speaker: Civilian
en: My husband... Where is he?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your husband and his friend were killed by the giant wolf after he killed its mate and unborn pups. I chose not to kill it.

speaker: Civilian
en: No! I hired you to protect them. If I see you again, I'll put a contract on your head!

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you for avenging my husband.

speaker: Woman
en: Help! Won't somebody help me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you need?

speaker: Woman
en: Peace of mind. And revenge. Can you bring me this, misthios? We will give you all the drachmae we have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need more information first.

speaker: Woman
en: The Followers of Ares are burning our villages and claiming our families for their sacrifices.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those malákes are making trouble all over the Greek world.

speaker: Woman
en: That's why I want you to make them suffer like we have - so that our living can find peace, and our dead can be - Be avenged.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My spear is yours.

speaker: Woman
en: Thank you, misthios. You have no idea how much this means to us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll need to know where the Followers are hiding.

speaker: Woman
en: The Followers of Ares live in caves among the mountain ranges of Zeus' Playground.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll flush them out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Followers of Ares are with Hades now.

speaker: Woman
en: Thank you, misthios. How can we repay you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing is free in this world, especially my time.

speaker: Woman
en: I understand misthios, I only wish we could give you more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't put a price on justice. Those men deserved the end they got.

speaker: Woman
en: You gave us something drachmae can't buy... peace. For that we'll be forever grateful. But we cannot leave you without showing our gratitude. Please take this. I have no need for it any longer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Need something?

speaker: Man
en: Well, if it isn't the great "hero" of Megaris come to save us all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You lose drachmae betting on Athens?

speaker: Man
en: Hardly! Megara had been stable for awhile. I equipped the Athenians for their battles until you wiped them all out. Now there's no one left to pay me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: War takes more than drachmae from most, friend. Count yourself lucky.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Athenians got what was coming for them, and so did you if you weren't smart enough to get paid up front.

speaker: Man
en: Bah! Keep your advice. If you really wanted to make it up to me, you'd help me get what's rightfully mine from the Athenians.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you want me to get it from the Athenians.

speaker: Man
en: Yes, it needs to be returned without a scratch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of it.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Man
en: Tell me it's been handled, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all yours.

speaker: Man
en: I'm a man of my word, so here's your reward.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this? A message.

speaker: Megakles
en: You there! Come here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is it?

speaker: Megakles
en: Some merc calling himself "The Eagle Bearer" came to Alponos offering to help out. Nice kid, and I've heard his name before. I thought to myself, "Megakles, that's drachmae well spent."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whoever came to Alponos lied to you. I'm the only Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Megakles
en: You? Impossible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I have an eagle. Also, I'm not a man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know who's been using my name, but you're going to tell me everything you know.

speaker: Megakles
en: What is there to tell? He came in, had some little bird with him. You know how legends go. One day he gets a bird, next he's called the Child of Zeus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She. And I do have an eagle.

speaker: Megakles
en: I see that now, don't I? But I paid this other Eagle Bearer a small fortune to get the villagers ready for a pirate invasion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the look on your face, I'm guessing that didn't work out.

speaker: Megakles
en: It didn't. Then I sent him to bargain peace, but he botched that, too. The pirates are coming, and we don't stand a chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Next time, hire the real Eagle Bearer. But I'm listening. Does the village of Alponos have a militia?

speaker: Megakles
en: Not enough. But if you get out there and stop the pirates before they land, I'll give you all that's left in the treasury.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll stop the pirates from reaching your shore. Then you're going to help me find this "Eagle Bearer" impostor.

speaker: Megakles
en: I'll help you kill him myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are the pirates sailing from?

speaker: Megakles
en: We saw the pirate fleet forming north of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How big is their fleet?

speaker: Megakles
en: Just two ships, but they may have hundreds aboard. They make it to us, we're dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to find the one using my name. When did you last see him?

speaker: Megakles
en: He came in with the last merchant ships... But I haven't seen him in days. He won't be easy to find, but if you sink the pirates, I'll track him down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to show the pirates what the real Eagle Bearer can do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hope you can swim, pirate scum! That's how the real Eagle Bearer deals with pirates!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the last one, crew! Let's go get paid.

speaker: Megakles
en: What were you thinking?! We're doomed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem pleased, General.

speaker: Lysander
en: Supply lines cut. Troops tremble. And I rise through the ranks!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Congratulations.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your strategy has served you well so far. What will it take to win?

speaker: Lysander
en: I'm not idle while you kill commanders. I've had enemy forts surveyed and know all of their supply runs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I've been a diversion.

speaker: Lysander
en: Soon I'll know their sea routes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've made it further than most leaders.

speaker: Lysander
en: Others boast of royal blood. I'm a descendant of Herakles. That gives me more legitimate claim to lead even Archidamos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all for now.

speaker: Lysander
en: If you're done wasting time... Go and strike the fort commanders down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As you command, General.​​​​​​

speaker: Kassandra
en: The task is done. Here are the seals as proof.

speaker: Lysander
en: I'll be commander soon. And then I'll be crowned by the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Athenians seem unsure how to react.

speaker: Lysander
en: Unlike Spartans, Athenians answer to the whims of ignorant peasants. It makes them slow to react. Spartans do what needs to be done. Such as eliminating enemy commanders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, statesman. I don't suppose you could use a mercenary's help today?

speaker: Man
en: You! You're the mercenary my lovely Anthousa spoke of. I've heard you have some sway with her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Your" Anthousa? I didn't know she was tied down.

speaker: Man
en: She and I have a unique connection. If she would only see it. There is someone else who's caught her eye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Only one person?

speaker: Man
en: A penniless writer who whispers empty words in Anthousa's ear. I've heard she doesn't even bestow gifts upon my love. She's clearly using her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So where do I come into this?

speaker: Man
en: Maybe if someone with Anthousa's approval found a reason to dispose of this writer, Anthousa would see clearly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to give her a taste of my blade.

speaker: Man
en: Her death is the only solution.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'm in.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you. Please be discreet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Man
en: You. Have you killed her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's no longer your concern.

speaker: Man
en: You do fine work, mercenary. Take this as thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I've started.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: You have the habit of appearing the moment I need you. What a power I may wield.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there ever a time you don't need me?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Good point.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The drunk politician you had me take home... We ran into a bit of trouble.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: That's terrible! I'm glad to see you're OK.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm fine, but nature can be cruel. We were attacked by animals, and he was mauled to death.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I see. Well, plans change sometimes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem pretty accepting of this.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: What else can I do? We should both forget this ever happened. Pretend you never even saw the man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, thankfully we both made it out alive.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Oh. I see. Thank you for telling me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem disappointed.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'm just... impressed you were able to save the both of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said you needed something?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Ah, to business already? Fine, it's simple enough, really. There's an item that holds great sentimental value I'd like you to retrieve.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do I need to find?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It's an olisbos. If you saw it on the ground, even you wouldn't bend over... to pick it up. But it means so much to me. To hold it again would mean more than you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never took you for someone who cared for sentimental things.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'm so much more than my beautiful face and flowing blond locks...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Like what?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Well, let's see... People forget I'm an orphan—that Perikles isn't my father.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what it's like to lose family, too.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Ah. We have that in common. There's more to you than I thought, misthios. Now, where were we?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That seems a bit emotional, even for you. You've gone soft.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I'm anything but soft, I assure you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Focus, Alkibiades. What is an olisbos?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It brings... pleasure. When my body grows too tired after a long night, having one of these can let the fun continue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then go get it.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I knew I'd see you again... But what I'd really like to see is my olisbos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a big boy. Get it yourself?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I sure am... But there's a small chance the woman who has it won't exactly be happy to see me again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There has to be a story behind this thing.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: When you see the olisbos, you'll know. When you have it in your hands, against your skin... When you feel the weight of it, you'll know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Every time we talk, it seems like you're about to sleep with someone... Or you want to... Or you've just finished. Is this woman the most recent one?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Who said I slept with her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was a safe guess. How do you find time for anything else?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Determination, mostly.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: There's a closeness you can only feel with someone in those moments. Who wouldn't crave that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get the olisbos for you.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: There's a small chance the woman may wish to keep it for herself... to spite me. It may be best to go unseen and hurry back. She lives east of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, you'll have it in your hands soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's made out of stone... I guess that could work.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Ah, that's it in your hand! You brought it. Hm, it's different than I remember it looking... And much bigger too. She's going to miss it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was never yours, was it? You had me steal it.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: We didn't just steal an olisbos—we stole a family heirloom and a husband's confidence. Without it, he'll be focused on his wife instead of his business. I think she'll enjoy the change of pace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So it's sentimental... just not to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You lied. Again.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I don't think I did. I was very particular with my words.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said it was sentimental.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It is. Just not to me. There wasn't a single lie.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not how it feels.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: The only thing that matters is you retrieved the olisbos and helped me a great deal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what about me?

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Now, now. We wash each other's backs, don't we? There's a reason you never turn me down, after all. How about I show you how this olisbos can make all the difference?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know, you've made me curious. Let's try it out.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I knew you'd be open to it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was... something

speaker: Alkibiades
en: It's different, but you'll get used to it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope you're right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not what I meant. Guess I can turn you down after all.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I deserved that.

speaker: Mob Leader
en: The stench of evil is upon her—she worships the Writhing Dread. She must face justice!

speaker: Bryce
en: No! Listen to me. Listen! Ligeia's still out there! The Creature took her, but she can still be saved. Help me, please!

speaker: Mob Leader
en: Oh, how she twists the truth. She sacrificed her own lover to the Writhing Dread. How dare you bring your curse upon us!

speaker: Mob Leader
en: Look at you, a finely-tuned instrument of justice. Help us destroy this vile woman!

speaker: Bryce
en: A misthios! The gods are real... Help me, please!

speaker: Mob Leader
en: Silence, snake!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on?

speaker: Mob Leader
en: We will bring this evil Creature to justice!

speaker: Bryce
en: They're lost in paranoia! They think I sacrificed my Ligeia to the Creature in the forest!

speaker: Mob Leader
en: Hold your forked tongue!

speaker: Mob Leader
en: This walking curse is in league with the Writhing Dread!

speaker: Kassandra
en: She just looks scared to me.

speaker: Bryce
en: Please! The Creature took Ligeia. If I die here, who will save her?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll save Ligeia and kill any creature that tries to stop me.

speaker: Mob Leader
en: What are you saying?! She will lead you to the Petrified Temple and your doom!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What exactly is this Creature?

speaker: Bryce
en: Evil. Heartless. Unknowable.

speaker: Mob Leader
en: We must end this girl before she leads the Writhing Dread right to us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The forest where the Creature lives—where is it?

speaker: Mob Leader
en: Beyond the Petrified Temple, north of here. A damned place, haunted by shade and filled with cursed stone... At its center lie ancient ruins, from which few return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned a "Ligeia." She's

speaker: Bryce
en: Beyond beauty, beyond grace... A Daughter of Artemis. Brave—not like me.

speaker: Mob Leader
en: What dark prize did the Writhing Dread offer for her soul?

speaker: Bryce
en: She lives, misthios! I know it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If this "Writhing Dread" has let Ligeia live, we'll need to move now. Follow me.

speaker: Bryce
en: Careful, these people are driven by fear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The girl's coming with me. I'd suggest not standing in our way.

speaker: Mob Leader
en: She's whispered spells in your ear, misthios.

speaker: Mob Leader
en: Citizens! We must save our city!

speaker: Mob Leader
en: And these interlopers... must bleed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hide in the temple, I'll deal with this!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're safe now.

speaker: Bryce
en: "Safe?" I don't want to be safe, misthios. I want to look deep into Ligeia's eyes, just once more—even if it kills me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Love might be the end of us all, but it's a price worth paying.

speaker: Bryce
en: I polished Charon's drachma long ago, misthios. I'm ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Be smart, be cautious, and with my help, you will look into your lover's eyes again. It doesn't need to cost your life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know, I don't want to call you "You" forever.

speaker: Bryce
en: My name's Bryce.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Bryce
en: Ligeia's waiting for me, Kassandra. If I'd been captured... I'd never have to wait for her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then let's not disappoint her. Where was she taken?

speaker: Bryce
en: From our sanctuary—the Dread Ruins in the Petrified Valley.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you're surprised she was taken by a Creature?!

speaker: Bryce
en: It's not safe here—we need to leave the city.

speaker: Rooting Out Spartan Forces
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not bad! But I don't think this is what Xenia is looking for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh. An offering box is missing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These ribbons tied the box shut. The lid of the offering box. Flower petals. These would have lined the offering box. Someone tossed the box here... but it's empty.

speaker: Laios
en: Didn't you like it? I thought you would like it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perhaps one of these couples saw something.

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: Doesn't matter if I liked it. You stole from the gods!

speaker: Laios
en: Do you have any idea how much it was worth?

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: What it's worth? What's a curse from the gods worth?!

speaker: Laios
en: Don't be a superstitious donkey! That bracelet was priceless!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hey.

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: All you care about is money! What about how I feel?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hey!

speaker: Laios
en: I wanted to impress you!

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: You wanted to get into my clothes, you mean!

speaker: Kassandra
en: HEY!

speaker: Laios
en: Huh? What do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Which one of you idiots stole the bracelet from the shine?

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: By Poseidon, she knows!

speaker: Laios
en: Shut your teeth! She doesn't know anything! How could she?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe because every goat-herder around could hear your spat? Give me the bracelet.

speaker: Laios
en: You don't scare me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tremble, you fools, for I am the wrath of Apollo!

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: I told you Laios! The gods come to punish us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Exactly! Give me what I want or I will smite you down!

speaker: Laios
en: And what do you want?

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: Fool! She wants the bracelet you stole!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You understand completely! Give me the bracelet!

speaker: Hyacinthos
en: I threw it off the cliffs, into the sea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka. Guess I'm going for a swim.

speaker: Makedonian Bracelet
en: A golden bracelet as beautiful as the laughter-loving, foam-born Aphrodite. Made with the ingenious skill of crooked-foot Hephaistos, crafted with the purest Makedonian gold, and left as an offering to the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. The entrance must be underwater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, this is the conch? It's heavy. I can see why Xenia wants it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd rather not swim through that tunnel again. There's a breeze in here. Must be another way out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. This is very nice... but I don't think it's what Xenia is looking for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This doesn't seem to be what Xenia's looking for... but it'll fill my purse nicely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gods be good, I think this is the right spot.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. Empty. Someone else had the same idea.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
en: The gods will abandon us!

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
en: We are doomed! The gods will curse our names!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It can't be that bad.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
en: Oh, it's terrible!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me what happened.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stop that noise!

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
en: Ahh!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Better. Now, quietly, tell me what happened here.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
en: The lighthouse was plundered by bandits, the Terrors of Kyknos! I fear they've gone to the Mycenaean Tomb of Ajax.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll deal with them.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
en: Oh, no. There are too many of them!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They won't expect anyone to come after them. I'll sneak up and surprise them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ajax is not the only one blessed by the gods. I'll crush these so-called terrors!

speaker: Golden Feather of Ajax
en: A glorious golden feather said to have been woven into oxhide shield (sic) carried by towering Ajax, son of Telamon. One tale says it was plucked from the body of Zeus while he was in the form of an eagle, but who knows?

speaker: Anais
en: I'm glad you came.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're married. Why didn't you tell me sooner?

speaker: Anais
en: Seeing you brought back so many fond memories, I wanted to live in them for as long as I could. Life's been hard since Dantos left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where did he go?

speaker: Anais
en: Once the war started, Spartans came for his sword. He was killed in battle... Leaving me to run the farm and raise our son.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have a son?

speaker: Anais
en: Arion. I'd love for you to meet him, but he's run off again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why aren't we looking for him?

speaker: Anais
en: He always goes to the same cave, where he trains to be a mighty warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never known a boy who didn't want to train to be the next Achillies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Training alone encourages bad habits.

speaker: Anais
en: Yes of course! You've given me an idea. You could talk to him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could?

speaker: Anais
en: Gods know he doesn't listen to his boring mother. But you've seen death up close... You could convince him to stay away from fighting and help me on the farm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll talk to your son.

speaker: Anais
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How should I introduce myself without scaring the boy?

speaker: Anais
en: Tell him you're a friend of his mother's from Kephallonia—the one with the eagle. The stories I've told him about you are his favourites.

speaker: Kassandra
en: is there anything about your son's father I should know to help me connect with him?

speaker: Anais
en: Dantos broke his finger working the fields. It healed crooked. When Arion asked about it, my husband said he was so strong as a baby, he grabbed it and snapped it like a twig. This is how we knew he was blessed by Herakles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find Arion.

speaker: Anais
en: My husband used to take him to the cave on hunts—they'd spend nights there. It's been taken over by wolves since then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait, did you say wolves?

speaker: Anais
en: Yes, worries me sick. He calls them his "friends," and believe it or not they seem protective of the boy. Please don't harm them, Kassandra. Arion would be devastated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they don't attack me, I won't attack them.

speaker: Arion
en: Whoa! You look like a mighty warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you must be Arion. I've come to bring you home.

speaker: Arion
en: Why should I trust you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your mother and I used to get into trouble back on Kephallonia?

speaker: Arion
en: Kephallonia?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'd sneak into the markets, grab as much cheese and grapes and bread as we could carry. My eagle Ikaros kept watch and warned us if there was anyone coming.

speaker: Arion
en: You're Kassandra the Eagle Bearer!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your mother trusted me with the very important task of escorting you home through this dangerous forest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your mother and I have known each other for a long time. She told me you like to come here to train, but she wants you to come home.

speaker: Arion
en: But I don't want to leave.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know you come here to be close to your father.

speaker: Arion
en: You know nothing about my pater!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know when you were a baby, you broke his finger with the strength of Herakles.

speaker: Arion
en: Pater's fingers were big and tough. That's why I train—to make these hands strong like his.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right. Maybe you could tell me.

speaker: Arion
en: I don't want to talk about him. I want to become a warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I understand, but first we need to leave this cave. The wolves are getting hungry.

speaker: Arion
en: They'd never eat me. They're my friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Um, yes, your friends. Let's go anyway, your mother misses you very much.

speaker: Arion
en: If I do, could you teach me to be a mighty warrior?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll see. Now come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've spent enough time here Arion, its time to go home.

speaker: Arion
en: I don't trust you. I'm not leaving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make you a deal. Come with me now, and I'll train you to be the mightiest warrior in all of Arkadia.

speaker: Arion
en: Really? You really will?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Really. Now Come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's enough. Your mother sent me here to bring you home, and that's exactly what I'm going to do. So get down here right now before I come up after you.

speaker: Arion
en: OK.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not still mad at me for the cave, are you? Fine.

speaker: Anais
en: There you both are.

speaker: Arion
en: You didn't have to send anyone after me, mater. I can take care of myself.

speaker: Anais
en: I know you can, my love.

speaker: Arion
en: She killed my friends, mater!

speaker: Anais
en: Oh Kassandra, why?

speaker: Arion
en: You told her about me, mater. She knew things.

speaker: Anais
en: I did. She wanted to know all about you so you weren't scared of going with her.

speaker: Arion
en: I wasn't scared. I was brave.

speaker: Anais
en: Thank you for bringing him home.

speaker: Arion
en: At least Kassandra said she'd make me the best warrior Arkadia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He wouldn't come with me, so I said I'd train him.

speaker: Arion
en: You lied to me?

speaker: Anais
en: She was just following my wishes, my love.

speaker: Arion
en: I hate you both!

speaker: Anais
en: His temper comes and goes like waves on a beach. Thank you for bringing him home.

speaker: Arion
en: She yelled at me. I was so scared.

speaker: Anais
en: You yelled at my child?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Arion, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to frighten you.

speaker: Arion
en: I hate you.

speaker: Anais
en: If I had a drachma for every time he's said that to me, I wouldn't need this farm. Thanks for apologizing - he's upset now, but he'll come around.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He wouldn't come with me, there were wolves everywhere... I did what needed to be done.

speaker: Arion
en: I hate you.

speaker: Anais
en: Next time think twice before you raise your voice to my child.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anais, wait.

speaker: Zeuxo
en: You wouldn't happen to be the Eagle Bearer, would you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me? Yes I am.

speaker: Zeuxo
en: Words do you no justice. Your hair must have been woven by Athena, your body is like a sculpture made by the masters... Your arms look so strong. Strong enough to...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Strong enough to...?

speaker: Zeuxo
en: Strong enough to carry this basket to my husband, Kalibos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh. Right. The magistrate mentioned you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It'll be easy to carry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have time for that.

speaker: Zeuxo
en: Please don't forget to bring Kalibos that basket I gave you!

speaker: Zeuxo
en: Thank you so much. Let me know if you need anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where might I find Kalibos?

speaker: Zeuxo
en: He's an important general. His unit is stationed in the northeast, near the Fort of Praisai, down by the beach.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's in the basket?

speaker: Zeuxo
en: What any man would need on the eve of battle to win the respect of the gods. Please, Eagle Bearer, it would give him an edge over his enemies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help with your delivery.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ugh, this is heavy. What's in here, bricks?

speaker: Kalibos
en: A misthios? Well met. What brings you to our camp?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are Kalibos? Your wife sent me to deliver this package. I think it might be some kind of offering.

speaker: Kalibos
en: Zeuxo is a good woman. She's gifted me with a basket fit for Dionysos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Earthly pleasures? She made it sound like it was a case of life and death.

speaker: Kalibos
en: A deathly hangover, maybe. Boys, we're having a good night! Care to join us, friend?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you sure you want your soldiers this intoxicated while in the field?

speaker: Kalibos
en: I must have misjudged you. Are you not also a Spartan? The only thing we're better at than fighting is drinking.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see your point.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never say no to good wine and good company.

speaker: Kalibos
en: I expected no less from you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you for offering. I don't like to dull my senses this close to battle. I will stay and keep you and your men company through the night.

speaker: Kalibos
en: Chaperoned by a messenger of Zeus? This will be interesting.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Could someone pass the waterskin?

speaker: Kalibos
en: Could someone pass my head? I think I left it further down the beach.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Surely this is the after effects of the mushrooms. I remember the chicken coop. I remember the farmer's field. I do not remember building a .

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Uh, it was just here when I woke up.

speaker: Kalibos
en: We offer it to the gods for safe passage across the seas! Boys, let's move this down to the beach!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't even drink last night. Why am I seeing a Trojan horse?

speaker: Kalibos
en: We can offer it to Poseidon for safe passage across the sea!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Careful, this was a trap the last time.

speaker: Spartan Brute
en: I don't trust that horse.

speaker: Kalibos
en: By Zeus, I can't believe I fell for that.

speaker: Athenian Heavy Soldier
en: For Athens!

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: For Sparta!

speaker: Athenian Archer
en: I can't believe they fell for that.

speaker: Kalibos
en: I once boasted to a friend that I was a better tactician than Odysseus himself... Today I was proven wrong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You live to fight another day. Learn from this.

speaker: Kalibos
en: Please thank my wife for her festive gift.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know if I should thank her or curse her.

speaker: Xenia
en: You flew like the west wind in retrieving my golden eagle feather. Now, fetch me another rarity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure, I'm up for whatever challenge you have in mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sorry, Xenia. Another time, perhaps.

speaker: Xenia
en: You're back. Good. Will you find the Makedonian bracelet for my pleasure?

speaker: Xenia
en: A wealthy noble from Makedonia is visiting various sanctuaries throughout the Aegean, looking for the most sacred to make a great offering.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh? What would he offer the gods, and why?

speaker: Xenia
en: The why is unimportant. Perhaps he asks the gods to make his drachmae multiply, or to harden his cock.

speaker: Xenia
en: But the offering is said to be crafted golden bracelet, as beautiful as Aphrodite, with workmanship to rival that of Hephaistos. It would look better on my wrist than on an altar.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, how far do I have to travel to find these sacred sites?

speaker: Xenia
en: I had one of my loyal crew, Anaximander, draw several maps to show you the locations. He's clever with a stylus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any guards at these holy sites?

speaker: Xenia
en: Probably not, though I suppose you risk offending the gods and earning their enmity for all time. If you take stock in that sort of thing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good enough for now. I'll keep an eye out for the bracelet you want.

speaker: Map to Sacred Site
en: This is one of the maps given by Xenia.

speaker: Xenia
en: Ah, my lovely misthios. What news?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The time I sink into finding these trinkets for you had better be amply rewarded.

speaker: Xenia
en: Does my little hoplite feel undervalued?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't see you risking your life over wild waters.

speaker: Xenia
en: Ha! In my youth I sailed every sea and explored every island as if driven by Poseidon. But now I carry a burden like Atlas. Don't worry, Kassandra. I have a fat purse for your efforts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An amazing piece. You will look magnificent with it, like Aphrodite herself.

speaker: Xenia
en: I am no soft and simple plaything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, of course not. It will look mighty

speaker: Xenia
en: Stop trying to insert your tongue in my ass.

speaker: Civilian
en: Ho-ho-ho, over the Aegean we go! We blubber, and stutter, and jubber until we drown below!

speaker: Orontas
en: Misthios! Over here.

speaker: Ariston
en: More wine!

speaker: Orontas
en: Here's the man we're looking for, misthios.

speaker: Ariston
en: Chaire, chaire, my friend! I recognize you... I took your ships, didn't I? At the docks?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've come to get those ships back.

speaker: Ariston
en: Why, would be my first question. But then I realized... I don't really care. Because you're a misthios!

speaker: Ariston
en: Let bygones be bygones, my friend! We drink! Except for the mercenary.

speaker: Ariston
en: Now, sail away from me. Oh right, you can't!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems like it'd be easier to silence you and your crew, then take back the ships.

speaker: Ariston
en: See? Your kind is always thirsty for bloodshed.

speaker: Orontas
en: Violence is not always the answer, misthios.

speaker: Ariston
en: This is why I hate mercenaries. They think violence solves everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can still hear you.

speaker: Ariston
en: Fine. Calm down. If we want to deal, we must do it like civilized individuals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you propose?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think we got off on the wrong foot. I'm sure a smart man like you knows when to make a useful friend. If you help me, I'll help you.

speaker: Ariston
en: Helping you would cost more than my left arm. If I am to risk incurring the Tempest's wrath, there should be a sizable benefit for me. I heard valuables can be found at Shipwreck Cove, not far from here. Or... I could always use more drachmae. You can buy wine with drachmae.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd rather not run around. Here's your drachmae.

speaker: Ariston
en: Now we're talking. Make sure it's enough—my friendship doesn't come cheap.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take a look around Shipwreck Cove for the valuables.

speaker: Ariston
en: Remember, misthios. I don't take trash.

speaker: Ariston
en: I got a lovely lady, but she looks a bit like Hades! Though her curves are wavy, just like

speaker: Ariston
en: Hey! Where's the wine gone?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There it is! Found it! Here it is. That's what I'm looking for. I see it.

speaker: Heracles Action Figure
en: The hottest toy in Greece! The clothes appear to be missing from this particular figure.

speaker: Pouch of Ancient Coins
en: Worth its weight in gold.

speaker: Fountain Face
en: Its eyes emit a life-like gleam. They seem to follow you.

speaker: Four Legged Sculpture
en: Is it a wolf? Is it Zeus in disguise? The ever confounding mystery of high-end art.

speaker: Glittery Pendant
en: Though its edges are encrusted with dirt, this pendant still shines.

speaker: Expensive-Looking Clay Pot
en: Impressively resilient to wear and tear.

speaker: Right Dove Knocker
en: A layer of grime hides the masterful craftsmanship that went into this door knocker. One of two matching door knockers.

speaker: Left Dove Knocker
en: One of two matching door knockers. A layer of grime hides the masterful craftsmanship that went into this door knocker.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These should be enough.

speaker: Orontas
en: Misthios, you're back.

speaker: Ariston
en: Do you have the valuables I want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found what you wanted at Shipwreck Cove.

speaker: Ariston
en: Splendid! Hand it over.

speaker: Ariston
en: This will do!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A deal's a deal.

speaker: Ariston
en: I never go back on my word! Only a dishonorable malákas will break an oath.

speaker: Ariston
en: I'll give you your ships back, but good luck getting past the Tempest. Just take a good look outside at all those wrecks, misthios. Now, if you'll excuse me...

speaker: Orontas
en: Thanks to you, misthios, we have what we need. Now, we

speaker: Kleta
en: Orontas. Kassandra.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Misthios, no need for bloodshed. I just need you to come quietly, please. Releasing the stranded has angered the Tempest. Someone just needs to take responsibility, and everyone will be fine.

speaker: Orontas
en: Take me then. They have nothing to do with this. I'm the one you're after.

speaker: Orontas
en: We have done enough, there's no need to escalate this further. Promise me that you will see our plan through to the end.

speaker: Kleta
en: Did she do all this? This destruction... all this ruin... It's painful to watch. It feels like she's becoming someone I don't know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No matter what happens, blood is blood. She's still your daughter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Tempest can't be redeemed. Look at the chaos she's caused to Achaia and to you.

speaker: Kleta
en: Parents always believe in their children, as foolish as that may be.

speaker: Kleta
en: I should have stopped her sooner—stopped her from joining the Order. I should have...

speaker: Kleta
en: When the time comes to face the Tempest, my Phila...

speaker: Kleta
en: What will you do, Kassandra?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I promise, I'll do my best to bring her back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sorry, Kleta. She needs to be dealt with.

speaker: Kleta
en: I was so proud of her. I don't think I ever told her that. There are still so many things I wish I had said.

speaker: Kleta
en: I should go help the rest. We'll meet up in Patrai when we're ready. Thank you, Kassandra. For everything.

en: Something happen to your shipment?

en: Did you say something, whelp?

en: I said "curse those clumsy fools!"

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get you your

en: What? Is that a yes? Did she say

en: She sure did, boss! Idiot.

en: Wonderful. My apprentice here will tell you where to find the obsidian.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thanks for doing this, 'else he wouldn't have shut up. There are stashes of the stuff in the Temple of Britomartis and the Sunken Ruins. If you have any questions, point them at me. I've had enough of his booming voice for one day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These ruins you mentioned, where are they?

speaker: Civilian
en: The Sunken Ruins are on the west coast of Messara. Fair warning, though—they're infested with sharks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good to know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've already been there. There wasn't much obsidian.

speaker: Civilian
en: Oh. That's not good. But at least you got whatever was there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where to find it.

speaker: Civilian
en: The Temple of Britomartis is northwest of Kydonia. But there are guards roaming about—be careful.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That temple has been ransacked – the obsidian is gone.

speaker: Civilian
en: I take it you saw that personally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong with him?

speaker: Civilian
en: Where would you like me to begin? He's spent all his life in front of the forge. He can barely hear a thing. Watch. You smell gross today, you old toad.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: That's very sweet of you to say—You too smell like a rose.

speaker: Civilian
en: The trick is to just smile when you say anything. You should try it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I like what you've done with the place.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: What? What did you say about my face?

speaker: Civilian
en: No, no! She said she likes the place.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Oh! I see. Thank you.

speaker: Civilian
en: You're not very good at this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're looking really good today.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: "Put the wood in the hay?" I'm a blacksmith, silly misthios. I deal with iron, not wood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't like taking showers, do you?

speaker: Blacksmith
en: No, I am not particularly fond of flowers. They make me sneeze.

speaker: Kasssandra
en: I've got all I neeed. I'll be back with the obsidian glass.

speaker: Civilian
en: She's going to get your stuff now.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Wonderful. Return quickly, misthios.

speaker: Civilian
en: Please hurry, my ears can't take any more of his complaining.

speaker: Kasssandra
en: The obsidian glass must be here for a reason. Better be on my guard.

speaker: Kasssandra
en: This must be where they keep the obsidian glass.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here's your obsidian glass.

en: Excellently done, misthios. She got the stuff.

en: Well done, misthios. Take my blade. May it serve you well.

en: Now he'll finally shut up for a bit!

speaker: Blacksmith
en: I heard that.

en: This should be enough.

speaker: Civilian
en: You are well-stocked. You a merchant or a misthios, eh?

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Excellent! This will do fine. Here you go, misthios. As promised.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something seems to be going on over there.

speaker: Student
en: We told you, he's not here! Stop coming back! Don't make me punch you!

speaker: Ide
en: You wouldn't punch a little girl!

speaker: Student
en: But we can kick you. Don't come here again!

speaker: Ide
en: Idiots! I'll be back, you can't keep me away forever! I'll find a way in!

speaker: Ide
en: You look strong enough. Can you help me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Depends on what you need.

speaker: Ide
en: Information! My brother, Solon, has been missing for weeks! No one listens! They say he ran away! But he wouldn't leave me alone, he wouldn't! He knows I hate being by myself. Anyway, he was last seen training at this school. I'm sure it has something to do with his disappearance! Please can you help me find out what happened to him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can find out.

speaker: Ide
en: You're nicer than you look. Thank you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't thank me just yet—my help doesn't come cheap.

speaker: Ide
en: What? You would demand drachmae from a child?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess we can work something out.

speaker: Ide
en: I don't have much, but I'll repay you with whatever I have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That will do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't discriminate.

speaker: Ide
en: Misthios. I have some drachmae, but you must first find out what happened.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll prepare to be shortchanged.

speaker: Ide
en: I think the trainer might know about my brother's disappearance, but be careful—rumor has it he can take out a Chimera with his bare fists. Or was it that he looks like a Chimera with bare firsts? In any case, I'd take caution not to look for a fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't look for fights, they usually find me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are there so many young athletes training at this school?

speaker: Ide
en: You've never heard of this place? This school is what Thasos is known for! It was founded by Theageneses, the famous Olympian. Many others like my brother train here in hopes of becoming the next Olympic champion

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brother must have been gone for a long time.

speaker: Ide
en: Weeks. It's been weeks. He would never leave me alone for so long.

speaker: Ide
en: He used to boast about future Olympic victories and adventures. He always said he'd make me the proudest sister in all the Greek world... But how can he do that when he's not even here?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out what happened to your brother.

speaker: Ide
en: Please hurry. It's been too quiet around here without him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like Mikkos was right. There is something going on here. I'll get to the bottom of this.

speaker: Student 1
en: Theageneses was the best! Euthymos didn't even stand a chance in that match. Look at how weak he is.

speaker: Student 2
en: Euthymos... That name seems familiar somehow...

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: If you've come to enroll in my school, I'm afraid you're at least ten years too late.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shame. You must be the one training these athletes.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Have you not heard of me? I am Euthymos, master Olympic trainer. Under my charge, my students seize victories as easily as Theageneses seized the bronze statue of Thasos. Everyone has heard of me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who? I've never heard your name before today.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Then you must be quite deaf!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They say that you loo—that you can take down a Chimera with your bare fists.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: These rumors, they are took kind! And all true.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard other things, though. In particular, that students of yours have gone missing.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Missing? Nonsense! My students are champions. They fly towards adventure all the time. Under my wing, they will soar to great heights like a hot-blooded Pegasos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you remember a former student named Solon?

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: You think you can storm in my school and demand answers like an impertinent slave? You'll sooner be gutted like one!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to know if your school has a connection to the disappearances.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Connection? Nonsense! This is a place of blood, sweat, and brawn! The only things that vanish here are the weaknesses in heart and body.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not if I cut the answers from your throat first.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Such pretty words! They almost scare me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: How about we put our skills to the test?

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: I'd rather not waste my time or my skills on the likes of a nobody.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like you're backing down.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Taunts won't work, misthios!

speaker: Student
en: Hold on... you seem familiar. I recognize you! You were in the Olympics! You're the champion, I'm sure of it!

en: Yes, you'are looking at an Olympic champion.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Get back to your trainin

en: Of course I'm an Olympic champion. Many times over, in fact.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: I don't believe

en: You're amazing! Tell us, what do we need to do to be a true champion?

en: A true champion needs a dominant power pose. Like so.

en: Power pose? My pose is so much better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A true champion runs daily with the weight of two cows slung across the shoulders.

en: Hmph. Doesn't sound impressive to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A true champion has to eat the Champion's Feast before a match.

en: I've never heard of it. What is it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Swallowing a dozen bowls of sheep and buffalo delicates. It gives you unimaginable stamina, and the strength of Herakles

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Lies! Don't listen to this liar!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't prove it's a lie.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Yes I can, because I've tried it. The only thing it gives you is an upset stomach! You are no champion. Prepare for the taste of defeat!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Anyone can be a champion. But it takes hard work and a commitment to your passion.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: That is what I always say!

en: So, an Olympic champion strolls into my school, steals my thunder, and dares to challenge me, the great Euthymos?

en: Does the great Euthymos accept this challenge, or is he too afraid?

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Afraid?

en: Try sparring with my students first. We'll see if you are as strong as you say you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have me wrong. I'm just a passing misthios.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Ha! I knew from first sight that you couldn't be the champion. You don't have the stature.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I advise you to not take me lightly.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Ho, is that so? What say you have a go at some of my best students, then?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's see what your students are made of.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Be careful, I heard the healers have their hands full these days.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure they will find time to tend to injured youth.

speaker: The Great Euthymos
en: Don't hit too hard, the misthios might cry!

speaker: Student 1
en: Can you withstand the might of my spear?

speaker: The Great Euthymos

en: I have the feeling you could talk about bears all day. I'll return when I have the skins.

en: Seems like he doubted Deianeira's loyalty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Should I have heard those names?

speaker: Timon
en: Deianeira is a champion of Boeotia, and Astra is her cousin. They do everything together - even kill.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wouldn't expect someone of such renown to need help.

speaker: Timon
en: Abreas and I used to spar with them as children. They work as one, covering each other's weaknesses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then they'll be weaker alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've lost family too. It's your duty to avenge him.

en: I don't want to kill Deianeira. I want Astra killed instead.

en: I'll kill Astra for you.

en: When they killed Abreas, they took a necklace I made him. I want it back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can do.

en: Boeotia is large, and I don't have time to waste.

en: I hope this necklace brings him some peace.

en: Your grandmother... was an oracle?

en: Told by vile people with evil intentions.

en: No, it has to be me. I need to kill her.

en: I do not know. But one of my contacts is nearby. Get your answers there.

en: Now, was that so hard?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's nothing.

en: It's nothing.

en: It's time to attack.

en: I know the price.

en: Not yet. We need to be more prepared. We can't let that snake get away this time.

en: What the

en: Hold your ground. We can't let the Eagle Bearer get away!

en: What are you afraid of? Pull yourself together!

en: Search every house. The Eagle Bearer is nearby. Watch your back!

speaker: Persian Soldier
en: They're somewhere here. Keep your eyes peeled!

speaker: Soldier
en: I can't see anything! The smoke is too thick—this is useless!

speaker: Persian Soldier
en: We only leave when we get the Eagle Bearer's head! We're gonna find you. We're gonna kill you!

speaker: Darius
en: Where is Amorges?

speaker: Soldier
en: The mines! But you'll never get around his defenses.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll crush his defenses. And then I'll kill him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing is impenetrable. We'll find a way in.

speaker: Soldier
en: You're insane. Both of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're going to tell Amorges that the Eagle Bearer—the great disruption of the Greek world—is here at his door.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You tell him I'm coming. For him. For Elpidios. And I don't knock.

speaker: Darius
en: Go! I'll take care of the Order guards.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to get to the mines. I'll take out as many as I can on the way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He must be here somewhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't hide from me, Amorges!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's too quiet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stop hiding, Amorges! Come get what you deserve.

speaker: Gergis
en: We meet again, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know this can't end well, Gergis. Just walk away.

speaker: Gergis
en: It's not that simple. Amorges has orders, and I have duties to fulfil. And... I have no intention of walking away, Kassandra. After all I've written about you, learned of your feats—I know I can't defeat you. Yet I cannot simply stand aside. We both have our reasons. For me, it's Persia. Make it through me, and Amorges awaits you in the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Amorges is using you! Don't be stupid. We don't have to fight.

speaker: Gergis
en: I do this of my own accord and my duty and devotion to Persia. The will of Amorges has nothing to do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know there's no talking you out of this. In another time, things might have been different for us. But— Not this time.

speaker: Gergis
en: Unfortunately.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your loyalty to your home and commander are admirable, Gergis. But the Order has no place in the Greek world.

speaker: Gergis
en: Everything the Order has done, everything I have done, has been in service of a cause greater than any individual's.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, all the deaths and suffering... That is justified?

speaker: Gergis
en: For all the greater good, Kassandra— All things are permitted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We didn't have to do this.

speaker: Order Scribe (female)
en: Look, the Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Order Scribe (short-haired male)
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is

speaker: Order Scribe (long-haired male)
en: Amorges? He's in the temple above the mines. But that time will come.

speaker: Order Scribe (female)
en: She's just like Gergis described in his entries. Fierce.

speaker: Order Scribe (short-haired)
en: Oh, Gergis. He was the best of us.

speaker: Order Scribe (long-haired)
en: You were his favourite character, Eagle Bearer. And yet you murdered him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I had no choice. But I'd kill him again if needed to get to Amorges.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Gergis was part of the Order. All of you deserve what's coming.
