en: We have no intention of walking away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get to my son.

speaker: Order Scribe (female)
en: Ah, Elpidios. She still has her littlest warrior in her heart.

speaker: Order Scribe (short-haired)
en: She still has... hope.

speaker: Order Scribe (female)
en: What a foolish thing to hold on to.

speaker: Order Scribe (long-haired)
en: We will fight for Persia until our dying breath. The lives, the razed cities. It is for Amorges' vision of peace. His grand design. All things are permitted.

en: Amorges is in the temple. I'm coming Elpidios. I'll find you.

en: There he is, hiding in plain sight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A decoy. Why am I not surprised?

en: Elpenor, you coward! Elpenor knew I would come for him. Used that imposter to lure me into a trap. Your plan failed, Elpenor. Soon you will join your imposter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Death is coming for you, Elpenor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can smell that malaka's stench.

en: What a shame. We would have made you rich. Before we killed you. Don't take it personally, misthios. Your mother's the one we really want. Don't fight it. The Cult always gets what it wants. We already have Deimos. We'll find your mother, and you'll be dead.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Killing me is a mistake.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Trusting you on Kephallonia was a mistake.

speaker: Elpenor
en: I'm the reason you left that island alive. The Cult wanted you dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What cult? Where are they?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The small shard I found on Elpenor is like nothing I've ever seen. Might come in handy.

en: Hey, shit-face! Get down here!

en: Cyclops's got a message for you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell your boss he can stick it

en: That's for last week!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka!

en: The Cyclops said you like to act tough. So act tough!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get a little closer, and I will.

en: You should know by now. The Cyclops always collects his debts. You have a lesson to learn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the Cyclops wants to teach me, tell him to come here himself.

speaker: Rogue
en: Never mess with the Cyclops!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Last week? This shit happens every week. I can't keep doing this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks for the warning.

speaker: Phoibe
en: What happened to you?

speaker: Mithios
en: It's nothing, Phoibe. All taken care of now.

speaker: Phoibe
en: The Cyclops again, huh? Hasn't he learned his lesson yet?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Apparently not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. Help yourself.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You hungry too, Ikaros? Do you think Zeus would bless me with an eagle? Like he blessed you, Kassandra? ...Maybe you could ask him for me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe...

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've been over this.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I know, I know. He's just an eagle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll try to put in a good word for you.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Finally!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So. What are you doing here?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Oh! I almost forgot! Markos is looking for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does that weasel want now?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Don't know. He wants you to meet him at his new house. On his vineyard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? A vineyard? Maláka!

speaker: Phoibe
en: It's on the road to Sami. He says wine will make him rich!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Since when has he had a vineyard?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Yesterday I think.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So Markos—who owes me drachmae—is buying vineyards? With what money?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I dunno.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find Markos's new, beautiful estate?

speaker: Phoibe
en: You know the statue of Zeus on Mount Ainos? It's south of that!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I guess I owe Markos a little visit. Thank you, Phoibe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I'll go tell Markos you're coming.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Skree!

speaker: Thug
en: My head...

en: Fun's over. Tell that one-eyed freak if he ever sends you here again, I'm gonna cut out his other eye and feed it to my bird.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You made a mistake coming here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see Markos as soon as I'm dressed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll have to go up top to get dressed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Markos knew this would serve young Kassandra well. Can't imagine fighting the Cyclops's thugs with it now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eugh, that smells lovely. Probably time I emptied it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe slept here again, poor kid. No place to call home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not getting caught without armor twice today.

speaker: Rogue
en: There she is! Get her!

speaker: Thug
en: By Ares, we'll slice you right open.

en: That's what I get for sparing you? No manners.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Guess this is the vineyard... Straight ahead. There you are. Let's see what you've gotten yourself into this time, Markos.

speaker: Farmer
en: Boss—I keep telling you—you can't do that.

speaker: Markos
en: Why? It's my farm! I can plant where I want.

speaker: Farmer
en: The grapes will die here—all of them.

speaker: Markos
en: You have to forget what you know about the past, my friend—together, we will revolutionize wine making! Believe me, you will look back on this day and

speaker: Markos
en: Kassandra, thank the gods—Phoibe found you in time.

speaker: Farmer
en: Thinks he can tell me about grapes...

speaker: Markos
en: I can still hear you...

speaker: Markos
en: I was worried sick. The Cyclops sent his scum to find you. I think they mean you harm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wish you would have told me that before they hit me. But that's beside the point. You bought a vineyard, Markos? A vineyard?!

speaker: Markos
en: Why not? I like wine, you like wine. Everybody likes wine. Everybody buys wine! Why not from me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Because you don't know how to grow grapes or make wine?

speaker: Markos
en: I'm a fast learner! You grow grapes on the vine, then you get some wine!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's that simple, is it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Please, Markos. You'll fuck this up like you fuck up everything else. You can't pay me back in grapes.

speaker: Markos
en: You know me better than to think I don't have a plan. Markos always has a plan!

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. Then do you have the money you owe me?

speaker: Markos
en: Do I have the money I owe you? Of course. Of course. Well, no. Not at the moment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then—get—it.

speaker: Markos
en: Instantly, my friend, instantly. But—maybe you should do that. There is a merchant in Sami—I'm not very good at these things as you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to collect my own debt?

speaker: Markos
en: It's just waiting for you in Sami, my friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's the merchant?

speaker: Markos
en: Duris. You know Duris. He's very nice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Duris? How stupid can you get? Stop giving him money!

speaker: Markos
en: He always pays me back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: After I threaten him.

speaker: Markos
en: Exactly—everybody benefits. Duris gets his money. I get my interest—and you have work. Kephallonia is wonderful, is it not?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Duris? Again? Why do you keep lending him money?

speaker: Markos
en: He's a loyal friend. I don't want his family to starve.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a good friend, but you're bad with money.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find Duris?

speaker: Markos
en: In a shop in Sami overlooking the docks—you know this Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Will he be there?

speaker: Markos
en: You mistake me for the Pythia. I couldn't possibly know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you want to handle this one?

speaker: Markos
en: Not like you handled that olive oil business. That was—that was too much.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got the money.

speaker: Markos
en: And now we'll never get any more from him. If you kill them all, nobody benefits. Threatening them and maybe more... Breaking things, certainly. Seal the money if you have to, but don't robe me of my customers. Unless you can't avoid it. These things happen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'd better have my money, Markos. I'd hate to have to sell our vineyard.

speaker: Markos
en: Of course he will! Oh, after there's another matter I want to discuss with you. After.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, but I'm taking a horse. It's too hot and too long a walk to go on foot.

speaker: Markos
en: But

speaker: Kassandra
en: Think of it as interest, Markos. Everybody benefits.

speaker: Markos
en: Of course, my friend, you shall have your pick!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about this one.

speaker: Markos
en: The Skyros! You have an eye for sturdy stock, my friend! That horse can cling to mountain passes like a goat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The one in the middle. Tell me about it.

speaker: Markos
en: Ah! You have picked a beauty, my friend. That horse is from Thessalonia. Bred for its courage.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I like the look of the one on the right.

speaker: Markos
en: Ah, the Makedonian. These are bred for battle. A true warrior's horse!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've made my choice.

speaker: Markos
en: Which one will it be?

speaker: Markos
en: A, uh, a fine choice. But, this particular breed has a few... quirks that you might not be aware of. I wouldn't want you to take an unworthy horse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the one I want.

speaker: Markos
en: Are you sure, because

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: Everybody benefits. Especially you! You've chosen the great Phobos. He's never let me down!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phobos.

speaker: Markos
en: Remember, meet me at the temple in Sami when you have, uh, your money from Duris.

speaker: Markos
en: Ah, Euterpe! There's plenty of wine left to buy. Don't fret.

speaker: Euterpe
en: Not now, you fool! Phoibe's been taken.

speaker: Kassandra
en: By who?

speaker: Euterpe
en: Thugs of the Cyclops—who else? Snatched her right off the main road!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where they went.

speaker: Euterpe
en: In the direction of Ktimene Beach.

speaker: Markos
en: The beach? Can she swim?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get her.

speaker: Markos
en: Yes, go. But don't forget about dear Duris, Kassandra!

speaker: Civilian
en: I hope you're here to buy fish and not just hang about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your face looks more sour than this fishy stink.

speaker: Civilian
en: Why shouldn't I be sour, eh? My no-good son sailed off with my boat and should've been back hours ago! Probably showing off for that Mytilene girl. Bah!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The smell... Of course your son ran away. Doubt he'll come back.

speaker: Civilian
en: Choke on goat dung!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can leave...

speaker: Civilian
en: Hmm... On second thought. Would you fetch my lazy son? He's at Fisherman's Bay. An easy errand for fair pay.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's probably just lost track of time. I'm sure he'll be back eventually.

speaker: Civilian
en: Of course he'll be back eventually—but I need him back now! These fish aren't going to skin themselves, you know.

speaker: Civilian
en: Say... Have you got time for an errand? Go look for my boy on the bay bordering the Petrified Valley and Ancient Pearl. And when you find him, scare him a bit to teach him a lesson. I'll pay you for it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Good. You find him, and I'll tan his hide.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And where is exactly is this bay?

speaker: Civilian
en: Fisherman's Bay is northeasy of here, and runs through the middle of our island. You can't miss it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more about the girl.

speaker: Civilian
en: I don't know... some Mytilene lovely, full of history and poetry from that school over there. She keeps my boy's head in the clouds instead of focused on his work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's quit chatting so I can go find your son.

speaker: Civilian
en: See that you do. I'll pay you, and then my boy's hide will pay for taking my boat out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to search Fisherman's Bay.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's the fishing boat. But where's the fisherman's son?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's blood in the water!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's the fisherman's son!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The fisherman's son. Looks like he got tangled up in the net trying to haul a heavy load of fish. Slipped. then the weight of the net dragged him down.

speaker: Civilian
en: Any word on my son?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your son is dead, drowned in his fishing net.

speaker: Civilian
en: No! My boy... my poor boy. I pushed him too hard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your son is dead, drowned in your own fishing nets. He died trying to impress his sour father, who pushed him too hard.

speaker: Civilian
en: My fault... You think it's my fault? Get out of my shop. Go!

speaker: Civilian
en: My poor boy! What did I do? What did I do? I pushed him too hard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your son ran away with the girl. I found your boat abandoned on the opposite shore, and two sets of footprints pointing to Mytilene.

speaker: Civilian
en: But he's safe? Oh... Thank Poseidon.

speaker: Civilian
en: ...Thank Poseidon for not robbing me of the chance of slapping some sense into that no-good boy.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: This is Roxana's year. She's going to win the Battle of One Hundred Hands for sure.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: What? She doesn't even have an official training partner.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: It's because she's too good for any of them!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Roxana nearly killed my son when they sparred this week.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: He's lucky. Had it been in the Battle she would have killed him.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: ...Yeah.

speaker: Roxana
en: You amateurs are wasting my time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These men look like they need a doctor.

speaker: Roxana
en: They're lousy sparring partners, every last one. I need professionals to practice with before the Battle of One Hundred Hands. I need a champion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe your "champion" has arrived.

speaker: Roxana
en: Is that right? If you're serious, I'm a sanctioned competitor in the battle. You practice with me, and Drakios will let both of us officially enter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just a working misthios, not a "champion". Still, I might be able to help you with your problem.

speaker: Roxana
en: Well, I won't be able to pay you in any traditional way, but I am a sanctioned competitor in the Battle. If you train with me, we can both officially enter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This battle

speaker: Roxana
en: The Battle of One Hundred Hands is the most grueling contest in the Greek world. The body count is high, and the chance of success low. Are you sure that's something you want to train for?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Killing's what I do, and I do it well.

speaker: Roxana
en: You have the right attitude, I'll give you that. But you can't simply power your way to victory in the Battle of One Hundred Hands. It takes preparation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm prepared to work hard. The rest lies with the Fates.

speaker: Roxana
en: Humility is a fine trait in a warrior—as long as it's hiding true ferocity below the surface. That's what's needed in the Battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If this battle is so difficult, why enter it at all?

speaker: Roxana
en: I'm not from a family of means, champion, and have always dreamed about the Hundred-Hands purse. My father, my brother tried to win it years ago. Even my mother entered last time, and now they're all gone. Dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want the drachmae.

speaker: Roxana
en: I don't care about the drachmae, not now. I need to save my family's legacy from the edge of yet another champion's blade - I need to win and become like a hero of old.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the battle's so hard, why do you think you'll win?

speaker: Roxana
en: I train at all hours until my body gives out. Before bed, I make offerings to Ares. I wake in the night to strategize. And then... I rise in the morning to do it all again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's an impressive amount of work.

speaker: Roxana
en: If I don't win the Battle, at least I'll know I've done all I can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned I should talk to Drakios about officially entering the Battle. Where can I find him?

speaker: Roxana
en: He's usually in the town on Melos - doesn't go far.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's say I want to fight in the Battle of One Hundred Hands...

speaker: Roxana
en: Then fight me and prove you are a worthy training companion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You asked for it.

speaker: Roxana
en: Come on, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That hurt.

speaker: Roxana
en: Ooh, I've made you angry. Stings, doesn't it, champion?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've felt worse.

speaker: Roxana
en: You're cute when you're angry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not angry.

speaker: Roxana
en: Of course not.

speaker: Roxana
en: You need to push me! Are you even trying? Nice move.

speaker: Roxana
en: It seems you are the champion I've been looking for. A real Spartan, if I'm right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are.

speaker: Roxana
en: I sensed it in the way you fought. Aggressive, but not reckless. My name's Roxana.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Roxana
en: Next on the agenda is archery training. Are you ready?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready.

speaker: Roxana
en: So eager! Well, a shipment of wolves has wrecked on shore nearby. They were meant to be part of the Battle, but now, they're our practice targets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go hunting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have other things to attend to first.

speaker: Roxana
en: When you're ready, there's a shipwreck on the north coast of the island. Meet me there.

en: I see why you're so determined to get the Spartans at a disadvantage.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: They are already at a disadvantage. They made an enemy of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know enough to keep going.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Do you have my seals?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: The Spartans must be aware of your actions by now. They can't be happy. Interested in upsetting them some more?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You left a note on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: A mercenary has been raiding sacrifices from our altar and sharing them with a nearby bandit camp. I'd sooner see our sacrifice to the gods destroyed than squandered on those vermin.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you're hoping I'll kill all the bandits?

speaker: Woman
en: That's right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

speaker: Woman
en: You'll be doing divine work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Down on your luck? Have I got a solution for you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's all this about?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: It's about adventure! Thrills! Danger! ...And untold fortunes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Danger... Ha. I never back down from a challenge.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Then step right up and put your drachmae where your mouth is... For this kind of opportunity doesn't come around every day.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I love a good adventure.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: If you've got the drachmae and the time, I've got a once-in-a-lifetime adventure just for you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Secrecy is key, misthios. We can't just have anyone knowing there's a fortune to be found. But first! Everything has a price. Pay up, and I'll give you a tablet with everything you need to know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here you go.

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Excellent! Here you go. This tablet will lead you directly to untold riches.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What? Just tell me where

speaker: Street Vendor
en: The tablet reveals all!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does that even mean?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Just look at tablet and follow the directions, misthios! My work here is done.

speaker: Treasure Tablet
en: Off the east coast of Kythera, on Diakofti Island, your reward awaits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Empty?! I'm going to snap that man's neck in two.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: The misthios beat us to it!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: The treasure is ours! Give it over!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's going on? The chest was empty!

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Inconceivable! Maybe you don't know how to read a tablet? I guarantee you there's something inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can you be so sure?

speaker: Street Vendor
en: Because I'm the one who put it there! Uh... I mean... malaka!

speaker: Street Vendor
en: No! No! No!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the last mercenary. I'll find the foul-mouthed old lady and take her up on that wine.

en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Hermit
en: I knew you'd be back. The owl knows. She's Athena's favorite bird, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for the key to the vault.

speaker: Hermit
en: Then what are you doing here? That's nearly ridiculous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're telling me it's not here.

speaker: Hermit
en: I hid it somewhere safe. It's underwater in the Ariabignes Shipwreck.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That doesn't sound very safe.

speaker: Hermit
en: How could it not be safe, surrounded by so many defenders?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do I never get the easy jobs?

speaker: Hermit
en: Whooo knows?

speaker: Hermit
en: I knew you'd be back. The owl knows. She's Athena's favorite bird, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for the key to the vault.

speaker: Hermit
en: Then what are you doing here? That's nearly ridiculous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're telling me it's not here.

speaker: Hermit
en: I hid it somewhere safe. It's in an abandoned camp on Aegina island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That doesn't sound very safe.

speaker: Hermit
en: How could it not be safe, surrounded by so many defenders?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do I never get the easy jobs?

speaker: Hermit
en: Whooo knows?

speaker: Hermit
en: Good luck finding the key!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found the key. Time to return to that strange woman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found your key. Your associate certainly kept it well-protected.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: He ought to have, I paid him well enough to do so.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where exactly are you getting your drachmae from?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I have very few needs and spend only on what I find important. I'm very nearly thrifty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now that I have the key, is there anything else I need to prepare to visit the island of fire?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You tell me, misthios. Do you feel prepared to explore the Foundry of Hephaistos?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait, you're not going to ask me a strange question first?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Perhaps I'll think of one later.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready to explore that island.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Very good. You are proving your worth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Am I now? I'm impressed.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: There is an island swathed with clouds of smoke, where the earth blazes with fire. It's called the Foundry of Hephaistos. A legendary helmet is kept there. Bring it here so I might study it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Seems like a dangerous journey for just a helmet.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: It's not nearly the only treasure there. You can keep anything else you find.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll go to the island and find the helmet.

speaker: Captain
en: Misthios! I prayed to Poseidon that one as mighty as you would come to aid us. I'd nearly lost hope, but here you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was told your village was in danger.

speaker: Captain
en: Yes. My brother sailed out to take on the soldiers threatening to burn us out. They take a dim view of piracy, you know. But they ambushed his ship and, well... My brother never saw home again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sharks are merciless.

speaker: Captain
en: How did you know he was killed by sharks?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I visited your brother's tomb. I'm sorry for your loss.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have ways of finding things out.

speaker: Captain
en: I suppose I won't ask then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, are those soldiers still threatening you?

speaker: Captain
en: Yes, but I have a plan. I'm going to build a warship, one they won't be able to sink. My village will survive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem determined. What do you have left to do?

speaker: Captain
en: Too much. There's a detachment keeping the pressure on us, not far from here. It's hard to gather building supplies while they're around.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you need supplies... or you need that detachment taken care of.

speaker: Captain
en: Well aren't you as clever as Athena herself! What would you be willing to do for us?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll make those soldiers regret taking up arms against you.

speaker: Captain
en: Many thanks, misthios! I've heard rumors they are stationed west of the Ruined Sanctuary of Ajax.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then that's where I'll go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one will hear from those soldiers again.

speaker: Captain
en: Then I'm safe to build my ship and what's more, my brother is avenged. You have my thanks.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I also rescued a prisoner. He should be on his way over.

speaker: Captain
en: Thank the gods. You've done us a great favor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: May your new ship bring you victory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the supplies you need and leave the fighting to you.

speaker: Captain
en: Fair enough. Though I might need you to take up arms against dryads. I need plenty of olive wood to make sure this ship is solid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get right to it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This should be all of it.

speaker: Captain
en: Thank you! Now there's just one last thing we need—an eye of protection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For the bow of the ship you mean?

speaker: Captain
en: Exactly! There's probably one in the Ariabignes Shipwreck. At least if Poseidon hasn't claimed it for himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it's there I'll find it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, will this eye do?

speaker: Captain
en: Yes... I suppose it will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is something wrong?

speaker: Captain
en: I remember this eye staring at me as the ship went down. So many sailors died that day...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know, there's more you can do with a new ship than just pirating.

speaker: Captain
en: I believe you are right, misthios. Perhaps you have come to show me wisdom after all. Here, take this. It'll be the last of our spoils.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. May you find a more peaceful path in the future.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should get back to that strange woman and let her know what happened.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I met the dead man's brother.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Ah? So, why did such a man go sailing in shark-filled waters?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He was a pirate and set out to fight the soldiers who threatened his family. They sank his ship, leaving him to the sharks.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: That's nearly tragic. So, how did you resolve the matter? That is what you do as a misthios, resolve matters, right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The pirate's brother asked for my help, so I eliminated some soldiers who attacked his village. He will be able to defend himself next time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The soldiers had already attacked the pirates. For the sake of justice I returned that attack.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I gave the shipbuilding materials to the pirate's brother to help him build a sturdier vessel. I think I set an example for him. He's decided to quit piracy and start a new life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I dove deep to retrieve the protective eye the new ship needed. Poseidon must have smiled on that, because he enlightened the pirate's brother and set him on a more peaceful path.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I see. That answer is quite revealing of your character.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you concerned about my character?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Something will come of it. Very soon I suspect. But here, take this for now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you... Though it seems like you have more plans for me.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Perhaps. You have proven you could survive the dangers of the ocean. But what about an island of fire and smoke?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like to explore this strange island.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Good. You're very nearly impressing me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh really? I should be impressed.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I would like to send you to this island of smoke and flame, but an associate of mine still has my key to the vault within. Without it, your trip would be in vain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are they as strange as you?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: That's nearly amusing. My associate lives in the graveyard you visited earlier. He lives as a hermit. He'll have time to talk, even to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go reclaim your key.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Gorgophone was an extraordinary woman born of Andromeda , daughter of the proud queen and king of Ethiopia, and Perseus , the Gorgon-slayer after whome she is named.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "It has long been tradition that women should marry but once, as virgins. If their husbands died before them, they were to live out their lives as widows. Gorgophone defied this tradition to become the greatest grandmother of Hellas."

speaker: Kassandra
en: "It is said that a warrior woman of advanced age brought so much chaos to the people of Lake Tritonis that Perseus himself arrived to take her life. And some wise people say that was Gorgophone, enjoying her last act of rebellion."

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Gorgophone's first husband was Perieres, King of Messene and Sparta. Their sons grew up to be bold princes and kings of Sparta themselves."

speaker: Kassandra
en: "But Gorgophone had a second husband, King Oibalos of Sparta, who would bring her even greater children and grandchildren. Helen of Troy, Kastor and Polydeukes, Klytemnestra , and many more were her descendants."

speaker: Kassandra
en: This helmet seems common, but it's been carefully hidden... I should get it back to that woman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That burning island and trapped tomb... You could say they were nearly a challenge.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Even for you? You exaggerate, Eagle Bearer. But did you find the helmet?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I did. But how could you have known about such a terrible place? And who are you to send me there?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Who do you think I am, Kassandra? Some say I show great wisdom, others say I am Wisdom herself. Tell me, who do you think I am?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You sent me to a graveyard, where I met a desperate man who said Athena herself had sent me to kill him. But I suppose that could mean he only thought you were Athena.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: It's unwise to give too much credit to the rantings of a madman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you sent me to a pirate in need who asked me to help him as he saw fit. Was that a divine test of wisdom, or just practicality?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You sent yourself to a pirate. I merely provided the chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you sent me to a village threatened by lions, with a strange wild man at the center of it all. Was it a divine test of wisdom, or just a coincidence?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You sent yourself to the village. I only provided the opportunity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Finally, that strange hermit with the key... He was even under a statue of Athena's Icon, the owl. Did you set that all up as a joke, or is there truth in his beliefs?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: So many thoughts in that head of yours. It's nearly too much to contemplate. Make your decision, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems you want me to believe you're Athena. Mysterious riddles, a helmet of all things to find. It's clever, but obvious.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: If this is the case, it is I who should congratulate you on your cleverness. Here show me the helmet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope this was worth it.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You have great faith in humanity. I hope you see it for both its potential and its failings. I'll make an adjustment and... Yes. I think this will be best suited for you.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You aren't very principled, are you? One who stands for nothing falls for everything... I've seen all I need to. Here you go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As the granddaughter of Leonidas, bearer of the bloodline, I must recognize you as Athena. This helmet you have asked me to return bears your own blessing.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: If this is true, I should accept your recognizance. But for now, let me see that helmet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope this was worth it.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You have great faith in humanity. I hope you see it for both its potential and its failings. I'll make an adjustment and... Yes. I think this will be best suited for you.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You aren't very principled, are you? One who stands for nothing falls for everything... I've seen all I need to. Here you go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I hope you've gained some wisdom from this journey.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, I've learned that profit can come from the strangest sources.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You have earned my respect, Kassandra.

speaker: Village Leader
en: We don't get many misthios around here. What's your business with us?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here to take care of your lion problem.

speaker: Village Leader
en: How do you know about the Curse of Beasts?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I visited the tomb of a farmer who fell victim to the "Curse of Beasts." You have my sympathies.

speaker: Village Leader
en: Thank you. It's comforting to know that strangers from afar will show us kindness.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When you are cursed to face the fiercest beasts the gods can create, it's my destiny to intervene.

speaker: Village Leader
en: Then thank the gods you've come to help us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more about this curse.

speaker: Village Leader
en: It's horrible. Lions have been attacking our village, slaughtering livestock, and ruining food stores. And then one of them killed my nephew! The lion ran away, a leg hanging from his jaw... It's nearly indescribable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Strange that it didn't eat the man whole right there.

speaker: Village Leader
en: You have the cold reason of Athena to notice that. The lions are swimming all the way from Aegina Island to attack us. No one dares set out fishing nets anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll track down these beasts for you.

speaker: Village Leader
en: Thank you. May the gods let you remove the curse on us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Bloodstains. From a recent kill.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A recent fire? But who was here to make this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Footprints? Someone else is alive on this godsforsaken island.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone's living here. I should speak with them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you doing here? This island is dangerous.

speaker: Brother Lion
en: Dangerous for you, maybe. My brothers will take care of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brothers... You mean the lions?

speaker: Brother Lion
en: Yes! Once, we hunted together. Now that I am sick, they hunt and bring me meat. When my strength returns, I will rejoin them. I'm nearly well enough now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The lions are attacking the villagers across the water. Their leader sent me here. Do you understand what those beasts are doing?

speaker: Brother Lion
en: Lions do what they must. Though I suppose if I was better, they wouldn't need to hunt for me. Some olive tree bark should make a good medicine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your story is madness. I'm going to protect those villagers by killing the lions.

speaker: Brother Lion
en: My brothers! No...

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the last of them. I should return to the village and tell them they're safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the medicine to help you. Once you're better, this lion curse should be lifted.

speaker: Brother Lion
en: Thank you. There's a big olive tree on the west side of this island. Some say Athena herself planted it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This should help with that man's illness.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, may this cure your illness.

speaker: Brother Lion
en: Thank you. You can tell those villagers my brothers will end their hunt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These lions aren't the monsters, it's you. And since those villagers can't wait for the gods to punish you, I will do so in their place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I killed every lion on that island. You should be safe now.

speaker: Village Leader
en: What a bold act! You must be the most powerful misthios in the land. Here, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The lions were killing to serve their master. I helped him and now he has called them off.

speaker: Village Leader
en: What strangeness is that! A human was the source of our curse? Well, I'm pleased you dealt with him in any case. Here, have this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your curse is over. Those lions were killing to feed a human master. With him gone, they should return to normal and leave you alone.

speaker: Village Leader
en: A human master! I never would have thought... You have done us a great service. Here, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to return to that strange woman and tell her what happened here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lions won't trouble that village anymore.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I had nearly no doubt you could do that. My question is, how did you judge best to solve their problem?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I killed every last lion on that island. There's nothing left to threaten those villagers.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: As response as fierce as that of the lions themselves. Why do you think it will be successful?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I helped the man the lions were hunting for. He promised to lead them away, and I believed him.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: A compassionate response showing great faith in people. Why do you think this decision right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I killed the man the lions were hunting for. Now that he's gone, they should go back to their lives as beasts and leave the people alone.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: A bloodthirsty response worthy of one who wants to be the head of their own pride. Why do you believe that will help the villagers?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do what anyone can do. I consider the situation and make what I believe is the best decision at the time. If I am right or wrong, only time will tell.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am the Eagle Bearer, heir of Leonidas. What I decide is right. Let the gods confront me themselves if what I do is wrong.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Ah yes, I believe I understand you better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's to understand?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Everything in this world is worth understanding. A reward for demonstrating your wisdom.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. Is that all you want?.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Not if you wish to enrich yourself further. You have already faced an island full of lions. Would you discover the secrets of an island wreathed in fire and smoke?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see the truth of this island.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Good. You're very nearly impressing me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh really? I should be impressed.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I would like to send you to an island of smoke and flame, but an associate of mine still has my key to the vault within. Without it, your trip would be in vain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are they are strange as you?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: That's nearly amusing. My associate lives in the graveyard you visited for me earlier. He lives as a hermit. He'll have time to talk, even to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go reclaim your key.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Misthios, may I trade your time for wealth? You look wiser than the average mercenary. Perhaps you're nearly as wise as Athena herself...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wiser and stronger. You might watch your tongue, auntie.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You might watch yourself, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You speak plainly, auntie.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I speak the truth, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know me?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Don't pretend to be ignorant of your infamy, Kassandra the Eagle Bearer. I have a series of tasks I thought someone of your reputation could handle. But if you feel you're not up to it...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What kind of tasks?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: To begin, I have a test of judgment. Which god is more dangerous, Poseidon or Apollo? The answer lies in a nearby tomb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is just a riddle.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Riddles are telling. And rewarding, when I give them. Prove your worth to me by going to the graveyard near the Sanctuary of Athena and solving it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't have time for riddles at the moment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, I'll figure out this riddle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Here lies my father, a simple farmer. A lion tore him to pieces as he brought in his grain. May the gods grant him peace."

speaker: Kassandra
en: A golden plate marked with the sun. An offering dedicated to Apollo and his youthful strength.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lions are a golden beast with manes like the sun. Surely they are the favorite of Apollo... Does that make him the more dangerous god?

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Here lies my brother, a brave man. He was chosen to confront the enemy threatening our village. But his ship sank, and sharks feasted on his flesh. What little parts were found, I sealed in this tomb."

speaker: Kassandra
en: A model ship as an offering to Poseidon. Clearly someone feared death in the sea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sharks are under the command of Poseidon, as are all creatures of the sea. Is he the more dangerous god?

speaker: Hermit
en: Whoooo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Protect us from teeth that tear and beasts that bite." Sounds like a child's prayer.

speaker: Dorykleidas
en: You! I know who you are. Athena sent you to kill me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would you think that?

speaker: Dorykleidas
en: I was to be tried for murder, but a great fire burned up the court and all the records. I walked free! But lately I've heard Athena in my dreams, saying I would meet justice. And here you are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, I am the emissary of the gods. Cause me trouble, and I'll end your miserable life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An old woman hired me to come here. You weren't part of that contract. But lose your temper and I might change my mind.

speaker: Dorykleidas
en: I know what Athena told me. I'll face my death blade-first!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen all there is to see here. Now to answer that woman's riddle.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You spent enough time in the graveyard. What did you find?

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you know I actually went?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I have my ways.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there dirt on my sandals? A look in my eye? It seems to me you're good at figuring people out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems you may have a gift from Mount Olympos.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Perhaps. But I want to know which god you think is more dangerous, Poseidon or Apollo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you so interested in knowing?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Because I have two tasks that require the attention of a misthios, but I can trust the easier task to nearly anybody. I'm going to assign the more dangerous one to you, naturally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was a farmer attacked by a lion while he harvested his crops. An attack by a golden beast under the shining sun... Surely that is the work of Apollo, making him the more dangerous god.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Gold is a seductive danger in many ways... Yes, Apollo is a sensible choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad you agree.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You've wisely considered the subject. I approve. Take this, it's for your judgment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You ask for my judgment, but you seem to be judging me.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Am I? Consider this. Lions don't usually eat farmers unprovoked.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you think something is pushing the lions to behave strangely.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I'm sure you could find out what that is and help the locals with their lion problem. You'll find them in Argolis, east of the Hypermnestra Camp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll pay them a visit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Both of those gods may be dangerous, but I met a man who claimed Athena sent me to kill him.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: How strange. If she could hear your words, I'm sure the goddess of justice would be amused.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was a man torn to pieces by sharks on his way to confront pirates. That sounds like the punishment of Poseidon to those who would insult him.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Defending a territory no man can invade with deadly force... Poseidon would indeed seem to be the greater danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad you agree.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: You've wisely considered the subject. I approve. Take this, it's for your judgment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You ask for my judgment, but you seem to be judging me.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: Am I? Consider this. A man took great risks to take to the sea. Perhaps you could figure out why.

speaker: Kassandra
en: His tomb mentioned pirates. Perhaps they're still a danger.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
en: I believe you should find his family in Megaris, south of the Ruined Temple of Apollo.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll pay them a visit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aiantides the Proud... Strange name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aiantides the Proud. What did I do now to deserve your gifts, friend?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Exactly where Aiantides said it'd be.

speaker: Aiantides
en: There you are, maláka!

speaker: Aiantides
en: Whoa, whoa! Wait, it's me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aiantides...?

speaker: Aiantides
en: The Proud!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Finally, Aiantides, we meet. It's good to see you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was a dangerous way to introduce yourself, Aiantides.

speaker: Aiantides
en: You should have seen your face, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Aiantides
en: But no! That's not why I'm here. You! Why can't you just leave me alone?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did I do now? Save your step-sister's cows?

speaker: Aiantides
en: My aunt was among the stranded people you saved from the fortress.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've got to be kidding

speaker: Aiantides
en: And now I don't have anything left to reward you. My pockets are dry, my house empty! I've come here to tell you that I, Aiantides the Proud, who shall never be indebted to anyone, will owe you, Eagle Bearer, a—favor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, no. You've done enough. You don't owe me anything.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Don't make this harder than it is! Tell me. What is it you need done?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right, I've done so much for you. I accept your favor.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Excellent! So tell me. What is it you need?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Join my crew and work on the Adrestia.

speaker: Aiantides
en: No, no. I have a family to take care of. Something else. Anything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to get some code books from the Tempest. Find them for me.

speaker: Aiantides
en: What do I look like to you? A thief? No, something else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a powerful commander here in Achaia that I need killed—the Tempest.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Murder? You ask murder of me?! Unacceptable! Ask for something else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are mercenaries trying to kill me. Take care of them.

speaker: Aiantides
en: I'm not fighter. Look at me! I owe you a favor, not my life. There must be something else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know what, just leave me alone. That would help—a lot.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Fine! But this isn't over, Eagle Bearer. I know we will see each other again.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Then I shall redeem my honor! You will ask something of me, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Unbelievable. I hope I don't run into him again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Could be one of Stentor's scouts. Looks like he's run into some problems.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Port of Nisaia. If I'm going to find Athenian supplies this'll be the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Those blue supply crates with the white owl are the ones I need to destroy. A single fire arrow should do the trick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fort Geraneia is formidable. This must be where the Athenians keep their war chest. I should use Ikaros to find what I need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should get the treasure and leave quietly. The Athenian soldier's won't be so eager to fight when they don't get paid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now the Athenian leader is dead. I should return to Stentor.

en: Fort Geraneia is formidable. This must be where the Athenians keep their war chest. I should use Ikaros to find what I need.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's what I'm looking for.

en: I should get the treasure and leave quietly. The Athenian soldier's won't be so eager to fight when they don't get paid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is Azaes a physician and an Archon?

speaker: Sick Patient 1
en: Azaes saw me yesterday. He told me I'll be able to go home soon.

speaker: Sick Patient 2
en: You're a lucky one. The man next to me hasn't come back yet. Maybe Azaes is treating him?

speaker: Azaes
en: What have I missed... What must I do...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Azaes. You have your hands full.

speaker: Azaes
en: Dikastes! You're a welcome sight. The only one I've had in some time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So many sick. I'm surprised anything can spread in a place as advanced as this.

speaker: Azaes
en: It's shocking. Nothing I have tried will cure the sick or stop the pathogen spreading. I've lost so many already.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When did you first notice people were getting sick?

speaker: Azaes
en: At the start of this cycle. It began quite slowly and I didn't think much of it. But then, the cases grew rapidly day by day. The more that fell sick, the faster the pathogen spread.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You seem really worried. Have you ever seen a sickness like this before?

speaker: Azaes
en: No. There are many odd phenomena during this cycle. Plants dying, strange insects and animal attacks. I worry what this could signify.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, we'll find a way to stop the sickness. Tell me what you need.

speaker: Azaes
en: Well, there was a device being worked on by a scientist named Consus. Its intention was to rapidly heal injuries and eradicate diseases.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Was?

speaker: Azaes
en: His device is missing. Scientists here have tried to replicate it based on the schematics, but it's still in the experimental phase. And, it hasn't been tested on humans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So it may not work.

speaker: Azaes
en: That's not the biggest issue. Poseidon has outlawed the use of our technology on humans. I fear that if we don't act quickly, the pathogen will spread across Atlantis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you think this healing device can help the stick, then I'll make sure that you have it.

speaker: Azaes
en: The wisdom of an Isu, but the compassion of a human—you were a good choice for Dikastes. You'll find the device in one of the Isu laboratories in the Consus Archive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In Athens, when the plague spread, Hippokrates thought the only option left was to burn the bodies—and the sick with them.

speaker: Azaes
en: You're talking about murdering innocent people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's mercy, Azaes. Better than even more dying because we wouldn't act.

speaker: Azaes
en: No, we are not barbarians. We don't waste precious life if there's a chance it can be saved. Please, find the device and bring it to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, we'll do it your way. Tell me where it is and I will.

speaker: Azaes
en: You'll find the device in one of the Isu laboratories in the Consus Archive. With luck, we can save these people my father discovers what's happened.

speaker: Atlantean
en: We have to stay here a little longer. The Archon said he'll have the cure soon and you'll be all better.

speaker: Sick Patient
en: I just want to go home. I hate this place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The device Azaes wants must be inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An Isu device. It's like nothing I've ever seen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've brought the, uh... glowing cloth you asked for.

speaker: Azaes
en: It's a nanotech matter regenerator in fact. But, you have it. I can't believe it.

speaker: Azaes
en: Now then, let's see what this thing can do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Azaes! What the fuck did you do?

speaker: Azaes
en: I thought I had calibrated correctly. Oh no, what have I done? I killed this poor human, the device doesn't work, and you stole it against Poseidon's laws. What do we do now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This device is dangerous. Maybe Poseidon outlawed it for a reason. I don't think you should use it on anyone else.

speaker: Azaes
en: I was so hopeful, but you're right. This device isn't ready to be used on live subjects. All I've done is add to the pain and suffering.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Some things can't be fixed with devices or intellect. There are problems even the Isu can't solve.

speaker: Azaes
en: I suppose all I can do is return this device to the laboratory and make sure the victims are comfortable until the end.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This device is your only chance of stopping the sickness. You need to keep trying.

speaker: Azaes
en: Yes, you're right. Not trying will just mean more innocent lives are lost. I think if I make some adjustments, I can get it to function on humans correctly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone seems to be looking much better. Well, almost everyone.

speaker: Azaes
en: The device still needs work, but it has incredible potential. Poseidon won't be happy that we broke his law, but I'm glad you were the one to do it and not me. In any case I'm eternally grateful for your help. Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's Brasidas?

speaker: Labotas
en: What do you want with him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't question me—take me to him.

speaker: Labotas
en: It concerns Sparta, so it concerns me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you were so "concerned," you'd be with your brothers preparing for battle. Now let's go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We fought together.

speaker: Labotas
en: A friend?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes... and a friend of Sparta. Now take me to him.

speaker: Labotas
en: Stop. I have orders—stand guard and wait for reinforcements. They were due two nights ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can stop waiting. I've arrived.

speaker: Labotas
en: You?! The Athenians are dogs at our throats. You won't talk so tough once you see them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I join you, and all they'll see is the ferryman.

speaker: Labotas
en: Ha! Well met, warrior. You better fight as good as you talk. Come. We go to Brasidas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't see any of your ships when I came in, but I can help.

speaker: Labotas
en: They're... sunk? My father was the captain on one of those ships. Come. Pledge your spear to Brasidas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas!

speaker: Brasidas
en: Yaaaarh!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deimos! ...This fight is between you and me.

speaker: Deimos
en: And it is one you can not win.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If Brasidas dies, his blood is on your hands.

speaker: Deimos
en: His, yours, and every one of your friends'.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you mad?! We can still stop

speaker: Deimos
en: Enough! We will not stop.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't want to kill you, Alexios. But I will stop you.

speaker: Deimos
en: My name is Deimos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: If we continue, one of us will die.

speaker: Deimos
en: Isn't that the point?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found mater.

speaker: Deimos
en: Finally reunited, only to lose each other again.

speaker: Persephone
en: I've given you everything. What more can I do?

speaker: Adonis
en: You won't let me leave.

speaker: Persephone
en: To be with her? Never.

speaker: Persephone
en: I never wanted this! I only turned this world into paradise to make it bearable. And then you arrived and made me blossom.

speaker: Adonis
en: Please just let me go.

speaker: Persephone
en: If you truly wanted to leave, you'd have already done it. Or have you forgotten?

speaker: Conversationalist
en: I wonder if Aphrodite would still love you if she knew what a coward you were.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not having second thoughts, are you?

speaker: Adonis
en: Persephone's right. She once gave me the chance to leave, but I was too much of a coward to take it.

speaker: Adonis
en: I also found out she sent Leonidas to Tartaros. He was to be our champion. I'm sorry, I can't do this anymore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis, I want you to close your eyes and imagine Aphrodite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't let Persephone make you forget why you're fighting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis, close your eyes and imagine all the people fighting by your side.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They believe in you. I believe in you. Don't let Persephone make you forget why you're fighting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis, I'm in this with you until the end. Don't abandon me now.

speaker: Adonis
en: You're right. It's Persephone's greatest talent, making us forget the ones we love.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keeps people from wanting to leave.

speaker: Adonis
en: Let's remind them, shall we?

speaker: Adonis
en: At the base of the Palace of the Kolossi you'll find one of Hermes' inventions, stolen from his workshop. It's said to destroy everything it touches.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are we destroying?

speaker: Adonis
en: Atop the palace is where Persephone keeps her sleeping Kolossi. Bring the device there and make sure they never wake again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are we waiting for?

speaker: Adonis
en: Try not to kill anyone. Success without detection and death is sure to convert more non-believers to our cause.

speaker: Adonis
en: When we first met, I laughed when you said you wanted to escape Elysium.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And now?

speaker: Adonis
en: I pity the god who stands in your way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what will you do?

speaker: Adonis
en: I have some preparations to make before our final assault on Persephone's palace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I meant when this is over.

speaker: Adonis
en: For the longest time, all I could think about was getting back to Aphrodite. But my heart broke when you told me about her spy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You deserved the truth.

speaker: Adonis
en: You've been a good friend. I never expected to find one here. Come find me before we launch our attack.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But what about Aphrodite?

speaker: Adonis
en: All this time you've helped me find my way back to her. But my heart broke when you told me about her spy. Our love was a dream, and in this paradise of lies the only person I can really trust is you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then shut up and kiss me.

speaker: Adonis
en: She's going to kill everybody.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good thing they're already dead.

speaker: Adonis
en: I have some final preparations to make before we launch our assault on the palace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come find you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't. I feel like too many gods are watching.

speaker: Adonis
en: You always struck me as someone who laughed in the faces of gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've already declared war on Persephone. I don't want to start one with Aphrodite as well.

speaker: Adonis
en: Perhaps you're right... I'd forgotten what's at stake. I need to go prepare. Come find me before we launch our assault on the palace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The rebellion's almost ready to make its stand. I should check back with Hekate in case she's returned. And get some answers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Anything you need a mercenary's help with?

speaker: Man
en: Athens has abandoned me, misthios. I was accused of trying to destroy a shrine, and now I have nothing. I have lost my citizenship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's a harsh punishment.

speaker: Man
en: I was framed! Now, I wish I had destroyed it. Or at least had my revenge on the man that framed me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to kill him.

speaker: Man
en: Yes. His death is the only answer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can count on me.

speaker: Man
en: It's time someone showed me mercy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you. For everything. Please, this isn't much, but take it.

en: She overheard the Sons of Xerxes discussing supplies they stole from a nearby fortress and returned to their camp.

en: Why are these scouts such a threat?

en: What if we're away in battle and the scouts return to kill those we've left behind?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need to deal with this now.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Which do we focus on, the scouts or the caches?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of the scouts. The last thing we need is an ambush.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: if you've chosen wrong, we'll be exposed with nothing to show for it! But if you must go, go now. Are you ready?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see you when it's done.

en: What is it that Spartans say about shields? With them or on them?

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: May the gods guide your path and the arc of your sword.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a scout!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all of them. Better get back to Lalaia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hunted them to the last.

speaker: Thyia
en: I'll sleep easier knowing that.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: I still worry about them overcoming our numbers in battle. But, thank you. This will change our fate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We'll focus on the caches... but we'll need to find the Sons of Xerxes' stronghold first.

en: I hope you know what you're doing. I'll be sleeping with one eye open. Are you ready to do this?

en: I'll see you when it's done.

en: What is it that Spartans say about shields? With them or on them?

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: May the gods guide your path and the arc of your sword.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all of them. Better get back to Lalaia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I destroyed the caches.

speaker: Magistrate Periktione
en: Thank the gods. We will win this war.

speaker: Thyia
en: The war maybe, but at what cost? We could still have our throats slit in the night. That sounds ungrateful of me. Thank you for all you've done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm. I need a boat. I should go see the shipbuilder.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's a fine ship, Telemenes.

speaker: Telemenes
en: Kassandra! She is that, ready to ride the waves for the right captain... and the right price.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What'll it take for you to part with her?

speaker: Telemenes
en: Oh, couldn't let her go for less than 100,000.

speaker: Kassandra
en: 100,000! Who has that much?

speaker: Telemenes
en: Someone who's serious about buying a ship. You think craftsmanship like this is given away?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I told you I had obsidian to trade?

speaker: Telemenes
en: I'd tell you I still need 100,000 drachmae! Besides, even if I took your obsidian, a ship this size needs an army to sail it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I really need a boat, Telemenes.

speaker: Telemenes
en: Everyone on Kephallonia needs a boat, or passage on one. You've seen this shit hole.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All my life.

speaker: Telemenes
en: Even if I had a boat, who's going to row it? You? I'd give my left grape to see that!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is Kephallonia. I could always find someone down on their luck and willing to work for next to nothing to get off this island.

speaker: Telemenes
en: The seas are treacherous now. Well, more than usual. It would be suicide.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not being very helpful, Telemenes.

speaker: Telemenes
en: Not sure if this helps, but rumor has it the Cyclops is coming for you and Markos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Rumors mean nothing. Don't believe everything you hear.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Malaka! How is that helpful?

speaker: Telemenes
en: That monster's held Kephallonia for too long. I figured if anyone could finally rid us of his stench, it would be you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Telemenes, what does this have to do with my need for a boat?

speaker: Telemenes
en: Rumor also has it his ship has docked in Kleptous Bay.

speaker: Kassandra
en: His ship, you say? I'll have to pay Kleptous Bay a visit.

speaker: Telemenes
en: Be careful. That one-eyed brute has a nasty temper.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I can take his ship and deal with the Cyclops at the same time. Two birds, one stone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This used to be a nice village, but now it's just a nest of anarchy and crime.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cyclops. Time to have a little chat.

en: The gods as my witness! I swear!

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: Which ones?

speaker: Barnabas
en: What difference does it make?

speaker: Barnabas
en: All of them! I swear! All of them!

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: I've never heard so much fucking god talk from one man in all my days.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let him go.

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: No one on this island is allowed to say that word!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did he say Cyclops? Did he hurt your feelings?

en: I don't like it when people call me that!

speaker: Barnabas
en: I didn't!!! I

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you're so fat—I mean big and strong—and you really do only have one eye.

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: My eye! Give it to me! Give it to me and I won't kill Markos for having you steal it. Give it to me!!!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go get it.

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: Nobody will recognize your body when I'm done!

speaker: Guards
en: To the death! I can't do this alone! You'll die here! Why me? Give up already!

speaker: Kassandra
en: We shouldn't delay here any further. Even rats like these have friends in Kephallonia.

speaker: Barnabas
en: By Zeus, the Kephallonian bandits are no joke! Good thing you're on my side! They really seem to fear you.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I can't thank you enough. After spending most of my life at sea, it would have been absolutely shameful to drown in a pot! Ah, where are my manners? I am Barnabas, captain of the Adrestia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, Barnabas. I am pleased to meet you. I'm Kassandra, misthios by trade.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Oh but you're much more than that, I'm sure!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Barnabas
en: When they forced my head under water, I prayed to the gods. And when they pulled it out, there you were!

speaker: Kassandra
en: All of Kephallonia heard your prayers. I just happened to be closest.

speaker: Barnabas
en: And you just happen to fight like Achilles while Zeus's eagle flies around your head!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You called, and I answered.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Many claim to have blood of the gods in their veins. You're the first I actually believe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where do you come from?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Everywhere, nowhere. The Adrestia is my home, but I was born in an olive grove in Mykonos. I haven't stepped foot there since I left for the military.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're a soldier?

speaker: Barnabas
en: I was. My brothers and I were captains in the Athenian fleet... until one night during a siege, Poseidon's fury destroyed our ships. That was the night I saw it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It? What did you see?

speaker: Barnabas
en: The sea god commands more than just the winds and waves when he truly unleashes his temper. I saw his beast, his murderous pet. Few believe me, but this dead eye is a permanent reminder. Punishment for looking on Poseidon's forbidden creature and living to tell the tale.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So why were those men attacking you?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Oh, you know the people here... No offense. I tell them a tale of my last voyage, and the next thing I know they're acting like a bunch of savages!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What tale could you tell that would make them so angry?

speaker: Barnabas
en: My last voyage. We found a man floating alone on a raft... Before he passed, he told us a tale to make your blood run cold. Something about a horrifying creature, ugly and beyond description. I mentioned the words "one-eyed monster." Next thing I know, I'm drowning in a clay pot!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, the Cyclops tends to take that personally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So... you have a ship.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Of course! Gods forbid I'd end up stuck in this place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is it now?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Thanks to you, it's still in Sami Harbor where I left it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Seeing as I saved your ship and your life, I'd say you owe me.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Mind of a misthios! You know who you remind me of? Me. Haha (unsubbed). A much younger me of course, before I found my true purpose... and lost my eye.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're changing the subject.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah yes, my apologies. You're right, I owe you my life. What could a humble Barnabas do for the mighty Kassandra?

speaker: Kassasndra
en: I need a ship and a crew.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Hahahaha (unsubbed) of course you do!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Perhaps the fates brought us together after all. I'm in need of a ship and a crew.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You saved my life! It would disgust the gods to not offer it in return.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, that's a yes?

speaker: Barnabas
en: My ship, my crew, and my services are yours!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You truly aren't from around here.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Gods, no! And I thank them for that. Come now and see the Adrestia.

speaker: Barnabas
en: We're ready when you are, captain.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Wait! Wait for me, Kassandra! I'm all packed and everything!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're coming, are you?

speaker: Phoibe
en: If you're going, I'm going.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe, you're not old enough. I can't look after you all the time.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I can look after myself. I don't need anyone to help me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Even if that were true, it's not your time.

speaker: Phoibe
en: But I wouldn't be any trouble. Promise!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kephallonia's the only place you've ever known. You'd leave your home?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I would if it meant staying with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't go where I'm going. I need to be alone.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Who's going to keep you company?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be fine.

speaker: Phoibe
en: If I can't come, then take Chara.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chara?

speaker: Phoibe
en: My pet eagle. She's my friend. Mater gave her to me. But she'll be your friend now, and it'll be like I'm there with you. You know, to remind you of me

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks, Phoibe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Besides, I'll have Kynna to play with—since you saved her!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go easy on her. She may still be shaky with the fever.

speaker: Phoibe
en: But you have to promise we'll see each other again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I promise. You haven't seen the last of me. Just stay out of trouble until then.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I will, don't worry! OK, you can leave now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's up to the Fates, but I'd like to.

speaker: Phoibe
en: The Fates know we're best friends, Kassandra. They'll make sure we meet again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I say so!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe, I'm never coming back.

speaker: Phoibe
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone's counting on me. To do something very dangerous. And there's a new future in it for me if I succeed.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I won't see you ever again?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know. Until we do, you just have to keep yourself safe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I will.

speaker: Markos
en: Kassandra! Leaving Kephallonia without saying goodbye to your dear Markos? Tell me it isn't true!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, you're here now, so it won't be true. Goodbye, Markos.

speaker: Markos
en: All these years as a dynamic duo. I'll never replace you! Well, I may need another assistant someday. But it won't be easy! Come now, give me a hug!

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, come here.

speaker: Markos
en: Yes, bring it in! Oh, will I ever miss you, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks, Markos. I'll miss you too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Partners shake hands.

speaker: Markos
en: The true signs of a woman in business!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what does the future hold for you?

speaker: Markos
en: Wine, of course! Though, you never know when the vines will wither. I'm always ready for another adventure! Speaking of adventure, I have a task for you, dear Phoibe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: An adventure? Yes!

speaker: Markos
en: Already following in your footsteps, isn't she, my friend?

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ready to set sail?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Prepare to cast off. It's time to leave.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Good. The tides wait for neither man nor woman.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to go.

speaker: Barnabas
en: So, what course do we set? Where in this big, beautiful world does the mighty Kassandra want to go?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Megaris.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Megaris! But we'll be sailing into war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I got a contract for some general's head.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Whose head?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They call him "The Wolf."

speaker: Barnabas
en: The Wolf! Who wants Nikolaos of Sparta dead?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nikolaos of Sparta?

speaker: Civilian
en: Silence!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Sto—You can't! Nooo! No, no.

speaker: Civilian
en: Murderer! She has killed him!

speaker: Civilian
en: Toss her over!

speaker: Civilian
en: Pay for her dishonor! For the life she has snuffed! She's not Spartan, Nikolaos!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Look at me Nikolaos! Don't! Don't listen! Nikolaos! Don't listen! No! Don't listen! Nikolaos! Why?

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: ... Pater!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Nikolaos! Stop! Nikolaos! No! Nikolaos! Nikolaos! Look at me! Look at me, Nikolaos! Don't! Don't listen!

speaker: Civilian

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: Pater?

speaker: Myrrine
en: No, oh my baby...

speaker: Young Kassandra
en: Pater!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get me to Megaris. Now.

en: But I don't understand. Of all the places under Helios, why risk our necks to go there?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Wolf of Sparta is my father.

speaker: Kallipedes

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get them. Then you'll be ready to work?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've got your tools right here.

speaker: Kallipedes

en: Woah!

speaker: Kassandra

speaker: Kassandra

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should get out of Alponos while you can, girl. This place is cursed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Poor Kallipedes. That's... That's not good.

en: The gods have abandoned us. The sick must join the dead if we are to save the living!

en: Many nights were lost praying. We had to take action—to scorch the blood fever out of Kausos.

en: Is there no hope for a cure?

en: You should thank the gods that I've come to help you.

en: The only reason you're still alive is that writ you carry. You're not an ally, just a weapon.

en: What's so great about these champions? They're just four people against the Spartan military.

en: I know he threw you off a cliff and chose me instead.

en: And who would that be?

en: When you put it like that, how could I not accept?

en: There is a boar not too far from here. Kill it, then bring me its pelt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to kill a pig?

speaker: Daphnae
en: This is no ordinary boar. Let's see if you're worthy of my challenge. Kill it, and bring me the pelt. I'm be waiting... with your reward.

en: That's a big pig.

en: I should get this pelt back to Daphnae at the temple.

en: Did you get lost?

en: Here, I killed your piggy for you.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Hmm. You are skilled, of that there is no doubt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You shouldn't doubt my abilities.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Lesson learned. But I'm also interested in seeing what else you can do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have plenty of talents, of that you can be sure.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Oh, is that so? Well, I look forward to putting them all to the test.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh? And what do you have in mind?

en: Many things... But first, to business. There are beasts that roam this world, but are not fully of it. They've placed here by the gods as trials—as tests.

en: These beasts are creatures, like any other. The world is full of mysteries, but not everything is unexplained by the gods.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Perhaps before this is over, you will have a different opinion.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Neither god nor mortal has stopped me so far from achieving my destiny.

speaker: Daphnae
en: We will see.

en: What exactly do you want me to do?

en: I want you to prove your worth in the eyes of Artemis, and hunt these creatures.

en: All right, I'll do it. Now, just how many of these animals are there?

en: Artemis has laid out eight trials, and you already started the journey. Hunt down those that remain.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How will I recognize the creatures?

speaker: Daphnae
en: Oh, you'll know. Bring the pelts to me. I'll await your return with my sisters, the Daughters of Artemis. I hope you don't make me wait to long to see your face again...

speaker: Kassandra

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: Out with it.

speaker: Dymas
en: I'll take double — a life's worth a lot. And for the sake of the gods, don't tell Hippokrates.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates would never put drachmae before a patient's life. But here, since you're so determined to be a mercenary.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll meet you there. Don't be late.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hippokrates! How is your patient?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Poor.

speaker: Hippokrates
