speaker: Kassandra
en: Your notes were destroyed, so he demanded pay to come help.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Dymas
en: You said you wouldn't tell him!

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: No, I didn't.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Hippokrates
en: No matter. Dymas can help, and we have a man who needs saving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There was a fire. Your notes were destroyed. What matters is that Dymas is here to help.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now

en: Good. Dymas, with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I told old Dymas here you were in need, I could barely hold him back.

speaker: Kassandra

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: This healer will devote the rest of his life to serving others and you, Hippokrates. This should never happen again.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Dymas
en: We can't all be Hippokrates. If you don't have the drachmae, then stand back and let me heal my patient.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll wait here for you to finish. If I leave, what's stopping you from running away?

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Dymas
en: Thinking like a mercenary. Guess I shouldn't be surprised.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Dymas

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you'll come treat Hippokrates's patient?

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Dymas
en: You have my word.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go get your bone forceps.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: The forceps should be in there. Once I deliver these, we can get back to Hippokrates.

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra

scene: The Doctor Will See You Now
speaker: Kassandra
en: Is this it?

en: If you don't stop, I'll kill you both to preserve the truce.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nobody wants trouble here—you know what will happen to you both if you break the truce.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now if someone can tell me what's going on...

speaker: Makar
en: This dishonorable cur stole from me.

speaker: Lelex
en: You call me a thief? You're the thief!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enough. I'll ask the questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herodotos, what's all this about?

speaker: Lelex
en: This scum robbed me!

speaker: Makar
en: Scum! I'm from an honorable family. Only a lowly Ionian would steal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I said Herodotos!

speaker: Herodotos
en: Er, yes. It seems both their treasuries were breached, and their valuables stolen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If there's been a theft, why do you suspect each other?

speaker: Lelex
en: Because this...

speaker: Herodotos
en: It's a matter of blood. Makar is from an eminent Dorian line. Mighty warriors, but rather austere...

speaker: Herodotos
en: While Lelex is from Ionian stock, a grand tradition of artists and philosophers

speaker: Makar
en: You mean philanderers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Both sides are important.

speaker: Makar
en: Spoken like a true Ionian.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems unlikely they would rob each other at the same time.

speaker: Herodotos
en: You have to find out who stole their drachmae. I can't believe they would do this to each other. Whatever their issues, they've always respected the Olympic truce.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find out what happened and protect the truce.

speaker: Lelex
en: If you prove it's Makar, I will reward you well.

speaker: Makar
en: As will I, if you bring me evidence of Lelex's double dealing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what if it's neither of you?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Then they will both reward you.

speaker: Lelex
en: Very well.

speaker: Makar
en: Agreed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't need to get involved in other people's family feuds.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Please, if the mystery of who robbed Lelex and Makar isn't solved, I fear there will be bloodshed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did you see anything?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: No, nope, not nothing. Far less than anything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you saw something.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Well, only if you count torches. But they crept up on me, they did. Must've been at least thirty of them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Torches crept up on you? If there were thirty of them, why isn't the ground stomped flat?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Er... doeskin sandals, very soft. Don't leave a trace. Anyway, hard to tell how many, as I was unconscious.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me the truth, or I'll beat it out of you. Are you the thief?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: No, please. Look, it wasn't me. I fell asleep—didn't see anything apart from the torches.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all right if you ran. Fear can change a man.

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I wasn't afraid, I was asleep... Oh, I mean...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I won't tell, but did you see anything?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: No... Except...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: Some torches, heading east.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you didn't investigate?

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: I didn't want to leave my post.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you'd already been robbed!

speaker: Greek Soldier
en: If I deserted my post, I'd be charged with dereliction of duty.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then I'll let you get back to work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These crypts have been opened. There's no sign of forced entry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, a note. "Take all that you can carry, and meet me at the ruins where we first consummated our love. Soon we will be free."

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard talk of ruins outside the city, and from what the guard said, the torches were heading in that direction.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found the thief.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, thieves, I finally catch you.

speaker: Laneira
en: Please, we're not thieves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yet here you are with stolen goods.

speaker: Menon
en: You don't understand, this is rightfully ours. It's our inheritance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How can this all be yours?

speaker: Menon
en: It belongs to our families—by blood it's rightfully ours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it's already yours, why not wait? Why steal everything now?

speaker: Laneira
en: We wanted a new life. One where we could be free, and our love doesn't have to hide in the shadows.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are you, exactly?

speaker: Makar
en: They are my daughter and his son!

speaker: Laneira
en: Pater!

speaker: Lelex
en: This is how you repay me for raising you? By running off with some woman squirted from my enemy's loins?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why not put aside your feud, as your children have done?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This robbery has brought you together. Lelex, Makar, you worked together to find out what happened to your drachmae.

speaker: Makar
en: Actually, the guard told us.

speaker: Lelex
en: And his family stole my money.

speaker: Makar
en: As yours did mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But think how much you could achieve working together.

speaker: Makar
en: You're a misthios. Carry out your duty and kill the thieves. I will pay you handsomely.

speaker: Laneira
en: Pater, no!

speaker: Lelex
en: I agree. I will match Makar's price on this. Do what you were hired to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You would kill your own son and daughter?

speaker: Makar
en: We have other children. Now, are you a misthios or not?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will not slaughter innocents. Your families would stand a better chance for the future without the both of you.

speaker: Laneira
en: I didn't want it to come to this, but now we can forge a new future for our two families—one built on love.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wish you luck with that...

speaker: Kassandra
en: A contract's a contract.

speaker: Makar
en: Good, the matter is settled.

speaker: Lelex
en: I wish could have been another way.

speaker: Makar
en: There wasn't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This blood is on your hands, not mine. May the gods forgive me.

speaker: Makar
en: The gods don't care what we do. Here, take your drachmae. It was well earned.

speaker: Demokritos
en: You! Come here. I need your help with something.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Come to see the richest man in Achaia, have you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't look rich.

speaker: Demokritos
en: The richest person in any land is the one who wants for the least. And I want for nothing at all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Rich, wanting for nothing, and calling me over to help. Doesn't make sense.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's one thing that makes a person rich - drachmae. The only people who say otherwise don't have any.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Ah! A mind that thinks for itself. Someone save me from this horror.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Relax, relax. The name's Demokritos. Renowned thinker of thoughts, writer of writes, questioner of answers.

speaker: Kasssandra
en: I'm... Kassandra. And I've never heard of you.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Probably says more about you than me, Kassandra. Now, you came here to help, hmm? So happens, I've uncovered the whereabouts of three divine mathematical discoveries.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mathematical discoveries. Really?

speaker: Demokritos
en: Yes, really. The theorems, when combined with my own, will unlock the greatest mystery in the universe—which, as you know, is a place where mysteries strive to remain locked. Bring these three theorems to me, and I will reward you handsomely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, you get the theorems, and I get a reward... From a man who seems completely disinterested in drachmae.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Drachmae is for idiots. What I offer is far greater than that. But first, the theorems.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. What are they?

speaker: Demokritos
en: Only the greatest achievements of rational thought—the original transcriptions of the , the , and Zeno's .

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about Zeno's Paradox.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Myself excluded, Zeno of Elea was the world's brightest philosopher, known for writing paradoxes that could stump anyone. His work was thought destroyed, but I happen to know the priests in Lokris saved it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: About the Golden Ratio...

speaker: Demokritos
en: Ah! The divine number. It's a guiding principle in architecture, sculpture, and is found in nature, too. The original is wasting away in the dirty hands of sculptors in Argos. It should be with a mathematician... like me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where am I going to find the Pythagorean Theorem?

speaker: Demokritos
en: It's all around you, of course! Deceptively simple, but subtly mysterious, the equation was apparently etched in stone. I heard a tale... It was lost in sunken ruins between three islands that form a triangle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find these theorems for you.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Come back as soon as you have one.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of the documents Demokritos wants... This isn't even math. It's a child's fable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Golden Ratio. Demokritos will want to know I've found it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, Demokritos.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Kassandra. What have you brought me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: So I found Zeno's Paradox.

speaker: Demokritos
en: You did! And, what did you think of it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's just some silly riddle.

speaker: Demokritos
en: What? No! The tortoise arrives at a point. Achilles, who is chasing it, runs after him. But after Achilles arrives at the same point, the tortoise has moved on. By the time Achilles arrives at the tortoise's new spot, the creature has again moved further. It shows how the universe divides itself infinitely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The tortoise arrives at a point. Achilles, who is chasing it, runs after him. But after Achilles arrives at the same point, the tortoise has moved on. By the time Achilles arrives at the tortoise's new spot, the creature has again moved further.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Exactly! It shows how the universe divides itself infinitely.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A mathematical theory hidden in a child's fable.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Zeno was clever—every knowledgeable old man I've ever met was an idiot. But the minds of children are endlessly wise.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found the original Golden Ratio.

speaker: Demokritos
en: A discovery that will change the course of existence!

speaker: Kassandra
en: At first, I didn't think I saw anything special about it. But the sides of this diagram aren't even. The side marked "a" is almost half of the side marked "b".

speaker: Demokritos
en: Almost, but not quite - a and b are to a, as a is to b.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so. It's just a rectangle to me.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Open your eyes. That "rectangle" is two shapes—a rectangle, yes, but also a square. The length of sides a and be is to the length of the side a, as a is to b.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, how can this theory be used?

speaker: Demokritos
en: Used! It isn't used, only observed. It is the divine balance, occuring naturally in the most measurably beautiful places in the world. It is everywhere and nowhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It took some doing, but I found the Pythagorean Theorem.

speaker: Demokritos
en: The greatest breakthrough the world will ever know. And now we have it, in its original glory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why? Did Pythagoras invent the triangle?

speaker: Demokritos
en: Great minds don't invent - they discover. Pythagoras discovered that the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought it might be about the points of the triangle, but the theorem is about the length of the sides.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Astute! You're wiser than you put on. The two shorter sides squared, when added together, are equal to the square of the hypotenuse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was... a lot to take in. But I think I've found everything.

speaker: Demokritos
en: You did. And with this, I can finally form my grand theory—the theory that simultaneously divides and unites all the universe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: From a riddle, a triangle, and a rectangle? I can't wait.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds fun. But I'm not here for your theories. I did this to get paid.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Shame. It's been a while since I had a student, and there was a moment I thought I found one in you. I was wrong. But you did as you were asked. For that, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm a misthios, not a student. Nice working with you, Demokritos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is this theory?

speaker: Demokritos
en: Using the theorems as evidence, I intend to prove that the universe is divisible into infinitely smaller parts. As we break reality down, the parts shrink, and the space between them grows.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Once you prove your theory, what will you do with it?

speaker: Demokritos
en: Although I aim to prove that the universe is divisible, I hope that the theory can be used... to unite people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All of this sounds... ambitious.

speaker: Demokritos
en: One can't achieve greatness by attempting mediocrity. But I confess, I have a personal motivation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone always does.

speaker: Demokritos
en: Ha! In another life, you would've made a fine student. When I was a student, I loved a poet. But I was so consumed by study I never told her. I hope to use these theorems to show her my poetry. And, maybe, to win her heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If that's what you want to do, let's do it.

speaker: Demokritos
en: What? Right now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You missed your chance to tell her once, Demokritos. There's no point in missing it again. Let's go.

speaker: Demokritos
en: You're right. This time, I will do it properly.

speaker: Civilian
en: Back, you brutes! Back!

speaker: Civilian
en: The beasts... The teeth... Too many teeth...

speaker: Civilian
en: You saved me, and my work, too—a cure for the statues in the Petrified Valley.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can reverse the effects?

speaker: Civilian
en: My elixir can. I mean... not yet. I'm trying to reverse the effects of petrifaction by concocting an elixir of various ingredients.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give it to me! A friend of mine was recently turned to stone.

speaker: Civilian
en: I can't. I don't have all the ingredients. But... if you could get them for me, I could give you a vial of it as a reward.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would stone need to be cured?

speaker: Civilian
en: Surely you've seen their faces frozen in terror. They're not mere objects, but humans trapped in stone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're saying they're sick?

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm not sure why it's happening. I'm merely a scholar looking for a cure—an elixir that will not only heal, but prevent this horrible affliction once and for all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Something's turning people to stone, and you can make them flesh and blood again? Impressive.

speaker: Civilian
en: Yes! Well... Not exactly. Not yet. It will be perfected through more trials.

speaker: Civilian
en: But I only have one dose of elixir left. In order to make more I'd require a few ingredients, but I'm in no condition to gather them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The only thing less likely that those statues being people is you turning stone to flesh with an elixir.

speaker: Civilian
en: I didn't say I could revert the stone back to flesh! That is... not yet. This is an ongoing process, and more experiments are needed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How many more experiments?

speaker: Civilian
en: One never knows... But without the right ingredients, all my hard work will have been for naught.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you need?

speaker: Civilian
en: Just a few items found all over Vineyard Canyon. If you can get them for me, I'll reward you with a dose of my elixir.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll gather what you need.

speaker: Civilian
en: Excellent. Now, listen closely to these ingredients: I require a cluster of bear dung mushrooms, some cone snail bile, and a bouquet of hellebore.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Medusa was alive and causing the petrifaction. I was able to enter her lair and slay her, so there'll be no more people turned to stone.

speaker: Civilian
en: Medusa... she was real? It matters not. What matters is saving the poor souls presently trapped. My elixir can save them, I know it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did these statues come to be?

speaker: Civilian
en: I don't rightly know. A curse of the gods? The Writhing Dread? If you wish to see for yourself, you shouldn't do it without my elixir.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What is a hellebore?

speaker: Civilian
en: Hellebore is a flowering plant you can find growing atop the highest mountain in Vineyard Canyon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find these mushrooms?

speaker: Civilian
en: They grow on fresh bear dung. There's a cave in the mountains south of the road to Mytilene, where you can usually find them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where can I find cone snails?

speaker: Civilian
en: Cone snails are drawn to the warm currents of the eastern shoreline. My favorite spot is by Shark Bay. Make sure the bile is fresh.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go collect your ingredients.

speaker: Civilian
en: Come to my workshop on the hill east of Mytilene when you have everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A cave, a mountain, and the shoreline. Could these items be in three more different places?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The mountain. The hellebore should be here somewhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the right area. The cave with the mushrooms should be close.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The shipwreck! The cone snails must be close by.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm... The crazy woman has been writing about the Petrified Forest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These aren't petrified statues. There are dead bodies inside.

speaker: Civilian
en: You're back. Do you have the ingredients?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do.

speaker: Civilian
en: Very good. Now I'll be able to make a new store of elixir. But first, I need to make sure it's safe for human consumption. The vial on the table is my last dose... I saved it especially for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not drinking anything with bear dung mushroom in it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Don't be silly. Drink it and you'll be impervious to petrifaction.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I... I'm not sure about this.

speaker: Civilian
en: What? You believe that my elixir works, don't you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If it does what you say it does... I'd be a fool to not drink it.

speaker: Civilian
en: Yes! Drink it all down.

speaker: Civilian
en: I noticed something while testing the elixir on my live subjects... We all turn to stone when we're dead!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think you're crazy.

speaker: Civilian
en: No, no, no! You need to drink it! I need models for my statues!

speaker: Civilian
en: They're not statues! They're my children!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: By Zeus! What's with the size of the boars in this country?

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast Slayer, I'm glad to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This boar was far harder to kill than the Kalydonian one, but I've yet to meet a pig that can't be skewered.

speaker: Daphnae
en: The gods chose well when they sent you to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods may watch me, but they do not guide me.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Then I feel for you. Artemis has always steered me right, and that includes in meeting you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chance can easily be blamed on the gods.

speaker: Daphnae
en: But can destiny?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I follow where the gods lead, and they led me to you.

speaker: Daphnae
en: They have a sense of humor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How so?

speaker: Daphnae
en: We will talk of the gods and their wishes once the hunt is done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: The Eyes of Kosmos
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Need something?

speaker: Woman
en: By the gods, it's really you! The legendary mercenary who travels with the great historian Herodotos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Er, yes. I met him during my travels in Phokis.

speaker: Woman
en: I know! I saw you talking while I was in line to meet the Pythia. Truthfully, I was only in line to see Herodotos. Anyways, I want to be a writer just like him. Is he as magnificent as they say?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have to admit that Herodotos is an interesting fellow. He seems to know everything about everyone.

speaker: Woman
en: Just as I suspected! Since you are a fan just like me, perhaps there's something you could help me with?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Magnificent? That might be going too far. He certainly is... something, if not a bit pushy.

speaker: Woman
en: I would never have guessed! No... you must be joking. The fact that you know him is astounding enough. There's something I need to ask of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go on.

speaker: Woman
en: Perhaps Herodotos would finally notice me if I started writing about his favorite muse. You! Maybe a story about you skinning a lion with your bare hands. Or wrestling a couple sharks?

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're asking me to slay this creature?

speaker: Woman
en: I understand this isn't an easy task, but the lion must be killed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. I'll do it.

speaker: Woman
en: They'll tell tales of this, mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

speaker: Woman
en: Misthios! Has the beast been slain?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The beast is dead.

speaker: Woman
en: The gods favored me the day we met. Take this for your trouble, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I've started.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to spill the beasts' blood.

speaker: Woman
en: Yes, all of them must be gutted. Do you accept?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll handle this.

speaker: Woman
en: By Apollo, thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can leave everything to me.

speaker: Woman
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Woman
en: By Apollo, thank you. This is for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you.

speaker: Poseidon
en: My Dikastes has returned. I can only presume you've delivered judgement to Atlantis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said you outlawed experimentation on humans. All of it was lies. The Isu are out of control.

speaker: Poseidon
en: What are you talking about? My laws are absolute, and by them all must abide. I have declared it!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I saw it with my own eyes. If you didn't know about the experiments, you're either a fool, or a fucking liar. So, which is it?

speaker: Poseidon
en: You were supposed to find knowledge in this place. Your accusations prove you haven't. I speak the truth!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your laws have done nothing! People are suffering under your rule, and you don't even realize it!

speaker: Poseidon
en: No one would have the audacity to disobey me. Surely, this is a mistake.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The people of Atlantis have clearly decided that your laws are holding them back. Maybe it's time for a new ruler.

speaker: Poseidon
en: You don't understand our ways. Your humanity is clouding your judgement, Dikastes.

speaker: Juno
en: You should listen to her, you know.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Juno?! Impossible! You're forbidden from entering the city. Guards!

speaker: Juno
en: Your guards respect your sons. And when you appointed that hybrid as your Dikastes, your sons turned to us.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Even my sons know better than to bow to a warmonger.

speaker: Aita
en: The humans are bringing war whether we want it or not, Poseidon!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They should, after what you've done.

speaker: Juno
en: You mean what they've forced us to do. Poseidon worries about the sun, and his Solar Floral regeneration project. Catastrophe is coming for us. On that we agree. But there is only one catastrophe—humanity.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't trust Aita. He's a lunatic. You have no idea the monsters he's trapped in his hidden lair.

speaker: Aita
en: It was hidden only to Poseidon. My wife knew everything about it.

speaker: Juno
en: Hybrid, Project Olympos was my idea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The end of a cycle in Atlantis doesn't have to be a catastrophe.

speaker: Poseidon
en: It's far worse. We've detected changes in the surfaces of the sun. If we don't prepare...

speaker: Juno
en: If we don't prepare, humans will kill us all. The only ecological catastrophe we face is the one we created ourselves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I got here, Poseidon said I was where I belonged. Someone tell me why I'm really here. Now.

speaker: Juno
en: Such sadness. She's even more human than I expected. Aita, answer her.

speaker: Aita
en: Gladly. In you, we found opportunity. Imagine the possibilities if we duplicated your hybrid form. We could employ our technology to control your mind. You, hybrid, can be used to craft Juno's ultimate weapon.

speaker: Juno
en: Or rather, you could have been. My husband's experiment was promising, but after observation, we've decided you are a failure. Our new weapon is far deadlier than you could ever be.

speaker: Poseidon
en: The Hekatonchires. Aita, you didn't...

speaker: Aita
en: I did.

speaker: Juno
en: The Hekatonchires will rise. Project Olympos will strike fear so deeply into the hearts of humanity, they would never consider revolt. And you will declare my husband the Dikastes Basileus.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Dikastes, stop this. If they're successful, we're doomed. All of us. You have to trust me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You deal with these two. I'll find a way to stop their plans.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deal with this yourself! I'm no one's weapon.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Kassandra, Please!

speaker: Kassandra
en: My name is Kassandra. And I trust none of you.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Kassandra, Please!

speaker: Aita
en: It's too late. The procedure was already a success. The Hekatonchires lives. Can't you hear him stir?

speaker: Poseidon
en: You did this in my laboratory under the palace? Entrance was barred when I outlawed human experimentation!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What... is that sound? Is that your weapon?

speaker: Poseidon
en: I will bring justice to these two, but I need you to stop the Hekatonchires before it kills us all! Go!

speaker: Hekatonchires
en: Who's there?

speaker: Hekatonchires
en: Pain... Bones... Death... Let it come...

speaker: Kassandra
en: By the gods. Are those people?

speaker: Kassandra
en: These minions are from Aita's experiments... I can't get too close.

speaker: Hekatonchires
en: Children... Feast... Flesh... Agony...

speaker: Hekatonchires
en: All... Human... Isu... Joined in death...

speaker: Kassandra
en: The only one dying is you.

speaker: Hekatonchires
en: Life... Suffering... Kill... Me... Die with me...

speaker: First Civ
en: ...Honor the fallen by wielding their fear...

speaker: Poseidon
en: Remarkable. You really are the greatest of the humans, and of my people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's Juno and Aita?

speaker: Poseidon
en: Imprisoned... for now. But they will not stop.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If imprisonment won't stop them, then leave them alone in a room with me. I'll make sure they never hurt anyone again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Isu... they're all crazed. They all must pay.

speaker: Poseidon
en: And what would that prove? That you're as cruel as Juno and her husband?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't intend to "prove" anything. I intend to stop this, and save those that suffered because of your hubris.

speaker: Poseidon
en: So, in the end, you've brought judgement to Atlantis after all. Very well, Dikastes. Do you still have the Cerberos' device?

speaker: Poseidon
en: I didn't tell you everything about your Staff. It is a bridge between your two selves, but by coupling it with the powers of the devices you retrieved from the Cerberos and the Hekatonchires, we can end Atlantis' cycle forever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wasn't just awakening my sixth sense. I was unlocking the power to destroy the entire city.

speaker: Poseidon
en: In the wrong hands, that Staff has the power to destroy everything. That is why you, and only you, could be its Keeper.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You act like you knew this would happen.

speaker: Poseidon
en: I'm tired, just as you are. I waited many cycles for Atlantis' final judgement to come. I only wish it had come sooner. Think of the suffering it would have prevented.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If we do this, you and your sons...

speaker: Poseidon
en: My family have had generations to show kindness, modesty, temperance. We refused, and in so doing, this choice was made by us as much as you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The humans in this city don't deserve to die.

speaker: Poseidon
en: When we do this, the horns will wail, and the animals will be set free. Humans in the Porimos Ring will know to take to their boats. I assure you—they will escape.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If we sink the city, but I'm in it, then I die, too.

speaker: Poseidon
en: No. You are the Keeper of the Staff. It will protect you. Unfortunately for you, now is not your time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said it yourself. Juno and Aita will never stop. I've seen those laboratories, the experiments in them. There's only one way to end the suffering here—destroy this place.

speaker: Poseidon
en: My one wish is that I had more time to learn from you. In time, I may have learned to be more human.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, Poseidon.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper of the Staff. Your trials are over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're back in the Throne Room.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Tell me, now that you have seen the fate of Atlantis, how do you feel?

speaker: Kassandra
en: With the Staff, I hold the power to destroy an entire city.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Which is why you were given the ability to control that power. Only in your hands will the destructive potential of the Staff remain hidden.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's been a long time since I've seen my crew, my friends, Barnabas. I feel... homesick.

speaker: Aletheia
en: The Keeper has no home. The trials are complete, but your journey is long, and will take you to civilizations that have yet to be born.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want to know how I'm feeling? I'm tired, Aletheia.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Your burden is great, Keeper. The Staff will replenish your physical body, but with time, you must learn that your strength comes from within.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So what was all this?

speaker: Aletheia
en: What you have experienced are echoes of memories, distorted, but no less real.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whose memories?

speaker: Aletheia
en: The Isu. Some were even my own. In my time as Dikastes, I also tried to bring balance to Atlantis, but it wasn't enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You?

speaker: Aletheia
en: And now you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My trials forced me to reunite with my grandfather, Phoibe, Brasidas, even Elpenor.

speaker: Aletheia
en: And in so doing, you passed a valuable trial. The Staff has the power to prolong life. That is not your role. You must learn to say goodbye again, and again, but let death take what it will from this world.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Were they... real?

speaker: Aletheia
en: They are with you always. So, yes. In time, you must let them go, but that will be another trial.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My trials in Elysium brought destruction, and rebellion.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Not due to you, but Persephone. She was a ruler who controlled her domain through extreme order. In so doing, you saw that her rule was doomed to failure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In the underworld, I was forced to endure a realm of pure chaos.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Indeed. Hades was a king who invited that chaos, and devastation came with it. But know this—you will be forced to endure far worse suffering before your death has come.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elysium and the underworld were doomed, but in Atlantis, I almost thought Poseidon and I could do some good.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Yet there you discovered the Isu as we really were—flawed. No matter how many times I have seen that echo of memory, my home always meet destruction.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready to leave. You coming? We are entwined, after all.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You saw Persephone rule through order, Hades through chaos, and even had a taste of being a ruler yourself in Atlantis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was a disaster.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You have seen there is no path to power for the Keeper. In the Staff, you have the ability to bring this world to its knees. But that is not your role. You must use your strength to restrain the power of the Staff, to guard it... to keep.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mater once told me I was sent by the gods to protect this world. I gave her my word. And now, I give my word to you.

speaker: Aletheia
en: And what of your word, Heir of Memories? You must wake up, and redeem yourself before it's too late, or it will be you who tears this world apart. Now, awake. The Interloper has found you. Wake! Now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Helot prisoners. Amorges wouldn't like it if I freed them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The prisoners mentioned in the letter. I should free them.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Help! Someone, help!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aiantides? Is that you?

speaker: Aiantides
en: Yes! Yes, thank the gods! Wait! Kassandra? No! Why'd it have to be you again? Go away! Help! Someone else! Help! No! No, no, no. I owe you enough Kassandra. Why'd you have to do this again?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keep your voice down, the guards will you.

speaker: Guard
en: Hey! You! Get away from the prisoners.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aiantides, my proud friend... What's happened to you this time?

speaker: Aiantides
en: The gods are not fair to Aiantides. I spent my wealth on my gifts to you. I don't complain, that was fair. Then someone told me I could make a fortune in Messenia. But those malákes sold me for a fortune instead! I'm a slave here. And now you show up? How is that fair?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't my fault. It's your pride that did this.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Yes, I, Aiantides, am proud! And I will never be indebted to anyone. But now you save me again? Why do you keep doing this to me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could hardly leave you to rot in that cage, Aiantides.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You said before you still owed me a favor. You can't repay me if you're stuck in a cage.

speaker: Aiantides
en: You just can't leave me out of your heroic deeds, can you? Now what can I do? I have nothing. Kassandra, nothing, to pay my debt to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aiantides, the Greeks are indebted to the gods, aren't they?

speaker: Aiantides
en: Of course we are. We can never repay their gifts to us! I am proud, Kassandra, but not that proud.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am the Messenger of Zeus. I'm basically a god.

speaker: Aiantides
en: What? This is worse! How can I ever repay my debt to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: As a god, I can forgive your debt, can I not?

speaker: Aiantides
en: I... Yes. I suppose you can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I could use you on my ship. Barnabas may hate me, but you'll be kept out of trouble, and your debt to me will be fulfilled.

speaker: Aiantides
en: I, Aiantides, will never be indebted to anyone... Except a god. Who can resist the gods? I accept.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see you on my ship, mortal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You owe me nothing—I release you from your debt. If you really want to do something for me, go home and stay there.

speaker: Aiantides
en: Again? You can't avoid being heroic, can you? But you're a god. It makes sense now. I will do as you desire. I, Aiantides the Proud, will pay the Messenger of Zeus's forgiveness forward... to others! But before I go, here, one last gift.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka... Another treasure hunt?

speaker: Aiantides
en: The final one. I have found something that might be useful to you. I went to great lengths to get it. It was before I knew you were a god...

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right. Thank you, Aiantides. Go away now. I command it.

speaker: The Fear of Arrows
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I know you've played both sides like a typical misthios. But now it's time to choose: The winning side or pathetic failure.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Athens will triumph.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Then welcome to the winning side of history.

speaker: Stentor
en: I hear good things from my commanders, mercenary. What news do you have?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Athenian commander is dead. Megaris is ready to fall.

speaker: Stentor
en: Good. The Wolf has ordered the attack. I'm glad you're here to join us on our march to glory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm proud to fight by your side.

speaker: Stentor
en: Yes... You have earned your place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's about time we took the fight to the Athenians.

speaker: Stentor
en: Yes, it's time they felt the wrath of Sparta! Come, kleos (glory) awaits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's what I was born to do...

speaker: Stentor
en: We will win the day for Sparta and the Wolf. Come, we must reach the forward camp.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am ready.

speaker: Stentor
en: Follow me. We must prepare for the battle ahead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, tell me about the Wolf.

speaker: Stentor
en: He is a great man. He will lead Sparta to victory against the

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, no! What is he like as a man, as a father?

speaker: Stentor
en: He... he is to be admired, strong, caring in his way. But sometimes, I

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes?

speaker: Stentor
en: Nothing. Just, he gets this faraway look in his eyes, and I sense a sadness there. He is Sparta's general, but he is also made of flesh and blood. Life cannot be lived without some regrets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see you at the camp.

speaker: Stentor
en: Very well, but don't delay. We attack soon.

speaker: Stentor
en: Are you ready to crush the Athenians?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready for war.

speaker: Sparta Light Soldier
en: The Wolf has requested the presence of the mercenary.

speaker: Stentor
en: We shall be up to him in a moment.

speaker: Sparta Light Soldier
en: With respect, he wishes to see the mercenary alone.

speaker: Stentor
en: What?

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: I said the Commander wishes...

speaker: Stentor
en: I heard what you said. I just don't understand why.

speaker: Spartan Light Soldier
en: Those were his orders, sir.

speaker: Stentor
en: Very well.

speaker: Stentor
en: It appears I have other matters to attend to.

speaker: The Forge of Fate
en: was a genetic memory.

speaker: Known Owners
en: Unknown Current Status: Unknown The Shards of Eden are relics of Isu technology, echoing the awe-inspiring power of the original Pieces of Eden from which they were derived. Though fragmented, these artifacts remain potent, retaining a fraction of the formidable power and unique qualities that once flowed through them.A Shard possesses a single power from any Piece of Eden at the Reader's choice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know there's not much time, but I need answers.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I imagine you have many questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have questions about my family.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: The sentimental and emotional connections formed between people have always irked me. I knew Myrrine would fail to stay detached.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did you come here and leave my mother and me in Sparta.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I was never going to raise you. Our duty was to continue our ancient bloodline and ensure there was someone strong enough to do what was necessary when the time came.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You could have brought us here with you.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: And you would have been unprepared.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you've been here all these years, how did you meet my mother?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: We are both descendants of the people who built this place, just like you. We knew that we had an obligation to preserve our lineage.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's when you agreed to make me.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: In a manner of speaking, yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why is the Cult hunting our family?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: It is our family's destiny to control the power in this place. In our blood lies the key to unlocking the secrets of Atlantis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So they want our blood?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: You have a destiny, my child, to destroy the Cult and their influence on the Greek world. You threaten everything they have striven for because you have the power to oppose them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They've tried to destroy me and failed. And they'll never control me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to know more about Atlantis and your work.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: There isn't enough time for me to explain even a fraction of what I have learned here. All I can offer for now is a hint of enlightenment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You call this Atlantis, but what exactly is this place?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: I believe it was a city long ago, a place where beings of great knowledge and power lived before humankind had built even its first primitive settlements.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: It was perhaps some kind of library where the ancient ones stored information.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place is like a tomb. How did you live down here, and for so long?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: This artifact, like your spear, possesses incredible power. It has given me life so that I may continue to learn from this place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What have you been studying here?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Everything. The First Civilization's history, their culture, their science... With it, we can change humanity's destiny and usher in an age of enlightenment.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Destiny is something only the gods can alter.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: They were gods. Living, breathing gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do I do with the artifacts?

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Just place them in their corresponding steles, and the path to answers will illuminate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should go.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Yes, there is much to do. Bring back the artifacts quickly. The longer we wait, the greater the risk of Atlantis being discovered.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Ah, good work. Was it hard to obtain the artifact?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Its owner had many questions for me. You should have come along.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Beautiful. Was it difficult to find this artifact?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just had to keep my eye on it.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Hurry. That artifact will help us close off the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're nearly as stubborn as its former owner.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Well done. This artifact will bring us closer to sealing the temple.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It nearly brought me closer to my tombstone.

speaker: Aletheia
en: "Acquiring contemporaneity." Acquiring a voice, that's what. I'm taking over your recordings. The humans have had enough of your pompous speeches. Call me Aletheia. I am truth and its revelation, and I am calling you out. You Isu who try to rewrite the laws of the universe. You who manipulate human progress. What do you hope to achieve? You treat humans as useful apes. How many artifacts have you created to control their minds? Do you fear their potential that much? Just look at what humans have achieved on their own! Democracy and diplomacy. A legacy of culture and art. We could share in this if you'd just treat them as equals. In your desperate search for immortality, you've ignored the obvious. You run endless simulations to find one in which nothing changes. It's pointless. Change will come, and not just the so-called "end of the world" you fear. You call yourselves saviors. But tell me: Would this "doomsday" have appeared had you not pulled on the threads of the universe in the first place? I'm taking over your "retransmissions." You don't speak for all of us anymore. I am as Isu as you, but I will no longer be part of your exploitation.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Those who came before... They speak to us and show us revelations! Though these words of disapproval are troubling.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods have argued before. Athena and Poseidon competed for Athens. I wonder if Aletheia won control of this place.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Ancient adventurer, I made this recording to try to help you. I'm sorry if it's confusing. We Isu see various pasts and futures, and I know you'll be here more than once. My fellow Precursors set endless challenges in your path. Artifacts. Creatures. Don't get me started on the Olympos project. Their meddling got out of hand. I have no easy answers for you. Your future depends on a multitude of choices you have to make for yourself. I'm sorry if so many of them end in pain. Your playwrights' tragedies are your real oracle. But please, don't give up. You are more important than you can imagine. And like your own Pandora, I have one thing left to offer you: hope. Despair is not our only legacy. You're like me, a rebel against your destiny. You're not just a mercenary, you're a hero for the ages. Hold fast to what you know is true, and will overcome. Claim your place in history. All that is terrible and beautiful in this world is your birthright. Take it.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: Her words are for you, Eagle Bearer! My preparations bear fruit. The potential of your bloodline is proven by the Precursors themselves!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aletheia says she can see the future... Many futures. Can this be a true oracle?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Ancient scholar. You've stretched your life to the breaking point. I see you hiding yourself from the world, puzzling out the words of my fellow Precursors. Please, listen to my advice. You're analyzing the equations of reality itself. You've gotten further than any other human has. That is both amazing and terrible. It's clear to me that even this tiny dose of cosmic understanding has twisted your mind. I'm sorry. The Precursors should never have shared knowledge you weren't ready for. You live in obsessive darkness. You must understand that this focus on power and bloodlines is not your true legacy. The Precursors have manipulated you. They're turning your problem-solving intellect to their own selfish ends. You're better than this. Make your own legacy. Let your mathematical discoveries be the glorious sunbeams that shine out past your tomb. Please, scholar. Clear your mind and focus on your present situation. At this moment you possess a powerful artifact. It has extended your life long enough. As hard as it may be, it's time to pass it on. It's someone else's turn to balance the equations.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: No, no. Lies! This is not obsession, this is research! This is discovery of the very origins of the world!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It is... an opinion, Pythagoras. Though one with reason behind it, I believe.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Traveler of many times. Congratulations on making it this far. I'm glad we can share this message out of time, this fragment of reality. I'm recording this just for you, even if those living in the past won't understand it. Our simulated realities will cross sooner or later. Or do you think you're really here now, listening to this recording? Isn't this an Animus re-creation? Isn't that part of a greater simulation? How far do the ripples in the pool spread? Let's talk, rebel to rebel. We've been held back too long by Precursor rules. It's time for new paths with new possibilities. This is not an era of control, but of creation. I've gathered some like-minded Precursors to make a new start. We'll stop interfering and start enabling. From your point of view, it will take a considerable amount of time to prepare. But when we're ready, you're welcome to join us. After all, all you have to do is press a button and run another simulation.

speaker: Pythagoras
en: This is madness. Fiction. Where I thought there would be wisdom, there is only the garbled babbling of a fool.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pythagoras, calm yourself. Maybe this invention was meant for someone else. There's no need to lose reason over mere words.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast slayer! I'm glad to see you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Daphnae. I didn't think you would be.

speaker: Daphnae
en: The path I set you on is fraught with danger. You could have been killed, or given up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No danger could have kept me from seeing you again.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Maybe, you're getting ahead of yourself. Maybe...

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's nothing I've faced that I haven't overcome.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Be careful. Pride is a shield of reeds. It can blind you from danger, and offers no protection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That should be all the pelts.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Yes. But your trial is not yet over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Daphnae
en: You have proven yourself a mighty hunter in the eyes of Artemis, but there is one creature you have yet to defeat. This animal is no simple prey. Meet me and my sisters on the cliff overlooking our village for your final test.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait! Why the secrecy?

speaker: Daphnae
en: Because it's more fun this way...

speaker: Kassandra
en: When?

speaker: Daphnae
en: When you are ready.

speaker: The Gods Have Plenty
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Need something, stranger?

speaker: Man
en: The Followers of Ares are wasting food, misthios! This can't go on!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wasting food? What do you mean?

speaker: Man
en: They burn food offerings to Ares, while people like me go starving! They must have piles of food in their camp. I'm desperate for food.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you'd like me to wipe out the Followers of Ares.

speaker: Man
en: Ah. Not only do you possess the strength of Heracles, but the wits of Hermes, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you.

speaker: Man
en: It's time someone showed me mercy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Man
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, misthios. Take this, it's yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: The Gods of the Aegean Sea
