speaker: Arsenios
en: Minotaur tours! Get your Minotaur tours here! Learn how to defeat the mighty Minotaur! Slay the beast with this one weird trick all minotaurs hate! Book your tour now to avoid the disappointment up at your own headless body while the Minotaur laughts at you—even he thinks the tour's great value for drachmae! Take the Minotaur tour to avoid bringing shame and dishonor to your parents. "Wife, I heard our child went off to slay the Minotaur. Have they returned victoriously yet? No Husband, they didn't take a handsome young man's very reasonably priced tour and were tragically killed. We're laughing stocks at the agora. We never should've had kids." Is this what you want your parents to say, hero? Is it? No?! Then sign up now for my Minotaur Tour now!

speaker: Arsenios
en: Warrior! Welcome to Pephka. Home of the Minotaur, and our world-famous Minotaur tunics! Tunics! Minotaur tunics! One size fits all!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't see how one size can fit everyone.

speaker: Arsenios
en: My name's Arsenios. If you want to know how to defeat the Minotaur, and become the Greek world's famous warrior, then this is the tour for you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't need the tour. Already killed the beast.

speaker: Arsenios
en: You think

speaker: Arsenios
en: You killed

speaker: Arsenios
en: The Minotaur?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was an epic battle. Lots of blood.

speaker: Arsenios
en: An epic battle with a man in a mask! You were scammed, warrior. But have no fear, you're in Pephka now—a land famous for its honesty and total lack of scams.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You sell it well, kid. Let's go on your tour. You're not worried someone's going to steal your "world famous Minotaur tunics"?

speaker: Arsenios
en: Who would? They're tunics for Minotaurs.

speaker: Arsenios
en: As you can see from the statues, the Minotaur is a fearsome foe—so don't forget this exclusive tour tip: He hates being stabbed! Particularly with sharp objects. They say it's his only weakness...!

speaker: Arsenios
en: Behold, an exact replica of the Minotaur! Actual Minotaur size may vary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where's the rest of him?

speaker: Arsenios
en: Up the hill. Some of the workers lost control moving it into place. It killed two of them. Horns torn them clean apart. Well, not "clean" apart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like even Minotaur statues are deadly.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Oh, they're the deadliest! They say Theseus himself was killed by a Minotaur statue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've heard many tales of the Minotaur. They usually make Theseus sound more... heroic.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Well, Sparta's not known for its quality education, is it? Next thing, you'll tell me Medusa's real!

speaker: Kassandra
en: She was, until I killed

speaker: Arsenios
en: She's a mythical creature! Like um, like a cyclops.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Cyclopes are real too, I've killed

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whether Theseus was crushed by the Minotaur, or... by a large statue shaped like the Minotaur, he was nothing compared to me. I will succeed where he failed.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Oh, a confident warrior! Perhaps you'll be the first to return...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's just continue the tour.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Hey, in Pephka, the hero's always right! This way!

speaker: Arsenios
en: Look out, that rock's actually a Minotaur dropping. He must have been through here! I can't believe we missed him! Here's another helpful tip you won't get on any other tour—the Minotaur... isn't a morning person! Trust me, I know my Minotaurs—I've been in this business 27 years. Just between you and me, I'm kinda hoping my boy, Arsenios Jr., takes over some day. Good kid, goooood kid.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Warriors from all over the Aegean come to Pephka to face the Mighty Minotaur, hoping to claim his head as the ultimate prize. So far, well, he's killed all of them. But! Drinking freshly squeezed Minotaur Hoof Elixir will no doubt give you the oomph you'll need to triumph!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where does this "Minotaur Hoof Elixir" come from?

speaker: Arsenios
en: The Hoof of the Minotaur, obviously! It's right there in the name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...Uh huh.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does this elixir do, besides... give me "oomph"?

speaker: Arsenios
en: Depends. What ails you, friend? Sore throat? Slow-healing wounds? Itchy bits on parts unmentionable?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Will it cure the regret of taking unnecessary tours?

speaker: Arsenios
en: ...Yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And let me guess, you've got a vial, ready for purchase?

speaker: Arsenios
en: It's just like pater always said, "Never leave home without the ground up hooves of a mythical creature."

speaker: Kassandra
en: You never know when you'll need some... Minotaur Hoof... Elixir...

speaker: Arsenios
en: You've made a wise purchase, my fiscally responsible friend! Now come! There's so much more to see!

speaker: Minotaur Hoof Elixir
en: This elixir, made entirely out of ground-up Minotaur hoof, is completely guaranteed to cure any problem. But wait, there's more...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll pass.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Of course, of course! You're under no obligation to help a poor kid from the streets of Pephka make an honest income in order to save his frail and sickly grandmother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If she's sick, why did you cough?

speaker: Arsenios
en: I'm very empathetic?

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's the most pathetic lie I've ever heard. And I lived on Kephallonia.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Yeah, well, it was worth a shot. Now come! There's so much more to see!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're doing all this for your grandmother?

speaker: Arsenios
en: She puts on a brave face for me, but I hear her crying at night when she thinks I'm asleep. She's always moaning, or vomiting, or moaning and vomiting. If only I could sell more Minotaur Hoof Elixir, we might be able to afford a physician...!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You never know when you'll need some... Minotaur Hoof... Elixir...

speaker: Arsenios
en: You've made a wise purchase, my fiscally responsible friend! Now come! There's so much more to see!

speaker: Minotaur Hoof Elixir
en: This elixir, made entirely out of ground-up Minotaur hoof, is completely guaranteed to cure any problem. But wait, there's more...

speaker: Kassandra
en: If your elixir's so potent, maybe you could give your grandmother a bottle or two?

speaker: Arsenios
en: Great idea! ...If you could just pay for them –

speaker: Kassandra
en: No.

speaker: Arsenios
en: No?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Now come! There's so much more to see!

speaker: Arsenios
en: I'm not saying I'm responsible for breaking the Minotaur statue, but I'm also not saying I'm not responsible.

speaker: Arsenios
en: And so concludes our tour!

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...That's the tour?! I didn't learn anything about the Minotaur!

speaker: Arsenios
en: My customers are always satisfied!

speaker: Arsenios
en: You can pay my associates on your way out. Please enjoy the rest of your stay here in Pephka!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good scam, kid. If I was ambitious as you when I was your age, my life would've turned out much better. Possibly making bad wine on an island somewhere...

speaker: Arsenios
en: Thank you.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Until next time, warrior!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh no, no, no, no, absolutely not.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One last thing—I'm told a man named "Melite" lives in Pephka. Probably someone powerful. Likes wearing masks.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Never heard of him before. But Leiandros, the town crier, might have. He knows everyone. He's in the center of the city. Ask him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leiandros? I've already met Leiandros. That man knows an impressive amount of nothing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're not getting one drachma out of me.

speaker: Arsenios
en: No, not one—I'm getting all of it. Get her!

speaker: Arsenios
en: Don't damage her gear! We can get a good price for it. She's basically walking drachmae!

speaker: Arsenios
en: ... Uh, well done, warrior! You've passed the... "Survive the Thugs" test! Not, uh, not everyone passes that! You've earned an extra 10% off our world famous Minotaur tunics! Or, haha, you know what? You've given me a great tour! A tour of friendship! Which I will totally pay for! here, a large drachma fee for your fantastic friendship tour!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A pleasure doing business with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: One more thing: I'm looking for someone named "Melite". A man with influence and an obssession with masks.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Never heard the name. But there's a man in town. Leiandros, he knows everyone. I bet he can help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leiandros? He's of no use to me.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Hey!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yeah?

speaker: Arsenios
en: What's it like being a misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Could be worse.

speaker: Arsenios
en: Can I interest you in purchasing some fermented Minotaur droppings or–

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you really going to try that on me again?!

speaker: Arsenios
en: Can't hit the target if you don't shoot the arrow!

speaker: Drakios
en: Ah, more fresh blood. By the look of these warriors, this Battle of One Hundred Hands is going to be one for the ages. Indeed, I think it will have people talking for years. Your gear could be the difference between victory or death. Don't forget to visit Gernadios for the best weapons and armor.

speaker: Blacksmith
en: Thanks, Drakios.

speaker: Drakios
en: Prepare, warriors. The Battle will commence soon.

speaker: Drakios
en: Ah, the misthios arrives. Then we can begin.

speaker: Drakios
en: We are gathered here again for the Battle of One Hundred Hands. Indeed, impressive warriors from all over the Greek world have come to test their might and skill against each other. Whether it is the sharpest sword in the Athenian army, or the broadest shield Sparta can muster, all now stand alone against the many.

speaker: Drakios
en: At our climax, the final two will face off on a special battlefield, but only one will be called Champion. Let the Battle of One Hundred Hands begin!

speaker: Drakios
en: Remember that horn. You'll hear it throughout the Battle, marking your progress. Now fight!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fighting with obsidian swords? I'd win against them using my fists.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The second horn. That means a quarter of the combatants are dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The other contestants must be somewhere else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Another horn. Half the fighters are already dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Smells like rotten eggs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to keep moving.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought this was every fighter for herself. These people are clearly working together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm nearly finished. I should return to Drakios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These bodies... Such a waste of life for sport.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't seen Roxana among the dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can only imagine the might of all these warriors aligned against the Cult. Instead, we came to Melos to slaughter each other over a sack of drachmae.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there a final challenger?

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed there is! Patience, Kassandra, patience.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me, Drakios! Is it Roxana? Is she alive?

speaker: Drakios
en: Your final challenger approaches.

speaker: Drakios
en: Come! We will finish this in the shadow of the volcano in the east.

speaker: Drakios
en: Well done, Kassandra. Well done. Your final challenge takes you to the volcano to the east.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And then you'll give me the information I want about the Cult.

speaker: Drakios
en: Indeed, I will. But before that, one contestant remains.

speaker: Kassandra
en: High Priestess. Open up.

speaker: Eritha
en: So you can kill me? Who sent you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Diona sent me. I'm a friend.

speaker: Eritha
en: What did that idiot girl send a misthios for? I gave her orders to follow, not to delegate.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I wanted you dead, I wouldn't have knocked. Diona sent me.

speaker: Eritha
en: To run her errands? You must be another one of her idiotic suitors. At least you look better than that other idiot at the harbor.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She says you think there's a traitor in your midst.

speaker: Eritha
en: You can't trust anyone these days. What do you want with the Cult?

speaker: Kassandra
en: They ripped my family apart! I'll have vengeance.

speaker: Eritha
en: Excellent. Anger is a wonderful motivator.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They have wronged my family and it's only right they pay for it. I'll have justice.

speaker: Eritha
en: Family is indeed a powerful motivator.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Cult of Kosmos have much to answer for. And they will answer to me.

speaker: Eritha
en: Perhaps you will be of use to me after all. I sent one of my handmaidens to spy on some of our own and

speaker: Kassandra
en: She hasn't returned.

speaker: Eritha
en: Indeed. Except I couldn't care less about her... it's the information she uncovered I desire. Retrieve it for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your dislike for your sister is obvious. What happened between you two?

speaker: Eritha
en: I'm the first born, and with that comes certain privileges and responsibilities. My sister is a vindictive, jealous creature. She undermines my authority constantly. Clearly, she thinks she'd make the better High Priestess.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see.

speaker: Eritha
en: But she is my sister. And I do love her. I just wish she wasn't a jealous little fool.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where should I start looking for her?

speaker: Eritha
en: I sent her to the outskirts of Kythera. Hm... I recall there being a farm in that area. She might've taken refuge there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's where I'll start then.

speaker: Eritha
en: She would be looking to avoid busy areas like the military camp - wait. Did you have something to do with my prisoners being broken out of jail at the military camp?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The harbor master did it. I tried to stop him but I was too late.

speaker: Eritha
en: Again with that worm! This is all Diona's fault. She has him wrapped around her finger. Every once in a while, she'll break his heart and he'll do something stupid. You did well trying to stop him. Now, get me my information while I deal with the harbor master.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, that was my doing. The harbor master said the High Priestess locks up innocent people and executes them. I could not stand idly by.

speaker: Eritha
en: I wasn't going to execute them! Torture them, maybe. But all stand trial here in Kythera. That liar! The harbor master strikes out at the temple when my sister scorns him. But this time, he's gone too far. I'll overlook your involvement in this. Just make sure you get me that information while I deal with him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where did you say to look again?

speaker: Eritha
en: Try the farm outside of the city. She might be hiding out there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get you the information your handmaiden found.

speaker: Eritha
en: Good, I'll make it worth your while. Now go quickly, she was last seen east of Pilgrim Hill.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found this note earlier on the body of a priestess at a farm. She was slain by Cultists before I found her.

speaker: Eritha
en: What? Read it to me, quickly!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It says, "Don't trust the Fates." The rest of the papyrus is stained with blood.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not many places for a handmaiden to hide in the outskirts of the city. This must be it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Cultists on a farm? Something's not right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Found her!

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Do not trust the Fates." Hm, it's addressed to the High Priestess. She needs to know about this.

speaker: Eritha
en: Well? What of my handmaiden?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She was murdered. It might have something to do with this note... it says "Don't trust the Fates."

speaker: Eritha
en: That's it?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The rest of the papyrus is stained with blood.

speaker: Eritha
en: That makes no sense.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She protected it with her life. It wasn't for nothing.

speaker: Eritha
en: Now we'll never know for sure if there is a traitor in our ranks. But I cannot rule out the possibility. Our situation is dire. Work with Diona. Secure Kythera for us, misthios.

speaker: Hedone
en: Hello! Have you come to learn about the mysteries of Hedone?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure, I'd like to know. Let's start with... what's Hedone?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not much of a mystery if you tell everybody about it.

speaker: Hedone
en: Hedone is the goddess of bliss. And since we all seek bliss, we are all Hedone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not seeking bliss. I'm seeking an actor.

speaker: Hedone
en: We have no actors here, only teachers and students.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look, his name is Tros. He's an actor working for Thespis.

speaker: Hedone
en: I recall hearing that an actor joined us... But now his name is Hedone. Like mine. Everyone here is Hedone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just give me a straight answer. I need to find that actor.

speaker: Hedone
en: I'm sorry. I'm the only one permitted to speak with outsiders. But if you pass our initiation, others will speak with you too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. Initiate me, Hedone. What do I have to do?

speaker: Hedone
en: Wonderful! You must complete two tasks to demonstrate your devotion. First, climb to the top of the Waterfall of Eternal Joy and dive into Froth of Fantasy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Right. And then what?

speaker: Hedone
en: Then, explore the Cave of Deepest Self Knowledge and return with the treasure you'll find inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Waterfall dive. Cave treasure. Got it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the waterfall. Now to pick a good spot and jump.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That cave must be around here somewhere.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ah, that must be the cave with the treasure inside.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's what I'm looking for.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I jumped from the waterfall and found the treasure. Now will you initiate me?

speaker: Hedone
en: You have initiated yourself! Welcome to the Mysteries of Hedone, Hedone! Go talk with your brothers and sisters, they'll be happy to meet you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go speak with them now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, do you know who Tros is?

speaker: Hedone
en: Sorry, Hedone. I've heard that name floating around, but I have no idea who it was attached to. Our former names and professions mean nothing here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll have to talk to everyone, then.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you Tros? I'm looking for an actor named Tros.

speaker: Hedone
en: What? I had nearly reached the third level of Hedone's godly bliss when you interrupted me. Now I have to start all over again!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You get on with that. It's probably best you stay away from acting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. Are you Tros, the actor?

speaker: Hedone
en: Um, I, oh... N-no. I'm not him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Otherwise Thespis is terrible at choosing actors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hello. I'm looking for the actor Tros. Is that you?

speaker: Hedone
en: Oh, an actor? I'd love to be an actor. But my friends told me I'd need to practice my stage presence first.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's wise advice. Good luck with that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hello, are you Tros, the actor?

speaker: Hedone
en: You must be new. There are no actors here. Our only role is to be Hedone, to inhabit her grace and tranquility.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You sound like you know something about the theater.

speaker: Hedone
en: I wouldn't say I know much about it. I might have studied a little Aristophanes, a little Euripides... Medea was robbed, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you aren't the actor Tros, you're certainly good enough to be him. Come act in Thespis' play.

speaker: Hedone
en: I'd like to help you, Hedone, but I need to stay here. Work on my enlightenment, all right?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Picture it – you, up on a stage, showing hundreds of people how wonderful the message of Hedone is. I'm offering you that chance, you just have to take it.

speaker: Hedone
en: That is magnificent. A chance to spread the joy of Hedone to so many people... I'll do it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Now go report to Thespis at Pelops Market in Elis. And get on with your rehearsals, Hedone... I mean, Ephialtes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Enlightenment is hard. The gods don't make things easy for us. If you truly want to follow their path, you have to challenge yourself. If you stay here and rot, you'll be a failure.

speaker: Hedone
en: That's harsh... But you're right. If I don't go out in the world, is my faith in Hedone really true? Only one way to find out, and that's on the stage.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Now go report to Thespis at Pelops Market in Elis. And get on with your rehearsals, Hedone... I mean, Ephialtes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to speak with some more Hedonists.

speaker: Hedone
en: That's a good name.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hello. I'm looking for Tros, the actor.

speaker: Hedone
en: Well, none of us use our old names here. But acting, I know about that. Make the audience laugh when they want to laugh, and cry when they want to cry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And how would you make an audience laugh?

speaker: Hedone
en: Well, I'd probably slip and fall on a piece of goat's bladder. Works every time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see... And to make them cry?

speaker: Hedone
en: I'd tell them about how much I miss my poor dead goat. And if that didn't work, I'd cut an onion at the same time. Old theater trick, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you aren't the actor Tros, you're certainly good enough to be him. Come act in Thespis' play.

speaker: Hedone
en: I'm flattered. But what am I supposed to tell my friends? We're supposed to honor the goddess Hedone together.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look, your friends here already understand Hedone's teachings. But if you were onstage expressing them, then hundreds more people could hear your message.

speaker: Hedone
en: You talk a good game. Sure, I'll do it to get the message out. Let everyone hear what Hedone can do for them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Thespis is waiting for you at Pelops Market in Elis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're living in the middle of nowhere claiming to worship the goddess of joy, when the real people who need her words are living just a few steps away. If you stay here, you're wasting your life.

speaker: Hedone
en: You're a tough one, but you have a point. Everyone in here already understands the word. On stage, I can make sure everyone gets it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Thespis is waiting for you at Pelops Market in Elis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thanks for your time. I'll speak with the rest of the Hedonists.

speaker: Hedone
en: We should use that name. Might get more people joining with a snappy name like that.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper. You came.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's... Am I seeing things?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper. You have come far to meet me here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Keeper? My name is Kassandra.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Names changes, but this task is eternal. You are the Keeper, she who keeps the Great Seal closed and the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any "tasks" I perform, I decide. Now who are you?

speaker: Aletheia
en: I am called many things, but you can tell me, Aletheia. With the Staff in your hands, we are now entwined.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your voice. I heard it in Atlantis.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You remember. My name is Aletheia. With the Staff in your hands, we are now entwined.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me more about this task.

speaker: Aletheia
en: To be entwined with mine. I've been called by many names, but you may call me Aletheia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Entwined... how?

speaker: Aletheia
en: I can now present myself to you in a form that you recognize. You must deliver me to the Heir of Memories. Even now, she watches us. When I speak to you, I speak through you to her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: None of this makes any sense, Aletheia.

speaker: Aletheia
en: It will. In Atlantis, the Great Seal hid itself from Pythagoras. It wants to be opened, but not by him. Your task is to prepare the Heir of Memories to open it. Pledge yourself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, I'm supposed to hold the Staff until this "Heir" person takes it from me. What will happen to me?

speaker: Aletheia
en: What happens to all of us. Then she will open the Great Seal to Atlantis. It longs to be opened. Your task is to be the Keeper until that time. Pledge yourself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is this Heir?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Not where, but when. She is yet to be, but even still, she is here watching us now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. I pledge to keep the Staff until the Heir of Memories, whoever that is, is ready to take it.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper, our task is to guide the Heir of Memories to the symbols. A man called Theras knows of their whereabouts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Theras... The guy who helped get Phidias out of Athens? Is that why you've brought me back to this place?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Here, the role of the Keeper bound itself to you, though you didn't know it yet. Now, to uncover the truth, we must go to Theras.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How will I know this Heir of Memories when I see her?

speaker: Aletheia
en: She will come to you. The end of your journey is in the Hall of Atlantis, where her true journey begins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't understand who the "Keeper" is.

speaker: Aletheia
en: The Keeper isn't a person, but a task. And it is yours. Pythagoras held the Staff to exploit its power. The Keeper's task is to restrain it and protect it from the hands of corruption until the Heir of Memories appears.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who, or what are you?

speaker: Aletheia
en: I am Aletheia. Pythagoras called my people the Ones Who Came Before, but we are the Isu. Like you, I invited rebellion into the world, though there complications. I replicated my consciousness in the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus so that I speak with you and the Heir.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Theras could be anywhere now.

speaker: Aletheia
en: What I know is that he was brought to Seriphos, but be careful. He went against his will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to find Theras. I'm guess you're coming with me?

speaker: Aletheia
en: Our tasks are the same.

speaker: The Heroes of the Cult
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Such a noble creature. The gods themselves will be envious of this hunt.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast Slayer, I'm glad to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Hind of Keryneia's pelt.

speaker: Daphnae
en: I remember being awestruck when I caught a glimpse of her through the trees, long ago.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was an honor to hunt such a noble beast. For all the suffering and death I've seen, when you see something as magnificent as this... Words escape me.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Artemis was right to to bring you to me. A warrior's heart beats within your chest, yet it is tempered by kindess.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The gods put animals here for us to hunt. Who am I to defy their will?

speaker: Daphnae
en: As a huntress I take no pleasure in death. We honor our prey, admire their cunning, respect their power—and revere their sacrifice.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are we that desperate? We're helping somebody move?

speaker: Barnabas
en: What? The guy's got a lot of stuff! Work is work. And a few extra drachmae never hurt anybody. Sometimes even the simplest things can be worthy of our attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That is much more worthy of my attention, Barnabas.

speaker: Civilian
en: Help! Please! Help me, please!

speaker: Magistrate
en: It's not my village, so it's not my problem. I don't know what else you want me to say.

speaker: Civilian
en: These poor people. They don't deserve this.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: I heard someone was lurking in the shadows. I bet it's that Eagle-Bearing misthios.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: No wonder the village is being attacked.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're here to kill. Why attack this village? They're innocent...

speaker: Aiantides
en: Please, I have a family! I didn't do anything!

speaker: Aiantides
en: Fucking malákes. That was close.

speaker: Civilian
en: Oh, thank the gods! They... they heard me! Thank you!

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank Zeus, misthios. Thank you!

speaker: Natakas
en: Misthios, watch out!

speaker: Natakas
en: More people near the Spartan camp need help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Persians?

speaker: Unknown
en: Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Natakas
en: You—You are the Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go!

speaker: Unknown
en: The Huntsman will be pleased when we bring him your head.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're welcome to try.

speaker: Persian Soldier
en: You're smaller than the stories say, "Eagle Bearer."

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more people to help at the Spartan Camp. I should head there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who was that who saved me?

speaker: Natakas
en: I knew you'd come. The Spartans are here slaughtering everyone. We have to stop them! Hurry! They're dying!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Misthios, you saved us.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: I wouldn't be here without you.

speaker: Natakas
en: Eagle Bearer

speaker: Kassandra
en: Call me Kassandra.

speaker: Natakas
en: My name's Natakas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They called me the Eagle Bearer. How do they know about me?

speaker: Natakas
en: I'm not sure. But they're certainly looking for something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Huntsman sounds like a name I should know.

speaker: Natakas
en: And if he's here, we're fucked...

speaker: Natakas
en: I need to take care of these people. That Order Elite passed through here, killing as he went. He left tracks nearby.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll follow him.

speaker: Natakas
en: Thank you, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For what?

speaker: Natakas
en: For helping. When nobody else would.

speaker: Natakas
en: I'll keep tending to the wounded here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Need something?

speaker: Hunter
en: I've hunted in this forest for years. I will not abandon it. I will be here as it heals.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there enough game left for you to hunt?

speaker: Hunter
en: Game remains and more will return. But I must protect myself. Carcasses are drawing out wolves in droves. Not to mention the bandits who comb the woods looking for easy victims.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And of course, you want me to kill them all.

speaker: Hunter
en: No bandit should be left standing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can count on me.

speaker: Hunter
en: Good. Get it done soon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can leave everything to me.

speaker: Hunter
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

speaker: Hunter
en: Take this as thanks, mercenary. You did good work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I always finish what I've started.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: What?! When did this happen?

speaker: Civilian
en: Earlier today. I was taking my boy fishing when we heard the screams.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: What were they doing out there?

speaker: Civilian
en: Hunting party, I think.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: We must send aid at once.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Thank the gods you're here. A hunting party has been attacked outside the city, near the Cursed Land of Oedipous.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Any survivors?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: This man saw dead bodies, but he could still hear screaming.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are many dangerous beasts out in the wild. If someone is injured, they won't last long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they weren't ready to face the beasts out in the wild, they shouldn't have gone hunting. Nature is not kind to those who underestimate her.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: I need you to go and rescue whoever is still alive, and put an end to the dangerous beast that attacked them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, I'll destroy the beast and if anyone's still in one piece.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: If they are, bring them back to me, and I'll do what I can to save them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not interested in saving foolish hunters right now.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: There's no time to waste. We must help those in danger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are a lot of hunting grounds nearby. Where should I look?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: They were sighted following animal tracks around Snake Head Rock.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know what attacked them?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: Not for certain. The roar could have been from any number of beasts... Many predators call the wilds of Boeotia their home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How many people will I find out there?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: It sounded like only one hunter was alive, but hunting parties usually contain three or four people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go and find the trail.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Must be what's left of the hunting party.

speaker: Galeos
en: Please, by all the gods, save me.

speaker: Galeos
en: Quickly! Kill that beast before it finishes me off.

speaker: Galeos
en: Thank you. Thank you. I owe you my life, brave hero.

speaker: Galeos
en: I feel faint. I'm getting dizzy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to get him back to Hippokrates before he bleeds out all over me.

speaker: The Illusion of Peace
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: The Informant
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories stored in the Abstergo Cloud and relived by an Assassin hacker in 2023 through the Animus.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Keeper... Return to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aletheia? She must need me. I should find her.

speaker: Aletheia
en: It's time, Keeper, to fulfill the most important part of your task as the one who holds the Staff. Are you ready to begin?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever it is you have planned, I'm ready.

speaker: Aletheia
en: The Keeper shares blood with Those Who Came Before and is connected to the Isu...

speaker: Aletheia
en: The blood that is shared must be offered... And the Great Seal will open for us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you say so.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Welcome, Keeper. You've entered the great Throne Room of Atlantis. What lies in this room are remnants of Isu tech I've adapted in order for you to begin your journey. I'm sure you have questions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place... Did Pythagoras know it existed?

speaker: Aletheia
en: No. I wouldn't show it to him. This room was built by the Isu to house something else—these thrones were once just thrones. Now they contain my simulations. Don't worry, I'll show you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You told me this room was meant for the Heir of Memories, but I got in so easily.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You paid for it in blood—blood that looks quite like ours when you look closely enough.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater always told me there was power in our blood. I guess she was right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more I have to do.

speaker: Aletheia
en: Always, Keeper. When the Staff belonged to Pythagoras, he used it selfishly for knowledge. He was weak where you aren't. You will endure lifetimes until the Heir of Memories takes this burden. The only way to carry the Staff's weight is to find the strength to wield it. You'll find that strength in Elysium. The underworld awaits, Keeper.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The—what? I'm alive. If I'm alive, how can I come back from the underworld?

speaker: Aletheia
en: These portals are simulations. They were made by me for you. In Elysium you'll find power sources known as Keeper's Insights. These will effect both the Keeper and the Heir of Memories. Moving forward in the underworld will be essential to finding all the sources of power.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're asking for blind trust, Aletheia.

speaker: Aletheia
en: You pledged yourself to me and our common cause, Keeper. Never forget that I'm on your side. I won't let The Ones That Came Before control your fate. Find the strength within you and show the Staff your worth. Approach the first portal when you're ready.

speaker: Hermes
en: Ah, you again! Always nice to see a friendly face.

speaker: Hermes
en: Keeper, you've found my workshop after all. I know it may not look like much, but it's home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told you. You can call me Kassandra.

speaker: Hermes
en: In front of the Staff? Pah! But I'm glad you came. There's much to show you in this great land.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're offering, I could use some help getting my bearings.

speaker: Hermes
en: Oh, give yourself time. The golden fields reveal themselves slowly and selectively. But I can help. Walk with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought Elysium honored heroes. I even thought this is where I'd want to come, one day. But this land isn't great. It's just... haunted.

speaker: Hermes
en: Pah! Persephone has endowed this land with a beauty only she could provide. Let me convince you. Walk with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe you're right. I need to clear my head. Where to?

speaker: Hermes
en: I consider myself a key maker. One of my keys might interest you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I appreciate the offer, but there are other things for me to do first.

speaker: Hermes
en: Let's stretch our legs. There's a place I want to show you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you do in your workshop?

speaker: Hermes
en: Invent. All of reality's secrets are hidden behind doors. My inventions act as keys that unlock those doors.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You... reveal the secrets behind them.

speaker: Hermes
en: Ah! You're as wise as Pythagoras. But why discuss what we can see for ourselves?

speaker: Hermes
en: Observe, way up there. Persephone's first keep. If only you could have seen it when it was new.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It seems like most of Elysium is in ruins. What happened?

speaker: Hermes
en: This place is beautiful, as are all of Persephone's creations. But it is a world that changes at her whims. When I see decay, I know she needs us at her side more than ever.

speaker: Hermes
en: Look there! Imagine all the heroes who have passed through those golden fields, basking in the glory of eternal peace. Each thinking they'd seen nothing more beautiful, only then to set eyes on Persephone.

speaker: Hermes
en: Look there, Keeper! That encampment is the site where Hephaistos built a home for Aphrodite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Doesn't look like much now.

speaker: Hermes
en: It stood tall until Aphrodite met that child Adonis. His ability to wreak havoc with a wink and a smile is second to none.

speaker: Hermes
en: Come! That cave leads to a key I built for the Staff. Consider it our secret. The Key Maker and the Staff Keeper, friends bound by mysteries.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to me in there?

speaker: Hermes
en: Imagine for a moment—inside you, inside all of us, are parchments twisting like ribbon. On those parchments is written the story of who you are, who you were, and who you will become. Does that make sense?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Like everything else here, I don't understand any of it.

speaker: Hermes
en: Let's call it the Fates, then. Your fate is predetermined, but what you experienced in there was a key I built that can unlock it and allow you to control it. I've built many.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, this twisting ribbon defines each of us, and what happened in there... changed what defines me.

speaker: Hermes
en: You understand. With these keys, you can unlock the secrets inside you and wrest control from them. I've built many.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. I'm not used to doing this on my own. On the Adrestia I had Barnabas as a guide.

speaker: Hermes
en: Ah. Well, I hope it's a long time before I meet him here. I'll leave you to your adventuring. You're welcome to come back to my workshop any time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, Hermes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You look concerned.

speaker: Hermes
en: I'm worried about Persephone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Persephone can look after herself.

speaker: Hermes
en: She's incredible, I agree, but these are strange times. I've heard that some ungrateful delinquents plot against her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't been here long, but I've already heard people want her overthrown.

speaker: Hermes
en: You have? What do these humans expect from her? I'd heard some of the more ungrateful delinquents are planning to rise up. Imagine!

speaker: Kassandra
en: These "ungrateful delinquents"... could they be right?

speaker: Hermes
en: Pah! You give them too much credit. Still, Persephone needs protection.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't look at me.

speaker: Hermes
en: There's a friend of mine and your father's, Kyros of Zarax. He's a strong and honorable warrior. He's been abducted, but if we could free him...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're suggesting we make a human Persephone's bodyguard?

speaker: Hermes
en: With Kyros at the ready, the humans will think twice before attacking one of their own.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I didn't know any better, I'd say you were in love with Persephone.

speaker: Hermes
en: No one understands here the way I do. Adonis sees a cruel despot. To her husband, she's a trinket on his arm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what do you see?

speaker: Hermes
en: Me? Oh! I don't know—I've never had anyone ask me before. She's... everything.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you know this Kyros?

speaker: Hermes
en: He was an aid, of sorts, to your father. Every great painter needs a hand to crush their pigment. That was Kyros. A warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Say no more. I'll find Kyros for you.

speaker: Hermes
en: I knew I could trust you. While you're gone, I'll arrange a meeting with Persephone. Bring Kyros to the heart of Elysium. We'll be there.

speaker: Kyros
en: You have the Staff?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyros of Zarax, Hermes sent me.

speaker: Kyros
en: That key maker is predictable. I'll give him that much.

speaker: Kyros
en: So, how'd you get that Staff?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pythagoras was my father. Things happened. Now it's mine.

speaker: Kyros
en: That right? That makes us family. I knew the man well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I heard. This way. Persephone's waiting.

speaker: Kyros
en: Persephone herself? This is going to be easier than I thought.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait... What's going to be easier?

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, Kyros, let's make this quick. You said this is going to be easier than you thought.

speaker: Kyros
en: Since we're basically family, I'm trusting your honor. I work for Adonis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But you were caged by humans.

speaker: Kyros
en: Yes, and Hermes "found out" about it, right around the time Persephone was coaxed into deciding she needs a bodyguard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You staged the whole thing and you're using Hermes to infiltrate Persephone's lair? You're no simple warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You talk about honor? You set up this lie and used me as a mule to infiltrate Persephone's lair. I expected to meet a warrior.

speaker: Kyros
en: Before I met your father, I had four sons. Each a "warrior." When my third boy fell in battle, there was only guilt. I'd cried all my tears for the first two.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Go on.

speaker: Kyros
en: And with the fourth, I felt longing—sadness had become my only friend, and I had no one left to grieve. Warriors don't bring peace. They bring sorrow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So by getting behind Persephone's defenses, you think you can prevent war. You could convince her to surrender or distract her while Adonis escapes.

speaker: Kyros
en: Anything but battle. But before we go to Persephone, I have to send confirmation this plan worked. Will you take me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, but be quick. We need to go to Persephone and Hermes. They're waiting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You really think you can save lives?

speaker: Kyros
en: I'm not sure how death works in Elysium, but suffering is eternal, and that is something I can stop.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're coming for you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's all of them. Let's keep moving.

speaker: Kyros
en: Once Adonis hears my plan worked, maybe he'll stand down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hurry, Kyros. We need to get back to Hermes, or Persephone might suspect something.

speaker: Kyros
en: I hear Persephone likes to test her new recruits, and I've got a bit of a temper. If you see me turning red...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll think of something.

speaker: Hermes
en: Where've you been? No one keeps Persephone waiting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It got complicated. We took a less direct route.

speaker: Kyros
en: What matters, Hermes, is I'm freed thanks to you. When I go to my queen, I will make sure she's grateful to you for my service.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kyros delayed us. Ask him.

speaker: Kyros
en: I... I'd been locked up for ages. You know how our queen feels about filth. I didn't want her judging us, judging you, for being unpresentable.

speaker: Hermes
en: Explain it to Persephone. She's waiting.

speaker: Kyros
en: I'll make sure she knows this was entirely my fault, not yours.

speaker: Hermes
en: I'm sorry I was ungrateful. Kyros will make a strong guard. Thank you again, friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, Hermes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It didn't go as you planned, but relax. Persephone's safe.

speaker: Hermes
en: I am grateful for the effort, my friend, but she's not. The delinquents are getting bolder. While you were gone, I was robbed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've already wasted too much time talking, Kyros. We have to go.

speaker: Kyros
en: You're as stubborn as your father. Still, you mustn't say anything to Persephone. If she knew what we were doing, she'd have my head.

speaker: Kyros
en: I hear Persephone likes to test her new recruits, and I've got a bit of a temper. If you see me turning red...

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll think of something.

speaker: Hermes
en: You've come back, and just in time!

speaker: Persephone
en: Kyros of Zarax. Tell me—are you the obedient dog Hermes claims you are? I do love dogs.

speaker: Persephone
en: Does he not speak?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He speaks. Kyros, take a deep breath and speak.

speaker: Kyros
en: Apologies, my queen. To hear of your beauty is one thing, but to see it up close is another.

speaker: Persephone
en: Beautiful, am I?

speaker: Hermes
en: Pah! Among other things.

speaker: Kyros
en: Chaire, Child of Pythagoras. If he were here, he'd be proud of what you've become.

speaker: Hermes
en: My queen.

speaker: Hermes
en: She... touched me!

speaker: Hermes
en: Kyros is right, my friend. I knew your father well. If he were here, he'd be proud. Chaire.

speaker: Hermes
en: She... touched me. Focus, Hermes.

speaker: Hermes
en: There's been a development. It's these delinquents. They've robbed me!

speaker: Hermes
en: Keeper! I've been robbed!

speaker: Hermes
en: These are dark times for Elysium. Those delinquent fools have robbed even me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did they take?

speaker: Hermes
en: I fashioned a key. A recipe, if you will, for an eternal flame. I intended to gift it to Persephone. With it, she could shine her light, even in the underworld.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An eternal flame could bring order to this chaos.

speaker: Hermes
en: You understand her burden better than you let on. By enduring her sacrifice, Persephone keeps us safe in the underworld.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No matter who the ruler is, if you give her fire, you're going to get burned.

speaker: Hermes
en: You still don't understand. Persephone wants to protect us from the dark horrors in the underworld. With the flame, she could.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, write the recipe again.

speaker: Hermes
en: What I wrote took lifetimes. We can't let it stay in the hands of humans who would use it against her. Keeper... Kassandra, we have to steal it back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take back the recipe, but only because I don't think anyone should have access to a flame that never dies.

speaker: Hermes
en: These are desperate times. You've seen the cloud these delinquents cast on our golden fields.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I said I'd get it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a good man for wanting to protect Persephone. I'll help.

speaker: Hermes
en: Ah! I thank you. You are quickly becoming my friend and ally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: An eternal flame sounds more like a myth than some simple recipe.

speaker: Hermes
en: Pah! I began writing the recipe with your father. It's as real as the danger we'd face without it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you go to these lengths to save Persephone? She wouldn't do the same for you.

speaker: Hermes
en: Since these humans started acting against her, she's been suffering. When she suffers, we all suffer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermes, has it occurred to you she might just be using you?

speaker: Hermes
en: Of course not. She simply needs someone to rely on. She needs me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find the rebels and get your recipe.

speaker: Hermes
en: That's all I ask. If you are spotted or cause a commotion, we risk retaliation. Go unseen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermes asked me to go unseen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These look like the scribbles of a madman, but it's been ripped. Where's the rest of it?

speaker: Hermes
en: We need to get the recipe back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: About that. Here it is.

speaker: Hermes
en: You've spared this realm great suffering, my friend! I wonder, were you spotted?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course not, but Hermes...

speaker: Hermes
en: Good. We don't risk retaliation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course not, but Hermes...

speaker: Hermes
en: Good. We don't risk retaliation.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was heavily guarded. Things got ugly.

speaker: Hermes
en: They will know it was us. They'll retaliate. I just wanted to help, but I've made things worse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm giving these torn pieces back, Hermes, but I'm trusting you. A flame that never dies could consume all of Elysium.

speaker: Hermes
en: I swear to you as your friend, I will only use the flame if it's absolutely necessary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's only one person in Elysium I'd trust with this power—Adonis.

speaker: Hermes
en: Have you lost your mind? I can't be the only one who sees that human for what he truly is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis can be trusted.

speaker: Hermes
en: You promise me, as a friend, that you know what you're doing. If anything happens to Persephone, I am holding you accountable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm keeping these notes. If rebellion is coming, this power could be used to light all of Elysium on fire.

speaker: Hermes
en: Perhaps you're right. So long as you swear to me you'll guard this secret with your life, I can rest knowing Persephone will never be touched by this flame.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's more for me to do, Hermes. I should go.

speaker: Hermes
en: When we met, it was as friends. If war is coming to Elysium, I want you as my ally.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermes, things are worse in Elysium that I've been letting on. The rebels are organized and ready to fight. War is coming.

speaker: Hermes
en: The humans are after us—you, me, Persephone—anyone not like them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen it too. War has come to Elysium.

speaker: Hermes
en: We must crush the force behind the chaos. Let's fight for Persephone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're so worried about Persephone you can't even see you're in just as much danger.

speaker: Hermes
en: You keep the eternal flame out of the hands of the humans, and you went unseen. We have the upper hand—we just have to strike.

speaker: Hermes
en: You want Adonis to have the key to the eternal flame, fine. But that just means I fight harder.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Calm yourself, Hermes. It's not like you're going to go on a rampage.

speaker: Hermes
en: And why not? There are so-called captains guiding the human forces. They invited chaos into this realm, so let's show them chaos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine, I'll kill the captains.

speaker: Kassandra
en: At least when you asked me to steal, it was from thieves. You're not a murderer, Hermes.

speaker: Hermes
en: You made me look like a fool when I sent you to Kyros. But I still can come back from that and prove my worth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told you we were diverted.

speaker: Hermes
en: You made me look like a fool when I sent you to Kyros. But I still can come back from that and prove my worth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told you, that was Kyros' fault, not yours.

speaker: Hermes
