en: Where to now, Eagle Bearer?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Smuggler's Dock. We need to meet the Magistrate.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Skyros it is!

speaker: Barnabas
en: That's no pirate ship... It's the Cult!

speaker: Barnabas
en: Battle stations!

speaker: Kassandra
en: They're coming from Skyros. Of course the malákas Cult's involved with The Dagger...

speaker: Barnabas
en: There is is, Smuggler's Dock. Bring it in easy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now to find the Magistrate.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Misthios! You came! We need you now more than ever. Please, help us finish The Dagger!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in.

speaker: Magistrate
en: If the information you uncovered is accurate, it won't just be the Kingfisher at the temple - it's a gathering of The Dagger's leadership. You can wipe them all out and free Euboea from their control.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Agapios will not allow his brother to be harmed.

speaker: Magistrate
en: I love Agapios, but Euboea must come first. When this is all over... I'll make sure your reward finds its way to your boat. Euboea thanks you for your service.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This isn't my mess to clean.

speaker: Magistrate
en: You're leaving?! But... but you're the Hero of Euboea...!

speaker: Magistrate
en: Misthios! The Dagger knows we're here! We need to move fast! Hurry, misthios! Agapios and his brother are at the temple on the hill. Strike now! End The Dagger!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Dagger won't go down without a fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope Agapios hasn't done something stupid...

speaker: The Dagger thug 1
en: The misthios! Don't let them reach the temple.

speaker: The Dagger thug 2
en: The temple's off limits.

speaker: Civilian
en: But I promised my brother I'd

speaker: The Dagger thug 2
en: Leave now, before my very pleasant mood changes.

speaker: Agapios
en: Please Neritos, this isn't you.

speaker: Neritos
en: Oh, you know a lot about me, do you little Robin?

speaker: Agapios
en: I know who you were. My brother's not a killer.

speaker: Neritos
en: Then take a closer look. We are not who we were.

speaker: Agapios
en: So, this is what's become of my brother? You've clawed your way back from Hades, back to life, only to take the lives of others?

speaker: Neritos
en: Not from Hades, little Robin. From the ocean floor. Poseidon remained silent as I drowned. I saved me. ME. There are no gods—only mortals. Know that, and you'll know everything you need to rule this world.

speaker: Agapios
en: Not everyone wants to rule the world. Some of us just want to live in it.

speaker: Neritos
en: Ah, a misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kingfisher.

speaker: Agapios
en: No! His name's Neritos! He's not just some codename you can cross off! He's my brother! He's family!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Family is all that matters.

speaker: Agapios
en: Yes! Yes. No one has to die here.

speaker: Agapios
en: Listen, brother. Please.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Family or not, that man is the head of The Dagger. He's caused a lot of suffering. For that, no one gets a pass.

speaker: Kassandra
en: ...Not even pater.

speaker: Neritos
en: You've been a slave, brother. But the world is my slave. Its wonders. Its wine. Its people.

speaker: Neritos
en: We could be master's together. We were always meant to fly, little Robin.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Agapios! You can't trust the Kingfisher. Think of what he's done to our people. Think of the lives he's ruined!

speaker: Agapios
en: He's my brother! I can save him. I know I—I can save him. Please, master, misthios, there's no need for violence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know him better than anyone.

speaker: Agapios
en: When we first met, you said I could trust you. Thank you for trusting me.

speaker: Agapios
en: When we first met, you said nobody could be trusted. I'll never believe that. I can't live in that world.

speaker: Agapios
en: I trust him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope you're right.

speaker: Agapios
en: Neritos. Brother, remember when we were young when we'd run through the streets of Chalkis?

speaker: Neritos
en: Father chasing us...

speaker: Agapios
en: He couldn't catch little birds, so little birds we became.

speaker: Neritos
en: The Robin and the Kingfisher...

speaker: Agapios
en: We can be again. Skyros, and Euboea, and The Dagger... We can leave them all behind.

speaker: Neritos
en: And never return?

speaker: Agapios
en: We can fly.

speaker: Neritos
en: Then fly little Robin, fly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No!

speaker: Magistrate
en: Agapios!

speaker: Neritos
en: Goodbye, brother.

speaker: Neritos
en: The Dagger is mine! The Greek world is mine! No one will take that from me. Not my brother and not you, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look around you, Agapios. Skyros is already drowning in blood! Neritos brought violence to Euboea's shores long ago. We're past negotiating.

speaker: Agapios
en: When we first met, you said not all mercenaries were cutthroats. That I could trust you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So trust me now.

speaker: Agapios
en: When we first met, you said nobody could be trusted.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't have to trust me. Just don't trust him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's not the boy you remember. He's not Neritos.

speaker: Neritos
en: I always preferred "The Kingfisher".

speaker: Agapios
en: You have no right to that name. That belonged to my brother... and he's dead.

speaker: Agapios
en: ...I have no one.

speaker: Neritos
en: You have no one?! Who did I have?! I—I washed away, got lost at sea... But I found my way home. And what was there to welcome me? Father dead, and you... a slave. A SLAVE! I crawled out of the fucking ocean! I was strong, but you? You were the one who died, little brother. No, I had no one. So I made my own family. My brothers. The Dagger.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Misthios...

speaker: Agapios
en: Brother, no. No, don't do this!

speaker: Neritos
en: Perhaps you'd like to meet them?

speaker: Neritos
en: Kill the misthios!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Dagger ends, now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your brother...

speaker: Agapios
en: He made a choice. Years ago. Greed, power... If that's what freedom looks like, I'm better off a slave.

speaker: Magistrate
en: You're not a slave, Agapios. You're free.

speaker: Agapios
en: Free?! No—I abandoned you to look for my brother. I should be put to a miserable death or, or

speaker: Magistrate
en: You performed a great service for Euboea today. You've been doing that for years, my friend.

speaker: Agapios
en: Master, I don't deserve this...

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've worked, and fought, and sacrificed for your nation. Take a malákas reward when it's offered to you!

speaker: Agapios
en: Yes, sound advice, misthios. Then let my first step as a free man be this—I will remain in Euboea. She needs me, and I need her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You might've been granted freedom, but you'll never be truly free, Agapios. You have duties and responsibilities, to the Magistrate, to Euboea, even to your brother. Some shadows cannot be outrun.

speaker: Agapios
en: Perhaps I'll never truly feel like a free man... but that doesn't mean I can't be a good man. I'll stay here. My brother deserves a proper goodbye, if nothing else.

speaker: Magistrate
en: With the Kingfisher... removed and The Dagger's leadership eliminated, Euboea is safe.

speaker: Magistrate
en: That's not something we'll forget. Thank you, Hero of Euboea.

speaker: Agapios
en: Most of my life, I begged for the gods to bring my brother back. Instead, they gave me a man who took my brother's name. As for the boy, he can never return.

speaker: Magistrate
en: I can't thank you enough for saving Euboea and Agapios.

speaker: Magistrate
en: Agapios, my oldest friend... I never should have let you go. Why did I let you go...?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You gave Agapios a great gift. He got to be free for a moment.

speaker: Magistrate
en: "A moment." I suppose that's all any of us ever gets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You never should have let him chase after his brother. That was a death sentence! You were his master, his friend! It was your duty to protect him!

speaker: Magistrate
en: I know! I know. I have no sons, misthios. No daughters. Agapios was all the family I had.

speaker: Magistrate
en: With the Kingfisher dead and his lieutenants crushed, The Dagger's done. Euboea's free thanks to you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hope it was worth the price.

speaker: Magistrate
en: It's freedom. It's always worth the price. Chaire, Hero of Euboea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, what's next?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: The play was a great success, as I knew it would be. With that and the proof you presented at the Pnyx, Kleon has lost much of his popularity.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Now he heads to Amphipolis in an effort to redeem himself.

speaker: Civilian
en: Kassandra! Brasidas sent me to find you. He's alive and well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is he now?

speaker: Civilian
en: Amphipolis. They're preparing for battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you reach him before I do, tell him I'm on the way.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So what are you going to do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kleon dies now. This is our chance.

speaker: Sokrates
en: The plan is already working. Death shouldn't be brought early, even to someone like Kleon.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's exactly the type death should come early to. Not all who live deserve to grow old, Sokrates.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And you decide who deserves it?

speaker: Kassandra
en: This time I do.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then safe travels.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas needs my help. I plan on giving it to him. Though should our paths cross, I won't hesitate to kill Kleon.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Whatever you decide, remember he is only a man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't promise anything.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Be safe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Look at that. Father of the Minotaur.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast Slayer, I'm glad to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The bull put up quite a fight, but his pelt is yours.

speaker: Daphnae
en: You are remarkable!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Years of training made me a warrior. Life as a misthios has honed those abilities.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Then at the least you should applaud yourself for your dedication to your... art.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No more than the bull. The gods have blessed us with a world of wonder, and we should honor it.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Spoken like a true Daughter of Artemis.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never seen such a monster! This beast isn't even native to these lands.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast Slayer, I'm glad to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, the hyena's pelt. Take it. These flea-ridden carrion eaters disgust me!

speaker: Daphnae
en: We must learn to see the beauty in all things.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right. It's just an animal, doing what's in its nature.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Aren't we all?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, not in something like this, that feeds off the dead!

speaker: Daphnae
en: It is part of the cycle of life. All things die, and it's not as if we don't feast on dead flesh.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sculptor has truly captured the beauty of Aphrodite.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Got it!

speaker: Aletheia
en: Once more, Keeper. I ask you to return to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's Aletheia - must be close to finishing my trials of the Staff. I'll find her.

speaker: Aletheia
en: We're nearing the end of your journey, Keeper. You and the Staff are nearly connected. Are you ready to proceed?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready. Let's go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aristaios. Found you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like I missed a fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Pater...

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Kassandra! What are you doing here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came to kill him.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: He wouldn't have been a challenge for you.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: But I'm glad our paths have crossed again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never thought I'd see you again. What have you been doing?

speaker: Nikolaos
en: You made me realize in Megaris that I lost my honor long ago. There's no way to go back and make it up to you, but I can fulfill my promise to Stentor now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is the last place I expected to find you.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I left Stentor with the greatest responsibility a man could carry. I couldn't leave him to face it alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How thoughtful.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Killing these champions will weaken the Athenian hold on the region and destroy the rebels' morale.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leaving Stentor to pick up the pieces in Megaris was a mistake.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I couldn't stay, not after what happened. I wasn't fit for command.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Neither is Stentor, but he isn't running from it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You came all this way to help Stentor? Good. He needs it.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: It's about time I started protecting those I care about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're right.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: You've changed so much.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is who I've always been. You just weren't there to see it.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I'll never be able to change that, but I can do something now for someone who needs me. There are things Stentor must hear to succeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've done enough damage. You should stay away.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I understand. He must follow his own path. Good hunting, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wish you'd helped me back in Sparta. But Stentor does need help now, even if he doesn't want to admit it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stentor is as much your family as I am. You can still be there for him.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He may hate me, but I'm glad to have met him... in a way.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Goodbye, Kassandra of Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like I missed a fight.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There stalks the mighty hunter.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This hut must be Nesaia's. I guess she prefers the quiet of the forest over living in the city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This fire's fresh, and the food still simmering. Nesaia can't be far away.

speaker: Kassandra
en: These tracks don't look human. They lead away from the camp to the north.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There stalks the mighty hunter.

speaker: Unknown
en: Eagle Bearer. Well met. I see you got my note. I'm surprised I'm still alive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That could change.

speaker: Unknown
en: Hasty. No need to be hasty, Eagle Bearer. Let me introduce myself. My name is Gergis, the last Magi of the Order. I've been eager to meet you, Kassandra. May I call you as such?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't really care what you call me.

speaker: Gergis
en: Confident. I like that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Only my friends can call me Kassandra.

speaker: Gergis
en: We may become friends yet—who's to say?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give me one good reason not to put my blade through your throat. Where is Amorges? Where is my son?

speaker: Gergis
en: I have the answers you seek, Kassandra. I know what happened in Achaia—in the village called Dyme.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Dyme? What do you know? Tell me.

speaker: Gergis
en: I was there. Things are never what they seem. Your reality is limited to what you perceive. Ride with me. I've been wanting to speak to you.

speaker: Gergis
en: I'll show you how beautiful our world can be. Shall we?

speaker: Kassandra
en: One wrong move

speaker: Gergis
en: I understand. This way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where are you taking me?

speaker: Gergis
en: Somewhere nice. I want to learn more about you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't trust you.

speaker: Gergis
en: I've followed your journey from the beginning. I've written quite a bit about you, actually. In fact, some of my most popular work is about the Eagle Bearer. In addition, I've heard of your tales from our friends.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Kosmos? I didn't think the Cult made friends.

speaker: Gergis
en: Allies then, if you prefer.

speaker: Gergis
en: I've written many stories scattered across the Greek world. I spread the word of our doings, of our heroic deeds.

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Heroic"? You call murdering innocents and burning villages "heroic"?

speaker: Gergis
en: Narrow. The Order sees things from a broader perspective. We do not seek ephemeral peace. Our work is eternal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka.

speaker: Gergis
en: Look around us—such promise! You must be wondering why we hunt you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've killed enough of you to have an idea.

speaker: Gergis
en: You're a force of nature, Kassandra. Have you noticed? Danger is drawn to you like vultures to a battlefield. And so we simply cannot allow you to exist.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You would kill someone because of their blood? You disgust me.

speaker: Gergis
en: We're not the enemy. Have you considered yourself? In our eyes you are the manifestation of turmoil, the disruptor of peace. Don't be so quick to judge, Kassandra. There are many perspectives.

speaker: Gergis
en: We've arrived. Look at that view!

speaker: Gergis
en: Messenia. Quite a beauty, isn't she?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Get to the point.

speaker: Gergis
en: I know what happened in Dyme. How Natakas died. Are you brave enough to hear the truth?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to know everything.

speaker: Gergis
en: We saw no one at the beach that day—no Natakas, no child, They had escaped. Or so we thought... until we heard a cry. It was coming from a ship, wrecked on the shore—the soft but unmistakable cry of a child.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Elpidios...

speaker: Gergis
en: There was nowhere to run. Natakas tried to resist, but... it was futile. The baby was all that remained.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will find Amorges

speaker: Gergis
en: I'm sure he would expect you to try.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know all I need to—Natakas is gone.

speaker: Gergis
en: Some tales are better left untold.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you want from me?

speaker: Gergis
en: Our stories are written by a rare few who have the power to shape them. It's not every day I can speak to someone like you. There are no absolutes, Kassandra. Not even with Tainted Ones. You are fire—born with the potential to destroy, but also to warm, to cast a light in the dark.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A warmth you tried to destroy.

speaker: Gergis
en: People die, Kassandra. Eventually, we'll all be forgotten—fading away like a distant dream. Our actions, however, if they are meaningful, will be remembered. Tell me, what do you want to be remembered for?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to be remembered as someone who never backed down from a fight, even if the odds were stacked against them.

speaker: Gergis
en: Insight. Such wonderful insight. Thank you. And now, we must part. The question is, will you allow me to leave with my life?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to be remembered as someone who helps others in need.

speaker: Gergis
en: Insight. Such wonderful insight. Thank you. And now, we must part. The question is, will you allow me to leave with my life?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I want to be remembered as a misthios who knows no mercy and strikes fear into their enemies' hearts.

speaker: Gergis
en: Insight. Such wonderful insight. Thank you. And now, we must part. The question is, will you allow me to leave with my life?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't let you live—not now, not ever.

speaker: Gergis
en: We are what we choose. I will live and die by my choices. Know this—you cannot stop the Order. Even in our deaths, we live on. We are everywhere, now and in the future. It was a pleasure to meet you, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave, before I change my mind.

speaker: Gergis
en: Your baby. Elpidios. He's safe. That much I can tell you.

speaker: Gergis
en: It was a pleasure to meet you, Kassandra. The next time we meet will likely be the last.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Natakas... Elpidios... I'm sorry.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Over here! Help me, please. Save me. Please, get me out of here.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Thank you. My legs... You'll have to carry me.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Thank you... I need to get to my ship. I'll reward you well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have a ship?

speaker: Onomakles
en: Yes. I came inland to meet an associate. You might have seen him... He enjoyed Spartan hospitality at the end of a rope.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Heremos? I was sent to rescue him.

speaker: Onomakles
en: We can still complete the mission if you help me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me who you are.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Captain Onomakles. I'm on an urgent mission. I need to get out of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spartan patrols could find us at any moment.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Agreed. We need to get to my ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get you to your ship. Just point me in the right direction.

speaker: Onomakles
en: It's on the coast... Just south of Marathon Beach.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's so important about this ship?

speaker: Onomakles
en: It's not the ship, but its cargo. It must reach its destination.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then what's the cargo?

speaker: Onomakles
en: I'm not ungrateful for your help, but it's better you don't know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why's that?

speaker: Onomakles
en: Just believe me. What we do is for the security and future of Athens. This mission must succeed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My payment relies on it. So trust me, it will.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Seems your crew met the same fate as you.

speaker: Onomakles
en: I don't blame Heremos for talking. Spartans lack the most basic empathy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay here. I'll kill the Spartans, destroy their ships, and free your crew.

speaker: Onomakles
en: You've done Athens a great service. On my return I will make sure to acknowledge it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, you did mention payment.

speaker: Onomakles
en: More than that, you will have earned the favor of some powerful people when they hear of what you've done.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I hear it's useful to have powerful friends.

speaker: Onomakles
en: The way the world is now, you need them more than ever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Onomakles
en: I've said enough, and my ship awaits. Thank you again, misthios. I hope we'll meet again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not interested in who I impress. I just want my drachmae.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Take it, but I know you have a heart in there somewhere. Remember, you didn't have to save me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can think what you like. My purse is still heavier than it was.

speaker: Onomakles
en: Chaire, misthios.

speaker: Kleon
en: You took far longer than I expected.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There were... complications.

speaker: Kleon
en: In what way?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your messenger was dead by the time I arrived, but I was able to free the captain, and the ship sailed. So I still did the job.

speaker: Kleon
en: Poor Heremos... but I should be thankful for your initiative.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You don't seem very concerned about "poor Heremos".

speaker: Kleon
en: Every struggle has its sacrifice. Heremos played his part well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's in Mytilene that's so important?

speaker: Kleon
en: People. We need as many allies as we can gather.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was more than I bargained for.

speaker: Kleon
en: You'll be amply compensated. You have done me and the people a huge service. One day you will see your part in this great work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There he is.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This was definitely poison, and Alkibiades wasn't the only victim.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The truce is fragile enough...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This food smells strange, but it's not rotten.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This proves it, poison! It must have been added to the food and wine.

speaker: Banquet Supply List
en: This is a grocery list addressed to Priam of assorted foods that were at the banquet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hmm, a supply list for the celebration... and the merchant's name. Time to pay this Priam a visit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now we're going to have a conversation.

speaker: Priam
en: Please, please, I was just doing what I was told.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Now you'll do what I tell you.

speaker: Priam
en: Please, I thought we were just trying to make them slow—you know, so they lose. Win a few drachmae...

speaker: Kassandra
en: My friend Alkibiades may already be dead, and you're talking about drachmae.

speaker: Priam
en: The golden boy? I was there. He didn't have much—if you can get him the antidote, he'll survive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where it is.

speaker: Priam
en: They're sure to have it at Fort Koroibos. A man there paid me to do this. Look there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whoever did this will pay, but I'll take care of you first.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whoever did this will pay. Go, and don't let me see your face again.

speaker: Priam
en: Yes, thank you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your actions could cost Alkibiades his life. Now you will pay with yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not after you. I'm after whoever wanted this done.

speaker: Priam
en: I don't know, I never saw him. I just thought he wanted to fix a race, but then I saw what started happening and I knew they'd been poisoned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My friend Alkibiades—I need to save him.

speaker: Priam
en: You'll like find the antidote up at Fort Koroibos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whoever did this will pay, but I'll take care of you first.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whoever did this will pay. Go, and don't let me see your face again.

speaker: Priam
en: Yes, thank you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the antidote.

speaker: Antidote
en: A strange, oily liquid that has a pungent aroma with hints of garlic and herbs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here, I have the antidote.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Ugh, more wine please, to wash away the taste.

speaker: Barnabas
en: A treatment worthy of Hippokrates!

speaker: Alkibiades
en: I can already feel my stamina returning...

speaker: Barnabas
en: Didn't you have one last fight in the pankration?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's go.

speaker: Priestess
en: Thank the gods! Misthios, I need your help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's the problem?

speaker: Priestess
en: We've been ravaged by storms and rough seas! Poseidon is angry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you tried making an offering?

speaker: Priestess
en: A simple offering isn't enough to appease him! We need to perform a ritual... but we can't do it without our ceremonial axe.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like you need to find that axe for Poseidon.

speaker: Priestess
en: I do, but not for Poseidon—for Swordfish.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There are hundreds of axes around—just use another.

speaker: Priestess
en: But the Arkalochori Axe was crafted for this very purpose!

speaker: Kassandra
en: To appease the gods?

speaker: Priestess
en: The gods? Swordfish would have me fed to the sharks before Poseidon could punish me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Swordfish? Who's that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Swordfish... tell me more about him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You won't be seeing Swordfish for a while.

speaker: Priestess
en: It's true, no one has seen him for ages. He lives in the shadows—all around us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Whatever you say, priestess.}}}}

speaker: Kassandra
en: This? You call this an axe? It could barely shave a man's beard.

speaker: Priestess
en: The Arkalochori Axe! Thank the gods. Swordfish will be pleased. Let me look more closely...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not so fast.

speaker: Priestess
en: What do you want, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What I'm owed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The axe was yours to begin with. Take it.

speaker: Priestess
en: You had me worried, misthios. Thank you, I owe you my life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I want with it. It's mine now.

speaker: Priestess
en: You'd let someone die for your greed? Watch yourself, maláka, your head looks like it would fetch a pretty price.

speaker: Priestess
en: He's the one who ordered us to conduct this ritual every month. He runs the fish market— I can't say any more. No one talks about Swordfish and gets away with it, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I insist?

speaker: Priestess
en: Then I insist you retrieve the axe for me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You insist?

speaker: Priestess
en: N-no! "Politely request." And of course there'll be plenty of drachmae for your help, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you know where the axe is?

speaker: Priestess
en: Bandits took it! There's a cave east of town. If you follow the path along the shoreline, I'm sure you'll find them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go take a look.

speaker: Priestess
en: ...And don't swing it around! It's a delicate, ceremonial axe!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Here we are.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the axe... Doesn't look like it could cut anything.

speaker: Priestess
en: Need something else to find that axe, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is this Swordfish you want to impress?

speaker: Priestess
en: He'll kill me if I tell you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And I'll kill you if you don't.

speaker: Priestess
en: Swordfish has always run the fish market with an iron fist—charges the fishermen fees. If they don't pay up... the sharks eat well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Point me in Swordfish's direction.

speaker: Priestess
en: I don't know where he is. No one's seen him for years, misthios. Some think he's dead. Just last week, some fishermen boldly said we should no longer pay fees to a dead man... Guess who's dead now?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take my chances. Where is he?

speaker: Priestess
en: He used to live at Fisherman's Beacon to the north—you could try your luck there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Remind me where Swordfish is.

speaker: Priestess
en: Try your luck at Fisherman's Beacon to the north—he used to live there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This axe would fetch a good price at the agora.

speaker: Priestess
en: No! You can't sell it. Give it back—I'll pay you. Take all the drachmae I have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The axe was yours to begin with. Take it.

speaker: Priestess
en: You had me worried, misthios. Thank you, I owe you my life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I want with it. It's mine now.

speaker: Priestess
en: You'd let someone die for your greed? Watch yourself, maláka, your head looks like it would fetch a pretty price.}}}}

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you fear Swordfish?

speaker: Priestess
en: Everyone does, misthios. He's not to be trifled with. Once, he took a man's nose off for sneezing in his presence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Quite the reputation...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This axe would fetch a good price at the agora.

speaker: Priestess
en: No! You can't sell it. Give it back—I'll pay you. Take all the drachmae I have.

en: The axe was yours to begin with. Take it.

speaker: Priestess
en: You had me worried, misthios. Thank you, I owe you my life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll do what I want with it. It's mine now.

speaker: Priestess
en: You'd let someone die for your greed? Watch yourself, maláka, your head looks like it would fetch a pretty price.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The size of it... That's no ordinary wolf!

speaker: Daphnae
en: Beast Slayer, I'm glad to see you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The pelt of the Lykaon Wolf.

speaker: Daphnae
en: A wolf is not only a vicious predator, but a cunning adversary. Many have fallen before it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll come to expect this from me. The impossible made possible.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If I fall for something, it won't be a beast, but someone here on Chios.

speaker: Daphnae
en: Don't talk of falling here. Rather think of ascending... to new heights.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll return when I have more pelts.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Help! Please!

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Please, dear gods, can anyone help? Those artless swine have ruined me! Ruined!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Divine winds have brought your cries to me. Tell me what you need.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Amazing! Please, friend, filthy bandits attacked me and stole all of my belongings. My tools are worthless to them, but invaluable to me. I am ruined unless you help!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I find the gods leave us to fend for ourselves. Tell me what you need, and maybe I can help you.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: True enough. You look like you can handle yourself. Filthy swine stole my prized tools, though they are worthless to them. I am ruined, unless you can help me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Point me towards these thieves, and I will bring the heavens down upon them!

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Praise Zeus! I am the artist, Polykleitos. Hunt down the bandits and recover my prized tools. Wait... what is your name, misthios?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am called Kassandra.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: By the gods... could it be true?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: No, nothing! Please, recover my tools and I'll see you rewarded.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found your tools.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: I can't believe it! Maybe you really are from Olympos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, I am of the blood of Olympos.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Amazing, maybe those villagers from Linou Farm had it right. That is where I'm going now, and I could use an escort.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, my friend. I am flesh and blood like you.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Oh well, at least those villagers from Linou Farm pay well. I need to get there safely. If you escort me, I'm sure they will treat you lavishly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about this village?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Linou is a small region of devout villagers and farmers. Hard-working people. Very serious in their beliefs. They hired me to make them a sculpture of, well, the Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Really. Why?

speaker: Polykleiptos
en: They know your name and your deeds, and believe you to be their savior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did you think I carried the blood of Olympos in my veins?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Your reputation proceeds you. And the villagers of Linou can't stop talking about you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lead me to Linou Farm. I'll make sure you get there safely.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Excellent. I'm sure they will honor you with gifts and riches.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then let's go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you learn of this village?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: My doctrine on beauty is renowned. Village priestesses came to my home in Argos and begged me to come and fashion a figure for them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You came all the way from Argos?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: They offered good drachmae. It's not easy being an artist, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And what is the statue going to look like when you are done?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Well, you, I suppose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: They worship the Eagle Bearer. They told me lots of stories. A pretty fair description, though I expected you to be taller. And to have a smaller nose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This theory of yours, who determines what is beautiful?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Math.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Math?

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Exactly. Beauty is an equation derived from the commensurability of all the parts of the body. From finger to finger. Fingers to the palm and wrist. Those to the forearm, and the forearm to the upper arm, and like that to include the whole of the body.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh. Math.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Gratitude, friend. You saved my hide. And you've given me great reference. Let us talk to the Priestess Hexione and be properly welcomed!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Good Polykleitos! You made it!

speaker: Polykleitos
en: Priestess Hexione, my journey was a test from the gods... but look what miracle they have delivered!

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Who is this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am Kassandra.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: The misthios you told me about! She appeared like a bolt from Zeus and rescued me from road bandits.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: The Eagle Bearer... This is an unexpected honor!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Glad to visit. Uh, how have you heard of me?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Certainly you jest! Your deeds are carried along the winds and sung through the stars. We are but a poor village, but your being here gives us hope to cling to in this hard world.

speaker: Polykleitos
en: And soon there will be a statue to capture a hint of your glory.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: To have our patron walk among us and give us divine fortune is a wonder. We will be eternally blessed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You do me a great honor. I am pleased to walk among your people.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Oh thank you, Eagle Bearer! There are many humble servants here who could benefit from your attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me their names.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are giving me honors I don't deserve. I am just happy I could help Polykleitos.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Great and humble is the Eagle Bearer! There are many lowly servants in our village who could benefit from a kind word from someone of your grace.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Uh, who are they?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: There is the shepherdess, Heriphile. You can find her near the stables, south of here. Akatos, the hunter, who has a small house on the west end of the village. And Menalkas, a young farmer. His fields are to the east.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who is the shepherdess, and what's her story?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Heriphile tends a small herd of goats. Recently she had a scare in the forest and lost two of her flock to wolves.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What can you tell me about the hunter?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Akatos is worried he cannot provide for the village since he recently injured himself. Perhaps you could ease his fears.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Priestess, who is the farmer?

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Menalkas fears he is cursed. A visit from the Eagle Bearer could restore his faith and purpose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will see what I can do for your people.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: Not my people, divine Eagle Bearer. We priestesses are but humble servants of your exalted greatness. When you have spoken to them, find me.

speaker: Priestess Hexione
en: My sisters and I want to prepare a proper celebration for your portentous visitation.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: Ah, you are a welcome sight. Your beauty brings light into the darkness of what has become my life.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: It's good to see you too, Phidias.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: Now this is important. No one saw you come here did they?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: No... Why?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: You're sure you weren't followed. Good, good. They're out there, though. Watching, waiting...

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's after you?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: The Cult of Kosmos. Remember Athens? They never stopped hunting me, Kassandra.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would they be after you now?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: They want me dead. Moving me here has only bought a little more time. I need your help.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: What makes you think you're in trouble now?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: The other day I received a scytale, and a note.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone left you a piece of wood and a letter... I can see why you're frightened.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: Oh, it's so much more than that.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: What's so special about a stick?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: It's not just any stick! The is used by the Spartans to send coded messages.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: OK, so let's talk about your stick.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: Scytale!

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, scytale.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: I need to get the code. Then I'll show you how it works.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: What did the message say?

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: Look to your art... The king of gods has a message to impart.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Kassandra
en: Fantastic, that's not a message. It's barely passable as a riddle!

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist
speaker: Phidias
en: It's obvious, the king of gods.

scene: The Message, the Stick, and the Artist

en: I'll bring back Aphrodite's Ore.

en: Amazing! I'll ready the molds.

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: Are you sure you would not prefer to spend your shiny drachmae

speaker: Kassandra
en: We fight.

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: Then let the crushing begin!

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: You should have bought my Token, yes? Very good price! Now you must pay a new price... DEATH. I will use your bones to pick your other bones from my teeth.

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: UGH! This isn't what winning feels like...! Crush, crush, crush...

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: What—what am I feeling? What is this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The shame of defeat.

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: This is defeat?

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: ...Winning is better, yes. The Token of Strength is yours. Have a wonderful day—and please don't hit me again.

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: My favorite bones! You have crushed them to dust INSIDE of my skin. You ARE a champion, yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no need for unnecessary bloodshed. I'll pay for your Token.

speaker: Pre-Trial Master of Strength
en: A wise choice, my spineless friend. May you one day slither out from under the metaphoric rock of your cowardice!

speaker: Token of Strength
en: This Token is acquired by completing the Pre-Trail of Strength in Lato, proving one's worthiness to fight the great Minotaur.

speaker: Civilian
en: Are we on break now? My legs are actually starting to cramp. Uhh... Is it break time yet? I feel like my legs will be actually crushed if I stay here any longer...

speaker: Priest
en: If you're here for your purification bath, you'll have to come back another time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for information.

speaker: Priest
en: In that case you can go straight to Hades.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to know about a Spartan woman who came through here many years ago.

speaker: Priest
en: Did that eagle of yours shit in your ears? I'm under strict orders not to talk to any mercenaries. Especially not about Spartan women or injured babies.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My eagle will tear out your tongue, priest!

speaker: Priest
en: Forgive me! Not the tongue! Not like Mydon! Chrysis threatened anyone who speaks to the Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did she? Tell me about the woman and her baby, and I won't drown you in your bathhouse. How's that for a threat?

speaker: Priest
en: Please no! There's already a corpse in there!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I never mentioned a baby.

speaker: Priest
en: Think you're so smart. Many women pass through with babies. Now leave me. I have my own problems to deal with.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe I can help you.

speaker: Priest
en: Snakes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Snakes.

speaker: Priest
en: They're everywhere! Must have escaped from the tholos. We keep them for treatments, but they invaded the bathhouse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The snakes killed someone?

speaker: Priest
en: A patient was purifying himself when they slithered in. Turns out he's terrified of snakes. Fell over dead. Now the snakes have made him their home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What if I took care of your snake problem... Would you talk to me then?

speaker: Priest
en: Oh most definitely. The purification bath is crucial in the path towards healing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does taking a bath have to do with healing the sick?

speaker: Priest
en: Asklepios only visits the dreams of the pure. When the sick arrive, they offer sacrifice, cleanse their bodies in the bathhouse. Only then do we let them rest in the abaton, where Asklepios appears and heals them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did all these snakes get loose? And why are there so many at the sanctuary?

speaker: Priest
en: Blame Doreios. He's supposed to keep them in the tholos. Patients with afflictions of the mind are healed by the snakes. Their tongues are like kisses from the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll clear out these snakes in no time. Ikaros could use a good feast.

speaker: Priest
en: Try not to kill them. Doreios will be furious if his sacred snakes get chopped to bits.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then how am I supposed to deal with them?

speaker: Priest
en: Snakes are drawn to the bath's heat. Flood them with cold water, and they'll slither back to their hole. There's an underground pipe that may help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll take care of your snake problem. Then you'll tell me what I need to know.

speaker: Timoxenos
en: Greeting young one. Come to offer Asklepios a sacrifice?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, but I'm searching for a Spartan mother who may have.

speaker: Timoxenos
en: The great goddess Hera guides many mothers to this sacred place. Surely I'm too feeble to remember them all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are these stone slabs for?

speaker: Timoxenos
en: These are records. We document all who pass through—their illnesses, treatments—so that the glory of Asklepios can be celebrated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then I don't need your memory. I just need to find the right stone.

speaker: Timoxenos
en: Um, yes, of course. That's very wise, indeed. If only I had the time to help you...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen, I'm not here to hurt you. I'm just looking for my mater.

speaker: Timoxenos
en: It's Chrysis. She's got every priest in the sanctuary under her thumb, and she'll squash anyone who feeds information to the Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then don't tell me anything—just bring me to the stone that can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mother came through here, and unless you want me to paint these stones with your blood, you'll tell me what you know.

speaker: Timoxenos
en: Please... It's Chrysis. She said that anyone who talks to the Eagle Bearer will be paying a visit to Hades.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then don't talk. Just bring me to the stone that can.

speaker: Timoxenos
en: Follow me, then. Quickly, we must be discreet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Priest
en: May Asklepios spare her from suffering.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Will she live?

speaker: Priest
en: Not unless the gods hear our prayers. Many sick Athenians have arrived in Argolis recently, and very few have left. This poor girl has the same sickness.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is there anything I can do to help?

speaker: Priest
en: I was warned of the Eagle Bearer. "Wants nothing but drachmae for blood," I was told.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're wasting time, priest. We can discuss what I want when this sick girl's needs are taken care of.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for information about a Spartan woman who came through here.

speaker: Priest
en: I was warned about the Eagle Bearer. "A ruthless killer," she was called.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you think it's wise to deny a "ruthless killer" the information she desires?

speaker: Priest
en: Healing the sick is my path. Help me get the attention of the gods, and I'll tell you what I can.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you asking exactly?

speaker: Priest
en: Her illness seems to have no cure, and it's spreading. Our sacrifices have done little to draw the attention of the gods. Pigs, goats—all have fallen on deaf ears. We need a beast whose blood will ignite these flames for Asklepios to see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did you have in mind?

speaker: Priest
en: There is a bull with skin as white as snow roaming the sanctuary outskirts. Head west of here towards the coast. Bring it to me alive, and we'll offer a sacrifice the gods cannot ignore. I'm touched you would help these people. But I know why you're really here. Chrysis made all priests swear oaths to seal our lips in the face of the eagle-bearing misthios, or forfeit our lives. But I serve the gods and the sick. My oaths are to them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The outskirts are vast. Could you be more specific about the location of the bull?

speaker: Priest
en: Last I heard it was grazing on Mount Koryphum, near the Asine Ruins.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you're just going to slit its throat, why do you need the bull alive?

speaker: Priest
en: But we're not just going to slit its throat. First, we pour water on its head. If it nods, we may proceed. Gods, mortals, and animals—all must be willing participants in a sacrifice, or it is impure. To save this many people, we will need the beast's blood, bones, and fat.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me about Chrysis. She has everyone terrified.

speaker: Priest
en: We taught her everything we knew about healing, about the gods. Then she found new teachers. People in masks. They changed her. Turned her heart black. They became her gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find this bull for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spying on those Athenians is no easy task, Spartan. Anything I can do to help?

speaker: Man
en: You, traitor! You deserved to be killed for killing our general, Stentor of Sparta.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I did kill Stentor. He left me no choice.

speaker: Man
en: I knew it was you! I'll do what the Spartan soldiers should have done at camp!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The man you speak of was my brother.

speaker: Man
en: Oh, I had no idea. My condolences, misthios. Maybe I confused you with someone else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe you did.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't know anyone named Stentor. You must be thinking of someone else.

speaker: Man
en: I thought I heard that the misthios that killed him had an eagle or something... Maybe I was wrong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe you were.

speaker: Man
en: Come to think of it... I did hear of another strange mercenary who arrived here recently. He must be the real traitor!

speaker: Kassandra
en: And you want me to kill this mercenary.

speaker: Man
en: His blood must be spilled.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll handle this.

speaker: Man
en: Good. Please be quick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Man
en: You again. Have you killed him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you, mercenary. Now, your reward.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Happy to help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis' troops should be strong enough to take Persephone down. I should let him know.

speaker: Adonis
en: I've had scouts looking everywhere for you. I didn't think to check Persephone's throne room.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course you didn't. And thanks to me, Persephone blames Hekate. We have the advantage.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You should be thanking me. Persephone knows what we're doing. She's prepared.

speaker: Adonis
en: That so? Then we need to strike, and we need to do it now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: For Aphrodite.

speaker: Adonis
en: And for your freedom to breach the gate out of this realm.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Adonis, I'm sure you're a fine warrior, but we're facing gods.

speaker: Adonis
en: Nothing will happen to either of us. You will be my shield, and I'll be yours.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All right, muster your troops. We're going to battle.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're marching against gods. Give me some time to prepare.

speaker: Adonis
en: We take the fight to Persephone, and we do it now. Ready your staff.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Before we fight, I have something for you.

speaker: Adonis
en: What's this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: One of Hermes's keys to the eternal flame. If your craftspeople can make it, you'll be able to ignite fires that never go out. But Adonis, only use it if you absolutely must.

speaker: Leonidas
en: Paradise awaits! Fight for your freedom!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermes, you shouldn't be here.

speaker: Hermes
en: Where else would I be while the humans burn Elysium to the ground? My friend, help me protect her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have helped you. But nothing is going to stop this. The gate must open. After everything I've done for you... Please, Hermes, listen to me.

speaker: Hermes
en: We haven't had the easiest friendship, the Staff Keeper and Key Maker, but you've done so much for me. Together, we'll get Persephone to stand down.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Thank you. Let's go together.

speaker: Persephone
en: Stop.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You really think I'm going to protect Persephone? These rebels are here because of me.

speaker: Hermes
en: This is no time to joke. We're the Staff Keeper and Key Maker, bound by mysteries.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're not friends. We're not bound. I played you and her to get what I want.

speaker: Hermes
en: It was you this whole time? You let me worry about these delinquents... All my worry, all this suffering was because of you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I told you I'm getting to that gate whether Persephone likes it or not. Now get out of my way.

speaker: Hermes
en: I will not!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then today is the day the gods themselves fall to their knees before me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It doesn't have to be like this, Hermes.

speaker: Hermes
en: It could have been different between us. You were my friend, but you've given me no option. I have to protect the one I love.

speaker: Hermes
en: So, this is what friendship means to you?

speaker: Hermes
en: Pathetic! Your father would be disappointed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'd be disappointed in you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're no god.

speaker: Hermes
en: I will... not stop...

speaker: Persephone
en: Stop!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't get in my way!

en: It was you this whole time? You let me worry about these delinquents... All my worry, all this suffering, was because of you.

en: Stop!

en: Don't get in my way!

speaker: Hermes
en: Humiliating me wasn't enough? You have to destroy my home... my love?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hekate isn't here to save you this time. Stand down!

en: I will not!

en: I will... not stop...

speaker: Persephone
en: Stop!

speaker: Persephone
en: Pathetic. You have failed me for the last time, Hermes Trismegistus.

speaker: Hermes
en: P... Perseph...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hermes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's it. Persephone's control over Elysium needs to end. Now.

speaker: Persephone
en: You. Don't move a muscle.

speaker: Hekate
en: You're letting a human get in the way of our friendship.

speaker: Persephone
en: You let her get in the way. You should have told me yourself, but all I hear spouting from your mouth are lies. I've had enough! In fact, I'm going to do something about that.

speaker: Hekate
en: Don't.

speaker: Hekate
en: You were never fit to lead Elysium! And I hate your dress!

speaker: Persephone
en: Good luck manipulating anyone with your lies ever again. If I were you, I'd leave before I say anything else stupid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How did you do that?

speaker: Persephone
en: It comes naturally to me.

speaker: Hekate
en: Don't let her get away with anything. We're in this together. I'll always be at your service.

speaker: Persephone
en: Even outside of Elysium? If it comes to that?

speaker: Hekate
en: I'll be there. For now, I'll leave you two. I'm sure there's plenty to talk about.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're making a huge mistake.

speaker: Persephone
en: With war brewing outside my window, I wonder what you'd suggest I do instead.

speaker: Adonis
en: Your beautiful Elysium has turned to rubble, all because of your stubbornness, Persephone.

speaker: Persephone
en: You fool, I made this place beautiful for you! Nothing I've ever done for your love has been good enough.

speaker: Adonis
en: You're a prisoner too, you should know it's impossible to love your captor. This is the last time I'll ask. Let us go. Let me go.

speaker: Persephone
en: You've turned this whole realm against me—but you didn't do it alone. Go. Your friend here won't be as lucky.

speaker: Persephone
en: I do love you, Adonis. And true love is selfless. Go. Treat Aphrodite better than you ever treated me.

speaker: Adonis
en: Thank you, Persephone. I'm forever grateful. Go easy on Kassandra.

speaker: Persephone
en: Oh, dear. Didn't you hear? There's no reason for you to leave now. Aphrodite heard everything you've been up to in Elysium and she wants nothing to do with you.

speaker: Adonis
en: No. I—Please, Persephone.

speaker: Persephone
en: No one will look at you the way I once did ever again.

speaker: Adonis
en: What have you done to me?

speaker: Persephone
en: After you went and fucked this lowly mortal behind my back? I don't think so. All I asked from you was loyalty, and you couldn't deliver.

speaker: Adonis
en: No. I—Please, Persephone.

speaker: Persephone
en: No one will look at you the way I once did ever again.

speaker: Adonis
en: What have you done to me?

speaker: Persephone
en: Your turn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We don't have to do this. Just let me pass through Elysium. Adonis would've rallied the people with or without my help.

speaker: Persephone
en: You're lying!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What about your lies? You made me a promise if I brought you Leonidas.

speaker: Persephone
en: After everything you've done against me? Don't make me laugh. But once I'm finished with you, maybe you'll be with your loved ones after all.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Persephone you don't have to control everything. You're free to let go. Maybe you can finally go home.

speaker: Persephone
en: You know nothing of what I've been through.

speaker: Persephone
en: I was stolen from your world. I had no choice but to take this one for myself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Huh?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What?

speaker: Persephone
en: And this world is mine alone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ros? ...Good dog. Good dog.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: I picked up your message on the board. What's happening?

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: The hardest part of being a traveling merchant is all the travel. Er... I mean, you have to find a place to sleep. I came across a bandit camp and they let me stay there. Even shared their wine with me.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: But then they robbed you. Because they are bandits.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: I figured if I was giving them drachmae to stay in the camp, they wouldn't take my drachmae. It made sense at the time. I think. No more drinking wine at bandit camps.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to get it from the bandits?

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: No.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: All the bandits must die.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: What a relief.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll be back when everything's taken care of.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: You're back. Have you killed them?

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: I took care of them. Every last one.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Man
en: I'm a man of my word, so here's your reward.

scene: The Rent Is Too Cursed High
speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Sokrates
en: You made it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course I did.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Barnabas was ready to go after you again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Like he said, it's the thought that counts, right?

speaker: Sokrates
en: Apparently. Come, the others are waiting.

speaker: Herodotos
en: We were worried you wouldn't make it.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Especially with every Athenian guard looking for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Kleon will have to do more than that to stop me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's all this?

speaker: Hippokrates
en: We've begun working on a plan to take down Kleon.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Although I hardly call it a plan. Lots of talking, not much... action.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It feels different without Perikles.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: But his inspiration lives on—that's why we're here.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Where once we gathered to forget our problems, now we meet them head on.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: And get back to what trulymatters

speaker: Herodotos
en: To restore Athens to its former glory.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you're taking down Kleon. Tell me the plan.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: It won't be simple. His death would disrupt the peace and be worse for Athens.

speaker: Herodotos
en: He's right. We must discredit him first.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Aristophanes apparently has some play he thinks will do the job.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Some play? It is so much more than that.

speaker: Alkibiades
en: Oh, don't get your tunic in a twist. I just don't see why we can't all love each other. It's so much more fun that way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's so special about the play? Will your famous "Orange Ape" impression be making an appearance?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Ha! Funnily enough, that was the inspiration.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Isn't it a risk to show him in a bad light in front of his admirers?

speaker: Aristophanes
en: I think the play will change their minds. Good art is risky, but my plan will work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can't just sit around. Kleon is sending a boat to Mytilene to kill the people there.

speaker: Herodotos
en: The people trust Kleon. They'll vote for whatever action he puts forth.

speaker: Sokrates
en: But that does not mean we plan to do nothing.

speaker: Aristophanes
en: Taking down Kleon won't be easy.

speaker: Herodotos
en: But with your help, it will be possible.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Good thing you arrived, Kassandra. I'm still exhausted from the ambush at the jail.

speaker: Hippokrates
en: This act will avenge Perikles. I know he'd be proud.

speaker: Herodotos
en: It's all coming together. I think we have a real chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Incredible, Phidias was right. The artist has captured Poseidon in all his magnificence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Got it!

speaker: Aletheia
en: You're needed, Keeper. Your bond with the Staff is not yet complete. When you're ready, you must continue.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm ready, Aletheia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So this is the "secret" chamber... They're not ones for subtlety, are they?

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, this is it.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Hidden chamber of the Cultists. Here, all along.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going inside. Keep my clothes for me?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Best not to go in with your weapons either. I don't think they'll look too kindly on that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do I look?

speaker: Herodotos
en: Terrifying.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good.

speaker: Herodotos
en: Find me once you've found out the truth in there. Keep your wits about you. Try not to do anything rash.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Me? Rash?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who thought these ridiculous costumes were a good idea?

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: You're late, very late! It's a good thing Deimos hasn't arrived yet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sorry. It's my, er—first time.

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: A new recruit? Welcome, welcome.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a lot of people here.

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: All share our common mind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good.

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: We're here to evaluate the strides taken by the Cult since the last meeting. We haven't met for some, some time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where did they come from?

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: The land and across the seas. We assemble as a community. Here, there is no war—there are no sides.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You mentioned someone. Deimos. Who is that?

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: You'll learn his name very, very quickly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's our leader.

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: I'm sure he believes that, but no, he's our weapon. He's... difficult, but he does important work for us. I don't envy his position one bit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go talk to the others. Thank you.

speaker: Female Cultist 1
en: Yes, yes, before Deimos comes. Who knows if you'll get a word in after that.

speaker: Male Cultist 1
en: Alright then, highest bidder gets an Olympic match thrown in their favor.
