en: I've killed the first Cultist, Elpenor. A snake I met in Kephallonia. His mask and cloak will get me inside the chamber.

speaker: Herodotos
en: So they're underneath the Temple of Apollo... Yes, by the Cave of Gaia. I think I know the place.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Find it, and I'll meet you there.

speaker: Perseus
en: Kadmos and Bellerophon, lend me your might! You dare challenge the slayer of the Gorgon?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm not here to challenge you, Perseus. I need your help!

speaker: Perseus
en: My help must be earned!

speaker: Perseus
en: Zeus... Father! Descend and fight with me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Snap out of it, Perseus. We're allies, and I need your help. Go to the gates and protect this place.

speaker: Achilles
en: I don't want to fight you, challenger. Stand down! Put down your weapons or die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Achilles, the underworld is in chaos. Serve Hades and go to the gates!

speaker: Achilles
en: If you want me to be a servant, prove it!

speaker: Achilles
en: There's no honor in this. Stop!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Achilles, Hades need you. Go to the gates and guard them with your life.

speaker: Agamemnon
en: Ah, finally Hades has sent me a challenge. Bow before your true king!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll bow if you go to the gates and protect the underworld.

speaker: Agamemnon
en: Your blood is as sweet as a Trojan's!

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place needs a king, Agamemnon. Go to the gates and protect the people the way you do best.

speaker: Herakles
en: You're the one who killed Cerberos! Been a long time since I had a good fight!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herakles, I'm not here to fight you. I need you!

speaker: Herakles
en: I said fight!

speaker: Herakles
en: Respect, young one! You fight like an Argonaut!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Herakles, rise up and be a hero for Hades and for all the people in the underworld.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That must be the farm where Praxithea is being held prisoner.

speaker: Praxithea
en: Thank you, my child! We must get away from here. Could more bandits be coming? Please, let's get out of here.

speaker: Praxithea
en: Thank you for saving me, dear child.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't thank me, voice of Apollo. Or were those someone's words you spoke?

speaker: Praxithea
en: So you've met my grandson. You're right, I lied to everyone. I am so sorry... The gods should have killed me by now.

speaker: Praxithea
en: Instead, they made me live with my remorse.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did you spread lies? People trusted you. You were supposed to bring them the word of Apollo.

speaker: Praxithea
en: I didn't plan to, not when I was chosen to be the Oracle of Apollo. But I met people there who told me I must speak the words they asked. Or else my family would suffer for my disobedience.

speaker: Praxithea
en: Family? Do you remember telling a Spartan family that their younger child must die? A grieving mother with eyes like mine?

speaker: Praxithea
en: I am so sorry for what you have lost.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who wanted you kidnapped? These brutals didn't come up with the idea themselves.

speaker: Praxithea
en: Please don't ask me that. The ones who want to punish me now, the ones who told me what to say... They would burry you alive if I told you about them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The ones with masks and dark cloaks. The Cult of Kosmos.

speaker: Praxithea
en: Do not speak their name!

speaker: Lykaon
en: Grandmother...

speaker: Lykaon
en: Did she tell you? Is she the oracle who brought ruin on your family?

speaker: Praxithea
en: I'm sorry for what I've done. I accept my punishment. But please, don't let my grandson kill me. Lykaon's a good man, a healer. This would break him.

speaker: Lykaon
en: No. She's my responsibility. I must be the one to end her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you don't finish this, Lykaon, you won't be able to live with yourself. Go on, kill her.

speaker: Lykaon
en: I... I... I can't.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then this is where I leave. Live as a killer or live as a coward, Lykaon. I can't help you any more.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've killed enough people to know that violence has no end. Better to move on and make the best if the lives the gods have given you.

speaker: Lykaon
en: Move on? But you said Praxithea ruined your family...

speaker: Kassandra
en: She can do no more harm. Killing her for revenge won't change what happened. Besides, didn't you tell me something about hope?

speaker: Praxithea
en: Thank you for your mercy. I promise I will do good with what's left of my days.

speaker: Lykaon
en: You're right, Kassandra. I might not be able to forgive my grandmother, not right away. But she can go on with her life, and I with mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I think you've made the right decision, Lykaon.

speaker: Lykaon
en: How do you do this? Decide who lives and who dies?

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do you do it, Lykaon? All those lives depending on you, needing your healing and kindess.

speaker: Lykaon
en: I... I think I need you, Kassandra. Not to kill anybody or find anything. Just to stay with me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't stay forever. But for now, let me take care of you, healer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm no healer, but I think you've been through a lot, Lykaon. You don't need a misthios in your life. Go back home and be the physician you're meant to be.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're a healer, Lykaon, not a killer. I. am. You still have a hope of a better life beyond this.

speaker: Lykaon
en: No, Kassandra, I can

speaker: Kassandra
en: This woman betrayed the trust of the gods and of the people who seek their wisdom. In the name of all those betrayed by your false prophecies, oracle, I end your miserable life.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's dead.

speaker: Lykaon
en: You didn't have to, I could have done it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Probably. But you didn't have to. You get to be the honorable healer. I'm the misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's... my home on Kephallonia. How is this possible?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe? Phoibe!

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: Been a long time. Heard you and the girl finally came down to join us. Couldn't pass up the opportunity to show you both a warm Kephallonian welcome.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you hurt her...

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: If?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will cut out your other fucking eye. And this time it's going up your ass, Cyclops!

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: No one calls me that!

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: Give it to me.

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: Maybe I'll cut out one of your eyes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Come and try.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will make you suffer, Cyclops!

speaker: The Cyclops of Kephallonia
en: The way you let Phoibe suffer? Didn't think I heard about that, did you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe! No, no, no, no, no.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ela, ela. Earth, mother of all, I greet you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aniazo.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're OK!

speaker: Phoibe
en: And you're here.

speaker: Kasandra
en: I'll always be with you, Phoibe. Forever. No matter what.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Thank you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was here this time, Phoibe, but you have to be more careful. I don't know what I'd do if something happened to you.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I just wanted you to be proud of me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was with you in Athens, too. You just didn't see me.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I see you now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can you stand?

speaker: Phoibe
en: What is this place? And where is the Cyclops?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't worry, the Cyclops is gone. And this is a doorway to Elysium.

speaker: Phoibe
en: So that's it. Through there, I'll find my real parents.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can do this, Phoibe. Let's go.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Seeing this place makes me miss Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We had some good days, didn't we?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I don't want to go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have no choice, Phoibe. You belong with your parents.

speaker: Phoibe
en: No, I belong with you. Please, don't make me go.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe, growing up means doing things you don't want. But you do them anyway, because you're brave enough to do whats right.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Staying with you could be right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't be afraid. I'm leaving this place too once I finish what I started. But I will be with you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I found this. Take it with you... To keep me close.

speaker: Phoibe
en: What if... my parents don't like me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: If they don't like you, that's their problem. But you have to give them a chance to love you. And if they don't take it, then you'll make a new family, just like we did on Kephallonia.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course they're going to like you. They'll do more than like you. They'll love you.

speaker: Phoibe
en: But I won't be able to forget you. You're my family, too. Can I come back here and find you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are strong enough for this. Never doubt that. If you ever feel lonely, find that strength, and you'll be able to push through it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do you still have the water the Cyclops gave you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: When you've met your parents and you're ready, drink it. Forget me. Forget the pain. Start your new life with them—the one you deserve.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. Once you leave, you can never come back. But one day, a long time from now, I will come to you, and we'll tell each other all about our adventures.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You'll always be my family. No matter what. I think I'm ready.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe, the warrior who sailed to the golden fields. Phoibe, who plunged into the underworld to save her family. Phoibe, the Eagle Bearer. You have made me so proud.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Walk tall.

speaker: Hades
en: I told you she wouldn't let the kid lose her memories.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Instead, she drew out the child's own strength and inspired her to endure her burden. Remarkable.

speaker: Hades
en: I still can't believe she told the kid to drink Lethe's water.

speaker: Poseidon
en: Her willingness to suffer alone is... remarkable.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why would Brasidas's shield be in a place for dishonored warriors? He was the most honorable warrior I knew. It doesn't make sense.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The door is locked. I need to find a way in. These symbols might be the key to opening the door. There are too many possibilities. Maybe there's and answer deeper in the tomb.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sands of time. Wonder what that means?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Is that a symbol for the mind? Memories perhaps?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Water...People drink Lethe's water here in the underworld to forget. Water, time, the mind. It's another riddle. I should return to the door.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course. This is the underworld. Drink the water, it makes you forget, your time spent living is lost. Clever.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Three shields. Now, which one belongs to Brasidas?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas's Shield.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your shield, General.

speaker: Brasidas
en: I'll never forget the day this was first handed to me. I was a boy, it was as tall as I was. My commander told me, To hold this is to hold up Sparta. Drop it, and Sparta falls.

speaker: Brasidas
en: Tell me what Elysium's like.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It isn't what you think. It's...Do you feel cold?

speaker: Hades
en: Elysium is boring.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not since I showed up.

speaker: Hades
en: Ah yes. You do have a knack for livening things up wherever you go.

speaker: Hades
en: Still dreaming of paradise I see. Well, no one wants you to get what you deserve more than me. I'm glad you two have found each other. We could all use a little help from time to time. Well, you've got your shield. Are you ready to face your enemy?

speaker: Brasidas
en: I am.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. What is wrong, my friend?

speaker: Akatos
en: Are you really the high-soaring Eagle Bearer?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I descended from the heights of Olympos to visit Linou Farm and see the good people for myself.

speaker: Akatos
en: Amazing. A blessing. I am small and not worthy of your attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll hear no more deprecations. The priestess told me you had a problem? Out with it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have an eagle, Ikaros, who travels with me. But sometimes it's hard to know if I'm in charge or if he is.

speaker: Akatos
en: So kind and humble. The grace of Artemis and the wisdom of Athena.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, uh, Priestess Hexione said you had a problem. Tell me.

speaker: Akatos
en: I have shamed myself. Normally I hunt for my family and to provide for the village. But the other day I slipped and wrenched my ankle badly. I can barely walk. I am unworthy of your attention.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You are not at fault for your injury. Go on.

speaker: Akatos
en: My daughter, Myrto, insisted she would go into the woods and hunt for me. She's brave, but still inexperienced. She has been gone long, and I grow worried.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll find her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You must be Akatos's daughter, Myrto.

speaker: Myrto
en: Yes. Who are you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am Kassandra.

speaker: Myrto
en: The Eagle Bearer?

speaker: Kassandra
en: These woods can be dangerous for common folk. Your father grew worried about your absence and begged me to find you and keep you safe.

speaker: Myrto
en: I can't believe it! I hope you aren't disappointed in me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, child. You honor your father.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Some call me that, but I'm just a friend. You've been gone a long time. Your father was worried and asked me to look for you.

speaker: Myrto
en: That's very kind of you. I hope he wasn't too worried.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure we can ease his mind.

speaker: Myrto
en: I've tried to follow all his lessons, but hunting is hard! I've had no luck getting the special deer meat he wants. I'm worried he'll be so disappointed in me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hunting is hard. Tell you what. You return home so Akatos stops worrying, and I'll hunt for the meat you need.

speaker: Myrto
en: I'll do as you say, Eagle Bearer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: With a strong teacher like your father, I'm sure you know more than you think. Stay close to me, and maybe I can give you a few tips.

speaker: Myrto
en: Thank you! You are so kind!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The trick to hunting is to find a spot where deer trails cross and to stand quietly downwind of that.

speaker: Myrto
en: Pater says the same thing! I forgot to check the wind!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Quietly!

speaker: Myrto
en: Right. Sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We need to get deer neck meat?

speaker: Myrto
en: Yes, the priestesses asked pater for it special to celebrate your arrival. He was heartbroken not to be able to get it himself.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How do the priestesses prepare it?

speaker: Myrto
en: Brushed with a pine branch dipped in the juice of sour grapes and plums and other godly herbs.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There we go. Deer neck for your father. See? Hard, but you can do this.

speaker: Myrto
en: You were amazing! I've learned so much!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I will get the rest of the meat your father needs. Why don't you head home and tell Akatos what you've learned.

speaker: Myrto
en: I will. Thanks!

speaker: Akatos
en: Eagle Bearer, I cannot thank you enough!

speaker: Myrto
en: Kassandra! Did you find enough meat?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Providing for you is a simple task. Enjoy my bounty ad share it with your village.

speaker: Myrto
en: Kassandra hunts like Artemis herself!

speaker: Akatos
en: Show respect, child!

speaker: Myrto
en: Yes, pater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was my pleasure. Be well!

speaker: Kassandra
en: The woods were generous, and Artemis guided my aim.

speaker: Myrto
en: Do you know Artemis?! You never said!

speaker: Akatos
en: Myrto! Contain yourself!

speaker: Myrto
en: Sorry, pater.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, Myrto, I do not know Far-Shooting Artemis in the way you mean. But I know she looks kindly over hunters. Pay her respect and you'll soon hunt as well as your father.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get you your seals.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: The sooner the better.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you think of the Spartans?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: If you were to ask General Neon that, he'd tell you they were mindless brutes. That's half true. They have a base sort of cunning. It shouldn't be enough to withstand Athenian might. Assuming the other generals make intelligent decisions instead of stalling.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You do know I'm of Spartan birth?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: You're more skilled than the average Spartan. In time, you might even manage Athenian citizenship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The true pinnacle of success.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Of course. I wish I had more say over our naval forces. What I could do to the Spartans then...

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you held this command for long?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I've been a general in the army for a long time. I made some mistakes in my early days, but I more than made up for them after. Still, everyone attributes my victories to luck. Never to my own decisions.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I see how that could be frustrating.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Other men take credit for my victories. Cautious men who cause needless deaths by overlooking opportunities. You know what happens to a General who loses his reputation? Who gets blamed for the loss of Athenian lives?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing good.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: He dies. So I will do everything to preserve Athenian lives. Maybe one day, I'll even get credit for my accomplishments.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you need these seals?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I need those seals to shove in the faces of the assembled generals, to get them to wake up. While they've been debating and stalling, I've been winning the war.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know what I have to do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Actually, I already have them. I may have killed a few more Spartan commanders than you'd mentioned.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: An overachiever. Maybe you are as good as they say. Would you be interested in more work?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Do you have the seals for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: More seals, and more proof what we're doing is working. Thankfully, there are at least some people in power willing to listen to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll leave the politics to you.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: As it should be. And I have more work for you, assuming you're up for it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm always interested in more work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have some other jobs I need to do first.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I was worried about employing a mercenary, but you've been a pleasant surprise.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes. That's what they all call me. A pleasant surprise.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: I suspect if they call you anything offensive, they don't live long.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I couldn't say.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: At least I have you working with me, instead of getting in my way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Other generals giving you trouble?

speaker: Demosthenes
en: They refuse to acknowledge I know what I'm doing. But it doesn't matter. I'll get the job done, and eventually all of Athens will know it. Are you ready for more work?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not now. Maybe later.

speaker: Demosthenes
en: Are you ready to work with me yet?

speaker: Spartan Heavy Soldier
en: The Wolf awaits you. You fought well today—for a mercenary. Don't keep the Wolf waiting.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is it... What do I even say...

speaker: Civilian
en: Murderer! She has killed him!

speaker: Myrrine
en: Kassandra!

speaker: Nikolaos
en: So you are the champion who won the day. Tell me your name, hero, so that I may greet you as a true warrior.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, pater. It's been a long time.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Impossible. I saw you fall.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I didn't fall, you fucking threw me to my death.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I did what was required of me as a Spartan. I've made my peace with that. You need to as well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You were my father. You were supposed to protect me.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: You were reckless. You forced my hand.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I was protecting my brother because you wouldn't.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: The Oracle decreed that Alexios had to die. Her word is absolute. You know that.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You can't cower behind your sense of duty anymore...

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Enough! I can't change the past Kassandra... I will live and die a Spartan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a large reward for the mercenary that can collect the Wolf's head.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Is that why you're here?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Duty won't save you from the ghosts of our past. Now you will answer to me. I'm going to watch the light fade from your eyes as you die by my hand.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I loved you and your brother...

speaker: Nikolaos
en: You were never truly mine...

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Nikolaos
en: This is something you need to ask your mother. Kassandra... Kassandra... Beware the snakes in the grass...

speaker: Stentor
en: What's the meaning of this? By all the gods, what have you done?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came here to get revenge against the man that tried to murder me, and that's what I did.

speaker: Stentor
en: Traitor!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It was the hardest thing I've ever had to do, but he left me no choice. You don't know what happened between us in the past. This was his doing.

speaker: Stentor
en: You and your lies can go straight to fucking Hades!

speaker: Stentor
en: I don't need to know why to kill you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Spartans will have my head for this. I need to get out of here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've avoided the past long enough. Now you will answer to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Though you deserve death, there is no honor in vengeance. You must face the ghosts of your past, pater. And that is a fate worse than death.

speaker: Nikolaos
en: I have failed in my duty. I failed to protect you... to protect both of you. I loved you—and your brother as if you were truly my own. But you were never mine.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Nikolaos
en: That is a question you should ask your mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Find your mother.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Find her?

speaker: Nikolaos
en: Wherever Myrrine is, she knows far more than I do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Where will you go?

speaker: Nikolaos
en: To find my honor. Beware the snakes in the grass, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I need to get out of here. I should head back to Barnabas.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Ah, misthios. How was Megaris?

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Wolf is dead.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Excellent. The full amount, as promised. You expected me to haggle? Come now, Kassandra. It isn't every day I have someone kill their own father. But he wasn't your real father, was he?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why did you send me to kill Nikolaos?

speaker: Elpenor
en: Because I knew you could. Oh, why him? Because he was brilliant. He would have taken Athens in a month, two at most. And Stentor doesn't have the Wolf's genius.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You wanted to save Athens?

speaker: Elpenor
en: There's no profit in a quick war.

speaker: Elpenor
en: I know, I know. It's a lot to take in all at once. Come.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Tell me, misthios, did you learn anything worthwhile in your dealings with the Wolf?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He mentioned my birth father, he might still be alive.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Not for long, if all goes according to plan.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Elpenor
en: You're going to bring me his head, of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Have you lost your mind?

speaker: Elpenor
en: You killed the man who raised you for drachmae. I merely assumed you wanted your family dead as much as I do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He mentioned my mother—she still lives.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Not for long, I'm afraid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Elpenor
en: You're going to bring me her head, of course.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you out of your mind?

speaker: Elpenor
en: You killed the man who raised you for a sack of coins. I only assumed you wanted your family dead as much as I do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm done talking. I should kill you where you stand.

speaker: Elpenor
en: Temper, temper. And they said you'd be different. But blood is blood, I suppose.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They? What blood?

speaker: Elpenor
en: You really are more brawn than brains, aren't you? A shame, I could have used you for more of my... errands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Malaka! You think you can play with me? I'll cut out your tongue!

speaker: Parmys
en: My friends, we have come a long way. I do not speak of the paths you have all traveled to be here, though I thank you for coming. I speak of the noble history of Greek shipbuilding. In this wonderful historic amphitheater set within prosperous Achaia, I think it appropriate to reflect upon that ancient duty of which, with all modesty, we have become masters. It is we, the Greeks, who took the world from the humble monoxylon to the papyrella, through the penteconter and bireme, and finally to the unconquerable trireme. We have plied the graces of patient Poseidon as the oceans slowly relinquished their secrets. And now the entire Greek world enjoys the benefits of our toil. Admittedly, we have been less successful in that respect with Zeus and Ares. So where do we go from here? Where can we go from here? Can we improve upon the mighty trireme, that conqueror of the tides? I say to you, yes! It would be a brave soul who limits the scope of Greek innovation. Could we not one day bear witness to the construction of vessels rivaling those of the gods? Imagine the magnificence of the ships not 130 feet long, but 400! Carrying not 200, but 2000! With not three rows of oars, but 20! And broad decks bearing catapults with which to vanquish enemies from afar!Why stop there? For the nobles, gymnasiums and gardens! All crowned with a temple to beloved Aphrodite! Imagine such worlds on the water. What would it take to build them? Who could do it? Come now brethren! I say to you, our gods-given Greek genius has never known human limitation. Our own Pythagoras discovered the secrets of angles, did he not? Another like him will rise to achieve these glorious constructions. Imagine a child of Pythagoras! What wonders might that child perform, as it would sit upon its father's shoulders?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Ma-lá-ka! I'll bet he couldn't calculate the chances of that.

speaker: Parmys
en: In the light of such exalted heritage, I say to you, it is not a question of "if" we do it, but of "when"! Welcome, then, to the Achaia shipbuilding symposium, and to the glorious future of Greek shipbuilding! This brand new innovation is called an oar lock. As you can see, it holds the oar in place and prevents it from sliding around. Notice how it affords unrestricted movement without inducing undue wear on the ear or on the rail. It's already improved the effectiveness of those vessels to which it has been applied. Captains report greater speeds from their crews, who are able to row harder and longer. Which is something, I venture, that would gain the approval even of Aphrodite herself. But what about sails? We already use the best linen available. Our ropes and pulleys are the finest ever made. In fact, they recently discovered that by "squeezing down" one side of the sail, the amount of wind captured can be increased. That means more speed, especially in critical moments of battle. Of course, these techniques will never replace a crew of strong slaves. But they are useful nonetheless.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: You different. Like me. Friends. Me Polyphemos. You Little.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure, "Little." Polyphemos, I'm looking for a woman who was here.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: No friend for long time. You help make friend. Friend fish together. You like fish?

speaker: Kassandra
en: So, I help you make a friend to go fishing with, and you'll help me find the woman I'm looking for.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Pretty beach! Little will see. Little will like. We go now.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Little follow. Show beach where lady helped Polyphemos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Polyphemos, this is important—do you mean "Leda"?

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Silly Little. Not "Lee-duh." "Lay-dee."

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Help Polyphemos! No want to hurt! Never again!

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Little think Polyphemos cyclops?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're nothing like the Cyclops from Kephallonia. He had one real eye and one fake eye. He picked on Little.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Pick on Little! What you do?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I shoved his fake eye up a goat's ass.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Little funny.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Bad men! Hate Polyphemos!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There, big guy. The beach is yours now, to fish all you want.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Little think beach pretty?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Depends on who's looking at it, but sure. I think it's pretty.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: But still need friend to share. Polyphemos like poetry. Can practice with you. Tell Polyphemos what make Little, Little.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have the strength of ten warriors. I could lift a whole mountain above my head.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Strong like Polyphemos! Careful not to crush small things. What else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, I have eyes. They're nice, I guess.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Polyphemos know lady with pretty green eyes. She nice. What else?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Nothing makes me happier than celebrating. Drinking and singing are good for the spirit.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: With friend! Polyphemos love to sing. More?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no better feeling in the world than crushing a skull with my fist.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Little scary. Polyphemos does not hurt. Never again. More?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I wish I could be with my family. The last time I was happy, I was a young girl. I miss those days. I don't know why I'm telling you this. You're a good listener, big guy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've never been able to rely on anyone the way I can rely on Barnabas and our crew. I wish my work didn't take me away from them.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Little hurt inside. Like Polyphemos. For you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is beautiful, big guy.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: More gift for Little. Spices from pretty green-eye lady. Only gift Polyphemos ever got.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This might be exactly what I was looking for. So, you have a beach to go fishing...

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Only need friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't stay here, big guy. But if I ever meet someone who loves fishing and poetry as much as you do, I'll send them your way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't stay with you, big guy, but I think I found someone you should meet.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eurylochos, this is Polyphemos. Polyphemos, Eurylochos.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Show you cave?

speaker: Eurylochos
en: Show me everything, my big friend. This is the grandest, most spectacular shore on which I've ever laid my weary eyes. I want to see it all!

speaker: Polyphemos
en: You Little. But big heart. Take this. Special gift.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Little think beach ugly. And Little think you ugly.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: You trick Polyphemos! No hurt! Please, no hurt!

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Please no hurt! Please!

speaker: Kassandra
en: A bag of spice. Where would he get these? I should tell Barnabas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Face me, cyclops. I've come to avenge one of your victims.

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Please no hurt! Polyphemos no want to fight!

speaker: Polyphemos
en: Please no hurt! Please!

en: I'm not here to hurt you.

en: About my Leda, do you have any news?

en: In the cave, I found a man. I took these spices from him.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah, my Leda. Do you think the man you found was a cyclops, then she concocted an elixir from these spices and helped him to grow a second eye?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas, there was no cyclops on Anaphi any more than there was one on Kephallonia.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Have faith, my friend. Leda was there.

en: That's exactly what happened. Leda saved the cyclops' life with magic spices.

en: She did. We should be careful not to use these spices. Who knows how many eyes we'd grow?
