speaker: Kassandra
en: I got your message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Man
en: The local Spartan commander enjoys figs with honey. I'd like to send him some, but he can't know they're from me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you sending him a snack?

speaker: Man
en: Not a snack. His last meal.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You want me to deliver it to the Spartan commander.

speaker: Man
en: Exactly. It must arrive without a scratch.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It won't be easy, but I'll take care of it.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you. Please be quick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should get going.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Someone thought you might need this.

speaker: Man
en: Thank you,misthios. Please, take this.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Korinth, the city of pots, prostitutes, and not much else. Alkibiades said the hetaerae here could help me find my mother. I should look around for Anthousa's whereabouts.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for Anthousa. Is she here?

speaker: Civilian
en: Wouldn't I like to know. Sunrise, sunset, I save my drachmae for a taste of the divine. The hetaerae are hard to come by!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So you haven't seen them.

speaker: Civilian
en: Not with the Monger's army on the loose. The hetaerae won't tolerate that.

speaker: Civilian
en: You let me know if you find those girls! They have to be somewhere in this city.

speaker: Civilian
en: Haven't done something wrong, have I? Swear I haven't!

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you have, you might see me later. I'm looking for Anthousa.

speaker: Civilian
en: Phew.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know her?

speaker: Civilian
en: No one really knows Anthousa. And the hetaerae got pushed out of here ages ago!

speaker: Kassandra
en: "Pushed out?" So someone didn't want them here.

speaker: Civilian
en: We don't like to say his name—in case his men overhear. Just know the hetaerae were forced to move out of Korinth's markets.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can you tell me where they've gone?

speaker: Civilian
en: I haven't seen 'em since, I swear it! I can't afford to pay 'em.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hm. Then I'll keep looking.

speaker: Civilian
en: Someone around here's gotta know. 'Til then, I'll be on my best behavior, misthios! Just minding my own business, misthios! I'm sure someone here can help you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Are you Anthousa?

speaker: Civilian
en: Me? Anthousa? I could be anyone for you, lamb. I charge less than the hetaerae, but do I ever know my way around a hay-bed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So her name means something to you.

speaker: Civilian
en: Anthousa? She's been around forever, but I never met her. I know the hetaerae all work as one—on equal footing—but Anthousa's special. She talks—they listen.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't met any hetaerae yet.

speaker: Civilian
en: Don't believe all you hear. They sell what a lot of us sell in Korinth—but for them, it's not just about the flesh. They're merchants of a sort. Streetwise—can talk as nice as they look.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a good trade to work in. You don't want to be a hetaerae?

speaker: Civilian
en: Not in my prime anymore, am I, misthios? By the time I study what they did, I'll be serving clients on my deathbed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: If the hetaerae aren't here, where are they?

speaker: Civilian
en: Their sort are too high-and-mighty to be down here in the dirt with us. You want 'em, you'll find 'em up on the hill—the Akrokorinth. By the Temple, keeping Aphrodite's worshippers satisfied. No pay, no play! If you want your precious hetaerae, go to the Temple of Aphrodite.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Please, leave us!

speaker: Monger Thug
en: The hetaerae! Where are they?!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: The hetaerae aren't here!

speaker: Monger Thug
en: Then you're gonna pay for the trouble we went through to find 'em.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: We're here in peace!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Aphrodite aid us!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who do they think they are? I need to stop them.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who were they? And why were they looking for the hetaerae?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Ai-ya! They think this temple is dedicated to them, the brutes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The thieves are here and the hetaerae aren't.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: The hetaerae? They're much wiser than we are. They realized their visitors were all getting robbed on the way in.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: There's no avoiding the Monger's men in Korinth.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll keep my guard up.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: He craves money, misthios.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Not only that, but power. Once he smells it on you, you're a goner!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who walks around with a name like the "Monger"?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Don't let him hear you say that.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Last time his name came out of a fool's mouth, the man's tongue was sliced out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So the Monger is a Korinthian criminal?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Master of the underground markets. He rules with one hand open for money, and the other clenched around a weapon.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: A drachmae—and blood-hungry monster's what he is!

speaker: Kassandra
en: So he's hunting for the hetaerae. For money?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Exactly. Since the hetaerae bring in so much drachmae, he wants everything they control!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: The thieves are better off robbin' them than us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If you know of the hetaerae, then you know of Anthousa. I'm looking for her.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: They say she's everywhere, though I've never seen her. But the hetaerae see everything!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: I've seen them gather by the Spring of Peirene, down the mountain. They meet clients there, and then take 'em elsewhere in secret.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. Maybe pray to Aphrodite from home next time.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: You taught those thugs a lesson of a lifetime.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: They won't be coming back here anytime soon.

speaker: Anthousa
en: It shouldn't be long now. No, it won't be, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Hetaera
en: Then they'll help?

speaker: Anthousa
en: Everyone has something they want. My job is to figure out how much they'll give for that something.

speaker: Hetaera
en: Then Korinth will be ours again.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Very soon, it will return to its rightful hands.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Ah, so Kassandra has finally found us.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know me?

speaker: Hetaera
en: And you know her. This is Anthousa.

speaker: Anthousa
en: We saw you help the worshippers at the temple of Aphrodite. You've proven yourself a friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hear that, Ikaros? Her sight's as good as yours.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Someone also spoke very highly of you.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Surprise!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Phoibe?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Aspasia sent me! I work for her now, remember?

speaker: Kassandra
en: But why here? Korinth isn't safe.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I had to tell Anthousa you were coming! Aspasia taught me a new word: "emissary." That's me!

speaker: Anthousa
en: And now Kassandra and I have met.

speaker: Phoibe
en: See? This is easy! And now I can help you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's a killer on the loose in a city with no morals to begin with. You can't just follow me around like in Kephallonia.

speaker: Phoibe
en: The Monger, the Cyclops... I made it all the way here, didn't I?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, you always find a way.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You and I will talk about this later.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I don't work for you—I work for Aspasia!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then the work she gave you should keep you busy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I guess that would be all right. Who knows what I'll get into?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Yes!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just make sure you're extra careful.

speaker: Anthousa
en: We need to move inside, Kassandra. We're not the only ones watching. Come with me, and we'll talk.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Can I come?

speaker: Kassandra
en: As long as you're quiet.

speaker: Anthousa
en: To what do I owe your visit?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Alkibiades told me about you.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Did he? Go on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for a woman from Sparta—a runaway, long ago. She may have gone by the name of Myrrine.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Who's that?

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's my mother.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Your mother? You don't have a mother! Markos told me he raised you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: What did I tell you about talking?

speaker: Anthousa
en: I see. There will be time to respond to your question, but that time isn't now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not the answer I'm looking for.

speaker: Anthousa
en: It's the only one you'll get until I've bargained a proper exchange. I've become quite the businesswoman, after all.

speaker: Phoibe
en: You better be telling the truth! Kassandra can get really mad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As long as you tell me what you know sooner or later.

speaker: Anthousa
en: You'll have to trust me. You don't get to where I stand without credibility. My word is yours.

speaker: Phoibe
en: And you can always trust Kassandra!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why don't you go play, Phoibe? Let me and Anthousa talk.

speaker: Phoibe
en: If you say so.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I propose a trade. Help me—help us—get stronger. Strong enough to rid Korinth of the Monger permanently. A simple transaction, I assure you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You have a deal.

speaker: Anthousa
en: A wise decision, dear misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I haven't made it this far being a fool. I know when to take a chance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: As long as you deliver what I'm looking for, we won't have a problem.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Negotiation always involves some compromise, you know.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Compromise I can do. But I won't be cheated.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Then we're in business. Now. You've heard of the Monger?

speaker: Kassandra
en: From what the worshippers say, he's someone I should watch out for.

speaker: Anthousa
en: They're right. I'm sure his victims wish they'd been more vigilant. My eyes are wide open.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I heard about him after I killed his men. Seems he's famous in Korinth.

speaker: Anthousa
en: For all the wrong reasons. His knife has shed much Korinthian blood—but that's just the way of commerce. The blood between us is bad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then you've held your ground well. You're not dead.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Not yet, anyway. But he's employed enough thugs to amass a small army. Now they're attacking people in the street—us included.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's been killing hetaerae?

speaker: Anthousa
en: Killing? We're smarter than that. But action must be taken before it goes that far.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I'm not the only one who needs help. My girls, Damalis and Erinna, are suffering too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: More Monger trouble?

speaker: Anthousa
en: I wouldn't doubt it. Work against their aggressors, and then it will be his turn to suffer. You'll find Damalis here at the spring, but Erinna has gone to Bellerophron's Garden.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's wrong with Erinna?

speaker: Anthousa
en: She's looking for Kleio—another hetaera—who's gone missing. I've been too distracted to help in the search.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Has Damalis told you what's wrong?

speaker: Anthousa
en: She hasn't told me much, but I know these girls as well as I know myself. Something's not right.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what I can do for them.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Good. The Monger feeds his thugs with the drachmae he makes smuggling—weapons mostly, which is all the more lucrative now that he has a war to supply.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So if someone interrupts the Monger's supply, his men go hungry.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Exactly. Go to his warehouse in the Port of Lechaion and burn his cargo. All of it. We'll let chaos take care of the rest.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why rob people who can't put two drachmae together if he has a business? It's illegitimate, but gets him rich.

speaker: Anthousa
en: Even the smuggling is a front. He steals slaves—innocents, who shouldn't be harmed. But his thugs can burn.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Seems to me that burning his biggest source of income is asking for trouble.

speaker: Anthousa
en: I want to put new muscle I've acquired on show. Plus, violence is the only language he understands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know many people who speak that language.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Then the warehouse will be cinders.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Remind me. Where do I find the Monger's warehouse?

speaker: Anthousa
en: It's at the Port of Lechaion. Burn it to the ground.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get to it. Look for the flames.

speaker: To Hell and Back
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Damalis
en: So you're here to help us, misthios? You don't look like a Monger spy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm more the in-your-face type. You have a Monger problem, Damalis?

speaker: Damalis
en: I might. One of my regulars has... changed. He was a decent man once, but now, he's gone bad.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Korinth seems to have a shortage of "decent" people.

speaker: Damalis
en: I need someone with muscle to figure out what's behind the change. Why he's different.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He's gotten you scared.

speaker: Damalis
en: He asks me questions I don't know the answers to about our drachmae. Where we keep money, what Anthousa invests in. As though we're Athenian aristocrats.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Can't Anthousa intervene?

speaker: Damalis
en: I'm not naive! I won't expose others to this. So he can go after them next?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He might anyway. Sounds like he needs answers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who was he before all this?

speaker: Damalis
en: Obsessive, but never threatening. He didn't stand out in symposiums, until he had his drachmae act for him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, something's sure giving him courage now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll see what he has to say for himself.

speaker: Damalis
en: If he's not lurking around here, he'll be at his house. I want this to end today.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It will. People tend to show their true selves to my spear whether they like it or not.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Kassandra! It's me! Kassandra!

speaker: Phoibe
en: Good, you found me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Shh! What are you doing here?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I heard Damalis talking about her crazy client earlier and I wanted to help!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. But you have to do as I say. No games!

speaker: Phoibe
en: I know that already—because you never let me have any fun!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You may be right. I could use you.

speaker: Phoibe
en: See? That was my plan all along!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm going to talk to Damalis' client and see what he has to say.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I've been here. Spying. And I heard him mumbling to himself! He's weird. But maybe if I tell you what he said, it could help?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's hear it.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Let me think... He said something about having to meet someone at Pig Farm tonight. That could help!

speaker: Kassandra
en: It could. Did he mention why?

speaker: Phoibe
en: To get something from them. A deed to some land, I think he said.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, that's something. What else?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Oh, he said their name! Deinomenes. Wonder who that is?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good to know. Thank you, Phoibe the spy.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Not bad, huh?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Time to act. Listen closely. You sneak inside and see what you can find in his house while I distract him.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Quiet like a mouse!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Good. But if you get caught, run. Right out the door. We'll meet afterwards. Promise?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I'm ready. Let's go!

speaker: Client
en: Do I know you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: No. But I know you.

speaker: Client
en: If Myron sent you, tell him I was going to pay him back this very night!

speaker: Kassandra
en: No one sent me. We need to talk. I know you're up to something

speaker: Client
en: Something? Something could be anything! You have nothing on me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're meeting someone tonight, aren't you? At Phaia's goat farm.

speaker: Client
en: A goat farm? You'll find no goats at Phaia's.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, I...

speaker: Client
en: Wait! Thief! Thieves! Get out! Guards! Get them!

speaker: Phoibe
en: What was all that noise?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Damalis doesn't have to worry about her client now.

speaker: Phoibe
en: That wasn't what she wanted you to do!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I dealt with him, didn't I?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Well... At least I could sneak in OK. Look!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're meeting someone tonight, aren't you? At Phaia's cow farm.

speaker: Client
en: A cow farm? You'll find no cows at Phaia's.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, I...

speaker: Client
en: Wait! Thief! Thieves! Get out! Guards! Get them!

speaker: Phoibe
en: What was all that noise?!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Damalis doesn't have to worry about her client now.

speaker: Phoibe
en: That wasn't what she wanted you to do!

speaker: Kassandra
en: I dealt with him, didn't I?

speaker: Phoibe
en: Well... At least I could sneak in OK. Look!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're going to Phaia's Pig Farm. And meeting some like-minded person there, I hear.

speaker: Client
en: Where did you hear that? You're wrong. Dead wrong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They owe you a deed to some land. What that land'll be used for, I don't know.

speaker: Client
en: A spy. What else do you have on me? Cough it up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Deinomenes will be quite upset if I don't let you meet him tonight.

speaker: Client
en: How? What do you want?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I know about Damalis. And as her client, you seem to think she owes you something.

speaker: Client
en: I do love her, you know. With my whole heart.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And yet, you're scaring her.

speaker: Client
en: Better me than another more careless man. Either I hurt Damalis, or I'm killed!

speaker: Kassandra
en: That's not love, it's weakness.

speaker: Client
en: You say it as though I don't know. He knew that too. That's why he's making me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Who's making you?

speaker: Client
en: Tell Damalis I'll stop. That I'm sorry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Fine. Chaire, old man.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's see what we found.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I wonder what this means?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What's this, a coin purse?

speaker: Phoibe
en: His things aren't very nice, though. If he's rich, why have all that junk?

speaker: Kassandra
en: He must have just gotten paid.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've seen that iron poker used before.

speaker: Phoibe
en: He didn't have a furnace! Why does he have this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not used for fire... It's a weapon. For torture. I saw someone use it in Phokis. Someone huge.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Huge like the Monger?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just like the Monger.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What does the letter say?

speaker: Phoibe
en: It's mean! It says he'll get hurt if he keeps doing things wrong.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought as much.

speaker: Phoibe
en: And it says more... That he needs to bring Damalis to a place here in Korinth. There's directions. What do you think it is?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't know... But I'll find out.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Right behind you!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Not this time. Go to Damalis and wait for me there.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Aw, please?

speaker: Kassandra
en: You've done enough for today, It could be dangerous. I'll come find you after.

speaker: Phoibe
en: Fine. I almost forgot. I got this sword for you from his house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Wow. You're a good thief.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A place to bring Damalis. A prison? I should find out.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This must be the place described in the letter. Anybody home?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's blood. Lots of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maláka. What is this?

speaker: Kassandra
en: A lock of hair. Smells familiar, somehow.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chains? Oil? This can't be what I think it is.

speaker: The Stalker
en: Gotcha! All right you little shit, who sent you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: What are you doing here?

speaker: Phoibe
en: I wanted to help?

speaker: The Stalker
en: Give her here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave, Phoibe. Now!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Don't take another step.

speaker: The Stalker
en: You're brave coming here. You want a whipping? The Monger would love to take you on.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'd rot in the underworld for that.

speaker: The Stalker
en: Prude. This is Korinthia! Anything goes in this sex andron. And the Monger will be satiated.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're as sick as he is, worm.

speaker: The Stalker
en: Whether they like it or not, any victim he likes gets his special treatment. I'll tell him you volunteer.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You'll get my special treatment right now. I'll fucking kill you.

speaker: Damalis
en: Kassandra. Your little friend beat you back.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You made it.

speaker: Phoibe
en: And fast. I know all the shortcuts now. I'm sorry, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all right. You had good intentions.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I thought I could sneak in... Like before.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm glad you didn't. Especially with what I found there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Listen next time I tell you to do something.

speaker: Phoibe
en: OK.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I promise it's for your own good. This time, especially.

speaker: Damalis
en: What happened to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I just left the Monger's sex andron, if you can believe it. And it's where you were headed.

speaker: Damalis
en: No.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's true. Your client was being forced to take you there. And we found these.

speaker: Damalis
en: What does this mean?

speaker: Kassandra
en: It means the Monger got to him. He does have his hand in everything.

speaker: Damalis
en: At least I know how to deal with him now that I know what he's after.

speaker: Kassandra
en: He'll leave you alone now. He gave me his word.

speaker: Damalis
en: So we really can trust you, can't we?

speaker: Kassandra
en: We're not all so easily blackmailed.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You won't have to. I took care of him myself.

speaker: Phoibe
en: I told Kassandra she shouldn't have!

speaker: Damalis
en: It had to come to this. Maláka, what a fool he was.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The Monger's the real fool. He'll find that out soon enough.

speaker: Damalis
en: There's nothing scarier than the unknown, and you've protected me from it. Thank you.

speaker: Phoibe
en: We sure helped Damalis! And it was kind of fun, too.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Mater told me to meet her at the Statue of Artemis in the Cedar.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: They called Arkadia the "breadbasket of the Peloponesian League." Wheat's the most precious resource in the Greek World...

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: There. Will be good to see mater and Brasidas again.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Who are you?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Me? I'm no one. But you? You're even godlier than Brasidas said you'd be. It should be your statue between these trees.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas? What does he have to do with this?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Warrior, he said! Look for the mighty warrior with the broken spear. I added the godly bit.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas knows a warrior when he sees one. Word of my deeds will outlive any statue.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Of course! Your story should be sung from the mountain tops. In Arkadia you are already a legend.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm just a traveler. And there's more than one broken spear in this world.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: And the eagle he mentioned?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: What eagle?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Where is Brasidas? I need to speak with him.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Of course you do! And the woman, you'd like to speak with her too, yes?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Wait...

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: She looks like you.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where they went.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: I should. It's what Brasidas paid me for, after all.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Then why don't you?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: He didn't pay enough.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Stop! Please stop!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: "My story will outlive any statue." Who says that?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: "Just a traveler," she says.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where they are, or I'll cut that shit-eating grin off your shit-eating face!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: He said you had a nasty temper. He wasn't wrong.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where my mater is and you may walk out of here alive.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: You show mercy. Arkadia will give you none in return.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Speak!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: You'll find them on a hill—a cliff overlooking Tegea.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where my mother is or I'll shove my spear so far down your throat, you'll be shitting iron at the gates of Hades!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Please! Show mercy!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Speak!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: They're on a hill—a cliff overlooking Tegea.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: You said Brasidas didn't pay enough. Who did?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: The Archon. He's paying more for your head than Brasidas could afford in two lifetimes.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me who the Archon is. I want a name.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Lagos. His name is Lagos. And he's the most powerful man in Arkadia—he who controls the grain, controls the world.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Consider yourself lucky. I've seen enough blood.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Oh, but you'll be seeing a lot more. Welcome to Arkadia, Kassandra.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Brasidas didn't pay you enough? Who did? Tell me, or I'll wrap your guts around your neck and hang you from that tree!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: The Archon. He's paying more for your head than Brasidas could afford in two lifetimes.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me who the Archon is. I want a name.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: Lagos. His name is Lagos. And he's the most powerful man in Arkadia—he who controls the grain, controls the world.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: You threatened the wrong people, maláka.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Sosipatros
en: I don't threaten, I promise!

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: I want the Archon dead.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: None of this makes sense. This isn't the Lagos I know.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: Thank the gods you found us.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I got your message.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Your messenger is lucky to be alive. He betrayed you, Brasidas.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I killed the messenger. He betrayed you, Brasidas.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: These Cultists Myrrine told me about—they knew you were coming and must have forced Lagos to place the bounty on your heads. Trusting anyone in Arkadia will be difficult now.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: Which is why I say we put that Archon's head on a pike. Our message to the puppet King in Sparta will be clear.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's find out more about what's going on in Arkadia. We should be able to solve this Lagos problem without too many beheadings.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: After what happened to the Monger in Korinthia...

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: That crowd wanted blood.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Violence doesn't always solve problems.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Excellent. We need to handle this how you handled the Monger in Korinthia.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll keep that in mind.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm sure he has soldiers everywhere in Arkadia... We'll just behead them all.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: And deal with it like you dealt with the Monger? Why not hire some musicians to entertain the crowd, too?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I know you wanted me to kill him in private. But at the time, it was the right choice.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: As long as those executions are carried out quietly. Like you did with the Monger in Korinthia.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Your advice was good, so I followed it, Brasidas.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Whatever happens, we need Lagos alive. Arkadia is Sparta's breadbasket, and Lagos keeps it full.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: That man is working for the Cult of Kosmos, not Sparta.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Then we need to free him from their grasp.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: What makes you think he wants to leave?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Bounties and threats aren't Lagos' style. He's a farmer, not a killer.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you have in mind, Brasidas?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Unlike your mother, I think we can handle this quietly. I'm going to begin by investigating a safe house he keeps. There might be some evidence there.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: What do you think we should do?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: I still say we send the Archon to Hades. Upsetting Sparta's breadbasket will send the false king searching for crumbs.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: The Archon is no longer the man you knew. The Cult has him now.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Looks like I came just in time.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: You certainly did. But it's time to make a decision.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Your strategy makes sense, Brasidas.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Thank you. I'm glad you agree.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: You're letting sentimentality cloud your judgment.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: My mother's plan is best.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: Ah, my lamb. United in blood and purpose.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: You're letting your impulses overcome your reason.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: Thousands of Spartans depend on Lagos for food and protection. His death would bring chaos.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Brasidas
en: There's a farmhouse northeast of Tegea where he has a safe house. Meet me there before you do anything you'll regret.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: And what if Brasidas' plan doesn't work?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: The Archon hides like a coward in Fort Samikon. You can't miss that monstrosity. You could go after him now, but be careful—he's well-defended.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Then we must weaken his defenses.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: He's got barracks full of guards and silos full of grain... It would be a shame if any came to harm.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Where exactly are Lagos' guards stationed?

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: Some rest their heads at a barracks in Tegea. There's also a camp and a fort in Smuggler's Forest. Destroy his guards there, and his defenses will be weakened.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me where to find the silos.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: The Archon stores his wheat in Pan's Cradle. Set the silos alight, and his livelihood will go up in smoke.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll go see what Lagos is up to.

scene: To Kill or Not to Kill
speaker: Myrrine
en: Good luck, my lamb.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: If you have a moment, I would ask you to help me with something.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: He seems to be resting peacefully now.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Yes, you helped ease his mind, but he'll never truly be at peace until he takes his last breath.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: When will that be?

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: It's hard to tell. Judging by his symptoms, it'll be sooner rather than later.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: I can lessen his pain, but to do so, I'll need some hemlock.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll collect the ingredients you need.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Thank you. It won't stop the pain entirely, but I hope it'll help him feel more comfortable.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: He doesn't want to feel better. He wants to die with some dignity.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: True dignity would be fighting through this so I can analyze his symptoms further.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: He wants to die and he's in pain. You should respect his right to choose instead of treating him like an experiment. What you're doing is wrong.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: I will not be lectured on the morality of my work by a sell-sword. I have a responsibility, like all healers, to use my knowledge for the betterment of others.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I can't imagine how difficult this must be, but I know you're doing what you can to help him.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Sometimes I worry that it's never enough. First the plague, and now this. The ailments that afflict man are as varied as the gods. It would take me many lifetimes to learn about them all.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: Hemlock is rare. Where do you harvest it?"

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: It grows all across Boeotia, but check near the Tumulus of Plataia. I'm sure I saw some when I was last there.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: Why are you treating him with poison? Hemlock is deadly.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Only in the wrong dosage. If my observations are correct, it should lessen the pain wracking his body.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll get the hemlock you need.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: That's what I'm looking for.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: That looks like hemlock.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hemlock
en: A bunch of herbs that Hippokrates requires in order to treat Pentheus. They smell very strange.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I got the hemlock you wanted.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Thank you. I know this task was a little beneath you, but it will help my friend here. I've prepared the elixir base, but I need you to grind the herb and add it to the mixture.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I think I can handle that.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Be mindful of the amount you add. While the hemlock is an excellent pain inhibitor, too much can be lethal.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: Just as the doctor ordered.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: He seems to be calmer now.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: The potion is working. With what I learn here, I could help many more who still have a chance at life.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: Gods protect you, Pentheus.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Come now, Pentheus. We must check to see how your symptoms are progressing.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Pentheus? Pentheus?! What? What's happened? He shouldn't have died yet.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: What did you do?

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: He was suffering. I did what was necessary.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I did nothing except what you asked me to do.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Do you think I'm stupid? I know enough to see when someone has been poisoned.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: He wanted a peaceful death, and I gave it to him.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: I did what I knew was right—and what you couldn't do.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: It wasn't your place. I needed more time—there was still more I could have learned.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: Keeping him alive so you can study him isn't right. He was in pain and wanted to die.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: My job was to save his life, not end it. I chose to not help Galeos and I was wrong.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: You and I both know that's not why you kept him alive. Stop hiding the truth behind your code.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: You're right. I knew I couldn't bring myself to end his life, but I thought the more I learned, the better chance I would have of saving others in the future.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: It was a noble cause.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Hippokrates
en: Treating patients should come before studying ailments, but I have a higher calling. If I'm to learn all I can, I need to travel and analyze the conditions other physicians are treating.

scene: Too Much of a Good Thing
speaker: Kassandra
en: Good luck, Hippokrates. I hope our paths cross again in the future.

speaker: Top Source of Problems
en: was a virtual representation of one of Kassandra's genetic memories, relived by Layla Hassan through the Portable Animus HR-8.5.

speaker: Civilian
en: The Eagle Bearer? Misthios! Over here, I need to talk to you!

speaker: Civilian
en: Misthios! And that looks like Barnabas' ship.

speaker: Kassandra
en: In fact it

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah! That ship belongs to the Eagle Bearer now. Legendary misthios, famed across the Greek world. I am just her humble servant.

speaker: Civilian
en: Barnabas! You're back!

speaker: Barnabas
en: In the flesh. A little older, but not a bit wiser.

speaker: Civilian
en: Mikkos sent me here to wait for your return. It's about Neleus...

speaker: Barnabas
en: Here we go. What has my nephew gotten himself into this time?

speaker: Civilian
en: I think the trouble is real, Barnabas. You should go to him. Mikkos told me not to return without help, and I mean not to.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I need to think. But one thing... I know my nephew. Ah yes. He's fine, that much is certain. I'll be on the ship.

speaker: Civilian
en: And you, misthios? I need someone to go see about Neleus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why doesn't Barnabas think something is wrong with his nephew?

speaker: Civilian
en: It's just... Neleus was a legendary nuisance growing up. He lied. He cheated. He brawled and broke things.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Some of us grow out of that.

speaker: Civilian
en: Well, now Neleus is a serious athlete, training to be an Olympic champion. And what's more, he's family to Barnabas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That is important.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help Barnbas' nephew however I can.

speaker: Civilian
en: Neleus lives with his caretaker, Mikkos. Their house is just up the hill north of here.

speaker: Barnabas
en: The amount of times this boy's been "too sick to work" only to hear, not two hours later, he's in the fields with his friends. By Zeus!

speaker: Mikkos
en: He's grown since you've been gone. He's not a kid anymore.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah, but still up to his old tricks, if you ask me.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Listen to reason, Barnabas. I saw him vomiting myself. And now he's like this!

speaker: Barnabas
en: He's faking it, Mikkos. I've seen this routine before. Gods! Grant me Penelope's patience.

speaker: Mikkos
en: It's not just Neleus. There have been others. All promising young athletes turning up sick or missing. Something's not right in Thasos.

speaker: Barnabas
en: What goes on across Thasos is not my concern. But I know my nephew. Ah, yes. He practically worships at the altar of Aergia. A devotee of sloth and idleness, he is.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Help me talk sense into him, misthios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You know your nephew best, and it sounds like he needs a firm hand.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I thought his caretaker could handle him, but apparently I was wrong.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Come on Barnabas, he's plainly ill.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Bah! I'll be at the ship when Neleus snaps out of it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Maybe you should be a bit easier on your nephew this time. He really does seem sick.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ah, you're right. I–I guess I didn't want it to be true. He's not a boy anymore, I can see that.

speaker: Mikkos
en: He may be grown, but he still needs help.

speaker: Barnabas
en: There's only one way I know how.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Let me know if there is any change in his condition. I'll be at the ship making offerings to Asklepios.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Give Barnabas some time.

speaker: Mikkos
en: But our time may run out. I have more leads to follow up on, but with Neleus like this I can't leave his side. Maybe you could help me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Barnabas is like family to me. I want to do anything I can to help Neleus.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Thank you.

speaker: Mikkos
en: You know, it's not often a beautiful and capable misthios comes to this house.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They may have brought Neleus sickness, but the Fates have brought us together...

speaker: Mikkos
en: I'd hate to get sick someday and think of all the fun I didn't have.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But first, there are those leads you mentioned.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We shouldn't talk like this with Neleus in this condition. Now, about those leads you mentioned...

speaker: Mikkos
en: Well, someone at the Champion's Gymnasium must know something.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Aietes was the last one to be with Neleus when he was well.

speaker: Kassandra
en: They were friends?

speaker: Mikkos
en: They were. If he doesn't know anything, you could talk to the doctor at the quarry.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If he's the local doctor, he's bound to know something.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What more can you tell me about this gymnasium? You say other athletes have disappeared?

speaker: Mikkos
en: Many, yes. A lot of the athletes came here to train from elsewhere across the Greek world, so when they disappear, people think they maybe just went home.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A convenient story if something bad were happening to them.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Exactly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'd like to have a word with that doctor at the quarry.

speaker: Mikkos
en: The Aliki Quarry is at the southern point of Thasos. The doctor there is mixed up with training athletes and the workers.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds like a strange connection.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Yes, until you realize half of the workers are athletes who have given up on their training. Something's happened to them, and that doctor is the only connection I see.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The last person to see Neleus before he got sick was Aietes. Where can I find him?

speaker: Mikkos
en: He's an aspiring athlete, too, but nowhere near as talented as Neleus. He trains alone on the outskirts of the Vineyard of Glory. You're sure to find him there.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll follow up on these leads and check back when I know what's going on.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Thank you, misthios. And feel free to "check back" any time.

speaker: Mikkos
en: You're back! Neleus hasn't gotten any better. But maybe you're here to see me instead?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've been thinking about you and wanted to see you again. I won't pretend otherwise.

speaker: Mikkos
en: You've stormed into my life like a creature from the summit of Olympus itself. It's safe to say I've been thinking about you, too.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We should probably leave our feelings aside...for now.

speaker: Mikkos
en: For the sake of Neleus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We can't do this now.

speaker: Mikkos
en: I know, I know. It's just

speaker: Kassandra
en: What happened to Neleus is still an open question. I need to get to work.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have some questions.

speaker: Mikkos
en: Is there anything I can do to help?

speaker: Xanthe
en: You! Are you... Kassandra of House Agiad?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I am.

speaker: Xanthe
en: I am Xanthe, Magistrate of Pitana. I have a noble task befitting someone of your high station. My son is to start his military training at the agoge. My husband is away at war, and I have official business to attend to. Can you escort him for me?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I can escort your son to the camp master.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Good. He'll learn how to be a man like his father and brother, or he'll die trying.

speaker: Kassandra
en: But my service needs to be rewarded.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Of course. You would be paid well for your time.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And they say Spartans don't speak sweetly.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It would be my honor to take him to begin his education as a Spartan.

speaker: Xanthe
en: You are an agent of Zeus.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't pretend to know the thoughts of the gods, but I'm happy to guide your son.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I have no time to be your mule.

speaker: Xanthe
en: Eagle Bearer, I hope I did not offend before. It would be a great honor for my son if you could escort him to commence his military training.

speaker: Xanthe
en: My youngest is a dreamer. His head is filled with boyhood stories. He must learn how to serve his nation first, and then his family.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's not an easy path.

speaker: Xanthe
en: He will find glory as a true Spartan soldier, or die bravely in the attempt. There is no greater way to honor Sparta. You'll find the agoge camp southwest of here, near the foothills of the mountains. Makarios, come here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Hello. I am Kassandra.

speaker: Makarios
en: I am honored to meet you, Eagle Bearer. I can't wait to learn to fight like my brother, Theoros. And to hear all your stories of deadly monsters and glorious adventures!

speaker: Makarios
en: This way Kassandra! The agoge is up in the mountains. So we can train closer to Olympos!

speaker: Makarios
en: What's it like, being a mercenary?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I do what I must to get by.

speaker: Makarios
en: My brother said the same thing about being a man in Sparta. We learn to fight, to die for our family and our country... I can't wait!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You love your home, eh?

speaker: Makarios
en: I do. We are strong and we are free! And any man would happily give his life for his city, his fellow soldiers, and his children.

speaker: Kassandra
en: So how many children do you have?

speaker: Makarios
en: Uh, no, none... but when I'm older I'm going to marry Athena, and we'll have the strongest sons!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Well, then.

speaker: Makarios
en: Do you know why a Spartan soldier can lose his helmet or spear without worry, but if he loses his shield, he is punished beyond all measure?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Tell me.

speaker: Makarios
en: It is because a soldier needs his helmet and spear to defend only himself, but his shield is dearly important for the safety of his brothers and the whole battle line.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stay on your guard!

speaker: Makarios
en: Zeus save me!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Stand your ground!

speaker: Makarios
en: Oh no, oh no, oh no...

speaker: Makarios
en: Ah! So fast!

speaker: Makarios
en: I will not fear!

speaker: Makarios
en: There's so much blood!

speaker: Kassandra
en: Life ends, hot and messy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: What of your brother?

speaker: Makarios
en: Theoros? He's the best! He's amazing to watch in the games. He's fast and strong, and he can throw the javelin and discus farther than anyone.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh yes?

speaker: Makarios
en: I'm faster than anyone my age, but Theoros is like Herakles himself!

speaker: Kassandra
en: He sounds like a god made flesh.

speaker: Makarios
en: He's my hero! He even sings like Orpheus! Do you want to hear me sing? Though mother says I sing like a harpy.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No, that's OK. I'll be glad to meet him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire. I bring you a new charge, Trainer.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Makarios, son of Serios.

speaker: Makarios
en: Yes sir! I can't wait to see my brother

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Quiet, boy. No questions. You'll focus on your own lessons and duties, and speak when spoken to.

speaker: Makarios
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: You'll taste dirt and blood here. I'll force you to eat a thousand bitter lessons to harden you into the bronze shield your city needs.

speaker: Makarios
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Now, misthios, you look like you've been in a few scrapes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: A scrape or two... hundred. I like to think I've given as good as I've gotten.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Ha! Spoken like a true warrior. What say we give these summer youths a spectacle? Show them a clash of Titans?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I don't waste breath describing my exploits or trying to scare children.

speaker: Iatrokles
en: You speak like a Spartan. Let's see if you've learned anything else.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let's give these kids a show they'll sing for years.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm no child for you to loom over. Feel no shame when you ask for mercy, old man.

speaker: Makarios
en: Wow! What a battle! You fought like Atalanta!

speaker: Iatrokles
en: Huh, you do fight with the strength of the gods.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You're the one who left the message on the board. What's going on?

speaker: Woman
en: The soldiers and their commander who have set up camp near the village are tyrants. They control our movements and won't let us leave.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why do you want to leave? Are you fleeing?

speaker: Woman
en: No, but there are several pregnant women who live outside the village. If the soldiers keep me from helping them, they and their babies will likely die.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Let me guess. You want me to kill him.

speaker: Woman
en: It's not an easy task, but yes, the Spartan must be killed./Yes, the Athenian commander must fall.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll help you. You have my word.

speaker: Woman
en: I'm in your debt.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'll come back when I'm done.

speaker: Woman
en: You again. Have you killed him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Woman
en: You do good work, misthios. Take this for your trouble.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That'll do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: No going back now. I have to trust her.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Aletheia needs to work on that landing.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Eugh!

speaker: Persephone
en: You don't belong here.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Oh, shit.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I picked up your message on the board. What's happening?

speaker: Woman
en: Eagle Bearer! I know what you did for my Himilko—how you stopped that traitorous Heitor from killing him.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My job was to retrieve a sword for him, not act on some petty quest for vengeance.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The fight between him and your husband wasn't something I wanted to get involved with. It wasn't my place to kill him.

speaker: Woman
en: Well, I wholeheartedly thank you. I only wish our mercenary troubles were over.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Mercenary troubles?

speaker: Woman
en: I was really hoping the trouble with Heitor would teach my Himilko a lesson, but since returning home, he's gotten into trouble with yet another mercenary.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And let me guess, you want me to kill him.

speaker: Woman
en: I know it's a tall order, but I want this mercenary dead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm in.

speaker: Woman
en: Good, please be quick.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Leave it to me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Job done.

speaker: Woman
en: You again. Have you killed him?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your man is dead.

speaker: Woman
en: You've earned your payment, misthios. Here. This is for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Doesn't look this life is offering you much, but another awaits aboard my ship. Sail with me – we need someone like you.

speaker: Woman
en: My family is here, misthios. I can't leave them behind.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Too bad. You would have loved life on the sea.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All in a day's work.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Welcome back! There's a message for you on the board. Came from the Delos Islands. One of the Cultists is there, Kassandra. His name is Podarkes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You reading my messages, Barnabas?

speaker: Barnabas
en: I may have taken a peek.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Ahh, the Delos Islands! Two side of the same coin. Delos, sacred birthplace of Artemis and Apollo. And Mykonos, where people do everything that's forbidden on Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Read me the note again.

speaker: Barnabas
en: "Eagle-bearing misthios." That's you.

speaker: Barnabas
en: "Podarkes, cruel leader of Delos Islands, takes money from our pockets and food from our mouths. All to feed his insate... insati..."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Insatiable.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Yes! "His insatiable thirst for power."

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes is one of them, Barnabas. The ones hunting my family. Keep reading.

speaker: Barnabas
en: "We are a modest but fierce group of rebels, who'd pay you handsomely to help us overthrow our vile oppressor. I pray the winds guide you swiftly to our shores, misthios. Our people are dying." Signed "Kyra."

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm here for Podarkes' head. The rebels will lead me right to him.

speaker: Barnabas
en: These are such beautiful islands, Kassandra. At least visit the Sanctuary of Apollo before you start taking heads.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We arrived just in time to help.

speaker: Barnabas
en: You see? Poseidon wasn't trying to drown you, he was getting you where you needed to go... ...aggressively.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I should go. There's work to be done.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Gods forbid we enjoy a single moment on this glorious beach.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Does the note say where Kyra is?

speaker: Barnabas
en: There are two locations marked. A camp along the northwestern coast, and a hideout that looks like it's... underneath the city.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Podarkes sounds like a cruel man.

speaker: Barnabas
en: He's worse. I once heard a family was late in paying their dues to the gods. Podarkes sent his men to their farm, and took the young ones from their beds... When their mater and pater woke up to feed the animals, they discovered the animals were already feeding on the corpses of their sons.

speaker: Kassandra
en: The sooner I send this monster to Hades, the better.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Even Hades would shudder in his presence.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This place seems... nice.

speaker: Barnabas
en: This island has a giant history, my friend.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We don't have time, Barnabas.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I meant Mykonos literally has a history involving giants. Apollo was once friends with ns from the snowy north. Until one day, they sent two maidens and five of their men to Delos with offerings for the son of Zeus. They were never seen again.

speaker: Kassandra
en: And Mykonos?

speaker: Barnabas
en: The island was built from the corpses of giants slain by the legendary Herakles.

speaker: Kassandra
en: My mind wandered. Remind me what the note said?

speaker: Barnabas
en: "Eagle-bearing misthios."

speaker: Kassandra
en: The short version please.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Podarkes... Cruel leader... Thirst for power... Pay you handsomely... Rebellion... People dying.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's time I met with this Kyra.

speaker: Barnabas
en: I'll have the ship ready in case we need any... immediate departures.

speaker: Kassandra
en: That was Kephallonia, and that was mostly your fault.

speaker: Barnabas
en: Chaire, Kassandra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Chaire, Barnabas.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's the rebel hideout.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Seems like a good place for a hideout.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I'm looking for the one called Kyra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I've come in response to a call for help.

speaker: Kassandra
en: You missed.

speaker: Kyra
en: Are you here to spy, Athenian? Or maybe you are Athena herself, dressed in a dirty disguise?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Do I really look like a spy to you?

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came to help a "fierce group of rebels." But I show up and you're all drunk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sure. I'm a god. You think it's wise to throw blades first and ask questions later?

speaker: Kyra
en: Podarkes and his men have hunting and killing us without mercy.

speaker: Kyra
en: His spies are everywhere. He won't rest until all who oppose him are dead. We are all that's left of the resistance.

speaker: Kyra
en: This is the first night we aren't fighting for our lives, and it could be our last. And suddenly, you show up.

speaker: Kassandra
en: This is why I'm here. It's your symbol, right?

speaker: Kyra
en: You're the misthios who bears the Eagle of Zeus. My apologies, these are dangerous times for anyone waging war against the Athenian empire and the Delian League. I am Kyra.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Your note mentions Podarkes. I'm going to find him.

speaker: Kyra
en: His house is on the coast, north of Mykonos City. But he's heavily guarded. We've never been able to get close enough without taking heavy casualties. This is why I sent for you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I thought Delos was the heart of the Delian League—Athens' pride and joy.

speaker: Kyra
en: We were. Until Athens took the League's treasury away from Delos.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Why?

speaker: Kyra
en: So they could build a statue of Athena mocking Apollo. The people pleaded with Podarkes not to trust Athens with the treasury. But his thirst for power made him deaf to his people.

speaker: Kassandra
en: If things are so miserable, why doesn't Delos abandon the League?

speaker: Kyra
en: Podarkes sends Athenian soldiers to collect money from us all. The moment that stops, Athenian ships will burn our islands to the ground.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I came here to help you deal with one man, not go to war.

speaker: Kyra
en: Which is why I sent word of our rebellion to the mighty Kassandra, and Sparta, too.

speaker: Praxos
en: Podarkes discovered the other camp and Athenian soldiers to attack.

speaker: Kyra
en: Maláka!

speaker: Kassandra
en: You and your rebels are too drunk to fight. Leave the soldiers to me.

speaker: Kyra
en: If you think I'm going to miss a chance to kill Athenians, you're the one who's drunk.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Did Sparta answer your call for help?

speaker: Kyra
en: A polemarch named Thaletas and a handful of Spartans landed on Mykonos not long before you.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's their camp we're head to, isn't it?

speaker: Kyra
en: Thaletas needs our help now, though he'd never admit it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Sounds Spartan all right.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Someone say Sparta?

speaker: Kyra
en: You're alive.

speaker: Kassandra
en: How are your men?

en: Alive as well, thanks to you.

speaker: Kyra
en: You've met. Good. Now that we're all friends, we need a plan.

en: That must be one of the camps.

en: You there, misthios! Fight by my side!

en: Well that got the blood pumping. I should talk to this Spartan.

en: You fight well. Spartan?

en: I was, but that was a long time ago.

en: Spartan blood is eternal, stranger. What's your name?

en: And who are you?

en: Kassandra.

en: What do you want with her?

en: We've all lost friends to this war. We can mourn together, but first I need to find Kyra.

en: What do you want with her?

en: I got a note from Kyra. Her rebellion is failing.

en: Kyra sent me a note. I'm here to kill Podarkes.

en: She's clever—Sparta got the same note. I will help Kyra reclaim these islands.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Just don't forget who helped you reclaim this beach.

en: I like you, warrior. The rebel hideout is an underground cave, southwest of here. I'll meet you there.

speaker: Thaletas
en: You there, misthios! Fight by my side!

en: Well that got the blood pumping. I should talk to this Spartan.

en: You fought well, Kyra.

en: You too. Spartan?

en: I was, but that was a long time ago.

en: This is Kassandra. The one I told you about.

en: Was?

en: Our ship was sunk. Our generals killed. There are only a few of us left.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Soldiers die—it's what they do.

speaker: Kassandra
en: We've all lost friends to this war.

speaker: Kyra
en: And we will mourn them later.

speaker: Kassandra
en: She's right. We shouldn't be standing here, drenched in Athenian blood.

speaker: Kyra
en: We'll be safe in the hideout. Let's talk there.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Will you come to the hideout now, or meet us there later?

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's no time to waste. We'll go to the hideout now.

speaker: Kassandra
en: There's some things I want to see first. I'll join you both later.

speaker: Kyra

en: His nose is so high in the air, he couldn't find the Statue of Artemis Agrotera if he was standing on her head.

speaker: Kyra
en: That's a terrible plan!

en: The Spartan phalanx is impenetrable in a ground assault.

speaker: Kyra
en: Not when there's only twelve of you! You think with your heart—that's what I like about you. But you're a general to those men now. You need to think with your head.

speaker: Thaletas
en: All you do is hide in caves and lurk in shadows. We didn't come here to hide. We came here to fight.

speaker: Kyra
en: And we will! But right now we're outnumbered. We must be strategic.

speaker: Kyra
en: Kassandra, what do you think we should do?

en: Kyra's right. Taking them head on would be suicide.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Sailing here was suicide. Right now, my men are on the beach. That's where I'll be.

en: Thaletas, don't.

en: If you decide you actually want to win this rebellion, come find me.

speaker: Kassandra
en: Spartans.

speaker: Kyra
en: Don't mind him. He'll be fine after he kicks something.

speaker: Kyra
en: But I'm glad you agree with me, Kassandra. Meet me at the Temple of Artemis. There we can discuss how to take down Podarkes.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I like the way the Spartan thinks. But we don't have enough swords to fight them head on.

speaker: Thaletas
en: What do you suggest?

speaker: Kassandra
en: When I arrived I saw Spartan ships. Can we get a message to them?

speaker: Thaletas
en: Not while the Athenian navy surrounds these islands.

en: Hmm. We need those reinforcements.

en: I got the two of you here to actually help the rebellion, not to send more people to their deaths.

speaker: Thaletas
en: Kyra, wait.

en: While the two of you compare swords, I'll be at the Temple of Artemis making an actual plan.

en: She has fight. I like it.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I suppose we're following the one at the top.

speaker: Kassandra
en: I follow the one with expertise. Surely they know better than I do.

speaker: Sokrates
en: Then your decision is based only on what another says.

speaker: Kassandra
en: It's all I have to go off of.

speaker: Sokrates
en: And if they lied?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Everyone makes mistakes! I would continue to follow them.

en: It's only natural to believe the person you follow is worth your loyalty. However, those who are untrustworthy do not deserve to lead.

speaker: Kassandra
en: People who lie to me don't deserve my trust.

en: Nor should they! After all, if someone lies to you a single time, what's to say they would not do so again?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Yes, you're right.

speaker: Sokrates
en: So you agree that someone who lies to you is not worthy of leading?

speaker: Kassandra
en: Of course.

en: O Athenians, would you not also agree that you can have responsibility for harming another, even through someone else?

en: And would you follow someone you found out had lied to you for their own gain?

speaker: Civilian
en: Of course not!

en: Now that you know the truth, you can take back your decision.

en: Another vote must be called! The lives of those people are in your hands, too. The ship must be stopped!

speaker: Sokrates
en: That probably could have gone better. But, even so, I believe the people are unable to deny the proof we presented.

speaker: Sokrates
en: That was a great display of rhetoric. The people will be unable to deny what they heard.

speaker: Kassandra
en: All we did was talk.

en: What we did was far more. We used proof and a clear argument to bring forth an outcome that will not just hurt Kleon, but hopefully save countless lives.

en: I guess I learned something. It must be from all the time I've spent around you.

en: Debate may not always be as quick as a blade, but it can have just as big an effect.

en: But was it enough?

en: I believe word of Kleon's misdeeds will be shared throughout Athens. Its citizens love the city and what it stands for. Nobody wishes for it to fall.

en: I know this is difficult.

en: It's like I don't even know myself anymore. Where I come from. Who I am.

en: Kassandra, I promise you that he will have answers.

en: I don't blame you for that. But there are things you need to know if we are to stop the Cult.
